title: Samsung GT-B2710 Solid Immerse
text:
Great phone but after using it for 2 months, I've found out a few things. The default phone firmware is a bit buggy. I haven't tried to update the firmware yet. Texting with T9 causes the phone to lock up periodically while composing messages. About three weeks ago, after getting the phone wet while kayaking, the microphone started to act up. People complain they barely hear me or hear a lot of static on inbound and outbound calls. I thought it was because water or sand got into the microphone port. I checked the microphone port a week later with a magnifying glass and the port is dry and debris free. All o-ring seals are intact and clean. The internals are totally dry with no trace of water exposure. The only workaround for now is to use a bluetooth headset. Other than the microphone issue, the phone has performed like a champ. It's slipped out of my hand while cycling and I didn't have any problems. The gorilla glass is tough but I recommend putting on a screen protector. The screen scratched while washing car with my phone and keys together in my trouser pocket.
11/14/12 - Phone is still going strong. Battery life is still admirable. However, the latest firmware updates still haven't resolved the T9 input crashing issue. I also noticed that after syncing my Google contacts using Kies in June 2012, the phone would start hang randomly for several minutes and then continue to operate as if nothing happened. The hanging was getting so frequent that I decided to factory-reset the phone a few weeks ago. After loading up my pre-Google sync contact list, the phone has been operating normally. The phone doesn't seem to either like the Google's formatting of the contacts or the sheer volume of contact info. The phone will detect a Rocksoul bluetooth keyboard but will throw up a "Unsupported Device" error.

title: The Beast
text:
This phone performs like a phone should. Everything that has been advertised and claimed concerning this phone is accurate. I get better signal with this phone than I did with my previous 15 yr old Nokia. My Nokia would pick up a signal when no other phone would... this one gets signal where the Nokia was spotty or had no signal. I showed the phone to a group of friends at the college I attend and told them it was a tough phone. One friend showed me his android tough phone and pointed out that mine was not a touch screen and could not browse the internet as well as his. I don't use the internet... I have T-mobile and pay for unlimited Talk/text. I don't want an android or an I Phone because I have a laptop that performs online tasks with better efficiency. Long story short I had my friend agree to put his phone to a test along with mine (this was about 15 min before our Microbiology Lab). I dropped my phone down the center of a 3 story stair well (each story being 12', so about 4 stories in some structures) and the phone was absolutely fine. My friend was very apprehensive about repeating what I had done, but after some intense peer pressure he complied and his phone's face broke off, the touch screen cracked, and the battery compartment fractured (he had insurance and was not as upset as one might guess). After this we put my phone in a fish tank throughout the duration of our 2 hour lab and then called the phone when we got out... the screen lit up inside the tank and reported an incoming call. I took the phone out and answered the call and could hear clearly.

I was an Infantry Marine (Sgt. in 2/3 Wpns Co. out of Kaneohe Bay, HI)... I wish I had found this phone when I was in to say the least. I had a couple of 'tough' phones and countless other phones during my 4.5 yrs of service and I did manage to destroy each one of them. Amphibious landing drills claimed the lives of 2 phones. I brought a motorola tough phone to Iraq because I thought the camera built into the phone was tough and took great pictures... it took a hard blow when I fell down a wadi and began turning on only when it felt like it; later a phosphorous IED burnt it to a pile of nothing. Another phone (the second tough phone/ Iridium phone) I purchased was a satellite phone that cost me about $250/month... I brought this thing to Afghanistan and it stopped working after being left inside a HMWV in the sun for about 9 hours. That phone was an absolute tank, but I guess the heat was able to breech its defenses. I am going to the Mojave desert next summer to see a buddy now stationed at 29 Palms Marine Corps Base and I plan on bringing the B2710 with me... we'll see what happens (plan on doing a good heat test). So far I am very surprised with the phone's performance and look forward to not having to buy another phone for quite a while!!

title: Excellent replacement for your GSM carrier's non-smartphone phone.
text:
I purchased this phone to replace someone else's "free" flip phone given by AT&T (which started to have random glitches after irreversible firmware update). That person does not want or need any smartphone functionality, and for this purpose, this phone is a perfect replacement. It is very compact, it works on all non-3G GSM bands (doesn't seem to be working with AT&T's 3G frequency, but that is not important for a phone like this), it has a good reception in all zones covered by AT&T and a pretty good battery life.
The body has a minimal set of buttons - no silly PTT (push-to-talk) or media player dedicated buttons on outside (which tend to be pressed randomly on other models and thus require the usage of key lock function, which is annoying), just a volume up/down button on the right side. The front display is minimalistic, but it does its function perfectly and displays all the needed info (current time or Caller ID info) using a perfectly legible and elegant-looking font. There are 2 charger "ports" on outside, one is USB (the "micro USB" kind) and the one is the round plug which requires the (included) proprietary charger. The phone can be charged through either of them and they are not covered by rubber "flaps", which is less "annoying" than other phones where you have to almost break your nails trying to extract the little rubber/plastic flap out of charging port.
The software is also minimalistic but pretty functional, with all functions required by such phone working perfectly and easy to set up (you have to do a little bit of typing setting up MMS/WEB gateway settings for AT&T network (visit AT&T's official forums, the Nokia section, to read about necessary settings), but if you don't need these functions everything else is pretty self-explanatory and don't require any "user manual" or Google searches to set up). The GPS function works with AT&T's "Family Map" tracking service, though you do need to enable data usage for GPS function to be able to locate this phone's user with more precision and with shorter time, but the data usage is very insignificant and you don't have to do that if you don't use the "Family Map" service.
What else... The built-in camera works well for its intended function - obviously not as good as similar cameras on smartphones but better than majority of cameras on other non-smartphones. Oh, and some people complained about the back cover being somewhat difficult to remove - it's true, it is initially difficult to remove it, but you can learn (after a few tries) to remove it easily, it just requires finding a right "spot" to press while pulling the cover, and the cover itself is made out of pretty flexible plastic so it is highly unlikely that you might break it (unless you are a very, very impatient person) and you don't need to remove it at all if you don't need to change your SIM card. Overall it is one of the best non-smartphone models I have ever had pleasure dealing with and I highly recommend it if all you need is to make calls and maybe occasionally send/receive a SMS/MMS message.

title: One of the Best Flip Phones
text:
First - I am shocked at the $30 rise in price in just two weeks for this well-made phone from Nokia. The only thing I can figure is this phone is not manufactured by Nokia anymore, per their web site (it's in their 'archive').

That aside, it is a great phone with excellent vocal clarity. The built-in voice recognition is also good. The Nokia's speed dial (unlike the LG LG230 Dimson) is able to assign different phone numbers belonging to the same person (e.g. a speed-dial number for your wife's work and a speed-dial number for you wife's cell). A note regarding 'voice dialing': No need to say "call" etc. - just say the person's name. E.g. "John Smith, Mobile"

PROS
Excepts up to 8GB microSD RAM
Speed dial number oriented (allows more than one speed-dial number per phone book entry)
Works well with Bluetooth: Tested with Bluetooth Headsets [[ASIN:B0035ZF0TI Jawbone ICON]] and [[ASIN:B002JIMZU4 Plantronics Discovery 975]]

FOIBLES
Battery Cover

As with other evaluations, the back of this phone is (putting it mildly) DIFFICULT to remove once the battery is inserted. I suspect the battery forcing the cover up along with the unusual hinge angle over the earphone jack as the cause of the difficulty. I have been successful in carefully prising the cover off the phone: the but-end and then the two sides so they snap loose; then carefully raise the end to unhinge the back from around the earphone jack. Poor design for the sake of elegance. Hopefully, Nokia gets it right on the next flip-phone cover design - WAIT - there is no Nokia flip phone on the American market.

15 October 2011 Correction to above comment regarding 'voice dialing': This phone cannot be instructed to pick one of many numbers assigned to a phone book entry - it uses the 'default' number only.

text:

title: A non data users delight
text: This is a wonderfully designed phone for people who don't have a data plan and don't want one.  It gets great reception, makes clear calls and will do texting if you so desire.  The main menu is super user friendly and it has some useful built in apps.  The GPS Maps and navigation are free and you don't have to access the wireless internet to use them.  You can download them with your home computer over your home internet connection and transfer them to the phone with the Nokia Ovi software suite.  The FM radio and MP3 player work well.  This little unlocked phone is far better than anything AT&T is currently offering for people who are not interested in accessing the internet with their cell phones.  The freedom from AT&T's locked phone software is a huge plus and greatly simplifies the phones menu navigation and ease of use.  I put in the AT&T SIM, 4 GB of extra memory and the battery and the phone fired right up.  Only minimal configuration was required to meet my particular desire to have the GPS function never access the internet and to run the network in GSM only mode to save battery life since I never access the 3G network.  If you are not technically inclined you need not do anything and you will be no worse off than AT&T's locked phone default configuration.  The setup menus are very user friendly.  I had no problem removing the back cover as some other comments suggested.  The camera is nothing special and lacks auto focus but does have a flash.  It is about equivalent in picture quality to a throw away snap shot camera.  I highly recommend this phone to any non data cell phone user.

title: It was great until..
text: I purchased this case about 9 or 10 months ago and didn't start having trouble until 6 months after. At first I loved this case. It fit well on my phone, never popped off and was easy to remove if I needed to remove it. After having it for a short while the "leathery skin" part of the case (not the plastic part, just the outer leather part) began to peel off. I haven't dropped my phone since I had the case because of the wonderful clip that it comes with. It never fell off of my pants pocket when I would go out. So I am guessing it started peeling off not because of being dropped but just because it was being used. After that incident I just super-glued the skin back onto the plastic of the case and everything was fine.. Until about 2 weeks later I needed to take the case off of my phone to remove the battery. The little "clip" part that makes the case hold onto your phone decided that it wanted to pop off. So then the front part of my case wouldn't stay on anymore. Although I believe this is a wonderful case, I don't really like how it didn't last as long as I had hoped for. Sure, a little wear and tear is normal, of course, but for it to become completely unusable after 7 months is a bit ridiculous. I am a tad bit disappointed about not being able to use the case anymore because, honestly, it is still my personal favorite. Overall, the case is wonderful and for the price it is worth it. Just don't expect it to last long or look like it did right out of the box after so many months (unless of course you don't use your phone or case as often). I would buy this case again, only next time I think I will be even more careful with the case to extend its life.

title: Gold standard in Smart Phones
text:
I did the iPhone 3G & 3GS. I did the Motorola Droid. I came back to the smartphone that started it all.

my (AT&T)iPhone randomly dropped calls. My (Verizon)Droid randomly deleted email accounts. Both featured poor phonecall voice quality: The Droid's voice quality was acceptable in the sticks, but horrible where I live & work (downtown Chicago). The iPhone was horrible everywhere. Battery life was dreadful for both.

Frustrated with it all, I came back to the Blackberry; the first smart phone I ever owned (courtesy of my employer at the time).

It just works and works well. My iPhone/Droid could barely make a phonecall from my office. My 9780 can make phonecalls from within its elevator. My Blackberry's battery lasts days whereas my Droid & iPhone could barely make it through a single work day.

Most people have no clue that I am on a cell phone until I tell them so. I don't know if this is a credit to the Blackberry or T-Mobile but, needless to say, I've found my ideal phone & service provider combo for the next two years.

-Battery life is incredible and it charges quite rapidly
-The new Blackberry OS is snappy and attractive and very configurable
-Accessories are far cheaper than those for iPhone/Droid
-light, thin and small. Perfect for your front pocket, but comes with an attractive holster also.
-Love the all black body. Not a huge fan of the fancy trim found on other phones.

NOTE: I also accidentally dropped it in a cup of hot tea (full submersed) the first week I owned it. Amazingly, after pulling the battery and allowing the liquid to drain, it still worked, albeit with a finicky touchpad and a screen that blinked at random times. I let it dry completely for 4 hours and everything was as good as new afterwards.

title: Crackberry Addict
text: This is my second Blackberry.  Upgraded from the old BB Curve 8560.  Love the new OS 6 and universal search mode.  New camera upgrade is great with useful settings.  The MP3 sound quality is wonderful.  Screen is crisp.  Battery lasts for days and I am a heavy user.  Love my BBM and its new upgrades too.  I thought of switching to ATT for the BB Torch but found it to be sluggish.  I like the ability to be able to surf and use this phone one handed when I need too.  I have been with TMo since 2002 and am sad that ATT has bought it over.  My husband has ATT and it has poor customer service at a higher price.  The Blackberry will also play MP4 format songs which works well since both my children have iTouches and we can share music.  As for the screen size, I am able to read books using the BB Kindle app with ease.  This is solid, well built and efficient phone.  There are more apps now and our favorite is the shared shopping list that works for both Android (my husband) and my BB.  Makes grocery shopping a breeze.  Hope this helps.  You can also share Kindle ebooks with the various Apple and BB devices.

title: Superb phone, great network-Update 1 year later
text:
I was a long time T-Mobile customer, and then was wooed by the iPhone4 and AT&T. After a year of frustration over typing on a touchscreen (maddening) and a total dead zone at work, I paid up an early termination fee and bought this T-Mobile Blackberry.

Like other reviewers stated, the phone works and works well.

The little keyboard is FANTASTIC! So much easier to type quickly and accurately as compared to a touchscreen keyboard.

I get 5 bars of service at my desk, where AT&T could only manage "no service" or one bar. I get the wonderful UMA calling, which routes calls over wifi networks, to use where T-Mobile lacks service.

Blackberry 6 is a great update. The various apps are nicely integrated with the device and with each other, you do not need to pop into the photos to find a picture, back out, then in to another app to post the picture, you can just roll through the menu to do it right from the posting app. Much more convenient. The universal search is very useful. The browser is still a bit slow and not as smoothly intuitive as the iPhone's Safari browser, but it is way better than older blackberry browsers.

I am very very happy with this phone!

UPDATE, July 2012:
I still love this phone! Still works superbly, and has held up really well; still looks brand new! I love the messaging capabilities of this phone, and it works really well as a phone too. Comfortable in the hand, gets good clear calls, easy to find and call contacts. I'm sad to read of BlackBerry woes, they make great phones! I would love to upgrade to the new ones but this one just works so well I can't justify the expense.

title: The faulty USB port makes it hard to charge at times
text:
First off, I want to say that I got this phone to simply text and make phone calls. I do NOT go on the internet, take photos, or anything else. I just needed a very basic phone for communication only.

Anyway, the keyboard on this phone is excellent! I used to have an LG Xenon, which had a full keyboard. Because it had a full keyboard, I texted extremely slowly. As soon as I got this Blackberry Pearl, however, I was able to text very quickly. Each key has 1-2 letters on it, which makes the keyboard a lot smaller and therefore easier to text. It has a dictionary, so it knows what words you are trying to text MOST of the time. Sometimes it gets it wrong, but most of the time I have no issues. The main word it mixes up is "see" and "are".

When it comes to phone calls, I never have an issue with that. The battery lasts throughout the entire call. I make calls that are a good 2hours sometimes. The Blackberry has no problem with battery life. The sound is perfectly fine. I can hear the other person very clearly. My calls are NEVER dropped on this phone. It is great.

Once in awhile I will take photos. The photos are good quality, but they honestly do not compare to my digital camera. If I need to take a quick snap shot, I will use my phone. If I need to take a good quality photo, then my digital camera is the answer.

One thing that bugs me about this phone is the alarm system. You are limited to ONE alarm, which really stinks because I could really use at least 2 alarms.

Lastly, the main reason I am giving ths onlly 3 stars is due to the fact that the faulty USB port makes it difficult to charge at times. My phone will be nearly dead, so I go to plug it in and the phone does not seem to realize that it is plugged in. I take it out, plug it back in, remove it yet again, plug it back in once more, and get nothing. I will remove the battery, place it back into the phone, and still get no charge signal. I then decide to remove the battery, remove my SIM card, replace the battery, try yet again, and SOMETIMES I will finally get a charge signal on the phone. It's one of those annoying things where you have to play around with everything until you can finally get it to charge up. I am not the only one with this problem. If you look it up online, other people have the same exact problem with their Blackberry Pearls. It is a result of the USB port being faulty, which makes sense because when I plug my phone in, the USB port seems to be slightly movable, when it should be solid and stable.

Anyway, if the USB port was not an issue, I would have given a higher rating. It is a great phone, but you may want to consider getting a battery charger, just in case you have a tough time struggling with the USB port like me.

title: The best NON-SMART phone I have ever used
text:
I admit that this phone is inferior to many smart-phones that are currently on the market. Those all, however, require a data plan to use. If you are like me and want a quality phone without having to pay for a data plan then this is the phone for you. I have been using a BlackBerry Pearl for the last 6 years, so I am pretty familiar with its pros and cons.

Pros:
-Modified qwerty keyboard. While it is not a full qwerty (most of the buttons share two letters) I only commonly run across one mix up ("see" and "are"). That is a HUGE improvement over 9 key.
-A smart phone quality calendar.
-Very good media player
-Bluetooth
-Great Address book options.
-Unlimited text inbox space; not the 250-500 text limit that virtually all phones have.
-Many text search options. Great for when you are looking for that text you need but can't remember when you got it or who sent it.
-Voice dialing
-Fits very well into a pocket
-Can set any size file as a ringtone, alarm, etc.

...I could go on

Cons:
-The camera and video camera are not very good. I understand that there are people for whom a phone camera is more important than a calendar or address book or wifi then this is not the phone for you.
-Much like a roller ball mouse, every year or so the track ball needs to be cleaned. There are many tutorials online that explain how this should be done. Once cleaned it works like new.
-The headphone jack is smaller than is standard for headphones. If you want the standard 3.5mm jack then you probably want to upgrade to the 8120 or 8130.

I have used many many phones, but this is far and away the best NON-SMART phone I have ever used. Ever.

title: Don't buy if you want to send or receive photos
text:
First, I love this phone;It was everything I wanted, without all the "smartphone" junk and expense I wouldn't use. I didn't want to get stuck in another 2 yr contract, and have to buy a data plan with AT&T, just because I had to have a new phone. I researced for weeks, with no cell phone, ended up buying a gophone, LG Encore (touchscreen horror story!) and using it for 2 weeks before I settled on this phone. So I didn't just jump into a new phone.
This phone is great as far as sound, dialing, texting, if ALL you want is a simple phone; If that was all, I'd give it 5 stars, so if you want to get a good, plain phone, at this price, go for it. You can stop reading now.
However, if you want a phone you can use to take and then send or ever receive multimedia messages, keep looking. The camera, although a 3.2 mp takes grainy, blurry pictures.
My biggest issue with the phone is that I can't ever receive or send anything except text messages. Forget the cute Christmas pics I was supposed to have gotten from friends and relatives! I had the phone for about 3 weeks before deciding there must be a problem, since I had more than 1 person ask what I thought of the pics they had sent! This phone IS NOT UNLOCKED to receive multimedia (mms)messages. Believe me, I have tried! I have spent literally hours on the phone with AT&T tech people over the last 3 days, trying to see if it could be set to receive mms. Every tech rep was extremely helpful and made calls, searched the web, and did all they could to try and help. After the first 2 days of working to find the problem, we even decided to return the phone and get another one (Amazon advertises the phone as unlocked for mms as well as web access). I received the new phone yesterday, and after letting it fully charge, went through the whole ordeal of set-up again. Then spent another hour on the phone with a tech, same thing.
This phone WILL NOT accept, or send, multimedia messages, and you CANNOT access the web (though it is supposed to be unlocked to do that and is advertised as such), IF you use AT&T services (I can't speak for other carriers), be aware this will not work for you.
One last thought, since I'm sure many of us might assume it is AT&T's fault, since this is not their phone maybe they just don't want to put in the codes needed. I also had a conference call with Nokia. The rep I spoke to was very rude and refused to help or assume any responsibility from Nokia. I had called Nokia and been told to have the AT&T tech person do a conf call with me and they would be able to help. When I got a tech person on the phone and called Nokia back, their rep was unbelievably rude and a huge waste of time. Nokia refused to help at all. I now have to either keep a "dumbed down" phone, or go through the process of trying to find a good phone all over again! So, buyer be aware!

text:
This phone has all the features I need at a reasonable price. Here are some of my favorites:

Size - Small enough to easily fit in your pocket.
Battery life - Very good. I can usually go about 5 days between charges. Previous phones I have owned usually lasted about 3 days.
Camera - It takes very nice pictures if the light is good and you hold it still.
Data - It is easy to connect to a computer with a micro USB cable (not included) to access the microSDHC flash memory card (not included). I recommend buying both a micro USB cable and a microSDHC flash memory card when you buy this phone.
[[ASIN:B004PCJQGS Samsung USB Home Travel Charger with Detachable Micro USB Cable for Galaxy S 4G T959V, Vibrant Plus, Vibrant 4G]]
[[ASIN:B0058GH450 AmazonBasics 8 GB microSDHC Class 10 Flash Memory Card with SD Adapter]]
Buttons - The buttons have a nice feel. They are good for the occasional text message. The predictive text works pretty well for typing with only 10 keys.
Media player - You can load MP3s on this phone and play them through the included earphones. It also plays FM radio. You can also select MP3s as ring tones.
Charging - Charging can be done using the included adapter or through the micro USB cable.
Compatibility - I use T-Mobile pre paid. I put my SIM card in, and the phone worked right away. It will not send pictures, but I have read that you can contact T-Mobile to enable picture send if you want it. Since pictures cost $.25 each to send, I choose to keep this feature disabled and upload any pictures directly to my PC.
Nokia Suite software - This is my only complaint about this phone. This software is confusing and difficult to use. It will allow you to put some extra games on the phone, but many of the games will not work without a data plan. Downloading music and backing up the phone is not intuitive. The software needs a Windows Explorer type interface to show you exactly what is on the phone, and it needs a simple copy & paste feature. It also does not provide access to data on the SIM card, so you cannot get a simple list of your contacts.

Overall, this is a great replacement for the old phone that came with my T-Mobile pre paid plan.

title: Helps Me Not Get Distracted
text:
The Nokia C2-01 is a feature phone. It does not do the web well. The 3G on this phone is pretty slow on AT&T when compared to the iPhone, and the interface is not touch screen. If you want those things, you should buy the iPhone. It's a cool phone, and you can play sweet games about birds and tweet a picture of the panini you are eating for dinner on Twitter, no problem.

After a week, I am in love with this phone. It takes good-enough pictures, does Gmail pretty well, has great bluetooth connectivity, and plays my music. I can tether my iPad and computer to its data connection (AT&T) at no extra cost. The data connection is not fast but it gives me the web anywhere when I want it and, more importantly, its limited connectivity/non-touchscreenness helps me forget the web when I'm with my family.

As a former iPhone user, I used to make fun of people with feature phones. Now, it seems like I'm more aware of actual life when I'm out getting my pizza party on with the wife and kids. Instead of sitting face-down in some Facebook with stuff going on around me, my phone stays in my pocket and my attention stays on what's important.

It's not the phone for everyone, but it helps me be a better dad.

If you feel distracted by your technology, but still want to retain some connectivity (for work or even with other gadgets), this is not a bad choice. And it's cheap.

title: What happened when I tried to go from an iPhone to a Nokia C2-01
text:
I have an iPhone. But I wanted to be able to text and drive like the old days. I wanted buttons and T9. I wanted a phone that would get a better cell connection; at home; with the iPhone, I have to walk out into the street to make a call. I wanted a smaller, less slippery, less needy phone for sailing and biking. So, I bought the C2-01. I moved my number to the Nokia device and put a new number on the iPhone. Here are my observations after a precious day of fidgeting:

1) The Nokia phone seems crufty. And slow. It's not because of any defect in the function of the phone. It's just very far away from a modern design. It's my fault for thinking I could go home again, maybe.

2) There's a problem with email that people have been complaining about online for years with Nokia phones. It doesn't appear to have ever been answered. One can set up their Internet connectivity okay, but still be unable to make the Mail application return anything but "Communication error. Try again later." I can't get to the ovi store either. I can surf the web... that leaves me with webmail as an option. That's a really painful prospect on this tiny screen with its clunky interface.

3) When you go from an iPhone to something else using the same phone number, your iPhone (iMessage) friends won't be able to send you messages on your new phone. I haven't figured out how to fix this, though I've tried a number of online recommendations, including unregistering the iPhone.

If I conquered the email issue and the iMessage stickiness, I'm not sure it would be enough to make me feel good about my phone experiment. As a minimum, I will swap the phone numbers back. Will there be any point to keeping the Nokia phone then? Probably not.

UPDATE >> I hunted and pecked until I figured out the solution to the email problem/ovi store problem. Once you've got Internet connectivity through the web browser, go back into SETTINGS/CONFIGURATION/PERSONAL CONFIG/Options/New -> Access Point. Under Bearer Settings, type the name you chose for the Web (internet) access. Back out and activate the new 'access point.' Mail and Ovi should work. I was able to set the phone up for my Google Apps gmail account with no problem -- just by entering the email address and password. I did end up swapping the numbers back. I kept the Nokia phone as a second, unneeded line.

title: Excellent basic phone for international travel
text:
I purchased this phone because I needed a quad-band mobile that could be used with different SIM cards in Europe and Africa--I have so far used it in Namibia, South Africa and Ghana, and will be using it in Ireland and France next month. I wanted something that wouldn't fall apart, as I needed it to last me for a year in Namibia and Ghana, but I also didn't want to spend a lot of money in the likely case it were to be stolen while I was abroad. This phone fit the bill. It is very simple to learn to use straight out of the box, has a surprisingly decent camera, and immediately worked with the three different SIM cards from three different countries and companies.

Battery life on this phone was also excellent, going at least a week between charges even when I was sending and receiving dozens of texts a day (I rarely used it to call people as air time is too expensive for many Africans to afford, but I did make and receive a few international calls from/to Ghana and found the quality of these calls to be surprisingly good).

The one issue I had with the phone was that I was never able to access the internet despite being on a 3G network. I was never able to determine whether this was a problem with the network provider or with the phone itself. This wasn't a big issue for me as I had other ways to access the internet, but I wanted to note this as others have complained about the same problem with US providers.

Overall, I was very pleased with the value and quality of this phone. I'd highly recommend it to those traveling internationally, particularly to those that travel to multiple countries that may be on different GSM frequency bands.

title: Nokia C2-01 Unlocked (T Mobile Users)
text:
I bought the Nokia C2-01 after reading reviews and being an Old Sckool kind of guy when it comes to phones. I need a Phone to Talk and Text, I got a Laptop for the rest....

I use T Mobile Prepaid. When I first set up the phone I had a Problem. I could Not send or recieve picture messages. The only way I could get internet was through the Browser. The other functions like OVI store, Nokia.mobi, Home, and Web Services would not work.

""So here is how these Problems can be FIXED"",
I went to T Mobile online, go to bottom of the page and click on Contact Us, a new page will come up, on the top left click on Get Support Online .
Now when you do this you will need your T Mobile PIN number, NO problem if you forgot it, the Live Advisor will help you set up a new one. After all the confirmation of who you are, The Live Advisor will send you a message to the phone and with a code (1234), open the message enter the code and "ALL is FIXED", just to make sure the live advisor will tell you to take a photo and send it to yourself. Yea send it to your own phone number, I did not use my area code and it worked, I got my own picture message. After doing this my Nokia C2-01 worked 100% all issues with sending picture messages, and other functions were FIXED !

Personnaly the only time I "might" use the Web Browser is to check my Lotto Numbers, if you do the Face Book thing this phone is not for you because the screen is to small.

I also bought on Amazon the "I Talk" phone case it does the job and all opennings are perfect, there are some on ebay , But I have noticed all cases for the Nokia C2-01 mostly come from England (Royal Mail) could not find any here in the USA and there are some from China(ebay). The only thing I could find sold here in the USA are Screen Protectors, "don't forget them".

Head Set (Headphones) I bought this Nokia C2-01 new from Amazon, for the few $$$$ more why buy a used one? Anyway the phone came with a Nokia Head Set (headphones), This phone only works well with is own brand the Nokia Head Set that came with it. I have several Head Sets and my favorite Skull Candy Head Set, but they do not work well, they sound awefull, must use the Nokia Head Set !

"Volume Control", are the other people that write these reviews about poor volume control "For Real"......This Nokia C2-01 Earpiece has Excellent Volume and Excellent Volume Control settings. .....Heres what you do....go to Menu, go to Settings, go to Navigation Key and select a short cut for the Volume Control on the Navigation Key (up or down or left-right, you pick). This little phone can get loud and the Media Player there is a different volume control that works well for the Media Player.

This Nokia C2-01 is small, light and sleek, never had a problem with number keys being small for my Man hands, Has USB and Memory Card slots on the side. Head Set and Charging Jack on the top.
Camera works, 3.2 MP for 1536x2048, 2.0MP for 1200x1600, 1.2MP for 960x1280, 0.5MP for 600x800, 0.3MP for 480x640, and 0.1MP for 240x320 this is a phone not a 14.1 MP Sony Cybershot, OK....
Signal is Excellent, I work in a Hospital and never lost signal anywhere in the building. There is a Lanyard Slot on the top left side but you have to open the back cover to string it up and use it (if your into using a lanyard). Battery life is Excellent, charge last a long time. Good choice of ringtones. comes with 4 games Sudoku, City Bloxx, Brain Champ. , and Block'd .
Media player is Great for this small phone, I use a 8GB micro SD memory card , listen to music with headset or speaker, I got a usb cable and the phone sync'd up with NO problem with my hp laptop music , photos, etc..and charges
This is a Nice Simple Little Phone that gets the Job done.

title: If it had properly written instructions, the reviews would be much better!
text:
I thought, what am I missing? Yes, there are no instructions, but many reviewers pointed out a note on Amazon that says to insert the "smallest round Jawbone ring first". So OK, I decided I should give Jabra a try, and I followed the (missing) instruction that's listed as a "Technical Detail". Quoting: "Insert the smallest original Jawbone Ear Bud first followed by the Jabra Ear Gel of your preferred size." So I did what the instruction said.

Most of us think of INSERTING as putting a part inside another part. Unfortunately if you INSERT the small Jawbone ring into the Jabra and then INSERT the Jawbone into the Jabra like the instruction says, the Jawbone doesn't stay attached (just like many of the reviewers described). The first time I took the Jawbone out of my ear, the Jabra earpiece stayed in my ear and I'm holding the Jawbone in my hand. At this point, I'm not a happy camper...

What the tech writer should have said is: INSTALL the SMALLEST Jawbone rubber ring ON the Jawbone, then INSERT the Jawbone into the Jabra Eargel. This actually works (though it's a chore to get the small ring on the Jawbone). But once done the assembly feels like it was properly designed.

So if you threw the Jabra parts in the drawer (instead of throwing them out), give this a try. The aforementioned positive reviews could only have come from users that figured out the "correct" assembly process, by ignoring the instructions... ;-)

title: Great New Update
text:
When I received my Jawbone Era the first thing that I noticed was that like other Jawbones, the product was great, but the earpieces were, well, less than optimal. I looked to Amazon for relief and sure enough found that Jabra made some eargels. THEN I read the reviews. Wouldn't take them as a gift. BUT I noted a few weeks ago that Amazon had a subtle change in their writeup. It noted that the small rubber ring supplied by Jawbone should be placed on the earpiece before the Jabra eargel is put in place. It occurred to me that this might indeed solve the problems that the earlier reviewers had had. So I clinched my teeth and ordered a set. They (six:right/left,small-large)arrived today. I did as instructed by Amazon (oddly the eargels have no instructions for such an important issue). The appropriate eargel fit beautifully, a real blessing in comfort and sound over the standard sets, and, MOST IMPORTANT, the eargel fits the earpiece. No looseness, no turning or drooping or falling out. This is the way it was meant to be. A great product.

Jabra makes a great product, but I do fault them for not giving instructions as to the need to use the small Jawbone ring under it. That is not intuitively obvious. Frankly, it would not have occurred to me. If you already bought this product and haven't thrown them away, put them on as noted and you should be very happy.

I do encourage Jawbone users to get these eargels. They are much more comfortable than the factory ones, stay in your ear better, and sound better in noisy environments.

title: Secure with O-ring!
text:
I really didn't expect these to be any different than the original Jabra Ear Gels (I have two packs of those, one clear, one with color), but they are. They actually have a bit more room inside (the space where the jawbone earbud goes into) than the Jabra originals. So these ear gels would not stay in place with the original rubber cover from jawbone.

I found that the best way to secure them to the Jawbone was with a rubber o-ring in the plumbing dept of your hardware store. I would take both the ear gel and jawbone to the hardware store to find the best match. For me, it was an o-ring with a 3/8" inner diameter and 3/32" thickness. First, remove any and all rubber covers that came with your jawbone, exposing the ridge at the end of the earpiece. Then put the o-ring over the ridge, then put the ear gel over that. (This size o-ring also works with my earlier jabra ear gels.) See my pictures at

bitDOTlySLASHA37sG6

[replace DOT with . and SLASH with / (and don't delete the leading A of A37sG6)]

The second thing to say is that these do have an extra ridge on the ear gel, making them harder to pop off the jawbone. You can see it in the pictures.

Third, although not a major problem, the color of these are just a little orange. Not as clear as the original clear ones from Jabra. I actually suspect that these are knock-offs, but I am happier with them than the original Jabra ear gels I have.

I will likely get a custom ear mold for my jawbone. If you want to read more about that, follow me on twitter (ATklaberte, substituting the AT with the correct character)

**Plantronics Voyager Edge Users**: These can be made to fit your headset easily, greatly improving earpiece retention and volume. I can only vouch for fitting the 'medium' and 'large' Jabra Eargels successfully, not the smallest one. The stock Voyager 'small' earpiece (when modified) fits into/inside the 'medium' Jabra earpiece, the medium stock earpiece fits into the 'large' Jabra ear piece. To get them to fit, the hoop on the stock earpiece needs to be clipped off, leaving the circular soft section intact. The circular section will then fit into the Jabra earpiece snugly with no other modifications needed. Headset will NOT fit in the Voyager portable recharge dock with Jabra earpiece attached, but it removes easily.

title: Should ship with Headset
text:
Hmm, where to start. These things really should ship originally with the headset, they turn a decent headset into a quality one. I guess I'll start with the inherent problems with the standard earpieces.

Stock:
- They are not ear contoured, they are round. No matter what shape your ears I can guarantee they are not perfectly circular.
- The rubber piece that holds the headset in place rests in the back of your ear, so when gravity pulls on the headset it just rotates and falls out.
- The rubber retainer relies on pressure against your ear to hold it in place, and gets very uncomfortable after about an hour.

Jabra:
- Contoured for your ear. These things fit like a hearing aide and are extremely comfortable.
- The rubber piece that the Jabras use to hold the headset in place rests in the front of your ear, resting almost vertically in the front-most vertical canal your ear has. this means when gravity pulls on the headset the piece just (slightly, you can't feel it) pushes on the front of your ear and stays in place. There is no room for rotation.
- No pressure used for retention here, extremely comfortable.

They do make the headset look pretty goofy when it is outside of your ear; adding a ton of mass and being a yellow-y color. Who cares though? That's not what you bought the ERA for. This add-on really makes the ERA worth purchasing, and it is a shame that they don't come with the headset (I understand it's a different company). Would recommend to anyone who has the ERA.

I do feel I should mention that if you are using either of the two bigger sizes you don't use the smallest stock rubber ring, you use the second smallest. With the smallest one the earpiece will rotate incessantly, but it's a perfect fit with the next size up.

title: Better Fit and Volume
text:
Pros:
1. The original Jawbone fit attachments do not seem to stay in my ears well enough. These ear gels improve the fit for me. It is better, but not perfect. Perhaps my ears are odd, since most earbuds do not stay in very well for me.
2. Likely due to better fit, these also increase the volume. They may distort the sound a bit, but certainly do not adversely affect understanding of the person on the other end of the line.
3. Multiple sizes provided to increase chance of good fit.

Cons:
1. The fit on the Jawbone so that the gel does not reduce the sound volume and distort is little finicky, though the gel stays put, if one places it over one of the small jawbone "rings" include with the earpiece. Unfortunately, no instructions are included with the ear gels to let one know this.
2. Positioning the ear gel / jawbone combo so that it fits well in one's ear and the jawbone sensor touches one's face is a bit finicky.
3. Cost is too high, especially after shipping from third party Amazon seller.
4. The ear gel prevents the jawbone from fitting into it's neoprene carrying case.

Bottom Line: I'm still using these. They improve my experience and would recommend, though Cons #1 and #2 prevents this from being higher than 3 stars.

I have measured the fields in each situation, contrary to the BS that you see on the net a wired headset has next to no
field strength near the head. The headsets that use tubes are not necessary and do no better then this one with EMF
exposure. The wires cannot carry the high frequency without great attenuation at the are piece,
I have tested this headset for EMF, it is so low in level that it is actually hard to measure it.
The sound quality of both the microphone and the ear piece are great.
I was really impressed, remember this is my business so I know good quality when I hear it. Don't pay attention to the
poor reviews here, I'm sure it is operator error form my experience.

title: The only one that works for the my applications in a value-minded offering.
text:
Servicable. For under $20, it works great for PS4 and Xbox, with the 1/8" (3.5mm) jack. Mute is hassle, as you need to hold it down, but then again, you won't be muted by accident. The cord is the right length, not too long nor too short. Quality on the headset is solid with more than enough gain. The major issue here is that smaller ear piece does not stay in ear, but loosely hangs without falling out. Pushing it back in does nothing, as the rubber wrap surround does not have malleability. The larger earpiece does work, but it will feel somewhat uncomfortable. Add more gain from the system you are using, and it works fine.

On phone calls for the Android / Samsung S series, the call quality is the worst I have ever heard- at most volume settings. At the lower volume settings, it is great- at most standard volumes, distortion and digital red-lining cause the thing to be unusable. Horrible stuff on something so simple.

For $30 here, today, it is a terrible value. I paid $15 or so here a few months ago. More Chinese garbage at inflated prices. Don't even bother with the brick and mortar retailers that charge up to $40 for this. Are there any other corded units I've found with the right 3.5mm jack and universal L/R fit? No way.. I've searched everywhere, and the market at this price point is again, complete garbage from any and everyone. Blech.

title: Better than decent funtioning, but lacking in refinement and protection.
text:
The sound on the receiving end of calls seems to be good most of the time. The foam mic tip really helps with wind. The headset is pretty light and comfortable, but if the ear piece isn't in just right, it can hurt all at once. The sound quality is pretty good if the ear piece is in right. I have listened to music and watched videos with it. It isn't like my headphones, but I can understand words and hear all of the notes clearly. I like the cable over bluetooth for a lot of reasons, but one is that the call recorder I use for business works with the headset.

Now to the five main down sides. The foam mic cover falls off all of the time, and you only get one. I put a piece of thread through mine. The plastic is brittle and there is no case. I had this in my pocket. I took a gingerly step, and I heard a snap. I now have the boom wrapped classily in scotch tape. Turns out it is four tiny strips of plastic glued around two wires. It still works, and it's still comfortable. A minor issue is the angle on the jack. I realize there is an argument for it, but I find often when I put the phone in a pocket, the jack comes undone just a tiny bit, and the line sounds dead. A straight end is my preference. The last and probably most minor issue is the cord clip (at least it has one!). It is oddly shaped and balanced (very short), so it always flips down pockets and out collars and button strips. Minor, but the solution is so simple...

All in all, it was almost worth what I paid for it. I will likely buy another not because I am so impressed with this headset on its merits, but because for me it is much better than a stereo headset, it is still much nicer than most of the competition in the single ear category, and the price to performance, so to speak, is the best I have found. I just wish they had charged a little more and put that toward a case, a clip, and some reinforcement.

The volume level of this item at max value on my phone is sub par to say the least and even further more, when the value of my phone is on max, there is a popping sound as if the speaker can't handle it. Not only that but hearing outside with any wind (even slight) is next to impossible. Also, immediately, the people I was calling would complain of a hollow sound coming from my end. Now it is entirely possible that I just have a bad unit, but I will not personally even try to get another unit as I am just way to disappointed.

Would I recommend? Absolutely not.

title: Great price, just good enough sound and pick-up, comfortable and good looking
text:
The Jabra Wave Corded Headset looks good and at $9.00 is cheap enough that, if you are somewhat interested, it's worth buying just to check out even if you end up tossing it.

I believe a headset needs to have a comfortable and secure fit, needs to allow me to hear the other person clearly, needs to pick up my voice well and should look good.

Fit is four stars. It took a little messing around with the position of the speaker (hint: pop the speaker tip all the way off and then put back at the position you want, don't simply try to twist) but fit was secure and comfortable. My ears are slightly on the large size and (I think) unusually shaped. Finding a comfortable headset has been hard, so this is a big deal to me.

Sound is three stars. Usable but quality was only OK and volume was low.

Pick-Up is 3 stars. The other party could hear me fine but microphone was far enough from my mouth that my voice came across as what's called "acoustically large." That slightly echo-y, 'bottom of a well' sound you often get, for example, from speaker phones. A common problem with heads and not a horrible but definitely far less good pick-up then you get just holding the phone to your head.

Looks are good - has a nice, space-age, not too big appearance.

Great price, just good enough sound, just good enough pick-up, comfortable and good looking, I think this product is a solid three stars.

title: Great headset, but not for a Samsung smartphone
text:
The Jabra Wave Corded headset is a high-quality headset and a good value. However, this item should NOT be ordered to use on a Samsung S-series smartphone.

The Amazon listing says, "Adapter in pack for compatibility with most phones from Nokia, Sony Ericsson and Samsung". However, there is considerable distortion when used on a Samsung smartphone because of a limitation in the phone itself, making the audio badly garbled.. This was confirmed with Samsung tech support, but they could not provide any solution for the problem by way of a change in settings.

A fairly detailed online engineering explanation at "http://www.jensign.com/S4Distortion/" describes the problem in detail. The Samsung phone's audio output is quite distorted when connected to a headset with an impedance of 12 ohms or less, but works better at 16 ohms and above. The standard earphone provided with the Samsung S-series is around 35 ohms, well above the problem range.

The headset was tested on several tablet computers and a notebook PC and provided good quality and adequate volume, so for devices other than the Samsung S-series smartphone, this could be a good buy.

title: Pretty darn good...best out there, for now and for HTC EVO
text:
Well, when recently I left behind my sturdy little Samsung Rant phone I also left behind a very beloved Plantronics 2.5 mm jack headset. THAT headset was awesome: had an online volume control; was NOT an earbud which seemed much kinder to my ears; easily switched between right and left ear as desired; excellent incoming and outgoing sound quality.

After a few phone upgrade glitches I wound up with an HTC EVO. But do not want to use a Bluetooth headset. Yikes: I have a 2 hour round trip commute made palatable by using the time for quality (safe, handsfree...) phone time. With the new phone suddenly my wired headset options TANKED. Most corded headsets out there are designed to multi-task for both music listening and phone calls; most of these are stereo earbud configuration with an in-line mic at the chest level...a problem because none that I found had any noise reduction properties and that made for crappy call quality - it seems that call quality takes a back seat to most music listening properties. SO......................................................................Continuing my quest for a decent wired headset for a Droid phone: I saw this and based on the other reviews it seemed worthwhile so I got it. Here is my experience to date:

PROS
1) VERY comfortable headset
2) My callers all say the sound quality on their end is the best of anything I have yet tried on the new phone...clear, natural, etc.
3) Online button is geared towards a Droid phone (maybe IPhone too, but I would not know); it works great for Answer/End Call, which is not particularly amazing, but it also has a feature where if you hold it in for a couple seconds it will bring up your Voice Dialing software and it works great for use of that feature.

CONS:
1) For me: I don't like ear buds: not good to have no air circulation in your ear canal as that is part of how the natural biological hearing function works - soundwaves w/circulating air. Based on my experience with other headsets, I would definitley rather have the earpiece sit against the ear canal rather than pressed into it.
2) I have had slightly muffled sound quality from my callers. I think it is particularly true for those who are ON a bluetooth headset; it has not been crystal clear on all my calls at all. Sometimes I have to get them to repeat something they are saying throughout the conversation. No one I have called however has complained about my voice quality.
3) No volume control on the headset: when it is on and I call, the ringer on the other end it LOUD...but then the voice of person I call may not be loud. I have toggled the volume on my fine little phone a lot but it doesn't really fine tune the sound quality on the headpiece (for calls) much at all..only minimally.

So, with this said, all in all, this headset is worthwhile if you want a wired headset for an HTC EVO or other 3.5 MM phone. If even SOME of the things on my CONS list were addressed, this would definitely be a 5* headset.

(NOTE: It comes with a 3.5 MM jack that is designed for HTC and several other brands; interestingly, it also comes with adapters for 2.5 MM phone jacks and, what I found weird, for 3.5MM jack for Samsung phones. Just before HTC I went through 2 Samsung smartphones and amongt the nightmare that was those phones was that I could not even begin to find a headset that would work AT ALL...not sure why Samsung has a different 3.5 MM jack than the 'standard' 3.5 MM jack....)

title: Great Call Quality. Iffy Functionality. Terrible Support.
text:
I've had my eye on this product for quite some time. I really have had hideously bad experiences with wireless headsets and despise having to constantly charge yet another device. I've also had only slightly better luck with most corded headsets as they are often too cheap, lack volume or features.

This one seemed like it might be the perfect "fit" for me.

The shape and feel as excellent. It easily sits on the ear. The ear piece easily sits in the ear at just the right angle and the boom reaches just far enough out to be effective as a boom mike. Furthermore the call quality both outbound and inbound is excellent. Callers hear me with ease and I hear them equally well.

Where the trouble starts is with the single button on the cable. It's supposed to act as a Flash/Hang-up function or, if held for a second, trigger a Voice Dialing response. I bought three of these for use on three different phones and all three do the same thing (iPhone 3, iPhone 4 and a Motorola Droid). The button will answer a call or hang up a current call. However, it will not, on any of the phones, trigger voice dialing. Instead it launches the music app on all 3 phones for no apparent reason.

I contacted support by e-mail after waiting over an hour on hold one day and explained the entire situation and asked for help. What I got back was a broken English response simply regurgitating the user manual to me and not addressing the issue at all.

If this final issue could be fixed this one would be a 4 and if support were reliable it would be a 5-star review. Instead it's stuck at a three. It works but with trade-offs.

title: Calls not clear; drop out.  Disappointed.
text:
In my long struggle to find a nice reliable corded headset, I had high hopes for the Jabra Wave. This was particularly the case after seeing many of the positive reviews for the Jabra Wave bluetooth version; thinking that the corded version would give me the same good results without the fear of draining my phone's battery and potentially getting brain cancer, I purchased it. Yes, I did see many of the negative reviews on here, but I decided to take the chance, hoping people who poorly reviewed this product were just being too particular/demanding, as sometimes reviewers can be.

After 2 weeks of use, however, I can tell you that those who gave poor reviews on the corded Jabra Wave were absolutely correct. This headset does not live up to the job. While sound quality on my end was excellent - perhaps even a little too loud and clear at times -- people whom I called all said the same thing: I did not come across as clear, things sounded too warble-y and distant, my voice would cut in and out. Surprisingly, people preferred when I used a bluetooth headset that I had prior to this one; so, I guess I will be going back to that.

title: The microphone decided to do its job less and less.
text:
I purchased this product because of the reviews stating that it had superior microphone clarity. I quickly became my default earpiece for talking on the phone and dictating notes. Lately (after 3 months of regular use), people started to complain that I was very quiet on the phone. When recording an audio check it seemed to work fine but in retrospect, was in fact quieter. Yesterday I was taking some notes and after reviewing the notes, I found a problem. The first 15 minutes I was coming through loud and clear, then the audio level started to fall and eventually faded into nothing but a faint echo of human voice, then towards the end, nothing. I lost an hour of work but more importantly, I was mystified by this hardware failure. Most often when headphones and microphones fail, it is due to a cable or connection being broken or having a short in it. This failure was not such a failure and instead was a part slowly working less well. The microphone decided to end it's usefulness as a microphone and transition into something less exciting.

The product has a good secure fit and the production quality on the exterior build is good. I won't be repurchasing but will instead be developing something that can meet my needs and hopefully last much longer.

title: Charged with battery
text:
(So sorry. I'll make it up to you by formatting this review in the time-honored pro/con tradition, despite the fact that such dichotomies do a poor job of capturing the nuances of human experience.)

Pro! I bought this dock for the purpose of turning my phone into a bedside alarm clock. It works well to that end, especially once the docking app native to the Samsung Charge is replaced with a (simpler, dimmer, equally free) app from the Play Store (formerly Marketplace). I guess that places me squarely in the "native dock app is too bright" camp, and I'll fight to defend that point of view till death, or till bedtime, whichever comes first. By the way, many of the Play Store apps seem to be called "Night Clock."

Pro! Judging from the reviews of those brave scouts who bought blind and reported back, the dock should come with an extra battery. However, it would seem that some unscrupulous sellers deliver the dock unbatteried, and, presumably, do something unmentionable with the orphaned lithium involving the shady and lucrative power trade. When in doubt, buy directly from Amazon. I can attest that my Amazon-purchased unit did indeed come in original packaging and with extra battery. Woohoo! No need to spend an extra $5 for an extra battery.

Pro? It turns out that I didn't really need the extra battery anyway. The dock sits on my bedside table, which means that I charge the phone when I get home in the evening, and it so happened that for me, docking the phone was more convenient than turning it off, exchanging the batteries, and rebooting. Nor was it appealing to walk around with two batteries. To add insult to injury (or shortcoming to bothersomeness), the presumably-new battery that came with the dock has a significantly shorter usage time than the one that originally came with the phone hundreds of charges ago.

Con? The phone sits snugly in the dock, and it is clear to anyone with an advanced degree in biomedical engineering that phone+case won't fit; ditto for phone+extended battery. Neither is an issue for me, as my phone is unsheathed and unenhanced.

Con. It would have been nice, given said snugness, if the docking/undocking action had been less rickety. The micro-USB plug doesn't always line up with the micro-hole in the side of the phone, and instead bonks against the phone's edge for a couple of approaches before docking is achieved.

Con! The dock's footprint is unnecessarily large. Even if you want that extra battery and a slot to charge it in parallel with the phone, surely you could have fit the lot of them more compactly. Bedside real estate is scarce and precious for me. You might sleep on the endless savanna, in which case you should invite me over sometime; I'll bring an extra battery.

Khan! I have had neither occasion nor desire to plug speakers into the dock and use it as some kind of micro-stereo system. The phone's micro-speaker works just fine to rouse me from my slumber.

In the absence of other Samsung Charge docking alternatives, I'm glad this one exists. What else do you want me to do, tether my phone to a charging cord and lay it flat on my bedside table? What kind of Luddite do you take me for?

title: Absolutely terrible product.
text:
I got this item as soon as it became available. The volume controls on the dock are terrible. When pressing up or down on the volume it is not incremental. Pressing left (volume up) just once results in the volume rocketing to maximum. Pressing right (volume down) just once results in the volume rocketing to silent. I thought I was doing something wrong, how hard could it be to operate a volume control right? I called Samsung and they stated they have had reports of the issue and were working to correct them. The AC adapter that comes with it has less output (just 700ma) than the OEM Samsung AC USB Adapter (1000ma). First off, that is a 30% decrease in output which means that you will be charging the battery in your phone 30% slower than with the OEM Samsung AC USB Adapter that your phone came with, or at least the adapter that most of the Samsung phones came with.

-> Excerpt from Samsung Droid Charge review: I say "most of the Samsung phones came with" because I have heard reports that even the 32gb microSD card speed classes have not been the same. Some reported that their Samsung Droid Charge came with a 32gb Class 2 microSD card (slow speed) while others came with a 32gb Class 4 microSD card (faster speed). Some people speculate that the speed of the microSD card is why sometimes their phones shut off completely when attempting to take a picture. That's not true at all, it just takes longer to save the picture. The phone shuts down completely when using the camera flash. My thoughts on that are that the flash capacitors are drawing too much current, kind of when the lights in your car dim when you start it up.
<- End Excerpt

The inconsistencies are extremely disturbing. Samsung's engineering is severely flawed. I could go on an on. I have an Otterbox case and I was planning on being content with removing it to use the dock, but what a piece of junk.

I returned my dock.

text:

The point is that I based my purchase on the first reviewer who said it came with the battery. Today I went shopping at the Verizon store for a spare battery, and the salesman pushed this dock at me with the battery included in the box. The catch? The retail package at the Verizon store costs the same as the non-discounted price listed here. That's right. The battery itself retails for $39.99. The dock is actually only $10. The seller who is pushing this dock at 17% off is quoting the normal sale price of the unit that comes WITH A SPARE BATTERY INCLUDED. If you were to buy this item from Samsung's store direct with the spare battery included, it would be cheaper than buying this unit and then going to another vendor for a spare battery.

Buyer beware!

You can always just close it and use something different. You can select a bright or dark background, and the phone goes into a very nice dark sleep mode that only displays the time. It has a spot to charge an extra battery behind the phone and a line out on the back so you can connect it to powered speakers or a stereo. It has the volume controls on the front since the ones on the phone are hidden inside the dock.

Note: If you order it directly from Amazon it comes in the original Samsung packaging with an extra 1600mAh battery. It looks like some people have had problems with not getting the extra battery when ordering it from other companies.

Pros:
Great way to use your phone as an alarm clock
Charges the phone and an extra battery while playing music
Very clean and simple design
The power plug for the stand can also be used to charge the phone directly if traveling and you do not want to take the stand.

Cons:
The phone will not fit with a case on it.
No built in speakers
Would have been nice if they had put the phone's HDMI output on the same side as the power so this dock could have been used as a media dock.

title: Very Good

title: Verizon Samsung Droid Charge desktop docking station

title: Battery charger broke

Meantime, even though the return window has closed, I'm going to return the broken item to Amazon and hope they do the right thing and refund my $$. I'll try to remember to follow up with the result.

title: Nice Dock - with Significant Shortcomings...
text:
I don't want to reiterate what others have said as to the cons of this dock - they are all true. It does look good and fits the Charge nicely - as long as you don't mind taking off the protector that is required for the belt holster every time you want to use the dock. I like that it came with a spare battery (I bought it from Verizon at a discount online). Why they didn't allow for a USB connection is beyond me. To copy any files from my PC to the phone I have to remove it from the dock and plug in the USB cable. As someone else said - REALLY DUMB. Access the the HDMI port would have been nice, too. But no. So how can they call it a true multimedia device when it just has a tiny little mini-plug I/O?

My biggest complaint is that when the phone is sitting in this dock it seems to open and close apps at random, sometimes even rebooting the phone for no apparent reason. The amount of activity (screens opening and closing, display turning on and off) is sometimes astounding. I bought a new car with SYNC voice command via the cellphone's Bluetooth connection and could not get the phone to maintain Bluetooth pairing with the car's SYNC - UNTIL I stopped using the dock overnight. Some weird things go on with the phone when docked that do not happen when it's just plugged into the AC adapter provided by Samsung. I haven't had the time to document them, it is just an observation sitting at my desk while the phone is in the dock. It is messing with the Bluetooth settings of the phone to the point that the phone can't seem to remember the car connection. I don't want to have to re-pair the phone with my car every single day so I've had to give up the otherwise neat little desk clock app the dock triggers. No biggy, but disappointing since the dock I had for my Motorola Droid was very functional and did nothing like this one does. So now I have a docking cradle that is only good for charging the spare battery. I guess it might just be my next EBay sale...

title: Does include a spare battery!

title: Do not buy this phone
text: This is a horrible product.  It randomly just stopped working. What a piece of junk.  No warning, nothing. It's a cheap phone, true.  I should have known what I was getting into.

title: Love it.

title: If you value your life.....
text:
The LG 500G phone itself seemed to be okay in the very brief time it was operable. Problem is, you will occasionally need to contact Tracfone. If you value your life, you'll get a phone from another company. A friend recommends T Mobile.

When I first got the phone, I needed to call the company to activate it. For 3 hours I had to enter codes into the phone because it wouldn't work. Based on past experience, I began to suggest the SIM card was faulty, but they wanted to be sure, so I had to continue to enter codes. I was exhausted by the time they realized or acknowledged a faulty SIM card. (They accidentally sent me 2 new ones.)

Today I accidentally locked the phone while trying to add a security code. To unlock it, I have to call the company. Their recording said wait time is approximately 30 minutes. I've now been on hold for almost 2 and 1/2 hours.

While on hold, I tried to register my complaint on their website (after typing a paper for a friend. My, what one can accomplish while on hold with Tracfone! There's no excuse for not writing the great American novel.) They repeatedly blocked my registration for the following reasons: they already have my email address; I then used another email address, which they also already claim to have. Because I'm an existing customer, I'm therefore not allowed to enter a review or join their forum. They also repeatedly said I had mistyped the security/cue word at the bottom of the page. Maybe some of my attempts were inaccurate, as the letters one is supposed to copy are illegible, but clearly some of my attempts were correct. I gave up and came to Amazon to publicize my experience.

A few years ago I called Tracfone for a busy friend whose phone would not function. For over 5 hours I had to enter codes into the phone. Finally, after being routed to every possible department, some guy somewhere realized or acknowledged that the SIM card was defective.

Adding up all the hours I have spent on my land line trying to solve problems with Tracfone, I come to a total so far of over 10 hours. So far. I will have to call again tomorrow and start all over again - waiting on hold and then who knows how long it will take to straighten the problem out? And what work will be required of me?

For some reason, I thought Tracfone had improved their service. I was wrong. My body aches from holding the phone. So, if you value your life, you'll buy a phone from another company. It would be nice to have a working cell phone, but life is short. With Tracfone, it can get even shorter. I'm going to hang up now.

title: Phone died with 7 days of first use. I ...
text: Phone died with 7 days of first use.  I will get a refund when I return it at my cost.  When I originally opened the package, the tracfone calendar was for 2011.  Beware when buying a tracfone online.  No way to make sure it's a current phone.

title: For what it is, its great
text:
I have had this phone for 11 months. If you are not a heavy phone user, or send 100's of texts a day, you should look into this phone, or Tracfone generally.
I send a couple texts now & then, and a few calls. With the Double Minutes for life, I pay $30 every 2 or 3 months. If you are looking for a smart phone, this isn't it. If you plan to surf the web with your phone, you need a different phone and a different type of plan. Although, it is possible to set up email apps if you are technically saavy. I can check my gmail and yahoo mail, but most people probably won't be able to figure it out. The "G" in 500G means its a GSM phone. If you can get Tmobile or ATT in your area, it should work fine. If you live in a rural area, it might not. One of the best features about this phone, I only charge it once a week! I'm upgrading to a smart phone soon, but I'll keep my LG500G as a backup, and as an MP3 player in my desk at work. I am also buying a Tracfone for my elderly parents. They're currently paying $90 a month for what they get on a contract. I've crunched the #'s and based on their usage, they will pay $20 or less a month on average with a Tracfone. title: Good cheap phone with only one flaw
text:
I have this phone and only use it for phoning and texting. I often don't use my cellphones much, so this was a nice option. It serves its purpose at a low price.

The one bad thing about this phone, as someone else mentioned, is its ability to start surfing the web on its own. I've had situations where the phone was either off or key locked in my pocket, and would suddenly hear it making noises. It seems the buttons for turning the phone on or unlocking it stick out rather too prominently, allowing it to turn on and suddenly waste minutes surfing the web. (Wasted several phone minutes this way.)

Other than that, its a nice no-frills phone for basic needs. I would have probably given it 5 stars if not for the annoying habit of it surfing on its own.

title: Very good for an ultra-low-cost phone
text:
I've had Tracfones for almost ten years, and this is definitely the best. Hardware-wise, the phone is solid. Sound quality is decent. Size and interface are fine. Keyboard is surprisingly good. Camera is serviceable for simple MMS snaps. MP3 player is crude, but works OK (requires a MicroSD memory card). Web browser is absolutely useless. Other features are so-so. There are very few decent Java Apps or games available, but if you're resourceful, you can find a handful online worth downloading.

But remember: all this comes in a phone that retails for less than twenty bucks and offers a year of service for about a hundred dollars. That's eight bucks a month. Just try to beat that.

But adjust your expectations accordingly. Tracfone's service is a bit spotty nationwide. I live in the NYC metro area, so I have no trouble -- but I've had some difficulty in other regions. Also, if you're looking for a "real" smartphone with viable web and e-mail access, this ain't it. This calls. This texts. And if you don't do too much of either, lets you do so very cheaply and reliably. I buy about 800 minutes per year for $99, and use less than half of them. As long you re-up before the end of the term, it lets you roll over unused minutes.

This is, without question, the best low-cost mobile phone currently available. (Summer 2012)

-- mattmchugh

title: Bargain MP3 player & Texting phone, poor camera

title: Love this Tracfone!
text: So glad I got this Tracfone.  So easy to use and never have a problem with it.  Sure beats paying one of those big companies tons of money every month!

title: So far, so good
text:
I read online reviews and looked at one in the store before I bought this phone. It is actually the first Tracfone I have bought that I was excited about! I have had a Tracfone for years, and it is now my "back-up" cell phone. I really didn't feel that I needed a smartphone with this but I wanted to be able to text more easily and have the possibility of web access not that I use it much. The phone was no surprise then after researching it, and I didn't expect a smartphone or even semi. That's not what this phone is.

But I like the more modern look and also that it is not branded Tracfone on the outside (I usually turn off the automatic screen display of minutes anyway). It was easy to install the battery and get it charging. Then I was pleasantly surprised that customer service had my number and service transferred so easily. This was the best experience I have had with them on the phone! My reception seems good, and testing works fine. I have not put a microSD card in yet, but I will update if I have any problems with that. The keyboard is small but is is nicely responsive for me and my smallish hands. Accessing the menu to change wallpaper, settings, and enter contacts was simple and for me intuitive. The keypad lock and unlock is different than what I am used to, but after a couple of times I like the way it works--you press a specific key to lock than you have to press first unlock than immediately press yes to unlock. This seems like it will prevent accidental unlocking.

So far, I have not found anything that I don't like about this phone. Just be make sure you know what it is, not a smartphone nor a touchscreen, and that the keypad is small. As with other Tracfones, the so-called user manual is scanty on details so you may need to look up additional information. It takes my standard 3.5 headphones although the jack is sort of at an angle. For the price, it is a great phone and I'm very glad I updated my Tracfone to this model.

title: Really nice!
text: While this is not the best phone out there, i am a tracfone customer, and it is one of the newer phones they are offering. I am very happy with the phone, as i did not have the capability to text on my last phone. And you get double minutes for life. Definitely a bargain!! Now if only Tracfone would offer the I-Phone, i'd be in heaven!!

title: Garbage phone

title: Great phone for the money
text: Got one of these phones for myself and one for my husband. Just got out of ATT contract and trying to save money. For the price, this phone can't be beat. I ported my old cell phone number to it (do this before you cancel your old phone!!) without any trouble and it works great. My only qualms with it are that the #0 is next to the 9, not below the 8.
