title: Great phone for the price but pay attention to the accessories.
text:
First, I am amazed at the number of features that can now be squeezed into a $12 camera phone. The very idea of a $12 camera phone is actually pretty amazing to someone who's been watching technology advance for the past 30 years or so. I can even say that as someone who's been using an HTC EVO 4G for the last 2 years. Now, my contract for the EVO is about to expire and I'm tired of the huge cell phone bill every month so I'm looking at going back to basics. I figured $20 for a phone and a double minutes card was a reasonable experiment.

This phone is pretty impressive for a basic pre-paid phone. There's a little bit of a learning curve to the menu system, even for a software specialist like myself but the phone comes with a manual so that should help. Once you dig around, you'll find that it has a nice list of tools available for a small phone:

Alarm Clock
Calendar
To-Do List
Notes (normal and secret notes)
Calculator
Stopwatch
Unit Conversions
World Time
MP3 player
Contacts List
eMail
Web Browser
Games
1.3 MP camera
Video camera
etc...

None of these applications are earth shaking and you wouldn't expect them to be for this price but they are there. The camera and the video are adequate for taking basic images and have some surprising settings for image manipulation.

Activation was simple and quick through the TracFone site and I saw where there is the option to move existing numbers to the phone, either from TracFone or other companies. Again, the menu system takes some learning and I'll look for awhile before going to the documentation so I had to search for a bit to find the voice mail number but I did find it, called in and the prompts to setup the mailbox were pretty easy to follow.

At this point, I've had the camera for about a day, tested the reception at home between the TracFone and my EVO and found it to be good. I also bought a 120 minute card and added it to the phone. So far, I'm happy. Having said that, I'll say this:

BE SURE TO ORDER THE ACCESSORIES YOU NEED WITH THE PHONE.

This phone comes with the activation card, a coupon book for bonus minutes, the battery and a charging cord that runs from the mini-USB port on the phone to an AC outlet. It does NOT come with a few other things you'll probably need. If you look at other phones, keep these things in mind:

MICRO SD MEMORY CARD - The LG 500g uses a Micro SD storage card for storing pictures, MP3s and anything else that won't fit into the 170 KB or so of memory in the phone. Be aware that the phone WILL NOT RECOGNIZE anything over a 4 GB card. These 4 GB cards are becoming harder to find in the stores and, when you do find them, they are unreasonably expensive. I went to five different stores and finally found them for anywhere from $17 to $29 a piece. This is odd since the 8 GB cards go for as little as $6. Amazon has the 4 GB cards for $5 each so it's best to order one with the phone. [[ASIN:B000SMVQK8 Sandisk 4GB MicroSDHC Memory Card with SD Adapter (BULK Packaging)]]. Another option would be to get another LG phone that holds the 8 GB cards and larger cards.

PHONE TO PC CABLE - The charger for the phone plugs into the micro-USB port on the side of the phone and then into an AC outlet. This USB port is the same one used on a number of other phones and the Kindle. Those devices often include a charging cord that runs from the device to a PC so you might already have a phone to PC cord that you can use. If not, you will need one if you want to transfer MP3s or other data between your computer and the Micro SD card in the phone. These cables can be around $20 in the stores. It's about half the price here. [[ASIN:B006BGZJJ4 Amazon Kindle Micro USB Cable, White (Works with Kindle Fire, Touch, Keyboard, DX, and Kindle) - Updated Design]]

MINUTES - The phone comes with 20 minutes / 60 days of air time. You'll use up at least half of those minutes setting up your voice mail and trying it out. The additional minutes cost the same no matter where you get them but it wouldn't hurt to order a card with an extra 120 minutes or so to start out. [[ASIN:B003D7CXXY Tracfone 120-Minute Airtime Card]]

I'm especially happy with the coupon book with all the bonus minutes and I'm hoping this turns out to be a good solution to cutting down my phone bill every month. The more I think about it, the dumber I feel for signing the 2 year contract on the EVO. Feature hypnosis can be expensive.

title: Great Price - Buyer Beware
text:
First, I'd like to say that I am not a huge cell-phone user. I have an Ooma (bought here on Amazon) for my home service, which is great - haven't paid a land-line phone bill since 2010. I do not spend that much time on the road - as I am not in a sales or on-site service profession. With this, I've kept a low-cost, pay-as-you-go cell-phone for many years. I use a cell-phone for emergencies, when the power/internet is out at home, and for when I am out of the house and am expecting to make or receive an important call.

For the first several years, I used Virgin Wireless - which was great until last year when my kids lost the phone. Starting a new plan with a new phone with Virgin became a much more expensive proposition - it felt a little like a "bait-and-switch/the drugs are free for the first year" scheme. I guess the bean-counters working for Richard Branson decided that being a low-cost provider just wasn't profitable enough: They got a jealous taste for all the "sheeple" who blindly sign up for the $60-$100/month plans that have transformed Verizon into a money-consuming Jabba-the-Hut. (Honestly, how many people REALLY need $1000+/year phone service - what a bunch of lemmings...!)

Ergo, I checked into my local Wally World (walmart) and found this awesomely cheap phone with a perfectly-priced plan for my needs. So, here's the good, the bad, the ugly:

The Good
Price-price-price - 10 bucks up front, $23 every 3 months. This gets you 100 minutes for that entire time, but I've never used up my minutes. That said, if you were to use more minutes, you can get an even cheaper rate (cents/minute-wise) by buying your minutes in bulk. Reception is nothing special, but it's not terrible either.

The Bad
Let's face it - this is what is now known as a "FEATURE PHONE" (aka "NOT a Smart Phone", aka "Old People's Phone", aka "Dork-Phone"). Released in 2004, it screams "I am so-behind-the-times/this is the same phone my parents use" to anyone who knows gadgets. If you're a "too cool for school" kind of person, this phone is not for you. If you still have a tube-based, non-flat screen TV in your living room, then step right up!

The Ugly
Even at this price, I am flabbergasted - you CANNOT LOCK this phone to deactivate the keys while you are traveling. As such, if you want to receive calls while you have it in your pocket/purse/gym bag/etc, it has to be ACTIVE the entire time. And with that, expect it to make unwanted phone-calls, web-browsing sessions, and text messages whenever the phone touches anything. You will get charged for these erroneous "butt dials", but there is nothing you can do about it. Except turn the phone off - and miss all incoming phone calls while you are on the move (which defeats 50% of the whole purpose for having a cell phone!).

Conclusion - great price, old-school look and features, and a horrible-design FAIL on the ability to prevent "butt-dialing". If you own this phone, you WILL accidentally call, text, or browse.

Caveat Emptor "Buyer Beware"

title: Overall a good phone and a good deal, but ...
text:
For a prepaid phone, this one does most things very well. Tracfone has good coverage in my area, and the call quality is very good. It fits my hand well, and the smallish keys are pretty easy for me to use. The camera is a convenience, it takes adequate pictures in decent light but it's no substitute for a real camera. The bluetooth works well and is a nice surprise at this price (I paid $9.99 with double minutes for life). It's not a true smartphone, but it's 'smart enough', and for ten bucks you get more than you pay for, IMHO. People that expect it to be an iPhone are clueless dreamers.

The issues with the browser button are well-documented and legitimate, but if you're careful you can avoid it for the most part. And it costs a half-minute per activation, not a half-dollar as someone said. HOWEVER, the music player was designed by a moron. It takes a 4Gb micro SDHC card, which is nice, but no matter what I do, this phone will not and cannot play an album through without interruption - it plays a song, then stops until you manually select the next song. Making a playlist with the phone has no effect. The only continuous play it has comes when you 'shuffle' a folder of songs. This is a spectacular failure and only an idiot would design software with this kind of an obvious flaw. I only hope the person responsible for this will someday feel suitably embarassed by his or her inadequacies - it's simply the WORST feature of this otherwise fine product.

I should also mention that, while Tracfone's coverage may be good, their support forum is most definitely NOT. They only respond to issues in private message, meaning that anyone else experiencing similar problems cannot search for a solution that worked for others. What is up with that? What are they trying to hide, and why? They will also force you to post 5 times in said forum before you will even be ABLE to read a pm, which seems like needless jerking around, since that's the only way you can get any help. It's like they went out of their way to be ignorant. Another in a long line of 'Customer Support' departments that are little or no help. Very few companies are even adequate in this area, let alone good. Fortunately, they did manage to transfer my number, ex date and minutes from my old phone with no issues, and it was quick.

Overall, I'm satisfied with the phone, it's nice to have some extra features, and it's hard to beat for the money. I didn't feel it was worth the extra to go to a full touchscreen like the 800, which seems to have some issues of its' own.

My significant other travels overseas quite a bit, and I use this phone to text and chat with him on his ATT phone while he's abroad. The charges for these international calls are no more than they would be for any call made here in the states. The sound quality for these overseas calls is great (except for the random clicking on the calls to/from China..maybe someone is eavesdropping??)

text:
No one buys a prepaid phone to use as their primary phone--it is for occasional calling. That said, I have probably used up more of my paid minutes from this phone connecting to the internet (a feature I don't even want or use) than from calls. Every so often, when checking for texts or something, I'll inadvertently hit a button and it is connecting to the internet: I know it's there and that I don't want to hit it, but it doubles as the "back" button, and it happens time and again.

I used to think it was just bad design--I'm pretty sure LG could have put the "connect to the internet" button in a different place or made it a two-step process-- but as the months have gone by and minutes go down the drain I believe more and more that Tracfone could come up with a way to disable it, or stop the internet connection from deducting minutes immediately when the button's pushed, but they don't want to. Tech forums explain that the only way to avoid this is to keep the phone on some page other than its home page and to keep it in sleep mode all the time, which really changes the LG500G from a high tech device to a crappy kid's toy.

The phone works okay--it makes calls, receives calls, all that you would expect it to do--but this slow constant leakage of my minutes seems intentionally hostile on Tracfone's part.

title: Good Phone
text:
I bought my LG500G today at Walgreens for $29.99. I wanted to upgrade from my LG420G flip-phone. The 500G does have some better features, but it is basically the same as the 420G.

I activated by phone and it took an entire hour from the time I called until the phone activated and assigned a telephone number. But, it did go through without any problems.

The 500G QWERTY keypad is an upgrade from the 420G. It makes texting a LOT quicker. The 500G screen is a little larger than the 420G. Also, the 500G has a video camera while the 420G has only a still camera. The 500G is longer than the 420G when the 420G is closed up and the 420G is thicker than the 500G when the 420G is closed up.

The email and Internet capabilities seem about equal on the 2 phones. The menu seems to be the same. Like the 420G, the 500G has only one ringtone unless you buy more.

I had only had the 500G activated for about 10 minutes when I lost my first .5 minute due to accidentally hitting the browser button. As many other reviewers have said, that seems to be a big problem with the 500G. The 500G keypad is small but that has not been a problem so far.

I don't text much, so I will continue to use my 420G as my main "carry phone" and use the 500G as a backup. The more compact size of the 420G makes it much easier to carry and there are no worries about accidentally turning on the browser, as other reviewers have mentioned.

If you text quite a bit, the 500G is the phone for you. However, if you don't text much, I think the 420G is the better buy. Also, when I got the 500G at Walgreens today, I noticed they had the 420G on sale for only $9.99. That is really a good buy for the money.

text:
When considering buying a Tracphone, remember, you are dealing with both phone quality and service quality. While my phone is adequate, experience convinces me it may be Tracphone has gone well out of its way to prove the title of this review factual.

A recent purchase of additional air time (not minutes, those are a separate charge) failed to ever appear on my phone. I tolerated this because the phone did continue to work. Unfortunately, this resulted in time running out without warning. Problematic, at the best.

Trying to buy time with a different card than the one Tracphone kept information on was an effort in futility. First, changing profile information was only marginally better. For example, my old address nowhere shows up on my profile information, UNTIL I attempt to make a purchase. All efforts to correct the erroneous address seem more purposed to frustrate than anything else. Tracphone's means of resolving the problem is to send you off to forums, rather than provide an agent from which to purchase time or minutes - not marketing genius at its best, to be sure.

I found changing the card information could, reasonably, give the impression Tracphone had no interest in making sales. Attempting to use other than the ancient credit card stored on the Tracphone site sends one off on an endless loop. In the end, I yet have a worthless phone with hundreds of dollars in minutes of talk time. The problem may yet be solved, but I am wondering if I need to make a career of it, or go to school for a degree in Tracphone quirks. I suspect I may be out of luck on the latter.

Perhaps Tracphone hired incompetent programmers to build its web sites. Alternately, Tracphone may do this intentionally to coerce customers into abandoning their old phones [and, maybe, even minutes]. If the latter, that may also explain what Tracphone did with my credit card information and why I found unauthorized charge attempts. Too, perhaps accessing the Tracphone site via another browser would have better results, however, my tolerance for companies attempting to control which programs I install on my computer are less than limited.

Obviously, I can only speculate on the honesty of Tracphone, but, meanwhile, I can enjoy the fact I can warn others of some of the pitfalls of doing business with Tracphone.

The "pro" side of Tracphone is, if and when you can get yours working, they provide "on the road" service for emergencies and so forth. As for me, I'm still waiting.

title: Rural problems
text: I thought it would be nice to upgrade to a phone that can take videos. I had an LG501C and kept wishing I could take videos as well as stills. So I spent a few bucks to buy an LG500G. It worked well although the ports seemed a bit more flimsy than those on the 501. However, the reception was generally 2 bars less than the 501 and sometimes completely disappeared. I called Tracfone and after going through 3 levels of help, finally got a reason. I was told that phones with a SIM card can not use the same cell towers (Verizon) as those without a SIM card. The person recommended that I get a phone without a card. After some searching, she told me that the 501 was the only such phone that would work in my rural area. So I had my phone switched back to the 501 and enjoy very strong signals. I guess the only way I am going to get a video phone is to switch to a non-Tracfone system. I refuse to do this because of the considerable difference in cost. So I will put up with no video but a strong signal. I would rate the 500 as a 4 but the reception for me as a 2 so for the purpose of this review, I'll give an overall rating of 3.

title: I'm pleased with this phone
text: Last week I dropped my LG 420G in water and permanently lost the display. I had considered replacing it with another of the same until I found this LG 500G and at a great price. title: Not what I was expecting.
text: The product got here on time, but my idea was to bring it to a third world country and be able to use it. Turns out we were not able to activate the phone and it was a waste of money. I'm sure around this area could be useful.

title: It's perfect for writing texts
text:
Been using this phone for about 3 years already. It's perfect for writing texts, I like the full keyboard. I get decent reception in my area and it works inside the store where I work where a lot of people complain about no service.

The internet feature is terrible. It's so slow that my minutes get used up just waiting for pages to load. I have been able to get on Facebook using this phone but it's so slow and hard to read that it's not worth it and I just wait until I get home to use the internet. Often times the Browser key gets hit on accident and it wastes my airtime unless I can hit the end key in one tenth of a second.

Another stupid thing is how much airtime gets wasted when people send photos to me in text, or include me in group texting. Half a minute just to begin "retrieving" and another full minute for opening the text. Plus a bonus .50 minute gets spent for some reason I haven't deduced yet. This wasn't really an issue before people could use the group text thing but no one with a smart phone realizes how wasteful it is for me when they send those messages, and it's unreasonable for me to ask them not to include me.

The camera is just as awful as the browser.

If you just want a phone that can send messages to a few people and make emergency calls, this phone is cheap and reliable. The keyboard and the screen are robust and I don't have to worry about breaking it. Over the course of riding in my apron at work for 3 years it has taken very little damage. It's been my trusty little sidekick for a long time but I'm ready to upgrade.

title: Great 2nd Phone!
text: I purchased this phone as a simple backup to my smartphone. My region of usage is more rural and believe it or not, this phone handles calls and texting more reliably than my other higher priced one. This phone has a web browser that is quite primitive for today's standards and it's not a feature I would ever use, given my access to other devices. But as a straight phone, it's perfect. I like the layout of the features which include a usable calendar and mp3 player. The LG 500G has a solid feel and the qwerty keyboard is easy to use. The double minutes is a sweet feature and it feels good to have a back up device that was not only cheap to purchase but cost effective to maintain. For what I"m using it for, it does the job. Recommend as a second phone or as a phone for a family member who doesn't need costly upgrades or complicated tech.

title: Very nice, with a few minor points...
text:
My wife has a touch screen pay-as-you-go phone and she doesn't like it. Let's face it...good touch screens are going to cost a little more. I played it safe when I chose mine, and I'm glad I did. The LG500G is a very good bargain for what you pay.

Audio quality is good, even through the speakerphone. I put a 4GB microSD card in it, but as yet, have not tried to use it as an MP3 player. EDIT: Works great as an MP3 player, displaying all ID3 tags and album cover art, if it is included in the original file. Shuffles and lets you create playlists. Audio quality seems to be pretty good. Plug it into an FM transmitter, and you can use it through your car's audio system. Best part: it also works "hands free" like this, allowing you to hear your phone conversation through the car stereo. Cool!

Shoots 3GP video. Quality is not great, but it is better than not having a video recorder. Likewise with the camera. You can take pictures with it, but don't expect miracles. Utilitarian is the best word to describe it. If you have the software to convert videos to 3GP, you can actually UPLOAD your own videos to the phone to watch later. I found this one: Mobile Media Converter from Miksoft. Google it. Free, works on all platforms. Anything you can convert to 3GP with that program seems to work on this phone. A 22 minute video is about 25 mb, so you can estimate your video size as "1mb per minute" and get pretty close.

Don't plan on stopping, resuming, fast forwarding or rewinding, though. EDIT: Holding down the left and right directional pad will seek video. The longer you hold, the faster it goes. It doesn't seek visually, rather, it freezes the last frame and shows the TIME at the bottom. Better than nothing, though, and means you can at least fast forward to where you left off so you can resume videos.

Get yourself a data cord to hook it to your computer, otherwise, you'll go insane taking the back off and pulling the battery out to get to the microSD card. Once you get a memory card, the phone acts much like a USB jump drive, although Ubuntu recognizes it as a mobile media player.

Since I've started playing around with it, I've found that the Opera browser is compatible with this phone. I tried several...1.X seems to be a bit primitive. 6.X is slick and polished, but will frequently crash due to out of memory errors. Opera Mini 4.3 seems to be a good compromise...it seems to work nicely all around. It does eat minutes rather quickly, so make sure you SAVE your frequently visited sites as much as possible to avoid having to search for them and incur extra minutes charges. Google Maps also works on it, but if you use the satellite view, it's not long before you run out of memory and the app crashes. Map view seems to work OK, though.

Typing is much easier than what I thought it would be. I am a giant man with giant hands and I can type comfortably, if not speedily. One issue that I have, and perhaps someone can help me find an answer, is that when I try to type some double letters, I get symbols instead. For example, when I type double "E's", I get a Euro symbol. If anyone knows of a way to turn this off, I'd be grateful! Otherwise, typing is not a difficult chore at all. I love the positive clicks of the keypad SO much better than a touchscreen.

After a well over a month, I'm still happy with the phone, which is something, considering I've NEVER been happy with a phone. Now, to peddle the wife's phone on eBay and get a second LG500G for her.

EDIT 6/21/12: After nine months with the phone, I'm still as happy with it as the day I bought it. Works reliably and has enough features that it can get you out of a jam...for example, I used the Mobile Web and a Google Maps app I installed to locate a destination on a street that was NOT listed on my car's GPS. This got me close enough to find what I was looking for.

Durability seems good. Mine's been dropped several times, a couple of times on pavement. The back popped off and the battery, back, and phone all went skidding across a parking lot in all directions. Picked it up, put it back together, and it worked fine, even if it was a little scratched up after that.

Can check my Gmail using the Opera browser, too. That's handy.

If you're the type who needs a phone primarily with occasional texting and web browsing, it's hard to beat Tracfone and the LG500G. If you're the type who needs a mobile web browser/texting machine that also functions as a phone, I'd look elsewhere.

Again, long term, I've been very happy with this phone. Since the price has come down in the intervening months, I'm tempted to get another one and keep it on hand to replace this one when it finally quits working.

EDIT 11/24/12 - I just ordered the LG500G's replacement. The ol' 500 has worked almost flawlessly from day one, and it packs a lot of punch for the money. But, pre-paid phone technology has progressed by leaps and bounds since I got this one a year and a half ago, so it's time to move on. I don't even know if I'll offer it for sale, as this phone new is now selling for just over ten dollars on Amazon, and is ubiquitous enough to be found for cheap on dollar store shelves. I'd still recommend this phone for anyone wanting a basic phone with a few nice features with a full keyboard and in a compact package.

The best endorsement I can think of is that I am buying another LG.

title: The Tracfone of the Century. Not.
text:
This phone isn't worth the time to manufacture, sell, and then have you buy. I was so happy when I got a new phone, I took a hammer and smashed this one. No joke. It now sits in the bottom of a watering can.

Pros-

You can lock the keyboard. This way, you won't be calling people randomly, and you won't be hitting the browser button and waste minutes.

The full QWERTY keyboard makes you more fluent on a normal keyboard.

Cons-

Once you're inbox/outbox reached 200 messages, you won't be able to receive or send anything. Also, it doesn't tell you which one needs clean. It just says it's 90-100% full.

There is no delete all button. That ticked me off the most. Unless you have an unread message, you have to delete all messages by hand. And in the outbox, you can't get an unread message, so if you're 200+ messages, you sit there for about 60 minutes cleaning out the outbox. Another 60 if you don't have an unread message.

It is really slow. If you hit browser on accident, you are stuck there for a few minutes until it fully loads. Also, if anything else is loading, it takes FOREVER.

The keys are a bit small, so if you have bigger fingers, they are really hard to click without hitting all the ones around it.

You could only have so many pictures. That's true with most phones, but this was ridiculous. I took about 15 when i got it, then I couldn't take anymore. I would delete some, try again, but I still had too many pictures.

If I could, it'd have 0 out of 5 stars.

text: This phone is great for the price. The only negative thing about this phone is where the browser button is. To fix this problem i locked the keys so i didnt accidentally go online and waste all my minutes.

title: What an improvement over the first Tracfone I had!
text:
After a decade of using cell phones with monthly charges, limitations, and spotty reception, I decided to forgo mobile voice communication. That lasted about one year until I heard about Tracfone, which seemed too good to be true. The original phone at Radio Shack was only $10 and it came with a nice accessory pack. The $10/month plan eliminated having to manually add minutes, unless I needed more (which I never have). The only issue was that the Samsung phone would rarely work without dropouts, speech cutoffs and digital delays. Reminded me of many cell phones I'd used in the past.

Then, I noticed that Tracfone offered the LG500 with greatly expanded capabilities for only $20 (with free overnight delivery and also a free accessory pack). Trackfone also allows keep your current number as well as the minutes and days from your current phone when you upgrade, and that was a big deal for me (had over 1500 minutes piled up). When the phone arrived, I went through a rather time consuming process with the Trackfone representative to convert the minutes/days, but it went well.

There are many features on this phone that you'll want to research, and I'd suggest you look for demos on You Tube. I just want everyone to know that the phone works absolutely better than ANY cell phone I've previously owned. No dropouts, no voice delays or digital distortion. My neighbor said I sounded better on this phone than on our land line. Plus, we both could talk at the same time without cancelling out each other.

For quality of service alone, this phone is well worth the initial and ongoing costs.

title: Mediocre Phone; not very text friendly
text:
For a phone that has a full keyboard, you'd expect the features to be more text friendly. The texts work in the very old fashioned way, coming in individually even when they're from one sender. It's much like one of the very old cell phones, but with a full keyboard.

Additionally, I haven't been able to remove the battery cover. It seems impossible to remove it without breaking it or pulling with force.

My experience with this phone: frustrating.

Edit: I've given up my Tracfone phone after a very unsatisfactory experience. My primary problems were the following:

1. I constantly got spam text messages, and as this was a prepaid phone I paid for every one of them. I spoke to Tracfone several times but they were unable to stop the spam, even after they placed me on the no-spam list. Apparently prior users of this phone number had signed up for many texts, and there was no way for me to unsubscribe except individually and by paying for the correspondence. I could not see if a text was personal or promotional until I opened it and paid for it.
2. The phone interfered with other phone lines and caused static or loud beeps if kept around while on a landline. I had to keep it far away from any landline.
3. It was hard to refill the phone card. I had to look up the Tracfone info on the internet; there was no convenient single button to refill it. This sounds minor, but it actually meant I was sometimes left without the prepaid service, and as I use this as an emergency contact phone, it was a big flaw. I could not use any service to look up the Tracfone info once the phone was out of minutes.
4. It was very easy to mistakenly press the web button and be charged .50 minutes. This happened all the time.
5. The device itself was clumsy and the keyboard very uncomfortable.

title: A brick and a very good, little phone.
text:
I just upgraded from this phone to the Samsung S390G because that one offers the triple minutes. But I have enjoyed the LG500G and would have continued using it if it could have been converted to the triple minutes for life. I learned to text on this phone. I liked the keyboard, once I learned to use it and figured out what the symbols meant. Yes, the browser button gets pushed 'way too easily, and I lost my share of minutes because of that. Also, many of my text messages failed. Again, a waste of minutes. I thought that was normal until I got the Samsung. Every one of my messages has gone through easily. Other than these two problems, the phone worked very well for me. And I must praise the construction. The thing is a brick. It slipped out of my pocket several times and fell so hard the back popped off and the battery fell out. I just snapped everything back into place and the phone kept working. Try that with an Iphone.

I agree with the person who complained about not being able to see who messages are from. There are plenty I would not have accepted. But this is the case on my Samsung as well. So I can't blame the phone for this annoyance. My Samsung is more sophisticated than the LG, but I still would recommend this phone. I found it comfortable to carry and use and, for the price, how can you beat it?

title: Works great
text: The phone came in it's original packaging, no marks, no previous use. Works like a charm even on low battery.

title: Lost $100 after LG 500G  was inactivated
text:
This was a great, simple, no frills phone before it was inactivated due to an expired service date. Tracfone sent a free replacement SIM. I bought a card for 1 year service and 400 minutes ($100). Replacing the SIM resulted in the message "Unregistered SIM". Multiple attempts to reprogram the LG 500G via Tracfone customer service were futile. I bought another Tracfone because Tracfone customer service declared the LG 500G dead, i.e unable to be registered on the cell phone network. and I was reassured that I could transfer the 1 year service and 400 minutes ($100) to the new Tracfone. The online transfer and interaction with 2 customer service representatives from Tracfone resulted in a LOSS of the 1 year service and 400 minutes ($100). I am sure there is some clause in Tracfone's terms of service that does not allow a refund. Be aware, that once the LG 500G is out of warranty and not able to be programmed to connect to the cell network, it becomes a paperweight. This is truly a disposable cellphone, especially in the context of the current advances in cell phone technology.
Conclusion: Tracfones are disposable phones. Trash when dead. Tracfone customer service is MOST unsatisfactory.

title: Good phone for the price
text:
This is a pretty basic phone, but definitely worth the price. I love the battery life. I've found that it will last a week of inactive time. I don't use a cell much and I love that though I've forgotten to turn it off while not in use, it still has full battery when I need it.
The biggest con is that I can't figure out how to change the menu buttons on the main screen, and I'm pretty sure you can't. I don't ever use my browser, but accidentally hit the button constantly and get charged for internet use. If I could re-arrange those keys, I would love this phone.

title: LG 500G Qwerty Phone is a good buy.
text: After losing my other Motorola EX124 smartphone in SF, I decided to go cheap incase I eventually lost this one too!  $19 from the Tracfone site + a few dollars for shipping.  The phone seems solidly built, and the battery life is great.  Features are fairly basic - if you're looking for bells and whistles, you're not going to find much here.  Call quality is great, and in the SF bay area I have no issues with dropped calls.  I'd suggest getting a cheap micro SD card if you plan on using it to store photos or MP3 music files.  It's actually a decent MP3 player if you plug in a set of earphones. The QWERTY keyboard is much easier than using the standard keys to type - I think it's even easier to use than my old phone's touch screen keyboard.  I like it, and I think it's a good buy for the price.

I bought this phone 1 year ago at Walmart. I was upgrading from a Samsung U350 (Verizon Prepaid). I was not expecting much, at the time it was only $30. Design is cheap, but what do you expect from an inexpensive feature phone. Navigating the OS (Besides being a horrible one) is slow. title: OK phones, but TERRIBLE customer service!
text:
I've been satisfied with the *PHONE* that I received from Tracfone. My real issue is with their SERVICE. Everything was fine for several months, until some time I had purchased did not get credited to my account. I then discovered Tracfone's incredibly awful customer service. I've now spent more than an hour on the phone (losing more phone minutes, of course) trying to resolve the issue with their call center people (obviously located somewhere in the Philippines) and as of today I have yet to receive the airtime I was promised. After my last (33-minute) conversation with a so-called customer service rep, I was told to CALL BACK (are you kidding me?) on another phone (that is, on a phone other than my Tracfone) so that they could run some kind of check. I think they're all working from a script that's designed to wear down the customer's resistance so they'll just give up. If I were shopping again for prepaid cellular service, I would NOT go with Tracfone - it's just not worth the aggravation you'll encounter if you have a problem with your service.
-
UPDATE: I've added a star to my review (from one to two stars) and added this note because I was ultimately able to resolve the problem I was having with Tracfone's customer service, and I did receive all the air time I had coming (actually, I ended up receiving a little more than expected). Dealing with Tracfone's customer service was a very frustrating experience, but other than that one isolated incident the phone and service have been pretty much as advertised.

title: Best prepaid bang for your buck
text:
I hate cell phones. In my opinion, long distance communication is best done via a land line (Limited Mobility? Oh, the humanity!) or a computer through e-mail, IM, or social networking sites. So if you're like me, you want a cell phone that you won't be using that often (business, emergencies, maybe even time-to-time socially), that you won't cry over if it is broken or stolen, and, most of all, MUST BE CHEAP. This product is very reasonably priced (7/2011: 22 + ns on Amazon, slightly more at a retail store), the value of the minutes is among the best for a prepaid cell phone, and the cell phone itself is pretty sweet. Buy it, carry it around with you or leave it in your car, toss it around, buy one for your ten year old to teach them about conservation, whatever.

Especially with Tracfone, double minutes are a necessity. Don't get a Tracfone without it. In fact, there's a version of this phone with triple minutes. It's something like 90 bucks extra but depending on how much you use your phone, you may want to look into it. Best value I figure is the 200 minutes purchase. After double minutes and a promo code (promo code book included with purchase, by the way), you'll get approximately 450 minutes. After taxes and everything, I calculated that each unit costs around 9 cents. Better than what Net10 offers. Higher minute packages may have better value, but if you have to make those kinds of purchases on a regular basis, you might as well look into a phone with a contract. Functionally, this item works pretty much in the same way you'd typically expect a prepaid phone to work: the number of units per minute (1:1) for a call is rounded up, whether you were talking for two seconds or 59.999 seconds; texts are .3 units, probably the best value you can find in a prepaid; the browser is lame and should be used only in emergencies, and is .5 units to start and .5 units for every minute in the browser.

As for the phone itself, I like it. A lot. But first, the three things which bother me the most about this phone MUST have the most elaboration, to let you know what you're getting into.
1. Text Previews: This is nothing new. Tracfone seems to utilize a tactic in which you cannot see from whom you are receiving a text. Is it from a colleague? Is it from a new number? Is it spam? You can't tell. All they provide you before you open it is the first few characters of the text which was sent. Can't blame them, really. Their texts are so cheap, they have to make certain that you at least open every single one you get.
2. The Browser Button: This is the most common problem I've found in all of the reviews I've read. Not only is the browser button a big soft key which you also use as the "Back" key, but it's also placed right next to the "Pwr/End" key. Key lock MUST BE ACTIVATED ON THIS PHONE, or you'll wind up punching this button while slipping the phone into your pocket and wasting a LOT of units. Horrible. You'll be pressing this button a couple of times when you do not want to. Bam. Half a unit expended. If you hit the "End" key quick enough, you might avoid it. Invariably, though, you will be wasting money thanks to this little baby. This, too, is suspected to be a ploy to cheat you out of your hard-purchased units. Frankly, I think it was just a stupid human factors mistake made on someone's part. It's really the worst aspect of this phone and it could have all been avoided if only the phone had...
3. Personalizability: I can change the background and ringtones, okay, fine. I CANNOT change what the soft key buttons do. If I could change the Browser Button to, say, a Camera Button, this would be the God of all Prepaid Phones. Unfortunately, we're stuck with a shortcut to a horrible, useless browser and guessing where the shortcut key to the half-decent camera is (tip: it's "Left" on the Navigation Key).

That's all the bad stuff, though! Let's talk about the good stuff. Remember, this is a prepaid phone. I'm matching it up to other prepaid phones I've seen before.
- Light
- Great-looking
- Great battery life
- SD card slot
- Good camera
- Excellent keypad (see below)
- Volume is on-par
- Full of other useful functions (such as games, mp3 player, and calendar - with event planning!)

The keys are small, yet are very easy to master (and they have a wonderful response), even if you have big fingers. I do not know the threshold between comfort and frustration; all I know is that if small keys have been an insane problem for you in the past, you may want to find a demo of this phone to check it out first.

This phone is worth it. You can laugh at the poor souls who have sold themselves into $600+ a year contracts while you thriftily expend $15 - $20 a month for a phone with nearly the exact same features. The difference could help you pay for a netbook, which more than makes up for any deficiencies you may find in the cell phone (and which is also a great selling point when you're negotiating with your aforementioned ten year old).

Just get it. The only time you'll regret it is when you hit that stupid Browser Button.

Edit: 8/4/2011

The phone charges with a micro USB cable. (There -is- a difference between micro USB and mini USB.) These cables are cheap from Amazon. You can have one shipped to you for about two bucks. I'd recommend getting a couple and a USB car charger, which, depending on the quality, should set you back around five to ten bucks. Being able to charge the phone from a computer is a great feature, but you may also be wondering what kind of data you can transfer between the phone and the computer. The answer is nothing -- if you don't have a micro SDHC card (4gb SanDisk w/ adapter is seven bucks). With the card installed, connecting the phone to the computer should both charge the phone and allow you to change the contents of the SDHC card. No special software should be required. The reason I'm bringing this up now is that lately I've been having issues with this feature. It started to work, but connecting the phone with the card installed to my computer now brings up a hardware failure notice. This is a minor issue, but an inconvenience nonetheless. I have to open up the back of the cell phone, take out the battery, remove the card, place the card into the adapter, and connect the card to my computer that way. That's the only issue I've had with this phone so far. I'd still have bought this phone if I knew it had this issue, however. I will update if I find a resolution to this issue.

Some other information. I mentioned getting a car charger, but you may never need it. I'm on day five without charging my phone, and it's still got half battery life. And yes, I have been using it. This totally makes up for the connectivity issue, and then some. Also, as far as adding things to the phone, buying the SDHC card has been a good idea. There's plenty of tiny extras for the phone you can find online. Ringtones do not need to be in a special format, mp3 will work. If you do a search for games for this phone, they're everywhere. I download mine from Mobile Heart. (You can play Civilization! I love this game.)

So, about a month in, I've found one setback and a couple of really big pluses. Rating still stands at five stars.

Edit: 8/27/2011

Still working great. The phone averages about four days on the battery without charge. (Compare this with maybe two days for a smart phone.) Also, I obtained a Bluetooth device (Rocketfish Rf-Mrbtad Micro Bluetooth Adapter, $11). File transfers are a lot easier, and it's nice not to have to worry about cords and stuff. A little bit slower, but it makes up for the problems with USB cable connectivity. Still the best prepaid phone I've ever owned. I think this will be the last edit until I stop using the phone. Rating still stands at five stars.

title: This Phone Does It All!!!
text:
I have been with Tracfone for years and decided to upgrade my basic phone to one that had web browsing capabilities. There were a few that caught my eye but I kept coming back to the LG500G for a couple of reasons.

First, I liked the fact that it also housed an MP3 player and that it took a 4gb micro SD card. I also liked the fact that it had a 1.3 megapixel camera. Finally, I loved the look. I went to a local store to see it in person and found this to be the phone I wanted.

I ordered the phone directly from the Tracfone website. They were advertising a special price of $29.99 for the phone and accessory kit with double minutes for life. You just can't beat that, so I ordered it.

It was shipped within three days of ordering. I am not much on reading directions so I basically took the phone out of the box and began charging it. While it was charging which only took about two hours, I activated the phone online through the Tracfone website which took about 5 minutes. I was impressed.

Once the phone was charged I went through the settings and customized the sounds and display on the phone. I then uploaded my mp3's to the micro SD card I purchased and then inserted the card in the phone and voila! I had an mp3 player as well as a phone. I then decided to test the camera. Went to my favorite gardens and got photos of flowers, landscape and murals. I was surprised at the quality of photos. I was also able to send them directly to my Facebook account through the phone.

The phone has web capabilities with many applications that you can download. However for me, I don't use the browser that often but I like to know it's there in case I have problems with my computer and need to get online. That is also another reason I upgraded and bought this phone.

I've always been slow when texting but with this Qwerty keyboard, I am gaining speed and love it. I can text photos to friends and family. There is also video capabilities of which I have not yet tried but will soon. Another good aspect is there is no charge to minutes when playing your mp3's which is great because I'm listening to them all the time.

Another thing I really like about this phone is the fact that you can lock the keyboard. I like having the phone on during the day so it's handy to be able to lock it so the browser isn't activated when in your pocket or purse.

There are also a couple of games on the phone though I don't use that. Another great thing about the phone is you can buy your minutes right over the phone when you sign up for that service through the Tracfone website. Oh, did I mention double minutes for life? If you buy for example 200 minutes, you automatically get 400. I signed up for their plan which will automatically get me 400 minutes each month.

I've only had the phone for a couple of weeks and love it! I've been able to use my mp3 files as ringtones and customize the wallpaper with my own photos.

This phone also has Bluetooth capabilites. I basically use my old headphones and they work great. You can set the volume for the phone and sounds for it as you see fit. You can also customize the setting to how long you want the screen and keyboard lit up or if you want to save power you can do that as well.

I have been all over the city with it and the service is perfect. I have yet to have a dropped call even on an underground train station. The service was clear.

All in all I love this phone - everything about it is fantastic!!!

title: Good upgrade for TracFone users
text:
After having happily used a TracFone for 3 years with no regrets, I really wanted something where I could send text messages, check my email and surf the Internet to find local attractions when traveling (the older "mobile" text-based web was really slow and wouldn't work on a lot of websites). After discovering that most of your minutes and your telephone number are transferable to any new TracFone, I began my search. I first considered one of the touch screen phones TracFone was offering, but after hearing reports that you couldn't access the keypad during a call, I decided against it (I kept thinking about all of those automated menus these days at banks and companies, "press one for this, two for that").

I have been very happy with this phone. There are drawbacks: I've hit the browser button by accident a few times because it is right next to the Power Off/End Call button, so you get charged half a unit when that happens. You can download the "Opera Mini Browser" off the internet for free, which doesn't use so many minutes, into your Apps folder. The keypad is tiny, but manageable. It's a little difficult when you're trying to enter a phone number, ironically (it is a phone, after all). But if you go a little slower than normal while dialing, and don't have problems reading small print, you'll be ok. Be sure to press the "Lock" key when done to avoid those "pocket dials" (it's easy to unlock, just follow the on-screen instructions to press the two soft keys in sequence).

Yet, there are some great features on this phone. Unlike older models, with a combination USB charger/data cable, you can charge your phone right at your computer, and if you like, transfer photos, music, videos, or apps back and forth to it! You can add a Micro SD chip to add the capacity that you'll probably need if you're interested in storing much media on it, but these are really inexpensive. Convert your video files to the 3GP format, and you can watch any video on the device (although if you want to fast forward to a scene, you'll have to hold down the key until it reaches the segment of the video you want to see). The only problem I've had with the media files is if you start to get towards full capacity on your chip, they will freeze up or not play properly, so to fix this you'll need to erase some files that you don't use. This definitely is not a replacement for an iPhone or any Android based phone. However, if you only need a couple of bells and whistles and not the whole enchilada, this is a great choice. I've even posted on Facebook and Twitter a couple of times, and checked the weather. But I'm not a heavy user. I don't plan to watch YouTube (this phone can't handle that) or Netflix on my phone or play lots of video games, so for such a cheap price, this is a perfect choice for me. If you are dependent on your cell phone for heavy data/internet usage, then you probably don't need to consider TracFone: there are other companies with better deals for you.

title: The best Tracfone I've ever owned!
text:
I cannot say enough good things about this phone. It's inexpensive, light, compact, loud, clear and easily the best prepaid phone for your money. I'm really glad Tracfone has released updated phones that are comparable to Smartphones. Both the Tracfone LG 500 and 800G are great models to own for those who actually like having newer phones without an ungodly monthly contract to deal with. The LG 800 I previously owned was a great deal with triple minutes for life at $49.99. However, I thought it didn't have a loud enough volume, so I decided to try the LG 500G since Amazon has it for $20 with the phone, SD card and USB Data cable. A very excellent deal too, b/c now I have close to a 1,000 songs on my phone and I didn't have to spend alot of money for a cool feature. You certainly won't get a contract phone, a SD card and a USB Data cable for around $20 at any cell phone provider I'm aware of. Needless to say, if you aren't a rich person like me, then you can't afford an expensive contract that has few positives over prepaid providers like Tracfone. I don't watch TV on my phone or surf the web on it, so having a very dependable phone with an awesome MP3 player is precisely what I needed.

The service a few weeks in is great for prepaid service. I haven't encountered any dropped calls(which is sometimes typical for prepaid or contract providers)yet. The calls are loud and clear, IMO as clear as any landline phone I've ever used. Of course, one of the major reasons I've always chosen Tracfone over all other prepaid service is b/c you don't have to add a card every month. I'm not an excessive talker, so Tracfone adding 90 days to your service days every time you add a card is tailor made for me. Meaning, between activation and adding a 90 minute card, I have close to 150 service days and close to 200 minutes. And since I don't talk alot, that would last me for a couple months or more before I have to add another card. This feature is particularly appealing to me, b/c adding another card or two could easily give me a year's worth of service at a decent rate. In all, I might spend maybe $200 vs. some contract providera charging that per month. That alone to me makes this model phone and the service well worth the price tag.

One concern I've seen on the reviews here I outright disagree with is the browser button being on the end button. Apparently, most who've reviewed that as a negative haven't noticed the browser button is to the left of the end key. I will acknowledge that the keys are small for those who prefer larger buttons, but it hasn't been an issue for me and I can't understand why it's such a problem for most. Besides, you can go to your settings and use the phone lock feature which will not allow you to hit that particular key when the phone isn't in use. Be warned though, if you want a phone with big buttons, then you need to buy a different model. However, the buttons on this model aren't any smaller than your typical Blackberry(or Blackberry knockoff in this case). So, if you are the texting type, then this shouldn't be of any concern to you.

I'd definately recommend this to anyone who wants a nice phone without all the insane fees and monthly bills. Simply put, I haven't found a better deal than this and is a great way of staying connected without emptying your wallet. I normally don't like to rate anything with 5 stars, but in this case the quality warrants the rating.

Terrible, nightmare customer service, and a phone that simply dies for no reason at all? I'd suggest buying from a company that cares...not TracFone.

Cons: Phone completely dead after three weeks, no way to actually get TracFone to respond to the problem so far; phone is still dead, no solution in sight. Can't resolve problem via website, e-mail, or get an answer on the telephone help line.

title: TracFone LG500G

UPDATE JANUARY 2013: I've now owned/used the LG500G since February 2012 (1 year) & it's still a great phone...for me. While I agree that the qwerty buttons are small, I find them easier than the touch screen on my husband's LG840G (which he loves). It's simply because I use my thumbnails & can type fast on the LG500's buttons, whereas I have to use just my right pinkie finger to type on the LG840. The LG500 is a sturdy phone & the gel case protects it well. If I need to upgrade for some reason, I'll most likely go with the triple-minute LG530G. The battery is still going strong; it typically last from 7 to 9 days between charges, but then again I hardly ever use it for browsing. Reception is great; we live in very rural Gadsden County FL near the capital, Tallahassee.
_______________________________________________________
I've had this LG500G for almost 2 months; battery is long-lasting, I only have to charge it once a week & the way I deal with the browser button issue [not a big deal for me] to keep the keypad locked when the phone is in my purse [in a padded pouch] or in my pocket - you simply press & hold the small lock icon in the lower row of buttons. I have only pressed the browser button 1 time by mistake in 2 months & closed it quickly. While the keypad is locked you can still answer calls & it's easy to unlock by pressing Unlock & Yes. This is not the only mobile phone with this "issue" & certainly not specific only to TracFone.

I bought a deep blue silicon skin for it, along with the data cable & car charger, from Amazon, plus I already had a back-up battery from Bed Bath & Beyond [$4]. I agree the camera is not the best but it still takes OK photos - I never expect to use my mobile phone as my camera anyway. The video works fine & once I installed a Sandisk 4GB memory card, I was good to go. And the browser actually works OK - I typically use it to get the weather & maybe a stock quote. Anything else I use my netbook. This is, after all, a mobile phone & I don't want it to be everything rolled into one. If I did, I'd pay much more money every month for a fancier smartphone.

title: VERY happy with phone
text: I bought this phone about 8 months ago, and I really like it.  It is wonderful for texting (which I do a lot of).  I was at first concerned over small keys, but even with my "pudgy" fingers, there is no problem.  I occasionally hit the wrong key, but hey, I do that on the computer too!  Because of the minutes usage on the web, I really only use it to look at the weather, and check the lottery numbers.  I simply saved two weather sites for my area to bookmarks, as well as the lottery page, oh, and my mobile bank page.  That way I can quickly access them, and use up a minimum amount of time (maybe .5 to 1 minutes....2 at the most).  It is not intended for tons of internet usage (like a much more expensive "unlimited data" plan). I like the phone so much, that when my original phone had an issue (probably caused by someone dropping it in a parking lot!), I went and got another one right away.  Luckily, both times they were "on sale" for $10.  Can't beat that!  And Double Minutes to boot!  Sure, you can accidentally hit the browser button, and "lose" .5 minutes while you frantically hit the button again to back out of it.....but I figure those are errors on my part when I'm not careful, and I do try to remember to "lock" the phone when I'm not actively using it, to keep those "goofs" to a bare minimum.  My signal strength is always good, and I live in a rural area in PA (near several mid-size cities).  Even with the house absolutely surrounded by trees, I have no problem using it at home.  I would HIGHLY recommend this phone.  I know people have complained about Tracfone Customer Service, but whenever I have called (which hasn't been often, because all of the phones I've had the past 10 years have worked well), I have found them to be very pleasant and helpful.  So, overall, I recommend the phone AND the company.

title: Tracfone and LG500G overview.
text:
TRACFONE

To begin with people tend to complain about tracfone and their general lack of feature-rich phones. I am by no means in love with tracfone. While their tech support is a pain, these days that can pretty much be avoided by the online interface which makes activating phones and purchasing minutes very simple and really is all you need to get started and maintain service. If you have the money and the need for a smartphone then by all means get one. I came back to tracfone after being on AT&T, T-Mobile, and cellular south Cellular-South plans and I can honestly say that I really don't miss my iphone or android smartphone. Yes there are times where it would be useful, but realizing that I pay less than 250 a year for service is more than enough of an incentive. The main reason tracfone doesn't release larger more expensive phones is mostly because of it's core demographic of buyers, cheap bastards and old people. Therefore, the people who complain probably should have been looking for a more expensive option to begin with. If you think that having a smartphone is a good status symbol I promise having extra cash is better. All in all tracfone provides a great bang for the buck and those who complain really need to look at just how much they're saving each year.

LG500G

My first cell phone was a tracfone. It cost twice as much as this phone and had less than half the features this one does. What do you get for $30? (less if you can snag on off ebay) Full qwerty, good MP3 player, decent camera, and other features I would have been very grateful for when I purchased my first phone at 16. Also considering double minutes are included this is an absolute no brainer. The phone is cheap, having said that the keyboard is excellent as is the mp3 player, and when I don't have my DSLR handy this is a very acceptable quick picture taker. I picked up a class 6 4GB card (4GB is the max supported memory size) and coming from the mp3 player interface on androind and iOS this is quite acceptable and very usable. I love not having to charge my phone. I alternate between huge ammounts of calling and texting to not making a single call in a week, that's just me. Therefore it makes sense that I may only have to throw my phone on the charger maybe once a week or two tops if I've been using it, also when it need juice it charges pretty quickly. I've had this phone now for about four months so plenty of time to get used to it. All in all I'm still thrilled to have such a good device for such a cheap price. If you are shopping for a case I got a rubber case for an LG saber that fits pretty well just a little trim at the charging port. I know tracfone has lauched several "smartphones" but if you look at reviews and specs they really don't have much more functionality than this device and their usually around three times the price. Also recently released is the Samsung T404G which gives you triple minutes for life. That said I will pick that up eventually but how happy I am with this phone makes me hesitant.

title: Terrible Experiences with LG 500G Phone
text: Terrible experiences with this phone. We bought two -- one for me, one for my husband -- and both have had problems. I had a clunky old Tracfone for years, reliable, great service nearly everywhere I traveled. My only problem was viewing text messages. But I wanted something new with more features, and the LG 500G looked good. NOT! At first, we were able to send and receive phone calls, but soon, that service was sporadic, and now we can no longer call or receive calls at all. Work associates, family and friends complained that we didn't have our phones turned on when they were. I don't think it's a problem with cell phone towers, because no matter where we are located, and we've been in many different areas near and far, we get the same frustrating messages: "No service" and "Emergency service only", and callers hear something to the effect that "This person is not accepting calls" or "No mailbox has been set up." The latter is true, as we were unable to set up the mailboxes. I thought it was our problem until I watched a uTube video showing how simple the process should be, and after reading some reviews of the LG 500G, I realized the problem was with the LG 500G phones. In addition, the browser key, easily hit accidentally, has cost us numerous minutes, not to mention the hours (yes, hours!) we've wasted trying to make these phones work and dealing with the aftermath of missed calls, especially business-related calls.

Next day the status still showed the same thing, so we contacted customer service, and we were told that we needed a new SIM.
It arrived 6 days later, and we called the customer service to activate it. We were told to wait up to 1 hour; so we waited and nothing happened.

title: Almost a year and still the best looking Android phone
text:
Have been using it from almost the first week the phone was released in Japan and I still don't feel like upgrading to the crazy new phones with monster specs like gigantic screens, cores that are sitting idle in the phone. Mostly because they all look ugly PLUS Arc simple does what it should do all very smoothly and in style.

SE stock launcher is buttery smooth and has lot of nice little features which most users may not figure. For example, you can drop apps on an app already on launcher dock and it will create a folder with a small icon of the app. It even lets you name that. You can pinch your home screen to bring all widgets on to one screen. In the apps folder it's now how it gives option to sort apps in different order. I prefer to have them sorted in the order they are installed.

Pros
1. Style
2. Screen
3. Onyx theme makes the phone UI feel very classy and rich
4. SE widgets like weather, music, toggle widgets, etc go very well with the themes.
5. Having nice big photos display for contacts is one of the excellent feature of SE android phones. They display in a unique aspect ration with stylish fading. (Please note that if you sync with Google for contacts the pictures show blurry as they are low resolution. The trick is to add the same contact again and save as Phone contact and assign high quality photo. This will automatically link the user with Google user and you can choose the picture from Phone contact)
6. Camera performance in low light. Simple amazing.
7. Sound quality of SE music player is far far better than any phone player I tried. I like the "Mettalic" equalizer mode.
8. USB port on the opposite side of 3.5mm audio jack. Initially, I didn't like it there and thought it should have been at the bottom like iPhone. But, once you get SE Livedock you will know why SE designed it that way. The phone looks gorgeous when docked in landscape more. 3.5mm jack is not on top and you can hook it to speaker system while phone is dock. Perfect bedside alarm clock.
9. Comes with factory installed screen protector. I wish more phones come this way.

Cons
1. A little too much over design on the sides of the phone and cheap plastic feel of the silver edge. They should have used real metal for the silver strap and also should have used a more simplistic volume rocker and camera button.
2. The batter cover feels creeky. I had to buy softer feel version from ebay for just few bucks and the phone feels much better.
3. SE laucher still feels very under developed and lacks widgets for calendar, facebook, etc that are more customized for the SE themes. You just have to use stock widgets which all have white background and ruin the classy look of SE theme. Well, you can always buy apps for this but it would have been a nice touch if SE included them.
4. Power button feels too tiny.
5. Bezel feels too big at the top of the phone. I guess it makes up by having it smaller at the bottom and hence making the phone more finger friendly.

All in all, this is still a fantastic phone and probably the best for anyone who like to take lot of pictures and listen to lot of music. At current price which sometimes is touching a penny less than $300, it can't be beaten.

title: Finally, Sony Ericsson gets it right.
text:
I previously owned an Experia X10 which I was content with as my first smart phone venture but after purchasing the Experia Arc, I can clearly see how flawed the X10 is. I won't go into the X10's problems since this is a review for the Arc. So that being said, will break down the review in categories. Looks, Software and Performance.

Looks- One sexy sleek phone hands down and one of the best looking phones on the market. The phone is super slim and the arc in the back actually adds to the sleekness. The back of the phone looks black but looking closely at it you can see it goes from a dark blue to a dark grey silver tone. But you have to look very close. The screen is beautiful at 4.2 inches and the sides of the phone are a chrome color which makes this phone look very classy and heavy, yet it's not heavy at all and pretty light.

Software- A huge flaw of the x10 was the lack of updates and an ancient android operating system. I am happy to say this phone comes with the latest 2.3 gingerbread operating system which includes flash for pc like web surfing, more stability, pinch zoom and the ability to download the latest apps requiring the latest operating system. Sony Ericsson has also perfected their skins and proprietary merged os. The system is much more responsive as well.

Performance- As stated before, this phone is stable, smooth and pretty quick. Sony is touting it's display as a display infused with their bravia engine technology which in short is just a gimick in terms of the home screen but does improve the picture in the camera and video departments. I compared the x10 with this and found very little difference in the home screen but the camera function is clearly better on this set and better than other phones I have compared. Still the samsung oled and iphone retina displays are still the best in the business. Even so the camera display comes pretty close to those phones.

On a side note, the recharging on this phone is super fast! about half an hour to an hour and it's fully recharged. 15 minutes and it's and it's 30 percent recharged. The standby time is also really good and impressed with the life of the batter during constant internet use.

I bought this phone unlocked and it only works on AT&T's network but definitely worth the price and piece of mind knowing i'm not held on contract anymore. Wonderful phone and kind of like that this phone isn't offered widely in the US as it's very unique and gets lots of looks. It seems like the whole world has an iphone these days and I feel like I have something most people don't, and I do. :)

Quick Update: As of 11/7/11 my phone still working like a champ. I just wanted to update everyone on a recent update for the phone. The update provides slight improvements such as advanced face book integration, screen capture, Zoom in HD camera 3D capability, new themes, icon pics in created files, better recording sound and speaker volume. The only updates I found any interest in was the screen capture which is a great feature to have and the zoom on HD camera. Otherwise all other updates just okay. The 3D capability sucks, All it does is allow you to take 3D pics in panorama view but in order to view it in 3d you need a 3D capable tv along with the 100 dollar glasses! Either way, it's nice to get some updates as giving it's unlocked status I thought I would'nt get any updates.

You can't plug it into the tablet while docked anyway. It's not like people receive the dock and not able to use it right away. The cables are cheap and tablet owners need several anyway. Get on Ebay and get one or two more for just a few bucks.

What I like about it and what really matters:
It works.
It fits my tablet.
It looks good.

What I don't like (just personal preferences):
The black plastic is a dust magnet, it's very shiny and magnetic.
The angle of the dock is too much. I would prefer that it would stand more upright. I put rubber feet on the back base to correct this which also aids in keeping it from slipping on my glass top desk.
It takes 2 hands to remove the tablet from the dock. It's snug in there.
The price COULD have included a cable but I wasn't expecting one.

As far as the price, I see other docks for other products and this is in line with that. In general, most docks are priced too high for what they are.

Some complain about how the tablet won't fit with a cover on. Maybe they do exist, but I have yet to see ANY dock that works with covers or sleeves attached. This complaint is ridiculous.

title: It works as designed, but the crossbar is made for other (slightly smaller) tablets - NOT FOR GALAXY NOTE 10.1!
text:
For those with the Samsung Galaxy Note 10.1: The stand DOES work with it, but WITHOUT THE CROSSBAR.
(The stand has two parts - the base, which is weighted to help keep the tablet from tipping, and the crossbar, which secures the tablet better and makes it so the connector for the base isn't the only thing holding it up.)

It DOES work, however, so I give it 4 stars. It should note what models it is compatible with. (Alternatively, make it fit the larger Galaxy Note 10.1, and add a liner to secure the smaller tabs.)

Yes, you need to provide your own cable... but you have one, because it came with the tablet. Does this seem obfuscated? It's not, because you can use it as a standalone dock, such as for photos, and you'd need a plug-in... or you can use it by your PC and connect it as a media source... etc. etc. So that makes sense.

Besides - how many people have 10+ USB A-B cables they never will use because everything comes with one?

Now it would be nice to add a USB port... but it would require more power.
And it would be nice to have an HDMI port... but that would require more power.
And it would be nice to have it bronzed with gold lettering.... but that would require more money.

All in all, it seems decent... but for the fact that its design is for a slightly smaller device.

title: Great phone, hotspot, PDA-decent GPS
text:
Nokia has had some issues in the past few years-but this is a solid device and one of my favorite Nokia devices (I have used an E71, E61 and few other non smart phones).

I really like the built in fm radio, and have mixed reaction to the media center on the phone-which takes some getting used to. I have never been able to get pre-loaded videos from the memory card to play on the phone, and I have tried a few different formats. The interface on the mp3 player mode is a little odd and takes some getting used to-however it does work well. The camera takes excellent pictures (5MP), and has an actual external flash. The phone takes decent videos as well, but the video sound quality is not great.

Image heavy sites do not work well on this phone due to limited memory issues, so if you are trying to use non-mobile sites for most sites this may not be a great choice. This has nothing to do with the proprietary browser on the phone-I have tried using Opera mobile, and everything to do with system RAM. Sites like youtube will work, but only in the mobile version and it takes a while for it to load.

The communication apps on this phone are solid. Google messenger, AIM and most of the pop3 email accounts and gmail work pretty well on this. Microsoft exchange also works well on this phone and has the Quick Office app that allows you edit MS documents and MS excel files-although the screen is small. Some of the older e-series devices were compatible with Blackberry connect-this one is not-and no ad I have seen makes this clear.

While some reviewers have commented that the keyboard on the phone is a little small, it is a little on the small side compared to BB-but this makes it easier to operate from one hand. This phone also has the Nokia predictive text built in-which is odd on a phone with a qwerty keyboard but makes emailing a lot faster. The trackpad operates very well but is very sensitive, and the soft key/home keys are also easy to press with one hand. However, the main screen is not as customizable as other smart phone devices.

Ovi maps is the GPS on the phone, and for the most part, it works well. What I really like about Ovi maps is the ability to download maps to the phone and use the maps/gps without a data connection. Google maps is still a downloadable file and it does work well.

T-Mobile bloat wear is abundant on this phone-beware.

I have been using my e73 for over a year-if you have any specific questions feel free to leave a comment and I can try to help!

title: I'd be upset if I had paid more than $25 for this
text:
I got this for free from T-Mobile when I agreed to renew my contract. My previous phone was the Nokia 6301 (also from T-Mobile) and I loved it so much I wanted to get another Nokia. Boy was I disappointed!

Good points

- Solid construction

- QWERTY keyboard for note taking and texting

- Battery lasts a long while, especially when you activate the power savings feature

- The back flashlight is very useful

- Great for travel - unlike the Nokia 6301, this is quad band and automatically adjusts clock based on location.

- Free visual voicemail

Bad points

- Buggy - on my phone if you hit Menu, followed by Exit, you end up locking the keypad. Why does it do that? One night I was talking to someone while the phone was charging and I noticed that the screen showed no indication that a phone call was taking place. After the call ended, the only way I was able to turn off the phone was to remove the battery. Also the visual voicemail is buggy. It often mis-identifies the name of the caller who left the voicemail.

- Unintuitive - it took me a long while to figure out where to go to set alarm clock. (in case you have the same question it is Menu > Applications > Clock)

- Poor features - this is the first phone I owned that does not save call duration. During the phone call, there is a ticking clock that tells you how long you've been on but that information is lost after the call ends.

Since I got this phone for free, I can't complain too much because I got what I paid for. ;)
