title: Great for teaching the kids how to cuss
text:
My husband got this phone. He thought it had been sent to him from the heavens. So my son got this phone. He thought it was the most awesome piece of awesomeness that anyone had ever experienced.
Finally, my contract was up! I too could bathe in the glory of contract-free, utopian beauty that was the ZTE WARP! I was so excited.... giddy. I had never had an Android type phone. No touch screen. No Angry Birds had graced my screens before.
I had planned to visit a couple of local stores, read reviews, make an informed decision. I had looked forward to the experience of picking out a new phone as much as buying one. Yes. I'm a woman. I have trouble deciding what to choose. I love to shop. The new phone was for me. What was the harm in taking my time?

My husband had different plans. Because he was actually PAYING for whatever new gadget I would have, HE would pick it out. He decided that since the ZTE WARP was clearly forged in the light of the Holy Spirit and baptized in unicorn tears, I should have nothing else. After all, what was good enough for himself and my son was surely good enuff for me.
At first, I too loved this phone. I'd never had anything like it. I've never had the black plague either. (I have a birthday coming up, can't wait) Soon, the men of the house were having trouble with their gifts from God. They both immediately replaced their phones with newer, more shiny models. Within a month, I was having issues too. Now its been over a year and a half. I'm using my Warp to write this review. Honestly surprised I've gotten this far without it shutting down. I can only talk on speaker phone. Most apps don't work. Its called the WARP because someone with a warped sense of decency unleashed this demon on unsuspecting android seekers. RUN! I would but its all I have. I can't afford a new phone. Since this one nearly caused the downfall of my marriage, hubby says he's not going to be involved in my replacing it. Please save yourself. Choose ANY phone but this one!

title: Great screen, buggy system, economical & reliable carrier
text:
FIRST, about Boost. (If you want to read about the phone, skip ahead.)

I've been with Boost for a few years now. I'm totally happy with them as a carrier. I got sick and tired of paying $95-150/month for my smart phone bills (because contract cell carrier smart phone plans did not include unlimited minutes AND unlimited texting WITH unlimited data -- so I was constantly paying overage for texting and talking too much). So a few years ago I switched to Boost. Boost uses the Sprint network, and I haven't had any problems with it (depending on the phone used). It was TOTALLY worth the $45-100/month I SAVED being on Boost. And now that Boost and other prepaid carriers are offering smartphones and Androids, I will NEVER go back to a contract mobile phone. Never. There is no reason to.

Every now and then, I pick up and try other prepaid phones. I'm not impressed. Net10, Tracfone, Straight Talk, and Virgin Mobile all "dumb down" their phones by disabling factory default features (such as ability to use phone as a wifi hotspot). Straight Talk is by far the worst for dumbing down phones (they disable *tons* of features).

Boost also removes some features (like the ability to use the phone as a wifi hotspot, damnit!). But on Boost smartphones, you can get around that with some apps (such as PDAnet). You CAN'T get around it on any of the Net10, Tracfone, or Straight Talk phones I've tried. I'm not sure if that's because they disable those services in the phone's hardware, in the phone's software, or on the cell network (by using the cell's unique address/ID to block certain services).

Boost also doesn't cap data service and then slow it down when you reach the cap. All other prepaid carriers (and most contract carriers) do this. I thought that was because Boost is a prepaid arm of Sprint, who also don't cap data service. But then, Virgin Mobile is also a Sprint subsidiary, and data service is capped on Virgin Mobile phones (once you reach the cap, your data service slooooowwwws dooowwwwwnnn...).

It's true, it's hard to get a human with Boost's customer service... but that's true of all the prepaid carriers, WORST with Straight Talk. For many of these prepaid carriers, you get heavily accented "English-speaking" customer service or tech support in India or the Philippines. Their English can be hard to understand. Never had that issue with the major carriers like AT&T and US Cellular, but I never called or needed their customer service often enough for it to be worth the extra $45-100 I paid monthly!

Boost also offers bill shrinkage. For every 6 months you pay your bill on time, they shrink the bill by $5. For regular phone users (who pay the $50 unlimited talk/text/web), you can shrink your bill down to as low as $35/month. For Android users, who start at $55/month for unlimited talk/text/data, you can shrink your bill down to $40/month. For Blackberry users, who start at $60/month for unlimited talk/text/data (by FAR the cheapest Blackberry service available ANYWHERE in the US), your bills can shrink down to $45/month, as I understand it. Basically, whatever plan you're on, if you pay your bill on time for 18 months, your bill will shrink $15/month ($5 every 6 months).

So, I'm very satisfied with Boost. I've been on Verizon, AT&T, T-Mobile and US Cellular. They are not worth the cost. I've also tried other prepaid carriers: Net10, Tracfone, Straight Talk, and Virgin Mobile. Not impressed, especially because they dumb down/disable features on their phones and cap data speeds. Boost doesn't cap data/speeds, rarely disables features/dumbs down (if/when they do, you can just find an app, or root the phone, to get around it). Boost also has WAY LESS bloatware than all the other prepaid carriers, and less than many contract carriers. So I don't see myself leaving Boost any time soon.

I realize this sounds like a Boost commercial. I don't mean it to. It's just that I've tried almost all other contract and prepaid carriers and felt like I was getting ripped off. I don't feel that way with Boost. They really seem to have the best combination of monthly cost for unlimited talk/text/data, phone/smartphone selection, reliable network service, rarely disabling phone features, and rewarding customer loyalty. Boost is not perfect (customer service; other carriers obviously have many more phones to choose from). But Boost is better than every other carrier I've tried, and I simply refuse to go back to paying $95-150+/month just so I can get the latest/greatest mobile phone... especially when Boost now offers so many Android phones.

Now about THE PHONE:

The ZTE Warp is a decent Android phone. It is not great. It is not total crap, either. It gets about average battery life.

Not using "location service" (GPS) increases your battery life. So does turning off wifi until/unless you need it. In fact, if you have to be somewhere that makes cell reception nearly impossible (like, deep within a hospital near shielded areas, like Radiology...), it's best to put your phone in Airplane mode so it will stop *trying* to connect to the network or Wifi, which uses up juice.

Pros:
Screen is large, hi-res; good for watching vide/reading ebooks/editing docs
MicroSD card up to 32G (download TV shows from your PC and watch them!)
Corning Gorilla Glass screen, not easily scratched like most touch-screens

Cons:
Buggy system software
Too-soft haptic feedback
Poor reception (unrelated to network)
Mediocre camera and lousy, low-res video
Crappy native browser*
Lousy input XT9 and Android keyboards*
Quiet (too quiet) ring tones*
Native MP3 player sucks*
Native video player sucks (and only plays 3GP video)*
Sucks up battery if using GPS/Wifi/3G/MP3 player/watching video*

One issue I noticed is, if you are outside and it's chilly or downright cold (40s F or below) and you are not wearing gloves, it's nearly impossible to use the touchscreen with your naked fingers, frustratingly difficult even with gloved fingertips. This may be a result of the cold outside temperature affecting the touch screen. Or it may be the cold affecting the Gorilla Glass screen; I'm not sure.

*All asterisked issues can be fixed or ameliorated with third party Android apps. I have found freeware apps to solve or work around all of these issues. Opera Mini or Boat Mini browsers are better than the native one. A ring-tone or equalizer app can fix the too-quiet ring tone issue. A freeware music/MP3 player fixes the music issue (I use the Amazon MP3 player, though it's not great, either). MoboPlayer and QQPlayer both will play AVI and WMV files, so all I have to do is load up my microSD card with my favorite TV shows, and I can watch them.

An app killer that automatically kills apps/services can help with the battery issues (I use Advanced Task Killer). However, if you're going to watch a lot of video or plan to listen to MP3s for a few hours while doing something else, you'd better have the charger nearby.

There is no solution to the lousy camera, low-res video that it takes, or the buggy system software, as far as I can tell. I'd rather have a better 3 MP camera that can take higher res video than this phones lousy 5 MP camera and low-res video recording.

Also, this phone does some weird stuff if you enable Wifi but then spend time in an area with no Wifi. For some reason, even when you have 3G network capability and full bars for the cell signal, if Wifi is enabled but there's no Wifi network available near you, the 3G often won't work for data. Any Internet service (such as browsers, weather apps, Gas Buddy) will say they can't connect to the network. Disabling Wifi and re-enabling it does not work to solve this.

To fix this problem, you have to turn the phone off and then back on, or put the phone in "Airplane mode" for a few seconds (which has it's own issues, see below)

This Wifi-makes-cell-service-stop-working problem may be an Android problem, rather than a ZTE Warp-specific problem; I have noticed a similar problem on my Virgin Mobile LG Optimus Slider Android phone. And I've heard of other Android users having this problem intermittently.

Then there is the Airplane mode bug. When you put the ZTE Warp in Airplane mode in the "Wireless & networks" settings, if you exit the "Wireless & networks" settings screen, when you go back to the Wireless & networks setting screen, you can't turn Airplane mode back off. When you exit the settings, and try to go back, the box for Airplane mode is UNchecked, even though you are IN Airplane mode (and can't access the cell network or use Wifi or GPS). With the box unchecked, there is no way to turn Airplane mode back *off* once you leave the "Wireless & networks" settings screen. If you check the box, it just turns Airplane mode "back on," like you would expect it to. It does not "toggle" the way it's supposed to.

The only solution to this that I've found is to turn the phone off and then turn it back on, then go back to "Wireless & networks" settings *again*. After restarting the phone, the Airplane mode box IS checked (BECAUSE you *are* in Airplane mode)... so you can finally uncheck it.

The desktop does not flip into landscape mode when you flip the phone into landscape mode for any other use (such as, to make the virtual keyboard bigger). I was told by a Radio Shack employee and also by a Boost Mobile employee that that is normal for Android phones without physical QWERTY keyboards. This seems stupid to me. It may not be a bug, but it does seem like poor design, to me...

The lousy cell reception of this phone seems to have no cure, except standing close to windows or going outside. I have a prepaid Virgin Mobile Android LG Optimus Slider, which I use for tenants and contractors/repair services for the building I temporarily manage (long story). Virgin Mobile uses the Sprint network, which is what Boost also uses.

Unfortunately, many times people who know both my Boost and Virgin Mobile phone numbers (like my boyfriend) will call both my phones, starting with the Boost phone first (it is my main personal phone). Although I will have both phones on me or near me, the ZTE Warp won't ring -- and often won't even list the missed call!

Then when my bf calls my Virgin Mobile LG Android phone, it rings right away. If he left voicemail on the Boost phone first, the ZTE Warp will suddenly wake up a few minutes later and tell me I have voicemail, although it does not list the missed call. Since both phones use the Sprint network, and I have both with me in the same place, it can't be the network that's causing the problem. It has to be the phone's poor reception.

Also, my previous Boost phone was a Sanyo Incognito (yes, I was without a smartphone for a time, horrors!), and it rarely had these reception problems, even in the same rooms and on the same floors in the same building. Maybe the Corning Gorilla Glass touch screen on this ZTE Warp interferes with cell reception? IDK, but it's really annoying, especially when you miss calls you wanted to get.

To sum up:

If the ZTE Warp is your first Android phone, and/or your first smartphone, and/or your first experience with Boost, you will probably be very happy with the ZTE Warp (and Boost).

If you like to read books/fiction on your phone, or you want to watch a lot of video, you will probably *love* the ZTE Warp, for it's big beautiful (and rugged) screen. It has the biggest screen of all the Androids on offer from Boost, and a bigger screen than many Android phones from contract cell carriers.

If you plan to watch a lot of movies/TV on this phone, you will love the big, beautiful, hi-res screen even more AFTER you install a better video app, such as Moboplayer or QQPlayer (as of this writing, both are available as freeware from the Google Play app store). The native video app -- as with most smartphones -- can only play 3GP video. That means all your favorite movies or TV shows that you want to transfer from your PC to your phone, must be converted to 3GP video first. That's a huge pain the butt, so installing an app that can natively play WMV, MP4, or AVI files will definitely make your life and video viewing much easier!

If you tend to drop your phone a lot or often stick it in places where it can get scratched (like in a purse or pocket next to your house keys), you will appreciate the way the Corning Gorilla Glass screen doesn't scratch up like most other phone screens do.

If this is not your first Android phone, or not your first smartphone, though, you may not be happy. The buggy system, the lousy cell reception, the too-quiet ring tones, the too-soft haptic feedback (maybe that's a result of the Gorilla Glass, too; idk), Airplane mode that you can't turn off unless you turn the phone off and then back on, Wifi making 3G stop working... these are all minor problems, but together they add up to pretty damn annoying, for me.

No mobile phone is perfect. Usually you have to tolerate some annoying crap in order to get the features you want. The ZTE Warp has a few Pros and a lot of Cons. If you don't value the Pros very much, you probably will not want to tolerate the Cons, and you'll probably be better off looking at a different Android phones from Boost.

I'm planning to switch to Boost's Samsung Transform Ultra. I don't regret "my time with the ZTE Warp" but the annoyances have started to build up and annoy me. Also, I just prefer a physical QWERTY keyboard. I go used to it on my old (very over-priced) Blackberry (on US Cellular, before I switched to Boost). I'm old school, I guess. Or just old... with "man hands", I guess!

title: ZTE Warp (N860) --- Boost Mobile
text:
(The main attraction of this phone is actually the service provider, Boost Mobile. While the cost, terms, and quality of Boost Mobile's voice and data services would greatly influence a user's experience with this phone, those are outside of the scope of this review.)

I was initially hesitant to buy the ZTE Warp, because of my lack of familiarity with the manufacturer. Don't let that stop you - I think this is the best value in Boost Mobile's current smartphone lineup.

The phone comes with a wall charger adapter with a single USB female plug, a USB A male-to-micro B charging/data cable, a brief "Getting Started" manual, a more detailed user manual, an "Activation Kit" manual, and a Qmadix screen protector.

Since this device is a phone, I should first mention that sound quality for voice calls is very good. I haven't had any problems with reception, but Sprint has good coverage where I live.

The ZTE Warp has a 1 GHz single-core CPU, which is far from cutting edge, but it is more than adequate. There is no lag at all when scrolling or transitioning between screens, even using fancy effects with a launcher app. Menus and apps load and run very quickly.

The screen is responsive to tactile input, with no problems tapping, sliding, or moving icons around. The screen is large, and looks nice. It is obviously not in the same league as a Super AMOLED or Retina Display, but this is not an issue unless you are doing a side by side comparison.

I have large fingers, and find it easy to type with the phone in landscape orientation, somewhat less easy in portrait. XT9's auto-correct feature sometimes changes words from what I've already manually (and correctly) typed to something else. This isn't sufficiently annoying to prompt me to install an alternative, yet.

There is very little bloatware. There is MobileID, which is a useless theme/skin app. (GO Launcher EX, LauncherPro, and ADWLauncher are far superior.) There is also BoostZone, which provides easy access to your account information and self-help guides, but doesn't do anything you couldn't already accomplish by browsing Boost Mobile's web site. These apps cannot be deleted without rooting the phone. Other than that, you get the stock 2.3.5 Android (Gingerbread) OS, and can customize it to your liking.

As mentioned in another Amazon review, rooting the phone is easily done via One Click Root. Doing so voids the warranty, and so I do not plan to root until it expires. There are tutorials on Android user forums and videos that explain the process, if you want to do it.

Though I don't expect any camera phone to perform as well as a dedicated digital camera, I have to say that the ZTE Warp's pictures and video are, to put it kindly, suboptimal. The autofocus takes a while to lock on, so there is typically about a two second lag between pressing the camera button and acquiring the image. My phone's LED flash does not result in the "ghastly tint" described in another Amazon review, but there is some normal variation in tint between individual LEDs. I was fortunate enough to get a neutral tinted LED, and the other reviewer probably got a blue or green tinted one. I do not take pictures with the phone frequently, and so I haven't bothered to install an app to improve camera performance (though I've read that HDR Camera for Android is good).

The bezel of the camera and flash sticks out a bit from the back of the camera, so it is possible to scratch the lens by setting the phone down on its back. However, most users will use some sort of case, cover, or skin to protect the phone, which should counteract this design quirk.

I have not figured out how to turn on the flash LED for illumination while taking a video. After reading the user manual, fiddling with the phone, perusing a few Android user forums, and reading and watching numerous reviews, I have come to the conclusion that it can't be done. If anybody knows how to do it, please post or comment! Also, I haven't found a (free) flashlight app that can access and control the phone's LED. However, I am a "flashaholic", and I always carry at least one "real" flashlight, so I consider this to be a minor disappointment rather than a flaw.

Other reviewers have commented that the ringer and speaker are not loud enough. In my opinion, the volume is adequate, but individual users' needs, sonic environments, and hearing acuity will vary. The speaker might be inadequate to listen to music, but I think most users would do so with headphones. The headphone jack is 3.5 mm, by the way.

I have not experienced any lockups or reboots yet. When I bought the phone, I charged the battery, activated it, and applied all of the updates (PRL, Profile, "ZTE Software", and firmware) before doing anything else with it. The phone requires the battery to be charged to a certain level (I think it was 50% - sorry, I don't remember what the prompt said) before downloading and applying all of the updates. The update menu is found via Settings --> About Phone --> System Updates. Alternatively, there is an application (Boost Mobile Warp Online Upgrade Tool.exe) for your PC that can be downloaded from zteusa.com to apply updates and to use the phone's "USB debugging" mode. This is done by connecting your PC and the phone with a USB A-to-micro B cable and running the program (phone drivers need to be installed on the PC). There is a manual for the software on ZTE's website (Boost Mobile Warp Online Upgrade Tool Introduction.pdf), which is written in "Zhonglish" ("Chinglish"?). Maybe I'm paranoid, but I don't want to install Chinese software on my PC, so I don't plan to do this. I concede that I am using a Chinese-made phone with access to my Google account and personal contacts, but I don't access bank or brokerage accounts with my phone, nor do I make any purchases other than apps.

I have not experienced any force closes yet, but these are probably inevitable unless you somehow manage to install apps that do not conflict with any others (good luck with that).

I have not had any problems with using Wi-Fi. Bluetooth works well with my car's audio system for calls. I don't use Bluetooth for music in my car, so I can't comment on that feature. GPS with Google Maps and the stock navigation software doesn't work quite as well as a dedicated GPS device, but it's good enough.

Battery life is adequate. I managed to burn through about 70% of the battery in several hours by downloading and trying out over a dozen GO Launcher EX themes, and letting my kids slingshot enraged birds at pigs and slash fruit in a ninja dojo. My typical daily usage (several calls, checking email, some web browsing, 15-30 minutes of casual gaming) gets me about 12-14 hours before draining the battery to 10-15%. Your results will vary. There are apps that claim to prolong battery life (e.g. Juice Defender), but I use the stock Android widget to turn off Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, GPS, and 3G manually when they are not needed, and I find that this suffices.

I cannot find any retailer that sells replacement batteries for the ZTE Warp. There are third party external backup batteries available, but I would prefer a replacement for the internal battery. ZTE customer support recommended contacting Boost Mobile, but Boost doesn't have any in stock currently. Mugen Power does not intend to make extended batteries for the Warp, according to an email dated 28 Nov 2011 from Mugen posted on androidforums.com. The unavailability of batteries is a potential drawback, but I would assume that they will become available as the number of Warp users increases.

There are a number of accessories currently available for the ZTE Warp, which were apparently difficult to find a few months ago. I bought an Amzer screen protector and Amzer hard case from Amazon. I found the Warp's screen to be a bit too reflective for my liking, but the screen protector fixed that.

If you are satisfied with 3G data speed, don't use apps that require a cutting-edge CPU and/or a dedicated graphics processor, and won't be disappointed if you don't have Ice Cream Sandwich installed on your phone, the ZTE Warp is a great choice.

This review tends to focus on the Warp's shortcomings. However, I wrote it bearing in mind that certain trade-offs must be accepted when value is a higher priority than high-end performance, and thought it would be helpful to highlight those trade-offs. In that light, I would give the Warp a rating of 4.5 stars based upon its performance for its price. Since none of my quibbles are major issues (with the possible exception of the camera), and I am generally satisfied with Boost Mobile's pricing and service, in my opinion the Warp's rating deserves rounding up to 5 stars.

title: Full Review - Non Favorable
text:
I've had this phone for probably about 5 months now. Overall, I am not a fan and would never buy another one. In detail...

Apps - I am not a heavy apps user, I'd say I'm probably average. The standards, Facebook, The Weather Channel, Fandango, WWF, Draw Something. You know, the basics. Still, this phone seems incapable of handling apps well. The main issue that most people don't recognize is that this phone is exactly like an iPod Touch. You need to manually shut down your apps or they continue running in the background and eat up your memory.

Battery - It's an Android. I don't expect Herculian potential from what is essentially a tiny computer with a battery not big enough to sustain much activity. I will say it does seem to drop rather fast. Standby battery life, not too bad. Overall, it's not great though.

Technical Issues - Yes, this phone freezes a lot. A LOT. Numerous times it will shut off and turn back on at random, even if I haven't used it at all that day. HOWEVER, almost every review I see about it freezing is shocking. You're NOT supposed to remove the battery. It's akin to unplugging your computer when it freezes. Bad things happen to it, mmkay? You end up damaging the OS by removing the battery when it freezes, which just causes you more problems and subsequently more freezing. Now, this phone will shut off and reboot itself **if you are patient enough**. Sometimes it takes 30 seconds, sometimes 2 minutes. If you leave it alone, 9 times out of 10 it will reboot on it's own. The consistency of it freezing up, despite what I just said, is pretty intolerable.

Calls - No real issues here. Some slight lag on button press on a rare occasion.

Texts - It's pretty common that I have to restart my phone to send and receive texts in a timely fashion. This thing practically craps it's pants if I try to send texts after charging it, which I find to be rather odd and pretty annoying. The truly difficult and irritating part is this... it'll say the messages are sent so you assume the other party has indeed received it. Wrong. After going all day a few times with NO responses to any messages from anyone, I restarted it on a hunch and my hunch proved correct. I got instantly spammed with over 20 messages I had been sent during the day that my phone just didn't feel like receiving. My friends told me that they in fact did not get any messages until that moment, and they got them all at once. I don't think it's a Boost problem, since my Husband has a different phone with them and he's never experienced that issue.

Navigation - Pretty middle of the road. Simple at some turns, and frustratingly inane and complicated at others. Some fairly common features of today's technology are missing entirely from this phone. Such as the ability to use custom notification text tones per contact. In fact, some of my custom tones decide to reset to factory default of their own accord rather frequently.

!**And one more tidbit... you have to manually update this phone very often. I do it once a week. And it does NOT notify you that it requires an update.**!

If I missed anything, shoot me a comment. Feel free to ask any questions about the phone. Overall I would not recommend this phone. I'd say save your money, do your research on the Boost website via reviews, and get something WORTH your hard earned cash.

title: Very disappointing
text:
I had purchased two of these phones (one for me and one for my wife), in an attempt to get out from under a contract. Prior to purchasing the ZTE Warp, I had never heard of ZTE before, so I did a lot of background checking on this phone. What I found were mixed reviews, but the consensus was that the ZTE Warp was a good phone for the money paid. What drew us to this phone was the screen size and not being under a contract anymore. Once we got the phones, we had some problems that neither of us could deal with anymore. Enough so that we returned the phones and renewed a contract...

What I liked:
-Large screen size
-Fast, smooth transitions between screens
-Apps loaded fast

What I did not like:
-For some reason, joining contacts was impossible for this phone... and I tried to find a way.
-Multiple freezes per day
-Multiple crash/reboots per day
-This is more of a Boost mobile issue, but despite the customer service being very helpful, they were difficult to
understand as their operators had limited English or thick accents.

The freezing up of the phone happened 3-4 times per day (on a good day) and on the last day I had the phone, it happened 10 times. Each time I would need to remove the battery and restart the phone. This was made horribly annoying by the fact that I had a case on the phone that was almost impossible to remove without injuring yourself. The phone freezing up seemed to happen most during use of apps.

The phone crashing and rebooting happened frequently as well. Not as much as the phone freezing up, but I'd say on average 2-5 times per day the phone would reboot. There did not seem to be any pattern to the reboot either. At times the phone was just sitting out in the open, at other times, was during use or even phone calls.

I very rarely return items that I purchase, and I tend to find a way to make something work, especially with electronics. I'm not the most tech savvy, but I can research something enough and find out how to get something to work properly enough. I just was not able to do that with this phone. So, I finally broke down and sent them back to Amazon. I pray my refund will be full and quick.

title: Worst phone I've ever owned
text:
I had the Samsung Galaxy Prevail and was frustrated that the low resolution camera would not scan UPC codes, and that there was not enough space for apps. I was constantly deleting apps to make space for new apps. When Boost added the ZTE Warp to their phone lineup, I was very excited. The ZTE Warp boasted a higher resolution camera and a ton of space in comparison to my little Prevail. I eagerly purchased a Warp.

I have never been more disappointed in a phone. After the initial honeymoon period ended, I began to actually try to use my Warp for real-life needs.

Battery Life
The battery life is terrible after the first couple of months (and yes, I followed all the initial charging instructions). I will charge this phone all night long, and it will be complaining that there is only 15% battery left by 9am the next day (after unplugging it at 7am). I have to take a charger with me everywhere I go. Buy a new battery and repeat.

Sometimes if I want to use the phone I have to have it plugged into the charger at the same time. This is a major inconvenience. Not to mention, if I move the wrong way the phone powers off.

Sometimes when I charge the Warp and I try to turn it one while charging it goes into an endless reboot cycle. One time I counted 15 reboots before I got frustrated enough to unplug it.

Oh, and sometimes when I plug this phone into the charger, it refuses to come on. No red light or anything. I have to take out the battery and hold the power button to drain all of the residual electricity before replacing the battery and trying again.

Freezing
This phone constantly freezes. It seems that the only thing that get's this phone's attention it taking out the battery and starting all over.

Camera
This phone is supposed to have a good camera. The camera sucks. My photos are distorted (and yes, I've cleaned the lense).

Incoming messages and calls
My Warp is extremely unreliable when it comes to receiving text messages. People will ask me if I got their text. No, I didn't. As a matter of fact, often it will be quite some time since I receiving any text message. Reboot the phone... and magic: 10 text messages.

Incoming calls sometimes also go straight to voicemail in spite of the phone being powered on with decent reception.

Demon Possession
I'm convinced this phone is possessed by Satan. Just kidding. But it certainly has a mind of it's own. On the rare time it is actually holding a charge, it will randomly reboot. No warning. If you are in the middle of a phone call, oh well. Call them back and apologize for your piece of crap phone, just remember to tell them that you didn't buy the cheapest phone on the planet, you just got taken for a ride and swindled.

I am shopping for a replacement phone, but I've learned my lesson and this time I am doing far more research before wasting my money. Until then, I can only fantasize about the day that I get to smash my ZTE Warp with a hammer.

title: Not great, not terrible.
text:
Alright so I've been on boost for a while and I've really enjoyed the service and the company. I haven't had any real SERVICE problems. Many of the issues I've had were with the phones I bought.

I originally had a samsung replenish. I can't say much good about that, it had poor memory, got poor reception (phone issue), poor screen size and resolution, terrible camera, the only thing I liked about it was the physical keyboard, though that eventually got annoying because my "I" button became half broken...Though this is not a review of the replenish, I say all that to say that the ZTE Warp was a very nice upgrade for me. I got it on sale on black friday in 2012 at a best buy mobile and was excited to have a large, full touch screen phone.

So here's what I liked about the ZTE Warp.
Nice, large, full touch screen
-Apps looked nice and were much clearer than before
Better reception than my old samsung replenish
More sturdy than the replenish
Swipe to text
Nicer, sleeker looking design.
MUCH more internal and external (memory card) memory.

That's essentially it.

The things I disliked?
Sucky camera and video recorder
Average battery life (fixed with a battery saver app)
Volume on ringer is quieter than I'd like.
Still kinda sucky reception in places
-It was better than before but not nearly as good as it could be.
The messaging/texting app.
-It was sometimes very sensitive, and wouldn't finish swiping a word even tho I hadn't lifted my finger.
-It wouldn't let me "add things to the dictionary" like some phones will pick up things that you type and remember them and stop correcting them. This phone won't.
-T9 swipe kinda sucks.
-Trying to just type and not swipe would make little hints come up saying "try swiping from letter to letter" and as far as I could tell there was no way to turn this off.
-When it's cold, or if your hand is cold, swipe is basically useless.
-The absence of a physical keyboard coupled with the bad haptic feedback made me not a fan of the texting app.
Soooo many buggy issues.
-I was consistently taking the battery out and putting it back in because the phone would freeze or shut itself off and not turn back on.
-The WiFi would be glitchy in places where it should be working quite well. Like a college campus.

I originally thought the buggy issues were just the phone that I had, so I went and exchanged it for the same phone at another best buy in mid-December. I got the same glitchy issues with a different phone. It's just the design of the phone.

I didn't totally hate this phone. It was definitely an improvement over what I had. If this is your first smartphone, you'll probably really like it. If you're coming off of a really crappy smartphone like I did, you'll probably really like it as well. But If you are an avid smartphone user, go for something a little higher up in the ratings.

title: What a disappointment
text:
After owning the Motorola i1 on Boost and watching the gradual rate of neglect grow on the part of MOTO, I decided to seek a newer handset with a bigger screen and updated OS. At first, I was set on buying teh LG OPtimus S, but after the purchase and the knowledge of it being a rooted phone from Sprint, I had to make yet another decision as to what next. I decided that cost-wise, the ZTE Warp wouild fit my budget well, I was never more wrong before as, after taxes, it came to $264. The purchase was made in March of this year and I was pleased with it for about two weeks, thats all, two weeks. It was then that I began to experience a wealth of bugs and serious issues that I'd never seen before. I consulted the place where i bought it and got nowhere as to how they could be fixed. So, after about two months of remaining as optimistic as I could, I started to explore the return policies of A)the manufacturer and B)the service provider and C)the retailer. Starting with the last, reltailer said they offered a 30-day return service after which I would have to go to BOOST or ZTE...cancelled C) out. Next, I inquired online at boostmobile.com and discovered that since i didn't purchase on their website, i couldn't be helped. Lastly and the most interestingly, ZTE explained i would need to send to repair facility in TX so I printed their label and boxed up to ship out. ABout 12 days later, it was returned to me all alone in a box with no sufficient packing materials!!!

There was now report, log or repairs, or evaluation summary to reference for my review. I was very alarmed by that and contacted ZTE once again to ahich i was told they dont include any type of summary. SO, i am closely examining my newly repaired Warp and sure enough, the same issues and they are as follows:

1) randoms restarts

2) excessive heat generated when using more than one app

3) call quality is very sub-par

4) the speakerphone feature is basically non-existent

5) earpiece volume is unacceptably low

6) overall performance is low-budget/entry level Mickey Mouse caliber

So they basically held my phone and did who knows to it...all i know is that i am very upset with ZTE and their scamming US customers with poor product. I emailed ZTE reps and had to demand in large font bolded typeface repeatedly, that my handset be replaced and after three days of the, and I quote ZTE rep's exact language here "The Higher Authorities" would review and offer a resolve.

After the three days, I received an email saying that they would, replace but only the handset itself not the battery or back cover. What if the battery could be adding to the issues present? I guess it's my responsibility to solve that one cuz i am sure as hell not going to attempt to demand anything further from ZTE.

LOng and Horrible story short here folks, STEER WAY CLEAR OF THIS PHONE...THE FACT THAT IT WAS DESIGNED WITH ONLY A SINGLE CORE, LOW POWERED PROCCESSOR STRAINING TO POWER THE HUGE 4.2" SCREEN IS OF MUCH QUESTIONABILITY!!!!! Just a testimony from a dedicated EPINIONs member.

title: Don't bother
text:
I didn't purchase the phone from Amazon, but I am returning to Amazon to buy another phone because this one failed.

This phone was great for the first two months. It ran super smooth, better than my old Galaxy S3, which I had some software issues with.

If I had known the amount of issues I would have encountered with this phone, I would have never given up the S3.

After a few months of buttersmooth operation, The Warp started to freeze and lock up. I haven't had some of the issues others have had (with the rebooting) but my screen would randomly come up as static. Like television snow, but still. It would go back to the normal display if I pressed a few buttons here and there, but then the phone would lag. Terribly. To the point where it because unusable. So while my phone never rebooted on its own, I've had to reboot it several times in a vain attempt to unfreeze the screen.

It would recover from these bouts. Sometimes. When it did, it would run as smooth as it did before. But then it'd start crashing again. No foreseeable reason. I reset the phone to factory, uninstalled some things, nothing worked. I never dropped this phone, it's been handled pretty well, and yet it acts like its water damaged or something, which I know it isn't. These freezes/crashes happened at least 10 times per day. On a good day.

I think anyone who has owned this phone and has not had it fail after a year, should count themselves lucky. From what I've seen, most users end up having major problems with it in the end.

Other small problems I had was with people seeming not to understand me, or saying I was breaking up, when I was on the phone. Could be network problems, but I'll include it just in case. Also the camera is terrible, pictures looks super grainy, but for the price, I wasn't really expecting much anyway.

What's sad is that this has been going on since the phone has come out. Some of these reviews are from 2012 and no patches have ever been released to resolve the problem. It's terrible. This phone should have been taken off the market.

The price seems like a bargain, but it isn't. It's not even worth it going through the frustration for free. I'm going to try my luck with the Moto G instead. Hopefully it won't mess up as catastrophically as this phone did.

I got the phone U740 in 2009 and it worked excellent from the start, I used the keyboard ALL OF THE TIME. It was also dropped a lot too. I mean I thought it'd break. I mean it eventually sort of did, but not because of dropping it.

One day I flipped it open to view a text landscape. The screen flashed back to the Verizon V cast background screen and I restarted the phone. Seemed like it started working again. And it would always switch my pictures. Because I'd always be able to set it to what I had it on before, but I'd lose it the next time I flipped open or closed the phone. Got so it wouldn't read the card. Had placed my card in another phone, and it read it but wouldn't show what my phone had on the card. Placed it back into the Alias and had the phone work again. Phone stupidly developed the same habit again shortly after, and I REMOVED the card to put into a different phone to see if the problem persisted. As an overall: This phone had a very good keyboard, and the music player never failed as well, and it always worked, but the memory issue, is messed up. I owned this phone when I started to text a lot, and the card would always reformat itself, or just change my background to the VCAST screen.... i got a different phone after this started happening. title: I like it despite the flaws and limitations.
text:
I bought two of these, one for myself, one for my wife, however, I'll post only one review for them both.

Why I bought this phone:

Although I am not a phone person, I decided to get a cell phone. My wife has had one for years. Her bill was more than $40/month for 400 minutes of voice, no data, no text, and none of the other stuff they constantly try to add on. Her "free" phone from the carrier was always problematic for contacts because they won't "give" you a smart phone with just a voice plan. The data plans can easily double your bill. Why? Because the cost of the phone is included in the monthly charges, and smart phones are more expensive. At the end of the two year contract, the carrier has to make a profit on the provided service AND make a profit on selling you a phone which is locked into their system. What I wanted was a smart phone which could synchronize my contacts and calendars with my wife's, but I didn't want the high price of a smart phone hidden in my phone bill for two years, a cost I would continue to pay if I kept the phone for more than two years. I want no more contracts, and no more hidden costs. Therefore the phone had to have the following capabilities:

1. Unlocked Android smart phone (no contract required)
2. GMS
3. Wifi capable, Bluetooth capable
4. Less than $200 ($250 max. For comparison, an IPhone may cost 2 or 3 times as much when bought without a contract.)

Things I don't want because I already have a laptop and two android tablets:
1. Facebook
2. Twitter
3. Movies
4. Readers
5. Texting

The Motorola Defy Mini XT320:
Pros:
1. The price was great. I would have paid this much "down" for a smart phone on a two year contract.
2. The little phone was designed to be rugged. See YouTube videos of people dunking their XT320 in water. I don't recommend this, but it does suggest that Motorola was not all hype in advertising the phone as rugged for everyday use.
3. I like the size. I have a large hand, but it fits fine. More important, it will slip into almost any pocket. I don't mind the small screen. I have tablets for entertainment, so I don't plan to watch movies or read books on my phone. Music is another matter, but that does not require a large screen. I have zero interest in sending or receiving text message or getting tweets.
4. I added a 32 Gig chip to expand the memory to store music--no problem.

Cons:
1. The first big mistake Motorola made was internal memory. They included too little. Memory is cheap. They could have doubled the internal memory and not added more than a couple of dollars to the price, but I suspect the bean counters over-ruled the engineers. Still that would have been okay had they not made the second, even bigger, and stupider mistake:
2. Second Mistake. Motorola jam-packed the XT320 with bloatware. I can only assume that money changed hands to include some of this junk. Of course people might differ on what Apps they want on their phone. For myself, I don't want the included Facebook, Twitter, Moto gadgets, and a variety of other USELESS Apps. Of all the bloatware Motorola pre-installed, I could only uninstall four junk apps from one company. The rest are locked into the Gingerbread OS, and only by rooting the device with a fresh operating system can you get rid of this junk. Rooting a device voids its warranty and is not for the faint of heart. Out of the box, you turn on the XT320 and you might get a low memory warning. If I could remove the bloatware, I would have given this phone five stars.
2.5. In response to void your warranty from #2, it does not matter on this phone. Although the phone is new in the box, it has no manufacturer's warranty. Motorola's explanation is that the phone has a one-year warranty ONLY IN THE COUNTRY for which it was made. One of the phones I got was intended for use in the UK: No warranty. The other was intended for Australia: no warranty. Bottom line: evaluate the phone quickly on receipt, it has no warranty and your only hope is to return it through Amazon if doesn't work. On the up side, you can root your phone and not worry about voiding the warranty.
3. May not be Motorola's fault. I installed a 32 Gig memory chip, surely that would be enough memory. Well, it would be if you could make better use of it. However, none of the pre-installed Apps on the phone can be moved to the SD card. In my experience with Android Apps on my tablets, very few Apps can be moved from internal memory to an installed SD card. I'm running Jelly Bean on both my tablets. I don't know if GingerBread is more restrictive about moving Apps. So the 32 Gig microSD card stores my music quite well, but is useless in terms of storing Apps (again, unless the phone is rooted).

I don't really want to root these devices, but I may have to if I can't get the Apps I want to work the way I want them to work within the memory constraints imposed by the apps I don't want. I've managed to set up my email, but I'm switching from Windows live for my contacts because installing Outlook takes too much space. For the same reason, I may have to switch to Google Calendar. Because we are in flux, the synchronization I had hoped for has not worked as well as I wished for contacts. Calendar is going a bit better, but I have yet to switch completely to Google. The good news, is that synchronizing these is not something that needs to be done more than once a day. That means I can wait for it to be done on WiFi at home without paying the phone carrier's digital fees. On a practical basis, my wife and I now each have a smart phone with access to our shared calendars and contacts and 500 shared voice minutes each month for a price at least $10 cheaper each month than her phone used to be alone, and we are not charged minutes for talking to each other.

title: Good Deal On Unlocked SmartPhone
text:
I purchased this phone from Amazon LLC knowing if it did not work, I could immediately return it for a full refund or replacement. But it worked just fine out of the box with a T-Mobile pay-as-you-go SIM card.

There is a lot to like about this phone. It's compact, nicely styled, and has one of the latest phone versions of Android. WiFi video calling via Skype using the front mounted camera works great, and this saves cell minutes. I do like the white color and silver trim.

What I don't particularly like is the 320x240 screen: it looks fuzzy. But then all smartphones with such a low resolution screen look fuzzy. And the main camera is only 2 MP.

However this is one of the lowest prices for an unlocked smartphone of any type, and the Samsung brand with no-hassle Amazon LLC shopping experience makes it worthwhile. You can shop around and find a better deal, perhaps, but then your phone would be carrier locked or an off-brand.

Four stars because the 320x240 screen, while serviceable, is a hindrance to enjoying this otherwise excellent phone.

title: From Excellent to Very Poor!
text:
First of all, I was very pleased with Amazon's 1 day shipping. I reckon I received this item in 16 hours! That was fantastic. When I opened the box, the packaging appeared good enough to transport crystal. Now comes the phone which was also a bundle of surprises. I have been using a HTC Sapphire One for a long time and after I switched to this, it made me feel that I was using the Android OS all over again but in a newer smaller smarter phone. WI-FI works very well and I did all the software and apps update in a jiffy. No complains about battery. Call processor, bluetooth service - A1. Overall I think it's a very good phone for the price. Fingers crossed!
After 15 days of use, I can add that if you have fat fingers, don't buy this phone. Texting is a real pain in the behind and also using the apps. Time to time the phone does become "No service" but I guess it's the carrier, not the phone. The virtual keyboard froze just once & a restart fixed it. Stay tuned for later.
3 months' update: It's getting worse and worse as the days are going by so I am reviewing my review from Excellent to Very Poor! The phone processor now reminds me of the 386 I learned Word Perfect and DOS in. It responds horribly slow despite keeping the minimum apps & always clearing RAM through the Task Manager; sometimes it responds to a command long after cancellation & it has once,for example, embarrassed me calling an important client twice in a row for nothing. Touch sensitivity, display sensor - pretty much screwed. It has restarted couple of times on its own & I am yet to figure out why. Internal memory is so small that I am desperately seeking to "root" it. Another funny thing I discovered is the display appears "cracked" when I go to check the "Phone status" under "Settings"...very weird! It appears fine in other menus/sub menus. I really wish I could give this back but I guess I am stuck with it. To all the potential buyers, lessons learned, #1 NEVER TRUST A "NEW" CONDITION CELLPHONE HERE-THEY ARE ALL REFURBISHED; #2 TO EASE ALL PAIN, BE PATIENT & BUY YOUR CELLPHONE FROM AN ACTUAL STORE. Best reviews, top sellers, top rated plus seller...don't trust them.

title: Cute & Functioning Little Smart Phone
text: Except for the internal Memory Capacity, the fast diminishing battery life when Apps are used, and the tiny keyboard on the screen (which improves a little when the phone is turned sideways) I don't have any complaints about the phone which I use mainly for SMS texting and making phone calls.  It syncs nicely with my google account and to deal with the first two issues above I have put in a micro card and have removed all none Samsung Apps except for Kindle.  It is unlocked and thus I was able to put my regular sized SIM card in and use right away after 4 hours of charging.  The radio function works fine once the earphones are plugged in, the earphones work fine for driving and speaking on the phone, the wifi also works well, and so does the camera (in natural daylight) which I used the day after receiving the phone to take photos at a wedding.  So all in all, if you want a little Smart Phone for mainly texting and making phone calls then you won't regret getting it (I have the white but the black with the metallic back is also nice looking).  If you want to run Apps on it then be prepared to get a Micro Card to store the Apps and for charging it every day or maybe more than once a day depending on how many Apps you are running.

title: Great little phone that makes me want to have a flip phone again!
text:
Bought this for my parents who travel and live between two countries and since it's so hard to get a hold of them, I thought an unlocked mobile phone with some internet functions will help. This is simple enough for those who don't use technology too much. But it has all these preloaded apps including Facebook and emails, chat, etc.of course, you can browse web too. However, I have yet to try these apps and see how they work as I only purchased a basic international SIM card with no data plan and low credit. I did try calling my own cell phone using this SIM card and the phone worked. The camera is OK. Good for this type of phone but don't expect a smartphone standard because this is not a smartphone. Camera isn't bad at all. I took pictures of my kids and my nephews so my parents can look at their grandchildren while away, and the images turned out great! Menu isn't as intuitive but if you've used a flip phone or old generation cell phones before smartphones came out, you will know how to navigate it easily. It's light, and its body is made of plastic (as most phones are, really...except for a few Motorola phones I've came across) so it does make me wonder about what will happen if it's dropped. But it fits so well in the hand so I doubt it'll fall out. Note, I do have small hands, and so do my parents.

I have not used it outside of USA, even when I tested the international SIM card so I don't know how it works outside the country, but if it allows calls from mY international SIM card, it definitely is unlocked, so I'm assuming all other SIM cards from other countries will work as well. It is so cute and user friendly that I wish I can keep it but I got myself another smartphone that's unlocked my own travels, and have an AT&T GoPhone (which is a flip phone with lesser functions than this phone) and my own regular AT&T smartphone for use in here at home in USA. I think I definitely have too many phones, so this phone will go to my parents as initially planned.

2) Seniors who want a "Phone, Phone" with no bells and whistles that is easy to set up and use! This is a carefree, no fancy stuff type of phone. If you just want the basics in a phone: Flip phone style, MP3 (music player), camera, FM Radio, this is the phone for you.

As far as costs for text messages, AT&T charges 20 cents to receive and 25 cents to send (Ouch), these come out of your minutes balance. T-Mobile is cheaper for texts, they just charge 10 cents to receive and I think it is 20 cents to send.

When you get the YEARLY PREPAID of just $100 with either AT&T or T-Mobile, this is the CHEAPEST way to go if you do not need lots of minutes and the cost is LESS THAN $10 per month.

The bad: volume control. There is none. You are expected to navigate through the menus to change the volume and it's nowhere near simple.

Then there is the price. I mean, in the age of marginally decent sub-$100 Android smartphones (with WiFi et al.), what does a "feature phone" offer to command a price of $70?!

Overall, however, if you want a simple (that is, simple in basic features as long as you don't touch the Byzantine UI) yet reliable phone and can live with the price, then this phone is a good choice.

title: Good every day phone
text: I bought this phone specifically for a trip to Europe, but I have started using it as an everyday phone.  We haven't gone overseas yet so I cannot comment on whether it meets those needs, but as it is unlocked, quadband and GSM, it should be just fine.  I like a flip phone and there are not many options anymore.  My previous phone had exterior buttons and I disconnected calls while trying to answer them by bumping those buttons - this one has none of those.  It has no exterior view screen, but it can be set to require a button push to answer, so opening it to see who is calling does not connect the call (screening calls).  I don't need a large selection of features.  I guess this one can do data, but I don't do data on my phone so I can't review that.  I can hear on this phone better than my previous phone which is one of the reasons that I started using it right away.  It is slim and lightweight.  The screen is easy to read and buttons easy to push.  I am not physically hard on a phone so even tho this one doesn't seem to be real "tough" (battery cover is plastic) - it should be okay for me.

title: Defective
text:
The phone I received is defective- the microphone is somehow attached directly to the case so that the noise of my hand on the case makes a loud sound, louder than my voice. It took me a while to realize the problem since I use the phone infrequently and only when traveling. People told me the call quality was poor and that there was a loud rustling noise but I thought it was just poor reception or from using the phone outside. I finally tested it calling my own landline and realized the problem. Unfortunately, this was after two months, so I could no longer return through Amazon. Global Mobile says I can send it to their German site for repair. I'm looking into what the postage would be and whether it is worth it. Probably not given the other limitations of the phone.
Otherwise, the phone is OK with a couple of drawbacks. The main one is that the boot process takes quite a long time. So if you keep it turned off most of the time, as I do, it takes a while before it is usable - much longer boot than a cheap $20 BLU Jenny phone I have, which overall is as good or better as a phone (though the Jenny lacks an audio jack) . Also, the quality of the photos is really poor indoors. (Not a shock for a fairly cheap phone, but in case this is important to you).
In the end I'll probably be out the $68 I paid. No complaints about the response of Global Mobile, which was rapid, or Amazon. It was my fault for not testing more carefully in the first month when it could have been returned.

title: I really like my new flip phone Samsung GT-C3520
text:
I used to be in the high tech industry for years but never got crazy about smartphones. All in all, I like the Samsung GT-C3520 for its simplicity and good quality calls. I want a reliable phone (no butt call) that I can carry around in my daily (and often messy) activities where dropping the phone happens too often and where the phone gets in contact with metal (nails/screws) and dirt in my pockets. When my friends join me, they often end up leaving their smartphones in their cars or in my house. Now no doubt that when we travel, I'm glad that my wife has a smartphone with a GPS and the ability to browse. However, on a daily basis, the GT-C3520 is all I need.

I purchased this phone to replace another flip phone that was slowly failing to charge. I have a basic pay as you go plan with T-Mobile and after swapping the SIM card, the Samsung GT-C3520 was up and running making calls and sending SMS on the T-Mobile network.

A few days later, I flew to France and purchased a new SIM from Orange SFR. The phone being unlocked, I was able to get on the SFR network and get/receive calls/SMS. I was told that the SIM card would only work in France. However, on my way back from Europe, I was even able to get a few SMS to the US from the Amsterdam airport (2 hours layover before getting back the US).

Back in the US, I'm again using my Samsung with T-Mobile. I got it to work with my Subaru outback using the Bluetooth capabilities. It is great to now be able to talk in the car (pretty rare) without holding the phone. The sound quality is really good.

Finally, since I had a 1 GB Micro SD card, I popped it into the GT-C3520. The card was immediately recognized (as expected). I now have my favorite music with me for the rare cases when I drive alone.

The only thing that I'm missing with this phone is a calculator. Maybe I did not see it yet or maybe I can download a calculator later. Something to investigate...

title: Great flip phone with some web functionality
text:
Pros:
Excellent sound quality
Excellent ring volume
Excellent mid size display
Very compact and pocket friendly
Incredible battery life, particularly on standby
Adequate camera and camcorder
Built in email, Google, and a variety of social media apps
Built in utilities like calendar, alarms, MP3 player
Uses optional micro sdhc memory card (I use 16gb)
Features like ringtones and wallpaper highly customizable
No problem using USB cable to connect it to PC. Files can be easily manipulated using Windows or KIES (including pictures and videos)

Cons:
No external display (which probably helps with the battery life)
User guide is a cruel joke, and nearly all online searches point back to it
Time of day has to be set manually
Keypad is adequate but there are others I like better

Note that I love this phone 5 stars worth in spite of the cons. The Consumer Cellular SIM card popped in and went right to work, although it did take some doing to set up the internet access (because this is an unlocked AT&T phone and not a native Consumer Cellular phone some advanced settings deep in the menus were needed). I mainly use it to talk and text and replace my wrist watch. I'm not a heavy user, but I carry it all the time on standby, and need to charge it much less than once a week.

All in all, this is a nearly perfect compromise between basic flip phone and smart phone.

title: Really good phone overall; a few small shortcomings
text:
I bought this phone to replace my Droid 2 Global. I am mostly satisfied with it. It's much faster, has a nicer larger screen, works reliably, and does virtually everything I hoped for. It also has a real slide-out keyboard, which is overwhelmingly the reason why I bought it. (I hate on-screen keyboards -- they offer no haptic feedback, and consume half of the already-tiny screen space.) Virtually no other smartphones offer real keyboards anymore.
There are only a few small shortcomings:
- When I slide out the keyboard, I almost inevitably wind up unintentionally pressing one or more keys on the keyboard. This is due to the design of the case, which all but assures that a finger will fall on the keyboard during slideout. The Droid 2 Global had a different case design that didn't result in this problem.
- The GPS receiver is much weaker on this phone than on the Droid 2 Global. I can no longer get a GPS signal or use navigation if I have the phone under my car roof. I have to place the phone on the top of the dashboard -- with no metal between phone and sky -- to get a signal. This is awkward. The Droid 2 Global had no problems receiving the GPS signal under my car roof.
- Like the Droid 2 Global, the Droid 4 camera suffers from an unpleasant behavior while taking still pictures -- the moment you tap the "Take photo" button, the camera defocuses to take a blurry image. (This isn't due to hand trembling; the effect can easily be reproduced with the camera stationary on a table.) The effect is less than with the Droid 2 Global, but it's still there.

title: If you're going to do this, a few tips...
text:
I've had this phone a long time. (I wrote my first review over 2 years ago). I'm on my second one, an insurance replacement, and I am loving it again now that I'm not dealing with a worn out battery. I did deal with most/some of the same problems others have described here. Looking back, I wish I had contacted Verizon to use the manufacturer's warranty much sooner, on the grounds that the battery was untenable and that there were basic functional issues (the phone speaker didn't work so I became dependant on ear buds for phone calls, the micro usb was finicky, working with only select usb cables and chargers).

I agree that it's too bad Motorola went away from removable/swappable batteries. That was something I loved about the orginal droid and the dx (which made for a solid backup when my d4 went down).

Personally, I like the smaller size (was considered big when it came out, but phones have grown since then) and the slide out keyboard. I also like the way Google and Moto Droids work together cohesively.

A few tips: 1) Go easy on the battery. After doing some research, I realized I should not have let it get too low (below 40%) and, conversely, I should not have overcharged it (leaving it plugged in all night), nor should I have left it in my car. Heat is the enemy of lithium batteries, and long charge ups--which I thought were needed-- generate lots of heat.

1b) I would also take the user who mentioned that using the mobile hotspot overheated his battery at his word and avoid using that feature altogether (there's a warning on my new one before it lets me use it).

1c) Also, if you dont have insurance and your back panel swells up due to the battery overheating (as mine did) and you are thinking about taking advantage of the warranty, bring it to the store and have them help you get at your sim and sd card so as not to damage the phone. The tool and mechanism for opening the back doesn't work right once the battery swells up and you will most likely damage the phone trying to open it, thus voiding the manufacturer's warranty (never mind that the defectiveness of the phone led to the damage--and oh yeah, verizon charges a hefty fee if your returned 'defective' phone is determined 'damaged' by the motorola warehouse. I am thankful that one of their more knowledgeable and responsible reps warned me beforehand..).

Had I not damaged the phone and had I used the warranty, I would not have had to fork out a deductible, but I would have received a different Motorola phone. So I guess it worked out for me, as I do like the keyboard when typing out emails (and product reviews).

2) One thing about slide out keyboard: cases are a little tricky--usually in two pieces to enable the slide--and they leave the space between the screen and keyboard vulnerable to debris. Beach sand is your absolute worst enemy. If you're at the beach, put it in a sealed bag and turn it off. Simply putting it under the car seat isn't good in terms of heat and one little piece of sand can make sliding the keyboard out painful.

A Verizon sales rep, speaking candidly and knowing he wasn't getting a commission either way, steered me towards newer phones for the added processing power and compatibility w/ today's technology. I figure I paid all this time for insurance, and might as well use it and save a few bucks on my next phone. Time will tell how long this phone stays viable, but I'm going to try to go easier on the battery and hope that it extends the life of the phone...for now, this 'refurb' seems as good as new...

title: The Mighty Droid 4!
text:
I bought a Droid 4 shortly after they first came out after waiting for that upgrade for many months. Eventually it died a hardware death a month before the contract expired and I got a nice free refurb Droid 4 replacement (yay), long after the model had been discontinued, and now I've used it for about two more years. It broke my heart 4 months ago when I looked at it and saw I'd accidentally scratched the screen for the first time. :-( Now, alas, there it sits, this model (and this particular unit) having served me better than any other phone...ever. I'm about to perform this unit's first factory reset. because it has locked up on me for the first time. How much longer will the ride last? If this phone could continue to take the punishment that I dish out, and perform well, I WOULD DIE OF OLD AGE WITH IT STILL IN MY POCKET!
I gotta have the slider keyboard...PHONE INDUSTRY WAKE UP! GIVE US A DROID 5 or EQUIVILENT!
I'm bookmarking this page and if this phone does die, I will be back here on Amazon (because Motorola and Verizon remain clueless) to get this one. text:
Let me preface this by saying this is not the first time I've owned this phone. I bought this one to replace my old DROID 4 that was just worn out. I loved it and thought I would get the same service out of this one. The unique qualities of this phone include the military grade toughness that you can't get with an iphone or anything else. I have difficulty with all touch screens, so the slide-out keypad is perfect.
However, I'm experiencing the same freezing problem with most of the apps, despite the version of app or OS I use. Does it work? Yes. Does it work well? No.
Unfortunately, I think there's just something embedded into the software that keeps phones from lasting longer than two years so we have to buy the new stuff from the phone companies. Oh, and the battery life isn't much better either. With a full charge, I get maybe 15 minutes of gps service and not much better with most social media apps. It's just not worth it to get another one of these remarkable creatures. Oh, and that slider function? Freezes the homescreen 8 out of 10 times. That's not an estimate. I actually collected the data over 100 uses and that's the result.

Bottom line: You'll not find anything that performs the way this phone did when it first came out. Not even the same model you buy today.

title: Great sound for the money!
text:
I purchased this headphone for use with my Nokia Lumia 1020 cell phone. First of all, the headset and the phone work perfectly together. You can change volume and answer/disconnect phone calls with ease.

The packaging is exceptional and truly representative of the overall quality of the headphones. One surprise was the semi-flexible hard travel case that is included. The case is zippered and easily holds the folded phones for protection.

The Nokia Purity Headset is a quality piece both in terms of looks and construction. Though made with some plastic, they are nicely finished and at least at the onset look to be long lasting given proper care. Two separate cords are included. Be sure to use the one with the audio controls for your electronics. I have read where the "other" cord supplied is for legacy Nokia products/cell phones only.

I have used the headphones with the aforementioned Lumia 1020, iPad Mini and varied other electronics. Sound out of the box is terrific and gets even better with a progressed burn-in. After a few days of regular use, the sound for the money is fantastic, a perfect balance for my kind of music. Not too much of this and too little of that ... they are nicely balanced. Please note well: the cord controls in my experience so far only function properly (being able to adjust volume up and down and answer telephone calls) with my Nokia Windows Phone 1020. They work fine with other audio products (including Apple iPad and iPhone) for listening to music, playing movies, etc. Bottom line, same rich sound but without control from the headphone cable.

Concerning noise/music bleed and isolation from noise. There is NO bleed. The phones isolate the "outside" noise very well but not totally, but darn good. Concerning comfort: they are comfortable, in fact ... very comfortable. As I am sure comfort level will defined by individual users, I can only say the Purity Headphones are comfortable for me both for short and long-term wearing.

title: Attractive, Overpriced for Quality
text:
First off, I just wanna say I've owned and used headphones from the Sony MDR-ZX300 to the Razer Carcharias to the ATH M50 and the Sennheiser HD 558, so I have a wide range of experience with different headphones from different manufacturers at their given price points.

The reason I was interested in these headphones was because of their aesthetics. They're quite unique, and there are few headphones out there with the design language that these cans have. I was pleased with them for this reason when I got it, but had a few gripes out of the box.
I'll list my pros and cons for these headphones over several months of using them regularly:

PROS:
1. The first thing that struck me as pleasant is the leather used for the ear pads. They're very soft and pleasant to the touch, and I believe memory foam is used inside of the ear pads.

2. The weight is pleasant. Not too light, not too heavy for the size.

3. If you get these for the looks, then you shouldn't be too disappointed with them.

CONS:
1. The plastic doesn't feel to great. It doesn't feel cheap, but a combination of the plastic used and the glossy overlay makes it feel less "premium" than other headsets. It doesn't feel sturdy or solid, even given its weight.

2. They're reasonably comfortable for up to 30 minutes to 1 hour. After that, they become horrible to your ears. As they're supra-aural headphones (over the ear, not around the ear), the clamping force on your head should be at a point such that they don't exert too much pressure on your ears over an extended period of time. These do.

3. I complemented the leather for touch, but have to ding it for it's inability to let air get to your ears. Combined with the pressure over the ears, the leather overheats your ears and it becomes extremely tedious to wear.

4. This is more of a minor gripe as it doesn't bother me too much, but I believe Monster should have provided better padding on the top of your head. It's a thin layer of a rubbery material that isn't spongy or soft in the least. Given the weight though, this doesn't usually become a problem until very extended usage.

5. This is the BIGGEST problem I have with these headphones. At $70 you would expect them to sound good right? While these headphones will likely please bassheads, for people who are interested in sound quality at all, steer away fast. None of the features of the sound are defined. The bass is big and boomy, but not controlled. As a result they leak everywhere and drown out the other qualities of the music.
The sound is flat - there's the muddy base right up at your ear, and all the instrumentals and vocals are pushed back and have no depth to each component. In well designed headphones, these components are layered, ie you hear the guitar closer than the violins and vocals closer than the guitars etc. That is entirely absent in these headphones.

TL;DR:
Good looking headphones with few redeeming factors, but are extremely uncomfortable after 30 minutes (pressure and heat on the ears). For $70, these headphones sound like garbage. Unbalanced sound signature, muddy bass that drowns everything else out.

If you just want big bass and good looks, go for these if you're willing to spend $70. Otherwise, look elsewhere. I suggest considering (or starting your search) with the ATH M30x. They're at the same price point, but the engineers of Audio Technica actually know what they're doing and give a rat's ass about sound quality beyond the extremity of the bass.

title: Great sound! Important info about the 2 cables
text:
These headphones have great sound and are on par with Beats Solo's (I own both).

Some people have been upset about one of the two included cables not producing quality sound. I found it hard to believe that Nokia and/or Monster would put out a product that would experience problems with something as simple as a cable. With a little effort I found the answer: The cables are fine! Now let me explain.

There are currently no defined standards for audio jacks on phones. Most jacks are using the 4 contact TRRS (tip, ring 1, ring 2, sleeve). On older Nokia, Samsung and Sony phones ring 2 = mic and sleeve = ground. On newer phones the mic and ground are reversed. This causes only mono (not stereo) sound to pass through when using incompatible connectors.

Reading the included manual (I know, who reads instructions for headphones) it specifically states that the cable without controls is, "...Nokia AV compatible with legacy Nokia phones with a 3.5mm plug."

Nokia included the other cable in case someone wanted to use the headphones with a phone using the older standard, not so that people had two cables to choose from.
