title: Very happy with purchase
text:
Product match all depends on what you're looking for and for me, this is turning out to be a fantastic product. Handset size is certainly something of choice, depending on how you're planning on using your phone, I was looking for something I could use as a phone/communications/productivity/navigational tool.

Pros:
-Call quality and signal: excellent so far, even in areas with traditionally poor signal.
-Nokia city view: Love it, very handy when I'm traveling and it has an awesome 'interactive' feel to it.
-Microsoft office integration: fantastic,syncing through your live account is easy and controlled, you only put what you want onto someone else's server and maintaining that split is easy for both contacts/calendars. OneNote syncing is the same way, again, very controlled and then seamless once you've setup what you're willing to share.
-Email: Love the windows 8 tiles (for the phone, I have the opposite feeling for the desktop and I'm ambiguous on the tablet) for separate email accounts, very handy for splitting work/business/priorities since you can control what notifies to your lock screen per tile.
-Overall OS feel: again excellent, surprisingly so actually. I was expecting more bugs but this is really polished and slick.
-App store: there's enough here to be functional, which is all I wanted ~ although someone really wanting a plethora of games will be disappointed. The nav/prod side is solid though.
-The Win7 desktop phone app ~ is really all about syncing your itunes to your windows phone and its AWESOME. Best itunes/win translation I've seen. Its bare bones visually, but recognizes all of your non-DRM content and pulls your playlists and catalog seamlessly from iTunes.
-The phone itself: great design, high quality, excellent feel. Camera is fantastic (amateur photog - it won't replace my larger cameras/lenses but I might just dump my point and click for it).
-New features: haven't tried out things like smartglass yet, but I'm excited about the queue of features coming out for the windows phone and what it can do as part of the msft platform.
-Micro usb: I can't tell you how happy I am they used a common standard as their physical interface/charging port. :)

Cons:
-Win7 desktop phone app ~ can't sync to your office suite directly, you can upload docs but it wont' handle merges/changes like the online sync does. Given msft's segmentation of their business lines, not surprising but I'd like to see it added at some point.
-ATT
-Lack of documentation ~ this is annoying. Very poor documentation on W8 phone and google turns up results about the OS, not the phone implementation. The limited manual that comes with the phone runs out real quick for usefulness. I disagree with their naming strategy, when I google the iphone (my family has them) finding the answer is easy, ditto with an ipad or an apple OS problem (have those as well) but with the win8 phone I can't find a good segmented knowledge source just about the phone section of the OS.

text:
I bought this phone for my Dad, think it's time he upgrades from old button phones! So first thing I noticed was how easy it was to setup, although I didn't get any headphones with, thanks Amazon, it was packaged well enough and the basics setup was a breeze. Depending on where you are and what service you use, some of the more detailed settings could be a bit tedious where you need to manually enter settings, such as access point info, etc.
The display is large and crisp, and very responsive and the wi-fi works pretty well. Transfer speeds were pretty good. I upgraded the phone to 4.1.2 Jellybean through my wi-fi, the install files downloaded in almost 3 minutes (128mb file). I had to wait a while for the OS to install, but it was smooth, and works great.

The camera could have been better, but has simple to use features and the exposure can be adjusted to compensate for low light levels. Internal memory will fill up pretty fast when installing apps, and I would suggest the use of apps such as Easy Uninstaller, app2SD and Advanced Task Manager to help move, stop or uninstall files easily. Sound quality from the phone speakers are decent, but sucks through most of the headphones I tried and some video files even when converted by the software provided didn't play, I had to use QQ player to play them. The radio doesn't work very well where I am (Trinidad).
The phone is very customizable if you know your way around a Sony xperia and it does perform tasks well. Calls work fine, sound quality on calls are excellent. For the price, I think it's worth a look as a budget Xperia phone.

An update, it just suddenly started rebooting as it starts up, and won't stop no matter what I try. I am extremely disappointed, since it was working great for a while there. Will be returning this phone to Amazon.

text:
Pros:
1. Very beautiful phone, striking resemblance to the Xperia T the Bond Phone. You will fall in love with it as soon as you see it.
2. 4-in display with decent ppi, matches the Retina display of ipod Touch 5. I don't really mind that but this can be important to others.
3. 1750mAh battery produces one of the most impressive battery performance in the Xperia family: I messed around with updating and downloading apps for the whole night and the battery level only dropped by 18%. Drops about 2% with WIFI and data off during the night.
4. Upgradable to 4.1.2 Jelly Bean.(But the upgrade comes WITHOUT the battery stamina mode as seen on Xperia Z, which is basically why I would ever bother checking for this upgrade.)
5. Camera takes decent pictures with 5-megapixels. Lots of options available. Adjusting exposure level, among others, is the most helpful.

Cons:
1. User interface experiences lags from time to time, i.e. when swiping through home panels, which from my perspective can be tolerated given its almost pathetic chipset.
2. When I tried to open and work on two webpages at the same time, specifically Google translate and Wiktionary as I'm learning a new language, the phone was slow to response. It took a good while to reach google translate, and it became a hellish journey trying to open a new tab and reach Wiktionary. This is the deal breaker. I did make sure to use ES task manager to close unnecessary background processes. I won't consider other browsers as integration of Google products is the only reason I can even bear the Android system.
3. Back cover is a little bit hard to lift up.
4. Wifi is rather slow: it took ages to download a 20MB Chrome update. While all the rest of my wifi-enabled devices can do much better than that at the same position.
5. Awkward placement of the power button: near the very top on the right-hand side above the volume rocker. Certainly takes time to get used to.

Conclusion:
I thought as a very light user it may be possible to get away with its poor chipset, but I was wrong. Too bad I have to return it, it is an absolute beauty. If Sony puts Xperia P level hardware in the J I would even be willing to pay $300 for such a phone.

5 stars for the design; 2 stars off for the disappointing hardware performance.

Note: I'm a user who uses the phone primarily for occasional IM chatting and web browsing during free times(about two hours a day altogether). The qualities I value the most are good battery performance, fluid UI, and fast internet browsing. To conserve battery and ensure a good performance I removed all the home panel widgets except for the connectivity control, the clock, and 3 or 4 shortcuts for apps.

title: Nice phone with limitations for US T-Mobile users
text:
The Samsung S3 Mini is a lite version of the Samsung S3 smartphone. It sports a smaller 4” screen with a resolution of 480x800 and is an entry-level phone compared to the more pricy and feature-packed S3. This phone does not support 4G, which is curious since the S3 does. It supports 2G and 3G, as long as it works well with your carrier.

And this is the part of the review where I state a friendly warning. The vendor selling this phone states the phone is compatible with GSM carriers, such as AT&T and T-Mobile. This may not be entirely true.

I purchased this phone while setting up service with T-Mobile here in the US. I wanted an unlocked phone that my wife could use with our new service. The vendor sent us a Samsung S3 Mini “Orange” phone that originated in Europe and had European firmware installed on it. While the phone worked fine and upgraded itself properly, we were never able to get any speeds more than 2G with a data speed of about 100Kbps, which is painfully slow. The smartphone was unable to host any smooth streaming media due to this slow bandwidth.

I then learned that the phone does not support the US T-Mobile 3G transmission frequencies. It will work with T-Mobile, but only at 2G speeds. If you live in the US and plan to use this phone with T-Mobile as your carrier, expect only to use 2G service. This may be fine for some people. If it is, this phone is worth considering.

The charger is an international charger that comes with a North American adapter. The phone comes with a pair of headphones and a battery. It does not come with an SD card, case, or protective cover, as is typical with cell phones in general.

We were able to return the phone and get our money back from Amazon. Amazon is very good about returns. While this phone didn’t work for us and it was advertised to work with AT&T and T-Mobile, in fairness to the vendor who sold it, they also do say that “not all carrier features may be supported.” You're best to take this into consideration before purchasing this phone.

This phone was put on the market in 2013, and once the alarm goes off - it cannot be silenced if one has it in one's pocket and touches the screen getting it out unless one totally shuts the phone off (holding on-off button for 6 seconds). - Battery Life is OK (not great but not bad either)

Cons:
- Dual Sims aren't very useful.
- Only SIM1 is 3G capable, SIM2 is 2G only
- Camera is useless, very poor quality pictures in most situations. Mediocre pictures in good light
- Phone would lock-up if a call was made on one of the SIMs and it was ended before the other other party answered.
- Random phone radio/dialer lock-ups (phone looks like it is working but no incoming or outgoing calls)
- Random phone restarts
- Phone doesn't shutdown after a lock-up, only fix is to remove the battery

These problems were with NO 3rd party apps installed. Just what was on the phone itself.

I regret buying this phone, it would have been better to just use 2 phones rather than this phone. It was bought so we could use it when traveling internationally. The Samsung dual SIM phones all supported 3G only on SIM1 (unlike Sony, Samsung was honest and stated this in their specifications). This phone just like the Samsung phones has one 3G radio which is for SIM1 only.

In most countries 3G wouldn't matter for voice calls but if you travel to Japan or South Korea you need a 3G phone/radio, 2G doesn't work at all. Which is why I wanted a dual sim phone that supports 3G on both SIMs. I only found out of this problem while the phone was in Japan, SIM2 radio didn't work at all in Japan. This combined with the radio/dialer lock-up issue caused major problems.

This phone was used by my mother (she knows how to use an Android phone just not troubleshoot it) and she had an awful experience with it. The phone lock-up and 3G radio issues left the phone inoperable for long periods during her trip. This made it impossible to communicate since we didn't know what was happening. The phone would work sometimes and not others. We tried several SIMs thinking it was a problem with the wireless service providers. What we didn't realize was that the phone worked for a little while because the battery was taken out and put back in during SIM swaps.

This phone caused lots of stress for my mother & others trying to communicate with her during the trip and on her return. The day of her return she spent over two hours waiting at the airport after traveling for over 22 hours. Her flight was early, airport staff routed some passengers through a different terminal she thought we hadn't arrived yet and waited for us thinking we weren't at the airport yet. We arrived early as well because we saw that the flight was ahead of its schedule. We waited for her thinking customs/immigration might be taking time. We tried calling her but couldn't reach her since the phone was locked-up. She tried shutting down the phone (it never shutoff the phone was locked-up). She tried calling us but no calls went through, she thought the wireless service providers were the issue. Luckily she got tried of waiting and a couple of Good Samaritans helped her out, they called me for her so I was able to find her.

Save yourself lots of headaches and stress, don't buy this phone.

title: It comes in handy.
text: I purchased this after I switched back to my BlackBerry Z10 when I could no longer sync my Yahoo! powered emails to my BlackBerry Z30. My carrier never sold the Z30, and Yahoo's new security protocols were blocking the integration of those emails to the Z30. I knew the original battery for the Z10 was bad because it would get hot when charging, it would not charge beyond 40%, and it was swollen. This charger bundle along with a second battery that I purchased allows me to always have a charged battery available in the event the battery in the phone needs charging and I'm nowhere near a charging source. With a charged battery in the charger, this can be used to charge the battery in the phone without removing it. You'll then have a charged battery in your phone that gives you more run time. When you get to charging source, you can then charge the battery that's in the charger. Alternatively, if you're not in the middle of something that needs to be saved when your battery get low, you can remove the battery from your phone and swap it out with the battery in the charger. You can also charge both batteries at the same time by plugging the charger into your phone, plug a charge cable into the charger, then connect it to a USB port on a computer, or use a travel adapter plugged into an electrical outlet.

title: Fancy special features at the cost of the basics
text: The device is attractive and slick; the graphics are clear and easy to see. The fancy nice-to-have's like hi-res camera and transfer-by-touch are all...well, nice to have, BUT they are rendered almost useless for the purposes of anyone who wants to use Internet, if the Wi-Fi doesn't work. Surprise! the wifi doesn't work. After trying for days to connect to office and home wifis, and getting a simple message repeatedly--"failed to connect"--I searched and found dozens of forums discussing the same problem with Sony Xperias going back to 2011. Sadly all forums contain messages along similar lines..."hit and miss" (ie, works some days and not others), "can't believe Sony has not addressed this yet"...etc. I received model # LT25i, serial #CB5A1UP7B4, and I CANNOT CONNECT to any Wi-Fi to date, after a week. I can't insert a link here but BEFORE YOU BUY try Googling "sony xperia won't connect to wifi". The "solutions" offered basically assume you are an idiot who has entered the wrong password or is standing a mile away from the router, etc. I have tried it all: rebooted every component in the network; turned off potentially competing signal-emitters like Bluetooth or any other 802.11x devices, re-re-reentered the CORRECT password, tested on other devices with the same conditions...everything points to a fatal flaw in either the hardware or the protocols, and this is corroborated by other owners. The phone just won't speak to the average household or small office Cisco or Motorola router. I CAN get data from the mobile network; I CAN make a phone call (what a relief), although oddly enough the "status" shows my number as "unknown" (the phone doesn't even know the number of its own SIM!) Absolutely unacceptable in my opinion for a $300 device. Please be warned!

title: Poorly Implemented
text:
I expected more from Blackberry. The plastic of the actual case itself is barely adequate. It feels cheap, but it does the job. The cloth part of the case is junk. The cloth will get collect dirt easily if you do something as basic as putting the phone in your pocket or place it anywhere that isn't 100% clean.

I could live with what I mentioned above, but the nature of the cloth part makes the case useless for me. There is no magnet or anything to keep the case closed, so it just dangles on top of the screen. Yes, it disables the screen, which is nice, but there is nothing holding it against the screen. I saw that this case is advertised as having "magnetic flip closure." This is deceptive advertising. I now understand that they must mean the magnet that turns off the screen, which is not obvious and was to be expected anyway.

Another problem with this is that the cloth part gets in the way of your hands when you are trying to use the phone. You must fold the cloth back (which isn't as easy as you would think) in order to hold the phone somewhat securely. Even then, the cloth wrapped around the back of the phone makes it more difficult to hold and more likely to fall from your hands while in use. I have nearly dropped my brand new Z10 multiple times because of this case.

Another major flaw is that the cloth part on the front covers up the notification light, rendering that feature useless while the case is closed.

I love the idea, but it seems to have been poorly implemented here. I've already ordered another case, and as soon as it arrives, this will be going in the trash can.

title: The perfect case for me and my Z10
text:
In the short amount of time I have been using this case, I have been extremely pleased by the protection as well as the utility it has given my Z10.

First off, the level of protection is superb for my needs. I have often carried my phones in one of the front pockets of my jeans, and thus most of the phones I had used bear some scratches due to them rubbing shoulders with everything else in my pocket. This case offers excellent protection from that. The downside is that the flap of the case, especially the edges, pick up lint like nobody's business, and its suede-like material scuffs easily too, but just a few rubbings of the case with a slightly damp microfibre towel (which I have aplenty) that I do every night makes everything look new again.

I do not see any reason why the lack of a way to lock the flap in place is a disadvantage, aside from the possibility that the flap might open when the phone is accidentally dropped. The flap stays flat and closed even after extended periods of the flap being folded out of the way and/or in stand mode prior. Its auto-turn off smart function always works, lessening the drain on the battery. Also, one's hand is enough to keep the flap closed when carrying the phone. In fact, in my daily use, this is an advantage: without a way to lock the flap closed, it is easy to use just one hand to flip open the flap with a flick of the wrist, look at the lockscreen for any messages, swipe up to remove the lockscreen with the thumb of the same hand, peek into the Hub if needed using the same thumb, even open the message if needed with the same thumb, then close the flap with a flick of the wrist again.

Although some have reported that the presence of the flap makes using the phone, especially typing, less comfortable to use, I have never found this to be the case. For those who have found the flap uncomfortable while holding the phone at portrait profile, try this: hold the phone with your left pinkie in between the phone and the flap folded at the back. You will find that this will equalize the height of the left and right thumbs from the front of the phone, and even makes your hold of the phone more secure than if the flap was not there.

Fold the flap into its stand mode, and you have a handle for your left hand, perfect for holding the phone when your right hand is busy, for example reaching for that can of soup while looking at the grocery list in your phone, and even gives you a good grip when taking pictures (although I have not checked the effect on the use of the flash, which is not covered by the flap in stand mode but whose flash may still be partially obscured at the left side).

I also do not understand why people are griping that there is/are no hole/s in the flap for access to the microHDMI and microUSB ports. No holes mean protection of the said ports and no weak points for the flap where tears can happen and where lint can get attracted to. Besides, the phone looks really nice when the phone is charging at bedside mode and the flap in its stand mode.

All in all, this official Blackberry product deserves a perfect 5/5 (or maybe 4.9/5 for its attraction to scuffs and lint, and no hole to see the LED at the upper right) for providing the protection and battery longevity I need for my Z10, as well as adding to its over-all usefulness and ease of use.

title: Great genuine BB product
text:
I was waiting for the case with a little trepidation since I was not sure whether it was a genuine BB product. It was!!! Half the retail price and all the glory ain't bad.

PROS:

2. The cover is indeed magnetic and shuts off the screen when flush against it.

3. It protects the phone and protects the inputs.

4. It's white!!! It's nice to the touch and has a velvety feel to it.

CONS (sort of):

1. White is indeed white. Although it looks absolutely gorgeous, it stays white only for a few days. I have not figured out how to clean it just yet.

2. For some people, the fact that the cover doesn't have a cut out for the inputs is a downside. I don't see it that way. It's not a big deal to have the cover open when charging. As a reviewer for a Playbook pointed out, it's important to protect the inputs.

Overall, I love my cover!

title: Theoretically nice... but too many issues
text:
I am in the market for a new Blackberry Z10 case because after having this case for a little over 2 months, I have had enough with its issues.

The Good is that is fits the phone nicely, doesn't add too much bulk and has a flip cover that protects the screen... mostly.

Another (theoretically) good feature is that there is a magnet built into the cover that interacts with the traditional Blackberry magnetic "sleep" sensor so the phone goes to sleep when in a case (always standard on previous Blackberry holsters.) - This is also the cover's WEAKEST FEATURE in my opinion.

As far as quality: At first it seemed, OK. The cover material (a microfiber / faux suade material) seems nice and won't scratch the screen, however in time it frays, and becomes a bit too flimsy. The plastic case, cracks too easily... I dropped the phone twice and both times, it cracked the case in different places... The first broke a small tab that holds the cover to the phone, dislodging the phone and in the other, it just cracked the case so the phone doesn't sit tightly within anymore. - The phone didn't really get damaged, so in theory, I guess it did it's job.

My biggest complaint, however is that the cover, which as others have pointed out is too stiff when you first buy the case and doesn't stay closed - eventually breaks in and closes quite nicely. BUT THIS IS WHERE THE COVER BECOMES A PROBLEM...

The magnetic sensor automatically "wakes" the phone when you open the cover. I've had all kinds of weird sleep / wake / reset issues with the phone because of this (I'll blame BB on that) but once the cover breaks in, it no longer stays in the right place.. so when carrying the phone in a pocket, the cover seems to move around causing the phone to wake / sleep / wake / sleep, etc... This has caused my phone to freeze, but mostly, it gets hot and runs down the battery VERY QUICKLY!

Some kind of a snap-close or magnetic closure would be helpful. (Of course, the ability to disable the "wake on cover opening" feature would be nice, too - I haven't found this on the phone if it exists. - I love the idea of the screen protection, but the rest of the problems is why I'm looking at a different case to buy at this time.

title: Pricey but awesome!
text:
Does anyone really need this device? No, but it sure is nice. Normally I wouldn't even consider getting a charging pad because I don't think that enough effort is saved by not having to plug in the phone to charge it. In addition it doesn't charge the phone any faster either. So why did I spend the money to get this thing? Well... I have a Sonos system in my place, most evenings I like to lay in bed and listen to some music or podcast before turning in and I needed my phone to control the Sonos. Having the phone plugged in and sitting on my night stand oriented the phone upside down so every time I wanted to skip a song, change the volume, etc. I had to unplug the phone and replug it back in. After a few weeks I was ready to scream! So as is the case with most things... I hunted around for a better solution. The charger pad turned out to be great. Lay the phone on the charger, bloop bloop, a little alert pops up that it's charging, done! I can now grab my phone, make changes to my audio, etc, lay it back down and roll over. Same goes for calls and texts. The back cover is a little thicker but I like it better than the one that came with my S4. It makes the phone a tiny bit heavier and has less of that cheap plastic sound if you tap it with your finger nail. I think it makes my phone feel higher quality. Potentially you could run into a problem if you like a protective case or cover. Me... I've always reserved a pocket that only holds my phone so I don't need nor do I want a cover, the pocket works just fine and keeps the phone polished up and looking new.

OK so in closing... I gave this 4 stars because I think that this device (as well as other Samsung branded accessories) is way over priced and also feel that it's not a must have item.

If you want convenience and don't mind the price... go for it.

title: Great Accessory for S4 with one exception
text:
When I switched from my iPhone 5 to the all-new Galaxy S4, I knew for a fact that I wanted to take advantage of all the different additional features that the S4 offers; most notably wireless charging.

So as soon as I ordered my S4, I also went for the wireless charging kit. The product came just as described very promptly. Everything works perfectly, however if you are looking for the added convenience of just dropping your beloved S4 onto a charging pad, you should take this into precaution:

THE TIME IT TAKES FOR AN S4 TO CHARGE WIRELESSLY TAKES ALMOST 8 TIMES LONGER THAN THROUGH A CORD.

No joke, usually after a day of use, the S4 will recharge completely within an hour through a micro-USB cord. However, when you're using this kit sold by Samsung, it takes almost 8 hours for a full recharge on the battery. You might think this is a user-error, but even when I place the S4 perfectly on the mat, the charge moves just as slowly.

Although I think wireless charging is the future of the way we charge our phones, this is a poor execution by Samsung. Save your $90 and just wait for the next variation of the Galaxy S series to create a better solution for wireless charging.

I did find out that other people were having NFC issues with another third party Qi charging kit and the fix turned out to be removing the aluminum labeling. Also, there is an add-on NFC antenna kit that others have installed to make the third party charging kit work.  The S-charger back plate that came with my wireless charging kit does appear to have this additional NFC antenna integrated into it but NFC still does not work.  Not sure what I'm going to do yet but I'm considering returning the kit and gettin the much less expensive third party Qi kits.

title: Updated: Huawei big name in global market, just not in USA
text:
** Update October 2014 **

Well after about 14 months of use this phone crapped out. It was not dropped, submerged, or otherwise abused. One evening it just decided to quit. The screen started to flicker and stay on, all buttons became unresponsive, it's dead. Pulled and re installed the battery, same thing. Completely unusable.

As time went on I became less and less satisfied with this phone. It developed tremendous lag with many functions. Sometimes I would tap a name in my contact list and it would take 15 seconds or more to bring up the call screen and complete the call. Beyond that, aps would constantly bomb out. It became a very frustrating phone to use. Honestly, I wasn't all that upset when it died, at least I could look forward to something else. I can no longer recommend this phone based on the entire 14 months of use and it's death.

I found a killer deal on a refurbished LG Optimus Showtime and have been using it for a week. So far I love it. It looks and works like new. Time will tell if it ends up being a clunker like the Ascend.

I did some research on the brand, and discovered Huawei is a Chinese brand, and they are the world's 6th biggest manufacturer of cell phones. They have more market share than HTC, Sony, TCL, Blackberry, and Motorola, only slightly less than LG and ZTE, and 1/3 that of Apple. By the way, It's pronounced "WAH-way" and the 881C is a very nice phone. Don't be scared off by a brand you've never heard of. I am thinking most people will hear of them soon in the USA.

This is my 4th ST phone and my second android. My previous android was a low end LG. The experience with this phone is 3X better than the previous. So far it runs every ap smoothly, Runs Youtube videos without a glitch when signal is 2 bars or more (though there may be some buffering at the beginning). This phone runs on Verizon which is much better and faster in the area where I live, rural Michigan. I should have been on Verizon long ago.

The look and feel of this phone are quality. The 4" display is beautiful and it's a good blend; big enough screen yet still small enough to fit in a pocket. It feels thin and sleek and not bulky. While I would not claim this to rival an I-phone it does have that look and feel and a similar experience. Compared to an iphone it's 500% cheaper and almost as good in my opinion. No brainer. For the $$ you will be hard pressed to find a better bang.

Do yourself a favor and buy a micro SD card immediately (well under $10). Then go into "Settings, Storage, Default storage location" and set the SD card as the default storage location for installed aps. This will prevent you from running out of memory quickly by installing too many aps, as there is not much extra internal memory.

The only area I would appreciate a little more performance is with the battery life. The phone has a 1750 mAh battery, which is big. However, battery performance is just average. Not a deal breaker, if you want a fancy phone with the bells and whistles this is the price you pay. Having a charger in the office or car to top it off is nice to have with this phone.

We shall see how this phone does over time. My LG developed lots of bugs and glitches after a while. So far this phone has exceeded expectations. If you want a great Android on ST through Verizon this phone will not dissapoint. I doubt there currently an ST phone that delivers more bang for the buck

title: The best inexpensive smartphone that uses Verizon towers
text:
This is my first smartphone and so maybe I don't realize how bad a phone it is, but still it is not so bad as some people are making it out to be. I've been using mine for a year and a half now and it does what I need it to do. It runs the apps I've wanted to run. Browsing the web can oftentimes be slower than I'd like, but frankly I'm still in awe that it can do all that it does for 30 bucks. The voice to text feature generally works well and I'm surprised how few people make use of the feature. I've used it for GPS navigation, although I prefer my dedicated GPS navigation device. I made use of the calendar function and appreciate being able to set several reminders. I've been happy with the quality of my phone service and although there are cheaper services, there are few that use Verizon towers. There are not so many phones available if you want to use Verizon towers on Straight Talk, especially in this price range.

The biggest downside of the phone is that it can be slower than molasses at times. I haven't really compared it against other phones, but it can sometimes take 20 seconds to get out of an app and start up the phone app and get to the point where I can make a phone call. That seems excessive, but I don't make many calls so that it is not really an issue for me. Receiving calls has never been a problem. I find the sound quality is good and the speaker phone works well.

Sometimes the text messaging app won't stay open. Apparently it's not good at managing memory and I sometimes have to run a memory booster app such as Clean Master to get it to run reliably. Usually I don't have to, but when I have problems with the messaging app closing spontaneously I know it's time to run the memory booster. Also once I free up some memory the phone seems to be zippier in general. It would be great if the phone would automatically manage its memory so that this wasn't an issue.

The browser that comes with it is not very reliable. It would frequently close spontaneously and I'd have to restart it and try to get back to the desired web page, often only to have the browser crash again. That can be very frustrating. I found that there are other browsers that are much more reliable. I prefer UC Browser or CM Browser. Google Chrome works well too, but uses a tremendous amount of memory.

For some reason although it comes with 2.7 GB of storage built-in they only make 630 MB of that available for apps. I assume this is just to frustrate people to force them to move to higher end phones so they can install all the apps they want. I was running out of app storage even with moving all the apps that I could to a 32 GB SD card using the built-in function for doing that. In hindsight I should have traded in Google Chrome for a browser that used much less memory. It had gotten so I didn't have enough memory available to install updates for my various apps, especially the updates for Chrome itself. Eventually I rooted my phone and installed Link2SD which allows me to move a lot more app related data to the SD card and thus allows me to install many more apps. Now that I can install all the apps that I want without worrying about running out of memory I am MUCH happier with my phone. Unfortunately the process of rooting the phone and getting Link2SD to work properly is not a trivial one, it's great once you get it all worked out.

The touch screen works well and I've been very satisfied with the quality of the graphics. It packs a lot of pixels onto that 4" screen. I've never had problems watching streaming videos. Youtube works well both via the app and on a browser. I've used Netflix and streamed other video using browsers with no problems. I sometimes stream music using Pandora or Spotify. I've never tried video games more demanding than Angry Birds, so I can't say how it performs in that respect. If I have a good signal I can stream both with Wifi and with cellular data.

I have occasionally had problems sending and receiving picture texts. That can actually be pretty annoying. Just keep in mind that you cannot send or receive pic texts while you are on the phone. I sometimes forget this and wonder why I can't see a pic that a friend I'm talking to just sent me. I have to remember to drop the call to allow the pic to be received. It's annoying that I can't receive the pics using Wifi because I can still surf the web while on a phone call if I have wifi, but I believe this is the way the Verizon network works and is not a problem with the phone itself.

The camera is decent, but I wish it had a flash. One thing that is good about the camera is that it takes good pics of documents with normal lighting. The auto focus works well on closeup objects. This is probably not a big plus for many people, but I recently had need of taking many such pics and was pleased with the results compared to other cameras I tried.

Another thing I like about the phone is that it has an easily replaceable battery. I strongly recommend buying extra batteries and an external battery charger. This allows you to charge your extra batteries without having to keep your phone tethered to a charge cable. I like to carry one or two fully charged batteries with me so I can swap one in if the battery dies. I think it's easier to carry extra batteries than other external battery devices. The batteries are light and thin and will fit unobtrusively in any pocket. You can buy batteries for about $5 each on Amazon or Ebay. I typically can go an entire day on one battery charge with a battery that is in good condition.

Another thing regarding battery life that people should keep in mind is that if you are in an area where you have poor radio reception (one or zero bars of signal strength) you will go through batteries much faster than if you have 4 or 5 bars. This is because the radios use much more power trying to communicate with the towers when the signal is weak. When people complain about battery life you never know if it's a result of poor signals or some other issue. When I first got my phone I found that I could not go more than few hours without having to charge my battery even if I wasn't using the phone. It turned out that there was a problem with Google Play Services. After doing some research I found this was the problem and uninstalled it. They have since resolved the issue and I run it with no problems.

This is the worst phone I have ever bought! Upon losing my old Samsung I went ahead and just grabbed this off of the shelf for $200 without realizing it was a Sony off-brand. Instantly I noticed it didn't even come with an sd card! I would be out of space without even messing with it! Note here- in the DCIM folder delete the folder named '.thumbnails' and make an empty text file with the same name.

Once that was out of the way I was in business- or at least I thought I was. Turns out it's got 2 gbs of internal space that registers as SDCARD1 which causes a hell of a lot of problems. Once I rooted it I thought my worries were soon to be over. NOPE! I removed the useless bloatware apps and came up with errors for other apps (my fault there). Needless to say I redid the whole thing and froze apps one at a time through Titanium backup to make sure it didn't happen again. Low and behold it started acting up before I'd even got to that point! There has not been a firmware update since I've got it a year and a half ago (guess they think they have a solid product for some mysterious reason). Now today the Google Play Store just quit working out of nowhere.. Just a ridiculous pice of junk to say the least. I can fit about three apps on the internal memory. I chose Hangouts, the Windows 8 theme and Android Tuner Pro. Every time I install something new I immediately have to transfer it to the sd card so no fancy widgets for me! I can't do a full backup/restore because everything tries to install to the system memory and just locks up the phone. Droidsail App2SD (or similar) is a must-have if you own this phone. I can't say there's really anything good about it. I got ripped off big time.

title: For once a fast Android phone with no lag!
text:
This phone is the best straight talk phone (in the less than $400 price range) on the market. It has a great size screen, android 4.0 operating system, and a good design (no cheap plastic look/feel). One of my favorite things about the phone is they seem to have everything geared towards google instead of bing (score)!!! It runs on Verizon towers so I have great service everywhere I go. It has a 5mp camera which is good for its price range but unfortunately it does not have a flash. I recently switched from Verizon to straight talk to save money and let me tell you, this baby blows my laggy lg revolution out of the water when it comes to speed. It opens/closes apps quickly, surfs the web quickly and with no problems, and you dont get the annoying system crashes and errors android is known for. It's nice to have a phone that actually functions as a phone rather than a paperweight. It has very limited memory but if you save your apps to your sd card and get a good task killer (I use "advanced task killer" - you can set it up to automatically kill apps youre not using), it will run smoothly. The battery life is average for a smartphone but it charges pretty fast - it can go from dead to full charge in 2 hours. Another thing I love about this phone is it has a data on/off button conveniently on the pull down menu so it's not a hassle to turn the data off when im not using it (which greatly extends battery life). Overall, this phone is great and a force to be reckoned with even when compared to the most expensive phones on the market. I would recommend it to anyone who has ever wanted to smash their laggy phone against a wall.

Let's recap: Pros Android 4.0 Low price Verizon network Fast/no lag or crashes Runs netflix/hulu smoothly Google search/chrome Data on/off toggle on pull down menu Charges quickly Large screen

Cons No flash on camera Low memory - can be easily fixed by storing apps to sd card (not included) and getting a task killer

And by the way, dont pay $300 for this phone. It is only $150 on walmart.com and straight talk's website.

title: I paid for expedited shipping on Weds and received both phones on Friday * Both arrived in good condition, in high-quality packa
text:
Trying to be fair in this review; the fact that Amazon drop-shipped the 2 phones makes it even more difficult:
* Shipping: I paid for expedited shipping on Weds and received both phones on Friday
* Both arrived in good condition, in high-quality packaging
* Went to Radio Shack to purchase the Sim Cards and the manager there told me the phones were fakes because they had LCD screens, not Amoled screens
* I think the screens are great, but this has certainly put a doubt in my mind
Other Issues, which may be due to my lack of understanding or simply the software:
* Wife's phone has Chinese characters showing up that I can't seem to get rid of
* Wife's & my phones both display temperature in Celsius, and I cannot find any option of changing it anywhere
* Voice Recognition works well, but has a substantial lag
* Downloads see to be pretty slow even with 4 bars
* My phone, Google Voice Search on main screen crashes every time I try to used it, my wife's is in Chinese
* My wife's weather gadget is crashed and won't work
On the positive:
* I think the screens are great, not sure if they are Amoled or not - just bugs me if I should have a higher quality screen or not
* Now that the Radio Shack Rep has put the concern in my mind, I wonder if I also have Gorilla Glass or need to worry about scratches

So - I hope I'm not being unfair, but my Radio Shack guy seems to be extremely knowledgeable and the person he showed the screen to agreed it wasn't an Amoled. This has diffidently put somewhat of a damper on the experience. It could be that the other issues I'm having are either due to my lack of knowledge or to the software not all being original. Guess I may never know. I wouldn't care if there were absolutely no issues, but there are so it makers me wonder.

title: Excellent phone, poor camera
text: The phone, by itself is O.K., but get a micro HCSD memory card and your phone has many, many more features.  I bought the 16GB (max) card from Amazon for only a little over $7.  You can swap between the phone  and computer: music, videos, photos and ringtones.  You can even transfer all your contacts from the phone to the card, then to the computer for backup.  I use the audio editor "Audacity" on my computer.  Audacity is free. With Audacity, whatever ringtone, or alarm you want is only limited by your imagination.  Then, I use the free "GIMP" (General Image Manipulation Program) to create wallpapers (which is limited to your imagination).  The reasons I gave it only 4 stars, is that though it's a great phone, my opinion is that the camera is lousy and the manual is fair.  The camera is 2 MP.  The camera does have several features.  However, I don't like it because to get a picture that is not blurry, you have to have a super, super, super steady hand (make yourself to be a bi-pod).  The manual lacks many of the detailed features of the phone.  I learned most by playing and experimenting with it.  I love the I.C.E. (In  Case of Emergency) in the contacts area highlighted in red. Not only do I have my primary doctor, my wife and my son as contacts, there is  also a place for personal information where I list my medications and supplements, my medical allergies, my medical issues (like high blood pressure) and my medical insurance information.  In summary, I really like the phone despite it's camera quirks.

title: I like it
text:
I prefer flip phones but it seems that for several years now, the only flip models available were an afterthought in the manufacturers model lines. Any upgrade would just be newer, not better, then I found this phone. It has an external LED dot matrix display for the clock and caller ID that I can read ....without glasses.....outdoors, a really big plus for me. On the other hand, the only negative I have with this phone IS with the external display for caller ID. It's a scrolling "marquee" style and instead of just showing who's calling, it alternates a phone icon between ID's, taking twice as long to ID a call if you look at the wrong time. This is the only reason I don't rate this a full 5 stars.
The other features I really appreciate is a large font option that I can read without my reading glasses and a high frequency enhance option for the audio which really does work. The screen is nice & bright too, also viewable outdoors.
There's a lot of other features on this phone that I don't use but it has the three most important ones I've been looking for. If you text a lot, be aware that you won't be working with a full keyboard but the T9 option does a pretty good job anticipating the words you're trying for.

title: My rating is really 3.5 Stars.
text: There are only a few things I don't like about this phone; the voice command and the fact that the flip needs to remain open in order to use voice command with a Bluetooth ear piece.  I knew about the Bluetooth/Voice command issue before purchasing the phone so I won't complain about that much.  It is stupid though!  The whole purpose of using a Bluetooth with your phone, especially when driving, is to be hands free.  Duh LG!  I tackle this issue be simply leaving the phone open in a holder when driving.  Now the voice command is another story; it works poorly!  My old Motorola Krzr never gave me any issues with voice dialing.  This LG phone seems not to understand English very well.  Training it to my voice did not improve the quality of the voice command.  I will say for instance, "Call Mom."  The voice command may reply, "Call, Did you say call mom, home?"  When I reply either yes or no it doesn't seem to understand my one word reply and continues to ask me the same question repeatedly.  Or it sometimes instead replies, "Call, Did you say mom?"  When I reply yes it then replies with either, "Call mobile" or "Call home," which I have to reply yes or no since there are 2 phone numbers for my mom.  If I reply no it does not then give me the 2nd choice like my old Krzr phone did; it instead keeps asking me.  Then if I say yes it then calls the number I wanted to say no to.  It sometimes also does not recognize when I say yes.  I can then start over from the beginning with the same command, "Call mom," and the voice command will reply, "Play all," and open my music catalog.  Crazy!!!  The Bluetooth quality is also not as good as with my Motorola Krzr which came out in 2006 or 2007 I believe.  Other than these issues I like my $14.99 flip phone.

As others have noted here and at Verizonwireless there is an issue with Backup Assistant. Some have suggested the problem has been fixed, others have proposed a fix. It doesn't work on mine. I USB'd my phone to the computer, and it did update the software in the phone. Backup Assistant still didn't work. Following the directions from a user posted here at Amazon I tried to update Backup Assistant, but the phone won't connect to the web.

Fortunately, I was able to move my contacts and pics from the Convoy to the Exalt using the micro-SD card. The only issue I had was the Exalt was not finding my contacts or pics, because they were stored on the card in folders the Exalt didn't like. Using the computer I was able to move the pics from "my_pics" to "photos," and "my_contacts" to "contact."

Otherwise, the Exalt is certainly not as solid as my Convoy I, so I guess I'll get one of the hard cases available for this phone. The back cover is cheesy, and flimsy, and I was afraid of breaking it when I swapped in the micro-SD, which is under the cover next to the battery. I would certainly not plan on removing it very often.

The screen is large and bright, and compared to the Convoy I like texting much better as I can see conversation history, a new feature my Convoy didn't have. It also seems to have more menu items, so I guess I'll sit down and see what those are all about. I'm not much on the front screen. It really don't give much information, unlike my Convoy, and those LEDs are hard to read.

May yet come back and if so I will keep it as a backup. Anyway the new phone arrived in 3 days and first thing that greeted me was a series of cards on the box informing me that Verizon was no longer activating CDMA phones as of June 2018. Another card listed a series of carriers which utilize Verizon older 3G network and would activate my phone. I still tried to activate it being an existing Verizon customer who had just lost a phone that was working fine on their network very recently. Tried online first but received standard message about CDMA phones not being supported anymore. So then I went on the web and found the only real answer to the issue. Do it on the phone using *288 and then following instructions.Worked like a charm and Verizon even backed up my data from the backup cloud. Only thing I lost was the pics since I wasn't using an SD card. Was so happy to get my new phone up and running I bought a TurtleBack leather case for it since I was always dropping my last phone which wasn't armored (see above).

9/18/2015- coming back to change to a one star - I am now unequivocally, absolutely, and totally fed up - and am now at the point where, after the SIXTH FACTORY reset in only three to four months of having owned it, that I am absolutely 100% comfortable in saying this is without a doubt, THE BIGGEST PIECE OF S*** PHONE I HAVE EVER OWNED SINCE 1993 - NO JUST THAT, BUT THE BIGGEST, MOST EXPENSIVE PIECE OF S*** PHONE I HAVE BOUGHT!!! I am so fed up - and now with a father who was just diagnosed with cancer, I have even LESS THAN ZERO TOLERANCE for missing any calls - and I'm still paying on this piece of s*** phone, but I just can't do it anymore... this is ABSOLUTELY IN-EXCUSABLE...

I AM COMPLETELY REMISS IN THAT I EVEN HAVE TO GIVE IT A ONE STAR; yes it is water resistant to an extent; mine got dunked in the pool for a couple seconds, is okay; and I am not freakin out when it gets wet in the rain, and it is pretty and did withstand a flight out of my Jeep going 10 miles an hour; BUT, HAVING TO DO SIX FACTORY RESETS AND LOSING ALL MY FREAKIN DATA OVER AND OVER IN ONLY THREE TO FOUR MONTHS... NAH... NO... NOT HAVING IT ANYMORE.... DISGUSTING!!!
*************************************************************
Had to come back in to change the number of stars to one because after this morning, I am done. I am so fed up. This has got to nearly be the worst purchase I have ever made. I am so irritated at this point I can't even see straight! My prior post described how I too was getting no signal found when I got this Samsung Galaxy S4 Active and had missed five calls from my mother and father telling me she had gone to the ER and been admitted to the hospital. Although the company's customer service was prompt to contact me off line at my personal email address to advise me to try a factory reset, one, I shouldn't have had to do a factory reset on a phone after only 48 hours, but, it did work, and I hadn't had much data saved at that point and hadn't performed the Samsung Synch yet. Because it such a pretty phone and I really was looking for a water resistant phone, I didn't want to give up on it. The factory reset did work, and has worked since then. And since then, I have synced all my data from my SIII to the new S4 Active and downloaded more. HOWEVER, this freakin thing JUST LOST SERVICE AGAIN!!!! I noticed a rather quiet day yesterday and mid-day notice the infamous circle with a slash through it indicating no signal... I tried taking the battery out but it didn't go away right away. At some point I did get some reception, but not internet, and my 4G never came back on... eventually got the slashed circle back and tried the battery trick again... eventually I just went to bed figuring it would work its way out by morning... NOT come morning I STILL had NO SIGNAL! I tried rebooting and taking the battery out several times but to no avail which means I had no other choice than to do a FACTORY RESET AND LOSE ALLLLLL MY FREAKIN DATA!!!!! The only reason I can give it even a one star at this point is because this pretty baby survived a flight out the Jeep going 15 miles an hour on to a busy highway in morning rush hour with mere scratch here and there and a couple of chips around the frame. I am heartbroken and beyond pissed at the same time! I really had gotten to be quite fond of this darling, but this having to constantly do Factory Resets is COMPLETE BS! The only person I can recommend this to at this point is someone who just needs an expensive burner phone and doesn't need to store any contacts or want to play any games or download any apps; because YOU WILL LOSE THEM WHEN YOU TOO HAVE TO DO A FACTORY RESET.

title: Nokia Lumia 1520 & Windows Phone 8.1 Are Awesome!!
text:
I've had an iPhone, and I've had a Galaxy Note 2. Prior to that I had older Windows phones and Blackberry's. I was very close to buying the Note 4 when it comes out but I started looking closely at the Nokia Windows phones. I tested one out too at a local store. I was really impressed. I never really cared for iOS, and Android was starting to bore me. 99% of the apps I use are still there. So I made the plunge and I'm glad I did.

First off, the construction of the phone is great. It is sturdy and well made (i.e. it won't bend and break like an iPhone 6) and the screen is gorgeous. And big. I was really amazed at the graphics quality. Windows phone is easy to customize. It's true that it takes you some time, but so do other phones. If you invest about an hour, it's more than enough to make it yours. Setup was easy too. The camera is by far the best on a phone, and better than my wifes stand alone camera. The pictures it takes are amazing. As far as assistants go, Cortana is much better than Siri. It's on par with Google now, maybe a little bit better. Then there's the apps. It's true, it does not have as many as Android or Apple. But what it does have are good apps. And all the common ones are there.

What don't I like about it? Two things, but not enough for me to subtract a star:
1. There is no text syncing to your computer app like Mighty Text or Air Droid (or imessage for that matter). I don't believe there are plans for one either. I must admit I do miss this, but I just keep the phone close instead.
2. It has one speaker. A phone this big and powerful should have 2. The sound quality is great so not such a big loss.

I really recommend that if you are shopping for a new phone, to give this phone and other Windows phones a good look. It is also (through Amazon) $200 or more less than the Note series Android phones. Do I miss the s-pen stylus? Nah. Just check out these phones. I almost discounted them but I wound up making the switch. BAttery life is pretty good. I've used it heavily all day from 430 am and the battery is at 74%. Not bad.

title: REALLY big phone, lots to love!
text:
This phone is really big. I really love it but I do feel a little self conscious pulling it out of my pocket to answer a call. I can fit it in my pockets of both my dress slacks for work and my jeans. I carry it in the left hip pocket and it fits well and does not bother me when I sit down.

Having said that about the size, the other side of it is that the screen is awesome. Reading articles, watching videos and even texting are so cool on the big screen.

Other reviews have gone into great detail so I will keep it pretty high level here. I upgraded from the Samsung Focus, a first Generation Windows Phone 7. The operation of WP8 is great. It has all the things I love about WP but has added more features as well. The quad-core processor is really fast and makes taking multiple pictures in a row work rather quickly with very little lag time (I read a review of the Lumia 1020 that said it takes about 6 seconds to load between shots). The updated Nokia Camera app is really cool. It allows for a lot of manual settings if you want to play with your shots and be more creative. Using more than one of the features will slow down your set up time but it does allow you great control over your exposure which I really like. It will likely take just a little practice to get very proficient with these manual settings.

The Nokia apps are some of the best apps on this phone and they come standard. Nokia Radio allows you to create a playlist (similar to creating a radio station on Pandora) and then download the playlist so that you can play it offline. I now have playlists that I can listen to at the gym without having to stream music and use all my data. I removed most of the AT&T apps because the Nokia apps do the same things even better.

I am really enjoying this phone. If they offered the same phone in a 5 inch screen I likely would have gotten that one instead, but having such a big screen has a lot of benefits too. I haven't even touched my Kindle Fire since I go this phone because it operates as my tablet now too.

title: Big phone, beatiful screen, great OS
text:
I have been a windows phone user for 4 years and have seen it slowly get better and better with each release. I can finally say that, feature wise, it is on par with Android and IOS. That is not to say that it doesn't have shortcomings, it does, but overall it is a feature rich OS with a clean, fresh look. There are very few "missing" app on the platform, but any apps that are on WP usually have a superior look and feel to their Android, or IOS counterparts.
As far as the phone, Nokia makes the best WP8 phone out there. I have had HTC, and tried Samsungs WP8 phones. I now own a Nokia 920, 1020, and 1520. They are all top notch mobile devices. The 1520 is huge. It has a large 1080p screen that is both bright and clear. Having larger hands, I had no problem holding it and typing with one had, although it is a stretch when typeing long text messages. You will definitely find yourself using two hands.
MS has one of the best on screen keyboards out of any of the leading OSes. Add to that kids corner, Onenote (and Office), and you have a winning combination.

For someone who is checking email, or on the internet more than talking on the phone, the large screen size was perfect for me. When I am on the phone, I usually use hands free, so I rarely hold it up to my face. I cant really comment on how comfortable that is.
The screen is also easily visible in bright sunlight, a big plus.
The device is soft to hold and comes in bright colors, like the red one I purchased. It has scratch resistant glass and I have not had a scratch that you can see on the body yet after multiple months of use without a case.

This is the phone to get if you want a true multi-media powerhouse.
It may not be great for those looking for a compact device, or have small hands and like "single handed" use.
I added 32Gs of expandable storage so I can have all of my music in one place.
Which brings me to one of the downsides. Xbox music. On W8, it is currently kind of a mess. It works, and at times works really well, but when it doesn't work, it is completely useless. There are times when music playback just stops after every song. Or time when Xbox music refuses to work when you don't have a good cellular/wifi connection. I have been an Xbox music user for a while, and the WP8 app is disappointing. Hopefully, they will improve on it soon.

Keep in mind, WP 8.1 is due out in April, which will add amny new features to the OS. It should really make this phone shine more than it already does.

title: I love this phone
text:
This is the first smartphone I have ever had. Originally, I was reluctant to join the hype about the Iphone and other smart phones. I didn't need one and was doing fine without it. But when the Lumia phones with their impressive photographic capabilities came around I really got curious and started to investigate more. At the same time Windows 8 hit the stores. Again I was very happy with Windows 7 and did not see a need to upgrade. One more thing kept me away from a smartphone was the size. The digital keyboards seemed to small for my large and old fingers. The Lumia 1520 seemed to address all my concerns. It had a good size, beautiful screen, and was compatible with Windows, both 7 and 8. So I finally decided to accept the ATT offer for a 1520. I might still get the 1020 as a second phone because of its 41 Mpixel camera.
Not ever having used a smartphone I am still working on getting acquainted with its possibilities which seem endless. I am impressed with the fact that I can now use the the smartphone on my home WIFI with both my laptop and my desktop. The fact that I can carry all the websites on it just like on my computers is a real plus for me. I am still working on getting a grasp of the potential of facebook.
All in all I am very excited about this product and would recommend anyone to look into it.

title: Love my Lumia 1520
text:
I have been an Iphone user for years and years. I first own the Iphone 3GS and moved on to the 4. I held out for as long as I could using the Iphone 4 and it was difficult for me to make a decision what the next step was in regards to a new phone. While I never jumped on the bandwagon with the Iphone 5, I was going to wait until the 6 plus came out. After several months reading reviews, looking at specs and images taken by each camera I was still not convinced. The main reason for an upgrade to a new phone was for a better portable camera. I finally took a leap of faith to experience something new and different. I am not a huge fan of Windows for the PC, but decided that the camera was my main focus. I am not all about the few nano seconds quicker one phone is over another. I am not concerned with all of the bells and whistles. I just want a great camera.

I am very happy I switched. The Lumia 1520, though big, is the right size for me. I love the tiles as opposed to little thumbnail icons. The camera is top notch. There are no disappointments here. The images are clear, vibrant and large. Don't get me wrong, the Iphone takes great images too, but the overall feel of this phone is just what I was looking for. There are some nice choices when it comes to color dynamics and the zoom is a great feature. There are a lot of similar characteristics to the Samsung line and those familiar operating such will also be comfortable with the operation of this phone.

Just wanted to let others know that Lumia does put out a good quality phone and for those thinking/contemplating about switching to a Lumia, its worth the risk.

title: Nice Phone

title: Personal Tech Finally Matches The Sci-Fi Promise
text:
It was a great phone before the Windows Phone 8.1 upgrade. Now with the upgrade, this is such a good phone, I stopped using my work supplied android phone even at work. I have my calls forwarded to my Nokia because it is sooo much better than the android phone. Windows has hit its groove with the phone operating system. And now that this syncs better with my Windows 8 tablet, they have become extentions of each other. People are takey aback by the phones size until they see me zipping through the apps and when I show pictures they can actually appreciate the photos on a screen that is almost the size of the 5x7 photos we used to go to a photo-mat to develop and share. The camera has amazing detail, and the best intuitive controls for adjusting the picture when needed. The video is smoother than my old android videos that had a hard time capturing when moving the phone around. No such problem with the Nokia 1520. And back to the size, it is bigger yes. Which is wonderful when in use. I had been worried about putting the thing in my pockets, no problem there. It has a big screen, but it is thinner than the android phones and that balances the big screen. I have no problem carring it around all day.

The Bluetooth syncs better than my androids too. I can go from my earphones to my car to my pool speaker without having to open up the controller to connect. And in my car, and with my earphones, the new assistant with the Windows 8.1 will automatically ask you if you want incomming texts read. After reading the text to you, you can ask it to reply and the word recognition for voice operated replies is great. I have coworkers who are amazed by the way it works when they see it in action in the car. My phone stays in the pocket and my eyes on the road, but I stay connected to people trying to reach me.

This is just the coolest and most practical version of a pocket sized do it all device I have ever known.

title: Great Technology, limited apps, Bing button very irritating
text:
I preordered the 1520 because of the chip, screen and camera. This is my first Windows phone since the HTC Tilt which was top of the line when purchased. My previous phone was Android. I chose this over the Samsung Note 3 because I preferred the better camera to the S pen.
The good
The phone is speedy and easy to use: The screen is beautiful! I have not really put the camera through its paces, but I took a couple of test shots of my laptop keyboard in dim light and every speck of dust showed! This bodes very well for the camera.
I had no trouble downloading Skype (which works on wifi!), Kindle, Audible , Google, Tune in Radio and Netflix. They work almost as well as on my Kindle Fire HD. I hope that Amazon will develop a full set of apps for all platforms.
It did not take long to set up ( similar to Android in many ways).I added a 32G SDHC card I had lying around the house. When (and if ) it gets full, I will upgrade to 64G. It may seem strange in this day and age, but I appreciate the FM radio which uses a speaker cable or headset cable as an antenna. My kitchen is a dead zone for Wifi and until I can solve the problem, the radio is a plus. It also saves data usage on the street at times.
The challenges
First of all when I hold the phone in my left hand, my fourth finger sits right on the on/off/sleep button and I have put it into sleep mode on several occasions. As a quick fix for my very small hands I tried to turn it upside down (with the headset port on the bottom), but even with the screen unlocked, I could not make that happen. I can get landscape mode in either direction, but only portrait mode one way, unlike my android devices.
Since I am not a heavy app user, I did not do my app homework very well. I found that Barnes and Noble had not developed a Nook app for the Windows phone (yet?) Also Pulse News is missing from the app store, although Fuse is not too bad as a substitute. Acorntv has not developed an app for any device. It would be nice if a Windows phone would play Flash.

Addendum:21 Dec

I have now taken off one star because of the Bing "button." It is both unnecessary and too sensitive. Too many times while holding the phone, my finger has brushed it by accident and the Bing Search screen appeared and shut off whatever I was doing. It could be just because my hands are small, but if I could I would disable the button so I could have the real estate at that corner. I would rather have Bing as an icon/app (or not at all). I am going to the Att help center tomorrow to see what can be done although I doubt there is a fix.

I was promised a free case from Microsoft but they were out when I picked up my phone. I will also go over the the Microsoft store tomorrow to pick one up. I have not had cases on my other smartphones, only on tablets. A downside of the 1520 is the limited number of cases available. No really nice leather options.

title: Excellent Phone - Excellent, Courteous Seller
text:
Shortly after arriving, my phone began to have a few hiccups. But, it's fully under warranty so I sent it off to Nokia Care for repair.
Two weeks later, I now have a like-new phone for an excellent price. Couldn't be happier. I'm not a cell-phone junkie so I was easily able to live without it while it was being serviced; others may have a problem, here.

The seller, BayShine, was more than willing to offer me an exchange or refund. But, I love the phone and didn't want to have to search for yet another (this was a replacement phone, already). So, sending it off to Nokia was a not an issue, for me, and now I have a phone that appears to be brand new. Save for the identification numbers (IMEI, etc.), this phone IS brand new: new screen; new body shell; likely all new internals and it works great.
So, don't be afraid to step out on what appears to be a limb, with this one. The price is right and the phone is likely still under warranty - don't be afraid to use it, you'll be more than glad that you did!

[Update] - 2 years later, the battery swelled up like a balloon. Had to toss it in the trash as I was afraid it would explode like a Note.

title: Review from an AVID iphone user and former Windows 7 Lumia 920
text:
First I will say that windows 8 is AMAZING. I had the Nokia Lumia 920 and likes a lot of the personalization features but it lacked my Pandora, pinterest, myfitnesspal, Spotify, and other apps I use daily so I went back to IPhone.

NOW, Onto the Lumia 1520. I had the IPhone 4S. I liked a lot about my iphone but was bored. Seems like since Steve Jobs passing...theres nothing awing about new phones 5, 5c and 5s. Same ol Same ol EXCEPT now...a lot of my apps are always crashing. My wifi isn't that strong in my room, my front camera quit...and it's almost the same as the first iPhone. A lot of good changes but not very many customization features for me. Plus with apple products...EVERYTHING costs.

BEFORE PURCHASE: I decided to get Nokia Lumia 1520 BECAUSE

1. Supposedly had many of the apps that I previously could not get on my old Nokia
2. More customization with Windows 8
3. Beautiful Big Screen Like a Tablet
4. Amazing Camera by Carl Zeiss
5. Mostly...Side by Side comparison that I did with IPhone 5c, 5s and Lumia 1020.
(if you can do this side by side comparison which I did on AT&T...I would do it because it answers a lot of questions and made my decision 100%)
6. Ability to Expand storage with the miniSD port
7. Ability to get phone in yellow. It was a hard decision between yellow and red because they are both beautifully vibrant but I went with yellow because I love the brighter.

UNBOXING:
Amazed by color brightness, screen brightness, size and beautiful camera.

In the first few days I learned a few more awesome things

1. the Lumia now does SnapShot and if you are or have been an iPhone user this is awesome.
2. There is a driving mode you can set up with a Bluetooth device to avoid wrecks. No touching phone while driving.
3. Some of the apps that were previously said not to be on the windows phones were now there. In face the only thing I do not have that I used a lot was weight watchers...they just have a rinkidink calculator but im sure that will update.
4. I can trim videos.
5. The live tiles are awesome.

Apps that I use a lot that are available that on some reviews were said not to be

Pinterest
Spotify
Rdio
Instagram
Amazon
Allrecipes
Netflix
Pandora
MyFitnessPal
App folder (to organize all your apps like IPhone)
FREE RINGTONES...NO MORE PAYING FOR THAT CRAP
KidsCorner
Wallet to store credit cards
Run the Map

Vine
YouTubeHD

I have had this less than a week so I know I will learn more and I will rereview or add to it but my current Conclusion is

If you are looking to upgrade and thinking about trying something new...better camera...more customization with out sacrificing simplicity...live tiles...mostly free apps...free ringtones...driving mode...no sacrificing your current apps, free office, ability to back up on skydrive and at&t locker....find your phone...ANNNND SOOO MUCH MORE...

SWITCH! You wont regret it.

Things to know:
1. This phone is huge...6 inches. I LOVE IT...some do not. I can see everything beautifully.
2. Get a CASE! SERIOUSLY This phone is very slippery on the back. You need some kind of protection and grip to prevent dropping it or if you do to help protect from the fall. *Be carefully applying tight cases...do not press hard on display screen because you can easily distort color on display screen*
3. GET A SCREEN PROTECTOR...I recommend armor brand. They have lifetime warranty and less than 10 bucks with amazon free prime shipping.
4. If you want smaller phone..you might try Nokia Lumia 1020...better camera and smaller but lacks some of the specs 1520 has. Do side by side comparison.

title: This phone is awesome! I know it is a bit of a ...
text:
This phone is awesome! I know it is a bit of a "dated" phone, and the new iPhones are out now, but this is still a far better phone/phablet. I am upgrading (or downgrading in terms of the camera) from a Lumia 1020. I lost 20mp in the camera, but honestly the 1020 was so slow on processing each picture after being taken, that I'm happier with the lower resolution and more picture options. The 1020 also runs very hot when playing games or under high usage, whereas this 1520 stays relatively cool keeping the speed at top. Dont get me wrong, I loved my 1020 especially for taking nice high red photos and being able to upload them to my computer in .raw format, I will miss that, but I think I'll just buy a good digital camera to fill that void.

All that being said, the pros of this phone are too many to even list. The size can be a bit awkward at first but you get used to it pretty quick. There really wasn't anywhere else for them to put the buttons, my only beef is I accidentally launch the camera a lot (but you can disable it!). Super awesome that they give the ability to take a video just by holding down the camera button and not having to switch to video mode (1020 doesn't have that feature!). Also the camera tracks a lot faster, picture taking and loading times are super fast. Games look beautiful and run smooth on the nice HD display. Video playback is awesome (via Hulu plus and Netflix). How awesome is it also that you can add an SD card up.to 64gb? Couldn't do that on the 1020 and with large picture file size, THAT was an issue for me.

Ok now for my cons...

This may be just my phone and I may need to have it serviced or replaced, but changing screen orientation has a major lag time. It takes a good 6-7 seconds before it changes, and sometimes I have to.shake the phone a bit to get it changed.
Speakers aren't the greatest when watching videos, maybe I'm missing a setting here but I'm only getting mono sound not stereo (there appears to be two speakers but sound only comes from the bottom one and it faces rear, which makes watching a video without headphones annoying).
There are no other cons. I am a long time WP user, and have had an HTC HD7, Lumia 920, 1020, and now the 1520. WindowsPhone OS is hands down the most user friendly and most customizable. People complain the app store is lacking, but that is no fault of Microsoft's, it is on the app developers. Lumias are also hands down, without a doubt, the MOST durable phones out there. I ran my 920 over with my mini van, and it didn't get but a small scratch on it. I have dropped both my 920 and 1020 more times than can count, typically off my lap out of my minivan, sometimes off the top.of my minivan as well. My husband works in construction, and also has a 1020, and has dropped his off the 6th story scaffolding to the concrete below, with NO HARM TO THE PHONE (granted he does have a speck shock absorbing case on it). Both of our phones still functioned like new after all that abuse (never cracked a screen either).

Someone said something about the weight of this phone being heavy, but honestly compared to the 920 and 1020 this thing is light as a feather!

title: Awesome phone with a few flaws
text:
Out of the box I absolutely fell in love with this phone. The 6" display is awesome and great for movies or just viewing pleasure in general. I thought it was rather simple to set up out of the box, however the microsoft app store is very limited. A lot of apps that I used on a daily basis were not offered my credit union, adp, candy crush saga, credit karma to name a few. The phone is customizable compared to an iPhone, but not as flexible as an android.

The flaws with the phone were that on my first phone: about 3-4 days after my buyers remorse period the phone began to stop charging, then the phone did an update and started charging again. At this point ATT had already sent a replacement phone. Then a few days later it started freezing up and needed manual hard resets, which was getting annoying. So I received the second phone which was a warranty phone that has been hand tested by ATT staff and it is still freezing up.

After both of these cases I made the decision to say the heck with Nokia products all together, and get a samsung galaxy S4. I also had problems with charging and connectivity with the nokia lumia 2520 tablet.

I rated this product with 3 stars because the phone truly is awesome as far as display, camera, and battery life are concerned. There just seems to be some other issues with the phone. I guess this can happen a lot, as an ATT staff member told me that only 1 in 1,000 phones are actually tested out of the factory.

I was leery of the device since it has only been out on the market in the US for about a month, but hopefully other consumers will have better luck with this product, as I continue to have flawless equipment with Samsung, I think I will stick with Samsung.
