title: My favorite phone
text:
I have been using/working on smartphones since the initial blackberry/windows mobile days. During that time I have pretty much used every platform (ios 4 forward, android gingerbread forward, windows phone 6.1 forward, blackberry) as my primary phone at least for a few weeks doing competitive comparison.

In the end, since windows phone 7, I have always come back to windows phone. I really just prefer the glance-ability, good ms exchange integration, web experience, reduced number of clicks to do the same thing, stability, battery life, etc.

As such, I have tried a lot of different windows phones over the years and this phone is my favorite. The screen is amazing, the battery life is awesome, the call quality is outstanding, the ringer is extra loud (I can actually hear it in my pocket when there is background noise). Many may make fun of the "giant" screen, but they haven't used it - now whenever I hold an iPhone it feels like a toy in comparison.

Overall, I simply love this phone and would highly recommend anyone willing to let go of their app collection (that they never use) and give this phone a try. After a few weeks I doubt you'll want to go back.

title: it's really fun getting your screen to be exactly how you like ...
text:
Second Windows Phone, upgraded from Lumia 900. The 6 inch screen is a little daunting at first but you get over it quickly and you soon find all other screens pitiful and small. I was deciding between large and thin, or smaller and thicker (there is another lumia with comparable specs but smaller screen/thicker. I can't remember the model number off the top of my head). I went for the large and thin. It's a pleasure to hold.

With such a large real estate for pins, it's really fun getting your screen to be exactly how you like it. With the new 8.1 update this phone just got (faster than all other windows phones, I might add), you can make your pins have one unified background picture. Like a puzzle made out of pin pieces. Hard to explain but cool once you see it.

Windows Phone OS is underrated. You can really glance at your phone and determine whether or not you need to actually pick it up. You can read your latest text right on the screen. See your friends' pictures scroll throughout the phone. All the apps you actually use and need are available. This phone has been perfect for my needs. I love having separate email pins: one for work, one for my spam account.

If you can't decide if a windows phone is right for you, find out what apps you really use and see if the marketplace has it.

title: I like the phone, but after a few months I am seeing signs of a sub-par refurb
text: I do like this phone, BUT - the particular seller I purchased from sent me one that I believed to be used/open box, but after using it for a few months it was obviously refurbished.  The screen has a bunch of white spots now (common problem so this alone isnt really an indication) and it cracked in three places without any dropping or impacts.  The microphone was very muffled and the screen is starting to pop out of the body on one side (I can see the backlight shining through the gap).  If the screen was gorilla glass as original I fully believe that it would have taken a lot more to crack it, and the other issues point to shoddy re-assembly. title: It's the Phone. It's Nokia! It's Windows Phone 8. And for me, it's Straight Talk too!
text:
I've been using Nokia phones since the early cell phone days. I have looked at and demoed many other phones, but until last year I have been primarily a Symbian OS person. Over the years, Nokia has produced an incredible line of business-type phones. These came with great media software for my audio books (simply drag & drop - I did not want to get into iTunes, just let me use Mp3s), incredible cameras, great synchronization software for Microsoft Outlook, and a primitive version of Microsoft Office. My latest Nokias supported 32GB & [[ASIN:B009QZH6JS SanDisk Ultra 64 GB microSDXC Class 10 UHS-1 Memory Card 30MB/s with Adapter SDSDQU-064G-AFFP-A]] cards. I carried a ton of stuff around with me, dozens of audiobooks and other audio content. Along the way, I graduated to the [[ASIN:B0088MUV3I Nokia 808 PureView Unlocked GSM Phone with 41MP Camera with Carl Zeiss Optics and Symbian (Belle) OS - Black]], which I got at a steal. It had the Nokia Belle OS, which I thought was great. It was a super phone, the best I had owned. I had no desire to change or to replace it until I fell asleep in my recliner, it dropped into the "mechanics," and getting up, I completely destroyed it. The price to replace it was steep and it looked as if support for Belle would not last very far into the future. Nokia was going Windows! I was not sure I liked that. I looked into all the top name phones. It seemed that people were getting tired of the iPhone. I wasn't crazy about the Samsungs or others. I simply wanted a business phone, like I've used over the years. I had received a Kindle fire HD as a gift, entered the "app" world and found these tools incredible. I found myself carrying this around with me and my Nokia 808. I had also switched my service to Straight Talk (see: [[ASIN:B00BD4BLM8 Straight Talk AT&T Micro Sim iPhone 4, 4s, Galaxy S3]]), working with AT&T towers (and for a year has cost me $42 a month with unlimited everything).

All my research, and it was comprehensive (you can start from the phonearena site and go from there), was pointing to the Windows Phone 8. I wasn't too sure I wanted to go that way. At the same time, most Windows phones were Nokia brands with similar, familiar hardware and capabilities. However, few of these, those that were GSM phones, supported MicroSD cards. Yet, I came across one phone I liked that did, the [[ASIN:B00H4F9WDA Nokia Lumia 822 GSM Unlocked + Verizon CDMA 4G LTE Windows Phone - Black]] which was both a Verizon CDMA 4G LTE, but also Unlocked for any GSM network. They seemed to be selling cheaply everywhere. I picked one up used and cheap, threw in my SIM card and was amazed. It was a great and powerful phone. It did not support AT&T 4G or LTE bands, but did everything else quite well. This is where I tested the Windows Phone 8 environment and fell in love with it. There were other great phones that were available, like the [[ASIN:B00DVRJ3WA Nokia Lumia 1020, Yellow 32GB (AT&T)]], but they did not support MicroSD cards. Back then, once satisfied with Windows and wanting to go to 4G/LTE, I set my sights on the Nokia Lumia 1520 (RM-940 Version), which supports the AT&T LTE700 (B17), LTE1700/2100 (B4) Bands and the 3G/4G 850 Mhz which are used by Straight Talk (and work well - be careful there are a lot of the RM-937 International Versions for sale out there which use different frequencies). Over a number of months, a number of sites were doing searches for me for an "unlocked" version of this phone. When the price was right, I bought it in this matte yellow finish. I am more than happy with it. The only CON I have is that AT&T gutted 16GB of the 32GB this phone can support internally, but it looks like I may never need it, the apps are quite efficient. This now is the best phone I've owned. I won't be looking for another anytime soon. Remember, it's not just the phone, it's also Windows Phone 8, and for me Straight Talk too! Note: it takes a Nano SIM card. I had to cut mine, but it was not a problem (see: [[ASIN:B009AQJNCQ QQ-Tech® Newest Noosy Black 2in1 Nano Sim Card Cutter & Micro Sim Cutter for iPhone 5, iPhone 4, 4S and other Phones + QQ-Tech® Sim Card Adapters Pack]]).

It does everything every Nokia phone I have owned has done and more, including having the 2nd best camera around. Some people say it's large, but it's not if you are used to carrying a Kindle around with you. This has a Kindle App and takes its place now. It has just about every other app you would want, comes with Mobile Office, great free GPS, a quad processor, a monster battery and an incredible screen. It fits in any of my pockets, even with a flip case ([[ASIN:B00GQM1ZJQ Poetic FlipBook Case for Nokia Lumia 1520 Black (3 Years Manufacturer Warranty from Poetic)]] which I recommend). The Live Tiles are incredible. The ease of use puts other phones to shame. I have six other friends right now who have switched to the Windows Phone 8 world in the last two months from just seeing my satisfaction and knowing the research that I did. They are all Verizon customers and have gone to the Nokia Lumia 822. They could not be happier.

You may not be looking for a Nokia Lumia 1520 right now. I do not think you would go wrong with it. You might, however, want to try the Windows Phone 8 world like I did. Should you try, you might be surprised as I was. Then you will be ready to choose which of the phones in that world would be the best investment for you. It might take a two-step process as it did with me. It might take having some fun with all of this!

title: Great camera - but it's no iPhone.
text:
UPDATE: After owning this phone for another couple of months, I still don't feel very comfortable with it. I wish I would have waited a few months for the newer/bigger iPhone - that's just my subjective opinion as someone who came from an iPhone to try out the Nokia Lumia.

I would like to also let you know that there was one issue with the camera. It developed a black spot right in the middle of the sensor. The good news is that a trip to the Microsoft store solved the problem, as they took a quick look at the issue, and replaced the unit on the spot.

If you have this phone and have any problem with it, don't waste your time by calling anyone, or going online - that was a waste of time, and very frustrating. Just go to the Microsoft store and get your problem taken care of without the headache. If you live too far from a Microsoft store to make the trek, I feel sorry for you.

I first took the phone to the AT&T store, and they told me I should seek help online. They couldn't even give me a phone number to call, just the general advise to look online for support. I thought that was kind of crappy, but I decided to call my AT&T corporate representative the next day (I have a business account with 7 mobile lines), and sadly, even my representative told me the same thing. Neither of them thought to advise me to check with the Microsoft store.

So, I searched online and could not find any real help. I first tried Nokia's online support maze of questions and answers that went nowhere, before searching for a support phone number, which I never found - not even after answering their automated questions and responding that they did not solve my problem. I finally found the support phone number on an obscure recall notice for a Nokia tablet charger, using a Google search for "Nokia support phone number".

When I called, I was routed to a call center in the Philippines, and spoke with a friendly lady who worked off of a scripted flip book to try and solve my problem. I patiently went through all of the steps she suggested (even though I had zero confidence that anything short of changing the phone would help, because I was sure the problem was with the camera sensor), until she had no more pages in her flip book, and no more ideas to try. She put me on hold 3-4 times after the flip book ran out of suggestions, and I assume was speaking with someone else about the problem - each time for about 5 minutes. Her next suggestion was that I ship the phone back to the national repair center in Texas, and in 7-10 business days I would hear back from them.

I explained to the nice lady that I use the phone for business, and being without a phone for 7-10 days was not an option, and if she could not help me, then I would like to speak with a supervisor. This was after about 15 minutes on hold waiting for someone to talk to me, and then another 30-45 minutes on the phone with her. She put me on hold again, and when she came back said that the supervisor was not available, but would call me back in 2-4 business days. That call was returned today, after over a week I finally received a call back that went to voice-mail as I was busy at the time. By then I had already solved the problem, so I haven't followed back up with Nokia.

Anyways, after getting off the phone with Nokia's call center, I remembered that Microsoft bought the phone division of Nokia some time ago, and decided to try and call the Microsoft store. Even though I called the local number for the Microsoft store, I was routed to the Microsoft call center. The person on the phone told me that yes, Microsoft does handle issues for Nokia phones, and that all I need to do is send it in to the Nokia national repair center in Texas and wait 7-10 business days! I again asked if they have any type of exchange program because I can't be without a phone for that long, but was told that their policy is to handle these types of issues through the national repair center, and they don't have any way to send me a replacement before they examine the phone - not even a loaner. After insisting that there must be a better solution, I asked what would happen if I just drove to the physical Microsoft store to inquire about a resolution - because the person at the call center would not let me speak directly with someone at the physical store. The call center rep said that maybe they would replace the phone in the store, if they had a direct replacement in stock, and if they determined that it was DEFINITELY an issue with the phone that would ultimately require replacement.

So, anyways, I called back and made an appointment with the automated system, and went to the Microsoft store closest to me - not a short trip, but better than going to Texas. The experience in the physical store was completely different - actually pleasant (notwithstanding the long drive). The rep in the store took one look at the device, and went to the back and brought me out a brand new replacement phone and set it up for me.

After I told the in-store rep about my odyssey to arrive at his counter, he told me that their in-store policy is to make customers happy, and anything they can do in the store - even give a different phone, if the original one is not available, is one of their options. (actually, they give you a credit for the list price of the phone, and let you get another one of equal or lesser value)

So, in summary, the phone is still so-so for me overall; the customer service from Nokia is TERRIBLE, and the customer phone service from Microsoft is not very good, but the customer service in the physical Microsoft store was as good or better than I have received at the Apple store.

One other observation I have is that many reviewers give the phone rave reviews, and 5 stars, but do not even mention any of the obvious shortcomings of the device/operating system. I think many of these reviews must be by fans of the phone and/or operating system; not really objective reviewers of the items they are purporting to review.

****** Original Review: *****
Before getting an iPhone 4, then a 4s, then an iPhone 5, I loved the Nokia phones of yesteryear - great call quality, long battery life, and simply indestructible.

However, my first smartphone was an iPhone 4 - I was a late adopter of smartphones - and I absolutely fell in love with it. I later got an iPhone 4s for my wife, then an iPhone 5 for myself and handed down the iPhone 4 to my son. So I have a lot of experience with iPhones.

But since seeing news about the Lumia 1020 I have been itching to get a phone with a better camera, as the camera function is the feature of the phone that is most important to me - and remembering how great the Nokias of times past have been for me, I really wanted to get one of these new Lumias with the great camera. I opted for the 1520 to get the larger screen, even though the camera is "only" 20 megapixel - not the 41 megapixel Lumia 1020.

Now to the meat of my review. First, the good: The camera and the screen are excellent. I love taking photos and videos with this unit, and the videos look excellent on my 50" 1080p television. We have kids, and I take a lot of photos and videos of family - and that is the main reason for wanting the upgraded capabilities. There have been many other reviewers who adequately review the prowess of the camera and the screen of this phone, so I will just add my general praise and not go in to further detail.

Now onto the not so good: It's no iPhone - not even close. This is not so much a shortcoming of the hardware, but of the Windows Phone operating system and the apps available. The OS is not at all intuitive for me as someone coming from an iPhone - and intuitive functionality of the iPhone was something that made me fall in love with that family of devices. It also seems like anything I want to do on this Lumia takes more steps to accomplish than it did on an iPhone - simple things like setting up an alarm, entering a new contact, making a phone call, finding a photo from the album, all seem to be more complicated to do.

The other even bigger problem is the availability and quality of apps for the phone. All the big name apps are available, but are seriously limited in their features and functionality compared to their iOS counterparts. And many smaller name apps that I used on the iPhone are just not available on the Windows Phone - such as the online banking app for my credit union.

so, in summary, this phone is just OK for me, because I really love the hardware, but the OS and app availability really are sub par.

title: Age ain't nothing but a number......
text:
For 3 Year old Hardware, it performs on par with today's technology (2016). If you want the definitive Windows Phone 8.1 experience without fear of Windows 10 Mobile, this is the phone to get. Very fast start up times, seamless app switching and launching, and a large, bright display. If you want a cheaper alternative to the Lumia 950/950XL, but want Windows 10 Mobile (official), this phone is eligible for the Windows 10 Mobile upgrade.

Personally, I have very large hands, so this fits perfectly in my hands. Unless you are wearing skinny jeans, the phone will fit fine in your pocket.
The phone was locked to ATT, but a quick device request got it unlocked for me, so it WILL work on Tracfone and other discounted mobile carriers that uses GSM. This phone has all the physical hardware buttons, so launching your apps, opening the camera, volume adjustment and opening task manager can all be done without interfering with the current on-screen display. If your one of those people who hate how you need to go through three different menus on your car's touchscreen just to turn the radio on, this phone's physical buttons will satisfy you.

Battery life is quite good for a phone of this size. Moderate usage of this phone after a day left me with 77% battery life. That includes music being played for an hour and a half, about an hour of gaming, hour of app usage, Wi-fi + Cellular on and the obscure things being looked up online.

Storage was adequate, and is expandable with MicroSD card. While it says it only takes MicroSD cards up to 64GB, that was the largest you could buy at the time this phone was released. This will works fine with a 200GB microsd card. If you prefer Cloud storage, OneDrive is included with 5GB now (free), and ATT Locker gives you 50GB of Space (free).

I would highly recommend this phone for anyone who wants a flawless mobile experience that is slick, practical for today's streaming standards and supported with updates even 3 years after it's initial release. If your a larger person (ie. large hands, tall), this is a good phone for you.

text:
My wife and I got these phones as part of the Cyber Monday promotions and have not looked back. Our previous phones were Samsung Galaxy S II Epic 4G Touch through Sprint. The service was horrible on those phones so I spent a lot of time researching whether it was the phones or the service. Turns out when Sprint switched to 4G LTE, the neglected everything 4G so we were stuck with 3G and roaming (mostly roaming) despite living in Oklahoma City (not the surrounding suburb, the city). We didn't want to let go of our Unlimited Data Plans so we stuck with Sprint for one last go and we could not have chosen a better phone to maximize everything around us. The processor is super fast, graphics are crystal clear, the Spark means I have had amazing speed away from the wifi in my house.

The 2 issues we have had with it are as follows:
- When turning off the screen, about half the time it takes at least 15 seconds to get the screen to turn back on.
- The battery is pretty small compared to similar style phones, but since there is no "bloatware" I have hardly noticed a difference from previous battery sizes to this one. I will say that getting a Task Killer app and setting it to close all applications regularly and setting its "Kill Level" at the highest level really does help extend the battery life.

Overall, I'm very happy with this phone. It took me a while to get used to some of the customization, taking for granted that "full" texting and voicemail apps are not initially installed, but I don't even think about the new apps I now have.

title: A 4 year Android User's review...
text:
I'm going to start this out with a preface. I have been on Android since Eclair, so my comfort level with the software is not an issue.

I won't go so far as to say there is a learning curve to Android, but I will say that anyone can pick up this phone, make calls send texts, surf the web. Where this phone shines is after that. Those are simply prerequisites in the smartphone realm so any review of, "It's great for phone calls..." aren't helpful. That being said, it operates well on those key items.

The devil is in the details on this phone though. When the bloatware and manufacturer skins are stripped away, Android is fast and very clean. On this Nexus with the advanced specs, it's astonishing how quick things are.

I have had an S3, Evo 4G, and numerous experiences on other android devices as well as a year with an iPhone 4S in my pocket alongside my android phones.

The screen is an 'A' it is very sharp, true to color and of good size without feeling like I am carrying around a tablet.

Memory is adequate, I would have preferred the 32, but with Drive connectivity and faster mobile networks, I feel like on-device storage will be a dodo bird in 2 years.

Processing and RAM are top notch. There may be phones with faster or more, but with the reduced bloatware and interference of skins, the Nexus is faster. It just has less to shovel every time you ask it to function.

Build quality. It's a black phone with soft-feel plastic and a gorilla glass screen. It's better than Samsung, it's behind the new HTC M8, and in my opinion ahead of it's pricepoint. The phone in your hands will leave you complaining about very little.

Battery life is adequate. Everyone has a different view of this. If you are coming from a phone that can go for a week without charging (feature phones) you will complain. If you are coming from a 2-year old Android device, you'll be fine with it, in fact you might even be happy with it.

So ultimately, who should buy this phone?
- Tech savvy people who want to really customize their smartphone experience
- People who hate bloatware on their phone
- The Not-Another-Samsung/Apple crowd
- People looking for the most screaming deal on a product that will always have the newest software

And the final question, "Hey Joe, should I buy this phone?"
Are you someone listed above? Then yes. If not, Are you a fan of Apple, or would you rather have a desktop with widgets that you can change infinitely to your heart's content? Go nuts kid, this one's for you.

At the end of the day, you need to figure out where you put your priorities when grabbing any one of the "Premiere" smartphones. If you don't want to answer any questions about what you bought, get the iPhone and go along with the crowd. If you want the best camera, Nokia and Samsung are really the only players there. If you top priority is build quality, the M8 destroys all others. But if what you want is the least amount of useless stuff tied to a phone with a very good camera and fast interactions and always the newest software, this is your phone.

title: When I ordered this, it said it was a 32GB phone...but Amazon claimed that was a mistake and sent me the 16GB version instead.
text:
Note: Since the time when I received this phone, Amazon has corrected the description to list the correct specifications for the phone.

I originally gave this a low rating is based on the difference between the promised specifications at the time I placed my order(32GB) and what I received (16GB). I specifically searched for a 32GB phone, as that was what I wanted--and, according to the description at the time of my order, that is what this was promised to have. Amazon said their supplier misled them--and they only had the 16GB version (moreover, they had no way to get a 32GB phone). In my mind, that difference was very material. Moreover, I have few good options to resolve it: 1) reactivate my old phone & return this one to Amazon, 2) Try to take legal action to demand performance according to the order they accepted (all the tiny print in their terms and conditions, however, keep them well protected from their own mistakes--if only I was that well protected!), or 3) Accept a $50 credit and keep the phone I got. Any more, the fine print lets companies off the hook for anything they do wrong while binding you to your word no matter what.

Now, about the functionality of the phone...

The phone is quite nice. It is way more responsive than my old Galaxy S2. The 4G-LTE works better (by far) than the 4G-WIMAX on my S2--in some places, it is blazing fast. I can't wait to see how the Sprint Spark network works...

Being a "stock" Android phone, I don't have all the bloatware (good!)...but there are some widgets and stuff that I kinda miss from my old S2. But, mostly, it's just getting used to a slightly different interface. Oh...and it seems like every different Android uses a completely different set of stock "sounds"--so I'm having to get used to that!

I've heard people say that the auto-brightness is wonky...but, so far, it's worked better on this phone than my last phone.

Also, so far, the battery life is a lot better than my last phone (I think one of the upgrades did something that caused it to suck down my battery).

The biggest downer so far relates to the memory. After loading the stuff from the previous phone's SD card (this new one doesn't have an SD slot), I only have 2.5GB free. That is likely to become a problem sooner rather than later.

Also, with my Galaxy S2 using Sprint's 4G WiMax, I could talk on the phone and do Internet at the same time if I was in 4G coverage. I miss that and hope they hurry up with Voice Over LTE which should bring that functionality back.

What has me most excited...is that I hope to get more timely updates of the software. The other devices I've had took some time to get new updates (even security patches) due to the convoluted steps needed to get the software to work with all the mods made by the manufacturer. This should be much faster.

title: Great as 450$ phone, not good as a premium phone
text: Let me just say this up front.  I don't like the fact that Sprint and all the other carriers are charging 450$ for a phone that Google on Google Play is charging 350$.  This is another way for these cell phone companies to keep the consumer under their thumb.  But, with that being said, the key word for me "price," and for the price I really do like the Nexus 5, although I do have a few complaints about it.  Let me begin by saying that the white version of this phone and the black version are surprisingly distinct from each other.  I had believed that the white and the black version were the same exact phone just like every other black/white variation of every phone.  But they aren't.  First, they come in different looking boxes.  Just something that I'd thought i'd share.  Secondly, the earpiece (where the ear is when taking a call) on the white version is white while the black one blends into the black borders of the phone. Moreover, the white Nexus 5 is glossy around the sides whereas the black Nexus 5 has dull black sides,  Something to think about if one really cares about fingerprints on their phone (personally, I like the white version).  Now with that out of the way, the things that I do like about this phone is that it is very snappy and quick when swiping and bringing up applications, more so than some of the better spec phones such as the Note 3.  Another thing I like about the phone is it is light but it doesn't feel cheap.  It has a build that feels good in your hands.  And, the resolution on the screen is pretty damn good.  I am pretty impressed by the definition and detail when looking at the screen, and colors look great.  Now that's good news, but here is the bad news.  One of the first things that I've noticed when using the Nexus 5 is that the speaker is pretty weak.  It is not loud at all, and at full blast I couldn't hear the person on the other line when I was out in public.  Another thing that this phone is not good at doing is staying alive.  What I mean by this is that on one full charge, the phone will last about 4 to 5 hours max with regular usage.  If I don't use the phone much I may get a few more hours of standby time.  This bothered me because I need my phone throughout the day and I'm not always near an outlet, plus there's no way to open the phone and throw in a replacement battery. So, that definitely is a large negative for me.  Finally, another weak point on this phone is the camera.  Although the phone has a decent 8 mega pixel camera, the pictures I take in good light are not of great quality.  The pictures seem to be not of the right colors and it seems to dull the light out a bit.  Furthermore,  I can't take rapid fire pictures as each successive picture taken requires a about 2-3 second delay between each other.  But, the camera is surprisingly good at taking low light pictures.  As a matter of fact, the Nexus 5 camera in low light is better than some of the more premium phones with better cameras.  This is something that I really enjoy about the Nexus 5's camera.  Overall, if I was to rate this phone as a regular priced phone, (650-750$) or 200$ with a 2 year contract, I would probably give it 3 stars due to all the flaws (camera, speaker , battery life) the phone has.  But, for a 450$ phone or 50$ on a 2 year contract, this phone is exceptional.  It is exceptional because it functions very well as a smart phone (the touch screen is very quick and responsive and on 4G the internet is quick) and it has great screen resolution.  Personally I bought this phone outright for 450$ and I am happy with it.  But, I think I wouldn't be as happy if I paid 700$ for it.

title: A very solid phone for a long time Android user
text:
I've had an Android phone ever since my former employer stopped using BlackBerry. I've used a variety of Samsung, Moto, and LG phones and even after owning this for a month, I'm still in love with my Nexus 5. The screen is big, bright, and sexy. The phone is fast and very responsive. I've always thought that screen rotation was slow on my old Droids, but this one is very fast. I mostly surf the web, check email and play the occasional game on my phone while I'm waiting for a doctor/dentist appointment or a meeting. For these purposes I have no complaints. With previous phones, I bought and used other apps instead of the built-ins (like the camera app). With the new camera app that comes with KitKat, I don't have any complaints. I use it instead of the app I paid for a couple years ago. Also, I easily rooted this phone in about five minutes. Instructions are easily found online. I haven't tried a custom ROM yet, though.

As for the downsides...

1) It's hungry. It eats through your battery charge like a hungry hippo. Fortunately, the charger is fast. I can charge my phone from 10% to a full charge in about 90 minutes, maybe less.

2) There is no replacing the battery or adding an SD card. This phone is sealed and intended to stay sealed.

3) The charging plug is on the bottom. This is minor, but I'm used to it being on the top.

4) The speaker is on the bottom, right where I put my fingers when holding the phone with both hands. Often I can't hear the phone when I'm holding it, because I forget to move my big fat finger.

5) Sprint's 4G LTE service isn't great where I live and tend to visit. Where 4G is prevalent, it works like a champ.

Overall, this phone is great. If you're looking for your next Android, this is definitely worth a look.

title: Great phone, but best pricing will vary.
text:
I upgraded to the Nexus 5 from a Nexus S 4G. An issue I had with my previous phone was how underpowered it was. After two years' worth of Android system updates, my old phone was pretty slow. A major problem with the Nexus S was the partitioning of the storage space into 2GB and 14GB divisions, which compounded the speed problem with memory issues as well. The Nexus 5 does not have either of these problems because of the new multi-core processor inside, and the entire 16GB of storage space is a single partition and accessible for both installation of apps and storage of photos, etc.

The Nexus 5 is very slim and sleek, but many of the cases available for it square off the slightly rounded edges of the phone in addition to adding thickness to the phone, making it a little chunky. This may be a reasonable trade-off if a case prevents your screen of becoming damaged when your phone is dropped.

The screen on the Nexus 5 is large and bright. You may want to turn the brightness setting down to conserve battery life, as the screen is responsible for as much as a third of my total battery consumption over the course of the day. With respect to the physical size of the phone, using it one-handed could be difficult if you have small hands. I wear medium/large size gloves, and have no problem with this. The large screen certainly helps with typing using the on-screen keyboard. Far fewer missed keys compared to my older phone.

I bought this phone on/around Cyber Monday, so it was on sale for $35 on Amazon for a device upgrade with Sprint. The price may have changed since then. If you're looking to buy the phone off-contract, the Google Play store may be a better deal.

When upgrading my phone, I was also considering the HTC One and the Moto X, which are both also great phones. I decided to go with the Nexus 5 because I prefer to run an Android phone without additional manufacturer-specific skins on top. These skins often add features or visual effects I don't use but will still consume system resources. Additionally, the Nexus 5 has a high repairability score from iFixit, which is also important to me. If a part of the phone breaks, I'd rather replace the broken part than buy a whole new phone. The Moto X also has a high repairability score, but the HTC One is not really repairable at all. Another advantage of the Nexus devices are the speed with which they receive Android system updates. You can read more about that elsewhere. Specific to the Nexus 5, the camera software was not particularly good upon launch of the phone in November. By the time I purchased and activated my phone in December, a new system update had been issued, and the camera software was upgraded in that release. The photos taken with the Nexus 5 rival those taken with my friend's iPhone 5, if that is a concern for you. I don't have a comparison to the iPhone 5S.

text:
This phone is an upgrade from a Galaxy S2 so I expected it to be a significant change as far as capability which it most certainly is. I've only had it for a day and a half so i really can't judge battery life yet which is a concern going to a fixed battery phone, but speed and performance is great. Sprint LTE in my area is decent so streaming full 1080 over the wireless network is good although it's not something I plan on doing often, but it is a good test for both the phone and network. Sprint is scheduled to start what they call SPARC next year which will use all three bands for data simultaneously which I am eager to try. There is very little Sprint Bloatware installed which was nice to see, but there is some. I also had to take the phone into a Sprint store to get it activated. I could have called customer service most likely, but the store was just down the block. One other thing to note was that when I ordered the phone through Amazon I changed my plan to the new all data for life, but when I took it into the store was told I still had my old plan. The service guy at the store changed it for me.
This was one of the three options I was looking at for an upgrade. The other two were LG-G2 and the Moto-X. A friend has the Moto-X and is happy as has some nice value added like the trusted zones which I really wish this phone had, but I am still very happy with my choice. The screen is definitely not an OLED as the blacks are not totally black and the colors can seen a bit washed out. For the price point of the off contract phone something had to give and it was the choice in screen. I don't mind it at all as I use the phone as a communication and productivity device mainly and I'd much rather have more computing power than a perfect screen. Also some reviews I've seen have disliked the camera. The camera is fine, but is slow to get into action/focus. I understand that this will be addressed in a software update in the future. I mainly use the a camera phone for documenting things as opposed to getting the perfect shot. I have a bunch of DSLR equipment for that. So far I am very pleased with the phone, but it has only been a few days. I'm giving it 4/5 due to the screen and camera not being perfect, but would not hesitate to make the same choice again at this time.

title: I am on my THIRD Google Nexus 5
text:
I purchased the Nexus 5, over the Galaxy S4, in hopes that this phone wouldn't disappoint me but boy was I wrong!

Initially, the phone worked great, but within 4 weeks, the camera stopped working. The wouldn't work with any application that uses a camera, even after performing a system restore. I sent it back to Amazon and got a brand new replacement, but I had much lower expectations, but never did I expect my NEW (not refurbished) replacement to go bad too.

Once again, a few weeks into using the replacement phone, it failed on me. One night, the backside of the phone began to get really hot. I thought it was because I had poor service. The phone continuously got hotter until finally, the screen blacked out. I tried troubleshooting with the help of Sprint, Amazon and the manufacturer and they were stumped too. Their only advice was to get a replacement.

There I was again, ordering a replacement phone for the SECOND TIME in less than TWO MONTHS. That means I was on my THIRD phone within 8 weeks - absurd by any standards. I don't know what happened, but Google really dropped the ball with the build quality of this phone, in my opinion.

It's been a month with the 3rd phone, and no issues yet.

Overall, when I wasn't busy replacing my phone, I have enjoyed using it. But, I am not going to count my blessings just yet.

2 minor (for me) downsides, first is that the phone is so new that some areas of where I live don't support 4G LTE for it yet, but that's a temporary problem as the network improves--and I'm on WiFi throughout most of the day anyway. Second is that Hangouts (default messaging app on this phone) and Sprint have a character limit of 160 in place for SMS messages. Rather than build out your text as one long message and send to the recipient as 1/3, 2/3, etc, you have to cut yourself off and send in 160 character chunks. This is annoying but it's a known issue that is not limited to the Nexus 5 (it's a Sprint + Hangouts thing); so don't let that stop you from getting this great phone.

title: 4.77" not 5.41"
text:
Just FYI, this phone is SMALLER than the Technical Details summary shows. It's not 5.41", it's 4.77". That's why it's a Mini, as opposed to a Maxx which is 5.41" high (both are XT1030, essentially the same phone). The specs shown here fooled me into thinking the Mini was bigger than what I was looking for, but in fact it's an ideal size for anybody who wants an HD display without the bulk.
Do a search for "droid mini phonearena" to find the complete and accurate specs.
For me the only real drawbacks to the Mini are that you can't add an external SD card, and the nanoSIM. My bigger Moto X has one of those and it's a bear to handle. Wasn't micro small enough? Otherwise I believe the Mini is a GREAT phone, and all things considered, Motorola makes as sturdy a cell phone as you can find. I've owned 3 and have another one on the way.

text:
My husband and I both got these on a 2 year contract with verizon. I had a galaxy before this and wow, what a downgrade.

The Pros:
Small, fits in pocket
Good call quality

Cons

Phone gets hot while charging to the point that it cannot be used for any long period while plugged in
Keyboard is small and awkward, to be expected with a small phone
Camera sucks
NO slot for SD card
Data is slow even with good service

This is an entry level smart phone good for those who are new to the technology and want to try it out, but for more serious users, this "budget" phone isn't much of a bargain in the long run.

Mine really saved us many times trying to navigate around, able to call for help when we had accidents (twice!), etc. It is small and so a little hard to type but that's to be expected with a small phone. title: Excellent partnership Microsoft - Nokia!!
text:
Nokia built an amazing phone with customized applications and Windows Phone 8 performs flawlessly. Super fast processor, smooth video; you can finally watch a video and listen to it with Bluetooth headphones (mine is Plantronics backbeat 903+).

For those skeptical regarding applications, there is Instagram and Whatsapp for W8 (download is free for both) and many more free apps, although Lumia 1520 brings a load of essential applications.

Very advisable to buy a cover, not only for its protection but for a better handling. I found the device extremely slippery in my hands. I purchased a cover with kick stand, so I can eat and read or watch a video.

W8 automatically backs up most your data (pics, docs and videos) to skydrive, which is very convenient. All contacts I had on my HTC HD7 (Windows phone 7.5) was imported as soon as I register my accounts (Hotmail, Facebook and Google) even without the sim card. A great feature is that you can access your Lumia 1520 from your PC as if it is an external hard drive. You can also receive and send several kinds of files via Bluetooth. The NFC (Near Field Communication) is amazing!!

I still donnot understand people who rather pay a lot more for an IPhone or Android!!

I also purchased a 32Gb micro SD (you can install up to 64Gb), which is another feature Iphones don't have.

Also amazing is the battery. You will now have a phone that will keep up with you all day, provided you make a normal use of it. Remember to charge it, use it until battery runs out and charge it again, so that your battery will be optimized.

Only disappointment regards to the charger which is European. Although seller sends (at no cost) an American adapter, it gets to be a very clumsy piece (both together).

Well done Microsoft and Nokia.

February 6th Update

Today I test the Here Nokia (the built in GPS) I turned it on together with my car's GPS, except that I made it work offline. Both GPSs took me from where I was to where I wanted to go flawlessly. The Here Nokia offers more detailed information and precision. I am being amazed day after day by its software.

title: Nice work Nokia!
text:
HARDWARE

Aesthetically this phone is BEAUTIFUL, a master piece! I like minimalist and simple things. I love the 1520 design, everything is placed where it should. Buttons are placed nicely!! The camera button comes very handy!

The back camera? Amazing, wonderful! As a photo enthusiast I can say the camera is one of the best phone cameras I have seen with many advanced features! And the camera button comes really handy! The flash sucks. It should have been xenon.

Front camera? Still needs some work, for my taste it sucks pretty badly. Grainy and slow if dark! Bad, bad, bad resolution.

Sensors are precise and work perfectly, I always turned them off in my S3, S4, Note, HTC's, Moto's because they were random and not precise... they made me rage more than once. Only thing missing is an IR blaster, that would be really useful! And maybe fingerprint scanner ONLY if it works as it should, I think that technology is not ready yet for prime time.

Also about Qi charging, once you go for it there's no way back! I even put a DT 900 hidden on my desk and nightstand, charges fast and it is so convenient!

Processor? Powerful. You can throw anything at it! If you updated to WP 8.1 DP... It is a DEVELOPER PREVIEW so it will lag a little sometimes and some things won't work as intended, you will have to make a soft reset-restart and hopefully it will resolve your issue or you will have to wait for the official release.

The battery in this thing is amazing, I'd never have thought that it would last forever with the screen size but it does! Using Xbox music to stream music all day! Whatsapp, FB and web browsing all day, by 10 PM is still around 15-20%. ~5 hours of listening to music with a Sony Bluetooth SBH20, 4-5 hours of screen time while using Whatsapp, FB, web browsing, skipping songs. Gaming, once in a while.

It has micro SD slot, YES! No micro SD slot is a deal killer for me!

SIM tray is loose! BAD!

Touch screen sensitivity is good, perfect! And I have no more issues with it!

Signal is good but it will chose slowest networks (EDGE, 3G, HSDPA+) if they are stronger than the fastest ones. And you CAN'T force it to HSDPA or LTE.

Screen is gorgeous, crisp, clear, stunning! But there's a defect with most lumias, in white backgrounds you will see brighter spots in a specific part of the screen exactly where the back camera is placed. Other than that is perfect for me! Anyway you won't notice the bright spot!

Glance feature is wonderful! I think it is not supported by 930 and some others phones because of the screen technology used.

VERY IMPORTANT. Screen seems to be fragile, still haven't drop it! Case or insurance could save your life, screen replacement is expen$ive. I have seen many post talking about broken digitizers and screens. Replacing only the digitizer is NOT easy at all if you manage to replace it without breaking the screen, that if you are lucky enough and didn't break the screen.

SOFTWARE

I've had about everything but iPhone, I do love my 1520 but as a power user WP 8.1 is still lacking advanced features/options. About the apps, I have the ones I need but they are lacking advanced options/features because of WP limitations and some others because apparently programmers aren't putting much effort in WP apps. But with WP 8.1 they finally added so much stuff that was missing and with WP 8.1 Microsoft is finally giving more freedom for making apps with everything we need but still not as much as Android.

For most people 8.1 will do! I am a power user, but most people are not! They have everything they need in 8.1 (just a few things missing, maybe some advanced options would be nice) BUT the 1520 is BLAZING FAST! Butter smooth! Not like my any other phone I've had!

Size of everything is about perfect on a 1520! The keyboard and the new swipe thing is amazing! Cortana is nice, and we have music recognition integrated (I'd suggest MS to improve it, is slow sometimes and if you don't have internet connection you are done. Some apps in Android store the recording so you can search that song later, you can't do that with Bing)! Also integrated translation and QR scan, pretty sweet to translate things just with the camera.

Now WP and Lumia has some unique features and apps that I love so much and are freaking good: IE sucks on Windows but on WP is way too good, beats any other browser! Nokia apps are awesome, beamer, maps, camera, etc.!

The integration with Microsoft services is good, you will love it! It integrates with many services very nicely!

For music lovers, Xbox music pass is the way to go! Better than Pandora, Spotify, etc.! Music player is kind of mediocre but it will do. Gallery is GOOD! Better than android!

Clean and simple OS, very good looking! I'd only add a few more advanced options and more transparent tiles for this new image backgrounds! And a color palette to choose our own accent and background colors, that would be sweet!

OVERALL

Hardware is good and this thing is damn pretty! Problems? Loose SIM tray, bright spots on the screen (you won't notice unless someone told you so), front camera sucks, FRAGILE screen. No IR blaster, no fingerprint yet. Battery, screen, processor, sensors, etc are amazing! Micro SD slot up to 128GB!

Software? You get everything you need, still missing some advanced features! But 8.1 is getting close to iOS and Android. Still has some advantages and unique design and features, and it is BUTTER SMOOTH. Integrates very nicely with MS services and some others. You have to try it to know what I'm talking about, but Microsoft is doing a good damn job with 8.1.

I think a 30-40% fanboys will betray Apple and Samsung if they had this thing for a day. Throw an IR blaster, fingerprint scanner and everyone most of them will be sold, you don't even need some advanced options in apps or OS level. Keep it going Microsoft!

Did I miss something? Any questions, doubts? Ask!

title: Really happy with it.
text: So far I have had this device for a month and it has been a really great experience. I started out on an iPhone, changed to Android  and have now gone to WP. What I am enjoying the most is that the experience is so slick, everything works, and its fast, efficient and a really nice user experience. I was never a really heavy app user on the other platforms so I cannot comment on the extent of everyone's needs, but all the apps that I required where present before I moved over. What however has changed, is that because of the greater screen size I have tended to use more apps than I ever had before. This I think is because the extra screen size has actually allowed the device to far more useful that it was on smaller screens. Initially my great concern was the size as I thought it might be too big. However, I have changed my mind and I think 6 inches is the sweet spot for a smartphone, and I couldn't go back to a smaller one. After a months use I find that it fits fine in my jeans and trousers and doesn't get in the way. Initially I was going to wait for the 930 to be released in OZ, but that still hasn't happened, but either way, I am glad that I didn't wait as this phone suits me perfectly. I don't miss the iPhone but I do miss the notifications dropdowns from Android, but I believe that this will soon be added in WP 8.1. I was quite surprised by how long it took to charge the phone, until I realized that the battery was so massive so that is a fair tradeoff and makes sense. On top of which, having wireless charging means that you can lay the phone around on a wireless charger and pick it up as you please, and thus phone charging is less of an issue. All in all, a great device and highly recommended.

text:
First I will say that windows 8 is AMAZING. I had the Nokia Lumia 920 and likes a lot of the personalization features but it lacked my Pandora, pinterest, myfitnesspal, Spotify, and other apps I use daily so I went back to IPhone.

Same ol Same ol EXCEPT now...a lot of my apps are always crashing. My wifi isn't that strong in my room, my front camera quit...and it's almost the same as the first iPhone. UNBOXING:
Amazed by color brightness, screen brightness, size and beautiful camera.

1. the Lumia now does SnapShot and if you are or have been an iPhone user this is awesome.
2. There is a driving mode you can set up with a Bluetooth device to avoid wrecks. No touching phone while driving.
3. Some of the apps that were previously said not to be on the windows phones were now there. In face the only thing I do not have that I used a lot was weight watchers...they just have a rinkidink calculator but im sure that will update.

Pinterest

Instagram
Amazon

App folder (to organize all your apps like IPhone)
FREE RINGTONES...NO MORE PAYING FOR THAT CRAP

title: Watch Out for Privacy - Microsoft at Work
text:
Microsoft automatically uploads your phone contacts and Calendar into its cloud (outlook.com). There is a way around it but it's not for the novice. This is also stated in their disclosure if you have time to read the fine print.

(The hardware is excellent. The Windows 8 software works fine. Remember this is a 6 inch phone; almost double the size of an iPhone).

So what's wrong w/ MS uploading your private information? Here is the list:

- If your email is hijacked the thieves will send money request on your behalf to everyone on the list with an email address. Or if you have your bank account info online things could get worse.
- The US government will certainly snoop into your data.
- The MS Sys Admins are also a potential source of snooping and passing on the info.

If you are a facebook type that puts sensitive personal information on the internet then do not worry. But if you are concerned about security of your data beware of this issue.

To get around it is not that easy. Here is what I did:

( I use MS outlook desktop version for my Contacts, Calendar, and email - Only if you have this then follow the instructions below):

- When you receive the phone - do not setup a microsoft (hotmail/msn) account. If you do they automatically upload your data to their servers (outlook.com)
- Don't use the 'Transfer my Data'. If you do they automatically upload your data to their servers (outlook.com)
- Purchase Akruto Sync (I am not in any way related to these guys - This is just to sync the outlook w/ your phone to bypass MS) and sync your contacts/calendar using this software.
- One last thing: If you are forced to login into hotmail/msn account delete your calendar and contact list first - then login to MS and do what's required such as updates - then go to the settings and set a wrong password for the hotmail (you cannot delete a hotmail account) - then use Akruto Sync to sync desktop outlook w/ Nokia 1520.

title: Great, but something to lookout for before you buy...
text:
Alright people, I'll admit I made a buy without enough research into how the unlocked phone will work on US carriers. So to try and help people avoid the issue I ran into I'll try and highlight something I completely missed. This particular model works with T-Mobile, except YOU WILL NOT GET 4G/LTE connections. The RM-938 model (AT&T version) is the only Lumia 1520 that can make use of 4G/LTE on T-Mobile (as far as I know).

Additionally, I installed WP 8.1 on it and here's a few things to note:
- On the device I received, the locale wasn't set to US. The keyboard and other region settings were either in Chinese or English (UK). If you want to get Cortana to work, you'll have to make sure your region settings are set to US.
- I had a few account sync issues and had to do a factory reset after installing WP 8.1, doing the factory reset does not get rid of WP 8.1 (which is nice).
- A lot of popular apps still don't take full advantage of the added screen real estate provided by the higher resolution. Expect text and other in-app UI elements to be a little blown up (probably wouldn't bother most people)
- I've seen many reviews say its impossible to operate this phone with one hand. I can do most tasks like texting, browsing and making calls (especially with WP 8.1 installed) using one hand without too much trouble. I even have a phone case which slightly increases its dimensions. I don't have the hands of a basketball player either.
- My device takes a considerably longer time to fully charge than my other WP devices (Lumia 925 and HTC 8X) but that's to be expected given it has a larger battery and lasts a lot longer on one charge
- I'd strongly recommend getting some sort of case or cover for this phone because the surface of the phone can get really slippery. Given the size of the phone, if you do not have a good grip when moving about on it (e.g. holding the phone when getting out of the car) chances are you'll end up dropping it.

That being said, the phone is incredible and everything I expected it to be, but in this case I imagine that is more of a personal opinion for people given the size of the phone.

title: it's okay, but not great - update, its bad
text:
The phone itself is very sturdy and feels great in your hands.

Windows Phone 8 seems at first like an upgrade but there are differences that don't' make it over from 7. One feature that isn't available that I used consistently on 7 is the speak to text option. It was a button right next to the send message, attach file icons on a conversation and it allowed for a better hands free texting option while driving than actually texting. it's no longer there and I haven't found a way to enable it if available, through the settings.

Next is the service. I looked before I leapt and everything said that this phone would work with American T-Mobile service. That it would not get 4g lte but would still get 3g service. I bout a Nokia Lumia 810 for my wife same time as this and in most cases I do not get 3g service. She has gotten 4g in my home, yet I standing next to her can barely get E, possibly H, but I've only gotten 3G in small places while in passing. unless I'm tied to Wi-Fi, the data on this is very slow.

Had I known about this, I might have gone with the 925, or even the 1020, but this is a very big let down, as now I have a outdated phone, before it's even available in the US.

UPDATE:

I wrote the above review after about a month of use with the phone. I stand by what I said and for the longest time I was very happy with my purchase. I was able to find the ability to talk to text, and with the recent patch from nokia I can now use cortana which has actually been helpful. I would've told everyone to buy this phone.

On 8.25.14 I experienced an issue with the phone not reading my SIM card. It was intermittent for about a week, and then it was flat out not working. Swapping SIM cards didn't help. After contacting nokia I found out (just like the others) that with no warranty on the unit Nokia would refuse to fix it, I couldn't even pay them.

I pushed a little harder and they said to contact Palco Cell Phone repair in Alabama. They are license to do nokia phone repairs. I did some investigating into my problem and every repair place around me told me that the phone was not repairable, it needed a new mother board as the SIM reader is soldered to the board. I called Palco and spoke with Rose, who assured me that their technicians were trained and certified by Nokia so they should be able to fix the phone. She told me to mail it to them and submit the order online and after receiving the unit they would email me a bill on whether it was repairable ($98) or if not then just a service fee would apply ($15). I sent in the phone with 2 day shipping, but I didn't hear anything from them. after a week I called, and was told that they receive my phone and were waiting on payment before repairing it. I asked, does that mean it can be fixed then? The answer I got (from Rose) was that their tech's haven't looked at it yet and will not look at it till the quote was paid, the $98 from before. I of course reminded her what she told me about $98/15 situation, and she wouldn't budge. I pay the 98 and 2 days later I get an email saying that my phone is not repairable, it needs a new mother board and they cannot do that work.

I love Windows as a Phone OS, and the phone was a very nice phone all things created equal. The fact that I am out close to 600 (when I got it from amazon it was a bit more expensive) for a phone that still works just not as a phone, puts a very bitter taste in my mouth. It s a very small tablet now. Considering I was even willing to pay to have it fixed, I don't see why I had to go through this and this will mark my departure from Nokia as the company I tell people to buy from.

I work out of a gamestop and we do cell phones now. I told everyone before to get a nokia over the Iphones and androids, simply for windows. Now I just keep my opinions to myself and sell the iphones. Nokia, you've lost my business and anyone that I may have swayed over to you before.

title: Very Poor Quality Control
text:
I've bought a lot of phones and this one was the lowest quality in terms of manufacturing that I've seen. The plastic rim around the edge was already starting to delaminate almost immediately after I opened the box, and eventually a piece of plastic surrounding the USB inlet broke off and lodged in the power source, so I had to fish it out.

Meanwhile the screen was very glitch -- sometimes the unlock buttons would not work and I'd have to restart the phone. Other times certain buttons would not work, or scrolling would freeze.

And finally, I dropped it once and the screen shattered. Now I face a giant repair. If you read the Nokia web site there are LOTS of complaints about the screen shattering, including a number of people who said it shattered in their pocket or even took it to altitude in a car or a train, and the pressure change burst the screen!! This phone is just so large with so much glass that I don't think it is very usable without a very high risk of breaking -- and the size makes it hard to hold and so much more likely to shatter.

The screen, battery life and camera are good, and the Windows iOS is great -- but this phone is a lemon due to its fragility, IMHO.

title: Great phone and the best of its line, but with minorish issues.
text:
I loved this phone. Out of all the Windows Phones that I've had, this being the second one besides the 8x, this performed the best. The larger screen bulges out of the frame for accessibility from any corner. Great for operating with one hand if you have larger hands. If you are familiar with the older models you notice instantly the extra space given to you for your home screen apps. The customization aspects of the phone is the same as any other model, but with more apps for stock performances.

On the negative aspect, I bought this phone this past July. I already had some issues within that time frame. The screen would bug out on me. flickering and jittering. The only remedy was to hit the lock button or shut down all together. My main issue was the charge port that needed repair. I've done a lot of research on the issue and apparently its pretty common and a $75 fix. But a fix I feel I shouldn't have to do before the first 6 months at least. This really became a problem after I installed the 8.1 update. Once that was done, I was never ale to use my phone for extended periods of time. Thats when the charging issue became a nuisance to a full blown problem. Also the headphone jack would mess up. This has been something I've battled with the 8x too, but that could also be from my doing. So I wont put it against the phone itself.

All in all, its a great phone, but with Microsoft buying Nokia out, I hope that if they do plan to come out with a phone line, they improve these issues. These Windows Phones could lead the pack between Apple & Android by giving the consumer a simple but customizable interface. They just need to work on the minor bugs.

title: The Mail Man among Windows Cell phones ... the Lumia 1520 delivers!
text: After having an experience with an Android based phone, This reviewer was not impressed with the operating system.  Using a Windows based PC daily made changing to a Windows based cell phone a natural choice.  The Lumia 1520 is the third Windows phone this reviewer has owned, and its functionality a huge plus.  As more users have turned to Windows phones, the number of available apps has grown considerably, so functionality should only improve.  Two other Lumia phones were considered including the Lumia 640 XL and the Lumia 1020.  The rated 40 megapixel camera rating for the 1020 was and is an impressive feature, however, seeing comparisons of photos taken with the 640 XL, the 1020 and the 1520, the Lumia 640 XL's photos appeared to have the best color renditions than either the 1520 or the 1020, yet the 1520's photos appeared slightly warmer than photos from the 1020.  This reviewer did not have either a Lumia 1020 or a 640 XL in hand to perform side-by-side comparisons, rather comparisons were made with photos from another tester.  The 1520's photos were considerably sharper than those from the Lumia 1020 whose images seemed to have noticeably fuzzy edges on objects in the photo frame.  The Lumia 640 XL is said to be equipped with a quad core processer, but it is slower than the 1520's processor.  Both were rated faster than the dual core Lumia 1020.  Other reviews of the Lumia 1020 noted that write times to either internal memory or SD cards was much slower for the 1020. Both the 1020 and the 1520 offer image stabilization which is lacking in the 640 XL.  The Lumia 1520 has  been described as the fastest Windows phone.  Though only using the phone for a week to date, the speed of the processor in the 1520 is impressive.  Connecting to the internet either through Wi-Fi or through a direct link through this reviewer's service provider was fast.  The phone's size is large, but screen visibility is drastically enhanced with the much larger screen.  For the size of the phone, it isn't too heavy, and the screen's auto brightness adjustment feature ensures a readable screen even in bright outdoor light conditions.  The only negative for this phone is that the "back" navigation button doesn't always light.  Even with it not lit, however, the function is still available.  Photos taken for this review were very good.  There was good color depth and contrast, and it, too, was fast for a camera phone.  Resolution and shutter speed are both faster than for my small NIkon.  The Lumia 1520 is incredibly fast.  It has a very good screen.  This phone has been equipped with a after-market case and glass film screen protector.  Though I doubt you will use the Lumia 1520 as a replacement for your NIkon SLR, it is a very good  phone with a very good  camera.  Telephone sound quality sounds much better on this phone than some reviews have reported. If you currently use Windows 8 on your PC, and you're seeking a Windows phone, the Lumia 1520 is a very good choice, and I recommend the Lumia 1520 to anyone seeking a Windows phone with a very good camera.

title: 5/5 Fan-tastic.
text:
I'm not the greatest at organizing things, but I try to touch on things in order of personal relevance and I think I touch a little on everything. I hope this helps!

I have used androids for five years. My entire family used Galaxies and then moto x's from day one. However, android lacked the Microsoft flare and efficiency I had come to appreciate from their computers - so this last summer, I took some of my saved up money and bought an unlocked version because I would be living overseas in the near future. I bought the phone and it actually arrived approximately two weeks before the estimated receiving date (very impressed!)

Mind, I had done a fair bit of research over what to expect from this phone running Windows 8.1 and the app selection as well as the camera performance. There ARE conflicting sources saying that you can use this phone with Verizon. Please do not listen to them. They are the worst trolls imaginable. When I received this phone, it took me several weekends of nonstop speaking with people at Verizon to see if they could find a way around their GSM incompatibility but to no avail. After 13 long years as their customer, I waited for my contract to wear out and went to straight talk for the remainder of my time in the US.

It worked flawlessly on the AT&T network (don't bother with T-mobile, many other reviews have already explained why) and I can receive - for those who are unfamiliar - E, H, H+, and 4G network bands. It has been difficult to differentiate between them, but from what research I've done, it appears that E corresponds to 2G (garbage, but rare), H is essentially 3G, H+ is the oddball and can be as quick as 4G or about as slow as 3G depending on signal strength (personal observations: don't take my word for it) and, well, there's 4G. I can barely tell the difference between 4G and LTE, so don't worry that much about it. Most anywhere in Wyoming with buildings will receive H+ or 4G, and the AT&T data map suggests that it is significantly better in other, more populated states.

The interface is very -- and I mean /very/ -- polished. The GUI and OS in general are clearly a labor of love. The battery life is astounding: 30 hours on a single charge while on automatic screen brightness adjustment settings and with regular (albeit brief) texting and reddit app use. Which brings me more specifically to the app market; whereas you will find just about everything that you would ever want these days, with the notable exceptions of snapchat and chromechast/google applications in general, you will have access to all else (sometimes through the use of 3rd-party apps like audiocloud for soundcloud which has a slightly older-looking interface but functions just as well.) Given, some apps like the one for Facebook are remarkably ignored (no updates since march of last year besides inclusion of Messenger) they will certainly be present and usable. Further, google announced at yesterday's (10/6/2015) tech conference that they would be bringing several of their apps (chromecast included, supposedly) to the Microsoft store, so improvements are always being made.

The camera is extraordinary in that I'm used to Samsung's standard 10 MP or moto's 5 MP and rear either .8 or 1.2. I am able to take some incredible pictures due to the exceptional quality of the lens and pixel count. Audio is also incredibly customizable -- Groove Music may not be as good as google music in offering free mix stations, but it is certainly organized better and prices are generally comparable and the audiojack plays well with all headsets. In fact, I would say that for a phone, the performance is phenomenal. Unlike my galaxies or moto x ('14), I can tell the difference between 124 kbps and 320 kbps. External speakers can be VERY loud if you want them to be and songs are crystal clear as long as they aren't 75% bass. The only thing I might be disappointed in is the generally too-quiet external speaker for when you're using your phone as, well - you know - a phone. Even maximizing the volume does little. I highly recommend using the free earbuds that come with this phone and the integrated speaker. It'll save you a lot of stress trying to hear people (but really only is this ever a problem when you're in a crowded place.) Speakerphone works, too, and the phone's mic seems to have very acute hearing even from a distance of 5 meters.

Being the clutz that I am, I had dropped it several times before the case arrived (for the love of everything good, order the case before the phone arrives) on a hard, cement floor at work from approximately four feet up. Nokia still lives up to its stereotype of being nigh unbreakable: not a dent or scratch anywhere on the darn thing. That being said, get the darn case or you /will/ eventually break your phone. Gorilla Glass only goes so far. I bought a hybrid hard plastic / gel case with a little flip-out stand, the Amzer Double Layer Rugged Hybrid Case Cover with Kickstand for Nokia Lumia 1520 and it has saved my phone at least a dozen times. (Remember when I said I was clumsy? I meant it.)

I don't actually own an xbox, but my room mate does and he absolutely loves the integration between windows phone and his console. He can walk on into a room with groove going and as long as his bluetooth is on, it will automatically start playing the same song from where he left off if he fiddles with the settings a little. Finally, a comment on Cortana: if you live in the US or UK (I think? If it's only the us, just set your region to the US when you first set it up and it'll work fine, assuming your accent isn't too severe) then your always-listening personal data assistant is pretty much exactly what I'd want in a science fiction world - it's making its way toward quasi-sapience. The voice actor is great and reminds me of EDI of Mass Effect or, well, Cortana of Halo, obviously.

If you have the money, buy this phone! Assuming you don't feel like shelling out double this price for a 950xl or just waiting for any potential successor. Still a great buy, especially with WP10 coming out so soon. All pictures included were taken directly following the last time I dropped it without a case.

title: Great Phone once Access Point and Name was set
text:
When we received this phone from Amazon, my daughter was ecstatic. Phone was great, BUT she could not send or receive messages with photos. Went to T-Mobile and spent several hours with their people trying to determine the problem and fix it. The problem: the phone would not connect to a data (2G/3G) network. In the end, the T-Mobile folks declared that the phone was defective. We returned the phone through Amazon (which worked very smoothly and quickly) and purchased another DEFY through a different vendor on Amazon, and when it arrived, it had the same problem. After deciding that the likelihood of two separate vendors selling defective phones was unlikely, I did some "research" on my own and discovered that the actual problem was that the APN was not setup in the phone (actually found the settings on T-Mobile's web site). After inputting those settings, the phone works like a charm!

My only complaint about the phone is that Motorola, the vendor, or whoever is selling these phones does not include the information about setting up the APN even if that meant consumers had to contact their service providers for these settings! It was a very simple "fix" in the end, but we went through lot of unnecessary run-around to discover it.

title: Buy for looks, not for protection
text:
I've had this case for some time now, lets say 9 months or so. I rate the case only 3 stars because I dropped my phone from 4 feet on to concrete back in October-ish and the screen definitely cracked with the grip shell on. The phone was still usable, but it was VERY disappointing. Message: Buy this phone for the grip, not protection.

Pros:
The grip is an improvement over the smooth basic shell here in New England especially with gloves and in snow/ice/mix conditions when the elements attack you.

Cons:
However, in warmer weather the added bulk to the phone adds a second or three to slipping it in and out of your pocket which becomes slightly annoying.

Neither here, nor there:
I love the Seahawks colors and both colors give the staid all-black device a very vibrant feel.

Verdict:
My advice, buy both the grip shell and a color regular shell so you can trade-off at whim.

title: Beautiful phone.
text:
I am a long time Nokia fan but these days they aren't what they used to be and no longer make anything that takes my fancy so I decided to look around for something else.These days it seams most people are obsessed with smart phones and the high street shops have little else except for very basic and cheap feature phones I however wanted something a bit better than what is on offer.

One of the annoying problems I have is my phone gets switched on and off at times accidentally due to being knocked in my pocket or bag and even occasionally makes unwanted 999 calls all of which are quite inconvenient.Therefore I decided to look around for a flip phone.There isn't much available these days except for the Doro phones but they tend to be too basic and have short battery lives. I also required an internet capable phone for occasional use and large buttons luckily for me I came across a Samsung phone so decided to go on their website where I found the GT-c3590 and thought this is just what I need.

Firstly let me say that this phone looks gorgeous in all three available colours although mine is the silver version.This phone is well built and has a great keypad although it could do with a skin as the phone is quite slippery.The interface is reasonable straight forward although not in Nokia's league and even has a few more welcome features than my old phone one being a dictionary.The other applications I like are also present those being a note taker,countdown timer and stop watch,converter,calendar and reminders as well as an alarm clock of course.The Opera browser also works well and is much faster than expected.

Using the phone is a pleasant experience once set up with your own preferences although strangely you cannot play music from the memory card without transferring the file to the phone memory and as this phone has so little it won't be able to hold many files but this is only a minor gripe.Using the phone for talking is very clearly and especially good in noisy environments probably because both my ear and mouth are covered by the phone.Texting is great once you disable the dreaded predictive text function.

Battery life is always an issue for me but as long as I get a week out of it I will be happy.So far I have made about 45 minutes of calls,gone on the internet for 30 minutes and listened to the radio for about half an hour and the phone still registers fully charged after 1 and a half s days use which is pretty good to me.

Well so far I am quite happy with this phone but if I were to pick holes it would be getting the instructions in two foreign languages and having an EU power lead although provided with an adaptor.
