title: Great Value - Maybe - Returned it
text:
I waited until I had this phone a few days before writing this review. Like everyone else, I am impressed at the build quality, lack of lag, call quality and overall value for a price under $300. But as has been pointed out by others, Huawei has quite a job ahead of it trying to make it in the US. As a country people in the US are used to buying subsidized $700 phones such as the iphone and top tier Samsungs for $199. Of course, they were paying thousands for these phones in the "rent to own" model where the top tier cell providers charged insane prices while keeping you in a forced contract. Thanks to T-Mobile Americans are finally starting to realize that buying your own phone outright saves you a lot of money in the long run - but top tier phones cost a lot more than $299. Assuming you're OK with a large phone, this is probably as good as it gets for $299.00. The build quality is not fancy, but it is solid and not cheap feeling for the price. The speed and lack of lag is excellent for normal day to day use, and the camera while not top notch is good for what people normally use a cell phone for. As for the cons:

(1) I've used Android since it first came out and am having real problems with Huawei's "Emotion" UI. I realize that I can easily install a third party launcher, but I want to give it a bit of time to see if I get used to it. My problem with it is that it's pretty ugly (the icons and so forth look like something a fourth grader would have drawn) and the lack of an app drawer means that every time you install an app you either have to have it on a screen or place it in a drawer. This isn't a deal breaker since you can install an app launcher if you want, and for people who aren't used to Android it may be easier to learn.

(2) I went into this knowing full well that there may never be a software update. Huawei is in the same position that the Japanese and South Koreans were in a few years back. They are unknown in the US and have a horrible reputation for not updating their phones. In terms of economics they won't sell enough of these to make it worthwhile to update Android in this model. The way I see it we're the first group of beta testers for Huawei in the US. A lot of people have asked me about this phone and I've been very complimentary so we're introducing the brand to the US. Now it's Huawei's turn. If they update Android at least twice in a somewhat timely fashion I'll continue to buy from them and help to spread the word, and they could easily become the next Samsung. If they don't, I'll use the phone for a while and pass it on to someone else (at $299 it's not the end of the world), but I won't buy another Huawei and will stick to more established brands.

So to sum it up, this is a great mid-tier phone at a very fair price. If you go into this not expecting any software updates and knowing that you're not buying the very latest in technology you'll be very happy. And Huawei gets an opportunity to prove to the US market that they can be relied on - they can either step up to the plate and make a big splash in the US, or they can move on to the next phone to make a quick buck, abandon the first people who purchased their phones in the US, and sink into obscurity.

Update: Unfortunately I had to return the phone and case today, but I guess I learned a valuable lesson by buying a no-name brand. I don't have T-Mobile LTE where I live, but I went to Atlanta this week where they have a strong T-Mobile LTE signal and saw that my display just showed 4G (not 4G Lte as is shown in Huawei's images). I went to a T-Mobile store where they exchanged my SIM card for a new one which worked fine in the store phones, but did not display LTE on the Huawei. I contacted Huawei support which could not even tell me if the display is supposed to show LTE but instead had me restore the phone (didn't help) and then told me that my carrier would have to help. T-Mobile doesn't sell this phone, so they did the best they could. I couldn't look at a manual (none up on the Huawei site) and when I asked Amazon users if any of them were seeing LTE on their screen no one answered. To top it off on the drive back home running just two apps (Google Maps for navigation and their music player) the phone would constantly slow down, inform me that I needed to close one of the two power intensive apps, and start bogging down with just these two apps running. Even my old original note with much less RAM and a slower processor has no problem running these two apps. As far as I could tell there is a huge memory leak in their software, since with just these 2 apps running the phone was running out of available RAM. Given Huawei's abysmal lack of help and information I decided that I would be better off with a Nexus 5. It's only $50 more. I'll miss the larger screen, battery and SD expansion, but at least it has current software, a manual and a large and involved user community. I may have gotten a defective phone, or else there may have been something else I should have done, but if this is the way Huawei is going to introduce themselves to the US they should save their time and money and not even try. I've been using Android phones since the original Nexus so I'm pretty tech savy, but when a company can't even tell you what icons are supposed to show on the display I can forsee a lot of unhappy customers. Amazon (as always)was great about taking it back.

title: While Consumer wasn't a good fit for me
text:
After years and years of being an unlimited data customer with Verizon, they decided to hike mu plan by $20 a month, putting me at about 130/month (with a corporate discount). That's just too much money, plus my old Motorola Bionic was on its last legs. I decided to look into the world of pre-pay and stumbled across this phone while browsing Consumer Cellular. While Consumer wasn't a good fit for me, I discovered this phone is also available as just a plain unlocked GSM phone, opening the way to lots of pre-paid carriers.

There are other comparable phones from Asus, Blu, ZTE, One Plus and others, but this phone seemed to have the best reviews, plus to big positives - a 6.1" screen and an approximately 4000mAMP battery. Spec-wise its mid-tier with an older Snapdragon 410 processor although it does run at 1.5GHz rather than the more typical 1.2.

Huawei puts their own interface over Android, but it isn't too bad. the only real drawback is there is no app tray, but this is easily remedied by just grouping apps into folders, if you don't want an icon for every single app on your homescreens. Bloatware is very minimal, a plus.

I've been very impressed with this phone over the six weeks I've owned. Its a low pixel density screen, but still looks plenty sharp, has good colr and brightness, and is easily viewable in bright sunlight. Battery life is outstanding. I get through the workweek one one charge, with fairly light use. Standby drain is less than 0.5% per hour.

Everything on the phone just works right. The radios and sensors are particularly good. It locks on to a cell or data signal instantly, wifi is also very quick to lock, as is GPS. Even flagship phones sometimes can't accomplish this as well. Call quality is quite good, speakerphone is adequately loud and very clear. The camera is very easy to use and has several modes in attempts to improve picture quality. Some editing is also available. Picture quality is pretty good. I'm sure there are better phones out there for photography, but pictures are reasonbly sharp, noise-
free. Auto-focus is quick, and burst, landscape and HDR are all available. I haven't tried videos.

Apps open very quickly and transitions on the phone are very snappy. The low pixel scree, the moderate processor and the huge battery are a great combination that make for a package greater than the some of its parts. The one drawback, maybe a killer, for some, is that the phone ships with 4.3. This model is nearly two years old and Android has progressed to 6.0. Huawei's site as a 5.0 build available for download to your micro SD card. Installation isn't simple and it wipes your phone. some people have reported some bugs, others not. I'm sticking with 4.3. If it ain't broke, don't fix it. Android updated its OS so frequently that you can drive yourself crazy trying to have the latest, and a new system isn't always better.

Overall, one of the best purchases I've made. Discover Card doubles the warranty to 2 years, so I'm not too worried about reliability, especially given the above average build quality and the lack of glitches I've encountered Highly recommended.

title: Ascend Mate 2 by Huawei is Top Notch!
text:
The Ascend Mate 2 by Huawei has proven to be an exceptional value. It boasts an amazing economy price for a unit that easily competes with units twice its price. There have been many reviews written about this unit, most good, some not.

After doing very thorough research for several days on many models, including unlocked and carrier provided, I went with the Huawei Ascend Mate 2. We purchased ours directly through Huawei, which provided over $200 in accessories and other freebies for FREE. Their customer service was most exceptional, answering all questions in immediate fashion and I received my phone in less than 24 business hours. My main concern in contacting Huawei was to determine whether they would be upgrading to Lollipop 5.0 in 2015 and their answer was an emphatic YES as of 1/2/2015.

An additional concern was AT&T compatibility. No worries here. As soon as I got the phone, we followed the quick installation instructions and placed the SIM card in the phone. The battery was 2/3rds charged so immediately upon startup the phone recognized my AT&T plan/signal and I was in business. In fact, the signal is way better than my previous iPhone.

The camera is better, the sound quality is superior, the screen is obviously better and the additional memory card slot makes this a keeper. Many phones of higher quality omit this feature.

Perhaps the biggest conversation piece is the battery size. Its carries a MEGA charge! You can use the phone all day and it will not give up on you. In fact you can charge your weakling buddy's phone when theirs starts to waiver.

I received a bluetooth speaker and two way charge cable as well as free activation and minutes from Huawei from their site. Amazon prime is a great deal but could not pass up all the freebies with the same warranties over at the Huawei site. BTW, for the size, the speakers sound awesome!

I am extremely pleased with this phone and will soon be saying goodbye to contracts from AT&T!!! While I appreciate their signal strength in Denver and their quality, contracts are terrible way to bind business. Customer service, value and quality signals alone should keep customers coming back for more business.

For any of you who are concerned about the AT&T compatibility, worry no longer. It works great, especially in my dungeon where my signal was previously a dead zone! :D Happy! Happy! Happy!

title: Definetely a Keeper - But for How Long?
text:
Switching from a standard smartphone to this phablet was one of my best recent decisions for increasing productivity. Now I have it all in one and do not need to carry several devices with me when on the road. The large crisp screen with its very well sized keyboard allows me to comfortably read and write all my daily correspondence without even turning on my computer. This is such an improvement compared to the cramped little screen and typing experience on my former phones which were just good for brief messages and emails. Not to mention all the other advantages of having a phone with a larger screen at hand that also gives me internet access wherever there is phone reception and with that all the productivity features that today's android devices offer. My former phones were so called high end brands. But except for the little bit higher resolution I don't experience any difference in speed and performance. (Alright, I am not a dedicated gamer and competent about higher processor power demands.) The only real difference in my daily handling of this phone is its absolutely incredible battery life ! It makes my life (and work) so much easier since I have not always to watch the battery level and worry about a second power source to not lose connection to the outer world. This thing goes on and on and on for days.

First I was a bit hesitating in purchasing this relatively unknown brand. I was just browsing for a phone with the best battery life. Good thing I listened to all those positive reviews here on this page. I love this well built device which handles everything I throw at it with ease. And above and beyond - call quality is incredible on both ends, which to me with having some hearing difficulties is the most important factor of a phone's functionality. I couldn't be happier, and THIS phone will be a keeper.

Why did I still give only 4 stars? Well, there are some things that deserve improvement, such as:

1. Huawei tries to find its place in the US market among those already highly competitive and established brands. The device definitely shows the manufacturer's capability and could generate a broad customer pool. However, in order to also generate brand loyalty for long term business the manufacturer has to build customer trust and brand identification. The key for that is customer service. And here Huawei has still a lot to learn about the American customer and his expectations.
I don't understand why Huawei is not providing a dedicated section for customer reviews and a customer forum on their page so they can build up a user community for tips and troubleshooting questions. I can't judge their call-in service yet, which is only reachable during office hours. As a busy customer I don't want to spend valuable workday time on the phone for a technical question that could easily be looked up on their web page.
(UPDATE: The manual can now be found on their Huawei/US page, and they also started a Q&A section.)
UPDATE 2: All Support info for Mate2 on their US-page is gone (they focus now on the Mate7). But you can find the manual by going to their gethuawei page, go to support, click on the "registration" of the pull-down menu. You don't have to register. Just scroll all the way down. There you'll see another support button with a little picture of the Mate2. Click on the Mate2 link, then click on the support tab, then on the manual button and the manual download page will open. (Pretty awkward for customer premium support).

2. In order to give a customer the feeling that he made a lasting investment in purchasing a Huawei device, a clear statement about IF and WHEN the manufacturer will provide software updates is crucial. There are already several important applications out there that require android 4.4 or higher. A lot of questions about that in different customer reviews as well as on the blog of their web page remained unanswered. Their answer in their Q&A section says that the phone's software can be updated, but they don't know if and when (hmm...) If Huawai customers are left alone on this issue, it will quickly build up a Huawei image associated with a cheap, throwaway "China" product that will be outdated pretty soon. Those first impressions will stick in the people's mind and it will take a lot of additional effort to turn this image around (if ever).
Huawei's silence about their update policy will certainly backfire against their own marketing strategy: To purchase your own device for independence from a carrier. Well, a contract phone can at least be upgraded when it becomes obsolete. But spending $300 for a device that might already be trash next year is still too much for most of us.

4. Some design improvements:

a) Since this is a factory unlocked gsm device, people are encouraged to shop for the most economical carrier. Among those is t-mobile/metro pcs with their great non-contract fees. Their downfall however is that their coverage even in well designated areas has quite some reception holes. T-mobile made this up with their opportunity for wifi calling, which I used in my office that otherwise gave me very poor reception. The Mate 2 does not have this capability. Since I like my new phone so much, I was forced to switch carriers with better signals in my area. Not every person will take this step, and Huawei would be well advised to add the wifi calling feature in their software update (if there will be one). Even Apple recognized the market importance of this issue and integrated it in their IOS8.

b) The location of a protruding multifunctional power/locking and wake-up button on the right side is a design flaw. My hand accidentally touches this button all the time and locks my screen in the middle of phone calls and other important tasks. When carrying the phone in the pocket, it sometimes wakes up by itself and does operations on its own. My only remedy was the purchase of a bulky protection case that covers this button and makes it less sensitive. However, this takes a lot of the phone's elegance away and adds significantly to its size and weight. A much better solution would have been the traditionally plane power button (may be on the top of the phone) and a mechanical wake-up/home-page button somewhere on the front.

Besides those issues I only can agree with all the other positive reviewers. This phone is a great device. I hope that Huawei listens to their customers. Then it could definitely be a brand to also look for in the future.

title: Huawei Ascend Mate 2 - A fabulous phablet at an even more fabulous price!!!
text: This is my first "smart phone".  I had relied on a simple flip phone for the occasional emergency phone call till I got this "phablet" - a phone combined with a tablet computer.  It's huge - even larger than the iPhone 6.  But I love it in part because of its large size.  One of its greatest features is its enormous battery, which I understand lasts twice as long as any other smart phone out there.  The large screen also makes it easy to type on its virtual keyboard, to see small print on web pages, etc. Under the hood of this thing is a great deal of computing power!  Take your pick - it's either a very large phone or a very small and powerful computer.  I have rather large hands and I still use both hands to control it. That's fine with me because that's how I like to use it, but if you're looking to operate your phone with one hand it may be too large. It has as much power and greater speed than my laptop computer which is only a year or so old!  Of course its memory capacity is smaller (16 Gb) than my laptop but it can easily be fleshed out with up to 32 Gb with a micro SD card (that you must purchase separately. I wanted this phone largely for international travel and though I haven't had it on the road overseas yet it looks very promising.  The huge battery of course will be a plus. It has good Wi-Fi sensitivity and this will be good when Wi-Fi connections are lousy in airports, hotels, etc. Because it is "unlocked" I can purchase SIM cards in other countries and stay on line with data and/or phone virtually anywhere in the world. I cannot speak with authority about the Android operating system provided (I've only used Windows in the past)  but I've been amazed at its capabilities and at the programs installed. My only complaint with this device is that the built in camera takes rather lack luster photos.  It has plenty of megapixels but pictures tend to come out rather dull and colorless, especially in low light situations.  This camera will do in a pinch but I'll still be taking an additional camera with my on my next trip to gather those beautiful vacation photos.  Overall I'm extremely satisfied with this fabulous phablet and given that it's less than half the price of a comparable iPhone, I'd buy one again in a minute!

title: Great if you know what you are getting - Updated 6/25/15!
text:
First and foremost, this is not a flagship phone. The only spec this phone offers that is worth mentioning is it's 3900mah battery since it is the biggest of any phone available. That being said, if you want a BIG phone, this could be exactly what you want.

While you'd think the only difference between the white and black model is the color, you'd be wrong. While the black model has a textured back to reduce fingerprints and improve grip, the white model has a slick plastic back reminiscent of the Galaxy S 3. I went with the white model since I was going to put it in a case anyways but the difference is something to be aware of.

This phone is BIG, but if you are like me and use two hands on your phone no matter the size then the only part of you that will complain is your pocket. In regular sized (male) pockets the phone just fits inside, but you do get a slight impression that you are wearing shin-guards on your thighs. The phone is noticeably heavier than your average phone, but if you are used to using a tablet then it shouldn't be an issue.

The screen is very nice with good viewing angles, although the color was a bit warmer than I was used to. It works well for reading or watching videos, but you may notice the lower resolution (720p) when zoomed out when web-browsing. The screen itself is larger than my last phone (Nexus 4) and is definitely a key reason to get this phone.

The Camera is a step-up from my old phone, but slightly more average than I was hoping. Colors are generally accurate, but very fine detail doesn't come through very well, especially in low-light. The Front camera was more of the same, but it was nice that has a wide lens to capture a larger area. The cameras are the same ones as seen in the LG G3, OnePlus One, and other flagship phones so software may improve this. The stock camera app can't mute the shutter sound so may want to use something else regardless. Overall pretty good for a smartphone, but definitely won't replace your DSLR. The camera can also store data to the MicroSD, so make sure to get one if you want turn this into your main shooter.

The performance is more than adequate. When phones nowadays have more power than most people will ever use, this phone brings in just enough tech that you should be able to do anything the newest phones can do. All games and benchmarks play without a hitch, but some intense apps like high-end emulators (mainly PPSSPP) may not run as smoothly as the newest phones. Since this is such a specialized circumstance (and since even the highest-end phones can have issues on the same applications) I don't count it as a loss.

Calls sound average compared to modern phones and so does it's rear speaker. Very much equal to some of the best I've used in a phone, but that only means it's what you should expect. It does support HD Voice so if you are coming from an older device your may notice a nice quality improvement when calling someone who also has a newer device providing your carrier supports this. T-Mobile does.

The battery life is amazing. Even my first day with the phone and using the 63% charge the phone came with, I still got over 5 hours of on-screen time while running every benchmark in the book before I finally plugged in with 10% battery. That's longer than I've ever gotten on my other phones. It's safe to expect 9-10 hours of constant usage before needing to plugin, or 2-3 days of normal use. This was on the "Smart" power-saving mode, but there is also the "Endurance" mode if you want even more battery or "Normal" if you want a bit more performance. You can even charge other phones!

Overall this phone only does battery extremely well, but does everything else so adequately that it's really a steal for the price. The phone does run Android 4.3, but a 4.4 update is promised and hopefully more. Basically a Jumbo (if not slightly faster) Moto G LTE, it should keep everyone in need of a large phone satisfied.

****UPDATES****

6/27 Update:
There is a thin, slightly raised, plastic strip that wraps the outside of the front of a device, including the earpiece. While not uncommon on a tablet, the proximity to the earpiece gives the phone a hard edge and can cause discomfort if you hold phones tightly to your ear. You can shift the phone to alleviate this, but is something to be aware of if you normally press your phone to your ear. The official flip-case adds padding if you call when it is closed so this could be a non-issue if this applies to you.

Also the vibration on my device is on the tiny side.

6/28 Update:
Everything continues to run well and phone is very stable. No crashes, FC, or anything of that kind since I got it. Battery life continues to be a non-issue. I was able to get 8+ hours of screen time including 4 hours of internet video and 1 of gaming. The phone gets a little warm near the camera when gaming, but not bad overall. Everything I've tried has run correctly.

The LTE on this phone is fast despite not having the latest tech inside. I was able to get 76mbps down and 23mbps up on T-Mobile in Seattle with their new faster speeds.

The area around the back, home, and menu button is a gray color, something that makes it stick out more than I prefer. Just a style choice but I wish it was black, especially on videos that don't auto-hide them. Root seems to be illusive on this device if that is something you need. There aren't too many useless apps, although the ones that just link to Huawei's website seem pointless and can't be removed currently.

7/7 Update:
Everything I ask this phone to do it continues to do admirably. I recently put it up against a Oneplus One (OPO) and it compared surprisingly well. The Mate2 was always a hair slower, but the screen experience was almost identical despite the resolution difference and the battery life obviously did better. The OPO rear camera took much better pictures despite having the same cameras as the Mate2 (which has me hoping for future optimizations), but the front camera on the Mate2 blew the OPO's away. The front camera may be average as far as cameras go, but it really does well when compared to what the competition brings.

I did have some MMS issues with the phone (something others haven't?), but all it took was adding in a new APN profile to fix this. YMMV.

Huawei has assured me that Android 4.4 is coming in July or August, so hopefully this phone keeps getting better!

7/30 Update:
This phone is great for people who use their phone a lot, but it is also great for people who barely use their phone. I was able to get EIGHT (8) days of use on battery with wifi and bluetooth enabled. This was with only 1 hour of screen time, but for people who use their phones as true emergency devices (of just don't call or play games a lot) this lets you go a full week between charges.

10/2 Update:
STILL no 4.4 update which is a bummer. Root is now easily accessible with info on XDA if you need that. Still hopeful and still a great phone, but hoping the ROM community steps in if Huawei doesn't release 4.4 which is already out for the Chinese Mate 2.

10/28 Update:
Changing rating to 3 stars. Phone still works as expected, but Huawei confirmed phone is no longer getting any updates as they promised. As this phone is already one OS update behind and will be two versions behind in about a week, I can no longer recommend this phone or this companies products. No ROM support to prolong it's life. Get the new Moto G instead when they offer an LTE model.

6/25/15 Update:
Huawei backpedaled and Lollipop should come to this phone soon-ish. This phone is now a year old and Android 5.0 will be replaced soon so good news for people still with this phone, but still wouldn't recommend this phone to new buyers due to age. At this point wait for something better.

I'll keep this updated if I find anything else!

text: Update: I've been using this phone for 5 months now and have not had any issues with it. In fact about 3 months ago I bought another phone just like this one for my wife so she would leave mine alone. She has had no problems at all with her phone either so I may update my star rating later if neither of us have any issues over the next couple of months. First off I want to make it clear that I really like this phone and I have to give Amazon 5 stars on their return policies as this phone did push that. Like I said I really like the phone but I did have some problems starting out. With phone number 1 it arrived late on a Friday so I spent most of my Friday evening moving everything from my Galaxy S3 over to my new Huawei Mate 2. I tried putting my sim card in there and it would not recognize it so I figured I must need a newer more up to date sim card since mine was 3 years old.  So using my home WI-FI and other apps I got everything moved over and operating on my new Huawei mate 2 phone. So Saturday afternoon I went to the local T-Mobile store to see about getting a new sim card. They informed me that my card should work in it but once again the phone wouldn’t recognize it.  So one of the employees put their sim card into it and once again it didn’t see the sim card. After numerous attempts to get the phone to work I was told the bad news that I had a defective phone.  So as reluctant that I was to have to move everything back to my old phone I didn’t have much choice. I contacted Amazon customer service and they overnighted me a replacement phone. The first thing I did was try my sim card in it and it came right up Yay!!! So I moved everything off the broken Huawei to the replacement phone. Everything was going great but then I noticed that I haven’t received any emails all day and the weather app temperature outside had not changed. So did a speed test and discovered I had no data connection but I did have cell phone service so I thought well maybe I need to reboot since I had made so many changes to the phone. So I did that and low and behold I had data again everything was great again. The next day I noticed once again that I had phone service but no data so I rebooted the phone and all was great again for about an hour. Then I noticed the temperature app wasn’t updating again. I decided to send myself an email from our house cell phone which is also on T-Mobile after nearly 30 minutes no email again. I checked my other cell phone and it showed it as sent and I checked the data speed and was running at a very good speed on my Galaxy S2 home phone. So I did a data speed check on my Huawei Mate 2. Nothing once again so I rebooted it and had my data back once again. Then about 2 hours later no mail and no temperature change. Checked the data speed and once again zero until I rebooted the phone again. At this point I knew I was dealing with a phone that going to have to be rebooted 6 or 8 times a day if you wanted to get any data from it. So I once again contacted Amazon Customer Service and they again overnighted me a replacement phone. At this point I have become an expert on transferring apps and data from one phone to another. I’m going out on a limb here in following the old saying 3rd time is a charm as I am now 2 days into my new Huawei Mate 2 phone and at the risk of jinxing it so far there have been no problems with this phone. I will update my review if this changes anytime soon. I still recommend the phone because when it works that huge screen makes it so easy to read news and watch movies and TV on. Once again I have to give Amazon Customer Service 5 stars and I would have given this phone 5 stars had I not encountered 2 bad phones in a row. But as stated I’m keeping this one and I hope it performs as well as it does today 3 or 4 years from now. My Galaxy S3 is almost 4 and it still works fine I was just looking for something with a bigger screen as my eyes aren’t nearly as good as they once were. But yes I would recommend a person to buy it, but by it from Amazon in case you have any trouble from the start as they have some of the best customer service I have ever seen.

You may want to do a serious cost & spec comparison between this phone and the Asus Zenphone 2. The AZ2 is slightly more expensive but comes with some much better specs. Although Asus support has a bad reputation, it's well rated.

-An app called stock spy, which I use frequently, would not refresh, sync or function. For some reason, the phone was blocking the app from accessing real time stock data. Perhaps it is a Chinese censorship block, I don't know. The fix was to use a VPN (I use 'private internet access', the green dude) and everything worked immediately

-Yes you can get a free wifi hotspot with this phone, if you know what to tweak. Google it.

title: Superb phablet style phone for the cost, you can't go wrong!
text:
I've had the Huawei Ascend Mate 2 for over 8 months now and I have to say it might just be my favorite smartphone of all time!

Each individual specification may not be the most impressive, but when you put them all together with the price it's just hard to beat a phone like this!

Let's just do a pros and cons here:

Pros:

+ Qualcomm Snapdragon 400 at 1.6ghz paired with 2GB of system RAM makes this phone really peppy
+ 16GB of onboard flash memory supplimented by a MicroSD slot that allows for up to 128GB additional storage.
+ HUGE screen at 6.1 inches with rich color and good viewing angles.
+ Battery life that's literally the best I've ever seen on a phone. 3900mah rated which lasts me two days with heavy usage!
* Full LTE band support for both AT&T and T-Mobile here in the USA
+ Really low cost for a 6 inch phablet!

Cons:

- Screen isn't 1080p, it's only 720p. Not a big deal especially for this price.
- Ships with a dated Android 4.3 Jelly Bean (Huawei is still promising a Lollipop update soon)
- Non replaceable battery

I absolutely love this phone and will continue to recommend it to friends, especially once the Lollipop update rolls out!

Like in the middle of a conversation, Airplane mode would turn on even if I was on speakerphone. Since I didn't know what had happened the other person couldn't call me back and I couldn't call out. So look at your notification area for the little airplane. Also, it automatically stops ringing the phone and callers go immediately to voicemail (their contact is not set to "all calls to voicemail", the phone is not in airplane mode when this happens, and the volume setting is not at zero). The wi-fi and bluetooth automatically turn off, screen brightness automatically reduces to zero. These are just a few of the settings which automatically turn on or off or down.
I bought this to be a phone and that is the most problematic app of all.
I must power off this phone several times a day to get it to work reasonably well.

title: A very responsive, very fast phone, that gives you a lot of room to write and move and view content
text:
[[VIDEOID:94ef37caa04bba023d04676a42443925]] Except for a brief stint with a cheap Nokia unsmart phone early on, I've always been an iPhone guy.

This phone, which I've had a chance to try out for a few weeks for the purpose of a review, could truly convert me. Of course, my teenaged daughter, who needed a new phone anyhow, very quickly wanted to take it over. She loves it. She especially likes that the screen size lets her do more with photography editing and drawing apps that she likes to use.

While one of the major selling points of the phone is that it's unlocked and so you can sign up for a plan without a contract, I'm already under contract with AT&T and have a few phones with them on a family plan. Adding this to our plan adds very little to our monthly bill so that made the most sense. All it took was adding one of AT&T's micro SIM cards and getting them to add this to the account. I plopped in the SIM card and it connected right away and was ready to go. Setup was very easy. When you turn on the phone it walks you through the process. It works best if you have a Google account and sign in with that, and then it sets up your mail and imports your bookmarks into Chrome and everything. So simple. Works great.

I was happily surprised that everything it does is very intuitive. There are a lot of features packed into this little phone, and it's easy to figure out how to use them. Most functions give you information about what they do, and most of them are very intuitive and clear. I had never used anything but an iPhone and in minutes I was working on this one just like it had always been my phone.

The home button is always at the bottom; you can just press another button to get to any open app. Slide down from the top and all of the settings are easily accessible.

What stands out:

-Built for Speed:
It is fast. I have to say, it is in almost every way noticeably faster than my iPhone 5C. I didn't expect that. I can run both of them side by side, using the same wifi or LTE connection, and apps open faster on the Mate2, there's no lag time ... it even surfs the web faster. I'm very impressed.

-Lots of Power:
The battery lasts a LONG time. It's a 3900 mAh battery - compared to the roughly 1500 mAh battery on the iPhone 5C. If I use my iPhone regularly, it runs out of juice somewhere in the afternoon -- of course, I charge it in the car, so that helps to make it work. With the Mate2, you can seriously run a couple days on a single charge. I still plug it in every night, but I've never had a problem with it running out of power. You can even charge other items that use micro-USB from the phone, if you have a micro-USB to micro-USB cable. (Also: it doesn't run hot. Sometimes my iPhone seems to get warm. I've never noticed that with this one.)

-Lots of memory:
It comes with 16GB of memory and 2GB of RAM, but unlike the iPhone, the memory is expandable on this one. You can add a microSD card in a slot that sits underneath the back cover, next to the SIM card slot, in order to add up to an additional 32GB of memory -- I've read that you can use bigger micro SD cards, but haven't tested that. That's a lot of photos and songs, and a decent amount of space for video storage.

-Big screen:
The screen is quite a bit bigger than you get on any iPhone. With it's 6.1inch screen, it nearly splits the difference between an iPhone and an iPad mini. The image is HD and looks quite good. It doesn't quite have the pixel density (pixels per square inch) as the iPhone 5c (or any "retina" display device), but it still looks quite good. Video looks great. Plus the extra size really makes a difference when you're going on websites and trying to read articles, which I do quite a bit.

-Cool Camera Features:
The basic camera is nice, and takes pictures and video of at least comparable quality to those I take with my iPhone. (Actually, the main camera seems to be slightly better than the one on the iPhone. I do like that the front camera has a wider angle.) There are some cool features built in, though, like the ability to take a "Groufie" -- which is like a panorama but facing you, and allows you to get a "selfie" shot that includes a bunch of people. You can't do that with the iPhone camera app, since the panorama function there automatically goes to the front camera. Another fairly cool feature is "smile capture" which basically means you can aim it at somebody's face and it takes a picture when it detects a smile. You can also set it to shoot when you talk loudly, so you can set the camera at a distance and don't need to press a button to shoot. The video shoots at 1080p, 30fps, and it looks quite good.

-Haptic feedback:
I was surprised how much I like the little buzz that the camera does when you successfully touch a button. You get a little feedback on your fingers when you type, for example. You can turn that off in settings if you don't like it, but I was surprised at first and then I really got to like it. I was thinking I might turn it off just to save the battery, but given the battery's serious power, I'll just leave it on.

-Built-in GPS:
It's very reliable, and gives good instructions. I've just used it with Google Maps, and it works great.

-Very customizable user interface:
You can change the background and wallpaper in a snap, you can adjust which applications are directly accessible from the lock screen, you can place your three main contacts front and center on the home page so that you can easily connect with them. It gives you a lot of control over accessibility, with too many options to list here.

About the video: I know it looks a bit grainy, since I shot it on a little camera. It's just here to give a sense for the phone in action.

Summing up: this is a very fast and responsive unlocked phone, that is superior in many ways to much more expensive phones. If you like a larger phone, that gives you some of the benefits of a tablet but the convenience and flexibility of a phone, this would be a very good option.

title: Not bad, wanted a large screen and good for the price.  NO support though.
text:
I've had my Huawei Mate 2 for over 8 mos. now. I am using it with prepaid AT&T in Phoenix area. It took me a bit to get used to an unlocked phone w/o providers operating systems, but I really like this phone with some exceptions. I've had a couple issues:

Proximity sensor position is in the corner. It should be more centered with a phone this size.. It easily turns on the screen when holding the phone with your shoulder while on a call.

I can't get any "call announcer" apps to work properly. Huawei should include a good one that pauses your ringtone when it announces the caller. To me this is a basic feature that should be on every phone.

GPS signal for navigation gets lost often! A real deal killer when you rely on navigation.

The phone does get quite hot while playing videos and I do get an occasional electrical "zzz' sound sometimes when changing apps.

Very limited selection of cases available for this phone. Have problem with camera flash reflecting off some cases, washing out the photo. Camera can be slow.

Support is non-existent. Huawei's support page is useless. If they would fix these things, I would definitely buy this phone again. But it's a gamble the way it is now.

Bluetooth works well. I LOVE the screen size - this is why I bought it. I actually found I like not having an app drawer, though that really bothered me for quite a while.

Update: 4/11/2017 - I really love this phone, EXCEPT the loss of the GPS signal that always occurs when I most need it. Customer Support is awful. My next phone better have local support or I'm not buying it.

Update: 5/25/2018 - Despite the above, I still love this phone. In 6 months or so I might replace it. It is starting to get a bit slow, but is still perfectly usable. I also plan on giving it my elderly mother so she has a big screen to play her games.

title: Best Bang for the buck!
text:
I ordered this, on a Saturday, received it on a Wednesday!
The reason I ordered it, was because another "flagship killer" was unable to produce enough fo their "killer" phones to meet demand.
Very high quality packaging, arrived in good condition. Turning it on, the battery was at 46%. I just set it up using wi-fi, synced my
apps, set up email etc without issue. I don't know what people are worrying about, with it "only" being a 720p screen, it looks fantastic
sitting next to my now retired Galaxy note1. The size is NOT that bad either. Spec wise, my note1 and this are pretty much the
same width & thickness, and only around 1/2" longer, but, with those reduced bezels on the Mate2, that gives me 8/10th of an inch
MORE screen size! Screen is bright & clear, no bad pixels. I shaved my standard size sim card down to fit it, came right up in H+
mode (shows 4g on the display). Need to stop by Walmart (I'm on straight talk) and get a new sim so the LTE light will come on.
I use bluetooth, and never the handset microphone or speaker, bluetooth is CRYSTAL clear, better than my note. The ring, sounds and other speaker sound is VERY loud. This one came with 4.3, which isn't a deal killer for me, it's an upgrade from 4.1.2 that I was using.
I don't use the built in launcher, but opt for Nova since that is what I'm use to.
Now, for that HUGE battery! Left this morning at 100% charged. After a couple hours of phone usage, few dozen emails, web surfing, text messaging, I still have around 90% left! It might take me a few days just to run the battery down, which is one of the main reasons I got this.
I hate running out of juice.
The camera, has some nifty features and the image quality is top notch. The built in software is pretty good, but I'm use to Camera FV-5, and the macro mode works pretty darn good!
Huawei hit one out of the park, in my opinion. If you like big screens, you'll love this!

Update, still going strong over a year after purchase. Huawei did update the device late June 2015, to LL5.1, and also provided an easy way to go back to JB4.3 if you didn't like it. First version of LL does have a couple minor bugs. If you switch the launcher, text messaging etc, from the default to a 3rd party app, once you power off/on, it goes back to the Mate2 default apps. If you are like me and never turn your device off, it's no big deal. The other minor bug is they need to tweak it a bit. It is using just a little more battery than before, but nothing that impacts that 2 day battery life. If I had to do it all over again, I would STILL get this phone, it's a winner!

I like everything about this phone however I feel a few things are not quite as good as others have stated....at least not for me. For instance, the battery life is supposed to last about 2 days or at least 18 hours if being used but I have not come anywhere close to that. I was excited to start using the phone on wireless connection and downloaded a few games to play. The play time was only about 5 hours of constant playing. Also, there were quite a few times where the games would skip momentarily. The games didn't crash but it was quite annoying.
I did a factory reset on my phone to try and see if I could get more battery life but it didn't make any difference. I have to admit that the battery life was the main thing that attracted me to this phone so I am disappointed. I bought 2 of these phones and both are the same so I doubt that I just got a bad one. I should mention that I thought I read that the recharge time is supposed to be awesome..something like 50% charge in 5 mins? (Not sure exactly) but I didn't see that recharge speed either.

On a side note: This phone is very easy to use and I really like the Emotion UI a lot. There are custom UI's out there to make this phone operate similar to a lot of other Android UI's but the stock one is awesome to me. Also, I read step by step instructions on how to load custom mods and how to unlock the bootloader. There are a lot of videos on Youtube but they are all pretty much consolidated on XDA Developers website along with information about other phones too. This is a developer website so they are helpful as well if you choose to explore that sort of stuff. I was told by one person there this phone was among their top 3 phones for everyday use.

I did a little bit more research online and found a youtube video showing how to replace the battery, but all the reviews lead me to believe that the battery was not replaceable. After watching the video, however it seems fairly easy to replace it if you are patient and work carefully.

Really, the only major complaint I have is the battery life not living up to what was advertised although 5 hours of constant use really isn't too bad. Therefore I thought 3 stars was fair considering that the battery life was one of the major reasons I chose this phone to begin with. I may update this review after a little more time with this phone.

title: Spec says it all
text:
Everything works as expected based on its specs. I consider myself a casual android fan, so my expectations and yours may vary. Some of previous phones were Galaxy Nexus, Nexus 4, 5 Moto G, and Optimus F6. I'm on prepaid network, so I resell my phones often. English is my 2nd language so don't bother me with grammar errors ;)
If you're wondering if this phone is too big for you, simply visit your phone stores/Target/Bestbuy and check out LG Flex, Galaxy Mega, or HTC One Max. They all have very similar dimensions as phablet category.

Additiona specs and features you might have missed from elsewhere

-16gb total, 12.69 available, 4.26gb for apps only.
-64gb microSD works, for me at least. It's made by Sandisk, bought from amazon.
-Phone comes with screen protector pre-applied.
-Cover case sold by Huawei(or the ones they gave away for free to early buyers) replaces the old battery cover, keeping the phone thin.
-Cover case's small window shows 2 screens. First screen shows analog clock along with # of missed calls and # of missed texts. Second screen shows limited number of notification logos(Wifi/LTE, signal strength, battery life, additional app notifications), along with the current weather and temperature. Both screens lack details.
-Phone has notification pulse light on top left, but cover case does not have an opening to show it, making the pulse light useless for case users.
-Phone has automatic brightness sensor and FM radio.

Here are the pros and cons

Pros

1.Processor Snapdragon 400 Quadcore+Jelly Bean are good enough to handle most apps smoothly, even desktop browsing. In comparison, I believe Galaxy Mega was S400+dualscore.

2. 2GB of RAM means apps don't relaunch as often, and this is something mostly reserved to high-end phones. One of my complaint from low-mid range phones was that due to many widgets I like to use, my old phones with 1GB of RAM constantly had to relaunch the home launcher after pressing home button. This was not the case with Mate2. Other phone makers need to realize that apps get updates and get bigger as time goes on, and 1GB simply isn't enough anymore.

3.Screen is colorful and crisp, and it looked perfectly fine compare to my older phones. Huge improvements for viewing videos and typing. Very responsive to every touches, and Glove mode does make it extra sensitive and worked fine.

4.I'm using T-mobile in CA, Orange County, and been getting LTE speed of 15-25mbps. YMMV.

5.Battery life is definitely the best feature of this phone, and personally, this justifies the lower-end processor+720p. Too many high-end phones featured larger battery to larger phones with newest, most expensive processor, along with 1080p, draining battery needlessly for my personal needs. Here are some comparisons, and only fair way for you to know how long this phone will last for you, is to look for percentage improvements of one of these phones you owned. Since we all use smartphones differently, you won't get same SoT(screen-on time) like I did. You kinda have to look at it proportionally.
Ascend Mate2=10~ hours of SoT, 1-day. (these numbers are all approximates)
Galaxy Nexus(GSM)=3~ SoT, 230%+ improvement
Nexus 4=-3.5~ SoT, 180%+ improvement
Nexus 5=4.5~ SoT, 120%+ improvement
MotoG=5.5~ SoT, 80%+ improvement
Optimuf F6=6~ SoT, 65%+ improvement
Also impressed that the recharge time(from 10%~) was 2.5~hours.

Cons

1.Stock launcher indeed does not have app drawer, making it a huge hassle to organize apps when you set it up for the first time. Widget list is also limited to 3 per scroll, making it just as annoying. After opening an app from a folder, and then pressing the home button, launcher will lag due to it trying to close the folder you opened earlier, AFTER you press the home button. 3rd party home launcher recommended.

2.Recent app button has "clean-up" feature that can wipe out and close recent apps to free up the memory usage, but it's slow due to unnecessary animations.

3.Its features like one-hand UI and W.O.W(window-on-window) button are bit useless due to lack of supported apps. I only found dial-pad for one-hand UI which I don't use often. W.O.W only supports built-in 4 apps, calendar, text message, note, and calculator. W.O.W button does not disappear during media playbacks like youtube, so it's more of a hassle.

4.Phone's website, [...]/ , is painfuly slow at updating the order status. They are fast at answering calls(phone/chat), but pretty bad at explaining what's going on with your order.

5.Phone's support for flip cover case is limited. Its window lacks details, due to its small window size(3~inch) and phone's low resolution(720p).

Neutral
1.Speak is louder than any Nexus phones, and almost as loud as Optimus F6, which is pretty loud.

2.Phone can charge other micro-USB devices, but cable is sold separately for $10. I received mine for free as early buyer, but you might not. As a one-of-a-kind feature, in my opinion, this cable should've been included with every phones to spread its wealth.

3.As mentioned above, flip-case covers the notification light. Its small window will not turn on nor show anything without pressing the power button, and when it does, there is slight lag/delay while trying to swipe it to the 2nd screen.

4.Camera is almost as good as Nexus 5 phones, which isn't saying much, but perfectly fine for my personal needs.

5.Due to its screen size and 720p resolution, widgets and some apps are simply overblown with less contents to see, requiring more scrolling than other 1080p phones. Still, this is expected given its price.

6.Physical size-wise, phone fits into my pocket just fine. One-hand use is somewhat possible, since I am able to hold it little more firmly by holding onto the flip case's cover with index+middle fingers, while using thumb to navigate.

7.Its Simple Home feature to make it look similar to Window phones, is somewhat useful for maybe my parents. It's something I definitely won't use personally, but would like to see it on other android phones for older generations who are not familiar with android.

Conclusion
There aren't many $300 unlocked phablet in US market, so this phone is definitely a one-of-a-kind for me. Phone truly maximized smartphone's battery life by sacrificing certain features that don't bother many casual consumers, like me(I hit the point where certain processor+certain screen resolutions are "good enough"), while holding onto features that DO matter(LTE speed+2GB RAM). It's common to see mid-range phones with no LTE, or 1GB of RAM, or 8GB of internal storage, or average battery life. I deducted 1-star due to phone not being able to take advantage of its screen size by utilizing multi-window feature, or any features that they came up with and did below-average job at them. This phone is all about hardware, not software. I don't even expect future android or Huawei software updates, and I don't care since its specs satisfy my needs. Battery life, big screen, and good-enough performances.

I started out with a Palm Treo 300 for Sprint in 2002, so I was one of the early smartphone users- back in the day when they offered $10 unlimited data to entice you into buying a $399 device. ( in 2002, unlimited meant you used 50-100mb a month, tops)

Battery life is probably the strongest asset for this device and if I was a road warrior ( I'm retired), having 2 days of usage would be great. title: Great phone, but be ready to install a launcher. *Edit 11/3* * Edit 11/21*
text:
*09/14/15 Edit* there is a publicly available Lollipop download available from Huawei. You can also now get nightly downloads to CyanogenMod, if you're into that. Both have breathed new life into the phone.

*11/21/14 Edit* my review will remain at one star until Huawei actually updates the phone. If they follow through on their recently announced promise to update to Lollipop, I'll change my rating.

*Original review below. I lowered the rating to one star since Huawei went back on their promise to update this phone. I purchased the phone based on a rep saying it would be updated, and now feel deceived.*

Look, this phone does not have flagship specs, OK? It does not have a super-duper hi-res screen. It does not have the latest Snapdragon processor. It does not have as much RAM as some other phones out there. It is probably not going to get many updates (although two separate Huawei reps have told me that it will get a KitKat update in a month or so, but do not expect L). It is so, so very large - when you first pick it up out of the box, you may think you've made a horrible mistake. When you fire it up, you'll find the Emotion UI is...not good.

Now that we've got that out of the way, this is a great phone. It is big. I will repeat that because it bears repeating: IT IS BIG. It is comfortably pocketable if you wear loose clothing, though I would think it would not be in skinny jeans. I have large hands, so I can do some tasks on it one-handed, but most people will need to use two hands to do pretty much anything and you won't want to take it jogging. It looks and feels solid in hand with a nice rubberized backing that provides a much needed grip on a phone this size (NOTE: this is not the case for the white version, which has a glossy back). The wonderfully large screen (which many will lament because it's only 720p) is sharp, bright, and vibrant. I've yet to encounter any instances of noticeable pixels. Videos and pictures look great. I've found that most people who complain about the screen have never actually seen it in person.

I gave Emotion UI a shot, but it has some pretty annoying shortcomings (no app drawer, a delay in returning to the home screen after closing an app that is in a folder, the text labels for apps wrap awkwardly if it was too long, certain widgets are not sized properly to take advantage of the screen). These are eliminated with the use of a launcher - I used Nova and would recommend it. The phone is snappy, and I haven't had any programs crash or even experience any delays in opening or closing apps. Phone calls sound crisp, clear, and plenty loud. In using the speakerphone, I actually needed to turn it down because max volume was, in contrast to every other mobile phone I've used, much louder than I expected. Music from the speaker and through headphones are louder than expected as well. The camera is decent. I took pretty clear pictures of my kids on moving carnival rides. The interface is simple, so you're not going to spend all day fiddling with it to get a shot off. The front facing camera features a countdown and a reminder to look at the camera lens and not the screen, which I thought was nice.

Now the battery. OOOOH LAWD that battery. This right here is the reason you buy this phone. If you're tired of having to look for a power source or carrying an extra battery (or something along those lines) to get through the day, you will love this phone. I activated the phone on a Wednesday evening and charged it overnight. I didn't need to plug it in until Saturday night. It lasted 64 hours with over seven hours of screen-on-time. That was with auto-brightness turned on, and using "Normal" power saving mode (the least of the three power saving modes) until I hit 10%. This battery will not leave you hanging.

In summary, for $299, this is a solid value. I'd give it 5-stars if it was great out of the box. But it needs a new launcher to overcome some glaring software issues.

title: Horrible customer service!
text:
Phone is nice but customer service horrible.

Wk1. Got the phone and a Net10 simcard after a week, switched to Net10. (Net10 has great monthly plans but their customer service is a pure joke, the Indian reps don't know what they are talking about, each one gave me different instructions, took me 5 calls and 3 hour conversation to learn that the switch failed. Net10 had to sent me another simcard to reactivate the service. Luckily this switch was successful on the new simcard, but there was no free airtime with it. Called Net10, was told they don't know anything about Huawei or its promo. (BTW, if you call Net10 number, you'll hear two choices for different companies so it is an outsourced call center which explains why the customer service don't know their stuff).

Once I was turned down, I went to Huawei's e-commerce site for help. Customer service found the issue quickly: they have never sent the airtime card to me. He told me only his supervisor can handle this but the supervisor is on vacation so the problem cannot be solved until the supervisor is back. He has sent email to his supervisor on this case though. I got nothing or no contact for the week.

Wk2: Following Mon I chatted with customer service again, went through the whole process to find that the airtime card was not shipped. Customer service told me only his supervisor can handle this but his supervisor never heard of my case and he needs to investigate what went wrong with the process before he can give me a feedback. I asked why cannot send me a card if they know this is their own problem. Was told this is the process and everyone has to follow.

Wk3: No update so I chatted again. Customer service told me they are aware of the situation and his supervisor is investigating the case. They can do nothing before the investigation is done. I asked to speak to THE supervisor, was turned down. Asked me to be patient, took down my phone number and email, promised that the supervisor will contact. Of course nothing happened this week.

Wk4:No update so I chatted again. Customer service told me they are aware of the situation and his supervisor is investigating the case. Is it absurd I am copying myself in the 4th week? Asked me to be patient, took down my phone number and email, promised that the supervisor will contact. I don't think things will happen. They are just trying to wear me down.

I have filed a BBB complaint on Huawei at local BBB site. This is only a $50 value airtime card, but the worst ever customer service experience I had in US. title: Great for texting and email
text:
I bought this phone last month through my new carrier (because I got the "Me" plan, which was really cheap lol). Compared to my last phone (a Samsung Galaxy through my EX-carrier), this is one HUGE unit. It takes some getting used to before you stop feeling like you're holding a laptop to your ear.

I do a huge amount of texting and emailing with my phone, which is why I chose such a large unit. It has a lot more app space than my last phone, and runs all my internet work very quickly. I was also able to get some fun stuff on it, like an accuweather app that shows video of current and predicted weather conditions, rather than just static photos. Irrelevant, I know, but a fun feature that I really enjoy.

Unfortunately, the call quality hasn't been all that good. Unless I put the phone on speaker, I can't really hear what a caller is saying. For me personally, this isn't a huge problem, since the vast majority of my calls are work-related and I need both hands to type while I'm talking, so I generally use the speaker anyway. It's a little inconvenient during personal calls, but I can live with it. Someone who does a lot of calling might want to think twice about this phone.

One other drawback is that I occasionally get a "contacts not working" error message. A little internet research showed that disabling the google+ app clears that right up. I did and it did, so it's all good now.

The call quality is the only reason I gave this unit 4 stars instead of 5. I've already dropped it a couple times, so it's pretty sturdy. lol

title: Longest lasting Android phone, ever.
text:
I'm a flagship phone guy, and I love Android. I've had Samsung phones (Galaxy S and S2), Nexus phones (4 & 5), and the fantastic HTC One M7. All of these phones have been great to me, but none of them lasted me a whole day on a charge. I'm a very heavy user. Video, navigation, streaming music, texting, browsing... my Nexus 5 gets me to about 3pm before I need to plug it in. I'm tired of it.

When I learned about this phone, and its massive display and even more massive battery, I had to try it out. There were a lot of factors that made me nervous. Huawei is a no-name brand to me. Even though they are #3 in the world, they are almost unheard of in the USA. Android 4.3 is... old... released in July of 2013 it's almost ancient by phone operating system standards. The rest of the specs besides the battery made me a little nervous as well. The Snapdragon 400 may be a quad-core but it is still fairly low end, and a 720p resolution sounds really low when the market is currently moving past 1080p and on to 2k displays on phones. At $300 the price seems right until you compare the specs to the Oneplus One which can be had for the same money (if you get an invite, anyway).

So, on paper, the Mate 2 is starting to sound only mildly appealing.

Luckily, I had a friend who happened to own one who graciously let me borrow it for a day. I was pretty much blown away by the experience and ordered one for myself. To go into better detail about why this phone won me over, I'll break it down by category.

Build Quality: This is a plastic phone. This is a turn-off for a lot of people who like the feel of glass and aluminum on their devices, but it's never bothered me. Plastic is light, it doesn't absorb heat so it's more comfortable to use while gaming or charging, it doesn't shatter when dropped, and it's more than capable of being attractive. The main problem I've had with plastic phones is they feel flimsy. They tend to creak or flex and can feel really cheap. This phone has none of those problems. It's as solid as any phone I've ever held and it has a very understated look.

Display: The 6.1" screen dominates the front of the phone. The bezels are very small, which keeps the overall size of the phone down. The colors are accurate and the backlight is bright. Honestly, the lower resolution is barely noticeable unless you set the phone next to a higher-resolution device. Coming from a 5" 1080p phone to a 6.1" 720p phone I am 100% happy with the quality of the display. I am definitely spoiled at this point and couldn't be happy with a smaller phone.

Software: This is my main gripe and the reason I docked a star. The fact that Huawei decided to release the phone with Android 4.3 instead of the current 4.4 OS isn't their biggest sin. Their horrible, terrible, really really bad EmotionUI Skin is the problem. Right out of the box the launcher feels like a cheap rip off of iOS from 5 years ago. It's so dreadful I didn't even bother learning it and went straight to the play store and downloaded Action Launcher. Many different launchers are available on the Play Store which all significantly improve the usability of this phone. Nova, Apex, Aviate, and Action are just a few. I also downloaded a few icon packs to replace the built in icons which are amazingly ugly. Now, these are things that I do ALREADY on every phone I own, so it's not a big deal for me, but the fact that the factory launcher is so laughably bad is inexcusable in my opinion. Also, Huawei claims they have plans to bring 4.4 KitKat to this device, I hope they follow through. If they don't, their reputation will be tarnished for me and I probably wouldn't consider buying another device from Huawei. Timely software updates are very important to me and that's why I've gravitated toward Nexus devices in the past.

Processor/Graphics/Memory/Storage: Grouping all of these together because my impression of all of them is pretty much the same. This device is FAST ENOUGH. It has handled everything I've thrown at it with ease. Games run smooth (tested XCOM and Leo's Fortune), loading up a bunch of apps in the background doesn't bog anything down, everything runs great. If you didn't tell me it had a lower end CPU/GPU I wouldn't have been able to guess. The 16gb of storage is plenty since it has an SD slot, which I use for music and pictures. Over all I'm shocked how snappy this device is and I have no complaints about the performance.

Camera: I haven't spent a lot of time with this yet, but I've noticed that it has a tendency to take blurry photos in indoor photos. The lack of optical image stabilization is probably the culprit. If you want to take good photos indoors, it's best that your subject is still and you have a steady hand. Outdoor snaps look great. I'm happy with it considering the price, but it isn't blowing me away. Then again, I've never been blown away by a smartphone camera.

Battery Life: This is my favorite part, because it's changed my life just a little. On my first full charge, this phone tripled the battery life of my Nexus 5. Over 40 hours of standby time and almost 11 hour of screen on time. For me, that's two full days of use. For most people it's 3 or maybe even 4 days. Every phone should have this kind of battery. But no other phone does, just this Huawei. I'm smitten.

I'm giving the phone 4 out of 5 stars simply because of the outdated and horribly skinned OS. For some people, this might be a deal-breaker, for others a non-issue. For me, it's a blemish on what could have been the perfect $300 phone. But it doesn't stop me from happily using it as my primary device. That big screen and incredible battery life are just too sweet to give up.

title: OK phone, ruined by terrible Huawei OS
text:
The Huawei Mate 2 looks great on specs for the price. The screen is nice and big, yet still fits in my male clothing pockets. Within a few days I adjusted to the size and other phones feel tiny. The phone is acceptable. It feels sort of cheap, but for the price it's fine. The battery is huge and regularly lasts over 30 hours, sometimes up to two days. It's quite nice not to have to always be looking for a charger.

However, the Huawei version of Android ruins the phone. It's based off the 4.3 version of Android, which is a very old version. Huawei doesn't release enough source or drivers to be able to flash a custom ROM, like Cyanogen. Which means you're stuck using their terrible version of Android. Huawei did nothing but impair the functionality and visual appeal of the device. Huawei clearly does not care about the

1. The processor is throttled by default to a speed so slow, even typing is laggy. Which is silly on this phone, because the battery lasts up to two days without throttling.

2. Huawei tweaked the audio system and actually broke basic functions like music playback. Using Google Play Music, once you turn off the screen by hitting the power button, the sound will stop after a short while. The OS still thinks it is playing music or other sound (it's not limited to one program), but until you stop and restart playing sound, no actual sound is produced. It seems to be related to the power-save, as setting the timeout to a very long time reduces the problem.

3. Other audio issues appear, such as text-to-speech not kicking in while playing music. Or sometimes notifications don't play. They lower the volume of other sounds, but don't actually sound off. I'm nervous every time I use this phone to set an alarm.

4. Huawei broke the Android task switcher. They introduced a "force close all apps" button that appears at the bottom when you go to switch apps. This means once a day, I accidentally hit that and close all my apps, losing open tabs or other progress. Huawei does this to "Free up memory" because their marketing or engineering departments are unaware that Android can manage memory fine (and I've never had less than half a GB free on the device). If I wanted unused RAM, I could buy a couple of 2GB DIMMs and leave them on my desk.

5. The background colour on the soft buttons is a bright grey. This is incredibly distracting and serves no other purpose other than to remind you that you're running a broken version of Android.

That's just off the top of my head.

Huawei literally has added nothing of value in their customization of Android. Everything they've done makes the device worse and hurts the user experience. Their add-ons, like the one-hand mode or "Windows on Windows" (no relation to the MS technology) are laughable, stupid, useless implementations. Fortunately, they can be left off and ignored. I mention them to point out that even where they might have done something interesting, they delivered a half-cooked feature.

If Huawei just shipped stock Android, this would be a top-class phone, especially at the price. As-is, it's a frustrating experience, everyday.
