title: Main issues with this phone 📱
text:
I purchased this phone August of last year, when it was being offered along with the reverse charge cable for free as a promotion.

Perhaps before I begin to write about the details of this phone and the quirks I've found during my use, I should preface with this so you have an idea what my perspective is:

I have only owned the international variant (i9100) of the Galaxy SII prior to this (before that were two or three feature phones). Long story short, when I found out about rooting, and flashing through Odin, I didn't keep the best practices (little psa here: make sure you have backups and good usb cables and enough charge and enough knowledge! BEFORE attempting to flash) so eventually the phone refused to turn on after one bad flash. It died May 2014 (I bought it Jan 2013).
After that, I decided I'd had enough of flagship phones, especially when their features are so great like the SII but their battery life cannot keep up to speed. I realized I'd rather have something that came bare bones with a superb battery life than something fancy that couldn't stay on long enough to exploit. Another key feature I was searching for was a low price.

I searched for something to replace my fallen galaxy but nothing seemed to answer my battery requirements other than the galaxy note phones and some obscure Lenovos. There was also the elusive Oneplus One, however when I realized how impossible getting an invite was, I discounted that as an option. (Now though it seems to be raining invites, and I have since purchased it for my sister.) ((I shall be writing a review of that phone soon and will link it here when it is complete))

So when I heard about this phone through articles about CES 2014, I couldn't wait. Finally something I could buy in the US from the original source.

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Now onto the phone:
I will only talk about things that I found out that I haven't seen written about before, since there comes a point where reviews all talking about the same thing are no longer helpful. If this phone was lacking in reviews it would be helpful to see lots of reviews confirming the same things, but that is no longer needed in my opinion. What is needed is a review discussing the issues people may run into with the phone, which is what I want to present.

SCREEN and SIZE: Mine does seem to have a defect; there is a rectangle in the center where it is lighter than the rest of the screen, most clearly visible on a plain white background like on most webpages (where I first discovered it).
I will be returning it to Huawei and how get can either fix it or supply me with a new device under my warranty.
I also noticed that the screen has that "liquidity" effect if you put enough pressure on it. And I don't mean a really hard press, I'm talking about the kind of pressure you would use trying to stop a device this big from slipping through your fingers. There is one youtube video about this, but in that video the man only shows it happening in one area. For me, this is an issue across the whole screen-that is, it happens no matter where I press.
It's given that the screen (and the device itself of course) is large, which surprisingly took me shorter than expected to get used to, and now I can no longer see (or hold) other "normal" sized phones in the same light. In the beginning people looked at my phone in mocking, but now that the iPhone 6+ has come out, which is almost exactly the same size in length and width, it is now somewhat normalized. Also, the device has a nice thickness, which helps you hold the phone. This makes me realize I would much rather have a phone be thick than thin. There comes a point when thin is bad, especially when the phone is big and could use the extra dimension for grip. Another benefit is the extra thickness means more room for battery! Just a thought for phone manufacturers to ponder on, not that this one review will reach them 😝

BATTERY:
Although it began very well, telling me I had 45+ hours of use left (which I never tested so I can't be sure that wasn't inflated), now, six months later when fully charged it tells me I have 25+ hours. While still good, I am disappointed about this turn of events. Reverse charging works fine, but drains the battery (obviously) very quickly. I haven't tried to charge this phone from another, so I have no idea if that works. Note my phone is fully stock & unrooted.

DURABILITY: I have dropped this phone at least 10 times (all accidental!) , half of which were on pavement and one was into snow on a sidewalk. Note that I do not have any protection on this phone other than the plastic screen protector it came with. The screen is unscathed, the only thing that changed was it now has some tiny bumps on the side bezel (not the "metal", but the black part surrounding the screen.) The back cover also earned a tiny battle scar (I shall be posting pictures later, since I am now writing the review on the Huawei itself 😁)

CAMERA: First I shall talk of the back camera, which is 13MP. It performs very well in ideal conditions, bright sunlight and stable hands and objects. Of course, being such a giant phone makes steady photography difficult, impossible if attempting to use one hand only. It does poorly when you are moving and trying to take a picture of a stationary object (ie. Trying to take a picture from a moving car of something outside.)
Something I recently discovered was that the camera had a macro mode, and only after lots of searches online and in the camera interface itself did I realize that it's NOT a separate mode (which it was on the SII), but it's built in to the normal mode. Of course! That's why all previous closeups turned out very good.
Ever since getting my sister her Oneplus One, I have been comparing their back cameras and found that the Oneplus is far superior. Also I noticed that the Huawei has a strange fisheye like effect in all photos, such that when holding both phones side by side zoomed out all the way, the Huawei always shows more of the background than the Oneplus does. It also means that when taking a picture relatively close to the object, it makes the object look rounder and stretched in odd ways. This applies even to the front camera, necessitating you to hold the phone further back for selfies to look normal, which is not a good thing because that also means you will have to show more of the background, which means you either deal with it or you have to crop the photo later. I found that overall, the combination of these flaws makes me not want to use my phone for photos anymore whenever my sister and her Oneplus are around.
I tried many other camera apps, but found that they all produce photos of seemingly lower clarity than the original app, so I ended up deleting them. One thing I am very disappointed about, however, is the fact that the video/camcorder does not have a pause button like my old SII (which came out in 2011) did have!!!! You either film and then end the recording, or you download a third party app that does have the pause button (It took me a very long time of downloading and trying apps to find one that does, so here it is: A Better Camera, by Almalence, Inc: http://www.amazon.com/gp/aw/d/B00J8F4LGW/ref=mp_s_a_1_1?qid=1422132466&sr=8-1 )

SOFTWARE: I am not one to be drooling in anticipation of the next update, so that will not be the point of this topic. I wanted to dedicate this to the various annoying bugs I've come across, mainly since updating to the B148 version. I only updated because it promised to fix some camera bugs and provide a better camera, but I haven't seen anything significant (or any changes at all). Anyways, before I updated, I never had auto sync on and would still get all my whatsapp messages and emails on time. However AFTER the update, I had to go to each app and manually change it to push notifications, and then turn on auto sync for it to actually work. And even now, with all of that, sometimes I will get notifications 10 or more minutes after the message is sent to me. This is highly obnoxious, and makes me seem like I am ignoring messages, which is outrageous. I wish there was a way to downgrade back to whatever version it was before the update, since none of this was an issue then. Hopefully whenever the next update is pushed, they have gotten rid of all these issues.
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

I will update this review as soon as lollipop 🍭 arrives as an ota update, and later this week to add the photos.

PS. How strange, they seem to have dropped the word Ascend from this phone's title.

title: "Huawei Premium Customer Support" HA!
text:
I wish that I had ordered this phone from Amazon. Maybe I wouldn't have had all of the problems that I had! I purchased my phone directly from Huawei. Unfortunately they do not allow you to post reviews on their website. The amazon order will be fulfilled by Huawei anyways. The phone, if it had worked right, would have been great. Unfortunately, the unit that I received would answer calls in my pocket without me realizing that someone had even called. In fact, I could answer it by touching to a chair armrest, my jeans, really just about anything caused the phone to answer the calls. Well, for obvious reasons, I could not have a phone with a potentially open mic in my pocket while at work. Additionally, it would answer incoming calls even when I was already on a call and had the phone pressed against my head! Anyhow, I really liked the phone so I opened a help ticket hoping that they could fix whatever was wrong with it. However, the tech who responded to my ticket stopped reading after I said that it dropped a call to answer another. He emailed telling me to call my carrier since they would be better able to troubleshoot dropped calls. Now, I'm pretty tech savvy and this problem had nothing to do with my carrier, so that meant that he took the least amount of effort to close my ticket without really trying to figure out the nature of the problem. Making matters worse, after the technician failed to even try to understand the problem, they sent me a customer satisfaction survey where I expressed my extreme Dissatisfaction. They ignored it!

The next day I called to request an RMA for the phone and all accessories. Now, they want to try to solve my problem, but I explained that ship has sailed and now I just want to return the phone that I had only had for about a week. You might think that was the end of the story. Phone returned and the refund issued. You'd be wrong of course. I shipped the phone back on 14 August. It was received by them on 18 August and I have yet to receive my refund or even an email that they had received the unit and are processing the refund. I even opened up a ticket trying to find out when I would receive my refund. As of 23 August, they have yet to respond.

At the end of the day, the phone really is a great phone. The phone was snappy even with the snapdragon 400 and the screen looked great even though it was only 1280x720. The phone felt great in my hand and I loved the battery life. If my unit had not been defective I would have been very happy with the phone. However, even though they claim that you receive "Premium" customer support, they really failed to deliver!

title: Good (not great) phone that runs lollipop (and that's probably as far as it will go)
text:
First things first - yes, this device can now be upgraded to Lollipop (5.1). The OTA update will start on July 8, 2015; but you can download the v309 preview and install it from a flashcard. I would say that a lot of people on several forums ow Huawei an apology, but this is a review, not a lesson in morality.

I've owned the phone for almost a year now. When I was running it on Jelly Bean (4.3), it was a good phone. I had it rooted, a bunch of ads installed, and had no real problems with the phone; although the phone would randomly restart about 3 times a week, the new firmware seems to have put a stop to that.

The reason I've rated this 4 stars is because there's nothing really spectacular about it; oh wait, you mean I forgot to mention the battery? Yes, I am aware. Under Jelly Bean, I'd get a solid 2 days of battery life if I didn't turn on bluetooth or gps. That's not bad, however today there are more and more phones that can meet or beat this - so this is no longer the only reason to buy the phone. The reverse charging cable works; however stupid an idea it is. I don't know of anyone that would actually want to use it - since charging from a standard 5 dollar charger would charge your phone faster...and cheaper. I'm guessing that the main reason for the cable is to showoff the battery size.

The screen is okay, it has Gorilla Glass 3, but it gets dirty quite often. I've had it in the 30 dollar trident case and have had no problems.

I've found no apps I could not run well...All of the WB games like Injustice, Batman AO, and others run well as long as that is all I am doing.

Bottom line is today, this is a decent phone - that's it, a decent phone. The 720i resolution is good, but again, there's several phones out today that suprass every reason to buy this phone...and soon, even the price.

All in all, it's an awesome phone - with an awesome price, coming from a company that does sub-par (meaning bad) customer service for being the third largest telecommunications business in the world.

title: Best Budget Phablet
text:
Easily the best big screen smartphone on a budget on the market right now. Most will scoff at the 720p display over 6.1 inches of screen but forget most monitors are far larger with either 720p or 1080p resolutions stretched over them. For a display to look sharp in book only requires 200 ppi or higher.

The screen is obviously 720 x 1280. Huawei uses a JDI panel which offers one of the sharpest experiences for a IPS panel and lowered energy costs. There are slim bezels to the side which makes me grip the phone more firmly lest I drop it while trying not to cover part of the screen with my thumbs. I don't make use of the auto brightness. I find it lowers screen brightness too much in darker rooms. I tend to stick with 40-50% screen brightness.

The phone is comprised either of plastic. The sides are a glossy smooth finish and the back cover is a fine grippy textured plastic (I think it is polycarbonate).

Although the back camera has a aperature of 2.2, the camera does poorly on low light and needs the flash to help brighten the scene. The front camera equally had its own problems. Ideally the subject should have a diffuse light source shining on it. Otherwise hard frontal light and harsh backlighting results in some fuzziness and pixelation.

Connectivity is excellent. I often get 5 full bars of LTE with T-Mobile and at least HSPA+ in other less saturated LTE areas. GPS works great and usually I get a solid lock within 15 seconds. Bluetooth is good with a mediocrely fast pairing. However, the Android version 4.3 that ships with the HAM2 suffers from audio and video sync issues with streaming video (audio is usually fast by 1-2 seconds). I am hoping the a future update to Kitkat will resolve that issue.

Battery life is downright spectacular. I'm a multitasker and a self professed power user. I can easily squeeze 1.5 to 2 days out of a single charge. This means 6-8 hours of standby time (sleep), 2-4 hours of gaming, 4 hours of streaming videos, 2 hours of streaming audio, and 3-5 hours of web surfing and email. At the end of all that I usually still have 25‰ charge left.

title: Bought Huawei Ascend Mate 2 and I love this phone
text: Bought Huawei Ascend Mate 2 and I love this phone. When my two year contact with ATT came up two months ago, like a dutiful customer eager for an upgrade, I went seeking another phone, only to learn that the phone companies have devised a new scheme of making more money. They said I would have no choice but to either pay for the phone upfront or in subsidized installments, both unacceptable given that I would be paying more than $800. The icing on the cake was that I would also have to pay more a month due to date upage. Neither options sat well with me. After much research rapture, I decided to try out the Huawei. The price you can't beat, or so I thought. I shelled out the peanuts, got the phone and now I'm in love with it. I have been mostly an apple-ite, minus a brief affair with an HTC. The family rolls with Apple too. But, without reservations, I am happy with my New Chinese made phone. What phone isn't manufactured there?! So, for anyone looking for the same comforts of your typical smartphone, I highly recommend this phone. Easy to figure out and manipulate. Iphone has better camera and Huawei's got some issues, especially at night, but it still works and has taken some nice pics. Yes, it will work under T-mobile. Make sure you get an unlocked one. Switch out cards. And be sure to load up on your SD card slot for more storage. Two months into this, my only complaint --- there are now two more Chinese companies with better smartphones, or at least as comparable AND CHEAPER than $280. Don't just think about it. Do it. Take the chance on a different phone. I did and I am elated.

Also I seem to get MUCH better signal with this phone than my old S3, not sure whether to attribute that to more space for an antenna or more power capability. Overall, I have been recommending this phone to anyone who has to purchase a phone outright for plans on networks like T-Mobile, since you'll end up paying massive prices for a flagship phone that might not be much better than this. If you're not a gamer or anything, this phone rocks for anything related to productivity, although you may look a little silly with a 6.1 inch phone held up to your face, this doesn't bother me in the slightest because sound quality of the built in speaker is great. title: My Review of the Mate 2-Edited
text:
Edit: Nov. 2

I am extremely disappointed with Huawei cancelling future updates for this phone. ESPECIALLY a mere 4 months after its US release. Worse, the Chinese version of this phone is on KitKat, so there is absolutely ZERO reason why ours should be on 4.3. This tells me that any phone released in the US by Huawei will not be supported, and for me this is a deal breaker. I will be selling this phone, and in good conscience can no longer recommend it to others. Review dropped from 5 stars to 2.

I purchased this phone from Huawei's site, and have had it for 6 days.
1: Battery Life
The battery on the phone is simply amazing. To go from my first charge to 1% battery left took 44 hours. Phone usage during this time was over 7 hours on screen time, from browsing, downloading, reading ebooks, playing a game, and listening to music. I kept the screen brightness at 100 the entire time, with power saving option set to "Smart". As this was only the first charge, I expect the second charge to go maybe another 4 hours on top of that. FYI, it takes about 3 hours to fully charge the battery from 1% to 100%, and Huawei thoughfully provides an estimated charge time in its Phone Manager app.
2: Screen
I know many people are put off by the simple HD screen on the Mate. While I can tell a slight difference, the colors on this phone are AWESOME. Very few phones can match the vivid colors I am seeing with the Mate, and it give a very deep black as well. Overall I give the screen a B+, simply because it is not 1080.
3: Build quality
Simply put, the build quality is excellent. Nothing on this phone feels cheap, and while the back cover is plastic, it is fluid and provides excellent grip. I can honestly compare it too the reports of how the OPO Sandstone Black's cover feels.
4: Software
Optimization is first rate. Everything runs smoothly, with absolutely no pauses or hiccups on anything I have tested(and I have tested every preloaded app and my own). RAM usage, with no apps open, hovers around 600MB, leaving plenty of room for multitasking.
My thoughts on EMUI.....I have not installed a custom launcher yet, as I want to give EMUI a chance. Overall I think Huawei did a decent job with it(especially optimizing), but IMO it is too much like IOS for my liking. I miss the app drawer, and personally do not like having tons of shortcuts clogging up my home screen. For someone coming from Apple and IOS, they would feel right at home. I'm going to install nova later this evening.
5: Preloaded apps
Huawei did an excellent job with keeping the bloat down, as every preloaded app(with the exception of their own browser which I have not used) is useful. It comes with a phone manager, which contains a very nice accelerator, cleaner, harassment filter, and power saving options. This app lets you know if there are any apps running in the background, allows you to prevent apps from running in the background, and offers one click cleaning, much like a number of apps from the Play Store. Unlike those apps, this one actually KEEPS those bothersome apps from running until you say so, and it's one click cleaning does a fine job as well. The power saving option allows you to choose three settings...Smart, which automatically adjusts cpu and network usage; Endurance, which throttles the CPU to save power, and Normal, which maximizes the CPU's performance for gaming. To be honest, from my experience, unless you are gaming or streaming, keeping your device set to endurance has zero drawback or performace issues and really saves power.
There are a few others, all which provide some nice functionality, but I won't go into those here.
As for gaming, I purchased and am playing Xcom...and have had NO stuttering, framerate issues, or force closes. Silky smooth
6: camera
The camera is very nice. The pictures are clear, crisp, and detailed. The only negative I would give is low light settings, which I believe could be fixed with an update.
7: LTE(US)
The modem is VERY good on this device. I am running on Tmobile, and today was with a friend who uses the S5 on the same network....I was actually picking up signal where he wasn't, and would be at 4 bars when he would be a 3 or even 2. VERY nice.
8: Negatives.
The only two cons about this device is the HD screen(and that isn't a huge ding imo), and EMUI. And if Huawei would add an app drawer, it would not be that bad. But like I said above, nothing Nova launcher can't fix. For some the size of the phone will be a huge turnoff, but for me I find it fits nicely in hand, and is actually only a little larger than the S5, which has a much smaller screen.

title: My search is over!

text:

The battery is 2+ days for me before charging and though it is large, I find it great for me. I have average size men's hands, and it is not too big for them. In the past, I came from an old HTC Thundbolt, a Droid and a Droid Razr as prior phones and tho they were one handed usable, I used them a lot with both hands, so the bigger phone is great.

The extra real estate on the screen is worth it to me. Also the screen, tho 720p is beautiful, crisp and clear. Text is sharp and videos are quite clear, vivid and the colors are accurate and rich. The viewing angles are amazing and the saturation levels are very accurate. IMO, it rivals many 1080p screens even with a little lower resolution this phone's screen is absolutely impressive. I gambled to buy this phone based on written reviews of others and online video reviews, and I am so glad I did.

I am only into the first few weeks of using it but so far, everything is fluid and fast. I have no regrets at all and would recommend this phone to anyone who is looking for a phablet sized phone. It is reasonably priced and you get a quality unit that appears to be made with excellent workmanship and it has stellar battery life. Also note that the stock launcher / home screen is ok and works well, but I am using Nova launcher and it works best for me. Both work flawlessly on this phone, but Nova is by far more customizable and versatile. My experience is that Nova + Ascent Mate2 = one awesome phone.

I have not done much with the camera yet, but so far it appears to be quite good as well. It does have a Sony lense and so far nice and sharp pictures, really good colors and details in good light. I have not tried any low light shots, but it does have a flash so I am expecting that the photos will be fairly good in low light as well.

This is a great choice for you if you want to spend less than the name brand's new flagship phones and still get something that can handle everything currently out in the Wireless phone arena with ease.

The camera does not work as good as my previous phones at low light. I am going to use the flash to avoid this issue. The pre-installed Camera does not allow you to turn off the shutter sound. This is annoying. I installed the Camera360 app, and it allows me to turn off the shutter sound and it comes with many useful options.

I took a long trip this past weekend, after using the Google map's navigation for 8 hours and listening to music for over 5 hours without charging it in the car, the phone did not get hot. It even lasted for one more day. I was very impressed.

title: You get what you pay for and more
text:
I have been using the Huawei Mate2 for quite some time now. I have found that there are many things I like and dislike about this phone. I have listed below the things that are the most important to me as far as what I like and what I don’t like.
The things I like:
The large screen – I am getting a little older now and the 3.5 screens don’t cut it for me anymore. About 2 years ago I switched from an iPhone 4 to the Samsung Note 2. The screen size was the major factor for me. I went from a 3.5 inch display to 5.5 inches and would never go back. Now with the Mate 2 I have a 6.1 inch display, switching to the Mate is not nearly the difference between from my iPhone to the Note 2 but it still is a larger screen and I like this. My daughter uses the phone for Netflix on road trips and loves the large screen
Memory – The Mate has 16G built in and I have put a 32G card in the back. I have changed the SD card to be my primary memory. I have over 1000 pictures in the card, hundreds of songs and lots of apps with room to spare. The reason I use the SD card as my primary storage is I have damaged a few phones in the past and with everything on the memory card I don’t lose anything when I get my new phone.
Processor is fast – I am not a big gamer but I am a power user and because of my job I am on it all the time except when I sleep. Even when I sleep my phone still has email come in and it downloads files. I have four different emails, run many apps, use GPS, Bluetooth, browser etc, my life is on this phone. If it slows down I have to as well.
Battery life – I was constantly charging my iPhone and my Note 2, it was common on the weekends to charge my phone every day. With the Mate 2, I can wait until Sunday to charge. The battery life is far superior to my last phones.
Things I am not fond of:
Battery isn’t removable – I have crashed all of the phones I have used for the last 15+ years. Some of the crashes have required me to pull the battery to get it to recover. The Mate 2 has a built in battery so I am not able to pull the battery but if I press the power button and the down volume button at the same time for 5 to 10 seconds the phone will reset.
Power button and volume button being on the same side – On many occasions I have needed to turn the volume up on my phone while I was in a call and I missed the volume button and locked the screen by pressing the power button. Then it takes a few seconds to unlock the screen and turn the volume up.
My opinion of the phone is, “You get what you pay for and more”. The Huawei Mate 2 is a very reasonably priced phone that works very well. It has lots of features and has been able to handle everything I have thrown at it. Overall I would recommend this phone to my family and friends that are looking for a phone with a screen this size.

text:
Let's get the technical stuff out of the way. Installing the SIM card is a bit of a hassle, but if you have a spudger or a pair of tweezers getting the back off is easy. Playing Battleheart has been pretty fun on this phone, but I don't play many games so I'm not sure how well it performs with more intense games.

Overall I'd say BUY the Huawei Ascend Mate2 if you want a good starter smartphone. Didn't I mention that this is my first smartphone? I'll probably start using something from Samsung once I break this phone or it gets too slow.

text:
Initially I was a little hesitant about the size of this phone, but since having it for almost a month now, all I have are mostly positive things to say:
1. 4G LTE speeds -the wireless data connection speeds are good, often faster than my home wifi
2. Decent processor + Plenty of RAM: so far I have had no performance issues with the phone. Whenever hitting the 'Home' button to exit an app the screen sometimes ghosts for a second, but other than that the response is very snappy. While the processor is not bleeding edge, it definitely does a good job, and playing games is smooth. The 2Gb of RAM is plenty and makes multitasking a breeze without the phone bogging down.
3. Battery Life: is excellent. I have had the phone last 4 days on a single charge, and that was with checking email, making calls/receiving texts, playing games, and surfing the internet. On average you'll probably get between 2-3 days of use (or at least I do), but I love not having to worry about charging the phone every night.
4. GPS: works well, and combined with the great battery life means that the phone will survive for even long trips
5. SD card: memory is expandable
6. Painless Setup: I use StraightTalk with this phone and the setup process was painless and all of my cellular services have worked flawlessly from day one. I cannot speak for the setup with other companies, but I would imagine it would be similarly easy.

Overall, I am very happy with this phone. Hopefully Huawei will hold to their announcement that they will be releasing Android 5.0 for the Mate 2, so if you really want Lollipop I would wait and see (supposedly the update will be released first half of this year), but for my purposes the phone is great regardless of Huawei's plans for future software updates.

title: A great handset, especially for $300 unlocked
text:
A great handset, especially for $300 unlocked.

HARDWARE
The phone is big, especially if you're coming from significantly smaller handsets. The phone has a massive 6.1" screen, but the bezels are relatively slim. The screen takes up about 75% of the area of the device; for comparison, a 5s uses about 60% of its front space. This makes it front-pocketable for me (a male who wears relatively slim jeans in a 30 waist), but it's clearly visible that I'm carrying a large phone. The top of the phone will jut out of my rear pockets on jeans. The phone is relatively slim, however, and weighs only about 200g. The screen is bright and has good colors; however, it is "only" 720p. For what it's worth, it is relatively easy to read text on the display and I don't have any problems with the lower resolution. The lower resolution also significantly improves battery life, which I'll get to in a moment. If you know you're going to have problems with a 240ppi display, then you can steer clear of this device and get, say, an Xperia Z Ultra (which I'll cover in the competition section). The buttons seem sturdy, and the back peels off a la Samsung to access microsd and microSIM, both of which are easy to slot in.

SOFTWARE
The Emotion UI is a relatively light skin, save for the launcher. If you're new to Android, the launcher might fit the bill, but more experienced users will already be installing their own favorite launchers (I prefer Nova, which is free on the Play Store). It has no app drawer, which killed it for me, but if you're migrating from an iPhone or a feature phone, you'll be fine on it. There is also a "simple" mode within Settings if you are new to smartphones, which makes all the major features easy to access.

PERFORMANCE
The Snapdragon 400 is a good chipset, and it's available already in the Moto G LTE. The Mate2, however, has 2GB of RAM, rather than the 1GB in the Moto G and G LTE, and it makes a world of difference. The Moto G could be stuttered by heavy multitasking, especially playing Spotify or another streaming service while browsing desktop sites in the browser. Here, I've never had less than 512MB free, and the Snapdragon holds up well to anything, including Asphalt 8 and even a PS1 emulator. You could get a Snapdragon 800/801 (same chipset) phone, but the power isn't really needed and it only hurts battery life. More OEMs should pair 400s or 200s with 2GB of RAM; it really makes for a smooth experience.

BATTERY LIFE
Significantly better than any phone I've ever owned. It browses the web for about three times as long as my old Galaxy Nexus with an extended battery, and while browsing on WiFi on medium brightness, loses about 1% every 8 minutes. Truly outstanding. I've never finished a day below 40%. It will probably get through two days of light use and will CERTAINLY get through one day of heavy use.

COMPETITION
The primary competition for this device lies in the few other midrange phablets on the market. The Xperia Z Ultra can be had for about $400 unlocked nowadays and has an 800 as well as a 1080p display, but it has 75% of the battery capacity (equating to about 60% of the battery life). It is also massive, with a 6.4" display and a significantly thicker set of bezels. I was originally going to buy it, but a quick hold in a store showed me that it simply isn't pocketable.
The OnePlus One also packs an 800, with 3GB of RAM, and a 1080p 5.5" display, but it isn't widely available. They operate a quite frankly offensive invite system; however, if you have an invite, it's a much nicer phone.
The Samsung Galaxy Note 2 can be had for $300 used at times, and has similar hardware specs. It's just smaller, at about 5.5". I'm wary of buying used phones, but it might be a decent alternative if you're fine with a smaller handset.

CONCLUSION
All in all, the Mate2 is the best midrange large Android phablet on the market. If you want big, buy it. If you don't know if you want big or not, go to a store and look at other 6" phones. If you can tote it, it makes videos and web browsing much better than a standard 5" or 4.5" phone; however, make sure you want a big phone before ordering.

title: Great for productivity and entertainment, yet can be handled with one hand.
text:
This baby must be one of the absolute bargains out there in phablets right now. Huawei Ascend Mate2 vs. Mate1: Twice the RAM (2GB vs. 1GB), a 13MP camera vs. 8MP, 4G LTE vs. 3G HSPA, 16Gb internal vs. 8Gb, KitKat 4.3 vs. JellyBean 4.1, 1.6Ghz Snapdragon 400 vs. 1.2Ghz home-grown K3V2 processor. Going the Snapdragon way is great for app optimization and compatibility, I have installed Cinema FV-5 (hardware limited to 20 Mbs video) & Kine Master movie editing apps and all work great).

I didnt get the Galaxy Note a year and a half ago because the battery wouldnt last a whole day. Anandtechs june review of the Mate 2 says "This is the first device that I've seen to come close to 24 hours of continuous usage. A combination of an efficient display, SoC/RF, and a giant battery means that it's almost guaranteed that the phone will last a full day, if not more. If battery life is truly the only concern you have in a phone, this would be the phone to buy." Dont buy the crap about the 1280x720 screen. It is the perfect resolution for the 6.1in screen. I am using it to watch movies, retouch photos, read e-books, edit movies, heck even become an Evernote paperless warrior.

With the FV-5 Pro photo app I can increase the ISO and even shoot PNG format (BEWARE 30 sec recording to card, but they process amazingly in Snapseed) and get great, available light night photos at ISO 1600. Some reviews state the 8MP camera sucks... Well it doesnt, the preinstalled camera app is the culprit.

Have had my Mate2 for about a month, bought it right here in Amazon (even got the very useful $40 flip case for free in June) and I am in Android heaven. With Feedly, Pocket, Cloudmagic and WPS Office apps, some days I dont even turn my ultrabook on. Even Huawei s EmotionUI v2 has grown on me as it packs some very useful maintenanceand optimization tools.

Cant go wrong with this phablet unless you are the kind that reinstalls ROMs to death or must have the latest Android version (or want a tiny whiney phone in which case you shouldnt be reading). People report issues with the latest Android and SD card storage - a deal breaker for me, so I went with the very stable KitKat in Mate2 and havent looked back. Check this review out: http://www.anandtech.com/show/8031/huawei-ascend-mate-2-review

title: The Samsung Galaxy S5 "Eight Inch Drop", and Other Issues--aka, DON'T Buy This Phone!
text:
I've owned five Samsung phones and a half-dozen tablets over the years, and I have to say, the S5 is the most horrible phone I've ever owned--and that includes my first phone, a flip-style one that I got from AT&T a decade-plus ago.

This phone had issues from the moment I woke it up: the battery life was horrible, the touch was either super-sensitive (how many apps CAN you open before you finally scroll to the one you actually want?), the mp3 port was almost too loose for my mp3 jack, when you used the mp3 player, it had the nerve to occasionally skip during songs.

But that wasn't the worst of it: last night, when I tried to unplug my phone from the charge cord, it slipped from my fingers, hit the counter top that was roughly six inches below--and damaged the digitizer. Brilliant green, red and purple lines look really cool... but NOT on your phone's screen.

Oh, and did I mention that I've owned it for less than 30 days?

As I said before, I've owned a lot of Samsung phones and tablets, and believe me, I've dropped every one of them more than once, often from as high as waist height. With the exception of The Kitten Incident, which cracked the screen of my S4, none of those phones have ever suffered the kind of damage that the S5 did from an eight-inch drop.

Thankfully, the business that sold the phone to me is allowing me to return the phone and get my money back, but... if you're looking for a phone model that's a little older, a little cheaper, and that serves the purposes that work for you, do yourself a favor, and DO NOT buy the Samsung Galaxy S5, in ANY of its permutations.

title: Great phone purchased at a great price, with features even the S6 doesn't have!
text:
I won't go over any technical details here, there are far better resources for you to check out there for that. I'll simply state that Samsung phones are, by and large, great for updating their handsets and giving longer life to them. A basic dual core, 1gb ram and 8gb storage device can be made to feel ancient or brand new, all through the updates to the O/S it may or may not receive. This isn't a Motorola phone--Samsung won't promise PUBLICLY and post on their website that they'll update the operating system, then, after many months of sales, backslide and give the finger to it's customers (seriously though, don't buy a Motorola anything without first checking out the history of say the original Atrix flagship phone, or many others--if you still want to support a company that did that, that's on your head).

The phone is built well, but does have some unusual design decisions. The whole water/dust proofing is neat, but more of a hassle in day-to-day life. The plug over the USB port is, in particular, quite annoying. Also, the USB port itself, as it is a USB 3.0, is a bit unusual and I've noticed the new S6 doesn't have this. And the heartbeat sensor/fingerprint reader are again a bit gimmicky. However, they are only add-ons to a spectacularly well-built and powerful phone. I've just updated to 5.1.1, officially from the carrier, and its smoother than ever. Battery life, with its user-replaceable battery, is great as after work I still have anywhere from 80% to 50% left (and thats anywhere from 10 to 16 hours of use, unplugged, and sometimes streaming music over bluetooth).

If I had the choice between this and a new S6, I'd still go for this. The camera is almost the same (the S6 has image stabilization, that is a nice feature) but the processing and storage are comparable. The S6, however, lacks a micro-SD port and doesn't feature a user-replaceable battery. And since any sane person is going to wrap up their phones in a bulky protective case anyway, what good are all the pretty design updates with metal and glass (yes, as much as I like Samsung and don't like Apple, I will freely admit they are copying Apple on the design here).

Unless there is some radical new design feature in the works that future phones will have, or if I loose/break mine, I can't seen replacing it with another phone any time soon. I know that Samsung, or the community, will keep up with any new Android OS updates, and the hardware is so powerful on most phones (seriously, check out the computing power these things have and remember its a phone) that I can easily see this lasting me 5 years, if not longer.

text: I purchased this phone with a warranty. Immediately after receiving the phone I put a screen protector and a case on the phone. Everything seemed to be in working order, I downloaded my apps and went on with my business as usual. Unfortunately, what I thought was a service issue or an issue with my app that was immediately noticeable upon first use was actually the result of the phone I received being damaged from the time I received it. I was unable to make phone calls regularly without trying multiple times, also I noticed the front facing camera had a black ring around it. I also assumed this was from an app. I took my phone to a repair center for someone to look at the problem and diagnose it. I found out that the problem wasn't the software on the phone at all, but the screen was lifting up in the corner and causing the front camera to display vignetting as well as the proximity sensor not to function properly. Due to the fact that I had a case on the phone the problem wasn't very noticeable. So, by the time the problem was diagnosed the 30 day exchange time was already up. I contacted the seller and they told me there is nothing they can do. I will have to pay 50 dollars additional in order to collect on a warranty for a phone that was already damaged when it arrived. I would not recommend buying a phone from this distributor, nor would I purchase any additional items from this distributor in the future. I hope this helps someone save themselves a lot of hassle and money.

My tablet had started smoking after the charger I used had a short in it. It ended up burning old charger port and therefore needed to be replaced - therefore I purchased this item to do it myself.

After receiving the item I opened up the abnormally large box that amazon had sent this in and noticed this was in a tiny little bag in the very bottom of the box underneath one of the boxes cardboard flaps. It would have been very easy to not see it and throw it away - just a warning.

Other people had mentioned that their headphones quit working after installing this - but I had no issues.

My tablet now works like new.

title: piece of junk
text:
It's junk. I've installed this three time, checking everything. Only two of the four legs holding the charge port surround are actually soldered. the other two are loose, which means that the USB plug wiggles around a lot. The sound no longer works. After a reboot, sound works for 2-3 seconds, then will route to the headphone jack only. (Turned off headphone detection with SoundAbout app to confirm.) If I try to plug in headphones, the new part will only give me sound if I apply heavy pressure on the headphone plug. If I leave it alone, I get crackling, and the sound disappears. At least with the old broken charge port, I could use headphones.

This only allows slow charging while the plug is in. It's so finicky that you can't use the device while charging. The plug pops out due to the flex and the fact that it sits farther back into the case than the original. I had to shave plastic off my USB plug to make it wedge-shaped so it could reach farther into the socket.

Even when plugged int, it charges so slow that you can't run any games while charging. It discharges faster than it takes on a charge.

This was not worth any amount of money for me. Spent more time in re-installing and troubleshooting than the entire tablet is worth. I'll look for another part supplier to see if I can resurrect my Nexus 7. Otherwise, will have to buy a new tablet. I don't believe this is an OEM part...it's actually worse than the crappy OEM part.

This connector fits the 2012 Nexus 7. It's easy to install if you have a spudger and a tiny philips-head screwdriver. It fixed my tablet's ability to charge.

Where it fails is: 1) It does not work as a USB port, only a charging port. So it's much more difficult to copy files to/from the tablet or sideload apps, and it's impossible to do more exotic things like unlock or root the device. 2) The sound port intermittently sends the signal that headphones are plugged in, even if they aren't. In effect, I can no longer use the built-in speakers most of the time. 3) The ribbon cable between the charging port and the headphone port is about 1/8" too long, so I had to bend an S-curve into it to make it fit. Works for now, but it's not reassuring for long-term reliability of the headphone connection.

title: Another Great Product from the Magnet Masters
text: This is made by Logitech, the same folks that have created the best magnetic clip-on keyboard for the ipad--so know something about designing a functional accessory for an electronic device involving magnetic adhesion.  The good news here is that mount is small and unobtrusive so it can stick to just about any surface (windshield or car panel).  Also, the magnet is powerful enough to keep your iphone in place even if you have a thin, protective case enclosing it--I'm not sure, though, if the magnet would be strong enough if your iphone case is one of those thick, bulky, rubbery ones.  Also, the magnet is not strong enough to keep your iphone in place if the roads are rough (not a problem here in Texas which has good, well-maintained highways). title: Best car mount I have ever used!
text:
At last, a perfect smartphone car mount that works on my car! This car mount requires you to attach a small metal plate to the back of your phone. The phone then adheres to the magnet inside the mount. The phone can then be easily put on the mount, or detached instantly to used as a phone if needed. The mount attaches to the window or to an adhesive backed plastic disc you stick on your dash. You attach it by moving a yellow-green lever (the end of it is visible in the photo of this item) to activate the suction on the bottom. The mount holds very firmly to the window or to the disc on the dash until you move the lever back to its original position, releasing the suction.

The mount comes with two metal plates to attach to two phones in the family, in case you are sharing the mount with another driver.

The only difficulty I had with this mount is that the lever, because it holds so well, is a bit hard for me to move at the angle I have to use it when attaching to the dash or window. I am an older woman and I don't have the hand strength that I used to, so this may not be such a struggle for someone else. Once you get the mount in place, this mount is the best I have ever used.

title: This mount is genius - I use it in the car and at work
text:
The design of this mount is elegantly simple and highly functional. The twist lock is a little difficult to turn but the suction base is powerful and holds the mount very securely on a windshield. With the included adapter it can also attach to the dashboard. The adapter is a disk about the same size as the base of the mount with adhesive on one side and a smooth shiny black surface on the other. To use it you need to attach the adhesive side to the surface you want to use the phone mount on.

To make the phone stick to the mount they include two 1 3/8" x 1 3/8" x 1/32" thick metal plates with adhesive on one side. The plates can be attached on the inside back of thinner cases or on the outside of thicker cases. To make them more attractive when attaching them on the back of a case or phone they made the plates in two finishes; a grey brushed metal and a matte black. I use soft cases and attached* the plate on the inside of a Fossil TPU case and a thicker Lucky silicone case and it worked great for both. The phone sticks to the mount very securely but is still easy to remove.

As great as it is for using in the car I love using it at work. I attach it to my desk using the dash adapter and I can easily glance at the phone screen to see notices or respond to messages without needing to pick up the phone. Great for speaker phone and FaceTime calls too.

Its small, roughly 2 1/2" x 2 1/2" with the top closed and doesn't weigh much so it is easy to tuck into a glovebox, bag or briefcase. I love it.

* When I went to attach the plate in my case I looked at the pristine back of my iPhone. Knowing a soft case allows the phone to move slightly I didn't want to have the exposed edges of the plate contact the back of my phone and possibly scuff or scratch it. Also I like to change cases and have more than two I use on a regular basis. I left the cover over the adhesive backing on the plates and used thin strips of clear packaging tape around the edges to attach it to my case. It workes great and now I can move the plates from case to case.

I have to compliment Logitech on the design of the packaging for this mount. It's mainly cardboard with a tear strip on top. Just pull the strip and you're in. Thank you.

First off this thing comes with a very powerful magnet and a suction cup. The suction cup attaches to your car windshield on the inside. DURABILITY

PROS

FOR NAVIGATION

title: is now my top rated and favorite smart phone mount for the car
text:
i've been on a crusade and have gone thru so many products to mount my iphone in the car (for GPS use). I can finally recommend this one and have decided to stop the search. Here is why and why all the other products fail.

1. Vent-clipped mounts. Great cheap solutions. Terrific view angle and looks great aesthetically. Problem with them is that not all vents are clippable. They could be loose and thus risk phone drops and damage. AND you now have a vent you probably rely on on those more extreme days of temperature - blocked. Lastly, in cold climates - probabl not a good idea to be blasting heat directly onto your smart device's battery.

2. Glued/Adhesive Based Mounts. These are mostly the magnetic mounts. Hot days the glue will melt and your base will be unstable and possibly even drop your phone for damage. Not good. Also with phones getting larger and heavier -the sheer weight of a smart device might be enough to unhinge a glue/adhesive based mount. They also don't necessarily adhere that well to a lot of textures surfaces car manufacgturere love to use now.

3. CD/DVD based mounts. Firstly - CD/DVD drives are becoming fewer in cars. Secondly, these "clamps" eventually loosen forcing you to tighten it more thus bending your internal drive to more extremes... NOT good.

4. Clamshell mounts. These are dashboard "claw-like" mounts that hold your device like a binder clip. Until i got this product i'm reviewing, these were my recommended products. Because they mostly were re-usable, movable industrial strength gel-based adhesives. This made them mobile and movable between cars. They also had great viewing angles. Only problem? they could get bulky and on hot days your phones could overheat.

5. windshield mounts. Quite simply on hot days windshield suction mojunts could fall off.. and the heat on your device from the windshield could get extreme.

So why this product then? It's a windshield mount with magnets! Well.. they solved most of the problems with a super strong windshield suction cup that truly works and does the job. It's EXTREMELY stable. The magnet allows for flexibility and ease of use and using different angles. It's so compact it doesn't become an obstacle to your vision. And heah.. there's stil the windshield heat. I guess you can't win them all.

Still.. someday somebody will figure out how to make the ultimate, no compromises mount someday. OR - the industry of creating mirrorable touchscreen screens of your device to OEM infotainment screens will take over - perhaps even a BT/wireless infotainment mirroring screen. Or perhaps - cars will become "smart devices themselves" that you can pair up on your wireless accounts with shared data with your phone?

This little device resolves or solves every one of the shortcomings of all the different devices except 1 - heat exposure. I'm willing to deal with that (even in CA) since we're talking maybe only 1-2 mos a year to worry about that.,

title: Compact, simple and good looking... BUT
text:
I love this car mount in theory, but it doesn't quite work well for me. Here's why. When the metal mounting plate/sticker is in the center of my phone (A Nexus 5) my NFC connectivity is seriously diminished, and when I add my case it's non-existent. I can mount the metal plate off center, but then the phone doesn't stay steady for the whole drive and can not me rotated. My car dash is excessively curved and textured, so I can't mount the suction cup anywhere on it, even with the smooth disk. On the windshield however it mounts fantastically, and even though I think the twist is a little difficult, it works really well. But once mounted I can only tilt in one direction (typically up and down). This works well enough unless you get a strong light reflection on your device, in which case a left/right swivel would've been a really nice feature.

Okay so those are my specific grumblings... Keep in mind this is still a gorgeous and simple way to mount your phone in your car. If you don't use NFC, or if your NFC radios are in the top of your phone, you'll be fine. If your dash has even a rough but flat surface, you'll be fine. If you need to take your mount from car to airplane to rental car, it's ideally portable. If you have two phones, you're in luck, they provide two mounting plates. And once installed it's a joy just to stick your phone on and then just as easily pull it off when you arrive. If this is you, consider this a 5 star review. Needless to say, I couldn't wait for this Logitech Smartphone Car Mount to arrive, but I was quickly disappointed. My HTC One is not in a case. Instead, I have a metallic bumper around the phone, but the back is completely exposed. The metal strip meant to stick to your phone case does not work on my cell phone because its back is curved. Even if it weren't, I wouldn't ruin the aesthetic with a metal strip. So I'm passing on this car mount, but I did test the magnetic strength, and it's pretty impressive. The suction mount is also easy to operate. To mount this on your dash, however, requires sticking a circular plastic strip on the dash where the suction would mount. Not a fan of that either. If I were to use this product, I'd opt for the windshield mount.

All in all, a great quality product, but not for my back curved, no case cell phone. You can't be all things to all people, but this Logitech product comes close.

text:
First of all, I did not purchase thru Amazon, but at Best Buy, where the price was a fair amount lower. As others will tell you, this is a well thought out mount. Nothing new, as suction cup mounts have been available for years. But, what sets this apart, is a unique "super suction" action that on a clean window, will probably hold for a very long time.

My only issue is the placing of the magnetic plate to the phone. I have a Galaxy Note 4 (Verizon), and cases are hard to find due to Verizon instructing Samsung to slightly change the location of one of the bottom microphones for their phones. Aargh! I was able to find a case and holster at a Verizon store for a reasonable price, but the back of the case is a heavily textured rubberized material that I don't believe will adequately allow the Logitech metal plate to completely stick to. Make sense? Can I take the case off and adhere the metal plate to the back of the phone? Sure, but the Note 4 back cover is made of a plasticized material. It might sufficiently hold. (Other phone cases will have similar textured back covers)

i think Logitech is missing out on offering more cases that have a huge metal area for the back cover. (You would not even need the sticky metal plate for those) They do have some cases for the Galaxy "S" series and others, but it doesn't appear that they are covering the newer phone market.

So....I'm on a hunt for a case with a metal, or at least smooth plastic back, that is really compatible with the Verizon Note 4 variant. Wish me luck.

title: Best iPhone accessory I ever bought
text:
This thing kicks ass. When coupled with the Logitech Protection Plus case, it's the best iPhone accessory I ever bought. I get in the car, hold the phone up and it snaps itself into place. Get out and it's just grab and go without fighting any mount points. Awesome.

You twist the little green knob to mount it. I like mine on the windshield close to the rear view mirror (I'm used to glancing that way so it's very natural to look at the GPS maps like that without taking my focus off the road). It seals down so hard that I would be nervous about using it as a dash mount. I drive a SUV over some rough roads and road construction areas, never a hint of it not holding onto the windshield or my iPhone. It's rock solid.

The hinge does not rotate so getting it to point directly at me required I mount it twice (just rotate the knob, pull the tab to loosen and it comes right off). Once I mounted slightly rotated, it all lined up perfectly so the phone is directly pointed into my eyes for maximum viewing ease. Since it's a magnet, it's very easy to rotate the phone around a bit once it's set on the mount so you get it just right.

I intend to use this for business travel in rental cars so it was important a mount be easy to pack. This fits that criteria since there are no points to snag on anything. Just close the hinge and it's a small, smooth cylinder. Should work great in my carry-on bag but I'm not sure I'd put it in my laptop bag. The magnet can't harm a phone (flash drive there, not magnetic media) but I don't know about placing it a bag right next to my laptop that has a disk drive (which is magnetic media). My carry-on has side pockets so it's easy enough to access there when I get to the car lot.

title: Near perfect!
text:
This is a near perfect product from Logitech as far as portable and universal mounts go. Logitech has always been a top rated company that stands behind their products with warranties.

I had previously reviewed a universal generic phone cradle that was used in our second older vehicle that did not have navigation. My husband continues to use that mount. When the Logitech mount arrived, we were initially impressed at the sleek but simple styling. After reading the included literature, cleaning our car window and applying the metal disc inside our Samsung Note's 3 Otterbox case, we were finally ready to go. Installation is rather simple when going onto a glass surface. If you have any manual dexterity issues then you MIGHT need help from another party. My husband couldn't get his wide fingers at the right angle. When I attempted to turn the knob, I found that it was just too hard. After a moment or two, my husband was able to turn it. Very annoying but it makes us feel as if the actual mount will not be going anywhere.

Once the phone is magnetically mounted it does not rattle or jump even when you throw some of the bumpiest NYC streets at it. If your dash is smooth, you will be able to use the suction cup. If it isn't, then you will need to use the peel and stick type adhesive.

The reason that this mount is great is because of it's portability and ease of use when dismantling. The small pod can be thrown in your glove compartment or even purse if tou fear leaving the item attached overnight. Logitech was kind enough to include a second magnetic disc for an extra phone. This comes in handy when sharing a vehicle.

The only and inly gripe which forced me to knock off a star is that you cannot swivel/rotate the phone, only move ot up or down a bit. The earlier reviewed and cheaper mount has that ability. This is what forced us to continue using the other product in our home vehicle. The Logitech cradle has gone to a work vehicle because ot can be easily attached and detached daily. So far it has been performing.

Highly recommend if you are in the market for an ultra portable UNIVERSAL phone mount that will hold your phone for hands-free operation. Logitech is a great brand that has yet to disappoint.

title: Very nice mount, a bit hard to deploy but very solid
text:
**** Update 01/26/2015 *****

When it is cold, the suction cup loses some of its flexibility and the hold is noticeably less. On a very cold morning it wouldn't even hold the phone unless I purposely pressed it flat prior to turning the yellow handle. Make sure you store it in the slack state and not with the handle turned. Even when in the 50s, the deformation of the suction cup results in less hold, though enough to hold my phone.

**************************
This is a very solid mount when attached to a windshield. It can also be attached to a dashboard but if the dashboard has texture to it, you'll need to use the included adhesive disk to provide the correct attachment surface. This attaches via suction. The center of the suction cup is pulled upwards when you turn the yellow bar about 30 degrees, until it clicks. Several folks who I had try it (plus me) said it was hard or that it hurt a little to make this happen. When you turn it back, the mount doesn't just come off, it needs a little oomph or you can peel back the cup.

When attached it works great. I used it with [[ASIN:B00K9YXXHY Mofi Flip Pu Leather Case]] which has metal in the cover. When flipped backwards it attaches very firmly to this mount in landscape mode. The included metal mounts work well if attached through just one layer of leather but not through a layer of leather plus the plastic part that holds the phone. So don't count on it being able to work internally if there is any more than a few millimeters of thickness.

The metal mounts (plates that are about 1" square) are adhesive so can be mounted externally, but I didn't like the look of that.

This is a great mount if you are going just attach it semi-permanently or use it just once in a while. It is five stars because I am assuming that is the use case; the magnetic mount is used for quick attach/detach and that works well, If you are going to attach/detach the mount itself everyday then you might want to consider a unit that does that more easily. There are also dash-focused ones that use an air vent that you could consider if you don't want to mess up your dashboard with an adhesive pad.

title: Logitech really nailed it!
text:
I've probably spent a small fortune looking for an effective and unobtrusive cell phone holder for my car. The best one before this was a mount that used the CD opening but that blocked the face of the radio or held the phone at an upward angle. Other auction mounts didn't create a strong enough hold, especially during hot (or very cold) temps. Plus the best mounting area on the dash is slightly curved and the mounting pad wouldn't work well. Both of these problems were exacerbated by having to slide the phone into the arms of the holder.

This Logitech model doesn't have those problems. First the phone connects via pretty strong magnets rather than arms. So you're not making adjustments to any arms that then disrupt the hold to the dash or windshield. Other holders I've used that also used a magnetic connection between the phone and holder had a tendency for slippage and the phone would slip off the mount over time or if you hit a bump in the road. And the auction to the dash or window is exceptionally strong. The holder is very secure.

So far, I couldn't be more pleased!

title: GENUIS! I wish I've had this for far longer!
text:
First, I have to confess, I am a big fan of Logitech. I have used and been happy with a number of their products, including my current wireless mouse. (The one time I had a problem with a product, they replaced it immediately, no questions asked, with great customer service.)

Second, my MO for using my iPhone in the car is to hook it up to my Belkin TuneCast, and then put my cell upside down in the cupholder next to me, which requires looking down if I wonder what tune is playing, or if I get a text, or someone calls. Well, that changed when I started taking a glass of tea to work with me... my cup had to go into the cupholder, which meant my phone had to go into my lap. Not the best location, especially whilst driving on Atlanta highways.

Third, I LOVE this product. It is simple, easy to use, takes up a small amount of room, and is GENIUS. And means I don't have to do my second point anymore.

See that yellow knobby thing in the photo? You use that to attach the *very strong* suction cup to your front window. If you decide you didn't place it quite right (which is what happened to me), it's easy enough to twist it, remove it, place it where you want it, and twist the yellow knob back and it's attached to the glass again. Easy peasy. That smaller gray plastic bit is adjustable so you can optimally view your phone.

If for some reason the best place for it in your car is on the dashboard, they handily provide a mounting adaptor for that too!!!

Now, how does the phone attach to the end of the mount? Again, genius, simply, and easy... They provide you with TWO, count 'em TWO 'metallic universal adaptors' - a little 1 5/8" square. You simply pull off the plastic backing and stick it on the back of your phone. It's so slim that it doesn't interfere a bit with your phone case. :) And the second piece o' metal is for your kid's, partner's, friend's, etc. phone... or your GPS, or your other phone....

So, NOW, I get in the car, pop my cup in the cupholder, plug my Belkin into my phone and place my phone on the car mount... and away I go.

I've got it positioned perfectly so I can glance at it and see what tune I've got playing, and I can lean forward a teeny bit to skip a song I don't feel like hearing, or I can press the 'home' button and tell Siri to find me directions.

Now, you do have to get used to it a wee bit.... and make sure it's not in your line of sight or will distract you from the road, but after a week or so, I didn't notice it unless I wanted to.

Seriously. Genius. Get yourself one. It is WELL WORTH the price.

title: Perfect solution for iPhone GPS navigation
text:
This is the perfect solution for having an iPhone as a GPS navigation device and in-car phone kit in the car. It's extremely easy to set-up and is visually appealing with a minimalistic look on the windscreen.

Initially I was a very nervous about whether this car mount would stay on the windscreen and if the magnetic hold on the front-facing mount would be strong enough and sufficient to hold my iPhone without falling off while driving around in the car. But I am happy to say, this thing is rock solid and there is no way the mount or iPhone is going to fall off. The magnetic hold on the front-facing mount is really strong and holds my iPhone really well. Even when I purposely drove over rough roads with potholes to see if this thing could handle it, I was very surprised and extremely happy to see that my iPhone 5s stayed in placed, and didn't even show any signs of sliding around. It just stayed perfectly in place.

The car mount is marketed to use with the Logitech +Case as it's magnetic on the back. But instead I used the provided universal adaptor (magnetic plate) on my thin case for my iPhone 5s, and it works perfectly. I hope Logitech will put out a +Case for the iPhone 6 soon as I'm hoping to upgrade my iPhone and might even consider using the +Case as well.

title: Best car-mount for your smartphone!
text:
If I ever need a car-mount for my iPhone, this would be it. This ingenious device from Logitech met all requirements for a car-mount: you can put it either on the dash or windshield, and even relocate it if you change your mind about location. It is the best looking phone mount that I know of, and I have several them.

It is much smaller than I envision, and weight very little. It has a nice and smooth texture, feels nice to the touch. To mount it on your windshield, just turn the yellow handle. Suction is really strong, I don't think it would fall off anytime soon. But time will tell, in my experience, most suction-typed mounts will become loose after a while especially under hot weather.

The mount comes with 2 metal plates (about 1" square each) with adhesive back that you could glue to the back of phone case, either inside or outside. The mount's magnet is strong! I tested the plate before stick it to the back of my phone case and am sure that the phone won't fall off while on the mount. Good news is, the glue on the plate is just as strong (or stronger) so the mount's magnet won't rip it off your phone! But it also means that it will be tough to remove the plate after you install it.

This is the car mount I like the most. I don't use a car mount often, but I put it in my car for long trips or when I need to use my iPhone for navigation.

title: Different Car Every Week!
text:
First these aren't cheap but wow are they worth it. I have 2 as I keep one in my car and one is my luggage (weekly flier). #2 gets put on and taken off of a new windshield weekly and I've come to learn a few things about these. One is that changing temperatures and condensation will affect the suction cup.

Being wary of breaking it as +- 15% of users have experienced I'm careful to grab the knob all the way at it's base so that I'm twisting that which the knob is connected to, not just the plastic. 44 times this year I've put it on and taken it off with no wear apparent on the knob function.

Last pro tip - before committing to positions by removing adhesive put it on your windshield/dash and attach the plate magnetically and then visually line everything up. If you have a large phone and you windshield mount you may have to go higher on the case with the plate than you think. On my Lifeproof with 6s it actually covers the apple logo. And allow the adhesive a little while to cure. It will work better.

I've paid full price for every one of these (3 total, left one behind in a rental) and am in no way reimbursed or discounted for this review.

title: A Very (Un)sticky Situation
text:
I received my One-Touch Smartphone car mount today. I drive a Toyota Prius so there is no flat space on my dash to attach the suction to. Knowing this ahead of time, I planned on using the dashboard mount accessory that comes with this to mount my iPhone. Upon opening the package and peeling the cover off of the dashboard mount adhesive side, it was immediately apparent that there was no actual adhesive on the adhesive side. Like, it sticks to nothing. It just slides down my dash as soon as the car moves. I therefore, can not mount this on my dashboard. I live in CA so I can't mount it on my windshield except in the lower corners of my windshield and I drive a Prius which means that I can't even reach the lower corners of my windshield. I'm hoping I received a dud of dashboard mount as I haven't seen any other complaints for the accessory. Also, to Logitech's credit, I've locked/unlocked the mount multiple times and haven't had any breaking issues that so many other users have experienced.
Right now, if you're looking to mount this to your dash and you don't have a flat surface to use, I suggest staying away from this product. I mean, unless you'd enjoy a $50 paperweight.

title: RIP Apple
text:
I was going to give it 3 stars, but the text that corresponded with 3 stars was "It's Okay". I paused and thought about that for a second, and concluded no. No, it's not okay. The company that Steve Jobs built is self-destructing before my eyes; it' not okay. It was the only tech company that 'got it'. It's the only company that felt like the product was tested with normal people instead of just staff at the company. It's iOS that worries me, not the hardware.

First off, the music app was butchered past the point of death. They are pushing Apple Music so hard that it feels like you are in an online store, not an offline app. It's littered with icons that basically cost money to touch. You don't have the option of having icons for songs, artists, albums, playlists, year or any other common-sense field that you may want to see in a music app. A "Recently Added" banner takes up half of the screen when you popup the music app in a desperate attempt to make people purchase songs from the store so they can see the banner change. You are unable to search more than 3 results at a time without navigating away from the search page. The list goes on, but I will stop here because one Amazon review won't stop you from worrying about the Music app.

It also always prompts you to update your software every day, with no option of turning off these prompts. If it was another company, like HP, that did this, I would take it easy on their software and give this a 4 star review, but because I am witnessing one of my favorite companies (not so slowly) burn themselves to the ground, it's a much more emotional review for me. I knew that Apple would go downhill after Steve passed, but I didn't know the hill would be 90 degrees.

This is a known issue and a simple Gooogle search will turn up tons of people with this complaint, which Apple will not acknowledge. Save your money. This issue started to happen within less than a year of owning my 128GB iPhone 6 Plus, which again Apple will NOT replace without a $329. title: NOT NEW - 15 months old and broken!!!
text:
Would give it a 0 if I could. These are absolutely NOT NEW. It was 15 months OLD when I got it and OUT OF WARRANTY!!!

First, the delivery was delayed by over a month (shipped from China). Then I had a problem with the screen (so it appeared) after two months, went to Apple store...Apple said it was originally sold on 12/21/2014 (I bought it here on March 26, 2016 --- 15 months OLD and OUT OF WARRANTY). The phone is advertised as BRAND NEW, but it had a previous owner. I had to pay $130 for a new screen. But that didn't fix it... after two months the screen was not working again! It turns out that the phone was bent (the Apple store tech saw this when I first went in, but the phone screen had failed a diagnostic so it got replaced) and not only was the screen damaged but also the motherboard (main circuit board in the iphone). So right after fixing the screen, I see occasional screen glitches...which get worse over the next 3 months until the touch screen capability fails. Take it into Apple store and it's the motherboard failing.. the apple store tech he has seen this a lot -- should always buy from an AUTHORIZED dealer to make sure the phone is really new.

So it was refurbished. During the first visit to the Apple store, the tech pointed it out and said the seller definitely knew it was bent (it was pretty obvious once pointed out). Bad enough I paid $770 for a falsely advertised brand new iphone, and to add insult to injury, KNOWINGLY (or incompetently) shipped a bad phone.

The Apple store tech said he sees this stuff all the time... big problems with phones bought from unauthorized dealers like this one..and the phones are ultimately almost all refurbished selling as NEW.

What ever happened to integrity and honest deals?! You will NOT find it here.

Apple took care of me...

title: Expensive Gimmick.  Get the Note 4 Instead!
text:
I love Samsung phones. I’ve owned the Note 1, Note 2, Note 4, S4, and S5 (personal and work phones). If not for the great Droid Turbo, I’d be rocking the Note 4 right now. The Note Edge is the first Sammy Phone I’ve handled in a long time that I do not recommend.

I got my hands on a review unit and was able to spend a decent amount of time playing with the phone. Below is what I liked and disliked about the Note Edge:

✔ PROS:

- Basically a Galaxy Note 4 with the additional “Edge Screen”
- Note 4 like beautiful screen. Works well outdoors
- Fast performance
- Good camera: good low light shots, 4K video recording, OIS
- Good battery life
- Removable battery
- SD Card Slot
- Includes a stylus pen
- You can interact with the “Edge” while the main screen is off
- Selectable/Customizable panels that can be used on the “Edge”

✔ CONS:

- The “Edge Screen” is a neat idea but there’s no killer application for it
- You may accidentally press the controls on the “edge” while swiping or handling the phone
- The “edge” displaces the usual locations of the power and volume buttons
- If you are left handed, you can flip the phone around. However, this would put all of the buttons and jacks in unexpected locations
- The camera app puts controls on the “edge”, making the app hard to use
- The Stylus Pen is good only if you bother to use it. I bet most will not take full advantage of it
- Contract and off-contract pricing is more expensive than the starting prices of all of the best phones

✔ BOTTOM LINE:

I wanted to like the Note Edge. I really did. It’s neat. It’s a conversation piece for sure. And it allows you to have a phone that most other people will not have. For tech geeks like me, that’s often a good selling point. :-)

While the “Edge Screen” adds some functionality, it also adds a few issues. Notable issues include accidental presses and button displacement. The Note Edge also has a starting price that is higher than the best phones available, sans storage upgrades.

If you are considering this phone, do yourself a favor and get the cheaper Galaxy Note 4 instead. If you do buy the Edge, make sure you hold onto your receipt and packaging so that you can return it. Until there’s a killer app for the “Edge”, this phone is more gimmick than practical.

✔ WHAT PHONE SHOULD YOU GET:

Here are the phones you should get, based on the feature that matters most to you:

- On Verizon? Get the Droid Turbo. Period.
- Big Screen: 1. Samsung Galaxy Note 4, 2. iPhone 6 Plus, 3. Nexus 6
- Best Camera: 1. Phone 6 Plus, 2. Samsung Galaxy Note 4
- Best Software? 1. Droid Turbo, 2. Moto X
- Best Battery? 1. Droid Turbo, 2. Samsung Galaxy Note 4, 3. iPhone 6 Plus
