I purchased this this phone from Mobile Connections on December 30, 2016. The phone was presented to me as being NEW. I expressly and directly asked if this phone came with a warranty. Mobile Connections expressly and directly told me that, "yes, the phone comes with a one (1) year warranty". Back in June of 2017, I started experiencing issues with my data network, texting, and calling. Then, I started getting an intermittent green line appearing on the edge of the phone that allows me to access my shortcuts, etc. This green line renders the shortcut bar inoperable when it appears. When I contacted Mobile Connections to have the phone repaired under my year warranty, SURPRISE! This phone is no longer under warranty! After several months of useless and unhelpful back and forth banter with both Mobile Connections and Samsung, It has been determined that Mobile Connections is activating the warranties at point of purchase from Samsung. So, Mobile Connections is sitting on a phone for "x" amount of time before lying to its customers and claiming that the phone COMES WITH a one (1) year warranty. Now, I am stuck with the repair bill for a phone that started having issues six (6) months after purchase. A phone that was advertised as NEW, though, it appears to be a re-furbished product. I feel extremely taken advantage of and am disgusted at the way Mobile Connections is conducting business.

My first ever Amazon disappointment. The phone never worked - has cost me countless hours on Skype, travelled to three continents and done enough air miles to have its own admirals club card.

Enough said.

title: A Tale of 2 Samsung Wireless Charging Pads...5-Stars & 1-Star
text: I own a Galaxy S6 Edge, with the Samsung protective "snap-on" clear back cover. I originally purchased (2) wireless charging pads (Black & White). The "Black" wireless charging pad works flawlessly per my expectations. I work virtual office, and I am constantly removing & replacing the phone on the charging pad during the day. I am frequently operating the phone, while it is on the charging pad. 1.) The charging pad always instantly recognizes the phone's presence, and the "Blue" Halo LED indicator light illuminates indicating charging is in progress. 2.) When placing the phone on the pad, the "sweet spot" [effective charging area] covers almost the complete pad diameter - I never have to place the phone twice. Either I'm extremely accurate (without trying), or the surface is very forgiving...I suspect the latter. 3.) The "Green" Halo LED indicator light will illuminate when the phone is fully charged, and will remain so until the phone is removed. The charger is inactive while the light is green. 4.) I was careless once and tilted the phone while on the pad, and slid it around the surface. The "Blue" LED indicator light began to blink, which I assume indicates some type of fault/error condition. [Note: As of last week there is no user manual. Also, the pad uses the same charging adapter as the one which came with the phone, and supports rapid charging.] This is the only time I have ever seen the blinking "Blue" indicator light condition. It appears that charging may be suspended in this state. >>>>> The "White" charging pad  was the complete opposite. 1.) The charging pad seldom worked when the phone was place on the pad. When I would finally align the phone with the small "sweet spot" there is a brief delay before the "Blue" charging light illuminated. 2.) Almost every time the phone was charging, the "Blue" charging light started flashing and would flash until the phone was removed (see flashing reference above). Even if the phone managed to fully charge, and the charging light turned "Green", if the phone was not removed within several minutes the "Blue" indicator light would come on and start blinking. Sometimes the phone would become unusually "warm" during the charging process. The "White" charging pad has been returned for a refund. Amazon support has been terrific thus far. Conclusion: You be the judge... (2) pads, exact same model number. One rocks, and has epic cool factor! The other was completely unsatisfactory. Did I get a lemon? Is there a firmware/hardware issue? Is the issue specific to one color model (production issue)? I spent much time investigating, with Samsung support, as the white pad matches my white phone. In the absence of a user's manual, dealing with the new technology has presented Samsung with many support challenges. The technology has been available for years, but this is Samsung's first attempt to build it into their phones.There are QI charging pads reportedly compatible with the Samsung Galaxy S6 other than Samsung's. I have ordered the TYLT Vu wireless charger and I am interested to see how it performs, for comparison.

title: Great charger
text:
When I became aware of the wireless charging option I decided it was something to try. I learned of various third-party offerings but didn't want to potentially degrade the water/dust resistance or possibly void the warranty, so OEM seemed worth a little extra money. Also, saw mention in various reviews of problems associated with some of the third-party options out there. I ordered this and the Samsung Galaxy S5 Wireless Charging Battery Cover (CG900IBUSTA).
Note - you MUST have either this back or some other charging back installed on the S5.
The charging pad is plug and play - literally. Plug the charging block (included) into the wall and the USB cable (included) into the charging pad. This is the identical wall charger that comes with the phone - so you now have a spare - bonus! No other setup required - except for installing the charging back on the phone. Looks nice as you would expect for a factory Samsung accessory - an attractive desk accessory. Small footprint, only 3x3 inches.
Charging works perfectly, dead simple. Using the Samsung system I have not encountered any heating problems I have seen mentioned by some, mainly non-OEM systems. Right off the charger my CPU temperature reads 93.5 and that's not hot. Right off the charger the phone back is only slightly warm to the touch, really no more so than if it had been on a charging cable. My impression is charging takes slightly longer (no empirical evidence to prove it) , but the convenience of not dealing with the port cover or cable more than makes up for it to me. Now whenever I'm not using the phone I just set it down on the charger and it stays charged. Answering calls or messages, I just pick it up without monkeying with a cable.
Some have noted that the pad is small - I don't see this as a problem. I have had no problems with placing the phone on the pad. The indicator light on the pad glows green when the phone is properly placed for charging, and I have not found it to be finicky at all. Nothing but gravity holds the phone in place. This should not ordinarily be a problem. If you have cats or kids or other critters that might disturb the phone on its perch, be advised.
Some have expressed dismay that it stops charging when the battery is full - well, good! Leaving a fully-charged battery on a charger is a bad idea. So overnight charging, in the morning my phone is at around 95%, and hasn't been charging a full battery all night. Pick up the phone to reset the charging cycle, put it back down for a few minutes and top it off. Tell me you don't pick up your phone first thing in the morning anyway! Not an issue to me, all chargers should be so smart.
I have really come to like wireless charging, especially knowing my phone's environmental protection and warranty remain uncompromised.

title: Probably best used for phones that support Qi wireless charging out of the box...
text:
This charging pad appears to work about 25% of the time. What happens is I set my phone (Samsung Galaxy S5 with a Qi wireless sheet inserted into the back) down on it, I get the blue indication that it is charging. I leave it alone, not touching the phone at all. Then anywhere from 1-4 minutes pass by and the blue light is flashing, indicating it is no longer charging. I lift the phone off and place it back down. Get the blue light again...but shortly afterwards, it'll stop charging. Averaging it out, 1 in 4 attempts of placing it on the charging pad will keep it charging for the duration. I've played around with placement angles and locations plenty. What works one day doesn't work the next. That is annoying. For full disclosure, I do have a protective case (Spigen series), but this same issue happens with or without the case attached.

Another caveat to be explained is exactly how hot this one gets; if I leave it alone on the charging (when it is actually charging), I can feel a good deal of heat coming off my phone, to the extent that it is almost too hot to hold and I wouldn't want to have to hold it while taking a call immediately after lifting it off the pad. I noticed the other day that my screen protector was starting to bubble from my usage of the wireless pad.

Lastly, this does *not* automatically shut off when charged full. So if I'm not paying attention to it, this little thing will start cooking my battery and screen protector for no gain.

Not anymore - this charger sits on my nightstand and waits for me to just put my phone down on top of it. It charges quickly while I sleep and in the morning I pick up the phone and go, sooo easy!

Two reasons it only earns four stars:
1) you have to be sure you hear the little "ding" sound when you place your phone to be charged. No sound = No charge. The sound indicates phone has connected to the charger. You have to place the phone correctly or the charger doesn't know it's there.
2). As you can see in the photos..the charger looks haunted in the dark! When using the charger it glows with this VERY bright neon blue LED light that is very annoying if you are trying to sleep. It also starts to blink on and off if it's incorrectly connected to the phone.

title: From excited to extremely disappointed
text:
I was super excited to receive this in the mail, to be slightly closer to eliminating wires from our life. But after a month of erratic performance, I can't vouch for this product. For a few days, the charger seemed to perform ok on and off, but more often than not, I would wake up with my phone charged to 70% or so instead of 100%. This probably happened 3 out of 5 days. After reading other people's reviews, I tried ensuring that the phone was *exactly* centered on the pad, and thought that this helped for a while. But then I went back to waking up to my phone at 70%.

A couple other strange behaviors I noticed. One, the charger turns blue when charging, and then changes to a bright green light when the phone is fully charged. Sometimes, though, after charging for a while it would change to a bright blinking light instead - perhaps indicating that something was wrong? But I hadn't moved the phone in the meantime when it was charging happily for over an hour, so I can't imagine what would have been wrong.

And the last straw was this morning - I woke up to find my phone completely dead, even though I had placed it exactly centered on the pad and verified that my phone was indeed charging last night. I can't risk that happening (that's my alarm clock!) so I will no longer use this product as it is virtually useless if it can't be dependable. Unfortunately this last straw came just 4 days after our return window was over, so apparently I can no longer return this item.

It might just be that my product was off, but read the other reviews as well and be forewarned...

title: A beautiful product with many flaws - read before buying!
text:
PROS: Beautiful looking product, comes in a multiple colors so that you can match the aesthetic to your phone, has a nice looking blue light which illuminates when your phone is charging (more on this in a moment), easy to setup, and it allows you to conveniently charge your phone without having to plug any annoying cable into your phones charging port.

CONS: There are a few surprising cons which could easily be deal breakers for some people. Firstly, there is no way to shut off the bright blue/green charging light on the pad (wow..really?) so unless you want to be kept awake at night or woken up by a disco you won't be able to have this charging pad beside your bed. The next con is that the charger will STOP charging your phone when it reaches 100% charge and from that moment on your phone will begin losing charge. If you are like me and you charge your phone overnight, the likelihood is that your phone will reach 100% charge in the early hours of the morning and then be down to ~85% charge by the time you wake up (again, wow really?). Lastly, the instruction manual is basically non-existent and provides no information on what the different colored lights mean (blue, flashing blue, green, etc) and does not mention any details of the 100% charging issue or what to expect from the product.

title: Works perfectly with the Note 3
text:
Works perfectly with the Note 3! Easy to just toss on and charge. No special position or perfect placement needed! I find about 10% of the time I have to move it slightly to charge. Great for night stands and work desks. No more cords, easy to grab and place back.

You will need this for the Note 3: http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B00F3587PW?redirect=true&ref_=cm_cr_ryp_prd_ttl_sol_9

For many people complaining and expecting miracles from this product, I will help a little with some key points

1. This is Wireless Charging 1.0: Meaning it charges at about 750ma-1000ma. Most of you are used to wired chargers that can handle 2000ma. This is wireless, it charges half as fast due to half the current. New wireless charging 2.0 pods can handle 2000ma+. This is NOT one of them.

2. Make sure your phone is even capable or wireless charging. Just because it says its CAPABLE, doesnt means its equipped with the technology. Like the Note 3, it requires the back cover first.

3. Noises, lights, notifications, etc are all varied from model-to-model and from OS to OS. Some show a charge light, some make noise, etc. Mine doesnt do anything except illuminate the charging LED on the front. Turn the device screen on and see if you get the charging indicator near the battery to be sure.

4. This is the most common/standard wireless charger out there. It should and will work on other brands. Ease of use or results will vary, but it does work

5. Cases might be an issue, expect a little trial and error

Worth it for me. But keep and eye on prices as they change greatly.

Note: The factory Note 3 image (meaning Touchwiz) works great with the Charging base lights. When the phone is fully charged it changes to green. The phone also tells you with a temporary notification that it is now using wireless charging. While using CyanogenMod 10, it simply stays blue at all times with no notifications other than the charging light.

title: So bad compared to its competition.
text:
New to wireless charging, I bought this one and another brand. This one had soso reviews but they all seem to because so many people complain it wont work with their phone or not at all. Most people are idiots so I had to try two brands. This one cost more because it comes with the plug in charger and cord while most you need your own separate chargers and cord. The other unit I got would not charge my phone because it was "slow charging" because I was using a 1amp charger, and I learned you need a powerful charging "cube" for the wireless to work. That charger is great. Now this Samsung charger review: its junk.

Its hard to find the "sweet spot" where it will actually charge the phone. Thats bad enough, but it will always give a sold blue light "everything is ok" and phone says its being charged then about a minute later will start blinking and the phone wont be charing anymore. By then you'd already walked away and come back to an uncharged phone. So you need to put it om the charger, and wait a minute or two to make sure the light doesnt start blinking to know its actually charging. My other charger is easier to put the phone down and it right, and when its not it will either give a solid light or blink right to tell you something is wrong.

Next problem: This Samsung charger, once the phone gets to 100%, it will start blinking and it will stop charging the phone, thats bad enough that now once you get to 100% the phone starts draining, but my phone will detect the charger so the screen turns on and will go back to screensaver, but a few minutes more the phone sees the charger and screen turns on again, but the light is blinking so it never charged the phone. This will go on all night so your phone screen is coming on and off all night which wakes you up and the phone discharges much faster because the screen it coming on and off all night every 10 min with no charging. Stupid design. Possibly its my phone (Droid with Motomod wireless charger back from INCIPIO with no case) but the other wireless charger will charge the phone to 100% and keep slow charging so the phone stays at 100% all night until you take it off and the screen never comes on and off with the phone seeing and noseeing the charger all night.

Another problem: the blue ring light around the bottom of this charger is super bright. So its annoying if you use this in the bedroom when you sleep. Then you add the fact that when the phone gets to 100% charger, the thing starts blinking all night. Really? Again maybe that is my phone that has the problem that it can no longer see the charger, but my other wireless charger doesnt lose the connectiong at 100%. Also my other wireless charger has a photo light sensor so the blue light ring is only as bright as the room. In a pitch black room you can hardly see it, perfect for sleeping.

So while yes it does charge the phone if you get it just right, but then it discharges after 100%. My other wireless charger has none of these problems. Big thumbs down on the Samsung unit. Buy elsewhere.

title: Works, but not as advertised
text:
This charger is very stylish and comes in the original factory packaging with 1 year warranty from Samsung. The inner ring of the charging surface is rubber, which helps the back of the phone grip the charger and stay connected. This is true whether your phone has a case or not. When the phone is properly aligned on the charger, the LED will glow blue; when the phone is misaligned, the LED will blink blue until the phone is taken off the charge or realigned. My criticism of this charger is the 100% indicator. In all tech reviews in the blogosphere, the green LED color for a complete charge is mentioned. What isn't mentioned, however, is that this is only for the latest generation of Samsung phones. I have the Samsung Galaxy S5 and when the battery reaches 100%, the LED stays blue and does not turn green. I was initially confused by this, but then saw the following sentence from Samsung's website for this charger:

"If using a Galaxy S6, Galaxy S6 active, Galaxy S6 edge, Galaxy S6 edge+ or Galaxy Note5, it will also alert you when your device is fully charged."

I believe this is a limitation of the GS5 devices and prior in that Qi Induction was still new and Samsung did not factor this into the charging behavior of the phone. Unfortunately this isn't well documented, and had I known this, I might have selected another charger. This is especially true given the price tag of this charger.

4. Data drops. Nearly every day for almost 20 min at a time i cant get any data connection. I dont know if its my area or T-Mobile but I wont have any data until i restart my phone and manually select what data service to run off of.

5. Speeds. This phone has an average clock speed that pretty similar to say a Huawei H868C ( my first android phone that couldnt handle even the intensity of its own calculator)
Finally, yes this phone is very great for an inexpensive decent user but will not match up with any Asus products. In the past ive seen a lot of good from Asus but this model of phone is a real downer for me to their name. Trust me when I say this, spend $100 more and get the 5.5in with 4gb of RAM or the zenfone lazer because either of those is a huge step up from this pay as you go phone.

6. Storage. The phone does have 16bg f storage but for some reason it has 13.6gb on system reserve that is not accessible so im limited to the remaining 2.4gb. title: Practically perfect phone.
text:
I decided to opt-out of yet another Verizon contract and instead purchased a phone outright because, honestly, no new device is worth losing my unlimited data plan. After using Galaxy Tabs for a few years I felt confident about getting a matching phone. I can't believe how much better the phones are than the tablets- there's almost no comparison. It also doesn't help that I came from an HTC Rezound, which started out as a good phone but was ruined by HTC refusing to optimize their devices for battery life and Verizon never updating the software.

I find this Samsung Galaxy S3 to be a perfect device. The size is ideal- not like those new ones that are uselessly large. The screen is clear and colorful however still difficult (but not impossible) to see in direct sunlight. It updated to the newest Android on the first network connection and runs smooth and fast. The 4G works well in an area that supports it and the wi-fi and bluetooth are much better than other phones I have used. The bluetooth consistently connects to my Subaru stereo, which my HTC struggled with.

The battery life on this phone was questionable- even frustrating for the first week or so. Fortunately, rooting this device is ridiculously simple as well as unlocking the hotspot. After rooting I was able to freeze and uninstall enough bloatware to greatly help battery life. With moderate use I now deplete about 50% battery per day. (It is amazing what a good 4G connection helps, but when I was visiting Los Angeles with 5-bars of 4G all the time I would get through a whole day using only 10% battery!).

Finally, the only disappointment about this device is the total lack of accessories. I use the RND desktop dock which works fairly well but NO ONE makes a car dock for it. The iBolt ones are a ridiculous joke- I ordered one that didn't work and they wouldn't honor return shipping. And it is impossible to find a clear TPU case to show off the blue back of the phone.

Overall, this phone is awesome. I have not been to an area to use the global feature yet, but it certainly is a nice option. I would recommend this phone without hesitation.

title: LG giving others a run for their money
text:
Currently, I am using a Samsung Galaxy S5 and an HTC One M8, having found over the past year that each has its special attributes. Switching between the two during any given day gives me flexibility and has well prepared me for the LG G4 which has similarity in function of both models. My last LG phone was about four phones ago and I think this one was worth waiting for.

This has a camera with superb options, the ergonomic body design has a mildly contoured back, its removable battery provides enough power to get me through a day without a recharge, it has audio that is better than my Samsung S5 but not as great as my HTC One, the memory can be expanded with an additional microSD card, and its large screen is superb for presbyopic users, especially when the Home buttons are hidden. The HTC One has prepared me with the double tap option to turn on the screen, but nothing has prepared me for the power and volume button on the rear, creating very smooth and uninterrupted side edges which give a very sleek look to the device.

I personally am not dedicated to any one phone manufacturer and upgrade mine every couple of years, generally retaining the last one for use without cell phone service, simply using it for wifi and camera capabilities. I donate the previous phones to the police department. The LG G4 is a model that has impressed me very much and I will be purchasing another one as soon as my plan allows replacement of a second line. Technical specifications are very clear on this site as well as the LG website, so I will not restate what you likely already know if you are at the point of reading these non-professional subjective reviews. title: Well, I liked the phone itself - I just didn't like what Verizon did to it.
text:
I was all excited to be able to try out one of these new LG G4 phones and had been reading everything I could on them before it was sent to me. Which I think is the source of my disappointment in this phone. Apparently Verizon felt the need to disable a number of the features that LG put into the phone. One being the FM radio. That was something I was really expecting to be there. It is something my current cell phone has and something that I use a lot while at work. While it might seem to be a small thing, it's pretty much the deal breaker for me.

Add to that, that I also took the phone into the local Verizon store with the intent of transferring over my cellphone account to them. Going in Saturday morning I found the store empty except for the three employees. So I was able to sit down with one and not only discuss changing service but had him go through the features and functions of the phone. Apparently he was demoing a G4 himself and been using it for awhile. Asking him about the FM radio he said it had been disabled, but that I could use Verizon's Slacker Radio app instead – but just remember that will make use of your data plan. He also mentioned that the theme feature was disabled as well as the multi-use profile function. Getting to talking about actual service plans – he suggested since this was a demo, to go with their no-contact monthly pre-pay plan. And that for $45 I could get unlimited calls & text and 1GB of data. Hmm, that's less than what I'm getting with my current provided I told him – for $45 I'm getting the same calls & text, but also 5 GB of data. Yes, he said – but Verizon's network is so much better. How much better?, I asked. With my current 4G LTE service I can watch You-Tube videos with no problems and stream music and watch videos. That's around here he said – if you travel you probably wouldn't have that same level of service. Problem I have with that, I don't really travel. So in the end I passed on switching my service over.

So I've been just using the phone without cell service and connecting via wifi. I have to say the LG phone itself is great – it takes fantastic pictures. And the speed of the processors make apps fly. I even like that the main buttons are on the back of the phone in the center. I especially like the Amazon suite that the phone comes preloaded on the phone. It combines all the other Amazon apps together into one screen.

I also purchased a case for the phone and a 32GB micro-SD card. I was happy to find that there are a lot of different cases available for this new phone (there doesn't seem to be any for my current phone).

So in the end, I love the LG G4 phone itself, just don't like how Verizon disabled it so that you had to use their data plan instead. (Which is why I'm giving it three stars.) So if you're thinking of getting one of these – get the phone somewhere else than Verizon.

title: Review for Verizon version plus list of default apps
text:
Rather than going into tons of benchmarks and specs which are available and better explained on sites like Android Authority, I will provide my own personal observations. I am reviewing the Verizon Wireless version of the LG G4. It is important to note that this variant has less features than those from other carriers. For instance, some of the missing features in the Verizon version are: LG SmartWorld, Multi-user accounts, FM Radio, Themes and Custom lock screen.

########## Color / battery cover ##########

Also of note is that the version I received has the basic plastic back, not the leather one that some models ship with. It is interesting to note that, even though I have the white version of the phone, the front of the phone is still completely black; no hints of white whatsoever [at least, from that view]. On the back side, however, the door cover and buttons are white. If you switch the door cover out with another color, the only white parts left on the phone are the buttons (and the small molding around them). So if you end up with a phone color you don't like, know that you can mostly switch it to one you do like.

It's important to note that the plastic back is slippery and hard to hold; very little friction. As a result, the phone took several dives out of my hand. If you get the plastic back, I suggest also getting a case. If you get the leather back, you may not need a case (unless you want something to guard the front of the phone). Just keep in mind that the leather back does not work with most third-party cases; they are designed for the plastic back.

########## Hardware features ##########

Because I knew my Samsung Galaxy S5 would eventually become outdated, I spent the last six months or so researching my next phone. I was disappointed to learn that many phone manufacturers are removing hardware features that I have grown accustomed to. For instance, the new Samsung Galaxy S6 does not have a removable battery (or at least one that is easy to remove) and it does not have expandable memory. Phone makers are follow Apple's tread of charging way too much for internal memory and then removing the option of using inexpensive SD cards as an alternative. Those of us who don't have unlimited data, or constant access to the cloud, often download videos and music so that we can listen to them locally. I realize that media is heading into a subscription base format rather than one where we own what we buy, but even [some] subscriptions allow for offline downloads. So for me, not having expandable memory is a huge negative, and paying hundreds more for memory that should only cost $20 is out of the question.

This is one of the features that attracted me to the LG G4. It has a removable battery for those times I need a hard reset, to swap a dead battery with a charged one, or even when the internal battery dies and needs to be replaced. It also has an external SD memory slot that holds up to 2TB!! I didn't even know they made cards that big!!! The external memory alone is what makes this phone so much more attractive to me than that GS6.

########## Camera ##########

Another huge feature is the camera. The front camera has higher resolution than the GS6, making selfies better quality, but as a photographer I am most excited about the ability to shoot images in RAW. Why? Because photo editors can do a lot more with RAW images than they can with jpegs that have encoding on them. Using Photoshop and Lightroom on RAW images makes taking photos with my cellphone a great feature as a photographer. Not only can I master things like white balance, but the owner of RAW images automatically proves ownership of copyright should there be any legal question to the rights of your images.

########## Button location ##########

Chinese researchers tested and discovered that a person's pointer finger naturally sits on the back of the phone just under the camera. This is why the HUAWEI Acend Mate 7 was designed with a fingerprint scanner on the back rather than the bottom front as was added to the Samsung Galaxy S5 and S6. I was skeptical at first, but after testing it for a while, I find the button on the back does indeed fit me naturally. You can power the phone off and on and also increase or decrease the volume all without having to "look." For those of you who don't like the idea of activating your phone's screen by using the back button, there is a knock code unlock feature. The beauty of this unlock is that all you have to do is tap a pattern on the inactive screen, and then the screen will automatically power on AND log in. This way you don't actually have to press the power button on the back to access your phone.

When I was looking to upgrade my Samsung Galaxy S5, I checked into several Chinese phones. The reason being that these phones are really well made and come at a lower price than American releases. One of the biggest problems I found with these phones is that the buttons are on the side and close to the center. Since most every car mount I've tested holds the phone at the center point of the sides, this makes mounting the phone difficult if not impossible (unless you go magnetic or sticky, which I'm not keen on). Not having any buttons on the sides of the G4 takes away this issue altogether.

########## Using phone on other networks ##########

Verizon's device unlocking policy states, "We do not lock our 4G LTE devices, and no code is needed to program them for use with another carrier." That includes this LG G4. However, during the setup process, when I tested putting a T-Mobile SIM card into the phone, I got the error message "Non-Verizon Sim". My options were to restart the phone or boot in Wi-Fi mode. So I booted in Wi-Fi mode and tested calling with the T-Mobile SIM. Neither calling out or receiving calls worked. But when I went into Settings > About Phone > Status, I noticed that the T-Mobile number showed up under "My phone number." Then, I went back a level and clicked on "Network." Verizon showed up as the network name. That said, shortly after clicking the network name, T-Mobile showed up instead. Once that happened, I was able to make and receive calls using the T-Mobile SIM. From there I needed to add T-Mobile's APN (Access Point Name) for the data to work (since Verizon uses different bands). Just keep in mind that this phone's software is designed for Verizon, so you may need to download some alternatives to get everything to work correctly (such as a visual voicemail app).

########## Default Apps, grayware / bloatware ##########

Here's a list of notable default apps I found on the phone, and whether or not you can uninstall them. From what I've seen, the LG G4 is far less bloated than the Samsung phones I've owned:

title: Solid Smartphone
text:
A modest step forward.
The LG G4, is a solid phone but not revolutionary. It retains many features some of us like, but doesn’t really add anything new or exciting to the mobile device conversation. By now there are tons of detailed reviews of this device online. You can even find people taking this phone apart piece by piece telling you everything that is inside. I am going to cover what I think are the highlights and lowlights for me, your average everyday person who regularly uses a smart phone to get things done or to just pass the time.

-Lightweight but sturdy in hand, I have the white case, which is plastic, painted in a glossy white ceramic paint. I am a bigger guy with large hands and a pretty big head and this things feels just right in my hand, especially since it is slightly curved. Just enough to barely notice and make it feel good in the hand.

-Nice, big, bright, slightly curved screen, very sharp resolution, and an auto-dimming feature that actually works pretty well compared to others. The brightness makes it pretty easy to read in bright sunlight which I appreciate. The response of the screen is quick and crisp, but the keyboard makes more mistakes than previous phones I have used, it could be me, but I notice I have to fix my spelling more on this phone so far than on others.

-No built-in wireless charging. When I took off the case and saw a pad glued to the inside of the back of the case, I thought there was built in wireless charging, turns out it is just for the NFC. As of now, if you want wireless charging you have to buy a special case to replace the back of your phone.

-Which brings me to charging the phone, I have multiple aftermarket chargers, I tried to charge the phone with them. And the phone said they were incompatible and I have to use the original charger. I even attached the phone to a charging port on my USB hub, and no luck. I found that kind of a bummer, as the OEM chargers are always more expensive then the aftermarket chargers. I am sure the aftermarket will catch up, but as of now that is a bummer.

-Sound quality is great when making calls, some say it has more to do with your network or connection, but the majority of my calls sounded really good….this is a phone first, right?

-No wait, the camera! The main camera shoots 4K video and looks great, really, really good. The back facing camera also does a great job at good looking selfies. Video quality is great, sound recording above average. Night time or low light photos, average, not better or worse than anyone else really.
-Small things that matter: this model has 32GB of storage built in, but you can add a micro sd card of up to 2TB (When they come out, they aren’t out yet) I kind of love this idea, I love having lots of music on my phone, since they don’t make large capacity music players anymore so this phone can take up that roll in my life and I can store my whole music collection on it, or even a ton of movies.

-The battery is also replaceable. Thank you. This batter wears out and need replacement, easy fix job. Unlike other phone providers where you are just out of luck.

The software is Verizon’s version of the lollipop operating system. It works fast, Verizon has a few tweaks and apps that make organizing information and media nice, but nothing that is so spectacular that I would go through a detailed explanation.

Overall a sold phone with good hardware and some old school features that many of us still want. Nothing amazing or game changing but a good phone to get me through the next few years. Any questions? Feel free to leave a comment below.

title: Frivolous phone to fix a "problem" that's not really a problem, and causes new ones
text:
The big draw of the curved screen is supposedly to get notification flashes even when the screen is face down. The solution to this "problem" that doesn't require an unnecessary phone just to be a walking marketing ploy for selling new phones to people with perfectly good ones is simple: don't put your darn phone face down. What a concept. You can use the "edge screen" to see extra tidbits of info along the side... what is this, a CNN rolling news bar? Or even better, the existing notifications bar that drops down from the top? What a completely worthless, redundant thing to create. I can't even call it a feature, a feature is something I would have to be able to use practically. You can turn both of these "features" off, and once you do it makes having this phone fundamentally worthless.
The Edge is difficult to grip because of the screen curves. The power button is in an inconvenient spot toward the middle of the phone, right where a palm or finger holding it would be, leading to nothing but annoying pushes in the middle of use. The internal lighting isn't enough to overcome the curve of the phone, so there are constant visible shadows (or glare, depending on your lighting) down the length of both sides of the screen. So on either side of photos, videos, and fullscreen activities you don't get true color display, there's a built-in shadow caused by the design of the phone REGARDLESS of what angle you hold the phone at. The screen is curved but the keyboard and display are not, so you have an awkward rounded space to click on a flat display item - especially problematic while using the keyboard with its tiny keys. And in terms of useless starter apps, this Galaxy is the most gut-loaded with junk by far. It even came with instagram, so you can partake in the commodification of culture straight out of the package!
Most irritating of all and by far what makes me loathe this phone the most is: this glorified flashlight is literally impossible for me to use. The screen being 3D and not flat gives it a sort of 3D-within-3D appearance like some kind of sci-fi haptic hologram (or, for a different visual, like a backlit layer of spilled koolaid). My eyes don't know what the heck to do with it! So using this phone not only messes with my depth perception (aka ruins it) but gives me motion sickness when I sidescroll.
I was pressured into getting this phone by a retail associate at my carrier. Between that and its terrible ill-conceived design, it's clear to me that it only exists for the sake of being a new phone to draw in people who need to have the newest phone at all times. If I could give this review zero stars, I would. I was going to really try and make this phone work, to give myself some time to get used to it, but it's so unusable that it's not even worth it.

title: Possibly not a good switch for Pebble users.
text:
I really wanted to love this watch, I gave it two days of usage before going back to my Pebble Classic. The watch is beautiful, and works well, but I had a number of issues coming from a Pebble:

1. Battery Life, even on minimum brightness this watch DEVOURS the battery. Even after I turned the watch face off (which, between notifications and wrist movements, it didn't seem to spend much time off), it still burned out pretty quickly.
2. Vibration is very weak. Makes more noise than vibration, noticed my phone vibrating in my pocket several times, and never felt it on my wrist. I know how to check the settings, and the watch was receiving the notifications.
3. I just expected more from the Android Wear App store. 1,000 fitness apps, no really good alarm clock apps. Granted, Gentle Wake on the Pebble is the most amazing app ever, so I may be unfairly biased here. The inability to search for Android Wear apps without a third party store app is also kind of bad on Google's part.
4. The Mesh Band is awkward. Maybe it's just been too long since I wore a good metal watch, but my goodness it should not take this much effort to fasten a watch band. A two hand and one table affair for me.
5. This thing is heavy. Again, maybe I'm biased toward the pebble, but the Hauwei Watch felt like a lead weight on my wrist. It was actually tiring to wear.

I will give this watch its dues though. The screen is beautiful. The aesthetics of this watch all around really are absurdly good. If I had a need to wear a smartwatch to a formal dinner, this would be the one. Also it's fairly snappy, you can tell the hardware is more than capable of handling whatever you want to throw at it. Finally, as much as I like the Pebble, having Google Now and GPS on the watch are two features I will miss leaving the Huawei Watch behind.

Bottom line, if you care about the look of the watch, and if you are used to/don't mind heavy watches, this IS a spectacularly gorgeous watch. But know that you'll be recharging it often, and the vibration is just not up to par. Returned it and went back to my Pebble Classic.

title: Still the Best  Smart Watch available today (May 2016)
text:
I have owned several Smart Watches over the years since Samsung released its first GEAR in September 2013 which was based on the regular Android OS (before android wear and Tizen took over wearables). That watch actually still has features severely lacking on many wearables today. Since then I have tried Samsung Gear 2, Gear S2 3G, Apple Watch (which is my least favorite of all of them), LG Watch Urbane and Urbane 2nd Edition, and now have settled on HUAWEI watch.

THE GOOD:
Huawei Watch is powered by androidwear (Marshmallow), so it recognizes apps on an android phone and gives notifications for apps you use most.
This watch is one of only a few androidwear devices with an ACTIVE speaker
You can Make and Receive phone calls DIRECTLY from the watch while your phone is connected via Bluetooth
There are some beautiful watch faces available for it and its amoled screen is sharp and beautiful
The watch is beautiful, solid stainless steel design, and the initial unboxing presentation through the beautiful box Huawei uses is second to none.
Battery Life in my usage is about a day, although you may get more if you use less brightness and darker watch face
The straps are Quick Connect and can be changed with most 18mm watch straps on the market.
The experience is much better than current devices as Samsung switched to Tizen OS, which has some benefit with battery life, but software on Tizen is severely lacking.

THE NOT SO GOOD:
Huawei watch is powered by androidwear. Yeah it is a pro and a con as androidwear, although improved in Marshmallow, is still a work in progress. There is sound for phone calls and alarms but still no sound/voice feedback for Google Now (OK Google results are silent) and there are no sounds for notifications. I am hoping a future release will give that as an option.
Price- Retail price, although within market pricing, is too high for many to decide to give it a try. (Deals can be found however and I ended up with about $80 off retail price through Warehouse Deals damaged box item)
Not every android app you use everyday has an androidwear sub-system.
Battery life could be better, it is not, in my user experience, as some reviewers have said up to 2 days. I usually need to charge it around 9-10pm after starting day at 6am.
The puck charger device is severely lacking. It is magnetic but you also have to be sure watch is lined up with pins on the charger and sometimes it takes several tries to get it on the base just right.
You still need the phone nearby to make and take phone calls. There is no Mobile based version of this watch yet which connects via your wireless carrier. Currently the Samsung Gear S2 3G (TIZEN based) and LG Watch Urbane Second Edition (androidwear) are the only 2 that can connect independently. I have tried both on at&t and neither performs all that well as Number Sync which is supposed to route your phone's telephone number to the watch is still very buggy. These watches also lack the ability to switch out their rubbery watch straps and their battery life is terrible.
Hopefully Huawei or some other androidwear manufacturer will find a work around for these problems as time goes by.

#1. I keep my screen turned off and just turn it on when I want to see time or use it. I use the double button click to turn the screen back off. This has the downside of "ok google" networking without turning screen back on but it EASILY extends my battery life past two days (including sleep tracking)
#2. Accelerameter seems to work well, my steps seems to track accurately compared to my VivoSmart, and my Sleep as Android nights seem correct.
#3. Replaceable watch bands is great, wish they had replaceable faces too, the black looks nice.
#4. Heartbeat seems to be decently accurate and does not eat battery, even when sleeping.

Cons:
#1. It has a speaker in it which is not enabled.
#2. It says IP67 waterproof, but EVERYTHING says do not put it in water. I would have liked to shower/bath with it on.
#3. Battery needs to last a week. Mine currently lasts two days or so which is more than enough for what I am using it for, but worrying about it does suck a tad.
#4. "ok google" does not work with screen off.
#5. To not have the flat tire look they did away with light sensor, but the watch it LARGE enough they could have easily put it in the watch face
#6. HUGE issue, the vibrate module is on the FRONT of the damn watch! When it vibrates you DO NOT FEEL IT. You can hear it vibrate just fine, but you don't feel it at all.

All in all this has been a great watch so far, looks sexy as hell, has good functionality... I hope they enable the speaker soon.

title: Huawei Watch Tethered to My Huawei Nexus 6P - an Ideal Combination
text:
[[ASIN:B013LKLS2E Huawei Watch Stainless Steel with Stainless Steel Mesh Band (U.S. Warranty)]]
The Huawei (wah-way) Watch arrived two days ago via Ontrac one-day free delivery. Two days later Amazon knocks $50 off the price (see above link). Nice! If I had just waited two more days I could have saved 50 bucks. My wife was very impressed with my sense of timing.
My wife and I waited for the watch all Saturday afternoon (thinking it would have to be signed for). It was marked "Out for Delivery" to be delivered before 9 pm. Just after 9 pm when we had all but given up on getting the watch I noticed in the tracking status that it had been delivered and "signed by 43." We hadn't signed for anything and had no idea who/what 43 was. Then I heard something thump on our front walkway and discovered the package had been tossed over our front gate as the delivery vehicle was driving away. There were a few anxious moments, but we were very relieved it wasn't delivered to the wrong party.

After setting it up with my recently purchased Huawei Nexus 6p Google smartphone Saturday night, I wore the watch the next day. Everything seems to be working as advertised. Considering the watch and phone were both made by Huawei, I would have expected nothing less. Everything it's supposed to do, that I've tried, it seems to be doing. Of course, I haven't had time to try everything, only those functions I deem most useful to me.

The AMOLED 44 mm display under the sapphire glass is very clear and easy to read and there is a satisfying variety of watch faces that complete the elegant look of the watch with its stainless steel case and mesh bracelet. That seems to be the main feature that sets this watch apart from most of the others in the smartwatch field, the overall "normal" watch-like appearance of a high end dress watch when being worn. Marketing folks and third-party reviewers emphasize that in their advertising and reviews. I have to agree. It is a very attractive timepiece, and much more. I'm somewhat of a watch collector owning more than 30 watches of various types, sizes, makes and models including a Galaxy Gear 2 smartwatch and was given a Gear S for a short while, which was rendered useless when I bought my non-Samsung Huawei Nexus 6P. The point is, the Huawei Watch blends right in with most of the other digital and analog watches in my collection in feel and appearance. It is very comfortable to wear and, as the advertising suggests, has the look of a high end dress watch but one that can be used as your daily wear as well.

It's a minor thing, but I noticed it necessary to be sure the magnetic connection between the watch and charging dock is secure to insure it is charging because it isn't a very strong snap on magnet. After insuring a solid mating of the two pieces it doesn't take very long to charge the watch battery which still had about 53% when I put it back on charge last night after wearing it most of the day, but admittedly didn't place a heavy demand on it other than displaying the time and getting just a few - It was Sunday. - notifications, including a couple of phone calls, during the day.

I browsed the many Android Wear applications such as an Android Wear mini-launcher, a calculator, Agenda calendar, Weather app., etc., on Google Play and downloaded a few to try on my new watch. I was not disappointed. The watch, tethered to my Nexus 6P, installed each application effortlessly and automatically and became ready for use almost immediately. There are a lot more Android Wear applications than I need, but I intend to put many of them to the test as time permits.

I find the huge selection of interesting watch faces developed by very creative and imaginative designers very intriguing, and most of them are free while the others are modestly priced around a buck each. One advantage of owning a watch like this, at least to a would-be watch collector is that you can have what looks like a different watch every day, if not every hour, by changing the watch face to suit your mood or situation. I'm thinking of selling a few of my other watches because of this. (I guess I'm not much of a collector after all.)

There are some fitness-related apps that come with the watch and others that are available on Google Play like those available in other smartwatches some of which are tailored to fitness types. But, nearing my 75th birthday, I'm not very athletically inclined, meaning I don't exercise as much as I should. That said, I still found it interesting that the heart rate function seemed to have no trouble measuring my bps as well as my wife's. Her's was significantly higher than mine, probably because I failed to take advantage of the Amazon $50 discount that arrived within hours of buying this watch. I may get around to measuring how many steps I take in local malls when I drive my wife to get her mall fix three or four times a week. That should be good for laughs.

I read a couple of reviews, although expressing overall positive impressions of the watch, thought the Android OS still needed more work to elevate the Huawei watch above the rest at this price point. They are the experts and know best about the finer points of what to expect from a smartwatch. Me? I'm just an everyday Joe who enjoys dabbling with high tech goodies and, so far, have found the Huawei Watch very satisfying. If the Huawei people decide with Google to upgrade the Android smartwatch OS in the near future, so much the better. However, the primary factor in my purchasing decision was the earlier purchase of my Huawei Nexus 6P smartphone. I was so impressed with the quality and performance of the phone, I thought it worth matching it with the Huawei Watch and, although owning it only one full day, I think my buying rationale was on the right track.

This is a smartwatch I would recommend to my tech-savvy friends who can afford it. It is a bit pricey. But hey! Amazon reduced the price by 50 big ones today. So go for it.

title: Great watch, rubbish charger
text:
I'm not going to repeat what everyone else on here has said about the beautiful build quality of the watch.
I was a one of the 1st Pebble owners, from Kickstarter at the very beginning, and I wore my 1st gen Pebble for over 2 years.
I got fed up with squinting to read my emails and texts, as you couldn't change the font size, and I don't have x-ray vision.
This time I fancied something less geeky looking, and something unlike the Apple Watch and Asus Zens that look like you have a small TV on your wrist.
Being an average sized woman, I was slightly concerned by the size of the Huawei, but I am a fan of big watches, and once I put it on, it didn't dwarf my wrists.
I got the stainless steel mesh, as it works well for both men and women.
For those people complaining about scratches-Yes, they are metal. Shiny metal does scratch! Smh
The Android wear interface is great, and for those things that are missing, there are a myriad of apps to add those functionalities you want.
My faves are Wear Speaker, for putting your phone on speaker from the watch, Feel the Wear, for customizing the watch's somewhat weak vibration to make it much more prominent, Coffee, a great app for text messaging, Wear Mini Launcher, for getting to your apps way more quickly and smoothly and Wear Charger, a widget that comes up on the watch face to let you know it's charging, similar to the Moto 360 charging face, as let's face it, you need good eyesight, which I don't have to see the pathetic little zig-zag thing that is the Huawei's charging indicator.
This is where the watch loses a star, for the frankly below standard charger. the charger lets down the overall top notch quality of the product. I'm sure they'll rectify that on the next gen, and I'll end up forking out another $400!
The battery life is OK for me, not amazing.
I'm now managing to get 15-17hours out of it a day, which is pretty good, as I like tilt to wake on, otherwise whats the point of being hands free? And I like the always on display. I don't want to be wearing a bracelet with a black screen on my wrist. I want a watch!
I've played with various ways to increase battery life, and I've found that turning down screen brightness to a more than adequate 3, turning off card previews, and blocking notifications from certain apps has helped. I don't need to know if one of my friends has liked a new cat picture.
Your watchface is also a big factor. I love some of the gorgeous animated faces, but they suck the lifeblood form your watch.
I've looked at Skymaster, Ranger and some of the other great faces, but they're all a bit 'Look at me, I look like a pilot!'
I'm using a very nice face called Ceres Paper watch, which is very informative, and doesn't have me sweating about whether I'll still have a watch at 8pm.
Overall, I think it's the best Android Wear piece out there. I considered the Moto 360...very hard, but eventually was put off by the flat tire, which would only have looked good with all black watchfaces....without the number 6...No thanks.

It's a great watch, if you don't get one of the dodgy ones with the red tint.
But if you do, don't moan about it, this is the joy of Amazon...Send it back and get another one!
I was 3rd time lucky.
But I have no regrets....until the new one comes out in 6 months....

title: Amazing Smartwatch by Todays Standards
text:
While these watches are a far cry from complete, the comparison between this watch and others (Moto 360, Apple Watch, Gear S2) reveals that this is the best choice at this time. Battery life always lasts at least my entire work day, puttering out by the time I go to bed after a day of moderate use (edit: more exact usage: I've had my watch for 4 months now, and after 7 hours on full battery-bleeding brightness it's still at 71% battery.) Moderate use for me is using this watch to control my smart home automation/security system, checking the many notifications I get, checking the weather, checking my stock, and occasionally finding my phone when I lose it.

I get loads of unsolicited compliments when wearing this watch. Many are shocked to learn it's not a analog watch, and it's definitely fun to watch people's faces light up when they realize what it really so. My father is a die-hard Apple fan that has purchased an Apple Watch, yet I've had numerous compliments on how much brighter and more brilliant this watch is over Apple's meager attempt. The screen is incredible - it could be higher resolution (you do sometimes notice the pixels), but it's high enough that it doesn't bother me. From two feet away it's definitely hard to see any pixels, and that's what this watch is made for. Android Wear is designed around simple, quick access - not around viewing images or playing games (although you can do this if you really want.)

Last but not least, I wanted the leather band initially but I had to order the metal link band because it was all Google offered at the time. I'm glad I did this in the end, because it also gets a lot of compliments. At the end of the day, this is a really fun accessory (and it looks SUPER cool at night), but it's more of a fashion accessory than a practical accessory. Don't buy one to make your life easier, buy one to enhance the sophistication of your attire or appearance. In essence, it will do both - but I think unless you're quite wealthy that a purchase like this will disappoint if you're primary ambition is to streamline your life (unless, of course, you REALLY want to do a lot with it and are willing to customize the heck out of it - then you actually may get what you're looking for. Just be prepared to learn the "tasker wear" app and do a lot of research.)

I have had two other smartwatches: the LG Urbane, which was very good but a bit big on my wrist, and the Samsung Gear S2 Classic which was great looking and more reasonably sized, but it's Tizen operating system I found to be irritating. title: Great watch, but a work in progress.
text:
I am a big fan of gadgets and love trying out the new gizmos.
This smart watch is well made but not perfect.

Pros:
1. Great build quality. It really is impressive how well this watch is built. From the moment you open the box, there's no mistake that this is a premium smart watch. The stainless steel on the watch looks good even though I've already banged my arm against the door, wall, etc a few times over the last two months. I also like the quality manufacturing of the band, and the nice bracelet-like heft it has.

2. The sapphire crystal glass is strong and is still perfect looking after a couple months of careless use.

3. The touch screen is responsive and the resolution of the display doesn't leave much to complain about.

But for such a high-end / premium smart watch, it has some obvious fails.

Cons:
1. Charger. The charger clicks into place on the watch using magnets, which would be super slick, if it worked properly. But everytime I find that I have to juggle/push the watch in several attempts to get the watch to charge.

2. The display does not automatically adjust the brightness. Usually leaving it at 1 (i.e. least bright) works fine as far as visibility is concerned. But I was really hoping that at least some of the watch faces would look like a real watch, but alas it cannot. The watch face always looks too bright or too dark.

3. Battery life: To get a full day's use out of the watch, I found that I had to manage the screen time even with lowest brightness setting. I.e. can't leave the full color screen on all the time, blank it out at times when it's not being used. The battery only lasts 14 hours or so even with the ambient mode (i.e. just a simpler version of the watch face that is usually black/white only.) and auto-on based on wrist motion.

4. No compass. It's not a big loss, but I have a smart watch that is half the price, (Sony Smartwatch 3), which has its own built-in gps and compass. Don't know why they couldn't squeeze it in there...although to be fair, the Sony Smartwatch 3 doesn't have the heart rate sensor.

I know that the wearable computing is still in its infancy and some issues (like the battery life) is common across almost all devices. But I also think that this is one of the best Android smartwatches out there, yet still it's just not good enough to make me want to wear it every day.
But it is good enough that I am really looking forward to what the 2nd gen watch will be like.

title: What a great watch!  Big step up from Moto 360 (1st gen)
text:
Update March 2019: It's still doing great! I've been wearing it every day since September 2016. No decrease in battery life!

This is a great watch! Coming from the original (1st gen) Moto 360, it is like day and night. What I didn't like about the Moto 360 mainly revolved around the poor battery life. In order to preserve battery, I had to keep the display off most of the time. I also had to keep app usage to a minimum. Lastly, it wasn't terribly rugged. The plastic on the back cracked (despite my purchasing Steelconnect m adapters) and the watchface scratched.

The Huawei watch, in contrast, has plenty of battery life. It is not uncommon to end each day (14 hours or so) with over 50% left, even though I have the "always on" screen enabled. I noticed that when the watchface "dims" after 10 seconds (this interval is variable and can be set by user), it only dims slightly - which makes it very readable, dimmed or not. I worried at first that this would eat up battery life and that it would cause burn-in to the AMOLED screen. Neither of these problems has happened. There is no burn-in, in part because the screen moves around, ever so slightly. I use watchfaces mostly from Watchmaker (they are free and there is a huge variety). I have the watch set up so that it rings whenever my phone rings. This doesn't seem to be affecting battery life, although my phone doesn't ring much.

The screen is beautiful. The AMOLED screen has the expected deep blacks and bright colors. It should be pretty scratch resistant since Huawei built in a sapphire crystal display. I find that setting brightness to 3 is plenty. I find a setting of 4 (out of 5 max) to be too bright. To be fair, I have been using mainly dark watchfaces, since I know that these watchfaces consume less energy on AMOLED screens. I don't know what battery life would be like with a white watchface. The watch is plenty bright in the daylight. And I can look at it anytime and read the time without any trouble, whether the screen is "dimmed" or not! Just like a real watch!

I like the styling and overall feel of the watch. The screen is slightly smaller than the Moto 360, but that hasn't been a problem. The steel mesh band is attractive. The watch feels rugged, with a protective metal lip around the screen. It's constructed of stainless steel ("Cold-Forged 316L"). The back of the watch is mostly metal, rather than plastic. The ability to make and receive phone calls from the watch (when the phone is nearby) is really cool.

In summary, all of the shortcomings of the (1st Gen) Moto 360 are addressed in the Huawei watch. I am a happy camper. This is an attractive, rugged, useful watch that I hope to keep for a long time! Highly recommended!

title: What a pleasant surprise!
text:
I wanted to write a review of this watch, but I see that a lot of people have beaten me to it. So I won't be long and windy but rather tell you that I bought the Apple Watch with the same sort of band and when it first came on the market. I liked the weight and feel of it and there was no question that it was a quality build. However, I returned it after two weeks.
I use my watch in the examination room when I am with patients. I would never be so rude as to allow my phone to ring while I am speaking with a patient. However, I sometimes get calls that can be important, such as from the emergency room or from the intensive care unit. I love the idea of this kind of watch, as it allows me to glance down and get some basic information about who's calling me without the patient ever being the wiser. Most of the calls that I get can wait until I am done seeing my patient so I do not answer them until I leave the room after the visit. With the emergency calls, it is a different story; I excuse myself, telling the patient I have an urgent call and that I will return in just a minute. I can step out in the hallway, return the call, solve the problem and return to the examination room, hardly missing a beat.
The other major purpose of this watch is telling time. That seems awfully obvious but there's a catch: I want to be able to tell time with one hand. The Apple Watch is supposed to wake up with your wrist movement, but I found event was often a bit more difficult than it should be. This watch is wonderful in that regard. When it is in its resting mode, the hands are still lighted, a little more dimly, and it is extremely easy to tell time without shaking your wrist or tapping the watch.
Battery life for me is always a good bit more than one day; when I get home and put it on the stand for charging and it typically has slightly more than 50% of its charge left. Is that a problem? Not to me. As I must plug in my cell phone every day, it doesn't seem any more taxing to simultaneously place my watch on its stand. In the morning, they are both ready to go and in a pinch, I think they would both give me two full days of performance on one charge. I don't really need more than that and if I did, I have a charger in my office and might put one in my car if I travel.
The watch itself is at least the same quality build as the Apple Watch. I think in some ways it is superior. If anyone doubts that, I understand that Huawei is a major corporation that it makes many, many products beyond this and they apparently know exactly what they're doing I would also remind the reader that your Apple Watch is likewise being made by a factory in China. The only downside I have found is the charger and its contacts on the back of the watch. It is a bit tricky to get them to make good contact and put the watch into its charging mode. It typically takes me three or four adjustments until the charging light is visible. It's certainly not a big deal and I believe that the current arrangement allows for its better waterproof designation, but I would be pleased with a simpler charging alignment. That small glitch notwithstanding, the watch is absolutely excellent and I am very glad I took the chance. By the way, I bought it here on Amazon and paid exactly 1/2 of what I paid for the Apple Watch!

title: Pretty product, poor quality, worse service. Don't buy.
text:
Update: 10 days since initial contact, I still don't have a return shipping label.

After barely 7 months of normal use, the screen has failed completely. Welcome to the world of Huawei Support (and I use the term loosely). Here's the deal: you call them, they send you an email where they ask for information you could have provided over the phone. I was instructed to sit tight and wait for a shipping label, only to learn a few days later I was supposed to have called them back after emailing because "they would have no way of knowing that they'd received an email". Um, check your inbox?

So I've lost a week in repair time and am waiting another day for a label (because "UPS can't generate one faster") - if there are any UPS folks monitoring Amazon reviews, you might want to know that Huawei is blaming you. Granted, they did give me expedited shipping. But, frankly, for a premium device, they should do expedited automatically. Worse yet, it is 10-14 BUSINESS days for repair. I'm told that it won't take this long, but reading other reviews, I'm wondering if I'll ever get my watch back. Or if it will last longer than 7 months.

What worries me the most is they keep asking if it has been exposed to water. Well, since the Huawei website says that it can be used normal, just don't swim or shower with it (which of course I didn't), then it is a given that it will be splashed when washing hands or damp in the rain. Even if they repair it, I'm left wondering if I can actually use it normally, as they describe.

Contrast this experience with another very well known brand of running watches and GPS devices that had a much less severe problem. After a couple troubleshooting steps, they asked for me to send the watch in so they could do diagnostics on it. "But its my running watch!" "No worries ma'am, we'll do an advanced exchange. We'll have a new watch to you within a couple days, then you send in your old one, and we're all set".

I paid about the same for both watches. They both experienced problems at about the same age. One company built my confidence. Another company lost my confidence completely. My next running watch? Same brand, no hesitation. My next dress watch or my next smart phone? Anything but a Huawei.

title: Best smart-watch I've owned
text: Best smart-watch I've owned.  The touch screen is so easy to use, bright and clear, and the design goes with both casual and professional outfits.  I get a compliment every time I wear it, and people ask what brand it is.  It connects the instant I get within range of my phone (which is quite a distance), and I have had no problem feeling the notification vibrations.  Despite the rather short battery life (you have to charge it every night, or else it's pretty much dead after 36 hours), I still give it 5 starts b/c the charging adapter is so easy to attach.

title: Even better than I expected!
text:
Absolutely love my watch! Definitely the best smartwatch out there, especially with the recent software update that allows me to use it as a bluetooth speaker.

It does almost everything that I want it to (on the software side, there is some room for improvement with Android Wear / Google Now) and, more importantly for a device like this, isn't bogged down with stuff I don't want. It doesn't have cellular radio--which is great because I don't need or want it. It doesn't have an ambient light sensor, which sounded like a "con" at first, but it turns out that it is totally unnecessary (I never have any trouble seeing my display). It doesn't have lots of bloatware apps or extra buttons or screens to tap through.

And the result is a beautiful, comfortable, fun watch that works well and does exactly what I need. It fits great, even though I'm a small guy, and is super light--much lighter than I expected. The metal "mesh" strap was definitely the right option.

The craftsmanship on the watch itself is excellent and I can attest that the extra money they put into the scratchproof sapphire glass is well worth it. Yes, the watch is a bit pricier than the competition, but in this case, you're absolutely getting what you pay for.

title: Absolutely love it.  It is extremely nice and exactly what I was hoping it would be
text:
Simply = I love it. Most important to me were three things -- appearance, effectively notify me of appointments/reminders and texts, quality of product. On these 3 is gets an A+. Details below but headlines are that this exceeds my expectation for looks, durability, battery life and ease of setup and integration into my daily life. Maybe I should have realized this but it is more of a convenient extension of my phone with some additional capability than it is a new device - and that is a really good thing and makes it very easy to use. I have only had for one week.

Background - I had not had a smart watch before so wasn't sure how much value I would really get out of it or how difficult it would be to set up. I currently have two "normal" watches - one for work and one for weekend/going out. I like to wear my watches all the time so only buy watches with Sapphire lens due to scratch resistance and water resistance so I don't have to worry about them. This watch seems to have replaced my work watch - which costs significantly more (but I bought years ago).

Rapid fire details - Received lots of complements in first week. At a party the other night I went outside (it was dark) and had a bunch of people complement me on the watch and had lots of questions. 2 had an Apple watch previously and both said that this was much, much nicer (neither use their Apple watch any more). Everyone's tastes and needs are a little different - for me this is great and exactly what I wanted. I charge in the morning while I shower and get coffee - battery has not been an issue at all. Also regarding notifications - I am still adjusting but I turned off work emails and some other apps - not the purpose for me - I use it for important updates like meeting reminders, texts and urgent weather/news. Band is great. The only thing I would want better at this point - an auto sleep tracking capability - haven't figured that out yet but the app i have requires me to "set" it and a nighttime mode that keeps the face in dim mode. These may exist I have not found them out yet.

IF your on the fence or wondering if it is nice enough -- stop what you're doing and buy it. I am thrilled with it - hope/expect you will be as well.

title: My favorite smart watch (for someone who has the Apple watch, Moto 360 2nd Gen, Fitbit Surge, Pebble Steel)
text:
I have a number of smartwatches, including the Pebble, Basis, Fitbit, Apple Watch, Motorola and now this. Have to say this is my favorite smartwatch.

Overall the watch looks like a high end watch, clean and elegant. The picture in Amazon makes it look small, but it is a perfect size for a 5'11" male.

I found a trick to make the battery last longer. I installed the following watch face https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.pujie.wristwear.pujieblack, enabled a discrete ambient (always on) watch face and disabled the accelerometer wake up. This gives me a charge that by the end of the day (10 p.m.) I have around a 45% charge (I take it off the cradle at 6 a.m.).

The only thing I don't like is the charger is not a NFC charger, but relies on four metal prongs. Generally the magnetic pad directs it to the right connection, but some times it misses. So I find myself having to verify that I see the lighting bolt charging sign.

Overall summary:

*** Pros ***
* Probably the most elegant looking smart watch I have seen
* Discrete
* Flexible when compared to the Apple watch
* Battery (see note on trick)
* Notification method is much better than the Apple watch

*** Cons ***
* Seemingly lack of availability of accessories (yet). For example, charging cradle, replacement charging adapter (now available through Google play store)
* Charging adapter could be better

title: Nice watch but big limitation on BlueTooth!
text:
I am using my Huawei watch with my iPhone 6 and am really enjoying it though the functionality is limited as compared to using it with an Android phone. All the functions work as expected with one BIG exception. When the watch is paired with my iPhone using BlueTooth, I am unable to use any other BT device at the same time. For example my 2010 BMW 335ix works great with my iPhone BT unless the Huawei watch is in the car at the same time. if it is the iPhone audio is garbled in the car speakers. To resolve I have to put the watch into Airplane Mode to disable BT. The same is true when I want to us my Plantronics BT headset with my iPhone, it garbles and finally disconnects from the phone while the watch is paired.

I contacted Huawei support concerning this problem and was told "As the iPhone is synced to the Watch, other Bluetooth devices may not be fully compatible to use at the same time. Please sync on one device at time to the iPhone and other mobile devices to ensure full usage." I find this response to be totally unacceptable since BT has been around a long time and I am able to pair many devices with my iPhone at the same time without having this limitation.

I don't know if this limitation is present with Android phones, but if you have an iPhone and want to use other BT devices at the same time while the watch is paired you will be very disappointed!

title: I like the watch very much
text:
I like the watch very much. The packaging was elegant, similar to opening an Apple product. The watch was easy to setup and worked exactly as I expected. I only gave the product 3 stars because Huawei support is absolutely useless. After having my watch for 2 days the button fell off. I read another review about this happening, but I hoped since my issue was so recent after purchase I wouldn't get a run around. I have a desk job and the primary reason I bought the watch is to wear at work to remind me to get up and walk around and to drink more water. On the second day of wearing my watch, I tried to press the button to bring up my apps, and notices the button was missing. I found the button on the ground near wear I had been standing. I tried to see if it was something I could just pop back in, but it doesn't work that way. When I first contacted Amazon, they told me the watch should be under warranty and asked me to reach out to the manufacturer. They also provided a link to the contact page for Huawei.

That's where my frustration began. First, when you try to send an email there are drop down menus with defined choices and no option for "other". Of course there are no options for the button falling off (or anything physical). I finally selected something else and typed up my issue. When I tried to complete the form, there's also a drop down for country/region. There is no listing in the drop down for USA or North America, or anything similar. Frustrated, I decided to call them instead. I wasn't on hold for long, and the customer support representative was friendly, but when I explain my problem he happily explained that they "do not cover anything physical". They provide some degree of technical support, but any physical damage (even if it's not actually damage), is not covered. He said I should go back to where I bought the watch. Fortunately, Amazon is great. When I called and explained my issue they were apologetic and offered to replace or refund my watch. For now, I elected to replace it.
