title: Running On iOS 9 with an iPhone 6s Plus
text:
Right off the bat, let me start by saying, I'm basing this review off of iOS. I know android wear is new to the iOS platform and that the using experience will only get better over time with of iOS.

I purchased this watch already owning an Apple Watch (and before that, the Pebble watch, off their Kickstarter campaign). I knew going in, that clearly, other then the Apple Watch, no other smartwatch will run as smoothly with iOS (snappy wise, functionality wise, and with notification display / interaction). I was willing to sacrifice function for a "smart watch that looks like a traditional mechanical watch" - until it was desired to be used as a smartwatch - even if, for my sake at least, meant only receiving push notifications from my iPhone (like my Pebble watch did).

With this watch "looking like a mechanical watch", I was really excited about the "always on display". Unfortunately, that however, is what also leads to my first biggest complaint. Even with the "always on watch face" (which all look BEAUTIFUL by the way), the chosen face only turns on for a few seconds, then (all of the) the faces simply "degrade" into a 1980's power saving mode display. Clearly, it's needed for battery life, but I was hoping for a "true" always on display that always looked like the marketing pictures. Also, with the "marketing watch faces", turning them on and being displayed was always unreliable and buggy, especially compared to the Apple Watch. This particular issue is with the watch itself and not with iOS. The "marketing watch display" seemed to flash on at random - with no clear learned arm movement or twist of my wrist inward towards my face. It was almost better to leave the face off - which defeated the whole purpose of why I wanted to love this watch. For no apparent reason, "ok Google" was displaying a lot, which also annoyed me.

Furthermore, although I can't speak for Android phones, the notifications with iOS were beyond annoyingly buggy. Some notifications wouldn't get pushed at all, while others would finally get pushed across minutes later, and some of the ones that did get pushed across were displayed at random in the "watch's notification screen" (with an upward finger swipe) with no order of time or sequence of when it came across. Others, that I knew had came across, I simply couldn't find anymore in the watch's notification screen. So, as far as smart watches go, it wasn't very smart - Especially, if ALL I WAS HOPING FOR from this watch using iOS, was at least push notifications and a clear way of seeing the ones that I had missed inside the watch's notification center. Also, nothing to do with iOS, but the watch's vibration of notifications were very mild. It was ok if was sitting, but out in public walking around, I'd miss a lot buzzes on my wrist, especially if my phone was only in vibrate mode.

Also, speaking of iOS, don't expect any customizations in the watch app. I knew that going in, but clearly, the system is more compatible for android wear devices. The only thing the watch app does is one thing - allow you to set your watch face (and even those, you can't customize the complications within the watch faces). Again, this isn't the watch's fault, but it's still an observation of "acceptance" of choosing to use this watch with an iPhone (in my case, the latest 6s Plus)

Minor for me, but for some, it may be a bigger deal, is the heart and health aspect of this watch. The heart rate monitor isn't nearly as reliable as the Apple Watch. I was getting readings all over the map (with the band properly fitted and with me sitting down / resting). My Apple Watch was always consistant. On those same lines, the Apple Watch automatically reads your heartbeat every 10 min. The Huawei only reads it when manually asked to. Even then, once it does, as of writing this, has no (Apple) Health App compatibility. So, your heart readings or measured steps won't be recorded or managed very efficiently (at least for an iOS user).

Other reviews cover this, but with no ambient light sensor - although that didn't bother me - I can definitely see that annoying a few people.

As far as looks go, this watch absolutely nails it! It's by far and away the most beautiful & aesthetic looking smartwatches to date! The craftsmanship, round unibody, and screen quality on this watch are all excellent!

If this watch updates it's iOS software and with future versions, improves the battery to a "truly always on display" option, I'd completely come back to this watch (even over the Apple Watch and even knowing all I was getting was push notifications). Of course, your platform (android) and desires functions from this watch my vary, but for me, I'm sending this watch back and sticking with my Apple Watch.

title: This is exactly what I was looking for!
text:
There were several things I needed to replace my HBS-730 (my cat chewed through the wire). I really didn't want to buy a new model, but I couldn't find any new HBS-730's. So I spent hours looking for something that has everything that one had... and I found it with this!

These are the features that were absolutely necessary:

> Independent volume.
This is the most important one. Most headsets these days control the phone volume directly, but Android has volume problems where the lowest volume is still too loud.
I really didn't want to have to use the "Sound Assistant" app or the "Precise Volume" app. With this, I can set the phone to a volume, and fine tune it with the headset volume. Perfect!

> Volume indicators
I like to hear beeps when changing the volume, and a double beep to let me know when I'm halfway. Otherwise I'm always wondering "What is my volume right now?" and "Did I just change it?" Sometimes I can't tell. Not a problem with this!

> Separate volume/media control
I don't like sharing the volume controls for next and previous. This has them separated. Wonderful!

> Standard (non-proprietary) charging cable
With all the cables around the house, it's good that I'm not limited to a special cable for this.

The HBS-810 has these four key functions. And it may be the only one that does. I'm so glad I got it!

A few things specific to the HBS-810:
> I wasn't sure if I'd like the retractable wires, but they're actually really nice. Better than dangling them. I don't have to worry about them catching on something.
> The wires are thin, though. Better not let the cats around this one ;)
> The volume uses a rocker control instead of buttons. This may be the only bad part on the product.
> I got a slightly different model than the one pictured - but it's better, so I'm not complaining.
> The box had water damage. I thought this was a returned product at first. I was happy to see that inside the box was fine. The unit was brand new.
> They kept the nice voice that says the battery level and power on/off in a non-annoying way.

Overall, this is everything the HSB-730 was and more. I'm very happy with this. Five stars for sure!!

title: LG gets it right with the HBS-810 Tone Ultra bluetooth headset
text:
Over the years I have purchased from Amazon several different models of the LG HBS headset. I have generally liked them all. However, some I have liked better than others. For instance, one model might have excellent incoming sound but be a little muffled on the outgoing sound, in the opinion of those I have spoken with using the headset. For other models, the outgoing sound has been very clear, while the inbound hasn't had quite enough volume or clarity for me.
The HBS-810 (Tone Ultra) sounds wonderful in both modes. The JBL speakers produce crystal clear sound and at sufficient volume for my taste. As to the retractable earpieces, I was hesitant at first, believing this to be a potential weakness, as every time you listen you have to pull them out by a seemingly very delicate line. And, since there are no magnets, if the spooling mechanism were to fail, you would be left with an unattractive dangling earpiece. An LG rep convinced me that they are very hardy. Besides, there is a one-year warranty, which would result in a replacement if the mechanism failed.
FYI I have tried and rejected the more expensive HBS-900 (INFINIM), which also has retractable earpieces. That model has great sound, but the neck piece is much stiffer than other models, which have more supple harnesses. Also, to retract the earpieces on that model, you must press a button. On the HBS-810, you retract by simply pulling the piece out a little farther outband letting it go. However, I realize that this feature is a matter of personal taste. The HBS-900 is also 50% more expensive. And to my ear, the JBL speakers on the HBS-810 deliver a crisper sound than the HBS-900's Harman Kardon speakers.
The bottom line: I think LG has finally nailed it with the HBS-810.

title: Best all around current gen headset with retractable ear buds!
text:
I bought these to replace my old and heavily used LG Tone 730's, which until the power switch on those starting failing, were excellent.

I did a lot of research and tried on a number of different models and brands that have come along since my 730's were bought and in the end, these are hands down the best option on the market for my wants and needs.

I knew I wanted retractable cords on my new headset, that was the one thing that was a regular annoyance with the old 730's and if anyone has owned any of the models like the 730's that had the external cords, you have all had or seen someone who's clips broke on them, making them a even bigger mess to manage.

I tried the cheaper though highly rated/reviewed Dylan's and just hated them. They didn't sound good to me, they were so thick and bulky and just seemed cheap in build quality.

I was about to by the LG Tone Infinim's but after trying them on from a co-worker that has them, I didn't like how the part that wraps around the back of your neck was made of a hard plastic and that they were not as flexible as my 730's.

Then I discovered the 810's and the checked all the boxes of what I wanted and was looking for and as an added bonus, they even cost less than the Infinim's!

The retraction on the 810's is accomplished by giving them a quick but gentle tug which pulls them back in. The Infinim's and the Dylan's both have a physical release button you hold which snaps them back in and I know multiple people that have been whipped in the face and even eye by them. Not fun! With the 810's requiring you to hold the ear buds to tug and get them retracted back in, this is a nonissue.

I can't recommend them enough! I have read some reviews stating the sound or bass was flat or not as good as some other model. This was a big fear of mine before ordering them and in a way, I can see why others have said this. It can at times sound flat or like the bass is missing but what I found was that 1: position in the ear makes a huge difference with this so play around with how they sit and rest in your ear. 2: Putting both ear buds in also has a big impact in the fullness and sound of what you're listening to vs having just one in.

One other key "feature" of the 810's and a "must have" for myself is that they can sit beneath the collar of my dress shirt without being obvious. This lets me keep them on me all day at work without anyone even noticing I have them.

title: I found the bass!  Now great music sound.
text:
It's about the earbud covers! Replace the ones that come with this headset. I bought mine at the local Dollar Store for, uh, a dollar! The bass is now heavy (thumping and bouncing) and the overall sound clarity for music is dramatically better.

The trick is that the earbud covers have to be more pliable to fit your ear better and the edge of the cover opening near your ear has to be flush with the earbud screen. The covers that originally come with this set are harder and recessed. Consequently, the sound doesn't make it completely to your ear cavity. (Simply stated, the sound, especially the full bass is muffled or disappears altogether.).

I can't take credit for this revelation. I saw a review on YouTube and the reviewer mentioned the strategy of the Dollar Store upgrade. So, whatever you paid for this headset, pay $1 more for new earbud covers and you will dramatically improve your music and sound experience with this set.

4 stars instead of 5 because I had to pay for gas for my car to go to the Dollar Store! :)

text: So I owned the 730s for a few years. I really liked them and used them on a near daily basis for work. Well I finally killed them, ripped the right ear bud off. Anyway, I researched these against the 950's and 1100's. I was willing to spare no expense. I read a review were the ultras were preferred over the other two because the mic was better. I can't speak for the upper level ones, but the mic on the ultras does work well. (That seemed to be a common complaint about the 9 and 1100 series.) The main complaint I read about the ultras was a decrease in audio performance from the 730's. I would disagree with this assessment (even though I agreed at first.) The ultras have less base out of the box and so the sound seems less full. However, the sound is more precise and not as muddled. Using the power amp app I added a bit of base and quickly had no complaints. Streaming I just downloaded and equalizer app and use it to add in a touch of base. Once I did this I was pleased with the overall performance. Instead of being treble and base the ultras tend to have a more complete sound than the 730's. I actually prefer it. I don't know how the pull out earbuds will hold up. Honestly the little tabs on the 730's didn't work much after the first six months anyway. If they break, I hope they just stop retracting so they can still be used. We will see. So far I like them well and I have no complaints with the call quality.

text:
***UPDATE March 2016***
Well I've somehow already broken this one, despite being super careful all of the time. Always seems to be the left earbud that goes out (same as my HBS 700). It's gotten much worse. I have to hold the mic up to my mouth or no one can understand me. The volume is frequently turned all the way up so I can hear the other caller. Music is still okay, but it's only coming out of one side, so what's the point?

I miss my HBS700.

***Original Review***
Got this to replace my HBS700 when one of the wires/earbuds stopped passing sound, so everything is a comparison to that. I loved that headset and wore and used it daily for at least 3 years. I've had this one a few months, and it's performed pretty well.

The sound on the HBS810 is good (but not fantastic) for listening to music, and I like the bass boost settings. I find the sound for voice calls is a bit muffled (I wonder if that's from my bass boost setting, though). The microphone is not as clear as my HBS700, because I frequently have trouble with Siri and also during calls.

Also, it's weird that they moved the power switch; I preferred it on the left. The slider buttons are not as convenience as the regular buttons were, and I hit them accidentally, often. However the retractable earbuds, despite my concern about pulling on the wires, are fantastic and super convenient. No more catching the earbud and wire in my hair (which is how I broke my 700...)!

title: Poor design contributes to Bluetooth problems
text:
After reading the reviews of the current HBS-900 and HBS-910 Tone Infinim headsets, I weighed the pros and cons in comparison to the HBS-800 and HBS-810 and decided for the money and the negatives of the 900 series to purchase the HBS-810 product. I wasn't sure at the time what the cause was, but the replacement had the same problem, but not as bad. Now I know that I have to use my hand to spread the collar away from my neck when I lose the Bluetooth connection. I sometimes wear the collar hanging down my chest where it cannot be blocked by my neck when I move. This is annoying but it guarantees me a steady connection. This is especially critical when using a phone connection, which unlike a music connection, the headset hangs up the call that cannot be restored.

I purchased the headset to replace an older LG HBS-730, which I've used for about three years with no problems (no stiff collars on the early models). From what I read, successive new models appear to have design issues that contribute to Bluetooth unreliability.

title: Just about perfect, all that I could ask for in a stereo Bluetooth headset. LG delivers...!!!
text: The online and retail market for Bluetooth stereo headsets is thick and dense with many to choose from, while trial and error for me hasn't yet resulted in the perfect stereo headset yet.  I've had 5 in the past 2 years.  But LG delivers a standout stereo headset worth both my time and money, more importantly my growing admiration for LG.  I first picked the Tone Infinim by Harmon Kardon thinking why not buy the best in the line. While they are a worthy headset, although durable, the size and rigidness of the design eventually became a negative in my opinion, making it impractical to where during a work day, although they worked decent during workouts -- but because of the larger size, they became noticeably wearing on me.  A few days later, fast forward with the next incarnate, Tone Ultra released, combining the best of all of the Infinim and older popular versions.  The Tone Ultra HBS-810 has great music sound with JBL performance, and better than adequate phone voice quality, with exceptional battery life, and best of all, it's capable of pairing 2 devices simultaneously and retractable earbuds.  In addition, the flexible design of the neck collar is light enough to feel effortless, drastically different than the Infinim.  The Ultra is a clear choice for me.  It's a smaller more efficient flexible design that allows me to take them off and curl them up in my pant pocket.  I pair it up with my Note 4 and LG G3 simultaneously.  Excellent wire management.  Might I add I also downloaded the free LG Tone app, which adds a few more bells and whistles to this already impressive headset.  I love these headsets.  While I've had these for just a week, I've grown to wear them all day, and with the battery life of at least a full day or more, I find myself effortlessly using them all day.  They do not disappoint, and I have yet to find a flaw.  Time testing follow up soon.

title: Be VERY Wary
text:
I originally purchased this headset off of Amazon in Sept., 2016 after reading reviews of multiple headsets-this one seemed a good bet. I liked that the wires are retractable and would be less likely to tangle. I LOVED these headphones and the buttons all worked well, as did the retraction. Sound quality was good for me (I listen mostly to audio books and podcasts and, as long as I can turn up the volume loud enough to hear over passing cars as I walk and make out the voices, I'm fine).

Unfortunately, the headset stopped pairing with devices after 9 months (it would indicate that it was paired and I could use the headset's buttons to stop and start the recording, but no sound came through. This occurred when trying to pair with my Ipad and my Driod phone). LG's online chat customer service asked me a few questions to understand the issues, then asked the standard warranty questions- Had I dropped it? Spilled anything on it, etc. After determining it was eligible for repair under the warranty, they issued me a return label and I shipped it for free (to me) for repair. Several weeks later, I'd received the "repair"-a refurbished upgraded device. I pulled out one earpiece to test it and the buttons and sound worked fine, but the earpiece would not retract (upon multiple attempts). Sigh. I contacted customer service again and went through the whole story with them. Same response-it was still under the original warranty (I have until Sept. 2017) and I could now return the replacement for repair. No pre-paid label this time.

End-of-story-I have now paid an additional $15 to ship back the broken replacement for my 9 month old broken LG HBS-810. I have 6 weeks left on the original warranty and will likely not get the replacement's replacement until late August. If it doesn't work or fails after a few weeks, I'm out some pretty pennies, thrice bitten, and looking for a new company's product.

A note to LG: 1) Focus a bit more on quality, not quantity. 2) Replace broken items under warranty with NEW products (or do a better job refurbishing the old ones). 3) Give each replacement product its own 1 year warranty. If you don't it means you clearly don't have faith in your own products-so why should consumers?

8-16-2017 Update
LG sent the second replacement via FedEx, but it got lost for 2 weeks because LG hadn't put the full suite # on the package.
Another note to LG: If your products require so many replacements, lost packages will happen more frequently. Just make a better product, please.

title: Has so much potential but comes short
text:
I owned the HBS-730 for 3 years and wore it almost everyday. I loved it for the following reasons:

1) Relatively slim/lightweight and doesn't stand out so much.
2) Excellent battery life.
3) Great sound quality.

I thought it was time for me upgrade since I had it for over three years. I also thought that the new models will be much better since they are later models right? Well below is how I feel about the new HBS-810.

What's great:
1) HSB-810 is curved so that it sits more naturally on your neck. Also, this design makes the headset more stable.
2) Earpiece cable is now retractable so no more fighting with tangled wire.
3) They god rid of the blue blinking light on top so people stop asking me what is the blue light blinking on your neck?
4) Phone software is nice. You can customize your headset features pretty easily and I like the fact that it reads me texts I receive on my phone.

What's not so good:
1) Volume control on the side feels awkward to control as opposed to being on the top previously.
2) Power button is much harder to power on and off. Way too stiff to power it on and off (Why not keep the previous design?)
3) Now here is the real disappointment for me which really baffles me.

WHY IS THE SOUND QUALITY WORSE THAN THE PREVIOUS MODEL? BASS IS PRETTY MUCH NONEXISTENT ON THIS MODEL?
REALLY? YOU THOUGHT PEOPLE WILL LIKE THE FACT THAT YOU PAY MORE FOR LESS? I AM LOYAL TO YOUR BRAND. PLEASE FIX THIS ASAP! I GET FRUSTRATED WHENEVER I LISTEN TO MUSIC WITH THIS.

YOUR OTHER INFINIM MODELS ARE WAY TOO BULKY TO WEAR AROUND MY NECK. I WOULD HAVE ATLEATS GIVEN IT 4 STARS IF IT WASN'T FOR THIS. VERY DISSAPOINTED BUT I WILL STILL USE IT BECAUSE I DON'T FIND ANYTHING BETTER OUT THERE YET.

Then found a tip to carefully remove the screens, and pull out the big cylinders of foam put of ear earbud. Then replace the screens and the rubber part.

I LOVE the new volume and track skip and pause set up. I wear these under lots of conditions, including on my motorcycle - so can easily skip a track w/o fumbling around.
And yes, they are noise canceling. I can't hear for crap even off, when they are in. (I can hear loud noises like horns, sirens, my bike, but not voices or my dogs etc).
Hope the taking the foam out tip helps those with issues with it!

Now only if someone made earbuds that are wax proof, I have to clean the screens weekly, but that's a 'me' problem with all earbuds

the seal well too.. it muffles outside sounds as well as traditional ear plugs..

text:
I have gone through 3 other brands before trying these out. I had the HBS 750 and 730 previously, and was happy with them (but you can't really use them for working out - sweat will kill them) until they died - so I thought I would try another brand.

I tried the Samsung Level U Pro - those sounded terrible on computers, but amazing on the S8.

The BackBeats Pro 2 were a bit buggy for the price and the Jabra Halo were just too choppy.

These LGs are fantastic! No issues with choppy connections and the bass is pretty solid. I played with the EQ on my phone and made sure the Bass Enhancement mode was turned on with the headphones, and I am really pleased. You don't get the range that the Backbeat Pro offers, but as long as you aren't expecting to be too far away, you should be fine.

I'm sure the $200-$300 bluetooth headphones are better, but in my experience, you are getting great quality for the money.

UPDATE : In the couple of months since I received these, I've found that the range is terrible. I get 10 feet from my phone and it drops out or disconnects. Also, when I turn my head left or right it cuts out. I haven't used these for exercise, so it isn't a sweat issue. I purchased these on prime now, so I don't know if I can exchange them.

Otherwise, the sound is still great.

title: Left ear buds keep dying
text:
I have owned two sets of the HBS 810's, and both of them have failed within 3-6 months. LG honored the repairs, but the units failed again within 5 months of the repair. Overall the sound quality is good. The mic picks up great, but can sometimes pick up too much ambient or background noise/talking. The unit is comfortable, and the retractable ear buds are a nice way to keep the ear buds out of the way when not in use.
However, It is hard to go above 3 stars when each headset failed twice for a total of four failures. 3 of the 4 failures were the left ear bud dying. The last failure was loss of adequate volume from the speakers. The 4th and final failure occurred 368 days after my warranty, but LG did replace the unit

Overall the headsets worked great while they were working, but I do not think a device that lasts around 5-6 months is worth ~100. Maybe about half that price would be a more acceptable price point.

title: Good for days of use
text:
I bought this headset to replace my lost Bluetooth mono earpiece as I needed something larger and bulkier that would be harder to put in a pocket and end up in the wash. It turns out this is s pretty nice choice and more!

To my ear the sound was tinny when I first used them. Once I figured out how to apply the built-in equalizer settings, the sound improved, though not quite to the level I had hoped. Not enough bass response to make my music roar with its usual intensity which is my reason for less than 5 stars.
The remaining features still make this a great choice and a recommended product:
The slim profile means that I can wear this to work actually concealed under my shirt collar. (I actually flip my collar up, out it on over my shirt and roll the collar down over it almost completely concealing the headset.)
The retractable earpieces make it simple to extract them from under my collar for one ear listening and hands-free phonecalls while driving, and both ears for my daily walks and casual listening. Then, when no longer needed, a light tug and release, all disappears out of view. Unlike other models that just have the magnetic holders but leave a loop of wire dangling, these retract and disappear completely.
If you make the effort to learn the controls, all can be done either through the fabric of my collar or by slipping a finger to or thumb underneath to make an adjustment.
Lastly, the battery life is phenomenal! I charge this up and leave it on for days! Taking a dozen or so calls and listening privately to music and video. I charge this maybe twice a week, once midweek and once on the weekend. With heavier use you may need to charge it every couple of days but this headset really suits me and I recommend it for good general Bluetooth use.
If you're an audiophile this will not come close, but then, you're also not listening to your music from mp3's or streaming from your phone either. Wired headsets still produce the best sound, in my opinion, but if you can compromise a little on audio quality, the remaining features make this an excellent choice!

title: Great audio (with proper earbuds) and exceptional functionality
text:
To begin with, I'm somewhat of an audiophile… actually… a little more than somewhat… OK… Audiophile is actually a mild term for my condition. Audio obsessive compulsive probably comes closer. But at the same time, I hate dangly wires. For a long time, I suffered with inadequate audio, to get freedom or suffered with dangly wires to get adequate audio. Life was tough, in those days. But today, the LG HBS-810 seems to have reached a new threshold in Bluetooth audio.

ATTENTION: Spend the extra $20 or so on the Comply Isolation Earbuds. The Comply website says that the TX-400 earbuds fits the HBS-810. But I found that the larger TX-500 earbuds that I use on my old Bluebuds, seems to work very well. Get the largest ones that will fit in your ear. This is critical to making the HBS-810 reach it's maximum potential.

I was an early purchaser of LG stereo headsets. My first LG was an HBS-700. The sound was mediocre, at best. But the convenience and Bluetooth connectivity and functionality was excellent. Everything worked exactly as it intended and designed. It was a compromise, for Bluetooth convenience. Then, after I read several very good reviews about the Jaybird BlueBuds X headset, I upgraded to it and was extremely pleased for close to a year. It was the best Bluetooth audio I had ever heard (but only after installing Comply isolation earbuds). But just before it ran out of warranty, I had trouble with one of the buttons, so I sent it in for repair. They replaced it and I must commend Jaybird Customer Service. I wouldn't be exaggerating to say that it was on a par with Apple Tech Support. Unfortunately, the replacement headset has several of the connectivity problems that I read about in a few of the reviews - connectivity issues that my original Bluebuds headset didn't have. The sound is still awesome. But the connectivity issues are really bothering me. This is where the HBS-810 comes in.

After tons of research, I decided to return to LG. It came down to either the 900 or the 810. Ultimately, the 810 won out, over the 900, because of the rigid style of the 900. Both had plenty of great reviews on their audio and I would have been able to live with the rigid style of the 900, had it been all that was available. Fortunately, the 810 came along and I didn't have to compromise. If anything, I think that the 810 probably may have a few more positive audio reviews than the 900. Anyway, I have not had this headset for more than a few hours. But I'm already impressed.

Let's get aesthetics out of the way. The buttons and microphone are all in the right places. In fact, the mic is positioned better than in the old 700. I like the curved design better than the old models. The rocker buttons took a few minutes to get used to, but I think they'll be fine.

Voice prompts are a nice upgrade from the 700, but I'm used to the voice prompts on the Bluebuds, so I expected it. There are, however, more voice prompts than on the Bluebuds. It's also nice to have the battery level displayed on the iPhone, as on the Bluebuds. I suppose that some people might like the three equalizer settings. The default is bass-boost and that seems to be fine. I may set it to normal, now that I have the Comply earbuds installed, just to see what it is like. Without the Comply earbuds, the bass boost setting would be an absolute necessity.

Now for the audio. I've found that the best sound is achieved with the equalizer turned OFF on my iPhone 6+, when using the Comply earbuds. I have several test tracks that I have found many headsets have trouble reproducing, in full. The HBS-810 did exceptionally well on all of them. Sure, a high end wired headset would do better. But I would rate the HBS-810 on a par with the Bluebuds X headset and that's excellent. The highs are crisp and clear and with the Comply earbuds, the bass rumbles. May I suggest that a good tune to test bass is Vince Guaraldi's "Cast Your Fate to the Wind". It opens with an arco (bowed) double bass and moves to a pizzicato (plucked) double bass. It also includes a very clear piano and brushed drums. This gives a very wide range of audio to test. Another good test track is Trans-Siberian Orchestra's, "Wizards in Winter". For vocals, try Jeff Wayne's "War of the Worlds", with Richard Burton, as the narrator. Burton's voice comes through on the 810, as though he is in your head.

If you have to have absolutely perfect audio, then you'll have to deal with wires. But the LG HBS-810 is about as close as you can get, without wires. Between the HBS and the Bluebuds X, I would have to give the Bluebuds a very slight edge on audio, although their volume is somewhat lower than the HBS-810 for the same track. OTOH, I have NEVER had connectivity issues with an LG headset, whereas, I has plenty of connectivity issues with the second Bluebuds X that I had and those issues mirrored some of the reviews. This leads me to believe that the Jaybird quality control may not be as good as the LG quality control. I have to give the HBS-810 a decided edge on controls and functionality. I had missed the vibration on ring, when using the Bluebuds. It's nice to have that functionality back. I'll have to wait to report on dependability, till I have had this set for a few months. But the old 700 was an exceptional product, as far as dependability is concerned. The 700 just had lousy audio. All in all, I think that the LG HBS-810 is well designed, well built and has audio that pushes the limits of Bluetooth.

Curved collar fits flush to my scapula unlike straight bar u shapes. Connect range is about 15 feet. While out of range it continuously try's to reconnect every minute. Each time it attempts to reconnect it vibrates which was annoying at first. Sound quality is excellent, I can here base notes that are completely in audible on other cheap ($50 & under) headsets. I have babied the hell out of these as a office headset and cannot speak to durability of sweat resistance. My one complaint is that the cord to each earbud coils and holds tension while completely extend. This leads to a feeling of tension between the earbud and the collar base EVEN when there is extra slack. The cords are long enough to reach any head articulation without lifting the collar base.

Update, 2 Stars 6/2018
After 14 months the left speaker stopped working. In it's 14 month life the headset never saw any abuse or got wet, it basically never left the office. The factory warranty is only for 12 months so I am out of luck. I could pay to have the headset refurbished but I will just take my chances with another brand. It's possible that this is a fluke and most of these model headsets will last much longer but I am not willing to spend another $100 to find out. This is really upsetting. I purchased this headset because it is what I considered to be expensive. After having several $20-$30 models only last about 6 months I decided to just spend the extra money to get a headset that would last. text: I love this headset.  Not for phone calls outdoor - in this situation there is no noise cancelling so they suck.  After trying these, I bought a Plantronics Voyager headset for phone calls.  Indoors, in quiet environments, they are fine for phone calls.  However, these are fabulous for listening to music which is the real reason I purchased them.  If I am listening to music outdoors and someone calls, I'll answer with these, ask the person to hold and switch to the Plantronics.  As said above, the music quality is fabulous, with a twist (which makes perfect sense when you think about it).  Some reviewers have commented about the sound quality being weak, muted, outside noise being heard, etc..  I had this happen as well until I realized, if I really push the ear buds into my ears so they make a complete seal inside the ear canal, then all those problems went away and the sound was fantastic.  As I said, when you think about it, it makes sense.  A complete seal in the ear canal will block out the outside sounds, it moves the speaker closer to you ear drum which increases the sound volume (eliminating the weak and/or muted sound quality), all which results in a fantastic musical experience.

title: A great set of headphones at a reasonable price. Preferred to the Infinims
text: The LG Tone Ultra 810 is a great set of headphones. I prefer these to the more expensive infinims because they have the flexible neck like earlier models, but still have the retractable cords and sound quality of their more expensive version. The battery life is amazing. I have been using them on the factory charge for about 2 weeks (2-3 hours a day, 3 days a week) and the battery is still on medium! For those who have reviewed them as having poor sound quality, I would say that it's all about finding the right size ear bud for them. The ones that were shipped on the set were WAY to big and didn't get a good seal. Therefore the bass was very weak and the volume was low. The 2 pairs of gels included (medium and large but no small) are very thick and rigid because of an extra layer of foam inside, most likely to improve noise cancellation, but can easily be replaced with any other gels you have lying around. I put some from some old samsung buds in there that I knew were a good fit for me, and the sound quality coming from them now is great! Very clear sound, good volume and decent bass. Like some others have commented, the range on them is not as great as I would like it to be, cutting out at around 20-25 ft. But since my phone is almost always in my pocket or purse, this wasn't really an issue for me. Overall, I would definitely recommend these over the infinims and previous models as they have the best of both worlds.

title: An honest review - The tone infinim contender
text:
First off this is my equipment:
Audio Technica IM70 w/comply foam IEM, Powerbeats 2, Tone pro HBS-760, Tone Infinim, Jaybird X2
Look: These to me look far greater then any other LG Tone headset on the market. I love the minimalistic profile of the buttons and the black is very stealth. The Infinim is nice too but is also very thick, bulky, and glossy. I love the fact that these are retractable! My daughter kept pulling on my Tone pro wires and I was afraid they would break so I upgraded to this.
Sound: The sound is VERY good. Looks like LG put some thought in here. The bass is very strong and rivals some higher end headsets. If my IM70 IEM's were a 10, the Infinim's are about a 7, the Jaybird's are a 6, and these are a 7 as well. The treble isn't as clear as my Infinim's but much better then the HBS-760. The bass is much better then any other LG headset that I have owned.
Fit: This is a huge win. 10/10. Wraps around my neck with ease and can easily be tucked away. The Infinim is like a dog collar and is very thick and non flexible. This is just like the other tone's where it is light and can hug your neck.
Connectivity: Same as all my other headsets. Go past 20 feet or so and it drops. No disconnects noted.
How I use them: These are my secondary office headset. I would put them along the lines of how I use my Infinim. I am always on conference calls so having a headset I can depend on is crucial. I seem to be using these more then my Infinim lately just because they are so light. It may also be because its my newest headset lol.
Accessories: The eartips I rate a 6/10. They are nowhere near as comfortable as the LG Tone infinim ones. They seem to be designed differently as well which may be for the noise isolation. The Infinim tips are more comfortable to me and you get 3 instead of 2.
Gripes: The retractable button on the Infinim is nice but not really necessary. However it retracted much faster than these do. I also wish they would have included another size of ear tip. I feel like the "large" isn't fitting as snugly as I would like. Other then that, this is a solid headset.
Final thoughts: The depreciation on this headset is ridiculous. I can't believe it costs $100 new and sells for $35 used. Seems like Best Buy is offloading a lot of these store returns on the 3rd party marketplace sites. I personally got mine for $35 used and now that I have tested it, I would have paid $75-$125 given all the features you get. Heck, the Infinim was $150 earlier this year! This is a solid buy and really takes the best of all of the LG headsets - Weight/comfort/flexibility of the pro, retractable buds of the Infinim, and sound of the Infinim.

title: Solid bluetooth headset
text:
This is a bluetooth headset with very good incoming and outgoing audio quality but some weird design choices, hence the 4 stars. I use these to listen to a lot of different media: metal, rap, house, classical, podcasts, youtube videos. The speakers in this headset handle all of these without any kind of adjustments on my part. The sound is clear, powerful, and distinct even at high volumes which is a big deal for me. It pairs easily with my Galaxy S5, my iPhone 6 and my personal and work PC.

Now for the weird parts. I'm not a huge fan of the retractable ear pieces because they do not always fully retract. It's not a huge deal but annoying. Also, I think the spring-loaded sliders for volume and track change are not as easy to use as just plain old buttons. I use this a lot when I work out and when it's drenched in sweat, the sliders aren't easy to use.

All in all I think this is a solid headset in terms of audio quality, and mediocre in terms of the interface.

title: Exceeded expectations
text: I was very skeptical of these earphones at the start. As soon as I put them in, I noticed absolutely no bass response and they just sounded tinny. I decided to try them for the remainder of the workday; if I still didn't like them, I was going to return them after work. Surprisingly, the more I used them, the better they sounded. It turns out the the problem was the foam eartips, rather than the earphones themselves. Once I broke them in by wearing them for a few hours, they started sounding great. People who expect the oversaturated bass of Beats will probably be disappointed, but the overall acoustic response is actually quite decent. If you are worried about the reported lack of bass, be aware that these earphones come with large eartips already installed, and they might be too big for your ear canal. Try the smaller tips that come in the box, or just wear the large tips for a while and break them in (they should go further back in your ear canal, rather than just resting in your ear). Sound quality wise, these are great for the money. Probably the best sound of any of the current TrueTone series (yes, they are better than the more expensive ones). These earphones are not audiophile quality, by any means, but they are some of the best Bluetooth earphones in this price range and well worth the cost. The 10-13 hour continuous use battery life is also really nice. They are quite comfortable to wear and are very lightweight. The built in microphone is the biggest disappointment, as it seems to pick up a lot of ambient noise. Most callers have asked me if I have them on speakerphone. Overall, with a few quirks aside, these earphones are an excellent value at this price range, and definitely worth a buy.

text:
I just returned my LG HBS 810 to Sam's Club and am on Amazon shopping for a replacement now. I don't recommend this one for a few reasons:

1. The left earbud stopped working after about 6 months of daily use, including running. This slowly came on. At times I could hold the line from the neck base to the earbud a certain way and it would work, but now that's stopped completely. It seems to have to do with the line itself; I suspect it's due to the "retractability". That's a nice feature but I believe it's also the source of the failure.

2. Sound quality was very tinny. Definitely not a full range of sound. When I would turn up the volume on a good song I just couldn't get to a level that was both pleasant and satisfying.

There are a couple of pros, and if you're okay with this lasting 6 months you might like that it connected very quickly (to my Galaxy Note 5 and my ASUS Android tablet). I also liked that there were built in voice indicators when it powered on: "Power on; battery medium; connected".

But for 70 bucks at Sam's, I was looking for something that would last a couple years.

text:
So I ordered this back in February. It wasn't the cheapest headphones, but it looked to work for what I wanted. I work in a shop with other technicians, so listening to my own music without outside noise is a must. This model fit the need greatly. It took awhile to get used to the ear bud tips, but after awhile it was fine. Unfortunately, last week the audio stopped working in the right ear bud. I am waiting for LG to respond as to what they will do as I haven't even had this 2 months. Depending on their response, I will add stars if it is a positive outcome.

**** UPDATED 12/10/2016 *** I forgot to update this after hearing back from Customer Service. They did in fact take care of fixing the problem I encountered. I wasn't really happy with the shipping service they chose as they would not deliver without a signature and ultimately forced me to drive 30 to 45 minutes away in order to pick up my package. Aside from that, I have not had really any issues with the sound failing since receiving it. The only issue remaining I would say is that even though I keep my ears pretty clean, wax and dirt still seem to get into the ear buds. I had to take it apart a few times to keep cleaning it out and after a couple times, the screen no longer stayed put. So I am using it without. I see this as a design flaw. They should be easily cleanable. But maybe that's just a petty complaint. Still a great sounding set. Worth buying.

**** UPDATE 11/2/2018 **** So, I've been dealing with lower sound volume out of the right ear for awhile. So I just switched to the left, since we are only allowed to use 1 ear bud at work (For safety reasons, apparently). Now the sound has started lowering in the left one as well. This is on the warranty "replacement". I suspect this was not a NEW unit when sent to me. For the money spent on these, I expected them to last longer. I wear them daily at work, not out in the elements. So they don't get wet or tossed around. I don't think I would buy these again unless they were lower in price. I have a suspicion it has something to do with the constant pulling of the cables to pull out of the headset in order to use. I had my doubts in the beginning and they sure seem to be confirmed.

title: Everything is better except the sound.
text: I was a huge fan and longtime owner of the HBS 730 headset. I was especially happy with the sound quality. However I was not a fan of the cable management; especially the little clips that were so easy to lose.  So when my old 730s finally bit the dust I was happy to see LG had created Tones with retractable earbuds.  The 810s are a huge improvement in function & design. It's great to not have to worry about the cables dangling and getting caught in a piece of clothing like the zipper of a jacket.  The volume control works directly with my iPhone 6s volume (the 730s had their own volume setting and trying to find a balance between the headset volume and the phone volume was occasionally annoying).  The slightly recessed buttons and the stiffer "jog" controls on the sides are far less likely to be accidentally activated versus the controls that we're on for 730.  Just like the previous model the battery life is excellent, and as many reviewer's have mentioned over the years the Tones are so light and comfortable it's easy to forget you're wearing them around your neck.  The sound quality on the 810s is very good for spoken word like audiobooks and podcasts, as well as for phone calls. However the sound quality for music is extremely disappointing.  The "bass boost" mode has about the equivalent fidelity of the EarPods that come with the iPhone. Actually, I think the EarPods have better low frequency response than this headset does. The "normal" mode is so flat and tinny  it's easy to mistake it for the trouble boost mode.  This came as a great surprise to me as the 730 audio quality was very good for music in both bass boost and normal mode.  But because I loved the improved functionality of this model I decided to stick with it and try to find better methods of playing what I was listening to.  I have tried multiple equalizer applications as well as different podcast applications (I work in the music entertainment business and I use music podcasts to stay current).  I found some vwru good apps,  but pretty much all of them involved some kind of trade off in using them over the apps I've been using for years with my order 730s.  Tonight I got so frustrated with the poor sound quality of a Music podcast that I hopped on the Amazon to see if I can still return them. Unfortunately  it's too late. Bottom line: if you intend to listen to music you need to think twice before purchasing this model. If you do purchase it, I recommend immediately listening to the music that you are going to be using these to listen to so as to make sure that the sound quality is good enough for you  before the window to return them closes on you as it did on me.

title: ~2 weeks in. So far so good.
text:
These are my step into the BT market. Went with LG largely because I have a G3 and the retractable buds were a plus.

I'm finding these pretty solid all around. Short of 5 stars because I can't attest to longevity, They've been useful at work and for cycling — one bud in, solely to answer calls as it's a million times better than pulling out the phone altogether. If I run the actual headset inside my jersey collar, people can still hear me loud and clear. The 810 has been going strong, but then again I generally don't sweat much up top.

Audio is surprisingly good, even though I shouldn't have a low bar for headphones that cost this much period. I just say this relative to the idea that I see these more intended for communication purposes. Like others said, bass and noise cancellation are heavily dependent on bud size and your years. The original ones felt pretty big to start but mine kinda broke in.

I personally think the complaints about controls are very petty/subjective. It's true that some people are so accustomed to other Tone configurations (and so LG should establish consistency), but getting accustomed to these isn't a big deal.

I share the concern over the thin wires, which goes back to me highlighting the fact it's only been two weeks and coming short a star. But so far there have been no snags. Retraction has been consistently smooth.

Battery took me 12 days before I needed a recharge. Calls, occasional music, turning off the headset at night. Seems about right to spec..

Overall I feel BT headsets are going to be a norm because of how functional smartphones are as visual tools. I can't go back to wires at all, and these are always around my neck for the day so I can say I find LG really nailed the shape and weight. The Tone 810's were a solid introduction for me. To upgrade to the 900's, I'd be looking for a beefier wire setup, much more premium finish and sound.

title: Out of the box the HBS-810 paired with the LG G3 and worked great with the LG Tone & Talk app
text:
I purchased the HBS-810 primarily to use for Skype/Lync calls for work, secondarily for my LG G3 and Samsung S4 cell phones. Out of the box the HBS-810 paired with the LG G3 and worked great with the LG Tone & Talk app. Ditto with the Samsung S4. I live in a 1400 sqft townhome and I'm able to leave my phone on the coffee table and walk to just about any part of the house and keep a connection, including upstairs.
It took me about a month to get the HBS-810 to work with my laptop (Lenovo x230, Windows 8.1 (64-bit), Bluetooth 4.0). It would pair but the headset wouldn't show up on the list of playback devices. I worked with my IT department at the high tech company where I work and verified all my drivers were up to date. They were baffled as well why it wouldn't work on the laptop.
LG Chat and Phone support were useless. I utilized chat and phone 3x. 1x on chat the tech just forwarded me a plethora of google links to help with my problem, all of which I'd already seen, none of which worked. 2x on chat the tech told me the HBS-810 doesn't work with a laptop, only Android and iOS phones, and I need to call the laptop vendor to "have the sound transfer activated." Finally when I called the LG 1-800 number for support I was told I needed to get a separate USB Bluetooth adapter to get the headset to work.
None of these options were correct, and after that experience of poorly trained technical support I would probably not by another LG product (hence the 3 stars). I finally got the headset to work on my laptop after downloading a driver from www.broadcom.com/support/bluetooth/update.php.
The battery life is good. If I'm not on a phone call I'm listening to music. I use the headset continuously all day and still go home with some battery left. It cuts out maybe 3x a day while playing music and handles the conference calls okay. I haven't lost a connection so far. Retractable ear buds are a plus.
In summary I'm satisfied with the functionality of the HBS-810 after I was able to get it to work with my laptop. I'd terribly disappointed in LG technical support. I'll update after a few months of use.

title: Beware of Amazon Warehouse Deals
text:
The headsets being reviewed were purchased through "Amazon Warehouse Deals" and be aware that even though it is Amazon, the purchase policies are different.

The first one received there was almost no audio from the right earpiece. Frustrating, but seeing that it was "refurbished" I thought I'd exchange it for another. That's where I learned that if it is a "Warehouse Deal" they do not do exchanges, only returns. After processing my return, I ordered a second one. When I received it, I had the same problem, but this time with the left earpiece. Upon closer examination, I discovered that the earpiece mesh was filled with what I could only imagine is earwax. I'm not sure what processes Amazon uses before slapping on an "inspected" sticker, but it is not very thorough.

I did test the sound with the right earpiece to see if I even wanted to go through the hurdles of buying ANOTHER one and returning this one, but the sound was nowhere near the quality I expected from JBL Signature Sound. It was tinny and had almost no bass to it. I made a test call and was told that it was hard to hear me when I was speaking. Granted, these issues could have been due to damage not caught during the "inspection" but it was enough for me to not want to bother with trying again. I did, however, like the fit of the neck band, and the retracting earbuds feature. In the end, I'm going with another brand, and am reconsidering purchasing anymore Warehouse Deals, as their inspection process is lacking.

title: Great bang for your buck, good camera and runs all apps fast!
text:
I'm 17, own this phone and love it! My dad bought it from this same amazon listing. It will work with AT&T, T-Mobile and carriers that use their cell-towers such as MetroPCS, StraightTalk, etc. I stuck my Verizon (CDMA/LTE) sim card in it to see what would happen, it did as expected, "No Service" and showed 0 bars. This model doesn't have LTE, but does get 4G HSPA+ on AT&T. It also has dual sim capability which very few people will probably take advantage of, and the SD card expansion works just fine. It has front facing flash which works pretty well and the rear camera takes pictures and videos that are the same quality as an iPhone 5s/SE/6. The phone runs the latest version of Android (as of 2016) and is fast, runs all the apps from the google play store with no issues whatsoever, no lag or any of that stuff cheaper phones tend to suffer from when playing games on the go. The actual specs of this phone are BETTER than the iPhone 6 from 2014, more ram and a faster CPU. The UI is the same as the Samsung Galaxy S5, S6 and S7 and comes with the same apps that those phones would minus the carrier specific apps, but those can be downloaded from the Google Play android app store. (such as MyAT&T and T-Mobile's equivalent, etc).

Overall a huge bang for your buck, the hardest thing for most people would be understanding if their phone carrier in the US is compatible or not and manually swapping SIM cards. I managed to stick a nano-sim in this phone even though it's meant for micro-sim cards and it worked, just takes a bit of effort. You will NEED to input APN settings, there are TONS of tutorials from carriers themselves as well as Samsung and YouTube videos that can help you if you need more info about this.

Please note that although the description says Cricket and MetroPCS are CDMA, this is outdated information. Cricket was bought out by AT&T and as thus now runs on their GSM network, same with MetroPCS which is now owned by T-Mobile and is on their GSM network. I have tested a MetroPCS sim card in this phone and after putting in the APN settings it made calls, texts and data worked as expected.

title: Beautiful phone, great camera, speeds up Touch ID and internet connection speed. Recommended for those looking to upgrade!
text:
I was super excited to receive my new 64GB iPhone 6s on it's release date. I ordered it from my carrier and waited anxiously for its arrival. My previous phone was an iPhone 6, so I was a little concerned that upgrading might feel like getting the same phone all over again. However, I was using a 16GB model on the iPhone 6 and needed extra storage, so I decided to go ahead and upgrade to the 6s at release. After using the phone for 24 hours, I'm glad I did. Here's why:

COLOR: I LOVE the new rose gold color! It looks a lot like copper, and it is really fun to have a new iPhone color. It also perfectly matches my rose gold Apple Watch. For those who are concerned that it is too pink, well, it is pinkish, but It really seems more coppery to me.

CAMERA: The camera upgrade is very nice. I especially appreciate the new flash feature for the front facing camera. I tested it last night against the iPhone 6 and it had substantially better performance in low-light conditions. I also like the live picture capacity. Yes, its a bit gimmicky, but it is pretty neat to have animated pictures.

3D TOUCH: I like the 3D touch capacity. It is nice to be able to access shortcuts just by pressing deeply on certain apps. Though it is not currently used by many developers, I think this has a great capacity for future growth, and I look forward to seeing what developers will do with this capacity.

SPEED: This phone is FAST! I was already impressed by Touch ID on my iPhone 6, but the 6S is incredible. Literally, you touch the sensor for just a moment and the screen unlocks. I also tested the connection speed on my home WiFi and found that the 6S generally achieved 8-9 MBPS faster connections than my 6. I think the improved processor and 2GB RAM are making a difference in performance in a very positive way.

Overall, I'm happy I upgraded. The 6S is speedy and has some cool new features. I was also able to gain more storage by getting the 64GB model. For those considering purchasing it, I do recommend it. However, if you have a iPhone 6, you will probably be fine waiting until the 7 is released. For those with 5S's or below, I feel this is a worthwhile update.

My final piece of advice: Be sure to get at least the 64GB model to ensure you have enough storage. With the newly released live photos and 4K video, it will be very difficult to maintain sufficient storage on the 16GB base model.

title: this feature will be even better when third-party app functionality kicks in
text:
On first glance, the 6s looks near-on identical to its predecessor. On every glance, in fact, little seems to have changed from the iPhone 6. Even when you get right up close and even inside its svelte aluminium casing you’ll find a screen with the same resolution and as little as 16GB internal storage.

Where does the truth lie? I’ve got the answer.

Let's get straight into it, the headline feature - 3D Touch. Practically every tweak that's been made has been so with the aim of cramming in the pressure-sensing tech.

3D Touch, or Force Touch as it's been previously known on the MacBook and Apple Watch, works by sensing extra pressure on the screen to activate extra features. And it rewards you with haptic feedback, so you receive helpful vibrations under your thumb or finger as the phone registers the increased force. The feature has evolved to become more than just the fancy right click it is on the new MacBook, too. It completely changes the way you interact with your phone by giving you options where you didn’t previously have any.

Take snapping a selfie, for example. Where previously you needed to tap two different icons with intermittent loading times, this action has now been shortened to one firm press of the Photo app icon. Then you can leap right into triggering the shot. Instagram obsessives, rejoice!

3D Touch also has some supremely convenient uses with other native apps - the ones Apple makes itself. You can can jump directly into a new email in Mail and open a new tab straightaway in Safari - shaving seconds off your smartphone navigation. That may seem small change in writing, but over the course of the months and years you may spend in the iPhone 6s' company it will equate to a snappier, more satisfying user experience.

In addition to skipping straight into everyday tasks, 3D Touch also offers up the ability to preview messages and emails, and even links within them. All you have to do is press down on them to read, and should you need to take further action, apply a little more pressure and you get transported into the task itself.

Apple terms the first glance as Peek and the full open as Pop, and they’re a prime example of what the iPhone 6s is all about: subtle changes that you have to feel for yourself. And unless you’ve somehow managed to get hold of a limited edition 128GB Huawei Mate S, you won’t find these features in any Android phone.

3D Touch is a typically Apple innovation then, right up to how you customise it: you can’t.

Even if you take Time-Lapse videos more often than you do Slow-Mo, the 3D Touch shortcut choice has been made for you.

Potentially, this feature will be even better when third-party app functionality kicks in. Imagine applying pressure in Real Racing 3 to speed up, just like you would gun the accelerator in real life.

PROS
* Series 7000 aluminium will protect the phone
* 3D Touch adds a new way to interact with your iPhone
* Live Photos will be great to look back on in future
* Touch ID is much faster and more responsive

CONS
* Same resolution as the iPhone 6
* Lack of third-party 3D Touch integration
* No fast charging

Here's the issue for dual sim:  The phone allows you to pick the primary sim card.  The primary sim card will operate on 4G LTE and the secondary sim card will be relegated to 2G.  That used to work perfectly fine because the primary card would be used for data and the secondary card would be only for voice and data for the second phone line which is perfectly fine.  However, AT&T has TURNED OFF 2G signals so the secondary sim card is essentially dead and you have toggle back and forth between sim and only one will work at any one time.  So again, it will still work with two sim cards inserted, but only one line will be active at a time, not both as intended.

title: This is a great phone that doesn't get the respect it deserves in ...
text:
Quick summary: This is a great phone that doesn't get the respect it deserves in the US market. I've read through some of the negative reviews on here and wanted to help explain some misconceptions of this phone.

A lot of negative reviews are because of user error so be warned!

Pro's:
Picture quality (one of he best on the market)
Video quality (up to 4k, you can downgrade it for higher FPS)
Screen quality (it's true 4k)
Processor speed (this phone will NOT lag, regardless of how many apps you have running)
Fingerprint sensor (only available on non-us Z5 premiums)
Chrome mirror back (girls could do their makeup in this thing)
Sturdiness (I've dropped this phone more times that i can count on cement, it's still kickin)

Neutral:
Battery Life (more apps = less battery life, my phone lasts about 12-14 hours with HEAVY use)

Cons:
Price (its expensive)
Waterproof (it is NOT waterproof, only extremely resistant. I dont care what sony says, do not go swimming with this phone)

Misconceptions-

Negative statement #1: This phones picture quality sucks! My *insert phone type here* was much better!
Resolution: Actually Sony by default sets this phone too 8mp 16:9 ratio. If you click the settings button while in your camera you can manually set it to 23mp 4:3. Be warned, it will be a STUNNING photo but it will also be 10 MB of data per pic. Also I've noticed Instagram and other social sites has a hard time compressing these photos because they are such a high quality. You might want to find a good compressor program as well.

Negative statement #2: There's no warranty Sony does not stand behind there product.
Resolution: Actually there is a warranty on the non-us version's of this phone. However you most likely will need to ship your phone to wherever that non-us location is. For example lets say the phone was originally for the Thailand market. You would have to contact support in Thailand. An easier way to deal with this is to get an extended warranty, OR purchase a US version of this phone at the sacrifice of the fingerprint sensor (id personally opt for a squaretrade warranty).

Negative statement #3 & #4: The phone wont charge properly or turn on / it keeps connect and reconnecting from the micro-usb port.
Resolution: This phone is built SOLID, i've gone through like 7 charging cables in 12 months from the micro usb cords becoming bent. This is a good thing, id rather the cords bend then my $500 phones micro-usd female port. Get some extra cords and test it!

Negative statement #5: It scratches to easily.
Resolution: Buy a case....? Why would you 1 star a phone on this, all phones scratch. The screen is SUPER resilient however. Also I just replaced the chrome finish on the back of my phone, it peels off with the right tools. But again this shouldn't effect reviews to much people..

Negative statement #6: Anything not cover in my above statements
Resolution: At the end of the day the z5 is a very complex electronic device. Sometimes for whatever reason a few bad eggs are made with ANY phone. And that's why warranties are important, chances are you'll be fine but there's always that 1/10,000 chance. If you're not sure where to get a warranty check out statement #2.

Give a thumbs up if you found this review helpful.
Hopefully this review helps fix or clear up any current issues people are having.

Cheers!

title: I wish I could return the phone but I've past the return date policy
text:
First off I would like to say the seller great. There are NO problems with the seller at all (for me).

My issues with the phone. Physically it is VERY, VERY, VERY slippery. If you go to Sony's support site the first thing you will see is a pop up with the words at the top "To solve issues and ensure optimal performance for your Xperia™ smartphone or tablet, try these simple steps." Unfortunately I have been doing that with the phone a lot. I have to restart my phone at least once a day. When the phone works the display is crisp, the camera capture is beautiful, sound is ok for a front speaker, and water friendly as advertised. I only use 1 sim so I don't know of any issues about 2 sim use. But as the day progresses and you use the phone more and more you would feel the back of the phone start heating up. I'd be on facebook and click on a video but when I rotate my phone for landscape view the video doesn't rotate. I'd go on youtube and it does the same. Restart the device and the switch from portrait to landscape starts working again. I enable the Do Not Disturb function and it works on the first unwanted call. The second unwanted call tho disables the Do Not Disturb and so I hear the phone ring to its loudest. IF you manually set the phone to vibrate only it works on the first call. When the 2nd unwanted call (this is not the same caller) comes in, lo and behold it's no longer on vibrate mode and the phone starts singing its tune. I would then notice I don't get phone calls anymore. My family would tell me my phone cannot be reached. I don't get phone calls anymore. Restart the device and I get phone calls again. The fingerprint doesn't work anymore. You carefully and slowly place your registered finger on the sensor, it automatically switches to Enter Pin mode (I setup PIN and fingerprint). Restart the device and the sensor starts working again. Turn off wifi? Yes you can. But if it sees another wifi source it turns on again. I found out later there is a setting to actually keep it off if you want to. I guess it's a feature in Sony? It's more like an annoying bug to me. Never seen that setting on an iOS, Windows, or other Android phone. As the battery drains, when you get lower than 15% it starts to eat up your battery quicker. 2 or 3 times faster than normal battery drain. Leave your 15% on the bedside table as you go to sleep and you'd wake up the battery fully drained. There may be a few more things that I can't remember now. You may say it's nitpicking the functions of the device but I say, it's the small things you notice as you use it everyday. I was able to fix my 3yr old SG Note 3 from water exposure accident at Niagara (not really ^_^ ). I may just stop using this new phone and switch back to my old phone.

To sum it all up, I wish I could return the phone but I've past the return date policy. I'll put it underwater for a few seconds and pretend I'm drowning my stress with it.

title: Be aware of Sony Support.
text:
I have been a Sony customer for years until I got a phone with overheating problems. This problem has affected more than one of Sony's top phones, and although it hasn't happened to everyone, it affected a few of us and I want to share the experience I had with Sony's US Customer Support. After just a few months of using my $500 phone, I started having overheating problems after recording videos with the phone, sometimes after just a couple minutes of recording. I contacted Sony Support, had it sent for evaluation but got it returned a few weeks later with a message saying the phone had gone through tests and showed no problems. I received the phone and gave it a try... the problem was still there. I even sent a screenshot (attached image) showing the message I still got after recording just a couple minutes of video. They just asked me to wait for firmware updates. Of course, that never solved the problem.
I accepted the fact that I had to deal with a phone with a great camera that just couldn't be used in it's full potential.
The problems did not end there. After a few months of limited use and after exposing the phone to rain, the screen stopped working. I immediately checked the phone and saw one of the corners in the back was raised, so apparently the support team did not seal the phone properly after the evaluation and now the water had gotten in. I wrote Sony support again explaining the whole situation, but their response was that US support could no longer see this case, and that I should take it to the manufacturer country (China) to see if they can do something.
I paid over $500 for a phone that lasted just over a year. The phone I purchased was an E6553, one of the top phones by the end of 2015 (when purchased) as the E6883 is now. That's the reason why I'm writing the review here.
It's not the first time I've received electronic devices with problems, but all other brands have responded as expected, with a repair, exchange of device or even a refund, but it's important for customers to know how Sony reacts to these cases.
Hope this helps customers who are trying to decide between Sony and other brands.

title: Sony Z5 Premium, THE smartphone for grown ups.
text:
Okay, just so you know, I am what you might call an "early adopter" In other words I am a sucker for smartphones. Every time somone came out with something new I just had to have one for my own. Ever since I brought home my brand new first generation iPhone, I have always been enthralled with these little magical rectangles made of metal and glass. I have had every iteration of iPhone, right on up through the 6S. I have had three HTC's including the amazing M7 and M8. I have owned a OnePlus one, an LG V10 a Samsung Galaxy S6 Edge, and I still use my S7 Edge as a back up phone. But, I can honestly and unequivocally say that not a single one of them hold a candle to the Xperia Z5 Premium. The 4K display is amazing of course, and the camera is incredible, but what makes this phone stand out is that every little feature that it has works flawlessly. I liked my Galaxy phones but both of them would heat up, lock up, refuse to connect to my car via bluetooth, refuse to charge ...the list goes on. On the other hand, the iPhones worked perfectly, but the un-customizable UI just became so damned tedious after a while. Enter the Z5 Premium. It has none of the cartoonish color saturation and UI of the Galaxy models that the tekkies fawn over. The Z5 Premium just has a 4K display that is smoother, cleaner perfectly colored and blows your mind when you watch 4K media. silky 16mm film, while the Samsung's images "pop out" but look like they are recorded on soap opera videotape. title: Better than the early reviews indicate
text:
Microsoft and AT&T have recently dropped the prices on these phones, so you may be looking into them. And you might be thinking "Wow, what a bunch of negative reviews!" But look at the dates. None of them are recent - Windows 10 Mobile was indeed a mess at he beginning, but things have improved considerably since then. I just purchased this phone to replace my aging Lumia 1020, and I am satisfied and then some with the experience.

HARDWARE

The display is superb. Like, probably the prettiest display you've ever seen. Black levels are perfect (being OLED), pixel density beats the iPhone's "retina" displays,, color is vibrant but not cartoonish. The brightness is adequate for sunlight reading and the auto-adjustment of brightness works well. The glass is Gorilla Glass 3 with a beautifully smooth finish, a joy to touch, with only moderate oil pickup.

The Snapdragon 808 with 3gb of RAM runs everything like a dream, no lags or standbys ("Resuming..." on the older WP8.1 hardware). IT does run rather warm under load and the phone gets rather hot while quick charging. Battery life has been improved considerably since early OS builds, and it is relatively easy to get a day or even a day and a half with moderate use (for example, a few calls, reading the news, email, and checking Facebook. Taking lots of photos does drain things more quickly).

The plastic back is a bit cheap-feeling compared to older Nokia Windows Phones. But it allows us to remove the back and replace the battery, as well as install up to 200gb of SD memory. With that said, when it's on the phone, you might forget it's detachable at all. The buttons feel premium and clicky and there are no creaks. Speaking of buttons, you get a dedicated 2-stage shutter button, which is way superior to an onscreen shutter button (which is also included for die-hards)..

SOFTWARE

If you have a Windows 10 PC, Windows 10 Mobile will seem very familiar, and there should be little to no learning curve. Settings are a bit layered, but there is a search function that makes things easier than Android or iOS. W10M is running WAY better than it did in lat 2015. My recommendation is to join the Windows Insider program and select the "Release Preview" ring. You'll update to the "Redstone 1" build which is very stable and has lots of extra features.

Customizing your Start menu is a joy, as it's always been. Live tiles are so much more engaging than dumb icon grids, too, with constantly refreshing headlines, weather, and app data.

Microsoft offers a superb suite of in-house apps, such as a News Reader, Sports, Weather, MS Office, Outlook, and Calendar. All of the major apps out there are represented with the exception of Snapchat and the Google suite, though there are some decent third party options if you are wedded to those. The "app gap" is real, and you may not find your favorite banking or device apps (though Fitbit is present, thankfully). My suggestion for app-houds is to look at your current phone and see what you truly use non-stop. Head to the Windows Store online and check out whether there is a first-party app available.

CAMERA

Look, I'm coming from a Lumia 1020. So my standards are high. the 950 **almost** lives up to it. Detail is excellent on close and medium shots, but faraway landscapes don't allow the level of zoom that the 1020 did. Colors are rich but not cartoonish. Low-light performance is better than most phone cameras, and the 3-LED flash beats everything but a true Zenon flash (which almost no current phones possess). This camera is equal to or better than the iPhone 6s or the Samsung Galaxy S7. But don't take my word for it, check out GSM Arena's Photo Quality Comparison tool for yourself. The 950 is almost up to the level of some of the dedicated DSLR cameras, and is equal or better to most dedicated point-and-shoot digital cameras.

CONCLUSION

A beautiful display with a chintzy back. Expandable storage and removable battery. Excellent native Microsoft apps but spottier 3rd party apps (e.g. Snapchat, Google, Pokemon Go). A best in class camera. Solid battery life. A constantly growing operating system that should be very familiar to Windows PC users. This is an excellent phone, especially at the reduced price. It has room to grow, and it runs a bit warm at times. I think it's worth a chance as long as you're not completely wedded to Google or Apple ecosystems.
