title: You'll never have the chance to know what you've been missing all along
text:
I'm so sad that Microsoft is discontinuing their phones. If you've never used one, you have no idea how great they became over time. They had gorilla glass for (8?) years before Apple realized it might be a good idea to make a droppable device that wouldn't shatter (and MS/Nokia never charged you $1,000 for that "luxury"); what you iPhone and Android users who don't like your cartoonish icons don't realize is that that they're the result of *poorly* mimicking Microsoft's WP 8 UI overhaul...

I sometimes talk to people who say they find WP counterintuitive to use, and it absolutely blows my mind. Whereas I have a simple, clean start screen where I keep only my most-used apps, with the icon sizes tweaked so they jump out at me just as I want them to (and the rest of the apps are tucked away on another single screen that's easily searchable and easy to jump around alphabetically), I watch these same WP complainers pull out their iPhones and swipe from screen to screen, muttering frustratedly under their breath, "Where did I put that freaking app...??" (Anecdotal: the most recent such conversation I had was with a person who said that he found his *dad's* WP to be counterintuitive. Well, that's a tribute to the ability to completely customize the layout. Whose dad is going to tweak a UI in any sensible way? ;)

Of course, the major drawback to Windows Phones was always the small number of apps. But I've never lacked anything I need from such a device. I lack lots of the games the rest of you play, yes--but do you want a professional, highly functional, easy-to-use, reliable, unbreakable tool; or do you want a toy? I'm particularly confounded when I see businesspeople insist on iPhones, while WP has native integration with the Office products they use every day (although, admittedly, trying to make Excel functional on a handheld device was a terrible idea).

Well, then, enjoy your toys.

Alright, as for this particular device I purchased, all of the above elation applies. I'll add that WP 10 has a lot of improvements over 8 (my last device [which served me really well for over 4.5 years!] was a Lumia 920), and of course, the inclusion of MS Edge pre-installed is a glorious reminder that IE will and should die.

With the caveat that I bought this *used*, my only (slight) disappointment is with the battery life. But oh yeah, you can actually replace the battery, so.

I'm so grateful for the seller I bought this from (Cellular Gallery Inc): for less than $200, they've given me something I'll really appreciate for years--and I don't yet have to give into Apple's business model of making you buy a very slightly altered version of the same thing every year for $400-1,000.

This is a nostalgic moment for me. This may be the last Windows Phone I'll ever be able to buy. But at least I have some years of contentment left before I have no choice but to follow the rest of the sheep.... I'm *not* a Microsoft apologist, because on the whole, they've gotten plenty of things wrong over the years. But they really innovated with their phones, in ways that others could only *try* to copy, long after the fact.

Get one of these while they're still around. You won't regret it.

title: Great Phone for AT&T
text:
Windows Phones have a unique quality about them. They have always run quite well even on the most minimal hardware specs. You don't have to worry about minimal specs with this phone though. It is very much a powerful phone.

This phone has 3GB of RAM, a 1.8 GHz six core processor, and 32 GB of storage. Because Windows Phone is so well optimized though, all this power doesn't really feel that fast when compared to lower-spec’d Windows Phones. It's not a bad thing really, it's just that Windows Phone seems to run well on any hardware. It runs very fluidly, aside from the occasional loading ellipses and circle of dots that Microsoft uses in Windows Phone. Sometimes this phone gets warm on the back, especially if you use it while charging.

Considering Windows Phone’s biggest flaw is the so-called "app-gap" (lack of apps), this 32gb of internal storage is more than enough. For me, as little as 8gb suffices. Installing games may eat up a lot of your space though. Luckily, the storage is expandable to 200GB for apps, videos, music, photos, and offline Maps downloads using a micro sd card. I place everything but the apps on the micro sd card.

The 20 megapixel camera’s photos have a unique look that separates them from other phone photos. You’ll notice when you take a photo, that the app says its “applying finishing touches.” These seem to provide the uniqueness. The camera can record 4k video HD if you prefer.

This phone is the AT&T model, which came in a custom AT&T box, that included a hardwired charger (non-removal USB C cable) and a separate USB A to USB C cable.

There are nicely placed volume and power buttons on the side. The removable back panel is quite easy to take off too. There is a slot in the bottom where you insert your fingernail to pry it open. Overall this phone feels well made, but is all plastic, and it creaks if I squeeze it or push on the back cover. Even though this is a high-end phone, I don't feel like I need to baby it, which is probably a result of it being plastic. It is lightweight and feels good in hand. At 5.2 inches, the screen looks only slightly smaller than my Galaxy Note 5, which is what I use daily. This screen is super sharp at over 500 pixels per inch.

Windows Phone 10 version 1607 is much, much more reliable and stable than earlier builds (like Windows Phone 8.1 and Windows Phone 10 v1511), which I experienced using other Windows phones. This phone ships with Windows Phone 10 version 1511 installed. Once you are set up and running, you should update to the current OS version as soon as you can. Version 1607 is current at the time of this review.

The "app gap” situation is not as bad as everyone makes it seem. Everyone seems to point out that Snapchat is missing. I don’t use Snapchat. Besides built-in Microsoft apps, I have Adobe Photoshop Express, Facebook, Flixster, Hulu, Instagram, Netflix, Starbucks, UPS Mobile, VLC, WWE Network, Swarm, and Twitter to name a few of the big ones you might be wondering about. There's even the Alarm.com app for supported home security systems. You won't find Gmail, Youtube, Google Maps, etc. Microsoft does have its own alternative apps for maps, news, weather, music, and email, and you can freely configure any email account in Outlook (Gmail, Yahoo, your business account or school account, etc). There is always the ability to pin a webpage to the Start Screen, simulating the app experience. I do this for Nest and Youtube.

The concept of developers building universal apps needs to gain some momentum and the “app gap” will start to shrink quickly.

This phone supports Continuum, which allows you to use miracast to turn this phone into a PC by using a miracast capable monitor or tv, and a blue tooth keyboard and mouse. Otherwise, you can use Continuum with Microsoft’s Display dock, which I have on order, but have not received yet.

I use my Note 5 everyday, but want to Give Windows Phone a try as my daily driver. The most important app for me is Google Voice, for which there is no app on Windows Phone. Google Voice is accessible via the browser though, but it is clunky trying to use it this way. Regardless, Windows Phone 10 is a good change of pace from IOS and Android, and fun to play around with and explore.

I like that the windows bar (with the back, windows, and Cortana buttons) disappears when viewing photos or certain web content to give you a larger screen. The best part of having done the W10 preview build is that all of my settings and all of my apps and the way I had my phone configured automatically migrated onto my new phone. This is one of the best things about the new way Microsoft is approaching the new operating systems. It took me only half an hour to go from open box to the phone set up the way I wanted it. Gone are the hours of migrating all of your stuff to a new phone.

I still had 2 months left on my ATT contract so my only purchase option was the Next plan. Now it turns out that I would have been miserable for the next two months if I had waited out the contract because ATT has announced dropping contract plans. I did go with the 12 month upgrade option hoping that the Surface Phone happens and is everything it looks like it can be.

In short, if you are a Windows Phone fan, this phone is worth the upgrade.

title: The Dream Has Become a Nightmare
text:
As a die hard Windows phone fan, I had such hope for the Microsoft Lumia 950 - a big, powerful Windows Phone running Windows Mobile 10. At first, it seemed like a dream come true, a fast, clean, incredibly functional device that was a virtual mini-computer in my hand.

Then, the bugs started to crawl out of the device - apps and programs crashing, incredibly slow app loading and web browsing, tiles inexplicably being deleted from my start screen.

Now, six month in, the device has started gobbling cellular data like a starving dog in a smokehouse. Inexplicably, the mysteriously named "System" function has begun consuming 100-200 Gb of background cellular data daily, even with a wifi connection. Three of the past six months, this phone has consumed 3+ Mb, when my normal regular usage is 500 Gb. In spite of consulting numerous forums that identify this as a major Windows Mobile 10 bug and disabling all background data usage, it keeps on gobbling. The only solution seems to be completely disabling the cellular data connection, which renders the device unable to text or perform any other functions that need a cellular connect.

Tonight, I have finally surrendered, having missed dozens of critical business texts and emails today, that are rolling in hours later this evening when the phone has finally decided whether it wants to use my wifi or the cellular connection.

I believe I am finally done with Windows phones.

As for the Lumia 920, the 950 can be wirelessly charged using the Nokia DT-900 wireless charging plate. It also fits in the Nokia CR-200 wireless charging car cradle holder but sadly does not charge in it.

I bought my Lumia950 a year ago unlocked on Ebay...refurb, $120...and it's amazing! I was angry when Nokia exited the market because they built phones like tanks. But Microsoft did fantastic with one , despite the fact its plastic. It's super thin and light weight...and doesn't feel cheap at all. The design is very simple and boxy, but once you wrap it in a sexy case(see pic) that point is completely MOOT. The display is crisp and brilliant...instant response to touch. The camera allows pro manual adjustments to iso, shutter speed, white balance....everything ! And takes exceptionally sharp photos...and slow-mo video too!
Yes, the Windows apps store is bare bones, but I'm 40, and don't need an app to escort me around the internet or Show me how much to tip a waiter. And I for one despise Apple and Android boxy,cookie cutter interfaces....wouldnt trade my resizeable,reshapeable, infinitely more interesting customizable live-tiles for the world! Get you one!

text:
I ordered at least five of s-pen so far. Except one, none of them lasted long.

Mainly due to the cheap imitation made in china product. Last order I returned it , because it didn't even work and the nip fell out.

Prior to that, I ordered from Awinner, and 2 of those pen didn't last 3 weeks.

The reason was, most of those none genuine imitation doesn't have replaceable nibs. It rather has a conductive polymer silicon material tip, backed by some carbon rod with copper coil.

I ordered this product from here, not because, this product was "Amazon recommended", but, also, it advertises as it as in retail box. It made me feel that this item is genuine Samsung product, or at least oem product.

Also, some of the review and the picture uploaded shows replaceable nibs included, made me think I was ordering a retail product.

However, I was using it Since May 7, this year, and it started work funny.

Such as, it double-click which wasn't intended. Or click or touch of the pen to the digitizer screen won't get recognized. It was very frustrating, so, I figured to replace the nib.

By the way, Mine didn't come with the extra nib and the pulling tool, not even inside the box pad, not like some of the picture you see in other comment.

I had extra nib from my phone box, so, I decided to pull out the nib from this s-pen I got it from here.

Once I pulled out, I immediately realize it's not the original s-pen.

It has small tip, backed by carbon rod with copper coil. The nib wasn't replaceable.

As you can see above picture, I made a comparison with the nib of the original pen. and plastic piece I pulled out from this purchase.

My previous made in china pen was in similar configuration but, it had even shorter nib.

Anyhow, this is at least my fifth pen I ordered, and at this point, I feel that I am intentionally being screwed by Amazon. I don't see any other explanation, assuming Amazon has at least decent quality control, and a strict regulation of the shipment from third party.

I also tried to check the serial number at Samsung site, but, I couldn't find a way to do it. If someone knows how to do it, please let me know. I am tired of used, fake, damaged, and non functioning products.

title: Learn from my mistake!
text:
The phone is working great, Yeah!
I very recently purchase a Lumia 950 XL, was very excited about the purchase, also purchased a heavy duty protective case determined to protect the device. Received both and married them together, they looked like they belonged together; the emperor looked awesome in his new clothes. Then the trouble started the phone seemed to take way too long to charge and it would not hold the charge for long, constantly depleted of power, ouch; disappointed I wrote the vendor to report the issue, so much as cancelling the order.

In one final attempt to avoid returning my shiny new toy, I stripped the phone naked, to the way it shipped and made one more "desperate" attempt to recharge the phone, plugged it in and checked in to see the progress one hour later; the phone went from completely drained to fully charge in one hour or less. Left the phone out of its protective case and checked back 8 hours later, the phone was fully charged, STILL.

Needless to say, in spite of egg on my face, still EXTACTIC to not have to return my new toy, the device works PERFECTLY. Sharing my shame so that all you folks who are experiencing issues with your device might learn from my experience.

Always a GOOD IDEA to first check to see if your device is properly working prior to making any additions or changes. Now I have cut holes into the device holder where the device buttons are so they are not restricted, as well as still protecting it, and I remove the rubber case when using for long stretched of time so it does not overheat. Happy to know it was a stupid mistake on my part.

Still EXCITED about my new shiny device!

title: I still love this small discount smartish phone
text:
Look, if you are glued to social media and need access to rideshare and bikeshare and other leading apps, forget this phone -- not going to happen. BUT if you need a quality discount phone for calling, emailing and texting and patient / basic web browsing, this is it, with some great bonuses.

The Windows app store doesn't keep pace with Apple or Google (at all), but there are some weird wonderful apps mixed in there, although they are likely not the ones you are looking for.

I love this phone mainly because I love the Windows 8.1 interface and classic Nokia design.There might be a way to upgrade this phone to WIndows 10, but likely not.

The FM radio is great as is the HERE navigation suite (which allows maps to be downloaded to the phone). Other apps that I use include a couple of interesting news aggregators by city and country, Whatsapp, a Soundcloud server called Audiocloud, Netflix, Pandora and Moovit (to supplement some public transit options that Nokia HERE transit route planning seems to miss). As a phone for navigating -- including turn by turn while driving -- I love it.

I stick with this phone even though I've experienced problems with build quality. The charging port on my last one gave out after about 10 months of use, but it was hard use. At this price point, it's a good worksite phone, noting the FM radio and other playback options.

I've read of people using this discount phone simply as a smart music player, and I can see that. Great output and I've been able to bluetooth connect to various speakers. There's also all sorts of interesting free music apps in the store. The pre-installed podcast player, though, went dead this year (although there are alternatives in the store). I could also see folks using this simply to hot spot an internet connection.

I'm giving it 4 stars due to the charging issue and as developers step away from Windows 8.1 -- losing Twitter and Uberr and the built-in podcast player in the last year. don't mind being out-of-step with this phone, but many might. I enjoy it as a $50 gadget. Features will likely worsen in coming months (somehow), but there's still plenty left that makes this an interesting phone choice.

Another bonus is the battery is removable and spares can be bought through Amazon for about $8. I find this useful, and it gives the phone a little more resilience. The phone has some bulk to it, but I like the small size. I would recommend a flip case to help protect the screen. Even with a case it is still a pocket phone.

title: A+ would buy again.
text:
I was deciding between the regular P9, the P9 Plus, the regular P10, the P10 Plus, and the Mate 9. It was a really tough decision but I feel like I made the correct one. Any of those phones would have been an excellent choice but I am very glad I chose the P9 Plus.

P9:
Pros: Dirt cheap at this point. Not that different from the P9 Plus. I like smaller phones.
Cons: Out of my options it's the lowest spec'd and most out of date.

P9 Plus:
Pros: AMOLED screen!!! This makes a world of difference and it's the only one of my options that has it. It's beautiful! The screen size, battery, and phone specs are all slightly better than the regular P9.
Cons: It's only slightly cheaper than the Mate9 and theoretically doesn't have as good of a camera.
Other thoughts: Is the P9 Plus worth $100 more than the regular P9? Thanks to the screen and spec bump, I say yes.

Mate9:
Pros: Very high specs at a low price.
Cons: It's larger than I want and the build quality is slightly more flimsy.
Other thoughts: The price is comparable to the P9 Plus. The Mate9 specs are better BUT the screen isn't as good. The P10 isn't that much more expensive.

P10:
Pros: The specs are better. I like small screens.
Cons: The price is getting slightly out of my comfort zone. I don't like that bottom button on the front of the device.

P10 Plus:
Pros: The best specs and the best camera.
Cons: Too expensive.

Final Thoughts:
* I'm glad I didn't listen to the rest of the internet and buy the Mate9. The P9 Plus is still an amazing flagship phone and the display is one of the best I've seen.
* It may be a year out of date at this point but that doesn't bother me and I get a huge discount for waiting.
* The camera quality is fantastic. It may have a lower score on dxomark but I love this camera.
* The speaker / ringer volume can get quite loud.
* The bluetooth, GPS, and wifi chipsets all seem good.
* The 4G isn't quite as good on TMobile as it was on my Sony XA BUT it's still 4G and still good.
* Works fine with Android Auto
* Works fine with a Samsung Gear
* Plenty of storage thanks to 64GB built in and an SD card slot.

title: After a few days and many tweaks, I love this phone but with some frustrations
text:
NOTE about this particular model: This particular listing is for the Dual-SIM version of the Honor 8 smartphone. The key advantage of the Dual-SIM version is that you can put in two SIM cards to operate the phone on two different networks simultaneously. The second SIM card does go in a hybrid slot that supports either the 2nd SIM or a microSD card, but it cannot hold both at the same time. The key disadvantage of this model is you lose 1GB of RAM, for 3GB (vs 4GB for the "single SIM" model).

So, if you expect to travel a lot between two places where you don't wish to keep swapping SIM cards, or you need the convenience of two separate networks, then get this model. But if you intend to use just one SIM most of the time, then get the "single SIM" model instead as it is faster with the extra GB of RAM and currently cheaper too.
--
EDIT (9/12/2016):
After using the Honor 8 for several weeks, several issues have popped-up that weren't initially apparent. As a result, I am dropping my rating of this phone from 5 to 4-stars:
-I've noticed my phone is running the July 2016 security update of Android. Samsung and LG are very prompt at rolling out security updates, so I find it disturbing that Huawei isn't doing so in a timely manner.
-I had popped in an old SanDisk microSD card into the phone, which worked fine for several days. But then I was getting messages that the card was corrupted and needed to be formatted. When I tried to format it, the phone froze. I tried to pop in the card into my laptop, and it can't be accessed anymore. Luckily I had nothing of value stored on the card, but this was alarming nonetheless. I've ordered a newer microSD to try again; I will update if I have issues with that one as well.
-I've discovered that the Honor 8 seems to either not follow some of the settings I've specified, or even change some settings on its own. This has happened several times now with the following settings:
->The ringtone volume: I've been setting the ringtone as low as possible and even test to make sure it sounds low, but when I receive a call later, the ringtone comes out blaringly loud! It has already embarrased me a few times in public spaces, so naturally I've been furious about it
->The display brightness: When set to auto, I found the phone to dim the brightness a bit too dark, so I turned off the Auto brightness. But, the phone is STILL continuing to change the brightness even though I don't want it to. For instance, I may set the brightness to full 100%, and a minute later, it will change it to 80% even though Auto is turned off.
-Most annoying of all, I've had a few instances now where the Honor 8's GPS indicates that I am somewhere in the middle of the Atlantic Ocean off the coast Africa...when I'm usually in the Washington, DC area. This was especially bothersome when I tried to use the Maps app to get myself out of a dead end yesterday. My wife's iPhone saved the day (but not my dignity), and the Honor 8 suddenly realized its accurate location later in the day.

Finally, another Huawei installed app, Phone Manager, started displaying daily notifications to "clean my phone", meaning I should clean up the RAM, etc. Some people may find this feature beneficial, but I certainly didn't like the daily notifications and was able to turn that off after some digging into the settings menu.

But I then came to a realization: I've made so many settings changes and tweaks on this phone now that if something were to happen where I'd have to reset the phone to factory settings, then I'd be very upset in losing every change I've made.

Overall, these glitches are very unacceptable to me, and as a result I am downgrading my rating to 4 stars. This is not something I would ditch the phone for, and hope that it gets fixed in software updates, but for now they are annoying.

--Original review below:

I got into the Android world only recently with the Nexus 5X (I had only used iPhones before) and immediately grew to like it through the stock Android experience. I wasn't very pleased with the speed of the Nexus 5X and how sluggish many apps would run, but I didn't want to upgrade to the 6P (also made by Huawei) due to the larger size.

Enter Huawei's Honor 8, which seems to be the perfect upgrade for me.

THE POSITIVES:
+The phone is very solidly built and put-together perfectly. It feels more expensive than it is
+The design is slim and fits in your pocket easily. Unlike my Nexus 5X with the same screen size of 5.2", the Honor 8 fits perfectly in my car's cupholder
+This phone runs fast! Everything seems immediate with practically no discernible lag, from web browsing to playing music (Apple Music, to be exact) to even unlocking using the fingerprint reader
+Battery life is better than my Nexus 5X. The Nexus would last me 8-9 hours on a charge through the day, the Honor 8 seems to be going at least 12 hours and more before I need to plug it in
+Speaking of charging, the fast charge feature is no joke. I've found the phone to go from almost empty (3%) to 100% fully charged in little more than an hour! The phone also charges fast with any regular 2.1A USB charger, such as the Anker Powerport. (The Nexus 5X will only rapid charge with its included charger)
+Forgot to mention call-quality: the phone does support VoLTE calling, which is indicated by a "HD" icon. VoLTE calls sound so clear that it is hard to believe you are on a cell phone. Non-VoLTE (or non-HD) calls aren't as clear, but are still pretty good quality. Of course, it all depends on your network and reception (I'm on T-Mobile, and usually get their LTE or 4G HSPA network most of the time).
+The Camera takes some great NIGHT shots. Try taking a picture of the Moon using the Honor 8 and an iPhone 6; the Honor 8 will render the Moon clearly, while it appears as a white blob in the iPhone's shot. For daytime pictures, I honestly couldn't tell much of a difference between an iPhone 6 vs Honor 8's shots of the same subjects. That is not to say the Honor 8 still takes impressive daylight pictures, but I'm not sure that the dual-lens function has much bearing on the quality of them. The camera app is super-fast and can be ready to take a shot in a couple seconds, unlike the Nexus who's camera app is very slow and not good for trying to catch quick one-of-a-kind moments.

THE NEGATIVES:
-Very simply, the software out of the box is so different from what I was used to with stock Android. I don't like many of the tweaks and visual flair that Huawei put into their version of Android (called EMUI). It is obvious they are trying to make their version of Android look and run very much like Apple's iOS.
However, after much tweaking with the settings and installing some other applications, I've been able to make this phone feel a lot more like what I was used to. I've listed my tweaks below under "Tweaks to Consider"
-As part of my tweaks, I tried to disable or at least hide many of Huawei's stock applications in favor of the Google apps. But one Huawei app in particular, HiVoice, keeps nagging me to give it permissions to access my content and what not. There is no way to disable that app and as much as I've tried to neuter it, I still get a random pop-up for it that annoys me. If any Huawei software engineers are reading this review, PLEASE give us the ability to disable or uninstall HiVoice. Or at the least, stop it from nagging constantly to gain permissions
-The phone does heat up after several minutes of use. This is regardless of whether you are just browsing the web, listening to music or playing a game
-Display and Resolution: On its own, the Honor 8's screen seems brilliant and renders text and images well. But compared side-to-side with the Nexus 5X, it seems to be pale in comparison. I've included pictures where I show the two devices side-by-side. I set both screens to display at 75% brightness; the Nexus screen (on the left) is obviously brighter than the Honor 8 (on the right). You will also notice that the Honor 8's screen doesn't display as much information or screen real estate as the Nexus does.

NEUTRALS:
+- Huawei will not win any awards for original design of the Honor 8. Just like the software, the phone itself is very much a copy of the iPhone 6/s, from the rounded edges to the glass screen to even the speaker holes. The back of the phone, however, isn't like the iPhone as it is glass. But then, I'd say Huawei was "inspired" by the iPhone 4/s or the Galaxy S7 for this aspect of the design
+- Since the phone was just released, there aren't many cases or specifc accessories out yet. But I'm sure the selection will expand very soon

TWEAKS TO CONSIDER:
The biggest advantage of Android over iOS is the ability to tweak the software to your liking. If you are someone who is used to the stock Android experience from a Nexus phone, then consider the following tweaks I made to get the Honor 8 to a similar, if not the same, type of experience:
-Launcher: (GOOGLE NOW LAUNCHER) I downloaded and installed the Google Now Launcher from the Play Store. This is the exact launcher that the stock Nexus devices use
-Lock Screen: (MICROSOFT NEXT) I hated the fact that I couldn't get some notifications to disappear from my lock screen without having to unlock the device (in particular, I may want to keep a message from a friend visible to remind me to respond, but I want a spam email notification to go away).
The solution I found was to download and install Microsoft's Next Lock Screen app from the Play Store. While it doesn't fully replicate the stock Android lock screen, it has pretty much the same functionality. In addition, you gain some useful quick shortcut icons on the bottom to open frequently-used apps. Most of all, you can keep the Next Lock Screen enabled and use the fingerprint-reader to still unlock the phone
-Visual Voicemail: The Nexus supports Visual Voicemail within its Dialer app, but the Honor 8 doesn't. The only substitute is to download your carrier's own app for Visual Voicemail (I have T-Mobile and their app works almost seamlessly. AT&T also has an app in the Play Store)
-Remove Bloatware: Huawei does ship the Honor 8 with a few bloatware apps, such as Booking.com, Facebook, Twitter and Lyft. But you can uninstall the apps you don't use
-Other apps downloaded: I installed the Google versions of Gmail, Calendar, Clock and Photos to replace the Huawei versions. Although, the Huawei versions are simple reskins that still run the Google apps underneath, so this isn't a necessary tweak. I did this just for my own comfort and familiarity, simply as I am used to the Google versions.
Additional Note: If you prefer to use Google's Clock app as your alarm clock, make sure to enable ALL notification permissions for that app (like Priority Notifications, Lockscreen notifications, etc.). Let's just say I didn't initially do that, and almost was late for work the first day I tried using this phone as my alarm...

OVERALL:
If I had rated this phone immediately after using it in its stock form for an hour, I would have given this 3 stars (for excellent hardware and terrible software out of the box). But after using this phone for several days and making the tweaks I described above, I have grown to like this phone enough to rate it a solid 5 stars. I like it enough that I have put away my Nexus 5X in a drawer and will be using the Honor 8 for the foreseeable future. I do recommend this phone for the power Android user and anyone else who is comfortable making tweaks, as well as someone who doesn't care about their software experience but does want a high-quality, fast and powerful phone. If you are someone new to Android who wants an inexpensive phone and can tolerate some sluggishness, I'd suggest getting a Nexus 5X instead. Or even a cheaper Android phone such as Blu. I don't believe the extra cost for the extra features of the Honor 8 will be worth it to the latter type of users.

title: Horrible failure of a phone
text:
My family purchased 4 of the LG G4 phones in fall 2015. Since then - 12 months of operation - we have had to replace every single one of them no less than TWICE for EACH line. Mine personally I've had to replace FOUR times.

These errors are 100% phone operation issues and were replaced under warranty. They are not user error. We do not root or overclock our phones. We take good care of our phones and are your typical users. For the most part, each failure was either the screen stopped functioning (there is a "known error" called "split screen" where the screen gets pixellated and only functions on one side); or the phone would try to update, ending up in a boot loop or just bricked.

My phone was the first to malfunction... it developed the split screen error within the first two months. When I got the replacement through my carrier, that phone "bricked" while trying to install a software update. When the THIRD replacement arrived, it also auto-updated and bricked before I'd even had it 24 hours. The fourth and final one I turned every "auto" feature off as fast as I could. It functions but there is a constant update notification. Sometimes it is glitchy with recognizing touch on the screen... but I'm not going to push my luck with an update.

This is not an old problem. One of the lines attempted an update, bricked, and had to be replaced last month. One of the phones is currently inoperable because it will not turn on unless you plug it in to charge (which wakes the screen up).

I normally don't write such scathing reviews, but these phones have truly been nothing but problems. If it was just one instance or if the problems were early on when the phones came out, okay LG just had some bugs to work out. But no, these phones simply do NOT function properly.

title: Thoughts after A YEAR of usage
text:
Design: Subtle curve display, metal rim & leather back! This is one the best designed touchscreen phone ever made! And it is THE BEST phone LG ever made (yes I'm counting latest G5 too!).

Performance: For normal day to day use, I never felt it is under power. Though CPU on this phone (SD808) is not my fav. SoC. I would love to see refresh of this phone with much better SoC. SD808+3GB RAM is good combination. Performance is not a issue here.

Camera: Again, this 16MP camera is one of the best camera ever putted on a smartphone. It is THE BEST from LG. Images are bright, clear, color accurate, focus is very quick thanks to laser module on the side of the lens. If you can focus correctly, you can get very nice blurry background thanks to the wide f1.8 aperture lens! I don't shoot selfie much, but front 8MP camera produces excellent images too!

Audio: It is an very good phone for listening to music, both through ear phone or speaker. Speaker is on the back (slight drawback, I prefer front or bottom speakers), and is 1W. Sound is enough loud with slight BASS. Sound through earphone is very good too. I didn't use supplied earphones much, but they are very good quality headphones.

UI: I just HATE LG's UI. It is UGLY. Features are there, but UI design, icons & colors... Oh.. Its a disappointment! Even with latest android OS (6.0 Marshmallow), it UGLY (but not compromising usability). Again, aesthetics/design are subjective matters. You might like it!

Battery life: Um... Mediocre. I get around 3 and half hours of screen on time. With moderate to light use, you can get through the whole day. But again, because of removability of the battery, you can change it or replace it with a third party large battery (of courge, by trading of the thickness of the phone).

As remote control: The phone got an "IR blaster" on top, which is a rarity in phones this days. I am able to control my TV, AC with it without any problem! It is an awesome feature!

After one year of usage, I still recommend LG G4 over other latest phones, that includes G5! For early batch of G4's there was a hardware problem, which lead to repeated restart of phone (bootloop). I experienced this issue too, after 10 months of usage. I contacted the seller (MEGA MOBILE), the were very polite & helpful. I sent the phone to them, they examined & gave me a replacement unit within 3 weeks! That was awesome!

title: Superb Flagship Phone
text:
I have been using this phone as my daily driver for a week now, and I am absolutely thrilled with it! I came from a OnePlus One and a Nexus 5, both of which I used regularly. The one thing I did not like about the OnePlus One was that it was rather hefty for the size, which the G4 immediately improves upon.

Display:
I for one always said that going beyond 1080p displays would make no difference, but boy was I wrong. This display is sharp! I am extremely impressed that I can actually notice the difference, but I undoubtedly do. The OnePlus One display looks simply paltry in comparison now. Additionally, this has some of the best colors on any smartphone display I have ever seen. Watching videos and consuming other media on it is a pleasure, and it is made better by the fact that this display has the blackest black colors which I have ever seen on an LCD display, almost makes me think it is an AMOLED display, which it is not.

Operating System:
I have always been a pure Android fan, though LG adds some useful functionality. The notification shade is improved upon in some ways, though I wish they had kept the stock Lollipop method of one swipe down for notifications, two for settings. Otherwise, there is not too much of a difference. It is so comfortable to use that I have not actually chosen to switch to the Google Now launcher, though I may yet do so.

Speed:
Nothing to really say here other than this phone flies! It's fast. If you're hesitant to buy this phone because it does not have the SnapDragon 810 processor, don't be! I cannot tell that I am not using the current flagship but instead one step down. I may update this section when I get my OnePlus 2 in a few days.

Camera:
Absolutely splendid pictures! Best phone camera I have ever had, and beats most point and shoots I have ever used. Participating in the Debaets Devos race on Labor Day, I snapped some pictures in burst mode (about 5 pictures per second I estimate) of the riders from sixty feet away. These riders were going in excess of 25mph when I took the pictures, and I could zoom in on someone's face and be able to tell who the person was. I could zoom in on the wheels and count each individual spoke of each wheel on every bike. Low light performance is as great. The camera is easily one of the top few in the smartphone world.

Battery life:
Battery life is solid, not quite as good as the OnePlus One, though that phone has been plagued with battery issues since the release of CyanogenMod 12, so it has gone downhill recently. The LG G4 gets me through most of the day on a single battery. I wake up at 5:30 AM for work on a given weekday. Today, I finally had to swap my battery out at 20:30 in the evening, a full fifteen hours, with roughly three and a half hours of screen on time, various calls, reading plenty of articles using LTE, and a handful of other usage.

Extras:
I bought a micro-SD card and several spare batteries. It's nice to automatically put all photos on the SD card, and keep apps on the internal storage. Additionally, having the extra batteries is great! I leave one to charge overnight in the external charger I bought, while my phone charges. By the time I need to change it out at the end of the next day, I have one to replace it with, and I put the dead one in to charge for the night. It works great! The leather back has been holding up well through the first week, with about half of the time spent in an OtterBox Commuter case. I will update if it starts to show wear, etc. I thought the buttons on the back would be odd, but they are actually pretty natural. Difficult to take pictures with the volume buttons, but otherwise, it hasn't bothered me in the least. The curved display is neat, though the curve is not nearly as exaggerated as the G Flex.

Conclusions:
If you're looking for a new flagship phone, I would not hesitate to buy this! Especially for the price. I ordered my OnePlus 2 around the same time, though after using this for a week, I would not be surprised if I continue to simply use this phone over the 2. The only major plusses the 2 have is the stronger processeor, which I would likely not notice, and the fingerprint scanner, which I probably would rarely use. The 2 also has a worse display.

title: Please read if you value your purchase in the USA
text:
I don't start most reviews like this, but I feel like you need to read the negative first.

I live in the USA and I ordered this even though it said it had no warranty because I've owned more than my fair share of cellphones over the years and never had any problems, unless I caused them. I've also owned a number of LG appliances / devices and been very happy with them. This is the first time I've definitely been let down.

So, first, the problem: within three months of owning the LG G4 H815 unlocked phone, half of the screen would just randomly not work. Just to be clear, if I held the phone vertically (portrait mode), the right side of the screen would be black - the backlighting was working, but there would be no display. If I rotated the phone horizontally (landscape mode), then the bottom half of the screen would remain black. The only way I could get the phone to start working on that portion of the display again would be to start some heavy graphic program like a game, and let it sort of "warm up" the graphics chip or something (this is a theory - I have proof as to what's really happening). So basically I have a phone that I have to tinker with for 30 seconds to several minutes to get the whole screen to display properly. To be blunt, that really sucks. You don't want your phone to work 3 minutes from when you turn it on - you want it to work NOW. Here's the crazy part - the touchscreen still works perfectly - so you can't see anything, but you CAN tap on anything you know to be there. Super frustrating...

So that's bad, right? There's a problem with *something* - who knows what...but, this is the reason that I gave it a 2 star rating - I can't get the thing serviced anywhere! I contacted LG US hoping to be able to get it serviced - sure, it's out of warranty, but a working phone is better than one that doesn't work at all...I mean, if it costs $100 or maybe $200, maybe it's worth it. I contacted LG US and they said they don't / can't work on it...WHAT?! So now, I'm stuck trying to find some way to salvage this phone that I paid $400 here on Amazon.

I wish I had done my homework and known that it wasn't just that it wouldn't be warrantied, but that I wouldn't be able to do anything with it if something went wrong.

If the phone worked....
I would have easily given this a 5 star rating. To be completely honest, I love the phone. It feels good, the screen is gorgeous, viewing angles are wonderful, the camera is amazing, etc. You've probably already read all the reviews, seen tons of video reviews on YouTube, seen the top phones to own right now and the LG G4 is at the top of all those lists. It's an excellent phone. Sure it has the 808 snapdragon rather than the latest 810, and yes, the 810 is slightly faster, but the 808 is no slouch. It's been a killer good device.

So again, my star rating has to do with buying a phone that is completely unsupported in the US. I've contacted LG (several times) looking for SOMETHING I can do, but I'm not all that hopeful. To top things off, I bought two of these phones - one for me and one for my wife. Knock on wood, hers has been functioning without any issues...mine is basically useless. I'm sad. I love this phone.

title: Amazing Phone that Nails Just About Everything, But Dies Way Too Soon!
text:
[[VIDEOID:892d683f36a51e25d9fe23c244563d65]] [[VIDEOID:8a3aface73f5689496570b5665586cc0]] [[VIDEOID:88aaa610d26f272ecbbc966ad7c40351]] [[VIDEOID:8f2c0fde0be1db3383e7e976147064ad]] [[VIDEOID:5e1ed9eeaa9ec9988da167138b9cbdcc]] [[VIDEOID:751f29578f6e048ef651695024f96c51]] **4/16/16 IMPORTANT UPDATE TO MY ORIGINAL REVIEW**
After owning the LG G4 H815 for 10 months and absolutely loving it, I am sorry to say my phone died suddenly. A few weeks ago out of the blue it shut down, and when I tried to turn it back on it starts to reboot, then dies, then starts to reboot, then dies, etc. Some research online confirms this is a common problem with the LG G4 (called a "bootloop" problem), so common that the company has publicly acknowledged that it is a problem with the phone's motherboard and loose connections between some of its components. There is nothing the user can do to fix it. It must be repaired by LG. They will repair phones under warranty under certain conditions, but NOT for the H815 model if you purchased it in the US. This H815 phone is an international model that has no warranty when sold in the US. LG has refused to repair my phone and I am stuck with a $500 loss after 10 months. I would absolutely advise against purchasing this phone if you live in the US. If you live outside the US, I would contact LG to see if you will have any warranty coverage before purchasing. It is a real shame - such a great phone, but with a fatal manufacturing issue that renders many of the phones dead within 6-12 months. Please search this problem on the internet and consider carefully before buying an LG G4.
*************************************
ORIGINAL REVIEW
The LG G4 is an incredible phone. It gets so many things right - big but not too big size, expandable storage, replaceable battery, tremendous camera, high quality, thoughtful user interface - and very few things wrong. My video won't hit everything, but here are some highlights. Feel free to post any questions in the comments section, I'll answer to the best of my ability. Great phone!

title: Hardware problems even for 12/2015 manufactured devices.
text:
I purchased this LG G4 phone in mid-January 2015 and the manufacturing date printed on the phone is 12/2015. I believe the origin country is Taiwan from the labeling and accompanying material. A little over one month after receiving the phone, I plugged my phone in for the night and went to bed; in the morning I go to check my phone and the right-hand half of the screen is black. The back-light still works (slight glow to the black side of the screen) and the touch sensor still works on both sides, but there is absolutely no signal making it to the right side of the screen. This problem persists even after a factory reset and also during the boot sequence.

I called up LG, gave them the IMEI, and yes: there is absolutely no warranty on this device. This was not unexpected, as I assumed this risk when purchasing this particular international model. Still, I thought I'd give it a try as I had read some reports that people were able to receive warranty service.

As for the phone itself, it is really unfortunate that the hardware malfunction above dominates what would normally be a very positive opinion of this phone. This phone line has been plagued with hardware problems since the start, but I thought that by now they would've been ironed out. Most news of these hardware issues were for phones manufactured on or before October 2015. I guess not. Maybe it's a fluke too: one of my family members also bought this model of phone around the same time and hasn't had this problem.

Ignoring the dead screen issue, I really do like this phone. It is fast and responsive. The screen is (was) very nice and clear. The camera is excellent. I absolutely love the fact that the phone supports an SD card for external storage. I also really liked the case I bought (UAG) for this phone, as it gave it a very nice grip.

It's for these reasons that I did not give up on the phone. I bought an OEM replacement screen from a parts website and I'm happy to report that it was only a screen problem and that I can now use the phone. The total cost of the phone, with replacement screen, is still lower than buying one through a phone service company, but I had to spend an hour or so taking the phone apart to fix it.

Conclusion: Even in the 12/2015 manufactured models, the LG G4 still has hardware problems. The LG-H815 truly does not have any warranty service (as expected); be prepared to fix any problems yourself or via non-LG repair centers. Finally, it is unfortunate that these hardware problems have marred an otherwise excellent phone; this is why it is only receiving three stars.

title: Yes, the bootloop issue is real. Stay away.
text: I have owned the phone for 8+ months. One day, all of a sudden, the phone just freezes and reboots.  Once rebooted, the LG logo screen keeps rebooting and it never got further from that ever since.  LG has issued a recall on this phone citing a hardware issue causing the bootloop, however because there is no warranty on this particular variant model (H815), there might be quite a repair fee involved.  LG told me to submit a repair claim for the phone, but from what I have read on various sites for owners of this model, LG doesn't seem to honor variant models if you purchased this through Amazon. Moreover, it seems most owners will need to wait around 30 days before they are told that LG refuses to repair this model.  You are betting off being safe by buying a new LG G5 when it comes out WITH a full warranty.  I certainly learned my lesson on trying to be cheap on a new handset. It was fun for a few months, but LG certainly has a potential lawsuit on their hands by not recalling it.

title: A compact point and shoot camera is better
text:
The True Zoom will certainly win you gadget points with your geek friends, and if you zoom in when shooting you'll get much better quality than what you could get from your phone's camera. But compared to a *real* camera, I think the True Zoom mostly falls short, except for the convenience of seamless photo editing and uploading (since the photos go straight into your phone).

Here are the ways in which I think the True Zoom isn't really better or more more convenient than a real camera:
- Even when it's not connected to your phone, the True Zoom is wider and taller and just as heavy as most small real cameras.
- It also makes the phone as bulky as a small camera - but if you only use it when you need to, you must first remove your phone's case or "style mod" (backplate) - and then replace it later.
- The True Zoom's sensor is comparable to what you would find in any premium smartphone; many real cameras offer better sensors.
- Pretty much any camera has more settings and modes, letting you take better pictures (especially if you know what you're doing).
- It costs more than many cameras of equal or better capability and quality.
- It uses your phone's battery instead of having its own power source.

The True Zoom looks like a largeish compact point-and shoot camera with half the back sliced off to make it thinner. It's a bit plasticky/toy-ish looking but it feels very solid and well made. The power button, shutter button, and zoom ring are all where you would expect to find them on a real camera, and they work the same way too.

Although the similarity to a real camera is welcome, I think the designers went a little overboard. For instance the area surrounding the lens seems artificially wider to make the lens appear more substantial (adding needless bulk), and there's a grippy bulge on one side. It all encourages you to hold the True Zoom like a real camera, but there's no wrist strap and as a result I always was worried I was going to accidentally drop it (it didn't help that it felt heavy too - how heavy depends on which phone you have; the Moto Z Play and Moto Z Force weigh more than the skinnier Moto Z). I would have preferred if they could have kept it thinner around the edges so that I could still handle it the same way I handle my phone when shooting photos.

At any rate, the "Moto Mod" integration with the phone is slick and seamless. You just snap the TrueZoom onto the back of the phone (it's held on with strong magnets). If it's the first time you've used a specific mod, you also go through a few intro screens and maybe a quick update, and then you're good to go; every time you hit the True Zoom power button, it automatically extends the lens and starts the Moto Camera app.

The Moto Camera app adapts itself by showing different settings; there's a flash menu (on/auto/off), a shutter delay menu (off/3 sec/10 sec), and an "H" menu to select the mode (color JPEG, B&W JPEG, or color RAW+JPEG), and the scene (auto, sports, night portrait, background portrait, night landscape, landscape). I didn't try the HDR or panorama, ISO, white balance, additional scene modes, etc. but those were supposedly accessible via the icon that looks like a camera.

To check the photo quality I did a few test photos where I shot the same scene with the True Zoom and then with my Moto Z Play phone's built in camera (I didn't try to compare video or low light shots). Here's what I noticed:
- Time to first shot and shot-to-shot didn't seem very different from my phone's camera.
- The flash is more powerful than the phone's little LED, but there can be a long delay between when you press the shutter and when it fires.
- Until I zoomed a fair amount, there wasn't any noticeable quality difference between photos taken with the True Zoom vs. the phone's camera.
- A small push on the zoom ring causes a big change to the zoom level. That can make it annoying to get the zoom "just right" if you're trying to frame a shot.
- It's better for macro shots (close-ups); you can get closer and still stay in focus, and has a larger depth of field.
- Photos have slightly "cooler" colors compared to the phone's camera.
- It has optical image stabilization which will help reduce blur when zoomed, though I didn't try to test this.
(The last 3 points above may depend on your phone; the Moto Z and Moto Z Force have better built-in cameras than the Moto Z Play).

Here are some other things worth mentioning:
- It sticks to the phone much more strongly than the back plate; I doubt it would accidentally disconnect during normal use.
- There's no tripod mount, which makes the shutter delay timer setting kind of useless (but with only magnets holding the camera in place, using a tripod wouldn't be super secure).
- It's a safe guess that it uses more juice than the phone's built-in camera since it's got a real flash and a zoom lens motor (unlike some other Moto Mods, the True Zoom doesn't include its own battery as far as I can tell).
- It's not compatible with all camera apps; the instructions say "most"; for instance Z Camera worked fine but Open Camera kept saying "Failed to take photo".
- Sometimes it wouldn't work when the phone was charging, showing the message "Disconnect phone USB to use your Moto Mod".
- You can still switch to the phone's front camera for selfies.
- The phone's flashlight feature isn't available when the True Zoom is connected.

I think the True Zoom is a neat idea, but it seems expensive for what it offers (I paid $200). I ended up returning it since my little Canon Elph camera costs less, zooms further, has better photo quality, is just as portable, and doesn't run down my phone's battery. To get its photos into my phone so that I can edit/upload, I use this [[ASIN:B01KXWIHZY Cable Matters USB Type-C Dual Slot Card Reader]].

title: Good, Not Great
text: I purchased the camera mod new during a sale last year. As phone cameras use digital zoom (except if they have additional lenses) the chance to have an optical zoom feature and great image resolution was hard to pass up at that price point, so I felt it was worth the risk. I was always carrying around a phone and a camera so wanted to reduce bulk and this was another selling point for me. The pictures are good, the optical zoom is excellent, but beyond the zoom feature, the camera and software are generally featureless and disappointing. For its size, there is no internal battery, even the Moto projector (which is excellent) has an internal battery. I knew this about the camera so I do have an external power pack. Optical image stabilization when zoomed in is exceptionally poor, you have to be very still or shoot supported or you'll get blurry pictures. The magnets are "incredibly" weak for this size and weight of a Mod; the camera can easily slip from the mount causing the camera to reset just as you were trying to take a picture. In addition, pretty much each time I attach the camera mod I need to restart the phone just so the camera and phone can properly sync. This is annoying and a waste of time - between weak magnets and occasionally needing to restart the phone, there is much to be disappointed with this Mod. Low light sensitivity is also surprisingly poor given modern camera sensors, so the xenon flash is essential unless you are trying to get a night scene of some type. Bottom line, for the cost of this Mod spend a little more and get a decent Sony point and click if you want optical zoom, low shutter lag, and good image stabilization. Yes, you'll carry around two items again, but will maintain about the same overall weight and size ratio as the phone and the Mod.

title: Works Perfect - Great Mod - Highly Recommended
text:
Works perfect on my Moto Z Force. Crisp clean pictures. Quality is amazing. Could not be happier with this camera mod. Easy to use. Seems very durable and should last several years. Comes with a nice case to keep it clean and protected. It is nice and compact. It is worth noting that the max resolution output is only 12mp, but with such a crisp clear picture that seems to work great for me. It also uses about 3 times more battery than using the regular camera. After using it for about 5 minutes (picture taking and settings and just getting to know it) it depleted my battery about 5-6%.

As for whether you can use the digital zoom with this mod, there were a lot of "No" answers. Yes. Mine does. I am not sure if this is a feature added in a recent update of the Moto Mods software, or if it is just on the Moto Z Force, or if I just received an updated product (I just got mine yesterday (2/26/2017) but mine will allow me to use the digital zoom after the 10x zoom is at max, it allows me to go to 40x with the digital. One caveat though, while the mod is connected to your phone, swipe the viewfinder right on your screen and there is a setting "Use Digital Zoom". If you check this option, it will allow you to use the digital zoom, but only after the optical zoom has maxed out at its 10x. There is even a section in the "Adjust Settings" portion of the owner's manual for using the digital zoom feature (page 5).

Nice to also be able to adjust the settings within the Hasselblad to take Black & White pictures and Raw image format.

The optic lens automatically activates when the camera app is opened and automatically deactivates when the camera app is closed, or you can use the power button on the Mod itself.

I have attached some pictures for comparison. I am not able to attached the full scale pictures taken by the Moto Z Force (because they are about 12MB in size each), but in looking at these scaled down versions, since all are scaled down the same way, I am trying to show the difference between the stock camera vs. the Mod with full optical zoom to 10x vs. the Mod with full optic zoom to 10x combined with full digital zoom to 40x. These pictures were taken indoors with zero sunlight, only light source is an incandescent bulb between the camera and the paper. I measured the distance to be 12 feet.

So far I have not found anything I don't like about this Mod. Should anything new come up I will return to update this review, but as for now, it fits my needs perfect.

title: Supremely disappointing
text: After reading the reviews about the great quality of Hasselblad cameras and lenses, I wanted to try out this Moto mod. But I was really disappointed with it and the lack of thought and planning that went into the design was shocking.  I did manage to squeak out a few photos before getting hit by the inevitable software "upgrade".  The photos are really unremarkable from any cellphone camera other than the fact that you can zoom in which was fun for a few minutes.  Once forced into the software upgrade, it was no longer easy to start.  So the main problem is that it still uses the crappy Moto software and then overlays a few extra software features.  However the upgrade killed the easy snap on and use part of the camera and gave it a nagging "Camera Error Please restart camera" error.  And, no, it wasn't just restart the mod software, instead the whole phone had to be restarted.  Every time you want to use the mod.  And after you've left the camera a few times to view the pics in Google Photos, when you go back to use the camera you get the error again.  So by this time I'm just ready to carry a working camera instead of this non-working mod.  The mod has no battery like the speakers mods do, so it sucks down your phone battery in a few hours of photos.  It has no standard threaded mount so you can't put it on a tripod (or clamp it) which is critical when you zoom in or if you want to take evening/night pictures.  Also, though I loved the zoom rocker switch and the physical focus/shutter button, the mod was still more difficult and clumsy to hold while attached to my phone than the phone by itself and nearly fumbled it several times.  Did I mention that several photos still came out blurry and unfocused?  Incredible.  And not like there is a macro mode for taking close up pictures.  I think most of this is probably Motorola's fault rather than Hasselblad since it has to do with the functionality rather than the quality of the components.  The Moto camera by itself also has typical difficulty focusing on barcodes.

title: Not bad, but needs some work
text:
Motorola cameras have always been somewhat disappointing. They aren't the worst out there, but they are nowhere near as good as an iPhone or galaxy. This mod helps, but it needs some work.

The build and design are fantastic. You get a nice textured rubber grip on the side and metal all around the camera lens. I do wish there was a way of controlling focus by twisting the lens, but autofocus is usually pretty good. My only issue with the build is the zoom slider. It only has two settings; zooming a little too fast or not at all. I wish there was an analogue slider so I could control the speed of zooming better.

The camera performs well, as long as you use it in good lighting, or are willing to wait for a good low light shot. Images are sharp and detailed, and the colors look good without being overblown. The zoom is a lot of fun to use and works well. In low light, it doesn't perform as well. Colors can get washed out and there isn’t a lot of light let in. The flash really helps with that though. Its able to brighten up almost any scene indoors, but not outside. Unfortunately, there isn't a tripod screw for long exposure shots. Video looks good as well, with many of the photo qualities carrying over.

This camera certainly beats the pants off of the stock Moto Z camera, but it isn't perfect. For one, it can be slow to focus, especially in video mode. The depth of field is also a weak point, with the aperture going only to 3.5. Overall though, I’m happy with my purchase of this camera, I'd just like to see some improvements in a second generation. As to wether you should buy this, I'd say not unless you can justify the expense. At $250 this isn't cheap by any means, but it is far more convenient to carry around than your phone and a dedicated camera. If it comes down in price closer to $175-200, then I would say its worth it.

title: Must-have mod, ignore some negative reviews!
text: This is definitely a must-have mod for any Moto Z-series owner. First of all something rarely mentioned: the craftsmanship is superb. Hasselblad is one of those items with amazing build quality that  you just admire to have in your possession. The magnetic lock is so strong you will not worry at all about the mod coming loose. The camera is definitely worth it's price, especially now that prices have dropped. The image quality is great provided you have good lighting (due to it's small aperture).  Don't be afraid to use the flash indoors. Colors are just right - not saturated or washed out. The optical zoom provides plenty of reach with no loss of quality. 10x means you can take a full-screen picture of a remote object that is marginally visible with the naked eye. OIS is good and you take a stable picture even if your hand feels shaky in full zoom. It does not support HDR but does support RAW. This allows to import a lossless image in a 3rd party software and enhance with HDR or other filters if you're into professional retouching. My only "complaint" is  about the flimsy button. There's a half-press to lock the auto-focus, full press to take the picture, and continued full-press to fire multiple shots. There's not enough distinction between the three functions, so I sometimes mistakenly take a picture while I just planned to auto-focus, or take multiple pictures while I planned to take only one. You eventually get used to it but there's a learning curve.

My gps hardware failed after 22 days of phone ownership despite the phone having been well taken care of (lived in a case, never dropped). I reset the phone to default but the GPS still remained unresponsive and continuously redirected. I called asus for assistance and despite saying that it sounds like a hardware defect the agent refused to send me another phone (exchange the defective unit). Instead it was recommended that I rma the phone and wait 2 weeks for its return. I don't know about you but 2 weeks in a city where you don't know the roads without a phone or GPS doesn't work for me.

I continue to use asus for my pc hardware but their lack of common sense in dealing with a defective phone has turned me off to their mobiles.

Brand new phones shouldn't fail for no reason within 30 days and if they do issuing a replacement should be par for the course .

title: After being recently disappointed by Aukey, I am very pleased with this charger
text:
I have purchased a LOT of Aukey chargers over the past few years, but recently they refused to warranty a charger I purchased through Newegg even though it was still within their manufacturer's warranty.

I have also purchased a few other Amazon vendor multi-port chargers that did not quick charge my Galaxy S9 +

I used the same charging cables that worked with my Samsung and Aukey chargers, but the lower tier charges would only quick charge for literally a second before switching to normal charging.

I've purchased many Anker cables over the years and a few sets of bluetooth headsets too, but this is one of my first charging stations.

Size/Portability: the box was surprisingly small... the charger was even smaller. My old leather wallet us actually bigger! I was blown away. For a charger with such a small footprint, I see myself replacing my Aukey multiport charger with this for traveling and days I am working on jobsite locations.

Function: the charger immediately was recognized by my S9+ as a fast charger and topped it off quickly. Even when I charged my Aegis Legend vape, Galaxy S3 Frontier, Aukey headphones, my wireless charging stand, and an iphone.. the juice never stopped flowing.

First impressions : it's a great value, takes up little space, and the slippery surface of the body isn't an issue with the included adhesive pad.

Shipping : I ordered the charger around 2pm on a Friday, and an hour later tried to cancel the order so I could get the one with 2 fast charging ports so I could also use the Fast Charge feature on my wireless stand, but I was informed I couldn't cancel it. The next day before lunch I got a notification from Amazon and the charger was already in my mailbox!
I couldn't believe it arrived in less than 24 hours in our rural area. Pretty mind blowing!

title: What two years of design brings...
text:
It's been a while since I've gotten a new Anker charger, but I passed my old 5-port charger down to my daughter and used it as a perfect opportunity to take advantage of one of Anker's flash sales. I was quite surprised at how the 5-port charger has evolved after the last couple years! The quick charge is a great addition, I've had it in a travel charger as well as a car charger, finally getting it in my main office charger was a very welcome addition. It will put just about half a full charge on my Note 4 in about 30 minutes! Great stuff!

Anker's also taken some recent criticism to heart and given a thoughtful solution... they made it such a sleek and smooth design, it has tendency to slide around the desk. They include a 1 1/2 inch long piece of double sided tape. Their engineers are thinking!

The power cord that comes with the charger has been lengthened also, the new one was about 9" longer than the old one. It gives you a little better options in placing it behind desks, bureaus, and the like. It was cool to see the evolution of the same product that I'd purchased two and a half years ago. It looks great on the desk, even desks you're trying to keep clean, as it's design is something you don't actually need to hide.

With two years of sliding cables in and out of the charger slots, they never got loose and always charged. With the dependability I've had from my last 5-port charger, I will keep buying Anker.

title: Be aware of inaccurate product description
text:
I love Anker products, they are outstanding!!! But for this particular one, I dropped two stars... (1) The description of the product states that the ports are Quick Charge 3.0, but only ONE of the five are; the other four are not. If you do not pay attention to the pictures, as I did not, you would not know this. I own more than two dozens of Anker products, so since I trust the brand I just went to the written specs/description/details and ignored the product's pictures. By doing this I totally missed the fact that there is only one Quick Charge 3.0 port - I figured it out once I received the actual product. (2) There is no power button... I have two other models of Anker wall chargers and they do have a power button, which I love and much miss on this one... But, bottom line, the product is good, as all Anker products are.

I am not returning this product because now I see that the pictures clearly show that only one port is Quick Charge 3.0, but the info on the listing is definitely inaccurate. I am a victim of well planned marketing strategy... I would not have bought this particular charger if I knew that there was only one Quick Charger 3.0 port.

title: How do you not have one yet?
text:
Can not live without one of these. It charges my phones faster than the stock tiny bricks the makers give you, and it does them all from one outlet. Travelling without one is a nightmare once you have. Finding an outlet is difficult in airports even today (really, let's get on that people!), and then you do they're almost always broken, or taken up by a kid plugged in so he can play his games while waiting for his flight 3 hours from now. With this, I just swap out someone else's brick - with their permission of course - and I get USB power, they keep getting power but at a faster charging rate, and we even have room to spare to make more friends. Really no idea how these aren't in everyone's travel kit, or just on their desk.

In our RV I have one plugged in by the master bed taking up one outlet, and the box is velcro'd to the wall. We can leave cables in and charge my girlfriend's phone, my personal phone, my work phone, our tablet, and a fit bit at night and never have to worry about running out of spots or moving cables around.

title: Well made!
text:
In todays world there is no shortage of USB rechargeable devices. So having one AC plug that simultaneously recharges multiple devices is almost priceless. Anyhow, I've have a very positive experience with Anker products in the past and ordered their Quick Charge 3.0 51.5 W 5 port USB wall charger. First impressions is this device is sturdy and seems well built. It comes with 4 regular USB ports and one Qualcomm Quick Charge 3.0 port. This allows you to very quickly charge a phone that is compatible with Qualcomm Quick Charge. It will jump the charge up to 90% +/- in a flash and then slowly recharge the remaining 10%...but still quick. It was able to top off my phone from 80% to 100% in about 10-15 minutes as well as 2 standard Gopro batteries, to extended bacpack batteries.

Anker also includes a self adhesive double mounting 3m tape. I'm going to mount the charger under my desk just out of site but still convenient...the wall plug comes with a 3-6' cord allowing for this.

Eventually, the charger and its LED indicator would only work for seconds before cutting out.

I notified Anker of the problem. They had me do a few checks and get back to them with the results. They sent me a replacement within days and it has been working well for the last month or two. Only time will whether this one will outlast the original, but I am quite satisfied with the responsive service that I got from the company and will not hesitate to order from them in the future.

title: It could have burn my house thankfully it was only my hand.
text:
Please read this review before you decide to buy this item.

I have two reasons for not being able to write this review sooner. The first one being that I have two kids.

I was actually watching the T.V. when I smelled something burning. I checked the kitchen, the garage, and even open the back door to find out where the smell was coming from and could not find from where it was coming from. The smell went away and I decided to sit back to enjoy my movie when I noticed that my cell was low on battery. I go to my counter where I have the Anker quick charge connected to an Anker Powerbank battery charger and I grab my Anker powerline braided wire to connect it to my cell and I notice that the tip of the wire is partially melted. Right away I reached to the Anker Quick Charge to disconnect it and the charger was super hot I pretty much burn my hand as I removed it. This brings me to my second reason why it took me forever to write this review. I was looking for the braided wire where the tip melted to upload it for this review but I could not find it. I want to say I threw it away because I have other Anker braided wires and I did not want for me or my wife to damage my phone. Now due to all these problems that I had, a few weeks to a month later my cell phone was no longer charging and I had to get a replacement phone. Maybe previous charges from this device damaged my cell.

In Anker's defense I want to say that I do have their braided wires and they work fine. Unfortunately, I do not recommend this product to anyone. It was a good thing that I was there at the house if not things could have been worse. Like any good American, I am a person that when I charge my cell I tend to disconnect my cell from the powerline but leave the charger connected. I am out $27.70 for my Anker Quick Charger which I had gotten a lightning deal and I am out $9.99 for the braided wire for a total of $37.69. The Anker Quick Charge device itself lasted only a week to maybe two weeks.

I would not recommend this device!

title: Great charger with lots of power
text:
The Anker Powerport 5 with Qualcomm 3.0 quick charge is a elegant and powerful charger. As always with Anker, the design and packaging is top notch.

I needed a charger that would utilize the quick charge technology in my Samsung Galaxy S7, and still have enough power to keep my iPad topped off. This device has the necessary wattage to charge tablets and USB type c Ultra books at full speed.

The chipset inside the powerport 5 automatically detects the optimal wattage and amps that your device needs. It's kind of cool if you think about it. It has a mini processor inside that query's the device and then looks at a database to find the optimal charge settings

I also love the blue indicator light because it lets me know when a device is fully charged just by glancing at the charger. The light is subtle and not overly bright, and the finish on the charger is superbly well done.

Anker also included a high quality power cord.

I can definitely recommend this charger if your in the market for one. Quickcharge 3.0 will change your life!
