title: Nice Charger
text:
[[VIDEOID:b7982a33a6c52f07b93aec0418bb9528]] Amazon had the PowerPort Speed 5 listed as putting out 51.5W of power which is quite a bit for a 5 port USB charger. Anker says it's “MultiProtect” system provides surge protection, short circuit prevention, temperature control, and other safety features (10 total). It also has an 18 month limited warranty and lifetime technical support. Plus Anker has great customer service. Although I really don't hear of it being needed for anything but questions about their products so I'm thinking problems with their products are rare. I can say that from Ankers reputation and my own personal experience Anker makes dependable high quality products and I have no problem recommending them. When looking for Anker reviews you can expect to find thousands of reviews that tend to average around 4.5+ out of 5. If for some reason you decide you don't want to keep it Anker also has an any reason 30 day return policy.

Unfortunately I don't have devices with Quick Charge technology (yet) so I can't give the Qualcomm Quick Charge 3.0 technology a thorough workout (it's supposed to put out 3 amps according to Ankers specs.) The top port is the one with the Quick Charge technology and it is backwards compatible with older technologies so you should have no problem using it with any device. Fortunately all the ports are capable of monitoring and safely providing a fast charge of up to 2.4 amps (up to 6.4 amps max across 4 ports according to the enclosed literature) to Android or Apple phones, tablets or even camera's and other devices so I will definitely benefit from that.

Shortly after the product arrived I cut open the plastic bag and took the clear plastic off the product box. I looked over both sides of the box and found some product info on the back such the model #A2055111. Then I took the charger out of the box, took the protective plastic covering off it and pulled the accessories box out. Under that was a very basic welcome guide that says next to nothing which is fine because there isn't much to know. You just plug everything in and it charges your devices. The guide points out the warranty, gives input and output voltages and some common sense things like plug it in, don't drop it, don't put it in liquids, don't take it apart, etc.

The charger itself is made of plastic and has a fine matte finish on it which makes it a little on the slick side. There is nothing wrong with the finish. It didn't come scratched or damaged in any way but I would like to see Anker use a rubberized finish on it which would help keep it from sliding around easily on smooth surfaces without having to use the perminence of the sticky pad and it would give it a nicer feel.

In the accessories box is the cord, a cushioned sticky pad and an extra velcro strap to tie up the cord. Although I can't see myself needing an extra velcro strap it's a nice touch and probably useful for someone that travels all the time. Both are quality velcro so the one that comes on the cord should last a long time before needing the replacement, if ever. The cushioning sticky pad Anker supplies is from 3M so it will stick well and keep it from sliding around. The cord measured 62” long which is 5' 2” but it may seem shorter than that at first because it is a heavy duty cord and has some memory from being tightly bound up inside the box. Unfortunately, the lack of a rubberized finish combined with the memory of the new cord resulted in a phone and charger that slid off the table while charging and ended up on the hard tile floor, but no harm was done. I just need to keep the charger closer to the wall until some of the memory comes out of the cord. As I was about to post this I seen where one reviewer said he put a rubber band around it to keep it from sliding so I may try that. If you have a permanent place to mount this charger with the sticky pad the slick finish won't be a problem or you could put a rubber band or rubber feet on it. Another thing I found that works well to keep the charger from sliding is to make a coil in the USB cord and lay the charger on top of it. I have some Anker USB cords that have a nice rubbery covering which work well for this.

The specs from Ankers web site are as follows:
Input................................... AC 100-240V ~ 1.7A 50 - 60Hz
Quick Charge 3.0 Output... 3.6-6.5V=3A, 6.5-9V=2A, 9-12V=1.5A
Power IQ Output................. 5V=4.8A (2.4A Max Per Port)
Size.................................... 102 x 75 x 28mm / 4.0 x 3.0 x 1.1in
Weight................................ 205g / 7.2oz
It's nearly a half pound so it's not a cheap feeling device.

A little confusion cleared up:
One thing you will notice when it comes to the specs is that the Anker website says each Power IQ output has a possible max output of 2.4A Max Per Port @ 5V but the four ports cannot combine for more than a total max output of 4.8A. However, when you look at the specs on the included literature you will see that instead of a 4.8 A max across the four Power IQ ports it states there is a max of 6.4 amps across those ports. I called Anker customer support when I seen this and was told the 6.4 A max is actually across all five ports (includes the quick charge port). I asked if the quick charge port was using the max of 3 amps then would that mean the max available output across the remaining four ports would be 3.4 amps? (Up to a max 2.4 amps for a single port.) I was told this was correct. I do not imagine this would be a problem for the average user, but it is something you may want to keep in mind if you plan on plugging in a lot of high draw devices at once.

Anker's website also says the dimensions of the charger are 4.0” x 3.0” x 1.1” but the enclosed literature claims 3.3” x 2.6” x 1.1” so I measured it and came up with 3 1/2” x 2 5/8” x 1 1/16” (3.5” x 2.63” x 1.06”).

So how did the charger perform?
This charger charged my normally very slow charging Alcatel Pixie Avion LTE with a 1780mAh battery from 0-100% in 2 hours and 45 minutes. It also charged it three times from 52%-100% in 1:43 minutes, 1:47 minutes and 1:40 minutes. A little variance is to be expected due things like different signal strengths taking more or less power while the phone is charging. These may not seem like super fast charge times for a 1780 mAh battery, but for some reason this phone won't take a very fast charge. However, with this charger it charged considerably faster than normal.

I tried 6 different devices in total and the PowerPort Speed 5 seemed to adapt the voltages to each individual device. From a low of 5.07 volts (0.6 amps) on an SJ1000 action cam which was below the standard unloaded charger output of 5.11 volts to the highest voltage which was 5.27 volts (0.31 amps) on an SJ4000 action cam. My Anker USB power pack which drew the most current (1.77 amps) was also 5.07 volts.

All the ports were able to supply all the current draw I could demand of them with the devices I had on hand and my Drok USB tester could detect no voltage drop when I had four devices charging at once. So that is a good sign that it had plenty more juice in the box. If I get a device that can tax the quick charge feature of this charger I may update this review in the future, but for now all I can say is if you are one of those people that still use a 1 amp charger that came with your device or worse yet use the USB on your laptop to charge your devices then you will love a charger like this. It can make life so much easier!

The bottom line:
I really don't like the slick finish and at this price point I think Anker could have added a rubberized matte finish or included some stick on rubber feet, but other than that I think this is a great charger and it seems to do what Anker says it will. Overall I would have to give this product 4.5 stars if I could do so on Amazon due to the mistakes on the specs and slippery finish, but nitpicking aside I'm going with 5 stars on this product.

title: It's a good phone case to have
text:
I bought this case from ZTE's website for half off using their promo code. It's a pretty nice case for fifteen bucks with free shipping (It arrived within a weeks time).

Pros:
-It feels like quality material
-Huge clear opening to see info
-Interactive touch screen while the cover is closed
-Stylish
-The flip cover can be used as a stand when watching videos
-You can stand the phone vertically, and take some limited but nice photos in manual mode with a longer exposure time (The cover essentially acts as a temporary tripod, but not really).
-All the buttons and ports are accessible
-Nice rich metallic color
-The cover can be flipped all the way back with ease
-The cover can be used as a secondary protection to prevent screen cracks
-The rear camera will be protected due to the bulkiness of the case (When laying the phone on a flat surface, the camera will be about 1-2mm off the ground)
-The case comes with a 1 year warranty

Cons:
-The phone will be a bit bulky with the case
-No cut-outs for the entire speaker grills
-You won't be able to see the notification light due to the front cover blocking it

Neutrals:
-Capturing videos/photos may be uncomfortable while the cover is flapped open
-Not sure if the metallic color on the case will fade over time.

Overall, it's a nice case for all the features that you get with it. It's not the perfect phone case, but it was totally worth fifteen bucks. It's a premium case with very minor flaws that are forgivable.

title: This phone is tied for best snapdragon 821 device with the google pixel
text:
This phone is tied for best snapdragon 821 device with the google pixel.

It is blazing fast and consistent throughout all of the ui animations. One of the best things about the oneplus 3 has been the software updates. As a contrast to the oneplus 2, oneplus has been doing an outstanding job with software updates, usually rolling out 2-4 per month between the bet channel and the main channel. Which works as a great segue into the next point.

The beta program for this phone is awesome. They are constantly introducing new features that do not add bloat to the phone. For example, I think open beta 15 or 16 introduced a gaming mode, that would allow you to add apps to "gaming mode" during "game mode" there are no screen interruptions from messages and the hardware buttons are disabled so you can avoid those accidental button presses in an intense gaming session, which serves as another excellent transition point.

Gaming, this baby tears through every game that I have thrown at it, implosion, asphalt 8, everthing it handles with ease . I extremely rarely get any laggs stutters or hiccups. Gameplay is very consistent.

Charging is spectacular. Leaving my phone for 30 minutes supercharges the phone. I can get from 0-60+ percent in no time. It's faster than motorolla turbo charging, and faster than huawei's super charging. I've owned a moto z, huawei mate 9, and op3, the op3 chargers the fastest AND what's even more important, it stays at the lowest temperature..

The camera perfomance is above average. When compared to the other devices in it's category, the ZTE Axon 7, the Idol 4s, the Moto z play, the camera on the op3 is beyond all of them. It takes some solid pictures and some pretty good video. Recording at 1080/60fps produces very smooth looking videos. Shake isn't bad either, providrd you have remotely stable hands. However,, when you compare it to the Galaxy S7, Iphone 7, or the fantastic pixel, it falls a little short. But unless you are a very nitpicky person, you won't be able to tell too much of a difference.

With that being said, this is a fantastic device. The only other android devices I would recommend if you're concerned about performance would be the Google Pixel XL. It's really the only comparable phone in my eyes. But the op3 literally comes in at half the price new so..... You do the math lol.

I would definitely recommend this phone above anything Samsung puts out. It's not as pretty, but it is far more consistent and performs far better than Samsung does with their phones.

title: Nice, sleek case
text:
I'm extremely particular about my phone case evidenced by the fact that I ordered over a dozen cases for my iPhone 7 and returned all but 3. Like most people, I hate change when you're so comfortable with something like I was with my last iPhone. I had the same exact case for the 2+yr duration of having that phone. Just wanted to give a background sense of my point of view. Onto the pros, cons, and suggestions...

PROS:
++ Lightweight, sleek, minimal protection
++ Gunmetal color looks great with matte black iPhone
+ Volume & power buttons have great tactility
+ Ring/silent switch very easy to reach
+ Micro-dot engineered clear TPU prevents ugly watermarking on back of phone
+ Decently raised edges to allow for lay on table without worrying about screen or camera damage
+ Price is very reasonable/competitive

CONS:
-- Clear/smoke TPU is notorious for fingerprinting
-- Bumper is very slippery even with the tiny raised bumps ("enhanced grip"), though the back TPU has a nice feel/grip
- Bit loose in the edges despite bumper, which allows more dust to accumulate and show on back over time

SUGGESTION:
? Prefer buttons to be color of the bumper, silver, or black rather than the clear color that dirties more quickly over time

Of the three cases I'm keeping for my phone, this and the Spigen NeoHybrid are very similar and nearer the slim, minimal protection spectrum, whereas the Otterbox Symmetry is more towards the moderate portion. I do like (and sometimes dislike) all three of them for different reasons and still haven't settled on "The One", but the Anker Ice-Case Lite is definitely a solid competitor.

title: Still the best phone in 2020
text:
After using this great phone since 2016 I started looking for an upgrade. So much has changed since 2016. All the new flagships look like TV remotes because of the new aspect ratio (20:9 or 21:9). The result is you get a tall and narrow phone which does not help if you are browsing the internet holding the phone upright; you get a very narrow reading space and narrow keyboard. Another issue with the new phones is the fingerprint sensor which is under the display (unlike Mate 9 which has it on the backside). The under the display fingerprint sensors are much slower, may not work with a screen protector on and more difficult to reach compared to a sensor on the back.

Huawei mate has a 16:9 aspect ratio which is ideal for me for web browsing, reading emails etc. It is only 79 mm wide which is very easy to hold in one hand even though I do not have big hands. The maximum display brightness is close to 700 nits which is excellent. Other new phones like Samsung are advertised to have 1200 nits but that is only under the sunlight with automatic brightness setting. In other words you cannot manually reach that level of brightness.

The processor of Huawei Mate 9 (Kirin 960) is more than enough for daily tasks including web browsing, watching movies and navigation etc. The aluminum housing is also perfect. Unlike the glass housing the current phones use, aluminum is much lighter and keeps the overall weight of the phone light. The current flagships are around 210 - 220 grams unlike Mate 9 which is 190 grams despite the huge long-lasting battery. Huawei and other manufactures should start thinking outside the box and must realize that there is a substantial consumer segment who are desperately looking for 16:9 or 18:9 aspect ratio phones with bright displays which can be manually adjusted to go as high as 700 nits (just like iphones) and with ultrasonic fingerprint sensors on the backside of the phone right underneath where the index finger rests. For privacy purposes having a pop-up front camera would be great. Therefore, instead of manufacturing only one stereotype of flagship phone which looks like a TV remote and weighing 220 grams, the manufacturers should consider variations of that flagship with wider displays and other attributes which still make the Huawei Mate 9 the best available phone in 2020 at least for me.

title: Mid-range performance for rock-bottom price
text:
I bought this to replace my Zenfone 2 ze551ml. The ZF2's screen started failing, so I figured I had to buy a new handset, but didn't want to spend a lot on a new sim-free device. The Honor 6x fit the bill.

Compared to the ZF2, the Honor 6x is almost as snappy. Gaming-wise, look elsewhere as it will not impress - there's definitely lag when gaming. Then again, if you're considering this phone, you aren't looking for a gaming powerhouse anyway. You also don't need to buy a screen protector --- it comes with one installed right out of the box. The Honor 6x also feels like a high-end phone when held since it's a metal-unibody handset. Try finding that on another $200 phone.

As soon as I finished the initial setup, the phone prompted to update to EMUI 5.0, which is Android Nougat 7.0. The update was about 2.x GB. Some folks are complaining about a drop in performance, but my handset never had that. In fact, I find it faster. The settings menu also got an overhaul and more options are available at your disposal. A tip, though: DO NOT CUSTOMIZE YOUR HONOR 6X'S UI IF YOU PLAN TO UPDATE TO NOUGAT. Install the update first, then customize the look and feel of the phone later.

The LCD display is nice. You'll also be able to choose the screen's color temperature if you find it too "cool" like I did. Audio quality-wise, calls, music, and videos all sound clear. The fingerprint scanner is QUICK. Unlocking the phone via that method is almost instantaneous. I can't say much about the camera as I have yet to test it. But for low-light shoots, the photos lose some detail as far as I can tell. There isn't much bloatware either, which makes it clean. Love the battery performance --- out of the box, with 54% capacity, it drained to only 43% after I downloaded apps, synced e-mails, personalizing the settings, and transferring files between two phones. That's with around 2.5 hours of screen time. Color me impressed. As for connectivity, the modem is pretty solid. No matter where I go, I always get full bars, and compared to the ZF2, LTE performance is way better.

Overall, for a handset that's around $200, I love it. Again, not a gaming powerhouse, but for everything else, it gets the job done.

title: A heartbreaking work of staggering genius
text:
This review I mean, not the phone.

If I would have written this review withing the first week of owning the phone, I probably would have given it 5 stars.

"It works just like any Samsung for 1/4 the price!" I'd naively tell my friends and acquaintances. But you wonder how they can make and sell it for that price, kind of like when you meet a super hot girl, and you're like "How are you still single?!?!" and then once you're committed you quickly find out exactly why she's single.

The cons:
- This phone doesn't have visual voicemail. That's right, I have grandmas making fun of me as I CALL my voicemail and type in my password (1-2-3-4), and then wait as the robot lady says "You have 3 unheard message," but I'm pretty sure I already heard 2 of them. Don't forget to keep a notepad with you because if you don't write down the callback number, you have to wait for the message to finish and then start alllll over again.
- The Bluetooth doesn't work too well. It took me longer than it should have to connect the phone to my car, and I couldn't multitask because the car doesn't let you do it while driving. Ever heard of a passenger, Toyota? Anyways, that's the subject for another review. Actually my Prius is great, 5 stars. Anyways, the Blutooth works okay after that, but don't you dare try to connect more than one Bluetooth device or things are going to go downhill really quickly.
- Group texting doesn't work most of the time, regardless of whether there's an Apple device in the group or not. So I get a text from Jim that I know, based on context that it was sent to more than one person, but I don't know who, and I can't ask because he's getting mad at us for leaving work early.
- The camera is okay, but when you zoom in it looks like everyone and everything is made of little squares. Look, Huawei, maybe that's appealing to your Minecraft fans, but do I look like I play Minecraft? I'm a 27 year old man for heaven's sake. I prefer other types of crafts, like Starcraft, and scrapbooking.
- I can hear people okay, except when I talk to my wife, who has the same phone. So maybe that just means the mic is bad. And I don't want to think that every time I'm talking to Carl, he just doesn't know me well enough to say "Come again?" 4 times after everything I say, so he just does that thing where you say "yeah" and chuckle a little, like you understood the person. Carl's the new CEO. It's probably good for my very unstable employment that Carl likes me, but can he even understand me, and if he can't, how will he ever know how smart I am? Anyways, I guess that's not an issue, I've never spoken with Carl. But he could call any time, you know?

Other than that, it's basically any other Android, the battery lasts a long time, and the price is great, but I kind of wish I would have just spent a few hundred more dollars so I don't pay in sadness every day.

Stay frosty.

-Steve

title: Submerged in saltwater 15 min. Still works!
text:
I am so happy, I had to share what happened.
Fishing on a dock in Florida, Indian River (ocean saltwater). Phone on the floor. Pushed it with my foot and it slipped between slats. I watched it disappear in the murky salt water. I thought that was all. Desperate and frustrated about all the info I'm losing, not feeling like fishing any more, I grab my gear and walk back to the house we were staying in. My wife insists we go look for it to recover the card at least, we go back, check the water depth and it's just waist deep, I calculate where it landed, and I find it in the mud, feeling for it with my feet. Total of 15 min submerged. I have a regular case and screen protector, nothing special or waterproof. At least I have the sim and SD card, if they still work, I'm thinking...
On the way back to the house, the screen lights up! Damn, I'm thinking, rice bag or something! Long story short, we got on Youtube, opened the phone with a credit card, removed card and sim, drove 5 min to windixie and got an eyeglass repair kit with small screwdriver, disconnected all parts, and used a hair dryer on it. It basically took it 1.5 days to come back to life. The affected parts were the usb charging port (cleaned at home with electronics cleaner spray), and the side buttons. The buttons didn't work at all. Got home, removed them (youtube video with simple disassembly), sprayed them with electronic cleaner and let dry. Put it back together, but the power button was dead. 5 hrs later, I saw that the phone kept on restarting by itself, so I assumed it was the power button making random contact. I was right. Right now, everything works perfectly. All 3 buttons, speakers, charging. Screen completely unaffected.
So, yes, it is VERY water resistant!
UPDATE: after 2 days it became clear that the power button was broken. It was working on and off, and rebooting the phone all the time. Ordered an $8 button flex strip (used) from ebay, replaced in 10 min, and everything is as good as new :)

title: Solid phone overall, wish Huawei would stop trying to improve on stock Android, because THEY can't
text:
Update:

I don't think I would change much from my previous review but the only thing to emphasize is the software can wear on your patience. It's not to the point of bricking the phone but you can just tell the software just isn't really ready for prime time. But it's cheap enough so I guess it means that happy spot where people like me want a cheap phone and can take some buggy software.

________________________________________
Great specs, yet as others say about EMUI, the software lacks. A number of apps require a restart to operate after I download them from the play store. Never had that problem with other phones. Some apps act like they are still downloading or installing but are actually complete seeing as how just a restart was needed. I can't find the icon or the Installed notification until a restart. Odd.

I use the Google Now Launcher because I don't like the EMUI layout either. There are so many EMUI defaults on this phone and it keeps asking me about HiVoice. Just go away!

Colors can be funky (washed out is the term someone used) but there are display settings that can make the colors warmer or colder, helping that out. You can also have nightime settings where the display takes on a yellow tone to be easy on the eyes. I like that.

I wish we could double tap the phone to turn on/off the screen. I couldn't find a decent app for it. Not much of the fingerprint fan maybe mainly because it's on the back but there are the pattern and some other options to unlock the phone... But they take longer.

Some other things are annoying like the notifications or slide down from the top to see 'shortcuts' and notifications, especially that it covers the whole screen when doing that. Just stop trying to improve on Android, because you're doing the opposite!

After tweaks that I think many people do, I'm pretty happy with the phone. I might throw the dang thing through the wall if HiVoice asks me anything again though.

title: Honorable Mention
text:
For the price, the 6X is a real good buy. The phone really works well and it does everything you would hope for, and more. It has tons of customizable options and adding the fingerprint sensor is a real nice touch. If you are someone who really puts emphasis on a phones camera (like myself), then this phone really is for you.

The Honor 6X has a 12-megapixel camera on the top and a 2-megapixel image sensor on the bottom. The dual cameras allow for brighter, more detailed photos and videos, and a wider color capture. The camera works wonders when there is enough light, the pictures come out crystal clear and very detailed. The only downside is the shots may become a bit grainier in low light. You can activate HDR and night modes to alleviate the graininess but it wont help much which makes taking pictures at night can be a bit of a challenge.

Battery life is solid, averaging about 5-6 hours with heavy usage. In regular stand-by mode, you can get up to 2 days worth of use, not bad off of 1 charge. If you want to get even more life out of your battery, then accessing the built in battery manager is a must. It allows you to reduce the power drainage caused by apps running in the background. There's even a nifty alert that warns you when background apps are consuming too much power.

The unlocked GSM phone comes with LTE bands 2/4/5/12/20/38. I have T-Mobile as a carrier and the phone showed strong network performance. The only downside is that you cannot use Wifi calling with ANY unlocked GSM phone because that feature is only available to T-Mobile Phones. Even without the Wifi calling feature, the call quality is very good. Calls are crisp and clear with the phone working particularly well in troublesome areas like basements. I wish all phones worked this well.

title: Not Cheap, All Quality.
text:
***The 7x With 6in 18:9 Display Is Now On Amazon Pre-Order And Begins Shipping On Jan 25 For $200! Similar Specs, More Screen And Unibody, Too. Go For It!!!***

This is a very good device. I was looking for a new phone because the screen of my entry level LG X Power was cracked to hell. My budget of around $100 had me looking at yet more budget phones from my carrier. 16 gigs of storage, 2 gigs of RAM, larger but mediocre screens, average chipsets, plastic build all around. I shopped here and stumbled across this phone for $200 and thought it a good deal but still twice my phone budget. Came back a few days later and stumbled upon a Flash Sale that saw this phone priced at $150 for $30 dollars a month on my Amazon card and considering all the strong reviews I thought it a no brainer purchase.

So glad I got it. Even at $200 regular price it is totally worth it in my opinion. It is a top quality product in its midrange segment. I am not tech savvy with phones so will keep this simple. It has a very good screen with high resolution and good pixel density. Colors are accurate and well saturated. Photos, video, and text are very clear and sharp. The screen appears three times brighter then my X Power at 100% brightness. Battery life is formidable, out gunning my old phone even though that phone has a higher capacity battery. After 5 hours of onscreen time and various app usage at 100% brightness the phone was still at 25% battery life from 100%. It does not have a quick charger but its high capacity battery charges fairly quickly nonetheless. From 15% with the included "brick" charger the battery was at 65% in under an hour and ready to roll again.

It feels quality right out of the box. The rear cover (it is not unibody as some have said) is made from aluminum and feels good in hand. The phone has a substantial feel to it. The android OS mated to Honors own UI operates fluidly and apps open and run smoothly. The look and design of the phone has nothing cheap about it and while it is not a high end or premium design it won't embarrass itself beside the typical iphone, etc. It looks nice and does not look like a pig wearing lipstick. Indeed it is attractive in its own right. You can hand this phone over for use to anyone and they would think "feels good, looks good." If it were a car it wouldn't be a 7 Series BMW but hey, a 4 Series is nothing to sneeze at.

The camera is very good, and great in its segment. Lots of functions and features I have not even explored yet, but shots taken out of the box in all manner of lighting conditions are of good quality, clarity, and color so far.

Call quality is very good and I noticed this difference immediately. No matter what sort of phone the person on the other end is using I can hear them clearly and without muffling or breaking up. Even if they are whispering. Unlike all the entry level phones I have used where I seemed to always be saying 'I can't hear you' and 'I can't understand what you are saying' with this phone I can hear the person talking almost as if they are sitting beside me.

Connectivity has been excellent be it data, wifi, or bluetooth. Always strong and well connected with no "drops" or hiccups.

That's about it. If I knew then what I know now about this phone after a week of usage I would have happily paid full retail for it and felt it a very good deal. It is "budget" only in price in my opinion. I will never go back to entry level phones again and may even stay loyal to this brand after learning more about the company and it's products. If you have doubts just research Huawei / Honor on the internet. Huawei is a major player in the global marketplace and competes very well in the flagship phone market. Honor is their sub brand used to sell high quality midrange phones. A Chinese company, yes. But don't be mislead by that. This is not a "knock off" brand or maker of cheap, disposable products. This is the real deal, folks. And if looking to "move up" from entry level in my opinion, at this price point and for what you get, is hard to beat.

Oh, and it's unlocked. Which means when you get your service you get it without carrier branding or bloatware. You just get the phone / data service. The software installed remains unchanged and unaltered, which makes the phone feel more personal and uncluttered. It's a nice phone.

Camera-Camera is frustrating as hell. I remember trying to take a picture, and usually, you would tap the screen to take it. This one, when I tapped the screen multiple times, it gave me mode after mode. I was so freaking frustrated and cussing at it.

Battery-People might view this as being picky, but 2% battery is NOT empty. Yet the phone shuts off around there. It shows you the battery is defective. I had a Motorola that on its last legs would indicate the battery being empty at around 15%. Is the 2% shut off a sign of battery issues with this phone in the future? I'd bet on it.

title: Support is Terrible, Don't Expect Your Warranty to be Honored
text:
This is my first Huawei phone. I've had this phone for a little under a year. Everything about this phone is great, but the reason I'm giving it a one star is due to the terrible support from Huawei. The phone comes with a limited year warranty that states that my phone will be covered if there are: "inferior workmanship, materials, and design" issues. Recently, my rear camera glass shattered while in my pocket. I must have leaned up against something at just the right angle. I'm surprised to see how weak the glass is on the back camera. I've heard that it isn't gorilla glass. What's more surprising is that my phone had a case on it.

When I contacted Huawei about it, they said my phone is under warranty but the warranty doesn't cover physical damage. So, even though it covers inferior workmanship, design, and materials (which sounds like it would cover physical damage if the person wasn't at fault,) it will not cover your phone being damaged due to these three issues. Fortunately, the rear camera glass is easy to remove and the replacement part costs about $5. I still feel like it should be their responsibility. I wish we lived in the days where warranties were honored and you don't feel like you're on trial every time something bad happens to a device under warranty.

Anyway, it's left a negative impression about this company in my mind. I will not be buying from Huawei again.

title: Generally good, but some  software issues and poor support
text:
I have had this phone for about a month and use it as my main phone. The screen is bright and legible in sunlight with the auto ambient light feature generally working well. The fingerprint sensor works very well. Sound quality is very good. The phone easily lasts more than a day, seems more like two. Build quality is very nice. My only real issue is the built-in email program. You have the option of seeing the mail from one account at a time or all of them at once. I keep choosing the latter, but the program keeps defaulting to the former. I could use the Gmail program which would solve this, but i don't want Google reading through my mail. There is a very helpful guy online [webcazine] who answers questions about the honor 8 which generally apply to the honor 6 as well and he says that the email program is supposed to remember the last choice and keep it. So this appears to be a software bug. And i have not been able to "cast" the phone screen to my TV even though I have a ROKU which is supposed to be miracast compatible and this phone is supposed to have miracast from what i can tell. And there does not appear to be a full product guide for the honor 6, although they have guides for the honor 8. These last 3 reasons are responsible for only giving 4 stars instead of 5. I will say that the online and phone support is open 7 days a week with almost no hold time and they try to solve your problems. In general I am impressed that this phone is a great value. If it was waterproof it would be perfect.
** After 5 months
This phone is not a good as I thought and I am removing a star. Two problems have arisen. First, my Garmin stopped connecting to my phone about 2 months ago. Garmin seems to have done their due diligence by keeping me informed about the problem after I contacted them and the sending me an email telling me that the problem had been solve, working with Huawei engineers (the problem was not just with the Honor 6 but all Huawei phones), but that the fix would need to come from the Huawei side. Perhaps it was just passing the blame, but calls to Huawei were not informative. They were answered but the Huawei spokespeople (who are easy to reach but less informed that I would like) would neither confirm nor deny that they knew about the problem. They told me that an upgrade would fix the problem, without saying when an upgrade would occur, and since they didn't indicate that they even knew about the problem I do not believe that they could have known that an upgrade to fix it was coming. This was very disappointing. One of my reasons in getting the phone was to have more compatibility than my prior Windows phone, and using the phone with the Garmin vivoactive was an important consideration because the windows phone had only mixed compatibility with the Garmin. Right now, there is zero compatibility between the phone and the watch.
The second problem is that the fingerprint reader stopped working. After cleaning it off and reinstalling my fingerprint, it is working again, but I wonder if I will need to repeat this every 3 or 4 months.

title: A Great Phone (Or Secondary Phone) at a Great Price!
text:
So I'll start off and let you know how i got here and how I came to purchase this phone.

I had a Note 7 on Verizon. After the first recall, got another Note 7. Held out with my second Note 7 until Verizon hotlined the Note 7 in late January rendering it essentially useless (redirecting outgoing calls to Verizon customer support).

So with my phone useless, Verizon didn't help me at all, instead wanting me to upgrade and in the process lose my upgrade. So not wanting to waste my upgrade on a device from last year, I purchased this Honor 6X and switched to AT&T while I wait for the new Galaxy S8 to come out.

When I first started using the phone, I couldn't believe how good it was for $250. Huawei is increasingly making more and more quality devices. I also have the more expensive mid-range Honor 8 which I got on sale for $280. What a great phone that is for the price I got it at.

Display:

While the screen is not 2K or AMOLED like my Note 7, it's still a very good 1080P panel. It seems to get pretty bright and the colors seem fine to me.

Performance:

Equipped with the HiSilicon Kirin 655 and 3GB of RAM, I haven't noticed really any slow downs or stutters with this device. In all honesty, it seems just as fast and smooth as my Note 7, believe it or not. It seems like Huawei included a pretty potent processing package for this device.

Software:

Took me a little while to get used to it coming from TouchWiz. It has a different style but is still functional. It ships with EMUI 4 which is based on Android 6.0. I was kind of disappointed it didn't ship with EMUI 5.0 on Android 7 but the update is coming (hopefully soon).

Gaming:

I don't really do any gaming on mobile so I can't really speak to it's performance in this area.

Camera:

The camera seems to take pretty good pictures. Of course it's no comparison to the sensor on the Galaxy S7s or Note 7. The only thing I really don't like is the time it takes to get the camera to focus to take the picture so I don't always get the picture I'm wanting at the time. When you take a picture the phone says "Hold device steady to sharpen".

Battery:

The battery life on this phone has been amazing. The Honor 6X packs a 3340mAh battery. Only having to push a 1080P panel instead of 2K really contributes to this devices longevity.
I do a lot of texting and listening to music and can go all day and not get past 80%.

Other:

I don't really don't like how it's equipped with the increasingly outdated micro USB. I would have preferred a Type C but really shouldn't complain at this price point.

Conclusion:

I think this is a great budget device. $250 is still a decent amount of money to pay for a phone, but I think this would be a great back up phone granted you use a GSM carrier. I plan on using it until the Galaxy S8s come out and will keep the Honor 6X as a back up.

title: Buyer be aware - May not work in your area
text:
The posting does not list the most important spec - LTE bands.

Honor 6X has Global Version, USA Version and India Version. The seller does not say it is USA Version although it does say the phone carries USA warranty. Some buyers report the phone supports Band 12. Chances are it is a USA Version phone since Band 12 is only available on USA Version. If it is the case, the phone will not work well outside the US.

Global Version: LTE band 1(2100), 3(1800), 7(2600), 8(900), 38(2600)
USA Version: LTE band 2(1900), 4(1700/2100), 5(850), 12(700), 20(800), 38(2600)
India Version: LTE band 1(2100), 3(1800), 5(850), 7(2600), 8(900), 19(800), 28(700), 40(2300)

I travel to Japan, Hong Kong, Taiwan, China and other countries. This phone will have limited reception in China but no reception in the other countries. If you travel quite a bit like myself. This is not the phone for you.

The cameras are just great. Rear camera takes amazing pictures in daylight and with the flash. Low-light pictures are better than most phones well into the $300 price range. Front camera is good enough.
The phone is very quick. I've not experienced any lag in any app and the phone will reboot in under 10 seconds.

Cons:

It's difficult to make photos save to the SD card. Switching the default storage location to the SD card in Settings seems to cause some apps to glitch out, so it may be best to use a third-party camera app that has the option to chose the storage location.

title: Great phone, great quality, and best value for your money!
text:
Straight to the point, this phone is awesome! Coming from a Nexus 5, the Honor 6X has so far exceeded my expectations. I'll leave the long technical bits to the other reviewers - the short story is that they are true and this phone is meeting my everyday needs. I don't play too many games on my phones (i use my computer and tablets for that) so I can't speak to that, but from a productivity standpoint, this thing rocks. The battery is extremely impressive. With moderate to light daily usage, I can get 2 full days out of this. Apps are fast and responsive and call quality is 100% better than my aging Nexus 5.

I bought my wife an Honor 5X (last year's model) late last year. That's a great phone as well. The most common complaint with that phone is that it lags a bit if you try to push it too hard, particularly with Google Maps. That has been completely alleviated with the 6X. No lag whatsoever - it's completely responsive and it's just gorgeous to look at and hold.

From a performance standpoint, this phone is right on the mark for most users. The camera is pretty decent and the fingerprint sensor is extremely fast. Unless you are an extreme "power user" (how hard can you really push a phone anyway? Isn't that what desktop computers, laptops and tablets are for?), this phone is going to meet the needs of 99% of most users. Highly recommended. You can't go wrong for $250. The extra money (compared to the 5X) is worth it. Plus you'll get Android N soon (I don't believe Huawei has plans to upgrade the 5X to Android N), so that's a big bonus as well.

The Emotion UI is not bad. I didn't think I'd like it but it's very intuitive and within an hour or so, I was already used to it. I find that the most complaints about it are really just an indication that people are stuck in their ways and used to their previous phone, whatever that happens to be. I say get over it people! Show some intelligence and learn it! Just like everything else in live (new car, new shoes, new whatever), you'll get used to it, I promise. After all, how did you get used to your last phone? By using it, period. Before you know it, it'll be second nature and you'll be comparing your "next" phone to this one.

The only "complaint" I have (and it's not worth a whole star) is that the notification LED is much dimmer than the Nexus 5. Not a deal breaker for me. It could be a bit brighter, but it's all good.

title: Good phone. Definitely worth the money.
text:
So I've had this since my birthday at the beginning of December and it's been my favorite phone so far, and for 150 bucks it's the cheapest smart device I have. I've had friends who just bought a new phone too got for 500+ and they looked at mine and really liked it. They're are features on this phone by default I haven't seen on others like screen recording, cool photography effects like light painting, and the OS is great being a mix of apple and Android. It's never gotten hot while playing games or watching video and it's pretty speedy and definitely powerful enough to play some hefty 3d games. The OS is incredibly stable and I've never had my phone freeze doing routine tasks. It did freeze that one time I picked invalid video settings for urquan HD but it recovered quickly and worked just fine after. I was really skeptical about this phone when I got it but knew the bf did his research before buying it. And I'm not horribly concerned if it breaks or is stolen in a few months because it's nothing compared to breaking or losing something like an iPhone X or the latest Samsung.
And while the phone isn't water proof or I assume even resistant, I would never trust to have a phone that claims so considering I've heard of failing usb ports and speakers because of salt water. I'd rather just keep my phone away from water.
It looks and feels solid but I still got a hefty case to protect it. I assume that stepping on it or dropping it on concrete would be the end of this device unlike my friend's 4 year old Samsung she dropped several times and only finally damaged the screen. Luckily I'm just very careful with all my devices in the first place.
As of now I still can't find anything really wrong with it. I can't even complain that the fingerprint scanner is hard to reach if I've got my phone on a table because I had the same problem reaching the front scanner on the iPhone when I was holding it a certain way with my small toddler-like hands. And I'd think 2 scanners would just be Overkill. I'm writing this review on my phone right now and the Swype action on the Google keyboard is fluid and fast. I tried all the other keyboards and they all work similarly quickly which was an issue I was having on my Kindle. Sometimes it wouldn't Swype properly because the Kindle was extremely slow as if something was draining its resources.
Also I didn't think I'd like having such a ginormous phone for my hands but it's actually a good size and haven't had trouble gripping it even with the thick case over it.
While I've had trouble getting Bluetooth mic to work with this I can't even say it's the phone because my computer won't recognize the Bluetooth mic on any of my headsets and that is running win 10 but the phone did come with a nice set of earbuds with mic and controls and they work very well. So again, I'm not complaining.
So I better not have jinxed myself and I hope the phone doesn't explode or stop working or end up in a never-ending boot cycle but for now I'm really happy with it.
And the battery life is awesome. I got a aibocn 8000 backup and never need it. My phone rarely goes under 60% during the day and I am at work 11 hours and have a lot of time to play on my phone.
150 bucks. Not even my shield and my Kindle were that cheap.

title: Totally worth the money!
text:
I'm tired of spending $1000 on a phone so I opted to try something new. I was skeptical, but that has gone away now. After 2 weeks of use this phone has proved to be more than worth its cost. I know, its only 2 weeks, but I had to return the Xperia L1 from Sony after 8 days due to extremely poor performance and the apps not updating even though I had ample space.

First off, kudos, Huawei, for including the screen protector. I almost peeled it off thinking it was the protector only like Samsung and Apple do, but its actually a full blown protector. I see no need to peel it off as it does its job as good as any aftermarket. It is not tempered glass, just the basic plastic one, but it still kept me from having to look for, and buy, one. This phone has 32GB of internal storage. Not an issue since I have a 128GB SD card in it and most of my apps are installed there. Pictures also save to this card so I'm not worried about running out of space and apps update just fine. With everything I have installed I'm using 15.2GB of the 32GB and I don't see that becoming a problem. I really like the mobile+wifi connection. I haven't had an issue with it yet. The UI is good. Smooth. I did opt to delete some of the Huawei bloatware. I use the Gear S2 paired with this phone and it works quite well so I didn't need Hauwei's health app. There were a few other apps that weren't for me, but you might like them so I won't try to taint your own opinion. They all work, by the way, just not something I would use. The BT connection works every time. Call quality is great. The build of the phone is a little sub-par, but I always have my phone is a case so this isn't a big deal either. I noticed the bezel down by the charging port wasn't held together very well and would make a creaking noise when I touched it. It took a while to figure it out, but, in the case, I don't hear it anymore. The GPU could be a little better. Its not terrible, mind you, and it will play your games. I spoiled myself with the top tier phones so, of course, something is going to be of lesser quality. I mainly play Star Wars Heroes and it works well, There are certain instances where it takes a little bit longer to load but, again, I'm just spoiled. Don't let that deter you from this great bargain. Ford SYNC connects every time and the audio sounds great, even with BT speakers. I really enjoy the finger print sensor on the back and all of the things you can do with it. I've found it to be a natural finger placement and manipulating pictures and menu's with it works well. The display looks really good. I'm actually more impressed with the image quality so far. I haven't taken many pictures so I can't comment on the camera, but others say it works well. I haven't had any issues with charging or the battery. The battery is impressive, actually. Even playing Heroes I get an easy days use from a single charge. If I didn't play that game so much I'm positive it would last a lot longer.

All in all, I would have no qualms with recommending this phone to anyone. If you're a name brand snob (like I used to be) you should give this a try and you'll quickly see how much money you're throwing in the toilet by buying into the hype of big brands. I'll try to post another update after a few months of use. I'm hoping this holds up as well as it is now.

text: I'm just a couple days into using this phone, but so far I love it. I'm moving on from my Droid Turbo 2 and found this on sale for $189.99. How bad could it be is what I first thought. Well to answer my question, this phone is everything that my Turbo 2 is. First out of the box it prompted me to hook up to my wifi and then proceeded to ask if I wanted to update to 7.0. After updating I was surprised at the pre-installed apps (bloatware) or the lack of it on the phone out of the box. I've bought some "cheap" phones and there have been a TON of bloatware on them. But not on the Honor 6X. The thing with these pre-installed apps that blew my mind is that you can actually removed the apps you don't want. Battery is amazing so far. The EMUI is not too intrusive and actually works well. The processor speed and RAM make for a great combination. No lag here. The camera is one of the best I have ever had on a cell phone. This thing takes killer photos. Bluetooth works well and when I stream music to a Bluetooth device, it shows the cover art on the lock screen and gives the option to skip or pause the track. The screen display isn't as vibrant as my Turbo 2, but it's definable not atrocious. Thus far, i'd recommend this phone to anybody who is looking for a good phone under $200. Phone only connects to wifi at 2.4ghz; whereas most phones nowadays can also connect at 5ghz. The 2.4ghz wifi connection give you greater distance, but 5ghz can support higher speed.  If you are in a location with public wifi, and they are transmitting on 5ghz, then you won't be able to connect. title: Huawei damages phone and will not repair
text:
At first my experience wasn't so bad. My phone’s camera stopped working, so I called customer service on the second or third of October, and they emailed me a label to send in my phone to get it fixed. A couple of weeks later, I got my phone back...but it wasn't fixed. I called them after I found that out, and they told me that the repair center said they were unable to replicate the issue and that the damage was not present. At that point, the camera was even worse, and the phone came back without my screen protector on it. They told me that they would email a shipping label to get it fixed (again). I had to keep calling, eventually contacting them seven more times in the span of two months, trying to get the shipping label because I never got one and still wasn't getting one. I finally got a shipping label from them. During this two month span, I didn’t use that phone, and it was collecting dust in my desk while I used a temporary one until everything got fixed
This is where things got bad with Huawei service. I got my phone back for the second time on January third (three months after I first tried to get it fixed). I was excited to open it... and it wasn't fixed. There was a letter in it saying that my warranty has been voided because of water damage (remember that when I first shipped it, there wasn't any water damage, and it was sitting in my desk the whole time after that, where it definitely was unable to get wet). On top of them not fixing it again, there was a lot more damage done to the phone. On the top right part of my screen, there was a bend in the metal from where they pried it open to “fix” it, and the camera app won't even open anymore. I called them, asking about the the metal broken on my phone. They tried to get away from the fact that that the metal was broken and brought up the water damage. Then I was told since the warranty was voided from the alleged water damage, they won’t fix it even though they damaged it. I told them that I would report them to the Better Business Bureau. Then and only then he said he could do something and that was transferring me to a person higher up than him. Several calls and hours later (both my dad and I called them repeatedly, and they actually hung up on him once), they informed me today that they will not fix it.
So now I’m stuck with a broken phone. I worked really hard to save up the money to buy it, I took really good care of it, and this company refuses to fix it. I’m posting this to spread the word that Huawei is a dishonest company with terrible customer service. In fact, at the end of one phone call, we were asked to press one if they had solved our problem and to press five if they hadn’t. If we pushed five, the recording repeated until we hung up; the computer would not register a negative response!! Steer clear of this company. They don’t care about providing a good product or good customer service.
Backstory: Because I was 15, I haven't had any money except birthday and Christmas money, so I decided to get a job to buy stuff with my own money. I needed a new phone, so I saved up for a few months to get one that was nice and wasn't junk. I was really proud of myself when I finally was able to buy myself a new phone, the Honor 6x.

title: Huawei build quality makes it competitive with Apple
text:
Got the Cyber-Monday/Black-Friday price and see its back again at Amazon! Bought two (for me and my wife, a strategy we used years ago in buying Blackberry phones (2 then too) to learn and help each other in using the features), one from Amazon and one elsewhere on a promo and where a service warranty extension promised (but the vendor and warrant-or when contacted said their co-payment for damage made their product of protection non-sense at the price of replacement this phone sells for - in other words, it makes more sense just to throw a damaged phone away and cheaper to replace it than to pay the co-payments demand when a claim is made in the future on a warranty guarantee!).
The touch screen may be less rugged by lack of gorilla glass so I ordered tempered glass screen protectors (slight curved phone screen makes edges of screen exposed and assures the case does not lift the protector though some buyers appear to object to the gap as too visible - I think it is reasonable compromise for protecting from drops and hard object scratches because I expect these phones to last several years in hard everyday use) that should make the Honor 6X just as rugged as those $700 phones. Got the Spigen case that seems to be a little more protective of the corners of the phone than the blue Remex and the twin pack of clear TPM cases I ordered. All are very slim, each helps avoid slipping out of hand while being comfortable (Remex a little less so with flat sides) yet still easy to slide out of my pocket without too much struggle. Amazon is the place (paid less than $25 for protectors and cases enough for both phones) for accessory selection! Right now the clear cases are not being used (four cases for two phones - I feel is not too extravagant at the price I paid here for them!).

After charging to get at least 80% battery available, I started mine near my wi-fi and before insertion of a SIM card and the phone processed an EMUI 5.0 update download through the wi-fi connection immediately. Patiently let it proceed till it requested a SIM card insertion to proceed. Then took it to my local Cricket Store and they put in my wife's SIM card (she was using a Samsung that already had the nano SIM size) where they charged me $10 for a new SIM card (hardware, not a connection charge) because my Windows Nokia phone was the micro size SIM. Cricket used their own app located in Play Store for free to do the transfer of contacts and pictures with settings where possible. Pretty successful but for some contacts and pics that didn't come over automatically with the app. Just typed the correct contact revisions in one phone and the Cricket rep in the store helped get the other stuff over where necessary. No further charge. This is truly unlocked and compatible on the local ATT network and the latest phone network voice and data technology standards.

Been happy with the use of the phones. Really found you need to enable and record and use the fingerprint feature (four prints may be recorded and used to open the phone or use a swipe on the finger sensor as an easy access to open the phone from the lock-screen). Lots of capacity available with the 32 GB internal storage up-and-running but I had procured and SD card for both phones and the Cricket rep put in the SD card and I later made it the default storage location. Turned off most all the apps to save all the frivolous notifications even though the storage space from deleting them was not needed. One phone is not even registered with a gmail account and we still find it useful as my wife is not interested (yet) in play-store apps. Not sure how the Cricket store downloaded their transfer app to her phone while she had no registered gmail to enable the play store... (maybe it has the Cricket mail access enabling it?).

Reading, It appears the phones are fast enough and conserve battery enough to go almost a week between charging if nothing but phone functionality is used... It now appears there is no downside to a smartphone even for users that are not going to use any functionality beyond what was available from a "flip-phone". Compatibility appears to depend on whether the app uses all the hardware acceleration of the display processor that may not fully implement some games (like the visual reality apps or the augmented reality apps - VR and AR). For us, the speedy responsiveness and battery savings was important and without us opening many simultaneous apps or our not using intensively display type games makes this phone IDEAL.

The EMUI with the latest android seems the best because I implemented the "app drawer" to clean up the home screen yet make all the apps just one press away (EMUI 5.0 uses android ver 7.0 with promise of an upgrade early next year to another android as automatic upgrade and assuring compatibility in the future). The GPS in google maps app works fine. With location and weather data always available we are very functional and have little need for further being prompted by apps pushing unnecessary impositions. The EMUI 5.0 seems to put us in sufficient control to be useful without unnecessary hassles. Green LED in corner of phone is handy in indicating when charging is done and conveniently noticeable enough indication of calls or messages that only take a finger (on print sensor) to access with a swipe or merely read by any button push that brings up the lock screen allowing me to ignore the phone and the audible prompt unless I need to actually pick up the phone and do something about it! My wife already snapped a hawk (predatory bird) perched near her car when it startled her upon pulling into our driveway! Very sharp and apparently easy and fast in use from the looks of the pic she took.

My research indicates Huawei has implemented this user interface to make the transition for Apple Users as easy for them as possible. In the process it seems they have accomplished a good selection of the best of Apple and of Android in this phone!

Be sure to indicate a gift purchase and Amazon has their no-question return available to you till January 31, 2018!

Joe

title: If you're considering it, don't
text:
This will be the most honest review of this phone on here. I never write reviews for any products that I purchase, but if I can keep ONE person from wasting their money on this jalopy of a phone, this time will be well spent.

I switched to this phone from a Samsung Galaxy J3 (the bottom of the barrel $60 GoPhone). That phone was by no means a powerhouse, nor did I expect it to be at that price point, but it got basic tasks done well enough. So, when I dropped $180 on the Honor 6x, I expected a substantial upgrade in performance.

BOY, WAS I WRONG. I researched the heck out of this ohine before I purchased. It came down to the Honor 6x or the Moto G5. Decided on this one because it was about $40 less, I was on a budget, and the tech/features were pretty close.

1. The camera is this phones main selling point. With its dual-lens, multi-setting camera, and other bullsh*t, this is supposed to be a top-notch camera (FALSE) The camera freezes every time you try to open it, and IF you can get it to open, it takes a solid 10-15 seconds to focus- which by that time whatever candid moment you were trying to capture has long passed. Not to mention, the quality is terrible, although I will say the front facing camera isnt half bad (if youcan get it to open)

2. Performance wise, its a joke. Apps constantly crash when you run them, browser freezes, etc. Its makes social media apps a nightmare that st I really just gave up on.

3. Only saving grace (hence the 2 stars), is battery life. The hr battery lasts forever, even as your closing apps and trying to restart it to get something done.

I really wanted to like this phone, but I seriously regret buying. Will be replacing with a higher quality brand in the very near future. DON'T WASTE YOUR MONEY.

-an angry consumer

title: Inferior to Passport SE in almost every way
text:
I recently received my keyone. I hate to write this but it is inferior in every possible way to the Passport SE except for Android app support. I returned mine within 24 hours of receiving it and went back to my Passport SE. It REALLY made me apreciate my Passport SE.

Passport SE has: 1) less cramped keyboard 2) display is square and has greater width which is perfect for webpage viewing and messaging, everything the blackberry is designed for. 3) superior display (i.e. aspect ratio of 1:1 versus silly narrow squished banana shape cookie cutter size of every other cell phone) 4) superior browser, when using it it hides the top icons that contain carrier information, because who wants to see that all of the time with no option to hide it, and the brilliant and experience changing ability to quickly change most webpages into a book format with all ads stripped out just by pressing 'r'. On the keyone, you lose so much of the already sparse screen area to the android navigation buttons, the top bar containing carrier info, and the url bar, its almost comical how little space is left over for actually viewing the webpage content.

I sat there talking to myself trying to persuade myself to stick with the Keyone, but at the end of the day (literally after a days usage) I thought why suffer on a cramped device with inferior screen size, quality and keyboard when I can go back to my Passport SE? I have a Mi Mix phone as well which is the same size as the Keyone. I noticed when I look at webpages I often look at only the top 1/2 of the screen anyhow on whatever device I'm using. What you need for productivity is WIDTH in the screen not LENGTH. I honestly dont understand why cell phones are shaped the way they are, the 1:1 ratio seems better for everything except watching videos, and I dont mind black bars/or can use a video app with crop features.

The Keyone was designed for greater mass appeal, but blackberry phones themselves are niche devices. Its like Blackberry stopped making devices they themselves loved and used and tried to make a device they thought people wanted. Great products are produced by one methodology and not the other.

Make a Passport SE with native android support and fingerprint security and it will be the perfect device. Everyone who bought a passport will buy one for sure (don't know if that is good enough), but hopefully those wanting native android support will also buy one.

title: Beware - blackberry fails at the basics!
text:
I bought a Blackberry Passport Silver Edition phone, and can say that I will never recommend it (or any blackberry to anyone).

Issues with the Blackberry

- The Camera lost its ability to focus (hardware issue, not software issue)
- Browser will reset and lose all tabs
- Browser is incredibly slow to load pages and freezes many times, timing out (incredibly frustrating)
- Phone will shutdown and restart on its own
- Phone will lose cellular connection
- Keyboard backlighting will go out, requiring restart to get it to function
- When using the calendar, and moving an old event up from the past, the calendar will reset and put you back at the current date, not where the old date is. This is frustrating when you are going back through the calendar to find missed events, etc. It requires you to scroll back to the dates you are working in.
- Some websites do not function well or load correctly. I cannot adequately express to you in words how annoying this can be
- Battery drain - I have missed morning alarms because of this issue.
- When watching videos, it defaults to a full screen. Buy you cannot even exit the full screen mode once the video is playing so you have to watch whatever video in its entirety or exit the browser. Very frustrating.

I have tried to list out the seemingly endless list of problems with my blackberry. When you cannot even depend on the basics like camera focus, keyboard lighting, or battery performance (including missing morning alarms), web browsing, or app functionality...it is time to consider whether any blackberry can be worth your time. The plethora of non-software issues should be cause for concern for anyone considering a blackberry. In addition, when I received my new blackberry, it had an issue with its SIM card rear cover, and I asked for a replacement. I believe they sent out a refurbished unit, even though I had just bought a new Silver edition.

Beware of blackberry because its hardware seems to not be able to perform basic functions!

title: A Good Phone, but...
text:
there are several issues that prevent me from rating it any higher.

I've been looking for a new smartphone for a while, because my old Boost MAX phone was running out of Memory (I was having to clear the Cache everyday + App Cache cleaning once a week just to keep the phone working). So, when BoostMobile offered me BoostUp, I figured why not. So, after researching the different phones available (I'm not one to spend $$$$, when a phone for $$ works just as well), I settled on the Stylo 3. However, I'm glad that I was able to keep my Boost MAX phone because:

1) I find the Alarm, Calculator, Calendar, Camera and NotePad apps are better, and easier to use. And, as you can see by the attached pictures, the MAX camera are a bit better (at least to me). Especially in Zoom mode.

2) Old Text app was better too. It showed the total number of texts sent/received to each person. And, I could lock and/or delete select texts.

3) The plastic Screen Protector (harder to install) didn't get dirty, as quickly as the glass one (easy to install) for the Stylo 3.

4) The belt-clip Carrying case allowed me to slide the phone in/out. But, on the Stylo 3, it snaps in/out. Which, makes it harder to get the phone in/out of the case (need 2 hands to get it out).

5) The Back and Home keys are on the phone, which makes it easier to exit a app. On the Stylo 3, it's on the screen, of each app, and doesn't always show up right away.

6) Minimal ads, regardless of which app I used. The Stylo 3 has ads, ADS and A-D-S! Especially, full screen ads on the home. And, these ads (specifically the new car; already got one and Small Business Insurance; I don't have a business anymore, which repeat most often) ARE NOT of any interest.

Overall, a good phone that allows me to keep the apps I need, and still have Memory to spare. Though, had I the option, I would have increased the memory on my old phone.

title: Excellent features & quality for loads less $.
text:
The LG Stylo Series has been a top value in a 5.7 inch screen phone in recent years. The five star reviews of this phone just keep piling up. It is particularly slim and lightweight which has caused some to believe it is fragile, but all it really needs is the aftermarket protective case we all buy anyway for around $10. I think it's a beautiful phone, extremely thin and I would say almost weightless, so no worries for someone who lives a low-risk adult daily life.

The Stylo 3 has 16 gigs of internal memory, as did the Stylo 2. I wish they had put 32 gig in this one, but that's my only gripe. This phone will accept up to and including a 2tb Micro SD card, so media storage is not a problem. The screen resolution is 720P, and the sound quality is loud enough and good enough. It also has a darn good camera which I have used a lot in the past. The new Stylo version adds a gyroscope so you can properly view those 360-degree photo images.

The removable battery is now the slightly larger 3200 and the Android version is the latest. The power button is still on the back of the phone, which I love, and the volume buttons have been moved out of the way to the left edge, which may not a real improvement since I can accidentally grip them in that spot, so they'd be better off on top or anywhere else. The stylus is stealthier but still convenient and easy to access, and pointier for better response.

I have found the LG Stylus series to have everything I need, and very little that I require which I can't have -- in a phone that cost me about $129. Yes I'd like to have a V30 but I'm probably saving $900 or so by having this one instead. Not to mention, I can have this on a no-contract Virgin account for very little per month while enjoying benefits like a much more expensive carrier.

My Stylo 3 did not include startup instructions which are available online, so if you need them I would read them on your previous phone or a PC. The LG phones do make it a simple procedure to move files and settings from your old phone to your new one. It won't do everything for you, but it will seem a bit magical that it will do as much as it can.

I have been seriously shopping the reviews of $1,000 phones. I've noticed new customers complaining about significant failings like inadequate sound volume or even finicky operation. I simply have nothing bad to say about the LG Stylo series. I use my Stylo 2 so much that I've nearly worn it out so it was time to get the Stylo 3 for now. I'm only sorry they didn't opt for 32 gig of internal storage for the primary apps. But again, File Manager can move your bigger media files to your SD card. A small concession for the fantastic value this phone offers to someone who needs a reasonably priced but full-featured phone. It was not built like a tank, but gracefully, and I think it works great for grown-ups. :-)

title: Suckjob phone.
text:
I hate this phone.

It isn't a totally terrible phone. I just opened it two days ago and got my email going, downloaded gchat, ig, and my meditation app, put up a wallpaper I preferred, etc. I'm sure Maps works fine, although I haven't needed it yet. It seems pretty fast. I'm coming off my HTC Desire 816, which I LOVE, it just hasn't had any storage left for a long time and I've been limping along with un-updated apps, no Maps, some episodes of the phone freezing on me, a scare where the battery died and I could not get the phone to start back up for a couple hours, and constant notifications that I need to make space. I stumbled upon the gem of budget phones, it seems, and I'm disappointed by my "upgrade" to the lg stylo 3.

Here's what I hate:

It typos me constantly, changing the word "and" to "ama", etc, and it doesn't capitalize the pronoun "I". I have no idea why it doesn't capitalize "I" and this wouldn't be a big deal (neither would the constant typos), except that this phone does not "learn" predictive text based on the user's preferences. No matter how many times I corrected "i" to "I", it never learned to use "I" above "i". Since the phone does not learn as the user corrects words, this will never end. It will always say "i" and will always replace "and" with "ama", and so on and so forth forever with many many words. It does not allow you to delete "words" such as "ama" from its dictionary, and you cannot add a word like "I" since it already exists, but is just not being used. In addition, when you tap to delete, it does not delete the entire last word, you have to delete letter by letter, so if you get a typo and the word you need isn't even suggested, you have to hold down delete. It doesn't seem like a big deal until every single ^&$^$^%* word is typoed. Yes, I could dl Google Keyboard or Swiftkey from the app store, but have you read all the permissions for those? And if that's not enough to scare you, when you install and open the app, it reminds you that it can read everything including passwords you enter using the keyboard. Listen, I know Google knows everything about me, they just don't have to throw it in my face like that, okay?

The camera drives me nuts. It has the same MPs as my HTC, but it tries to get alot more area in the shot. It seems like the way it does this is by using some type of fish eye function where its pulling in from the outer edges and concentrating everything in the center. The result is a selfie where my nose, which is not exactly a tiny button nose, looks outlandishly gigantic. When I tilt the phone, you can see how blown up the outer edges get as everything gets sucked towards the middle. The screen and resulting photos seem dark and all I see are bags under my eyes. I did not realize my last camera had a "beautifying" function until a few weeks ago (I had it for over 2 years), so trust that my HTC was not pulling one over on me; I didn't look perfect in those photos either, but this camera outright makes me feel bad about myself.

The speakers. When I was researching my HTC, it lauded itself for having "BoomSound!". At the time I was like mhm, great, good for you. BoomSound and front facing speakers. Man, I didn't know how good I had it. The speakers on the phone are back-facing and tinny af, even when you're wearing headphones. I played the same youtube video simultaneously on both phones and this is so inferior. I could get past it by itself, but piled up with these other complaints it just sucks. And who puts the headphone jack on the bottom of the phone?? Ahhhhh! Also, I assume to make up for the poor quality speakers, the lowest volume setting is blaringly loud. With my HTC, I could watch videos in bed on the very lowest setting without waking my boyfriend, or use my alarm at work as a reminder for things, but now when the alarm goes off, the absolute lowest volume setting has it yelling out "BEEP BEEP BEEP BEEP! BEEP BEEP BEEP BEEP!" I've changed the sound of the alarm, but the volume does not go any lower.

Let's see...oh yes, the notification led light only blinks red. When I see a blinking red light I feel like there is cause for alarm. you cannot change the light to green or blue or anything besides red. Why red, LG?? Once again, I could use an app to change that, but I get super sketched out by the permissions. Not to mention, what's going to happen in a year or two when the phone has gotten "old" and is weighed down with updates and is saying "you need to delete apps to make space!" and then I have to get rid of all this stuff anyways and deal with typos galore and red lights just to avoid dropping another couple hunna on yet another new phone? Why can't I just keep my HTC??? ::shakes fists at the sky::

Things I like about the phone. You can hide apps and you can put photos of your choice into a locked folder that only opens with fingerprint/pattern/code. Convenient when you hand a family member your phone to look at a picture and they don't know swipe-etiquette. As in don't. Phone takes a photo when you make a fist in the photo or say "cheese" or "kimchi", so you don't have to awkwardly press a button. Opens amazingly fast with fingerprint. Thin, light, but not insubstantial phone. Clear screen. I do like the stylus as it's fun to create little doodles on the phone.

It sucks cause those things are cool, but all the factors I mention above just kill it for me. Typosontyposontypos, $%^&&y speaker, fugly selfies. It doesn't get much worse than that. It's a miracle I didn't throw this phone at a brick wall. Listen, I just want my tech to work, that's all, I don't ask for much. Everyone's phone is stapled to their face nowadays, its not like its palatable to walk around with a crap phone and just deal with it. Do I want to go through the ordeal of figuring out whether I can even and how to return this phone to Amazon? Do I totally love that I'm gonna eat $30 that I spent on a case and screen protectors (I initially purchased screen protectors for the wrong type of phone)? No. But can I deal with all those things I said for the next couple years? Also no. This phone's gotta go. Turns out a decent phone is worth the money when you use it all the time. HTC, for the love of all that is holy, please come out with a new budget phone for me. I'll make it worth your while.
