title: One of the best out there
text:
It takes about a week of online shopping to go through all the selfie-stick offerings on Amazon, and I found that this one from Anker is one of the best. Its a good combination of ultra-light weight and features.

What I like:
* Very light at 7oz, and very short, neat and compact when folded, so it's easy to bring anywhere.
* Great mount design with everything included and nothing to lose, supports camera, action-cam and Gopro.
* Seamless integrated bluetooth remote, which is removable, and can be charged with Micro-usb cable.

What I didn't like:
* tripod mount screw is too short, and comes loose too easily
* Neck rotates 360-degrees, but doesn't hold firmly enough.
* Not quite strong enough for my 8oz Olympus TG-870 action-cam

This stick has a better mount mechanism than most. Firstly, it's completely integrated, with no parts to lose. Competing designs require you to unscrew interchangeable parts, for phone/actioncam/gopro, which you need to keep track of when out and about. If they don't provide a carry-case, then you need to devise a sensible way to bring it along with all the spare parts. The Anker design has everything in one piece, you fold down the phone cradle, and flip up the tripod mount.

The tripod mount is genius. Just loosen the screw and flip it up from under the cradle's neck. Unfortunately, it's a very short screw, so it doesn't hold firmly enough, and might possibly damage the camera's tripod mount hole. It always comes loose after a while, and i'm reluctant to crank it down too tight, for fear of damaging the camera's mount. The screw is short because of the neck design, as it is tucked into a recess underneath. If they made the screw longer, the entire neck would have to be longer to accommodate it. Anker should definitely revise the design, as this is the main weakness.

It also has a neck that rotates 360-degrees, with a ball-spring that clicks into place each 180-degrees. While this is a great feature, it's not strong enough to stay put. The phone is usually mounted off-center, to avoid buttons the power/volume buttons on the side of the phone, and as a result, the whole rig sags to one side, and the neck easily spins around. Similar issue with the Olympus action-cam, where the tripod mount is off to one side, so again, the whole rig is lop-sided, and often forces the neck to rotate unexpectedly. While this is OK for taking photos, it's a deal-breaker for videography.

When I brought on on the trail for a long hike, I found that these limitations most glaring. It's suitable for cellphone use, but not suitable for videography with the Olympus action-cam. Too bad. I'm still keeping it, but i'll be getting a more heavy-duty stick for videography on the go, with the Olympus. Overall, I recommend this stick, and it will work very well if you understand the limitations.

from March 19, 2019

This is a followup to the below review. Upon returning from my trip, Anker customer service was in constant contact with me, refunded my money for both tripod sticks that I had purchased before I returned them, then sent me two new ones. I tested those in February, and they seemed to work, but didn't have time to use on vacation yet. I gave one to a friend's family who is also taking it to Europe for a week over Spring Break, so eager to see those reviews. That said, the rep from Ankersupport has been following up with me regularly, and I really appreciate that. Kudos to Anker for standing strong behind their products. I remain a loyal customer.

from Jan 1, 2019
Camera trigger only works rarely. This is one of the most frustrating devices I have ever purchased. Do NOT buy it if you are counting on this device to work when you need it. Fully charged and connected, it does not release the shutter of the camera, except on rare occasions. Physically well built, it looked like the perfect travel selfie for a trip. Also came in an official-looking Anker box. Purchased two just prior to our trip to Europe, and here we are, and day after day, no matter what we do, connect and disconnect, recharge, etc., they do not trigger our iPhones. We have missed many an awesome moment and great picture. The box says Anker, which is a very reliable brand md we are big fans of Anker (we are here in with Anker batteries, wall chargers and cords), but I am wondering if this is a fraudulent device. Will write to Anker and investigate when we return to the states. Contacting Amazon also. Do NOT buy this until Anker and/or Amazon resolve this issue.

title: Solid and well designed but insufficient RAM to be functional
text:
I made the mistake of thinking "good 'ol Nokia" – but the "Nokia" brand has been shopped out and bears no resemblance to the dependable phones many of us had years ago.

This is a sub-$100.00, 5” Android "1 & 8" device (marketed as 1GB RAM/ 8GB ROM) running a fairly clean version of Android 7. I use my phone as a...phone - and for navigation/texting/emergency web browsing/non-critical photography, etc - especially when I'm traveling – and I prefer a smaller phone – unfortunately there aren't many decent 5” Android phones on the US market.

If you know how to taper down background data exchanges/apps you can get it to run reasonably well - but it still lags and certainly won't multi-task well. The reality is I could not discern more than 890 MB of RAM (yes, LESS than 1 GB) - looks to me like they rounded up.

So - IMO it's a flawed device and I ended up returning it. I was initially drawn to it because I'm frequently navigating in cities/places I'm unfamiliar with and it's got a GREAT GPS chipset - GPS/AGPS/GLONASS - this thing sees all of them – but as many other reviewers here have stated, it’s just too underpowered to run apps with any fluidity.

There are several Motorola phones on the market at this price point (sub-$100.00) running Android 7, with 2GB RAM, 16 GB storage and an 8 GB camera – so there’s no compelling reason to buy this. Cannot recommend.

title: Look and feel of a much more expensive phone, but it's slow
text:
I’ve tried a lot of cheap phones for my job and this Nokia is unquestionably the best phone you can get for $100 as of mid 2018.

The chassis and buttons look and feel solid and high quality; the screen is bright and sharp. The camera is surprisingly good for a low cost phone, and the Android OS seems to be stock without any annoying manufacturer tweaks. The 4100 mAh battery lasts nice and long. It even has two SIM slots which is useful for frequent travelers.

The areas where Nokia appears to have cheaped out are with the weak processor and limited memory - the phone is noticeably pokey; apps judder and lag and notification sounds are often broken up. Installing an SD card will certainly help with capacity, though that won't have much impact on speed.

Overall considering the price of this phone and the quality software and build, the so-so performance isn’t really a big deal since basic functions like email, browsing, calling etc. all work fine.

title: Not fully compatible with T-mobile
text:
I'm generally impressed with the value for money for the Nokia 2. However, I recently discovered that the Nokia 2 is not fully compatible with all T-mobile 4G LTE networks. According to Nokia Customer Service the Nokia 2 TA-1035 model operates on the following bands and frequencies:
WCDMA: Band 1, 2, 5, 8;
LTE: Band 1 (2100), 3 (1800), 5 (850), 7 (2600), 8 (900), 20 (800), 28 (700), 38 (2600), 40 (2300)
This means that the TA-1035 DOES NOT work on LTE Bands: 2 (1900) & 12 (700). You need those bands to use T-Mobile's 4G LTE service in many places. So, this phone is not fully compatible with T-Mobile. Unfortunately, I have not yet found a reliable way to check which 4G LTE bands T-mobile uses for specific areas. So, if you plan on using T-mobile, and don't want your service dropping as you travel across the US, you had better not get this phone.

title: Excellent phone for $100
text: Based on the value of this phone, I give it a solid five stars. It obviously doesn't have the most powerful processor, but it runs Android 7.1 quite smoothly, if not as speedily as phones with better specs. I've heard complaints that it lags, but it's not enough to bother me in the slightest. My only previous experience with Android is with a couple of small tablets over the years (Nexus and Amazon Fire), and this thing runs circles around those. Even with the cost of adding a Micro SD card, it's a huge bargain. I replaced my aging Windows 10 phone with this Nokia, added the Microsoft launcher, a 64GB memory card, and a few apps that I need, and I'm ready to roll. The fact that it's Nokia was a huge selling point for me. Even though the phones are made by HMD Global, I'm sure Nokia wouldn't put their name on crap. When you pick it up, you can just tell that it's well made. It feels solid in the hand, with just enough heft. And from what I've read, Nokia will be rolling out Android updates as they're available, unlike a lot of other manufacturers. Full disclosure: I'm on my second unit of this phone, the first one wouldn't recognize the SD card I had installed. The seller replaced it with zero hassle, and this one doesn't have that issue.

Camera doesn't seem to be on par with previous Nokia's with the Carl Zeiss Tessar lens. No problem, its still a great value. And i have yet to get a feel for it. TBD. . .

title: Great phone for the price! Stock Android with continued updates, Dual SIM, SD card slot...
text:
This is a great cheap smartphone for under $100. Sure it is not very good in the spec department but depending on what you are looking for it might be the right choice.

As mentioned earlier the specs are nothing special. It is definitely the weakest part of this phone. From personal experience the performance feels like on par with a Samsung Galaxy S5 or an iPhone 5s. If you are someone who always gets the latest phone, you will be disappointed.

I'll highlight a couple positive things that this phone does well.

This phone is perfect for someone who doesn't use any demanding apps. Forget about most games. Don't worry though because calls, texts, email, and chatting work perfectly. I see it as the best communication device under $100.

I'm using this device as a back up/travel phone. I currently have an AT&T and a T-Mobile SIM in the dual slots. The phone can switch between them on the fly. You can route calls and data between the two SIMs automatically or manually choose it each time you place a call. Most dual SIM phones I've used don't handle it this seamlessly or they make you switch one line off before switching to the other one. The status bar shows the signal strength of each line and also the type of connection (LTE, 4G, 3G, etc...). Keep in mind that each frequency of the radio can only be used once. This means if the 4G connection for each SIM you have uses the same frequency, then SIM #1 will get the priority and #2 will fall back to the next available. The Nokia 2 really shines in the dual SIM functionality.

The processor used in this phone is the snapdragon 212. It does not use much power since it is not very high performing. This combined with the huge battery (4000mAh) means you really do get great battery life. I have the brightness set to the max, wifi and bt on, two SIMs, after a day of use (7am-7pm) I still have 75% battery left. This is on track to get me two days of standby, you could probably stretch it if you power down over night or go into battery saver modes.

One neutral point of this phone is the storage space. It is only 8GB with about half of that available after the OS is considered, since it has expandable storage I didn't make this a negative. A microSD card is a must with this phone. Get a decent SD card and combine it with the internal storage. The phone isn't that fast so you won't really notice much performance difference between launching apps off the internal memory vs the sd card.

Don't get this phone to play games, fly your drone, or for the camera. Get this if you need the connectivity of dual SIMs and the long battery life.

EDIT: I also forgot to mention that Nokia has promised continued support for Android 8 and 9 for their new phones that were released this year, the Nokia 2 was included in this announcement as well.

title: An odd mix of high and low end features.
text:
This is a phone with a weird set of features and components. It has a chassis made from a single piece of aluminum, a Corning Gorilla glass screen and a big honking 4,100 mah battery. Parts that would be found on higher end smartphones, but also has a slowish Snapdragon 210 processor, 8GB of internal memory and 1GB of RAM. The user can add an SD card and Nougat can format the card so that it can act as an expansion on the paltry internal storage. I have a 64GB SD card on this phone which expands the 8GB into approx 70GB. But not all Android apps are designed to run off the SD card. The starting 8GB would be standard on a smartphone from five years ago. The phone comes with Android Nougat out of the box and Nokia says that it will get Oreo 8.1 when it passes muster. It also has dual SIM capability which is good for travelers. The Android experience is almost pure. Only a few items like a Nokia support app and FM radio are added extras. The screen is pretty good. It is a bit laggy as a phone with the low amount of RAM, the low end CPU and internal storage would have. I ran a Geekbench 4 benchmark on this phone and it did not fare well. The Nokia 2 fell below the least powerful phone in the benchmark, The Nexus 5. A phone that's been obsolete for almost three years. So for those who are into speeds and feeds and are looking for the newest and fastest, this phone is a dog. Battery life is very good. I've had the phone on for close to 24 hours with average usage and mostly the stock apps installed, only about 10 apps of my choosing installed and it's at 77%. I have yet to run the battery down to zero. If you are looking for an entry level smartphone for a low price for a child or a first time or light phone user who's not going to push this phone's capabilities to the edge, the Nokia 2 is a servicable device.
Pros-
1. Quality build.
2. Low Price
3. 4,100mah battery = excellent battery life.
4. Nice camera and screen.
5. Nougat out of the box with Oreo coming.
6. Mostly pure Android experience.
Cons-
1. Slow CPU and laggy performance
2. Only 8GB internal storage (can be expanded with SD card.)
3. 1GB RAM.

title: Disappointed!
text:
The Nokia 2 is by far the cheapest Android phone one can get with timely Android security updates every month. The next closest is probably the Nokia 3, but the Nokia 3 is not available with a US warranty.

The Moto E4 and Moto E4 Plus, which may be the prominent competitors to the Nokia 2, do not receive security updates monthly. I would never buy either of them.

The Moto X4, which is part of the Android One program and therefore receives security patches monthly, was intended partly to provide a cheaper alternative to Google Pixel models with Project Fi. However, "cheaper" still means a price tag of around $300 at the very least for the Moto X4.

I suspect and hope there's a sizable niche of people like me, who are dying for an Android phone that receives timely security updates every month and who don't want to pay for a Pixel or Moto X4 or an Android Blackberry (not super inexpensive and from what I can tell not always super timely with monthly security patches). As a result, I was very excited about the Nokia 2's prompt availability in the US.

However, I was sorely disappointed to find out that the phone I received, which shipped out on December 7, only had the September 1, 2017 security patch. It didn't even have the September 5, 2017 security patch, which patched a critical WiFi vulnerability, one that would allow the attacker to take over the phone just by being within WiFi range when WiFi was turned on for the phone.

I can't believe it. The Nokia 2 was publicly announced on October 31, 2017. Surely, it should have shipped with at least the September 5, 2017 patch, if not the October 1 or October 5 patches. This is complacent and irresponsible.

I haven't tried yet, but I doubt I will be allowed to update over cellular, which means that when I try over WiFi to get the WiFi patch released in the September 5, 2017 update, I'll be exposing myself to the WiFi attack. While I may have higher security requirements than most people, this is reason enough for me to be returning the phone.

All the complaints about security aside, the Nokia 2 is a very decent phone. It looks very elegant, in a subdued and minimalistic way. Sitting next to my iPhones (5s, 6, and 10), the Nokia 2 looked more aesthetically pleasing than the much more expensive iPhones.

As for what might not be immediately apparent unless seen in person, there are several things worth pointing out. First, the pewter doesn't look grayish as it does in the photos on the Amazon product page. Instead, in person, it looks brownish (picture brown leather shoes or a brown leather belt), but very dark brownish. Although not my very most preferred look, it looks very nice and leans towards conveying masculine. Second, it is not a lightweight phone. According to one website, it weighs 5.68 oz (161 g), whereas, for reference, the iPhone 6s and iPhone 5s weigh 5.04 oz (143 g) and 3.95 oz (112 g), respectively. Third, the battery life is amazing. It can sit for days (on airplane mode) without battery life dropping more than a couple percentage points or so. Initially, I hated the weight of the phone, but now I think the extra weight but might be a worthwhile tradeoff for the massive battery life.

text: Opening the Nokia 2 was fun. I came from a galaxy s7 that I lost but couldn’t afford to replace. So I suppose I am comparing it to what I had before. The Nokia 2 design and first impression is amazing. Powering on the phone was quick to boot up. The battery came with 83% charge. The OS was extremely clean free of bloatware. Everything was downloaded photos, old apps, contacts etc. took about 20 mins for my photos and such to come in (several hundred). I ran a game that would sometimes freeze up my old iPhone 5s and rarely my Samsung S7 called “Clash of Clans”. Just to stress the processor. Surprisingly the game loaded but not as quickly as in the S7 (yes I understand the Nokia has an entry level processor) the game played well. No freezing however under a heavy base attacks frames started to slow but not to where I would be frustrated. Next I tested the network speed on my carriers T-Mobile and ATT (personal and business). The Nokia 2 connects fine with both networks when I had the respect SIM card in. 25mps LTE band 12 on T-Mobile and 31 mps on band 4 on ATT. Phone calls are crystal clear and volume is robust however speaker phone and video watching the volume was a tad low for me through the single speaker. Battery life. 3 fulls days of use and game playing before I finally start to charge it. Battery life is the best I have ever had from a phone. I would assume the slower processor saves battery life. The only time the phone gets warm is on a charge. Overall this phone is a winner of your remember to close apps after using thing instead of letting them pile up likewise with browsers tabs. My daughter complained the phone was slow on loading videos for YouTube. Upon looking at the phone I noticed she had 13 YouTube videos loading at the same time on different chrome tabs. After I close all except the tab she was viewing the video zapped right in and started playing. Memory. This is where I deducted one star. After all of my google photos and apps finally downloaded along with a few required updates the phone had 2.1gb left out of 8gb. So adding an SD memory card is a no brained if you choose this device. It will take a 256gb SD Card. Well hope I informative enough Cheers!

title: Not the Nokia you remember (garbage can special)
text:
UPDATE May 15 2018 --I woke up this morning but my Nokia 2 did not -- after being a loyal customer, I won't buy Nokia smartphones again unless they are able to get back to their roots of affordable and DURABLE smartphones (see my original review below).

I can't stress how light my use of my Nokia 2 was since I bought it at Christmas to use as a secondary phone -- barely at all, and not often even carried around. I've never had a Nokia totally brick before, but this one is bricked. It won't power on. I can only imagine some issue with the integrated battery.. Repair shops won't touch this phone.

Meanwhile my Nokia / Microsoft Lumia from 2014 keeps hammering on, and the battery is easily replaced if there is ever an issue. As my Nokia 2 is dead after minimal use and just out-of-warranty, I just bought a Moto G5 Plus (also a sealed battery phone) from a retail big box today as my Android device. Out-of-the-box, the Moto G5 Plus operates light years ahead of the Nokia 2, including MUCH better call quality. If you are looking at the Nokia 2, I would recommend going with the Moto G5 Plus that is nearly identical in size to the Nokia 2 and can be found for under $160 new currently outside of Amazon.

***

I'm going to hang onto it through the holidays to see if it improves but my first impressions aren't great. The sound quality on calls does not seem to be as good as past Nokias I've owned -- including Lumias and an XpressMusic. It has started to randomly reboot a few days out of the box, which I never experienced with any previous Nokia I've owned. I am by no means putting my new phone through any paces but I'm concerned that the Nokia 2 does not seem to be very good as a phone or very stable as a smart device. The screen is better than other phones I've owned and the battery life is impressive. We'll see if it somehow smooths out and improves operations but it has already cost me a work call. I suspect there are other happy and frugal Nokia customers looking at this phone but I can't give it a strong recommendation... yet.

title: A Solid Budget Device
text:
I purchased this for my wife to replace a Nokia Lumia 521. She uses it primarily for phone and text, and taking pictures. It is a perfectly adequate device for her needs (and is reviewed in that context). Coming from the unsupported Windows Phone ecosystem, it was also a nice perk to install a few home automation apps on the new phone.

This device will not win any awards for speed, but in this case, that isn't an issue. It calls, it texts, it takes pictures. Switching between apps is a little slow, but not annoyingly so. It is pretty much stock Android (as of this review, it is running Android 7.1.1, 8.1 is in beta for the device but I won't subject my spouse to beta testing).

The build quality of the device is top notch. It feels more like a mid-range device than a budget handset (especially compared to the old Lumia 521). The screen is clear and sharp. I added a basic case and screen protector to the phone just in case.

Storage is definitely a compromise. After installing updates, about 3 GB of 8 GB were still free. If you want to install apps or take pictures, you'll want a microSD card. Fortunately we had one from her old phone, so that wasn't any extra cost at this time.

Overall, this is a solid budget device, and I definitely recommend it.

Pros:
-Low cost
-Stock Android
-Receives Android updates
-Good build quality
-Decent battery life
-Nice screen

Cons (this is a budget device and these are definitely not dealbreakers):
-A little slow
-Low storage

title: she is in love with this phone
text:
I ordered this phone for my little sister as a gift for her birthday. She is becoming of age and felt it was time to be able to have a personal way to communicate with the family. Although she is surrounded by iPhones and Samsung devices, she is in love with this phone! The phone arrived in a nice small box. The box contains a charging block, micro USB, and even a pair of headphones with a mic! Even though the phone has a nice sturdy premium feel to it, it does have its ups and downs.
Pros- The phone feels nice in the hands. Apparently, it weighs about 161 grams. It also has a 5in display with gorilla glass 3 that I think goes up to 720p resolution, Which is not bad considering this phone cost sub 100$. Another great thing is that this phone is receiving all of the latest software updates and security patches. It is going to be supported for at least 2 years so you cant go wrong with that. The phone has all necessary bands for the use in the USA and also contains all wifi bands. The last pro that I can remember is the HUGE battery it has at 4100 mAh. This thing can last you about 2 days.
Cons- A big let down is the Snapdragon 212 they have this thing running on. If you are a speed user ( I have a Pixel and a Galaxy S7) then don't consider this phone as a daily driver. Instead, it is the type of phone you take with you on your travels or as a backup. But in my case, My sister is patient and understands that her first car isn't going to be a Ferrari. It is perfect for calls and texts, surfs things on google with ease and can handle a game or two but don't plan on having things running in the back too long since it only has 1gb of RAM. The camera on this phone is also just ok but also again for my situation it is perfect. She isn't going to be posting on social media or taking pics of the grand canyon. Instead, she'll use it to take pics of the cats and dogs etc. The storage is also pretty small at 8gb but can be expanded since it has an sd card slot.
So to recap, This phone is great for 100$. Do get it if you're going to gift it to your grandma, mom, sister or anybody who has never had a smartphone before. Also if you need a backup or travel phone this phone is great for that too. Do not get this if you're used to the speed of the newer flagships as you'll find yourself getting upset over the small lag that seems to be an eternity. Anyway good luck!

title: Incredible phone
text:
I'm loving my V40. I'm coming from a three year old Samsung S6 so this was a huge leap up for me in speed and power. The display is stunning and its large size is particularly good for using Google Maps and watching youtube videos etc. I can't stand notches but downloading the free app Nacho Notch hides the notch in all apps. The 'Second screen' feature on the phone only hides the notch on LG apps.

Sound quality through the headphones is top of class and there are lots of customizable settings. (For the 3D sound settings I recommend the 'side - side' one, or nothing at all) When listening through the speakers, 90% of the sound comes from the bottom boom bass speaker, the rest comes from the earpiece which is almost nothing. The sound is fairly loud but a bit dull sounding and when watching a video in landscape, it's obvious the sound is mostly coming from one side. When placing the phone on a table or better yet something hollow, the bass quality and volume increases and it's pretty impressive, probably as good as any phone out there. What really sounds great through the speakers is the SPEAKER PHONE! Or listening to voice mails etc. Voices are loud with a rich/full tone. Calls sound great through the earpiece too.

Some reviews online have complained about battery life but I end the day with a surplus and coming from the abysmal battery life on my S6 which just had a brand new battery installed, the V40's battery is great for me. I haven't used the camera much but so far so good. The front selfie camera has a default filter added which smoothes the skin both in wrinkles and in color and imo doesn't look good or natural. To disable, click the icon on the bottom left of the screen and select 'none'. You may have repeat this if you close the camera completely or restart the phone. Shooting video is where this phone really shines! And the audio recording quality is great.

It's impressive a phone of this size and build quality only weighs 169 grams. But for me, I wish it was a bit smaller. So many phones these days are going for that tall/skinny look. When watching videos in landscape, you often end up borders on the side and it's a waste of screen. If they could fit the power of this phone with its speaker into the notchless aspect ratio of the LG V35, this would be the near perfect phone. But it's very close as is!

CONS:
1. Does NOT have a way to act as stand unlike the old version
2. Does NOT have a magnet so the flip cover doesn't even close all the way (hence the 4 Star rating)
3. Too expensive
4. Stylish but not for maximum protection. Great for protecting against scratches but I wouldn't let this thing fall since the cover doesn't stick to keep it closed.

Overall, this case is built exactly for the S10. I wish they didn't take away the ability to turn it into a stand and I really wish there was a magnet to keep the cover from opening. Is it worth $60, probably not but you are buying the name here, first and foremost. If you want protection from drops, this is NOT for you.

title: Great Phone, some info about unlocking.
text:
First of all, I want to clear up some stuff about the carrier of this phone.

The version of the phone that is being sold here is the V35PAWM, the AT&T unlocked version of the phone. From what I understand, it will work with GSM carriers without modification. However, I wanted to use the phone with Google Fi. It is quite easy in this case to flash the phone with the V35OULM kdz found here, no urls allowed in reviews, but it can be found on the LG firmwares website. I used the tutorial on the Flash Stock Roms website.

To be clear, the phone should work with GSM carriers without this process. However three are some advantages of flashing the kdz. No more AT&T bloatware, quicker updates (I have heard that some people using the AT&T software with a different carrier are not getting the android 9 update). For Google Fi specifically, some features of the service are not available without using a completely compatible phone. Flashing the OULM software makes the phone "completely" unlocked and compatible.

Now about the device itself.

I bought this to replace a Pixel 1 hat had picked up in preparation for an extended trip to Europe. However, the Pixel 1 was very buggy and rather outdated. The LG V35 has more than effectively replaced that phone. With the updated kdz it actually seems to work better with Fi than the picel did and the breadth of options within the os are overwhelming in a positive way. The screen resolution can be changed along with the way the volume interface works for example. Another nice touch is LG's theme options. I am using a theme called Pix Color. This applies a system wide dark mode and also makes the on screen buttons look like those on the pixel, a design that I prefer to LG's. However, the buttons can be hidden to take advantage of the whole screen retaliate, something that can not be done on the Pixel devices and some other android phones.

Speaking of the screen, it is huge and beautiful. The POLED panel looks quite good. My only complaint about the phone so far is actually that I think it is a bit too big, though I realized that is the current design trend. I much preferred the size of the LG G6 that I used to use.

Great phone overall, no real complaints so far.

text: I am very satisfied with this purchase. I have always used an iPhone and finally made the decision to switch to an android. I am not disappointed! This phone is awesome. This seems to happen with Facebook mostly so could just be the app. Portrait mode on the camera is amazing. Crystal clear images that almost look professional. The phone doesn't have a lot of memory but you are able to import a micro SD if needed. The sound quality on this phone is great, too; I don't really need a speaker anymore. Remember though that this phone will only work with carriers like Cricket and AT&T, not Verizon or Sprint. I recommend this phone 100%!!

In most respects it is a great phone, but the camera, one of my favorite features of the V30+, is not NEARLY as good. I don't know what they did, but the sensor is terrible in moderate light with manual settings. I frequently photograph my artwork in progress, so I really need a good camera. I did a side by side comparison--color balance and exposure was comparable at the same settings (ISO 100 at 1/25 sec), but the V35 was horribly grainy and mushy when zoomed in, didn't pick up nearly as much detail as the V30+. title: Unlocked flagship ATT phone updated to google-fi OS and working on tmobile for cheap!
text:
I wanted to upgrade my LG V20 on tmobile's network, but didn't want to pay 800+ or lock myself into a 2year contract so I was looking at cheap phones. I came close to buying a renewed/used Essential or similar for 150, but then came across the ATT unlocked V35 thinq. I was very worried about using an ATT phone on tmobile, but figured I'd try it.

I'm so glad I pulled the trigger. After receiving the phone I realized I may not be able to get updates as I'm not on ATT's network.. I then noticed this phone was an official google-fi phone, which should mean its 100% compatible with tmobile, and should also allow me to get updates.

It was easy to use the LG software to update the phone to the latest firmware for Google-Fi (listed as GFI on LG's website), leaving me with a debloated OS that will allow me to obtain future updates. As far as using the GoogleFi on Tmobile's network, it works perfect. The phone's hardware has the same bands as the V20 so I wasn't expecting to get the 600mhz band. I'm getting at least as good reception as my V20 and speed tests are perfectly fine (140mb in some cases).

I've been hyping this to everyone I know who might want a new phone and may be on tmobile, att, or google-fi. Yes it's not a 2019 phone with the latest bands but its easily better then many phones and was very much over-looked in 2018.

title: LG hits another homerun!  Best performance and most affordable smartphone on the market.

The major feature I wanted is to play old school console games and have an OLED screen.  The LG v35 ThinQ amazing's OLED screen of 1440 x 2880 pixels, 18:9 ratio.  There is 64gb memory installed which means I should never have to deal with running out of space from installing apps that my previous X Power with its 16gb internal memory.  Switching from my X Power smartphone's screen to the new LG ThinQ the difference on the eyes is night and day.  The LG v35 ThinQ isn't state of the art a huge much-needed upgrade for a person who relies on their smartphone on a daily basis and also enjoys casual gaming.  If someone out there needs help there are multiple videos to research and adjust the settings for the emulators.  Now I just need to find a decent case and controller attachment.  Don't get me wrong.  The LG X Power is still a really good smartphone for  new android users, but the LG v35 ThinQ is a long overdue upgrade for more experienced android users.

title: This particular phone had issues....bought another one and it's great
text:
I ordered this phone as a new unlocked gsm phone. I recieved an email from the seller before the phone arrived about contacting them for an unlock code if needed when trying to activate on my network. I've bought unlocked phones for years and never had to input any code to make it work. They assured me that the phone was new though. I got the phone, inserted my sim card and powered up to an AT&T logo along with the standard AT&T bloatware, I'm on Cricket so its the same network and the data and calling worked. After a little while playing with the phone i noticed that on a bright white background the center third of the screen looked dingy/yellow, brown. I did some research and found no related issues to this particular phone but some problems with other OLED screens having ugly whites. I changed the screen tones and it was a little better. Several hours later after playing an online game with my son I set the phone down on the table and it sounded like a thin piece of plastic, I looked and found the the back upper left corner of the glass was pulled away from the frame of the phone with a very noticeable gap, I could see glue residue where it should be sealed at. That was the final straw, I immediately started the return on Amazon, swapped my sim card back to my old phone, boxed it up and sent it back the next day.

The phone was very smooth. It took good pictures and played games at the highest resolution and frame rate. This particular phone did not come close to the quality I expected after reading so many great reviews.

A couple of days later I found this same phone through Cricket for 299. I went to the store and put my hands on the last one instock. The screen was excellent with clean bright white and no signs of the back coming loose from the frame. I bought the phone and have enjoyed it since. I also found that the phone Cricket is selling is truely unlocked, it doesn't even have Cricket logo on starting and the only bloatwear is from LG. I recommend this phone but be careful where you buy it from.

After updating it using said exploit though, the phone settles down at 2 GB of RAM with all bloatware removed. improved battery life by 1.5 hours.

The phone itself is great, amazing specs for the price.

Sadly its a hassle to get every bit out of it, honestly this is borderline a scam

title: Flagship components at a budget price
text:
I looked over a lot of phones looking for a replacement aging nexus 6, pocophone looked good but has questionable carrier compatibility and a lot of other unlocked phones in the >$300-400 range. All the budget phones had some serious down side, missing some key feature or just a low spec components. Then I stumbled on to the LG V35 and specs were on par with much pricier phones, the screen is oled witch I prefer and better than 1080, had expandable memory, cameras very good, battery hold charge for a long time. I was a little worried about LG as had bad experience with nexus 5x in the past, but looking at the reviews those issues were resolved. I also looked at the V40, but not a fan of the notch, and it is more money with similar specs. So my opinion is this is the best phone for the money right now, yes its been released a year ago, but compared to current phones in the price range V35 beats them no question. It is odd that this phone is not more popular, I guess at release $900 price tag scared people and then it faded out of the spotlight.

What I did not like: I am coming from a 6 inch phone the older wider screen, this screen is a little narrower. It is still good size, length wise about the same. When watching youtube vertically feels like a smaller screen. It is a little less bright than my old phone, could be a good thing as nexus was too bright at lowest setting when using at night. Coming off of stock android, I don't like LG and ATT bloatware and skins. The shareware is not a deal breaker, nothing that can't be worked around, but thought I mention it.

So I'm happy with the purchase and with the better components this phone should last me for a while, highly recommend this phone.

title: Fantastic phone for the money!
text:
I bought this device to activate on Straight Talk GSM, and as advertised, this product is unlocked. AT&T's bloatware is relatively unintrusive, and after cleanup it doesn't take up much of the device's internal storage.

With that said, it's an excellent phone with few compromises.

Overall, the LG V35's build quality is excellent. Beautiful glass exterior with a stylish design reminiscent of a Galaxy S9+. It feels great in the hand, even with a bulky impact case on. The 1440p OLED screen is fantastic as well. It's nearly as good as a Samsung panel.

Performance-wise, this device is quite snappy. The Snapdragon 845 and 6GB of RAM make multitasking a breeze, and there is no lag in LG's stock ROM at all, even with all the apps I have installed. The LTE modem delivers outstanding performance, as does the Wi-Fi modem. I've never been able to get 70mbps download over LTE in my back yard, but now I can.

The camera is great as well. The rear cameras take great still shots, and the front camera is more than adequate for Snapchat. Video is also quite good. The images are very vivid and crisp.

Battery life is acceptable, and it isn't really a problem if you have the included Fast Charge brick on hand.

Audio is also pretty good. It comes with a high-quality DAC for 3.5mm headphone audio playback, which sounds excellent. The mono speaker is decent for voice calls and talk shows, but is pretty shrill for music.

It does come with AT&T-specific features like Visual Voicemail, voice over LTE, and WiFi calling, but I have yet to get them working on Straight Talk.

My only concern is software updates. The included software is pretty good, but the security patches only reach November 2018, and LG is notorious for being slow with software updates. If you absolutely need up to date security patches, beware.

I would normally expect a phone like this to cost $700, and even then it's a reasonable price, especially if you're an AT&T customer. However, it's only $350, and it is an excellent deal. Would recommend.

title: A lot of potential, but not quite there
text:
After doing a bit of research I decided on this phone to replace an hold Honor 8 that I’ve been using with Metro PCS. My first impression is that the hardware was excellent, especially at this price point and the proprietary operating system was a bit buggy, but that wasn’t a deal breaker for me.

Pros:
Excellent battery life
Good cameras, especially at this price point
Fast finger print reader
Decent build quality

Cons:
Does not support many U.S. LTE bands (cross check with your carrier)
Screen brightness is good, but the screen is very reflective making it difficult to see in bright light
Screen appears to have a polarizing filter, meaning if you are wearing polarized sunglasses you will NOT be able to see the screen when holding the phone horizontally. This is very inconvenient, especially for taking horizontal photos on bright days.
Audio quality when using headphones is not as good as other phones I have owned
Intermittent issues with vibration alerts
Proprietary MIUI works well enough but it can be buggy and inconsistent at times

After using it for a few days I started to notice a few of the issues noted above that I unfortunately just can’t get past so I will be returning the phone. For me, the biggest issue is band compatibility for Metro PCS. I’m not very well versed in mobile lingo but I read many reviews that stated it worked well with Metro. I would say it works okay but I found that it did not work as well as my old Honor 8. After doing a bit more research I discovered that Metro operates it’s LTE service on six different bands. This phone only supports two of those six and the Honor supports three of the six. The one band that the Honor supports that this one doesn’t is band 12, which I understand helps with cell reception indoors and in some rural areas. I like the phone enough that I would be willing to accept the other flaws I mentioned but the poor reception compared to my old phone is a deal breaker for me. It’s an awesome phone if it works well on your network, but do your research and make sure it supports the bands you need.

title: Works great for about six months, then not so much
text:
I bought this in June 2019 because it had so many good reviews. The USB C Fast Charger, Anker 30W PIQ 3.0 Power Adapter worked great for the first few months that I bought it, then I started noticing when I plugged the USB C cable into my phone or my wife's phone it would not charge. Sometimes I would get a "incomplete connection" message on my phone. I thought it was the cable so I bought a brand new cable and at first that seemed to take care of the issue, but then within a couple of weeks it was doing it again. I thought maybe the Amazon Basics USB C cable I bought was just not good quality so I bought a different brand. Once again that seemed to resolve the issue for a short time but then it returned. So I tried yet another USB C cable (I guess I don't learn very fast) which once again seemed to get everything working for a few weeks, only for the problem to return.

Finally I decided to try other possibilities so I removed the Anker charger and replaced it with a different USB C wall charger using the exact same cable that was not working with the Anker charger. Lo and behold, it worked flawlessly and has been now for about a month.

The bottom line for me is that a charger should work way longer than just a few months before it starts having problems. At about $25 this isn't a super expensive charger but it's not super inexpensive either. If you want a charger that lasts longer than 4-6 months, you may want to try other options.

title: Outstanding Customer Service
text:
I purchased this USB C charger for my daughter’s iPhone 12. The charger did not disappoint; charging her phone much quicker than Apple’s charger. It is also very well constructed with a pleasing appearance and convenient foldable plug. Since it worked so well, I purchased a second charger for my wife’s iPhone 11; with the same results ... quick charge, easy to use, happy iPhone users. Unfortunately, approximately 9 months after I purchased my daughter’s charger, the charger stopped charging her phone. I figured I would buy another one to replace her charger but first reached out to Anker’s customer support (via email) to see if they could help. I was very impressed that they immediately responded to my email; recommending I’d try to reset the charger by leaving it unplugged from outlet and phone for 5 minutes, then retry it. I did that and it appeared to fix the charger. (The little light on the charger was remaining lit (not blinking) and the phone was charging.) I thought, great, that was a quick and simple fix. Unfortunately, after about 5 minutes, charger stopped charging and light was blinking again. I let Anker know what happened and they immediately responded that they would send me a new charger. They also emailed the return postage label for me to send back the defective charger. I let the Anker customer service rep (Cathy) know when I mailed their charger back to them. At that point, Cathy sent the replacement charger to me. Of course, delivery was delayed due to USPS struggles with keeping up with demand, but no problem ... I still had one quick charger in the house for the two professional surfers and charged my phone using the slow route. I got the replacement charger via USPS shortly after Anker sent another charger believing their first replacement charger was lost. Replacement charger works great ... just like my original...and USPS delivered the “lost” charger yesterday...

Really outstanding customer service and an outstanding product. I highly recommend this product based on its technical merits, but will remain a loyal customer to Anker due to its outstanding customer support.

Thanks Cathy, Thanks Anker!

I have been using this phone on Cricket, and it has been working fine, although it does not have all of the AT&T bands, but it has most. My main problem with this phone is that it was stuck on EMUI 9 and a very old security patch. That was a problem, because when you have the phone in the USA, it did not update because of the trade embargo and it was seen as out of region, but I bought a Hong Kong SIM card on Amazon for $5, inserted it, and the updates started flooding in. The SIM card did not need to be activated; it just needed to see a SIM card that was not for North America. It did over three hours of updates, and I eventually got up to EMUI 10 (Android 10). The phone has such great specs for the price. The screen is just amazing; I will not go back to a non-AMOLED screen; those blacks are just so rich and dark. title: Not for use on AT&T
text:
This is a beautiful phone, but it has significant drawbacks in my daily usage.

Drawbacks:
1-Cannot be used on AT&T (or possibly other networks phasing out 3G capabilities)
a) Although the phone does have 4G capabilities, AT&T will treat it as a 3G phone and eventually boot you off the network if you try to activate your existing SIM card on this device (because AT&T is phasing out 3G support by 2022 and will suspend the lines of users who attempt to activate new devices that it recognizes as 3G on its network)

b Also, while I was able to use it on AT&T (both before they suspended my line, and after they re-activated it), I had horrible call quality. I could hear people well, but they couldn't hear me; even the AT&T reps that I called using 611 asked to call me on another phone. This issue may follow the device on other networks other than AT&T where it chooses to use 3G. I have been informed of possible resolutions to this issue, such as going into network settings and choosing a preference for 4G, or using a network switching app to detect and change network preferences, but because of 1a) (I don't want my line suspended again), I won't be investigating those solutions.

2-Not IPX7 (meaning does not meet the standard of being able to be underwater for up to 1m for up to 30min). I checked my GSMArena and PhoneArena specs and they indicated that the Mate 20Pro is rated IPx7, so I felt comfortable strapping it to my arm and dipping into Lake Michigan for a splash (think horsing around in the water, not swimming laps or a triathlon). The phone functioned normally during and for about a couple of hours afterwards, but then its screen started to show lines and the camera showed issues. Eventually using the phone because near impossible. The vendor sent me a replacement, but I am in no mood to test it again to see if I just had the bad luck to get a bad apple.

3-Back texture manages to both be slippery, but also have a grating feeling when I run my fingers across it (similar to the hair-raising feeling I get when knives are sharpened against other metal). The clear back cover that comes included with the device deals with both issues, but I hate using covers, especially with such beautiful devices. So I have to be extra careful to ensure that it doesn't slip. And the metallic plate I placed on the back gives me a surface to touch that doesn't have that grating texture.

4-Cannot take videos near loud speakers. This is a funny issue; I attended a dance competition and wanted to take pictures, but I think that the Optical Image Stabilization was overloaded by the vibrations for the loudspeaker nearby and resulted in blurred images. From looking at the images, I may as well have set the phone on the speaker itself. PS this wasn't a huge speaker, and it wasn't especially loud, but it seemed enough to render the camera unusable.

The nice things about this phone:
1-It looks nice...without a case.
It is a lovely phone to look at. I love the red accent on the power button against an emerald green phone. It also manages to look nice when you use the clear plastic back case that comes with the phone.

2-Working Dual-SIM, this was one of the primary reasons for which I got this phone, and it does work (unlike other manufacturers who lock this feature for phones sold in the USA).

3-Decent software support, it is currently on EMUI 11, but I don't know how much longer it will get software support after 2021.

So given the first drawback (Unable to use on 4G networks in general), I would not recommend anyone buy this device as a phone for use in the USA, especially on AT&T.

title: A beast smartphone packed with key features
text:
I've had this for about 3 weeks as my main phone. Contrary to "light leaking" and glue gate claims, the model I received is fine. So there are no issues to report regarding that. I'm in the US on AT&T. No issues with coverage whatsoever. Ok, onto the pros and cons.

Pros:
- Battery life: Absolutely the best on any smartphone right now. I easily get around 35 hours (moderate to heavy usage on YouTube, Instagram, FB). I've had the iPhone XS Max, Pixel 3 XL, Samsung S9+, etc and with this phone, I don't feel the need to search for an outlet.
- Super fast charging: this is on par with the OnePlus, if not better with 40w charging. 70% in 30mins is factual - I have tried it myself.
- Form factor: I have smaller hands but the 6.3" screen in this frame is a joy to handle. Easier to hold than a Note 9.
- Camera: You won't get a perfect shot everytime like the Pixel 2/3 series but the versatility of lenses is unmatched in 2019. The wide, telephoto, and 5x hybrid zoom are fun to play with and sharp. You just need to play with all the modes depending on what you're capturing. There are many modes to choose from. I'd rate this camera just behind the and Pixel 3 but ahead of the iPhone X's.
- Gestures: You can maximize screen real estate by using screen gestures similar to the iPhone X's. Love this btw. No need for the usual 3 nav buttons.
- IR blaster
- Desktop mode mirroring onto your smart tv (similar to Samsung Dex but totally wireless)

Cons:
- Notifications: they do not always display on the lockscreen (which is odd). Kind of a bummer but not a deal breaker.
- Vibration motor: iPhone X is still King in this department. Huawei's is a tad weak.
- Carrier availability: not sold in US.

Overall: this is a true beast of a phone. It's a shame Americans don't have a chance to experience this powerhouse jam-packed with features. With outstanding battery life and super fast charging, amazing camera, great form factor, gorgeous screen, this is truly worth every penny you pay for.

title: Most Impressive Smartphone of 2018, period! No exassuration!
text:
I am a mobile app programmer, and have dozens of both Android and iOS devices out of necessity. As I have been doing this for some time (since 2011), I am quite jaded when it comes to smartphones and for the last several years, have not been at all excited about new flagship smartphones that have come out. I am, however, pleasantly surprised and excited enough to write a quick review on this Huawei Mate 20 Pro.

First off, I do not work for Huawei or any device manufacturer. Second, I was lucky to get a unit that does not have the screen bleed issue that some users apparently have unfortunately, from the first shipments of the device. I have now used my Mate 20 Pro as my daily driver for a full work week, and actually enjoy picking it up and using it, like when these type of devices first came out.

Some things that are notable and what stands out----

(a) The phone is noticeably fast... actually very fast. I know it's got the latest and greatest 8-core Kirin 980 processor, but until you use it for daily activities, you don't realize the difference from other devices. Example: I can scroll through a Facebook or Instagram feed very fast, while every video is *playing back* in each post with no stuttering or glitching. Any button I tap, or app I start instantly loads up, and is addictive to see everything respond so quickly.

(b) Something about the screen is very very sharp. I keep mine at the full 3120x1440 WQHD+ resolution, and for some reason, it seems sharper and brighter than other flagship phones I had as my daily driver this year including the LG G7, iPhone X and the Huawei Mate 10 Pro.

(c) The 4200 mah battery is incredible. Example: I'll go to sleep with the phone fully charged. I'll use my phone all day as usual, and by the time I go to sleep, it's still at 56% or so battery left. This is with watching Youtube videos, listening to music, emails, Facebook, Instagram, testing my apps and the usual. Also, it has this 'reverse' wireless charging feature, and my friends trip out when I take my iPhone X, and place it on top of the Mate 20 Pro and it starts charging!

(d) The in-screen finger print scanner is something else. It has this cool bright blue/white flash for a second when it reads my finger and it logs me in instantly. I've also got the face recognition turned on so I have both, and its novelty is still amusing 6 days in.

(e) The build quality is top notch. It feels like I have a very premium device, as it should, having paid $1049 for it. Well worth the money.

(f) The ability to clone apps (i.e. have 2 Facebook apps, each logged in with a different account), as well as completely cloning your phone, so there's a completely separate copy (like a dual boot PC) is very cool for a device of this calibre. Very useful when testing environment needs are different than what my daily driver settings are.

(g) The 3 cameras main cameras, the 40mp main, 20mp ultra wide angle, and 8mp telephoto work very very well. I have been partial to LG phones for a while because they were the only ones with the wide angle camera, but now that this flagship Huawei has it, I'm sticking with the Huawei now.

(h) I have a pair of some wireless bluetooth Sony WM-1000XM3 headphones that I use with it, and the audio is incredible. This of course may just be the headphones themselves, but I got both at the same time.

(i) Everything is just incredibly fast on this device, so it makes you want to touch every app, tinker with it, etc. just because everything comes up instantaneously.

I realize the U.S. Intelligence agencies warn against Huawei devices because of suspected ties to the Chinese government, but as a random civilian user with nothing really to hide, I have to say this is an excellent device and really shows Chinese hardware makers have upped their game to the top of the global food chain. I highly recommend it for those who don't mind spending money for quality products.

p.s. As a final note, I do not use the Huawei ID, nor created an account. I just use only my Google Account with it, so I may not be getting all the frills that come with that, but even without, it blows away all other devices I've had this year by a wide margin.

title: HUAWEI, Where Have You Been All My Life? THE BEST PHONE!
text:
7 months of ownership. Mate 20 Pro. One hell of phone better than Samsung or Apple for seriously about half the price (when I bought it pre-COVID in Oct. 2019). I'm a 25+ year pro commercial photographer, and the camera / lenses (Leica, no less!) are nothing short of amazing. I also do pro printing, and I can display the 30" prints from the Mate 20 Pro right alongside the 30" prints from my Sony A7RIII. Especially the semi-macro stuff! Camera is fast, responsive, but lenses and resolution are just incredible. Phone function is perfect. Battery life longer than a day, usually 2 days, and I use full power all the time, and this is my business phone so it gets A LOT of use. Phone supports fast charging and it is FAST. Goes from 8% to 98% power in about half an hour. Also has wireless charging which is also really convenient. This phone came with Google Play, so it has all the Google Play apps AND you have access to all the Huawei equivalent apps, so it's the best of both worlds. I find myself using many of the Huawei apps. HereWeGo mapping app is at least as good as Google Maps. And I prefer Huawei email apps. Lots and lots of options, many of which I do not use as I really bought this primarily for the crazy good camera. Phone can double as a hot spot. Huawei's desktop app is very useful. You can backup your phone to your own PC, not just to someone's "cloud". And it works great.
Had to throw a Hong Kong SIM card (cheap, 13bucks, on Amazon) in the phone to BEGIN receiving software updates, but after that it has received all Google updates, security updates, and HUAWEI updates on its own. So whatever it cost, add thirteen smackers for that convenience. Still a great deal. Updated to Android 10, EMUI 10, and yes, it is nice! You will need a case. The phone without a case is too slippery. It will slide off anything. I recommend the Unicorn Beetle case. And I don't throw my phone around, but I do get around carrying it mostly in my pocket. This phone has held up better than any phone I've ever owned. Especially the charging port...All is like new, seriously LIKE NEW after 7 months. Absolute keeper. I think USA sanctions HUAWEI because HUAWEI is making such great phones with latest tech and pricing them where they are AFFORDABLE for anyone. But the Mate 20 Pro came out before the sanction nonsense, so you're good with this phone if that is a concern. You have Google and HUAWEI and all updates in one device.
CONS: It's slippery. A case is a requirement if you use a phone like I do. And hat's it. I cannot find fault with this magnificent device. I waited 7 months to write this review because this was my first HUAWEI device and wanted to make sure it was built solid for the long haul. Well, it is, and this is my first HUAWEI, but it will definitely not be my last HUAWEI.

title: Exceeded my high expectations
text:
I don't buy a new cell phone very often, but when I do, I do a lot of research ahead of time. Every review, especially those from Europe and Asia, led me to buy this phone. I figured that if the Europeans with their tough privacy and cyber security laws, and the savvy Asian tech shoppers from Singapore and Hong Kong like this phone so much, I was going to give it a try. I figured Huawei overtook Apple to become the second largest smartphone brand in the world for a reason.
I have had this phone now for a week. I can say that I am surprised that I am using it over my (new very fast Macbook pro) lap top for the first time. This phone is very fast and has very sharp images. The wifi and LTE reception are super compared to a dozen of other units in my household -- a true pleasure to use. I work in hospitals that require me to log into the hospital computers no matter where I am to review detailed, often urgent and complex cases that often contain large image files. Patient confidentiality is also a big cyber issue. Up to this point, I could never do that with a cell phone nor even on a high resolution IPad. With this phone, with its amazing speed and QHD resolution, I am finally able to give up my laptop. The facial recognition, the thumb print entry features on top of pass codes are reassuring.
This phone came with a very nice "tips" icon. I have only tried out a few of their amazing artificial intelligence features. They actually worked. I was shock that you can point the camera at any document in any language and get it translated instantly into any other language in the world. The camera images are truly amazing -- very very sharp, telephoto lens...!
So far, smoothly running all my google apps, investment apps, audible, Netflix ... -- no complaints at all.

title: BEWARE VERY BAD REPAIRS!!!
text:
Ordered end of November around April screen started flashing and then it was unusable. Amazon said no warranty on them, local Huawei dealer would not take it under warranty either.
Around July I decided to try and repair myself, in any case it was bad already. So I bought screen replacement.
My surprise is that when I tried to open the battery cover it came off easily without any heat. It was glued with just some pieces of double tape!!! SO THERE WAS NO WATER RESISTANCE ON THE THING...
When I started to disassemble I found it had 5 SCREWS MISSING...
There was a big fingerprint in the metal of power board...
The little board where antenna cable connects had a BROKEN PIECE where the screw goes in...
There is a frame that holds the front camera in place but it was gone in the phone THEY DID NOT PUT IT BACK IN...
Almost no thermal paste for board cooling it was just barely touching the metal

When I described this to amazon customer service they understood and gave credit for a local repair since I am out of the country, I have to recognize them for that. When I found out how the phone was inside I felt very cheated.

title: I hate to have to write this review
text:
I loved Google phones. I've had them all my life. The Pixel 3 was the latest one I bought, about 18 months ago. I also loved the Google Fi ecosystem. I spent around $600 dollars on the device. I was so exited. Reviews were great too.

A good pro - it charged up very fast, but battery life wasn't spectacular. It did have a very nice display + camera.

Hardware wise - it was an absolute nightmare for me. Headphones did not reliably work after six months. Sometimes they would "kick in" and work, sometimes they would not. I tried multiple headphones. After about a year, the phone started shutting down on its own, entering into a constant reboot loop and heating up. This happened occasionally at first. Then it happened all the time. Then it stopped happening for a couple of weeks only to start up again. Factory rebooting it once in a while was a nightmare. As an FYI - I never dropped the phone and it still looks great.

I use this phone for work too, so I really need something reliable. After this phone rebooted during a call with a colleague, I decided I had enough. It was downright embarrassing. Google gave me a rough indication that it would cost me around $400 at least to fix by an authorized third party company, and I'd be without the phone for a while.

So I just quit. Something I paid $600 or so for should be reliable for a little while. I turned to what I thought was the dark side and purchased an Iphone, After all these years I never thought I would turn to Apple.

I think Google Android systems have so much potential, that said having had this iphone now for a month - it just feels way more stable. Maybe a little less sexy, but it feels so much more reliable. I also ditched the Google FI plan and don't regret it.

So yeah - Google, we had a thing going there for a while, but I kind of feel you bailed out on me. Good while it lasted.

title: Worst phone of all Google products that I ever had
text:
Ok, Google, you failed me BIG time.

I was a faithful android user for years, I had almost all of the Google phones there were.
Although they all had some minor glitches, nothing too big to stop me from enjoying my google phone.

I purchased this particular phone with the consideration that Google equals quality.
I could always rely on my google phone and be sure it won't fail me.
This had been my statement for many years, I even managed to convince several determined apple product users to give Google a chance.

However this particular phone is the WORST I ever had.
To say that I over-payed to be extremely dissatisfied is to horribly underestimate.
I wish I have returned this piece of horror while I still could.

1) Day 1 it arrived it started having bluetooth connectivity issues.
The sound will cut off/disappear and then come back.
Not the connection issue, definitely the phone's bug.
Problem was solved by reloading the phone.
This problem arises almost every day and I have to reload the phone often

2) Day 2 - phone shut off due to overheating.

3) after about a couple weeks of having the phone I started having proximity sensor issues.
When my hand will be close to the top of the page, the screen would just go black.
Guess how this was solved? Yes - just reload. Kind of reminds me of Windows :))))

4) Unlimited storage in the cloud has something going wrong,
because my cloud always reminds me that I have a tiny amount of space left and need to do something about it.

However I was hoping that all of the issues would be resolved with the new version of Android.
Guess what?
After a new Android version was released a couple of days ago and I installed it, things got WORSE!
A new bug in addition to unresolved previous ones is introduced - the hotspot could not turn on!
I can not believe it. My Google product is getting worse and worse.
I literally feel like throwing this thing into the garbage.
Here you go reliability, quality etc.

Although being Android faithful for years, I am seriously considering to go all the way Apple.
What is going on with you, Google?

UPDATE:
I contacted Google and obviously overheating is one of the major issues with this phone, because they have a special team dedicated to this!

These ridiculous instructions were handled to me by Google regarding overheating.

These basically mean: don't use GPS, wi-fi, 4G, daydream view, any apps the phone did not come with, do not adjust display brightness, turn off your device frequently so it can cool down.
don't use anything normally and comfortably on this phone, limit everything and turn off everything. If the phone can not do the simple things, why would I even use it?

And mind you, why do you talk about the watch in "Android wear section", could you have at least edited the copy-paste you have sent to me? I did not contact you because of the watch!

QUOTE FROM GOOGLE:
"If your device sometimes feels warmer than normal, there usually isn't cause for concern. Letting the device ‘take a break’ from use or limiting/turning off features (even those running in the background) could remedy the situation.

Here are some tips/suggestions:

Media apps (music, video games):
Close or turn off other apps and features that you're not using; they may be running in the background.
Discontinue using the media temporarily until the temperature normalizes.

User-installed apps:
Put the device in safe mode to disable 3rd party apps and see if the issue improves.
Try uninstalling recently installed apps to pinpoint the app causing the issue.

Display brightness:
Manually setting the brightness to be very bright may contribute to higher device temperature.
Consider setting to auto brightness or manually reducing the brightness setting.

GPS / 3G / WiFi - prolonged data connectivity:
Turn off feature when not in use.
Stop or limit use and allow device to cool down if it gets warm.

Exposure to direct heat :
Remove from heat and keep away from direct heat or excessive sunlight.

Poor ventilation:
Expose the device rather than keeping it tucked away in poor ventilated/tight areas (layers, small pockets, bags).

Cases:
Don't use a case that covers the front and back of the device.
Use an official case (available on Google Store in some countries).

Chargers:
Don't use unofficial chargers which can overcharge and degrade the battery.
Use official charger (available on Google Store in some countries).

Daydream View:
Daydream View requires high performance from the device. The device's temperature should stay within safe limits.
Remove any protective cases from the device to improve thermal ventilation.
If your device feels too hot, stop using Daydream View and allow the device to cool down.

Android Wear:
Power off the device for 5-10 minutes and turn it on again.
Try using the watch for another day to see if your issue improves. If your watch is still warm after a day, reply to this email and let us know.

Please trye below steps if the issue is not fixed.
Steps : Reset your device to factory settings.
If the issue is still not resolved or if you can't enable safe mode, resetting the device to factory settings may help. This will erase all local data on your device, so I'd recommend backing up your personal pictures, music and video files."

title: Updated review -- returned and still waiting for a refund
text:
I have returned this phone and am waiting for my refund, but have not yet received it.

I bought this phone to make use of the Live Caption feature that Google offers. The reviews saying this is a verizon locked phone is partially true but partially not. It comes with a Verizon Sim card you can remove, but when you go to your own company for their Sim, it will give you a verizon number and mess it up for you with the company you are going through (I tried it with TMobile and they couldn't figure out why the number I was issued was a verizon number). The Live Caption feature is horrible becuase it has some silly recording at the beginning that anyone that calls you or anyone you call has to listen to before you can have a conversation. Most people hang up becuase they think its a scammer. Forget trying to do automated calls with it where you need to pick 1 or 2 to get in touch with someone, it won't work. The calls made from this phone or sent to this phone come out all garbled and fuzzy so the other person cannot understand you at all. The calls are NOT clear on wifi nor are they clear on cell, we tried both and calling was really bad.
The battery length they advertise is not accurate at all. I had to recharge this phone 3 times in one day. My old moto e 6 I can run a whole day and a half using it before charging but this pixel phone has to be charged OFTEN and I don't do much on my phone at all, just some texting and my email coming through once a day that is it. I do not play games on it or do any social media on it and still it needed charged 3 times in one day. Looking at battery use, it wasn't showing anything using that much battery.
I also don't like that hte battery is not replaceable. In my older moto e6 phone I have a replacable battery.
There also is no phone jack on this phone, but for me that wasn't an issue. they are supposed to come with earbuds but mine did not come with them, but that didnt matter to me.

I would not recommend this phone to anyone unfortunately. After finding out that the calls on the other end were so horrible this phone would not be a good fit for anyone.

text:

But the battery..... beware, the battery on this phone is known to swell. Mine happened about 14 months after I bought the phone. At the time I didn't know the battery bloat was a known issue. I actually didn't take my phone out of the case, so I didn't even know it was swollen. I just knew my battery was dying. Their customer service just kept saying to do a factory reset. or delete apps until you find the one that was killing battery charge. Even though they knew battery issues were happening, and that they were replacing batteries, free of charge, for out of warranty phones (like mine). Nothing worked, so I preordered a pixel 4A to be delivered in a month when they were released. I processed a trade in for my pixel 3 and got a decent price. Over that next month, my phone was useless unless it was plugged in.

Then I got the 4A, which isn't as good in my opinion. but at least the battery works now. Then google only gives me 1/3 the estimated value for my traded in pixel 3. Because of the battery. Which is THEIR defective product. But still, it becomes my financial liability. And all they keep saying is their terms and conditions say the refund given depends on the condition the phone arrives in. Even though the phone is 100% fine outside of their own product defect.

So I paid a lot of money for a phone that died in 14 months due to a defect, and they did nothing for it. Avoid google. Their customer service is horrible. They just want your money.

title: New, unlocked, software upgradeable.
text:
March 15, 2021. A previous reviewer left a very helpful tip about these being delivered with a Verizon SIM installed.

When I received this, the sealed box had an overlay sticker saying New, Unlocked All Carriers. It does appear new and unused, all accessories are present and also new and unused. Before I turned it on, I checked and it did indeed already have a Verizon SIM installed. I removed it and put in a Mint Mobile SIM, and then powered it on. Set-up went fine, and it showed Mint service and made calls fine.

It was running Android 9. I hit Check Updates, and it offered Android 10. No problems updating. Reset and checked update again, and it offered security updates. Repeat after each update. Eventually I got through the backlog of updates, it's now on Android 11 and the March 2021 security update. Completely current. The Pixel 3 is scheduled for one more major update later this year, which is good news for future use of this phone.

It updates fine directly from google, has a fresh battery, and there is no evidence of any Verizon bloatware. The Access Point Names settings only show expected data from my Mint account, nothing Verizon. I think this is truly a factory unlocked phone, that Verizon only preintalled their SIM into when they initially were selling this stock.

It's a premium up-to-date Android experience with another major update to come, and a fresh battery, at a fraction of the cost of a current Pixel flagship. I'm very satisfied with the value.
