title: Good price for moderate users
text: This phone came unlocked as stated  Upon turning on the phone, the AT&T sign popped up.  I was a bit nervous initially as I have another GSM carrier T-Mobile; however, it did not turn out to be an issue.  I put in my SIM and was able to start using my new phone the same day without contacting T-Mobile. Transferring data from my old Samsung to the new one using the apps is simple and fast.  The phone is thin and the width is about right as I can have a good grip without a phone case.  Battery life is better than all the Samsung phones I had in the past. I was able to talk for 3 hours and played a simple video game for 2 hours without an immediate need to recharge.  I haven't downloaded any movies; therefore unable to comment.  Pictures I took are crisp.  I used to have issues using the Google Translate app in Samsung phones.  The words I typed in the app would automatically get duplicated.  It was an ongoing complaints for years and Samsung finally fixed the issue - at least not happening on this new phone. In terms of functionalities, there is no special surprises; however, if you are a moderate user and need a budget smart phone, it should satisfy your need.

title: Kinda pricey, but great at what it does.
text: I'm using this 45W charger primarily to recharge my Valve Steam Deck. For those curious, it works fantastically well and seems to put out just as much juice as the factory charger. I can play games at full load and it'll still put juice back into the battery. Packaging is minimal, like all Anker products, which is totally fine; packaging waste is awful. The charger itself is surprisingly compact and has a single USB C output, so you'll need a cable to match your device. It uses PD power delivery so it can 'negotiate' with your device to determine the proper amount of power to pull. My Pixel 5 fast charges with this charger as well. When plugged in I get the "Charging Rapidly" notification. I've also used it to charge up my DJI Mavic 3 and the RC Pro, both of which it handles well. All-in-all I think it's a great product although it seems a bit pricey; admittedly I've never bought a high-wattage charger before so that's just me feeling cheap. Anker hasn't let me down with any  of the stuff I've bought from them and I think this is another quality product.

title: Well, you cannot ever get enough chargers.  Can you?
text:
I have multiple devices with use USB power. Can probably find a charger around here with my eyes clothes. BUT speed of charging is the key. Although we have several fast chargers and some Samsung 35W super fast charger, I was intrigued when I saw a tech video, where this 'ultra-fast' 45W ultra fast charger was featured.
1. It is bulkier than the Samsung 35W chargers, but it has folding electric plug tongs, so it still takes up only a little bit of space in a travel bag.
2. I tested with a phone that had a level of battery charger indicator. With the phone at about 20% of full charge, this device reduced the charging time by about 10 minutes compared to the 35W Samsung. Essentially for any phone I have, they will be fully charged in less than 1 hour, from near empty.

3. Tablets with a big batteries obviously take a little bit longer. But I saw improvements in their charging times by about 20 minutes. I'm impressed.

NOTE: As with any new charger, I never leave them in overnight, until I am comfortable they are working appropriately. Also, for the very first charge of a device, I check the temperature of the new charger and the device to make sure it is not faulty or being overloaded. Hot devices are definitely a sign of trouble.

Every device can't handle that much power going into it.

title: Life on the road with the Anker Nano II 45w charger
text: One of the things I truly enjoy is finding solutions which will work across my devices with no problems. I was after a single device for use on the road since I basically vagabond forever being retired. I wanted to charge my iPhone 12 Pro and my MacBook Air M1 and just buy two decent cables. The 45w charger fits the bill perfectly for me since it fits so easily into a smaller messenger bag that holds all my stuff. I can be in-between hotels or airbnb locations at a Starbucks or in the lobby of the hotel I checked out of and this one small device will power anything up I have. I have had such good luck with Anker products over the years so it was really a no brainer when I saw the 45w Anker Nano II come out. For travel, the plug ends fold in which I think is a necessity for fitting in smaller messenger bags. I dislike plug ends that stick out in the bag. It just doubles the size of the device basically. I don't have subjective measurements for charging my iPhone 12 Pro but the thing works in so many settings from hotel rooms to train stations to airports. Also it provides a lot of flexibility if the desire is to have a single device do multiple things for you. Anker clearly designed this with flexibility and use and for my type of vagabonding around, ease of storage and carrying. Excellent device to use in all the settings I care about.

text:
now that I am starting to get out more, travel, ETC, I need something I can rely on and something which is compatible with my various types of devices. I have an HP Spectre Windows laptop, a MacBook Pro 2019, an iPad Pro, and a Google Pixel 6. Let me say that this little square baby can handle them all. I paired it with an Anker USB C to USB C cable, and it's a match made in heaven. About the only slight issue, and this is not the fault of this charger, is that my HP Spectre charges a bit slower than what it would normally charge if I keep using the provided charging cable. However, this is simple math. This Nano charger is 45W and the one which came with my HP is 65W. Still though, that is a small price to pay for the smaller size and the greater flexibility. So, if speed of charging a laptop is not an issue, you will be fine. While this charging cube gets a little hot, that is normal and it doesn't get so hot that it will pose a fire hazard. The foldable prongs make it so you can travel with it easily andnot risk punching holes in your travel pouch/purse/case/pocket. I love this thing so much, that I bought one for my wife, just so I don't have to share.
Get it, I think you will be pleased.

title: Quick, flexible and tiny
text:
Anker makes such good products generally speaking but these chargers with the 45W charging capacity charge my iPhone 13 Pro extremely fast, meeting Apple’s fast charge specs. Plus they’re flexible in the sense that because they can charge up to a 45w performance level, they can also charge my iPad Pro 12.5 using the same charger. And they’re flexible also in the sense that it’s really a travel charger all in one because of it’s size. And this Anker model has the collapsing prongs, which means it’s footprint is even smaller.

One thing to note is that the port on this charger accomodates USB-C devices so if you don’t have a USB-C cable on one end and the required connected (whether USB-C or Lightning) on the other, you’ll have to get a different charger.

The quality of the chargers build is extremely good. It feels solid and the prongs don’t simply fall down when folded away; a good sign if a high quality build and design.

As I said, i gave this charger 5 stars and definitely recommend it to someone looking for a charger flexible enough to charge your tablets and phones.

title: Possible false advertising. Doesn't charge at 45w
text:
Using an S22 Ultra, charging my phone brings up 'super fast charging' on screen. This Amazon page tells you it will charge at 45w, but it's actually not true.

When you're charging at 45w, you'll see the prompt 'super fast charging 2.0'. If you don't see 2.0, you're only charging at 25w.

I didn't spend $40 for a 25w charger. I bought this because it advertised to charge samsung phones at 45w, but it clearly isn't true.

Using the Ampere app which monitors battery details, it states the highest rate of charge it received was 4330 mAh, which is around 20w. It's clear that the 45w feature just isn't working.

Writing this on 3/4/22. Going to update it if I find a solution. If I don't, I returned it and bought the official charger.

title: Great for the price & travel
text:
I’ve always loved Anker products, and when I saw that they released the Nano II charger, I knew that I just had to get it.

Beginning with the build of the charger, as always, Anker has yet to fail me. You can pick up this charger and just tell it was made to be durable.
The connection prongs toward the rear are also quite durable. I’ve plugged this charger in at an angle of around 20-35 degrees & haven’t bent the prongs. The best part about the connect prongs is that it can fold in itself, making it a GREAT charger for travel.

When it comes to charging, I haven’t been able to “scientifically” test the difference between charging speeds. If you’re upgrading to the Nano II charger from a regular Apple iPhone wall charger, there’s a significant difference in charging speed that you’ll obviously notice.

Just like everything else that produces electricity, heat will be produced. If you were to touch the charger while it’s been actively charging, it won’t be enough to give you a first degree burn, but it’s hot enough for you to realize. You won’t act in reflex & suddenly pull your hand back, the heat produced hasn’t been that bad in my experience.

With at least 5 months of use, I haven’t had any complaints with this charger. It’s been able to maintain the same speed from when I first began using it.

If you’re looking to upgrade your charger, the Nano II is the way to go.

title: It was great while it worked... then it caused problems
text:
I used this adapter primarily as a travel adapter, and when I worked away from home. It was the block/plug I'd use for my MacBook Air, iPad Pro, and everything else that has a USB-C. It worked great at first, then after a few months it stopped. While I'm not sure if it's related, when the problems started - the USB I'd plug into on my MBA also burned out.

Unfortunately, I was outside of the return period for this product - so I filed a warranty claim with Anker. But they require you to send the defective product back to them before sending out a replacement. However, they later emailed me saying they would send a replacement on the front end (which they stated they normally don't do), but I still need to send the defective one back. I wouldn't have been so annoyed except I don't own a printer for the return slip, and the hassle to print something exceeds the hassle to just buy something else off of Amazon, or the same amount of hassle as going to the store to buy a similar replacement. If this was an expensive product, I would have gone through the warranty process, and left a better review as long as I didn't have the same problem with the warranty replacement. However, for such an inexpensive product, the inconvenience of their warranty process exceeds the value of buying something else.

The first gen nano I purchased is still going strong, same with other products of theirs I own - so I'm disappointed that this one didn't pan out as it's much smaller and compact than the ones that come from apple

title: Operating temperature limitations.
text:
With any new product, I read the instruction manual (or instruction sheet) first.
With this product, I read that "The maximum ambient temperature during use of the appliance must not exceed 25 degrees C."

This is ridiculous. 25C is equivalent to 77F.
So that means make sure you're in an air-conditioned room when using this device ("the appliance"), or else, presumably, it may become over-stressed and/or fail. As an electronics engineer, I can tell you this seems like a mediocre / marginal design. Plus, who knows what the likely resulting failure mode might be: if the device simply stops working and generates 0 volts, then who cares. But if failure means generating voltage larger than the spec (something that may damage your device that receives this electricity) that means propagation of failure.

I suspect I'll be returning my newly acquired "appliance," as referenced above.

title: ** UPDATE **Folding prongs bad design
text:
See update below review:

Looks can be deceiving. The ANKER USB-C 25W PD Fast Wall Charger looks well designed and sturdy, but the smallest error in calculations or the manufacturing process going awry can destroy the best of intentions.

It was about a month after receiving the charger that I started to have issues with it working. I started to send it back then (about 6 weeks ago) , however my past experience with Anker products being reliable, at a lower price point than top of the line of electrical/electronic products and not wanting to go through the return process had me hesitate. Now it is acting up again on a more regular basis.

The problem is that the folding of the outlet prongs don't stay set internally and the prongs fold just enough to lose contact inside the unit and then it stops charging. I have jiggled and fiddled with putting up with it for too long now. I don't feel that sending back an electrical product after using it this long is proper.

However, I did see that even though the return window had closed, there was product support for 90 days and it was within this parameter. So I chatted with an Amazon support bot and finally had to request a call back. The Amazon live agent did a good will return on this. Not sure I should have used a 'good will' credit for such a low priced item, but I did.

All in all I would not recommend this charger. In the future I think I will try not to get a charger with folding prongs for travel. I have plenty of these that still work and the chance of them not being made correctly and thus not working is multipled over a simple normal stationary prong.
*** UPDATE JAN 13 2023 ***
Anker saw the review that I did on this charger and the problem with the folding prongs that were defective and not allowing electricity to flow through to the charger. They reached out to me and asked if I would like a refund or replacement. This was done quite a while past any normal return period. They say that they guarantee most of their products for 18 months (I think I have this correct) but I was surprised to get such a message for an electronic product. I accepted the full refund as I had already purchased another charger without folding prongs. Kudos to Anker for such a responsible, caring attitude!!

FAST/SUPERFAST CHARGING: When my S23 battery is really low this charger definitely charges it a very fast rate of roughly 2% per minute, and then properly slows down the charging level as the battery gets fuller (definitely charges much faster when battery is at 0-20% than at 60%-70%) so that the phone doesn't overheat. I actually put a battery heat app on my phone and checked it periodically throughout the charge, and it never got above the high 80s laying on a cool desk with no apps actively running (other than the battery checking app).

REGULAR CHARGING: I've also hooked it up to plenty of USB devices that don't support fast charging, and it has charged them just fine.

Very happy camper.

title: Fast, reliable, and durable charger – a full charge in just over an hour
text:
I bought this charger because my phone unfortunately did not come with one and I wanted something faster than the 10W wireless charger I had. When I first took it out of the box, it had a good weight to it—not too heavy, but not like typical plastic chargers that you have to be careful of not to break. It also has a retractable plug which I thought was nice for storage and travel.

When I charged my 2-year-old 4000mah Galaxy S21 with the wire it came with, starting from 10%, it went to 100% in 1 hour and 9 minutes. It also charged my other devices that didn't support 25W charging, such as my wireless headphones. Note that you do need a USB-C cable (not USB-A) for this charger.

Overall, I have no complaints. It's reliable and having a 25W one is great as it wastes less time waiting for devices to charge.

title: Potential Coil Whine
text:
[[VIDEOID:31a1906aca3056fab6f3e1cf008c23e1]] Honestly the charger is super portable and the fact that you can keep the prongs folded makes it a good traveling option. My unit has coil whine and is ver noticeable, specially at night when everything is silent, if you keep your phone near you. The sound is only present when I am super charging, and it goes away when I turn it off. This happens to me with a Samung S23. Aside from the noise, the charger works as advertised, fast charging times with very good heat dissipation.
It is important to say that coil whine can be annoying but it not something that impacts performance. And it is not something every unit experiences, I just had bad luck. ANKER has great customer service, reach out to them with any questions or concerns.

title: Note 10 Pro-What's In Box/Clarifications/
text:
I just wanted to clear up a few details from other reviews I read prior to purchasing the Redmi Note 10 Pro.

I purchased the item in late July 2022 for $240+ tax. Tax was around $18. This is my second Redmi; I also have the Note 7. I loved that phone, but wanted to upgrade because the battery was losing life, it was slowing down, and I wanted a better camera. I seriously researched this item for several months before deciding on the Note 10 Pro (over the 5G model and regular Note 10, Note 9, Note 11, etc).

Confusion in other reviews: I live in Utah, United States. I use MINT MOBILE for a service provider. There are absolutely ZERO ISSUES with the Mint sim card and this phone. It works fine. I have seen other reviews saying it the phone "doesn't work in the US". This is flat-out wrong. Research the item and your provider before buying. DON'T WRITE AN INACCURATE REVIEW telling people not to buy the phone because you have a provider that doesn't work with this brand. Amazon should take these reviews down. The phone is compatible with GSM providers. Period.

Secondly, regarding the charger. The phone comes with a Euro Type C wall charger. However, the vendor included an adaptor so that it works with American wall outlets. I was worried about this before buying, but again, the vendor included an adaptor. The vendor I purchased from is called OMEGA DISTRIBUTION USA. I cannot vouch for other vendors in Amazon including the adaptor, however, you could always purchase an after-market adaptor if you really want the phone and live in the US.

Finally, the phone comes with a soft rubber clear case in the box. It also has a Gorilla Glass screen protector already installed. The rubber case is so-so; I am thinking about upgrading to something a bit tougher.

So far I love the phone. The pics are turning out great and the fingerprint scanner is lightening fast. I would not hesitate to buy again.

title: Love this 4G (not 2G!) phone, it's my 2nd Xiaomi Redmi!
text:
This phone has 9/10 of the bells and whistles that any popular flagship phone offers (in the US), but at 1/4th the price. The battery life is great, its fast and it has a decent amount of memory. I did a TON of research to find these phones, and I recommend writing down your must-haves (Is a budget friendly phone a must? Want a phone jack? Is "just" an above average camera enough? How about a better than 1080p screen? Want Dolby Atmos STEREO sound (there are speakers on both the top and bottom of this phone model, a first for me, and make a huge difference)? Yup, this has one has all those things, which were on my list), then googling 'X phone model VS. Y phone model', so you can see the features of each phone you're considering, side by side.

title: NO LONGER WORKS with ATT in SF bay area ( ATT DEACTIVATED. UPDATED REVIEW )
text:
7/3/21
Works as it should. I'll post a more in depth review as I get used to it.

Edit 7/24/21
I just updated to MIUI 12.5.3.0 running android 11 and it seems to have made the phone a bit more snappy. The new style upper right side settings / upper left side notifications menus are more responsive as well as the google search / news section.

Once an app like instagram or facebook is loaded in the background it recalls it within a second or so. No issues at all with AT&T. I can use the hotspot with my computer and it is very fast.

My partner did say the microphone does not sound as good on an instagram video call as my redmi note 8 pro when I get further away from the phone. I remember reading somewhere that this was an issue so we will see if that is fixed with the latest update. It does sound notably better for video though when narrating holding the phone close to me. Much crisper and possibly a compression algorithm. It is better than my Redmi Note 8 Pro all around for video / photos. Much less grain in low light situations. Still not a flagship, but it works great for what I need it for.

Overall its a great phone, a little buggy at times but its a cheap flagship clone and with the headphone jack, ir blaster, killer camera and expandable sd storage being must haves for me I'm okay dealing with a few glitches that should be cleared up as Android 12 comes along and Xiaomi releases MIUI updates. I'm one of the few that actually really likes MIUI as I got very used to it on my Redmi Note 8 Pro.

I will continue to update this review as major updates with notable performance improvements come along.

Edit 1/27/2022

I still love the camera on this phone, but it is having a lot of issues.
1. The charging port is already starting to go. I've treated it well, never abused. Very frustrating
2. The hotspot does not work anymore. I have tried a million different fixes and nothing seems to work.
3. It is getting very very buggy. I have to constantly reopen and close apps. The camera app takes forever to start filming video.
4. Battery life has gone down considerably. Does not last nearly as long as it used to.

Its really a shame because if these issues were not present it would be my favorite phone so far :/

Edit 2/23/2022
My phone was just deactivated by ATT. I will try to go to the att store to get it activated but due to HD voice issues I believe the phone is blacklisted :(

title: NOTE* Not International Model. This is the Indian variant and only works in India GSM networks
text:
I bought this phone to replace my Asus phone I had for 3 years. I've been following Xiaomi/Redmi for a while and heard good things about their phones. I wanted to personally experience their phone so after research and reading reviews I heard a lot of good things about the Redmi Note lines especially the Note 10 Pro.

When I first ordered this phone the listing said International Model and even listed the International Network bands. I live in the US and saw it had some of the network bands supported by Tmobile. The shipping speed was rather slower than expected with ETA changing two times. Initially the shipping ETA suggested 3-5 days than that changed to a week later than another week after that. I guess I can't complain with free shipping but still I expected this device to arrive in the few days it initially estimated.

When I got the phone it arrived in mostly new condition with the box and accessories. Not bad for a Used device. The box had a sticker on the front that said "India". I did not understand what it meant at the time I just assumed the phone must be well received in the Indian market so it was sharing that notion. Well I plug my sim card in and initially I get LTE signals around my house and area. I thought Okay I guess I'm good to go. It was not until I left my area just a few miles that all signal and connectivity dropped. I wasn't able to reliably receive and send out messages, make calls, and my data speed was a abysmal 3G. The network issues made what would otherwise be a good phone a horrible experience.

I made the request to return this phone and ordered a 11T Pro this time making sure it was a Global/international model and it supported Tmobile network bands. All in all I thought the phone was pleasant to use with good performance, good battery life, and the phone felt nice in the hand with a polarizing back cover. I just wish the listing and seller clearly listed this device as Indian model and not a International model. It would of saved me some unnecessary stress.

title: This is a solid upgrade from the the Note 9 pro
text:
Where to begin. I've had this phone for almost a year, and when I tell you it bangs, it bangs hard.

The camera is incredible, which I believe is due to using Samsung tech.
The color presentation is gorgeous. The orange is vibrant and stands out from the typical grey/silver, white and black you often see.
The sound is crisp and loud.
The display is gorgeous and for the price, having an OLED display rocks.
It has some snappy performance, and with the upgrade to MIUI 13, only made things better in my experience.
Storage is the typical 128gb but after you factor the operating system I believe you still have a sizable 119 or something like that.

title: Like an S9+ on steroids, but with some side effects (some camera issues)
text:
Great phone, but has some issues.

After accidentially breaking my S9+ (an absolutely amazing phone, I must say), I decided to upgrade to this model. The S20 Ultra is definitely faster. Battery life, even with the 120 Hz. screen refresh turned off, is only slightly better than my old S9+ (maybe 20% more life with actual real-world use). Camera zoom is amazing - I can zoom to see birds and vehicles with OK detail from nearly a mile away and better detail when closer. Compared to S9+, the phone slightly heavier (not a noticeable issue) and I can fit a few more icons onto my home screens which helps a lot.

The camera is love/hate, however. Quality is basically the same as the S9+. But the glare is worse. You MUST keep the camera glass cover pristinely-clean to help avoid this. But even then, the camera tends to boost nearby lights and it washes out detail - which is really bad for night use. The camera focus is the most frustrating issue with this phone. Samsung appears to have reverted back to the S5's focusing, where it struggles to auto-focus even on close-up objects. It's hit-or-miss. Most of the time, it focuses just fine, but it seems to struggle when you need it the most, causing blurry shots. It's as if the camera has ADD and gets distracted by the slightest movement of something else and tries to focus on it instead. I've fully updated the software and reset the settings but the issue persists.

The lack of a 3.5mm aux audio port is disappointing but using a 3.5mm->USB adapter hasn't posed any issues.

The inclusion of an SD card expansion slot is an excellent feature this model still retains. It's easy to gobble up tons of space when you're recording high quality video.

title: To all the skeptics
text:
I am a real person. I am not paid nor do I have any affiliation with the seller, I am simply writing this for others to know that this seller is legit.

The phone I received that was offered was a Samsung Galaxy S20 ultra 5g unlocked NEW. I was very skeptical about this on Amazon and messaged the seller my skepticism and after he confirmed that it was the real deal I went and bought it. I received the package EARLY which was nice, the box was a little worn but I’m didn’t buy it for the box probably happened in transit or just plain wear and tear, the phone was immaculate. Still sealed in plastic throughout even down to the speakers. I still of course was skeptical that this was a real deal. So I did some digging. I turned the phone on and first thing I did was run the IMEI number to verify it matches. I ran this FROM THE PHONE using a code to verify it and it in fact matched not just the box but the system code I was given therefore it was a real deal model and not likely to be refurbished. Still I was skeptical. I downloaded the app phone info to check the refurbished status and while phone info is typically a rooted only application it has a 90% rate to be true for checking refurbishment. The result was ORIGINAL. So that made me feel confident that this was a legit NEW product. Finally I checked if the phone was indeed unlocked. I did this in two ways, the first of which was run the debug mode and check the bands on the phone (network operators) and sure enough those came back as UNLOCKED. The final test was using two different sims one Verizon and one AT&T, which is what the phone came listed as, and sure enough it read both cards.

The seller is legit, and the phones are the real deal. Buy the last one or lose a damn good deal on one of the greatest phones of this decade. 5 effing stars.

title: VERIFIED RETURNED -> Every product is worse than the last - This is the worst
text:
I have owned every Motorola Bluetooth headset since the HX500, HX550, HX600, Boom1, Boom2 and now HK255. They get have gotten worse every year.

The HX series were largely fine, sounded great, had adjustable volume and great noise canceling and the earpiece fit comfortably in your ear, the plastic ear strap was optional on all of these models because the gel insert fit snugly and securely in your ear w/o the plastic hook. I could run with these and the bluetooth would stay secure w/o the plastic hook. Each of the HX models lasted me over a year before the flip piece broke or the unit just gave out. Entirely worth the 35 to 40 bucks I paid for them.

Then the Boom and especially the Boom 2 comes along and the flip breaks within two weeks. I bought a replacement thinking I might have gotten a faulty unit. I have owned the Boom 2 for 3 months and have broken 3 flip pieces. This is entirely because of the positioning of the flip. On the previous HX models the flip laid flat against the body of the earpiece when it was closed. With the boom 2 the earpiece sticks up at almost a 45 degree angle. If you accidentally push it down against the body of the headset you will break the flip (this is what happened the first time). If you get a phone call and pull the bluetooth out of your pocket and the flip gets caught on the edge of your pocket you will break the flip (this is what happened the second time). When the Flip breaks the unit is worthless.

Now the HK255 has done away with the flip altogether, which is the only good thing about this unit. It uses a physical switch you move with your thumb when you put it on. Unfortunately, everything else is worse, starting with the earpiece. They have changed the gel piece that they used with every other model. Now it won't stay in your ear, you HAVE to use the plastic ear hook. The plastic hook has the same issues as the ear flip that sticks up on the boom 2. It gets caught on things in your pocket and is easy to break. But worse than that, it is harder to put the bluetooth in your ear! You have to fiddle with the ear hook to get it in your ear. It will not fit securely in your ear w/o the ear hook the way all other models before it did. Additionally, there is no volume +/- button there is one button that switches between three settings. Those settings are: Ok if there is no background noise, whisper mode, and useless.

Furthermore, the sound quality (at any level) is nowhere near what it was on the HX series. Tinny and muffled.

This is the last Motorola blue tooth I will be buying unless they re-release the HX550 or HX600

title: You get what you pay for... Does not run Android! - Runs "Android One"
text:
I bought this as a burner phone, and chose it because it has a USB-C charging port. Compared to a 4 year old OnePlus, this Nokia g10 is slow, sluggish, laggy, kludgy. The screen protector collects so many fingerprints that it's difficult to see through. I would not want this as my primary phone.

The most important thing to know, that isn't mentioned in the description (as far as I can tell) is that this phone runs Android One - a closed-source Google OS that is based on Android, but dumbed down. If you're expecting a mainline Android phone, this is not it. It's intended to bring new people to Android platform with inexpensive $100-$150 phones.

Also note that this phone is compatible with normal GPS, and also China's BeiDou global positioning satellite network rather than Russia's GLONASS.

While initiating the phone, you're prompted with about a million choices that you can opt out of the vendor collecting your personal data. Be very careful as most of these are presented as "NEXT" buttons, and the skip options aren't as obvious. Don't be tempted to click through all the options without reading first!

Nice that it comes with a screen protector built in (though it's a finger print collector) and it comes with a very basic flexible clear plastic case to cover the back.

title: Great for 60 - somethings like me
text:
We (me & my betrothed) replaced both of our 5–6-year-old Nokia 6 phones with Nokia 12 phones. There was no need to shop around as we have owned Nokias since the 1980's and trust and admire the company.

It's simple; high performance (I do not 'game' however); long lasting (my last Nokia is 6 years old and great to the day, even with the cracked gorilla glass)

TIP: Google Apps greatly impact performance of the Nokia for the worse. Google Camera is especially a drag on this Nokia - it will freeze it solid. Replace all of your apps with Microsoft apps. You can get these from Google Play. Once you have done that, deactivate or uninstall all of the Google programs (including Google Launcher) and replace and load the Microsoft Launcher (very important). Anyway, doing all of this makes for a not as flashy phone, but its way more stable and I don't have to worry about all of my data being stored and mined in the Google cloud/fog.

With that, I leave you.

title: Factory reset functionality stripped from phone by Nokia
text: As per Nokia's misnamed "customer care team" because they clearly could care less about their customers, their developers intentionally stripped the ability to enter recovery mode from this phone and all other Nokia phones produced since Android 9. What this means is if you are like me and want to preserve what little privacy these devices offer by choosing to disable the Find Your Phone feature, and you are unable to unlock the lock-screen with your PIN for any reason, your device is effectively bricked. Nokia support refuses to provide instructions or software that will allow you to restore your phone to factory defaults. Your only option is to ship your phone to a Nokia service center and hope they are slightly more competent than the support team. They claim this is because customers abused this functionality and bricked their own phones, and rather than making the process easier or safer they decided in their infinite wisdom that it would be a better idea to take that functionality, which is common on ALL mobile devices, completely away without disclosing this fact to new or existing customers. They appear to be completely ignorant of how utterly insane that decision is. Based on my experience with the Nokia "customer care team", not only will I never purchase another Nokia product again, I will be filing a complaint with the FTC. I would rather buy a new mobile phone from a different manufacturer than ship this piece of garbage to the service center, even though my G10 is only eight months old and still in warranty. What a sad joke this company has become.

title: Keep the slim design, but sacrifice protection.
text:
Simple to install and feels great in my hand. Used to have the a bulkier case for more protection, but I am not the type of person to drop their phone. So I decided to slim down a bit with this case and it feels like a brand new phone all over again.

The texture keeps the phone from slipping out your hand while making it comfortable to hold for long periods of time.

Just understand, that the lip of this case is very slightly raised and the spine is not covered, so small tiny drops on the corner may be fine, but dropping on concrete while walking outside I can imagine still doing damage while the phone is folded. If your phone is unfolded you pretty much have 0 protection for the big screen.

To give you an idea about the lip size, with this case on, if I were to put this phone face down over a penny, the penny will most likely touch the screen, so if you were to drop this on any small object that object could scratch the screen if it has any kind of actually thickness. So this case is more for oops I dropped it on the carpet or maybe the kitchen floor if I am sitting and eating, but dropping this outdoors will be very risky. More for an office enviroment and not for outdoor jogging and such.

That being said, it you just want to protect from minor bumps, this is perfect. If you need more or you tend to drop your phone often enough, look elsewhere. For a $1800 phone, don't skimp out if you are drop prone.

Overall, great case for those you still want to maintain the sleek size of this phone and have "minor" drops once in a blue moon.

title: Great product, wish it wasn't a sideload
text:
I needed a device I could use as both a tripod and a gimbal to make some product videos without help from a cameraman, and this fit the bill perfectly. It allowed me to use my Motorola phone as my camera and switch from closeup shots moving around the products to static positioned distance shots easily, which made my editing tasks much, much easier (I'm not a good editor, so getting things in one shot, one take is my general goal).

The drawback to using DJI is that their software is side loaded. That always introduces security concerns. It would be nice if we could get a way to get compatible working software into the Play store. It is simple to use, powerful and does just work. You can do a lot of really nice things with pan, zoom, rotate and overall control. The phone is easy to get balanced in the holder, which is designed to accommodate a super wide variety of phones.

Outside the software, I couldn't find any real negatives with this little device. It did exactly what I needed it to do as simply as I think it could, which kept my learning curve exceptionally flat. I think I spent 5 minutes figuring it out, if that. I don't think you could ask for a better device for making really good videos from a phone.

title: Lacks some basic gimbal functionality for landscape-oriented video that is deal-killing
text:
Imagine that you've mounted your camera on this gimbal in landscape orientation. You want one of the most basic gimbal shots there is: smoothly changing the height of the camera from chest to ankle. With any legit gimbal, you slowly drop the gimbal down to ground level and there you have it. It is easy because the pivot point is to the side of the camera and therefore out of the way. With the OM5, the pivot point is behind the camera and therefore gets in the way, forcing you to contort your arm and wrist to try to capture this simple movement smoothly. It's an absolute deal killer. Interestingly, it is possible to achieve this shot pretty easily if you're shooting vertical video, which tells you the target audience of this product. If you're shooting vertical tik tok videos with the OM5, you're golden.

A critical but very helpful video about the OM5 is available on YouTube. Search for "Samuel Sotiega" and look for his OM5 review where he demonstrates a number the limitations that go unmentioned in most other reviews of this product. It's good due diligence before spending your money, even if they don't apply to you. (And, no, I'm not Samuel and don't know him.)

title: Tilt issues matter
text:
I’m leaving my 5-star review below in case my reasoning for returning this item isn’t relevant to someone. I decided that the tilt issue is a big deal to me. My IT team needed me to create a how-to video. All I needed was for this damn thing to tilt downward a few more degrees so that I could do a demonstration on an iPad right in front of me with both my hands. I get it now. The low star reviews are valid. I had to put this thing on a tripod lean it over the edge of the table just to get those extra degrees and then sit with the tripod in my face just so I could do a damn how-to video. When I turn the holder downward by hand, it tilts those extra degrees further but then of course it shoots back up into place. I don’t understand why the motorized capability and space and room is there, but the software and the mechanism refuses to go with those extra degrees. What in the entirety of a fcck were they thinking? It’s even worse with the selfie stick if you decide to take a selfie with the stick fully extended. It doesn’t tilt enough for your face to show in a lot of angles. Again, what the hell was the point of this thing?

This was the ultimate dealbreaker for me: the weight capacity isn’t enough for a tricked out filming setup. If you’re finding that your phone is a little too heavy with the lens on, I recommend sliding the holder up closer to the camera area, instead of being centered on the phone. That’ll help rebalance and give you those few extra ounces. If you are looking to add a lens, and then an adapter, and then a filter, and you’re like me and you’ve got a case with the built in 17 mm thread, just know that it basically stops there. I tried to plug in a splitter to give myself a line for audio, and one for charging while I’m using the device. This thing cannot handle the smaller iPhone X with anything more than an additional lens. Once I started trying to add the adapter and the filter, and then if I needed to put the line in for the audio, this thing was not having it. If you’re looking to add things to your phone, you’ll want to look in the camera grade gimbals. This is truly for social media people and no one else.

================================

I think a lot of droiders are trying to mitigate their feelings about needing to upgrade and comfort themselves to remain with the 4 and it’s frankly a disservice to those of us earnestly in the market for a new or first time gimbal.

For one thing, the play store has not updated the app so droid users have to go to the website to download the compatible version. I don’t understand why people are writing 1 star reviews over this. The packaging gives you the scan to the download page. You’re doing the rest of us a disservice by turning people away from this product for inconsequential reasons.

Then, there is like one guy on the internet posting about “restricted tilt” being a deal breaker for him. He uses the same verbiage every time so ... it’s one guy. This guy delayed my purchase by two weeks. I watched several tutorials on getting epic gimbal shots and NONE of them used “tilt of poltergeist” levels to get amazing shots. This is my first gimbal purchase, and I would appreciate it if this grand video artist would post an epic looking video where the extra five degrees (literally the difference) made the difference in his storytelling. In fact you get more degrees in the rolling shot on a 5 than you do on a 4. I don’t understand why I can’t just tilt my hand those couple extra degrees... and I really tried to find a shot where this critique had any relevance at all. For two weeks, I tried.

Then, you have folks posting that you might as well just put a monopod on your 4 and save yourself an upgrade. That’s a pretty ludicrous comparison since the controls would be feet away form me if I were gripping this with a monopod arm. I like the extra inches in getting the shots. I don’t plan to use the selfie stick for selfies and it’s not “just for social media” and non serious filmmakers. The added inches give me that much more distance when wrapping around buildings/objects and !especially! when mimicking crane shots.

I bought the 5 locally at Best Buy and I don’t have any jitter or motor heating issues.

I’ll update my review if the lens filters I need to add prove too heavy.

title: Coming from an Osmo mobile 2 - this took some getting used to
text:
I understand they wanted to make this more foldable - but I found that coming from an Osmo Mobile 2 (OM2 from this point on) took quite a bit of re-learning how to hold it. The OM2 was able to rotate on its vertical axis to where you could hold it down to the ground and it was able to fully rotate to remain level. The OM5 requires you to hold it vertical- the rotate the arm sideways in order to allow the ground shots. If you push it too hard past the limit (which is pretty easy) the gimbal will violently try to center itself before going limp and requiring you to recenter it again. The OM2 didn't have this problem as I could easily and naturally hold the gimbal low and then back up while keeping my arm in the same position.

I also found the DJI Mimo app confusing to use as compared to the OM2's "DJI Go" version. I dont know why DJI has to release separate apps for their OM gimbals. The functionality and easyeof use of the former app was superior. The Mimo app is clunky and difficult to access some of the features (like the 3x3 shots...etc) I find myself having to squint at the small white icons and have almost given up using it completely. I prefer using the standard camera built into the phone for simplicity.

The OM5 has the finger trigger to lock the gimbal from auto rotating with wrist twisting - this is helpful. However, the OM2 double tap to disable was much easier to use. I find the wrist rotation of the gimbal on the OM5 to be jerky at best, especially when rotating the gimbal to the side for lower shots. The gimbal finger controls and wrist movement now change the axis based on the direction it is being held. Good, yes, but awkward and requires learning with a little frustration.

In the end- the OM5 size is great! I just miss the simplicity of the older versions even though they were physically larger. I think a lot of these issues can be fixed with updates or maybe somebody with more patience. Coming from the OM2, this requires more "training" than I expected.

title: NOT compatible with S21 Ultra
text:
Been a software engineer for 20+ years, this is not a user issue. This product is junk.

Cons:

• Bluetooth connects/disconnects almost instantly -when it connects at all.

• Bluetooth will attempt to find the device indefinitely until I have to force quit the app.

• Searching for my issues results in many frustrated customers on various forums complaining about the same thing. DJI's response? "We're sorry, please go download our app". Nothing more frustrating than receiving junk, then when you spend time trying to force it to work properly, the company replies with some pre-canned garbage response.

• App itself isn't on the play store, you have to download an APK from their site. Why? What's the app doing that Google won't allow? Also the APK is being blocked by security companies, as confirmed on various forums.

• The Mimo app even when it works for a few seconds is hot trash.

• Centering the magnet to your phone is a nightmare and you risk scratching your phone with the magnet as you adjust.

• I managed to run the video for 30 seconds ONCE before it disconnected and the VIDEO WASN'T EVEN SMOOTH. I held the camera steady and walked slow, didn't matter. Compared to a shot of me just walking with the phone & no gimbal, the result is bordering indistinguishable.

• When confronted with these issues, one of their recommended fixes is to REPLACE YOUR PHONE. Yeah, I'm going to replace a $1200 phone to TRY to get your $150 trash to work.

• Another recommended fix is to clear all of your Bluetooth settings. Huh? So I have to reconnect my vehicles, bookshelf speakers, ear buds, temperature probe, and the half dozen other things that function properly? You need new software devs. The problem isn't on my end, I promise you that.

Pros:

• LITERALLY none. I mean literally. It doesn't do what it's supposed to do. Compatibility on the website lists my phone.

I own a Mavic Mini 2, which is fantastic, so I thought DJI must be a good brand. Well, stick to drones, boys. Because this product makes you look like amateurs.

title: To weak, design flaws, mostly useless for iPhone 13 Pro
text:
Ok, so I'm very new to gimbals. This one is actually my first one. I bought it to capture more stable video with my iPhone 13 pro without the case.

To put it simply, this thing is useless. It asks for calibration every time. That's a lot of time wasted prior to shooting. Motors are weak. I don't know how they deal with other phones but my iPhone 13 pro (NOT MAX) is certainly too much for it. Rotors are very slow and find it hard to track my subject. If the subject doesn't move slowly it fails to fallow. I adjusted the settings to max speed but to no avail. Footage wasted...

This gimbal doesn't twist 360 degrees. When shooting certain angles, the gimbal arm falls into the composition. You literally see its arm in the video. This is horrendous! Too many of my clips were wasted because of that.

I'd give dji mimo app 3 stars max. Somehow, it isn't intuitive and setting up modes takes some time and effort. Moreover, I cant set it up, if the gimbal is turned off. While it's on, I have to struggle with it to browse or adjust settings. A very poor app design, if you ask me.

A built-in extension rod is a great idea. It's stable, so no complaints here. Battery life is great.

Conclusion: I would certainly not recommend this gimbal to my friend. Just skip it if you value your footage and nerves. DJI has awesome drones but the gimbal game isn't their thing.

P.S.

It doesn't work with action cameras.

title: Please overall. A few quirks.
text:
[[VIDEOID:2bbaad582894aa9f0e784c5609ece884]] First off, I am a pro photographer. I am picky and notice things most people don't.

This is my first gimbal. I think I was expecting super smooth panning, smooth exposure transitions from different lit areas in the scene, the footage to look like perfect, cinematic. I expected too much. My first couple of uses were frustrating so I took it on a trip and used it every day, a lot. I learned how to twist my wrist when panning and sort of work with the gimbal to achieve different types of shots. The results while not perfect expand my shooting capabilities quite a bit. This takes me to a level I can not go hand held. So keep that in mind.

I have an iPhone 11 Pro so the size and weight are fine with the 5. Heard newer or Pro Max models might struggle.

Lots to love about this unit. Just be aware... when I used the selfie stick the footage got jittery. I stopped using it except on still shots.

The phone was rarely completely level. So I fiddled with the position of the magnetic clip on the phone and re-calibrated a lot. I could overcome this, but when a shot arises you can lose it fiddling with the leveling. I had the same problem on the DJI OM 4. Make sure your mounting bracket is dead center on the back of your phone. Use a ruler to make sure it is equidistant from top to bottom and the spring loaded center is dead center. It helps. Be OK with the phone not being 100% centered even after re-calibrating.

For some reason in the DJI app when panning it would jump or jitter sometimes. Going from different lighting areas in a scene it would struggle to slowly, smoothly transition. Not sure why, but it made that footage unusable and sometimes you only get one chance to shoot things. It seems using the native iPhone app in some scenarios works better. If your shot is crucial, try it in both apps. In either app holding the zoom is OK between say .5 and 1x, but as soon as you hit each new lens threshold there is a jumping effect. So only zoom in between lens thresholds.

The app itself is decent, but definitely not intuitive, lots of stuff buried in menus you have to click around to get while shots are passing you by. That said there are some cool shot guides to give you ideas on how to shoot.

Also, in wide angle lens on iPhone the DJI often captures part of the gimbal in the shot. So I had to go between .5 and 1 zoom levels and find a sweet spot. DJI says you can just move the mounting clip, but then you'd have to move it back and re-calibrate for the next, non wide shots.

Nice things are the hand strap and having a tripod. Battery life is really good. Pano feature is neat, however, the phone will often tilt vertically entering Pano mode. To overcome, pull up the selfie stick and slightly angle it so the phone is level. On the DJI MO 4 the phone tilts to the side entering Pano mode and there is no way to adjust. It's why I kept the 5 and returned the 4.

Tracking is definitely nice and works well.

Overall I think most people will be happy with the 5, I'm a pro photographer so I'm a bit more picky.

title: No SUPPORTED app. DJI uses SPYWARE!!
text:
This item needs an unsupported sideloaded app to work which is not a safe option if you care about your privacy and your data. Also, DJI uses Spyware software. They can turn on your Microphone and Camera even if the "app" or device is not being used. This also applies to thier Drones and other items that need thier software to operate. The information regarding the Spyware, was presented to me by my employer. An issuance from the Governor of Texas banning the use of any devices manufactured by DJI and some others, as well as the TikTok app, Kaspersky Security and several other companies. If you use any of these mentioned, you should remove them immediately or at least, check your permission settings for them. Even if no permissions are granted, does not guarantee they wont be able to still use the Spyware that has already been downloaded on your devices if the app remains installed. Everyone should do your own research and stay vigilant. When we Learn better we should do better.

All the Best.

W.
Quality Assurance Analyst

title: Disappointed...
text:
I bought this from my local camera store as they had an unused but previously purchased (the guy bought it and then decided he wanted an OM6) example for $30 off. The build quality seems solid and all the controls have a nice positive feel to them. Lots of them are dual purpose, though which makes accessing some of the app function hard to remember. I'll return to the app in a bit. Overall, it seems like a decent bit of kit.

I have a Samsung S22 Ultra and the stabilization works fine with this phone. The clamp is a bit of a squeeze on this phone with a fairly slim Speck case and you need to slide the clamp up on the phone a bit to get it to balance. This makes it hard to hit the side button to wake the phone up, but it is doable, just a bit of a PITA.

My main complaint with this device is the app. The S22 Ultra has a sophisticated camera module with four different lenses: an ultrawide (about 16mm), normal (about 27mm), telephoto (about 75mm) and super-telephoto (about 270mm). All of this is achieved w/o using the dreaded digital zoom. The DJI Mimo app supports only the 27mm main lens. All zooming is done digitally which considerably degrades image quality. This makes the app almost useless with this phone, and so considerably degrades the usefulness of this gimbal. You can still connect to it via Bluetooth and use the stabilization using the native app or the Samsung Expert Raw app. Doing this allows you to trigger the shutter with the shutter button on the gimbal, but no other features are available AFAICT. But using the advanced features in the app is limited to the main camera, the 27mm lens. DJI has added support for the additional cameras on the older "Ultra" and "Note" models so eventually this support may be added. When it will be added is another question.

The gimbal does the basic job I ask of it, but on the Samsung S22 Ultra the app is sadly lacking. If you are considering this gimbal, I strongly suggest that you look at the phone compatibility list before you purchase, though. If your phone is fully supported, this is a good gimbal. If your phone is not fully supported, consider whether you can live without the advanced features provided by the app before you buy.

title: DJI OM 5 Gimbal Android Mimo Galaxy S21
text:
[[VIDEOID:7c55560eb0552dce3f1048f3a8c66b82]] I did not buy this from Amazon. I did however buy this directly from DJI website so have had it for several days before Amazons delayed launch of the product. I have never had a DJI OM or another phone gimbal for comparison. I am not a content creator but I did purchase it to bring along to family events, family weddings, vacations, etc. My wife and I use this gimbal with Galaxy S21 so our experiences may be slightly different than iPhone users as I have read on previous reviews for OM3/OM4 there are some differences between the Android/iPhone apps and full usability.

I will start by saying if you own an Android phone and wish to get the most benefit out of this product, you may need to download the DJI Mimo app directly from DJI at https://www.dji.com/downloads/djiapp/dji-mimo. I initially downloaded the Mimo app from Google play store and as of 9/17/21 it is NOT the version 1.6 needed for Android 11/12 compatibility. When I downloaded the app from Google Play, the Mimo app would NOT find the OM5 via Bluetooth no matter what I did. Side loading the 1.6 app from Mimo's webpage resolved this problem.

Let me begin by saying, as an Android user, you can do a lot without ever installing the Mimo app. Before I downloaded the app, I was able to find the gimbal via Bluetooth via my phone and sync the phone to the gimbal. I read in previous OM gimbals you had to initially use the Mimo app to orientate the phone before switching to the phones OEM build in camera. This is not the case with the OM5 because as soon as you put the phone in the gimbal and turn it on, it self balances/aligns on its own without reliance on the Mimo app. I was able to use my Samsungs camera app without any problems with gimbals stabilization. Without the app - only using the phones built in Bluetooth you are able to record/take photos with the red record button, switch between horizontal/verbal orientation, switch between selfie/rear cameras, and change the direction of the phone on several axis using the build in joystick. The zoom in/zoom out button does NOT function w/o the Mimo app. Without the Mimo app, the trigger only can be used to reset/re-find the orientation if it gets off.

In the box you will find the gimbal, a nice carrying bag made of a microfiber-like feeling material, a charging cable usb-a to usb-c, the magnetic phone clamp (no light), tripod, and instructional material.
I purchased the grey version of the product (also comes in a white color). The gimbal is light and feels like a quality product. The magnetic phone clamp fits snuggly onto our phones over our cases. It is not obtrusive but it is big enough we would not leave it on our phones unless we were at an event/location where we may use it. The extended selfie stick is nice to have as well as the tripod.

The phone gimbal does a fair job keeping the video recording stabilized. It is quiet in its adjustments. I have been able to use the gimbal experimenting for a couple hours without having to charge it yet. The grey color is medium darkness grey with a dark grey textured grip. It does look and feel like a premium product. The gimbal is not too heavy and does fold up small enough for a fannypack/handbag/backpack. It could fit in large pockets but probably would not be the usual preferred storage. I was pleasantly surprised with the compact size of the product.

On the Mimo app on my Galaxy S21 the functions all appear to be working. I am limited to rear camera 4K30FPS and front camera 1080p30FPS. My native Samsung camera can do rear 4K60FPS and front camera 4K60FPS. The hyperlapse, timelapse are just okay as my build in phone app has these functions as well. The active tracking does seem to be the best functionally in the app. It does a good job tracking a subject as defined by the user. As it stands right now if I am tracking a moving subject, I will use the Mimo app but if I am just needing the stabilization, I may defer to my Samsung app for 4K60FPS option. The app comes in with several tutorials for creating specialized captures. I can see this being helpful for someone trying to be more creative or trendy. For myself, just wanting stabilized homevideos, I do not see myself ever using these specialized tutorials/modes. I do like the tripod as well as the extending selfie stick.

For now, overall impressions - gimbal 5/5, Android Mimo app 3.5/5. This product is not something I will carry around every day but if I know I may be shooting some video, it is small enough to bring along knowing the video will not be as shaky as just me holding the phone. The gimbal functions well and I like that it can be used without ever having to install the Mimo app. Android users, YMMV depending on your phone and the Mimo app version. 1.6 appears to function well with the Galaxy S21. The price is high currently on this product ~150 USD. This gimbal does seem targeted toward younger, hip content creators but will produce nice stabilized video. This may be worth a buy if you think more stabilized video or some of the features of the Mimo app are worth the one time purchase. I will keep it for now and see if I get my moneys worth.

title: Very Poor Support for 4K on Android 11 &12 Phones
text:
I would recommend that Android users steer clear of the OM5 for now. The Android app does not support 4K video for most Android phones and this is compounded if you've upgraded to Android 11 or 12. Their supported device list may have your phone on it, and it may say that it supports 4K, but this may not be true. I would suggest you google your phone and this device to see the number of issues other users have.

I have a OnePlus 9 pro with Android 12 which DJI lists as being compatible and supports 4K at 30fps. After loading everything up and upgrading the firmware, there is no menu option for anything over 1080p at 30 fps. That's when I started googling 4k issues with the OM5, and there are dozens of posts from Android users with the same problems. The issue has been noted for more than 6 months with no updates or fixes.

It's just not acceptable that a gimbal costing more than $150 doesn't have the software support for Android users wishing to record in 4K. I'm returning the item, and giving my fellow Android phone owners a warning! Do more research than I did before buying to make sure you will actually get 4K support!!!

title: Seriously impressed for under $150
text: I purchased the DJI OM5 primarily to record automotive and wildlife videography. If you're getting into stabilizers I'd say this is the one for you. The DJI mimo app is very user friendly, teaching you how to use your device. I mean this thing is strong enough to carry an iPhone 13max with a filter and counter weight, while still being able to fit in your pocket. The included tripod allows you to set down your device quickly and works fairly well for long exposure, and gives you extra grip space. Now of coarse everything has its cons. The 6 hour battery capacity is a huge downgrade from the OM4's 12 hour, but is compensated by the lighter/sleeker design. Personally 6 hours straight is plenty for me. You'll notice some of the features will not work on your native camera/filmic pro. Such as the zoom. My only other issue is that it can be quite snappy, and not as forgiving as other gimbals. In the end, For the sub $150 price point, simplicity, and overall power. I can't think of a better tool for a beginner videographer to get.

title: Fraught with problems…
text:
Despite what John F says about the new 5 gimbal, it is once again a poor product. I am an early adopter of various products and tend to follow those that get the bugs out and work.

He is correct in all the accommodations you have to make (case off, delicacy of balance requirement), but you have to separate the “learning curve” from the fundamentally flawed and poorly made product.

Read no further if you want the solution to this problem product. Further backup commentary follows:
** When buying a gimbal, buy UP ONE LEVEL on the scale of gimbal motor strength**

Simple as that. The downside? It will cost you more, but you will solve 75% or so of your problems. I don’t understand why a consumer, who, in this market is most assuredly new to the whole idea and use of a gimbal, has to make all these accommodations to simply get the thing partially working. Prime example: Most people these days buy cases to protect expensive phones. These “phone gimbals” ONLY work you take the case off (let alone any attempt to add a lens). The cradles are not even designed to accept case profiles. You can actually cut and adapt them - I did - but why not accommodate them from the beginning? Adding counter-weights does not work as the optimum location for counter-weighting is in the way of the arms. Also this product is supposed to be entry level - why have to go through 5 minutes of setup that has no guarantee of working because the placement of the weights is so sensitive?!

IF you own a small phone, and don’t use a case, and want to chance a short product life, buy this or similar. Don’t waste your money if you have any other camera/camera phone! I mentioned “short product life”. The biggest failure point (per the facebook groups) is battery performance. They CANNOT be replaced. The is no customer service to speak of. These are/this is chinese companies - they are classic examples of cheap, inferior marketed products that appear as solid, workable ones. Not so. The tried and true test that us old China buyers recognize is the following: Read the instructions. If you almost laugh at the bad English, lower your expectations or don’t buy the product in the first place. This company had some English speaker re-write their literature but it still comes through. But I digress.
Remember, the only way to get a motorized gimbal that will work with larger and larger phones is to find a maker of a line of gimbals - and buy up. Don’t say I didn’t warn you!

title: DJI requires you to download unknown and uncertified software - (get this) >> FROM CHINA !!
text:
I have worked inside technology for over 30 years. In all that time I have never seen ANYTHING like this product. The MFG should be fully investigated based upon what they ask their customers to do. Once you have the hardware charged and working you are asked to download an APP for your phone. In my case Android.

There is NO APP in the Play store and this should worry everyone who purchases this product. Therefore the 'APP' has not gone through the process of being published and certified, RATHER you are asked to download an unknown Android APK THEN are further asked to permanently disable your phones ability to block software from unknown and untrusted sources, in this case the servers are in China. The act of disabling this primary security function within the phone is essentially a 'Security 101' no no. After this is disabled you are further asked to install unamed and unknown software onto your phone. Furthermore ANY software maybe installed in the future without you being asked to disable this fundamental security feature leaving the phone open to ANYTHING.

In 2022 this is entirely UNACCEPTABLE and anyone who does as they ask are knowingly and purposefully supporting the spread of potential malware. Merely connecting to your home wifi after installing this unknown software will automatically make your entire home network infected and a potential danger to not only yourself but others.

title: Android users beware
text:
They may say that the gimbal and software is compatible with Android, but what they fail to mention is that the Android app is so stripped back and limited compared to the iPhone app that it renders the gimbal almost useless.

The DJI app on Android can't record any video above 30 FPS. In fact, 30 FPS is the ONLY option available; you don't even get the option for a cinematic 24 FPS. I also can't record any video above 1080p with a smartphone that supports 8k video recording (Galaxy Note 20 Ultra) which completely destroys any idea of shooting high quality video with the app. While you can opt to use your phone's native camera app, you will lose access to all of the tracking features of the gimbal which makes this nothing more than an expensive stabilizing selfie stick for Android users.

Overall I'm disappointed with this purchase because of the lack of care given to Android users with DJIs half-baked software. We have Android flagships capable of producing footage equaling, and many times rivaling, that of the iPhone. Having software that is missing features and can't even record a video above 1080p/30 FPS on Android is completely unacceptable.

I won't give it 1-star because the hardware seems to be sturdy, although it seems to struggle a bit with heavier phones unless they are perfectly balanced and the tilt range of the motors isn't the greatest.

title: Not usable for phones in a case
text:
This was my first gimbal purchase. I have an iPhone 13 that I keep in an OtterBox Defender case. I am a casual video maker and wanted up my game a bit, but my primary use of my phone is as a phone, so it stays in a nice protective case. The OM5 could barely handle the weight. Due to the design of the case, the phone has to be pushed over a bit off-center. The OM5 constantly complained that the phone was off balance. Strike one. The magnetic clip doesn't fit around the case. Strike two.

I tried doing some basic crane & sweep up shots. The OM5 has very limited vertical tilt. If you search YouTube, you'll find a few reviews complaining about this. I don't really need a gimbal for basic selfie shots or tracking someone walking; I wanted to do more dramatic panning & sweeping shots. The OM5 just doesn't have the range of motion to pull these off. Strike 3. Back it went.

I did like the extendible stick. That helps get the camera away from you, or up over crowds. Having the controls available to pan or tilt while holding the camera way up in the air was nice.

Update: After returning the OM5, I bought the widely reviewed and liked Feiyutech G6 Max. These are radically different products. The OM5 is a "consumer" product. The G6 Max is "professional". With all the good and bad those two terms imply.

The OM5 is small; something you can throw in a jacket pocket, pop on to shoot some stabilized footage, and put away. It folds up in a tight clean bundle. The G6 Max is much larger, has knobs & sliders & fiddly bits that need to be adjusted just right. It comes in a case, and you'll most likely use it by taking it out, getting it set up, and then shooting footage for a while.

The OM5 comes with slick, feature filled software (whether you want or those bells and whistles or not). The G6 Max software is far clunkier. If the OM5 is a Mac, the G6 Max is Linux. Another example: When I fired up the G6 Max software & connected it to the gimbal, it told me there is a firmware update available. Go to the firmware update page and there are four different firmwares available - the gimbal, keyboard, Bluetooth, and "HUB". Why should I need to manage four different pieces of software? Oh, and the firmware updates haven't worked, so far. They get 100% done and then fail.

The G6 Max is clearly a much stronger gimbal. And it can support much larger cameras. If you have a larger phone in a case, you may find the OM5 is just not up to the task (as I did), and then you'll need to step up to one of these larger gimbals. But the larger gimbal is far less convenient than the OM5. If you can live with the limitations of the OM5, it is a slick little product.

I owned a first gen DJI Osmo Mobile and really liked it! It was easy to use and decent quality for the price. Since my first gen was loosing battery life and became a pain to charge (thanks micro usb) I decided to get a new one. I did some research and landed on the DJI OM 5 since it's familiar.

The differences between the OM 1 and the OM 5 were vast and not in a good way. To start, its hard to balance your phone on the OM5 which DRAINS battery life, and it doesn't have any to spare to begin with. Then comes to the max movement capabilities which are very very poor. It can move 180 degrees horizontally and about 10 degrees up or down vertically. This means that it does a good job if you are walking on level ground and in a straight line but you can NOT do anything creative.

Then comes the big issues starting with the app. If you search for the app on the Google play store then you will not find it, and scanning the QR code in the setup guide just takes you to their store page. The only way to get the app is to side load it from their support page. Once you do have the app it will only shoot a max of 1080p 30fps (on a Galaxy S22 Ultra with can do 1080p 240fps). Of course you can use your onboard camera app and bypass theirs but then the only functional button on the gimbal is the cheap feeling joystick.

I then picked up the Zhiyun Smooth 5 which is the same price and in a whole other class compared to the DJI OM 5. I left a review on the Smooth 5 but the short version is that you don't need to use their app for anything but the AI tracking, everything else is handled on the device itself.

title: Dont listen to the bad reviews. It works well. Read this first
text:
To start I’d like to say I am a veteran videography and photographer. I’ve used large gimbals with full frame camera and small Gimbals line this. I think a lot of the bad reviews are from user error and lack of knowledge. I suggest reading the instructions and watch some tutorial videos to learn when you get new gear. There is most likely a simple fix or oversight your not seeing. Regarding this gimbal I have both the OM4 and OM5. I got the 5 because of the extension rod and I really like for low shots after a few days of use. I will agree with others that both the OM4 and OM5 stress to carry the weight of the iPhone 12 and 13 pro max. I use tested the 11 and 12 pro and had no issues. The max I would get some vibration which is disappointing. Please realize the just little weight difference is a big deal on this little gimbal. Remove your case and any attachments on your phone. Less weight the gimbal has to work with the better. Also make sure to balance the phone on the gimbal before turning it on. Hold the motor that goes up and down and then balance the phone so it does not drop to the left or right and stays level on its own. That the only adjustment you can make on this simple gimbal and it’s very important. I believe a lot of people complaining of vibration are not doing this. It’s really easy to want just put on the back plate and stick it to the gimbal and power on but balancing is important step. I blame dji marketing a little as the promo vid shows someone just slapping it on randomly to the phone and sticking to gimbal. You can do this one you balance it once and then remember where to place the mount on your phone each time but the first time make sure to figure out where that spot is and you will prevent a lot of head ache.

Another point to bring up is to learn the modes and buttons. Figuring out the features and limits of each mode will help a lot. These gimbals are turn key and can get great content right out of the box but the difference between good and great content is practicing a little bit and getting to know your gimbal. Little things like proper settings, smooth body movement and shot planning can really help. Have patience and learn the tool.

I rarely leave reviews but wanted give my two cents on this one as I’m quite experienced with gimbals and think some users are giving bad reviews that aren’t accurate because of lack of knowledge and experience and may turn off some buyers that could really benefit from this awesome product. It’s amazing that this product is under $200 and paired with a new iPhone 13 pro it can create the quality of content that would have taken 10k + of equipment to produce 10 years ago. Amazing what we have access to these days. In one small backpack I have this gimbal, a mavic air 2 and misc filters and I shoot amazing pro quality content. Dji has made that all possible. I’m not affiliate or paid by them. I just really appreciate their gear and think they do in excellent job.

I’ll try to find the time to do a tutorial on it and show some of my work in the future. OM5 is an exciting release :)

text: There were some issues in the very beginning since the ASUS default interface is not what wed expect from Android phone, especially those, who spent years if not decades, with Samsung phones. The highly familiar 3 buttons on the screen bottom were missing. Oops! I was able to run through the quick settings and restore them, so the interface became more familiar and some lost functionality returned. Other thoughts... I used to see the control buttons on both sides of the phone, but I realize why they all have been moved to the right side because the main purpose of this phone is not the phone itself, right? Well, actually I'm not a phone shooter player, but I needed a powerful phone, ideally with 2 SIM cards, and I got it! This phone is REALLY POWERFUL. The CPU is great and the amount of free available RAM is a key thing, making this phone unbeatable nowadays. The configuration was rather fun, than trouble. Unfortunately, I was able to restore all apps and most of the app settings and files from the old phone backup, but the desktop, or I'd better call it Home Screen, was not restored, making the entire process less convenient. What else I can say - a very annoying for me is the way how the system works with the additional home panels. Yes, there are many cool ways and effects making fun for the user while switch them, but I didn't find a way to add a new panel if I need to and to change the panel order, which is a very handy feature. Partially this problem was solved by circling the home screens, so once you get to the end screen you can see the first one again. It's kind of artificial way to add a panel to the left side of the home screen, which is impossible in this implementation and makes me little frustrated, since I used to keep the stores and finances on the left from the Home screen and some technical stuff on the right side. It's kind of possible, but still, I cannot change the order of the panels and I'm not sure why this functionality has been restricted or rather never implemented. Other than that - the phone is great! Btw, it comes with the case, which is great, but the case is too hard and I don't want to drop and lose my phone just because of that. That's why I just ordered a new polyurethane case, I've been using these for years and found very convenient and safe enough. The rear part of the phone looks and works great, there are some color LED's showing some phone status, possibly its temperature. Having the real panel very cool, but too busy, completely excluded a way to attach some small velcro and use it inside my car as a simple way to attach the phone to the dash as I used to do for the last decade. Well, will invent something  else, the phone is pretty good to pay attention at these small inconveniences. The fact, that it doesn't have magnetic wireless charge feature is very understandable and I'm ok with it. It would be great, but I know, that it has 2 powerful batteries and a weak wifi charger won't satisfy it to an acceptable lever, keeping in mind a 65W charger, so it makes no sense even to try, and it's not a deal breaker.
