title: Comes with a Super Fast Charger
text:
First up: In terms of Value for price, this is a good value product, as it comes with a Samsung 25 Watt Super Fast Charger (35 USD on Samsung's Website) in the Box. If you've purchased any Samsung S-Series phone after the S22, you will not receive a charger in the box. The 25-Watt Charger will enable wired Super Fast Charging.

Next: The marketing on this product is a little misleading. There's no such thing as "Super Fast Wireless Charging" as of writing this review. Using the Included 25 watt charger, along with a 5 amp USB-C to USB-C Cable doesnt display "Super fast Wireless Charging. It will only display "Fast Wireless Charging" on your Samsung Device. This is with "Fast Wireless Charging" enabled in the phone's settings. However, this will wirelessly charge your device at 15 Watts.

Finally: This Wireless Charging Station works. For those using the "Ultra" models, you may have to find the sweet spot while on the charger. The Charging Station has excellent grip on any surface it's on. However, there's very little grip between your device + the charging station, so be careful not to bump whatever surface this device is on.

Additionally, this will wireless charge your other devices, such as earbuds, and other phones that support wireless charging (including iPhones).

title: It has a minor flaw in protection, but overall is sturdy and looks good.
text:
[[VIDEOID:e1424071ee52a2e4d9387604bdfe15d1]] The case is very well made, and looks great with a Bora Purple S22. It's easy to hold, and both of the stand levers are well made. I'm giving this four stars because it's good, but has room to improve.

First, the biggest reason for a case is protection, and any flaws there are harder to accept.

The case provides a nice rim around the screen to protect it in a fall. On the upper right corner of the case, where the hard plastic structure of the case is weakest because of the cutout for the camera bump, the rim can be pushed back very easily, exposing the upper right corner of the screen to impact. It cannot be pushed forward, because the hard plastic actually has a lip over the camera bump. This case somehow protects the metal camera bump better than the glass screen.

Next, the kickstand.

It's well made, but I would have made different choices on angles. Neither kickstand leg gives a good angle for watching videos on a countertop. Worse, the kickstand is a raised and rounded ridge down the middle of the back of the case, ensuring that the case never sits stably and flat on a table or, importantly, on a wireless charging pad.

Some minor changes could have made this a real winner. It's still pretty nice.

----

Edit: I've spent some more time looking at it, and I don't think it's likely to give any appreciable protection to the corners of the screen. The protective rim moves out of the way too readily, allowing the corners of the screen to make contact. I've changed my rating.

title: Fastest Charger I've Ever Used
text:
Ordered one of these to use with our Samsung Galaxy S22 Ultras. It was on sale $10 off, so the price was very good.

This charger has surpassed all expectations. We leave it in the kitchen for those days where we didnt charge our phones overnight or just need a quick upcharge. It charges so fast that we can plug it in, make a quick lunch, and by the time you're ready to eat we've gained 30-50% more battery. Leave it for a little longer and it's at or near 100%.

It's perfect for how we use it; as a quick charge up. I wouldn't necessarily use it as a bedside charger, since it will charge your phone completely before you're even fully asleep. We usually use wireless chargers for bedside stuff.

As a note, we have also used Samsung 25 watt chargers, which are also amazingly fast. We did notice a speed difference between the 25 watt charger and this 45 watt charger. It doesnt appear to be twice as fast, but it is noticeably faster.

By the way, all these times are anecdotal; we didn't do any timed tests, just what we've noticed through actual use. Our primary devices are S22 Ultras and and the Galaxy Tab 8 Ultra (the large tablet). We also use it on our work iPhones.

The charger also works with everything else. It detects the devices' highest charging rate and automatically adjusts. We use it for our kid's Amazon Fire 7 and any other electronics we need, including some rechargeable flashlights.

Highly recommended.

title: Best Charger for Samsung Galaxy Tab S7/S7+, Real 45 Watt Charger
text:
Samsung 45W USB-C Super Fast Charging Wall Charger is the best charger to get full speed 45 watts charging on a Samsung Galaxy Tab S7/S7+. It also comes with a high quality 5 amp cable that's about 3 feet long. All other third party chargers I've used do not charge the Samsung Galaxy Tab S7 at full speed 45 watts and/or only come with a thin 3 amp cable. The Galaxy Tab S7/S7+ can only get max charging speed at high amps (4+amps), only some chargers and cables can do this.

You need both the charger and cable to support 4+amps to archive the max charging rate on a Samsung Galaxy Tab S7/S7+. I know, I tried with other cables and chargers and found out this limitations. Some off brand cables or chargers would just freak out and keep disconnecting, or just limit my charging rate to 28 watts. This happened even with the best third party brand chargers. Many third party chargers and cables do not support the necessary high voltage/amps combination to Super Fast Charge; make sure to double check! You need a charger that supports PD 3.0 PPS and at least 4+amps to get the fastest Super Fast Charge; this is an optional spec so not all chargers or cables support this high amp rate.

title: Will this charge your device faster? Misunderstood by many.
text: A little advice. Before you pay for a 45w, or even a 25w charger, you need to understand the charging capabilities or limitations of your device. Look up the max charging that it supports. If your device will only allow a 15w charge then no 45w or 25w charger will charge it any faster. Only some select Samsung devices support 45w charging so even if you pay for a 45w charger if your device doesn't support it then it's not going to charge any faster. It's just that simple. Example, all Samsung Galaxy Note 10 phones come with a 25w charger, base Note 10 models do not support 45w charging but a 10+ does support it despite only having the 25w charger included. You have to check for your specific model, not just model range. So if your device does not support 45w fast charging why would you expect that buying a 45w fast charger would change that? It won't, the device will control the charging rate.

title: 8.5% faster charge for $50 is a bad deal
text:
Using a professional watt meter to track voltage, amperage, and wattage, we compared the 25W charger that comes with the Note 10+ to this 45W charger. At no time did the 45W charger actually provide 45W. It runs at 24W at 380 mA almost the entire time while the 25W ran at 27.5W at 350 mA almost the entire time. What this suggests is that this charger is slightly more efficient and will use a little less wall power to charge. It will also likely generate slightly less heat. HOWEVER, on either charger it only takes about 20 minutes to go from dead to 85% (which is when the phone drops down to 10W on both chargers) This nets a potential time savings of one to two minutes. Please do not waste your money on this charger. For the Not 10+ you should be spending around $10-$20.

We also tried plugging this into other non-note 10+ devices. None supported the higher amperage, lower wattage charging. Our assumption is that the note 10+ itself has software on-board allowing it to communicate with the charger.

In regards to build quality, the charging block is larger than stock and comes with a thicker cable. While this may or may not be necessary for function, it did likely cost more to manufacture.

title: It's a misunderstood accessory.
text:
I see a lot of complaints that come from a place of misunderstanding about how this actually works. It's a great charger just like you'd expect from Samsung.

No, it's not "slow" or a scam. Here's the thing: the power output you're getting depends on the current percentage of battery you have left. You won't get the full 45w of charging ALL THE TIME and this is by design. At 0-50% or so you'll get *up to* 45w, sometimes closer to the area of 35w. After that, the charger trickles the power down to protect the battery from overcharging and overheating which makes it appear "slower." The closer you get to 100% full, the less power it will output. So if you plug it in when the battery is already at 75% you'll start out at about 20w and bypass the 45w totally.

In this, you will only see the benefit on short charges when your battery is really low and this charger excels in this context. I can charge my battery from 20% to around 60% in 20 minutes.

The system will also notify you in the pull-down bar if you're using it on a supported Samsung device. I'm using it on my Note 10 Plus and the charger is recognized as "Super Fast Charging 2.0."

It helps if you understand exactly what you're buying and part of the confusion can be blamed on Samsung for how they marketed it to a general public who doesn't understand these things. They just say "WOW! 45w!" and that's what people believe. It's true, just not in the way you'd expect. The 45w is conditional.

With that explanation out of the way, I would definitely recommend this charger if your device supports it. There's no downside. You can only gain advantage by boosting charging output at low percentages over the standard 25w charger.

Yes, this is a genuine Samsung charger made in Vietnam with retail packaging and not a bootleg. I wouldn't trust anything else out there. Go for it if you can spare the extra cash. I feel that it was worth it.

title: It is indeed a fast charger.
text:
This charger is of the quality that you'd expect from any of Samsung's official chargers. With charging just over an hour or even much less depending on how low you've run your battery, you can't go wrong. I myself have an S22 Ultra that is often times between 20-30% at the end of a heavy use day (for me) and I am able to plug it in and have it topped up by the time I'm all settled in and ready to relax at home.

It charges very quickly at first so you can always add a quick bit of extra juice if need be but do note that after 30-40 minutes, it does slow down as charging does cause heat and Samsung is trying to save the integrity and longevity of your battery. And by slow down, I mean it charges as fast or faster than the 25W chargers.

Overall, I've been using it for over a month now and I couldn't be happier with this purchase.

I've used tempered glass screen protectors for years but the fingerprint reader was finicky and somehow it fell face down and hit right at the edge and it cracked the protector and the glass and the screen underneath. After paying my deductible and getting a brand new phone I decided to try the flexible ones again and I am very happy with this Samsung brand one.

title: Best low relection/precise cut/curve screen adhesion(w/out pealoff) factory s.protector you can get!
text:
Base on my pass experience with Samsung factory installed screen protector, it is very well made & stick strong even after year of two (although it still full of scratch on that time, but it is expected with such thin & not glass made material, at the end it’s job is protect the screen being scratch & can be replace, so it done the job well). Compare to other made screen protector, which usually peal off at the curved zone, poor visibility during direct sunlight, difficult to touch (due a poor and soft rubber usually used), and high reflection (most disturbing), Samsung made screen protector feel like glass, and it last very very long unless being hit by any sharp object, it just —— stick very well even until the time you upgrade your phone !

So back to this order, well, since last year, Samsung stop install factory screen protector on it’s new phone anymore, so I am force to buy 1. And I will not give any chance to other brand anymore base on my last poor experience, no matter how great their advertisement, and I know it gonna be replace soon once it have full of scratch anyway, even you have a toughest glass screen protector, the screen still will break if the impact zone is right. So, I will gonna buy Samsung one, and I expect it will be same quality/material as my previous Samsung phone — a very thin layer of protector.

Here in Malaysia, Samsung store did sell at much cheaper price compare to Amazon US, but sadly, it is out of stock since months ago, and I wouldn’t want to wait any longer as my S22 Ultra has showing few hairline scratch on it’s “Victus+” screen even I taking care very much. So I just brought one here even it is 2X more expensive than buying at my country (no stock).

The package arrive before promised delivery date, and it is in good shape. It come with 2x screen protector (which is best, you can replace again next year) , micro fiber clothe, plastic holder for fixing the phone position when installing, 2 dust removal sticker, and 1 Paper Card (for applying pressure after sticking protector).

Here is my tips for anyone would want to have perfect application, this is my first time to stick screen protector (usually I let mobile store done the job as I have no idea how to make it good!) But it is simple if you follow my guide, and you won’t need to waste 1 protector, you can save it for next replacement, here we come :

1) Do this job in any closed room, alone, with good interior lighting. Sitting down with a clean table (with more space is better).

2) Turn off any fan, air-conditional, air purifier, any device that can made air circulation, turn all off. Stay away from any fabric made item (eg. Bed, pillow, ) that can generate fine dust/debris.

3) Torch light or Table light that can generate reflection for the phone screen. (In my case I use my iPad Pro LED Torch with MagicKeyboard) The light will make you see any debris/dust easily during installation.

4) A Sheet of A4 White paper. This will make the light from torch only reflect on your phone screen, not together with your table.

5) Slow & steady, step by step following the number from the protector (eg. step 1 > step 2).

6) Turn off your phone. Then wipe your phone (especially the curve screen area) with wet cloth, let it dry for few mins. Wipe the screen with included micro fiber cloth, use 1 of the dust removal sticker *(Cut to small size before use, it will be more easy to do) to remove all dust. Don’t throw away just yet, it will still need during installation process.

7) Do not apply too much pressure before all screen area has been applied. Let the protector slowly sit/fit into the screen, only apply pressure when all zone is apply (no worry for the small bubble if have any, it still can remove/move before the curve screen area be sticked).

8) !! REMEMBER !! Do not apply pressure to curve screen area before all flat area has been completely stick well. (As the protector has very good adhesion, once the curve area been sticked, you can’t remove any bubble anymore), only apply pressure when everything is okay *(Very last stage !)

8) Use dust removal sticker to remove latest dust mm by mm while installing the screenprotector (removing the bluecolor layer), so that you wont have any dust left inside the protector. Even-though you have done it earlier, it still will have dust coming when installing (from your moving hand and cloth), so you will need to repeat doing until the protector fully covering the screen.

9) Apply pressure evenly across screen after all stick.

10) Let it sit for 10 mins before turn on the phone, do not put any case just yet ! You will see some tiny bubble within 10 mins, no worry, it will disappear once you apply pressure on it. It will take time to stick in. Just wait.

After 10 mins, everything will be alright. You are now have the most clear / smooth / low reflection / perfect screen protector on your S22 Ultra. Remember to Add / Modify finger-print again, it will make unlock process more responsive. (In my case I add the same finger-print one more time for more accurate detect)

So why I remove 1 star ? No, everything is perfect. The quality is top notch. Just that, there is two line visible in curtain reflection angle due to the bluesticker cut out (manufacture process) which you can see in 1 of my picture. It will be disappear when the screen is on, but noticeable during screen off. It is inner side of the protector, so you wont feel when scrolling, it is not annoying but you know it is there, that’s all.

Anyway I am still very satisfied with the protector and I bet there has no other better option than this.

title: An excellent "side phone" that does all the things your iPhone doesn't anymore

For a cheap phone, it's still a Samsung. It has a dual sim tray plus a memory card, which is wonderful when traveling internationally. The combination of face and fingerprint is a bit spotty but rarely gets in the way. The response is a bit laggy when you want to get a picture but then again, it's a $200 phone - this is not the best Samsung can do. It even has a headphone jack and a USB-C port.
Basically, as Apple keeps deleting features like hardware sim cards that are critical to travel internationally, a system like this is ideal to close the gaps in your Apple ecosystem without transitioning completely to Android. I liked it enough to get a Mint Mobile contract for it to keep playing with on return to the US. And since Galaxy Watch systems work better with Samsung and now support base Google watch features as well, this may be a good "gateway drug" to a full Apple replacement ecosystem if they continue to make worse products over time.

Camera: Probably the best camera I've used on a phone but the zoom camera it's not S22 ultra.
Audio: Powerful front facing stereo speakers and there's a headphone jack.

title: Looks nice, fits okay, but...
text:
I bought one of these cases last year when I first got my phone. Right off I noticed that the opening for the camera lenses didn't really match the phone - it is too large, which surprised me for a case that is supposedly manufactured by Motorola. Otherwise it is a good fit - the buttons operate nicely and the case is designed to make it easy to find the fingerprint reader. It makes the phone feel slim and it is easy to handle.

Everything was fine until a couple of months ago when I dropped my phone for the first time. It slipped out of my hand as I was putting it in my back pocket (from less than 3 feet) and landed hitting the bottom left corner of the case on a hard, flat surface. Rather than protecting my phone, the case transferred enough energy to crack the glass along the bottom half inch of the display. Since the phone was still functional, I didn't bother to replace the display. That was lucky, because this week my phone slipped off of our coffee table from less than two feet, landing flat on the display side of the case. This time, the glass was shattered over the middle to top half of the display as if the phone was not in a case at all!

I don't know what kind of drop testing they did with this case but it certainly wasn't from 6 feet as described in the product page. I've been using open face cases like this one for a decade or more with several different smart phones and I have never had any display damage at all despite numerous accidental drops. Needless to say, I will be ordering a different case to go with my replacement phone. Buyer beware.

title: Want to touch it!
text:
What strikes me first is how nice the pattern feels to rub my fingers across. It's rough, but in a most pleasant way. I almost feel like a cat rubbing it's face on a laptop monitors corner. I just want to keep touching it.

I haven't had any sort of drop to test the durability. But I have confidence. Lip comes past the screen, but just barley. Phone feels snug in the case.

It doesn't slip while propping it up on a shelf like my otterbox would horribly (previous phone). Otterbox seemed better for protection, but this is a lot nicer for being more stable and less likely to need protection. And it's designed intelligently, with the case power button having a distinguishing texture apart from the volume keys.

I am just completely stoked about this case! The only think i don't like is the motorola logo on the back. It's subdued, but the fact that you already get the logo on the back with the thumbprint scanner makes it highly undesireable to me. Plus the ring holder I stuck to the back has it's own logo. So that's 3 subtle logos on the back. REALLY not a fan of this. But I think everything good about the case still keeps it at a 5. But the redundant logo did make me consider making it a 4. All the same, thank you Mororola for making a smart case!

There is one other "almost" down side. The photos make this case looked washed out, while other cases have exaggerated contrast to hide the face that they are washed out in person. Do don't let that fool you when looking at competing cases. Consider the contrast in person to be about the same on all of them.

title: Amazing camera with a full featured phone attached
text:
I got everything working great on this phone even 5g at full speeds on T-mobile. You simply have to disable dual sim mode. Which I don't use anyway since I put in my SD card.

I just entered these digits in the phone app to access the debug mode
*#*#4636#*#*

Selected Phone Information

Toggled off "Enable DSDS" to disable the dual sim standby

Rebooted and poof full fat 5g on T-mobile with the international version of the phone.

The heating really hasn't been much of an issue accept when charging because it charges super fast. The OTA update seemed to help this a lot. I did have some heating issues when first transferring everything over from my original phone. If you like to use your phone while plugged in that might be an issue but I rarely do that and since it charges so fast you can just put it down for 20 minutes or so and it will get a bunch of charge. My wife handed me the charge cable last night when I was at 15% and it was at 43% when I looked next.

THE CAMERA IS AMAZING. The default LUT has rich deep colors and it has good low light support/mode. The few low light photos I've take it's done a good job of detecting the situation and doing a long exposure. Only one time last night I was trying to take a picture of a dark scene and the long exposure didn't auto kick in. I'm sure there is a way I can manually trigger this. I haven't had a ton of time or reason to dig into the deeper manual modes and all the camera settings. For the most part the basic mode is very functional for all my simple shooting needs.

title: If you think this will replace your Sony Mirrorless Cameras... think again.
text:
TLDR: The camera features are not as good as advertised...

Let me start off by saying that I do NOT like Andriod OS. I'm an iPhone user till the day I die. I got this phone with the intention of ONLY using it as a camera as the 3 lenses, picture quality, features looked UNREAL. I was misled. This camera is NO WAY a replacement for your bigger Sony cameras. The dynamic range is laughable, the colors are trash, and the camera loses focus VERY often. The 85-125mm lens turns to absolute mush when you shoot anything above 500 iso.

I could go on about how awful the camera is, but just know, if you're looking to use this as even a B-CAM to your Sony Alpha's, you will be VERY disappointed. I had high hopes but was let down.

title: A well-rounded package.
text:
Replaced my water-damaged Mark III with this. I find the previous version's form factor having better ergonomics; but I like that one can disable that annoying always-on fingerprint reader with this one.
Pretty much as speedy as the previous one. And that gorgeous display is back!
I don't have VoWifi. I had no 5G connectivity at the beginning either, but I got that to work by sacrificing the set's dual-SIM capability. *#*#INFO#*#*, tap phone options and disable DSSD or something along those lines. No going back from that though, but then you're 5G ready all the time; and while I do miss that second SIM slot when travelling, the benefit balances the scales nicely for me.
The main camera temperature seems a bit cooler than the one on the predecessor; otherwise there is nothing of note to distinguish between the two. As novel a feature as it may be, I am not convinced that the limited range of the variable lens is enough to suggest a sensible upgrade over the Mark III.
Plenty internal space too; makes that micro SD slot provision feel redundant for most people; but if you're as finicky with the quality of your multimedia files (seeing that this thing is squarely aimed at audio/video-philes) as I am, you'll find its availability an equally welcome blessing as that of that headphone jack.
A noticable improvement in the battery as well; lasts a bit longer than the Mark 3 off a single charge. The older model charges up a bit quicker though.
That missing star's due to the omission of the data transfer cable. Ya, I know.

title: Excellent USB-C charger. Delivers the watts and you get TWO ports.
text:
Just about everything is moving to USB-C these days. I have a iPhone that still uses lightning, though I hear that will be changing to USB-C you in the future. I also have a iPad 11 inch which uses USB-C. I have always been impressed with Anker. I've been buying their products forever. This 40 W charger did not disappoint.

Now I only need one charger when traveling. You can easily find USB-C to lightning cables. That cable along with a standard USB-C cable is all I need. One charger for my iPad and iPhone. This charger also supports the two important fast charging protocol: power delivery and QUALCOMM quick charge.

My understanding is that both of these allow the voltage and amps to increase, if your device supports it, on each port. Your device will charge faster if it supports power delivery or QUALCOMM quick charge. My iPhone definitely charged faster, but that's compared to the 5v/1amp cube charger. I'm not sure if my iPad charged faster or not. It's not something I can to take with me.

You won't go wrong with the this Anker charger. It will deliver consistent power up to what your device can accept. You get 2 ports in the same size as a OEM 1 port device. Great solution for people looking to reduce the amount of devices they have to carry.

title: It chargers fast and saves space
text:
When I got the new iPhone 13, the whole USB-C switch thing was annoying but necessary. They don't even include a charger in the box anymore lol ridiculous. But the 20W chargers that Apple sells are great for caring with you when travelling, but they're a waste of a power outlet--it's inefficient in terms of both space and power consumption since you would have to leave it plugged in unused if you want it to be there for you when you need it, or unplug, put it away and plug it back in when you need it and you might just lose it. You might as well just buy a full MacBook Pro USB-C charger!

This Anker 40W 2-port USB-C charger makes so much more sense to me! It lets me leave a USB-C chargers plugged in at all times, while using one USB-C outlet for leaving my Apple HomePod mini plugged in, and an additional 6 foot long USB-C to lightning cable for charging my new iPhone or my iPad. It charges fast, so you can pretty much just plug your iPhone in for like an hour and then unplug it to switch to another device. It's also compact and unobtrusive. Lastly, it's also affordable and comes from a good reliable brand you can trust.

Highly recommended.

text:
This has got to be one of the best wall chargers I've ever used. I've nothing but the best experience with this brand of charger and consider myself a lifelong customer. I paired mine with official Anker USB-C cables for my iPhone 11 (which any cable brand will do really) and whether my phone is on 1% or 10% I've watched my phone get up to 50% charge in sometimes under 30 minutes with minimal warming of my phone's battery. After it his the 50% range it optimizes to a lower rate (probably iOS's built in dynamics) but still quick charging to full capacity. There's not much else to say other than it can charge an iPad Air 3 at the same time without skipping a beat. Though my iPad obviously has a larger battery and capacity it takes a little while longer to get to 50% but it's still nicely done at a reasonable rate.

I would highly recommend this product as well as their line of cables and car chargers as well.

title: Supports Rapid Charging on Google Pixel 6, but not on Galaxy S20
text:
Overall, I really like this charger. It's Anker, so you know it's built well and reliable. I recently bought a new Google Pixel 6 Pro and my girlfriend got a new Samsung Galaxy S20, neither of which came with power bricks. Luckily, we still had our power bricks from our previous Pixel and Galaxy, so we were good, but I figured I'd take a chance on a new one, for when we travel.

The Anker brick supports "Charging Rapidly" on my Google Pixel 6Pro, but not "Fast Charging" on the Galaxy. I don't know if this is a wattage thing, or a "standards" thing, but the Anker says it supports PIq 3.0 and Fast Charging, so a little surprised that we're not getting the "Fast Charging" message on her Galaxy.

Anyway, for the price, I'm happy and it gives us the option to have two USB connections on one brick, for when we travel

text:
Having recently had a power bank of theirs explode in my office, nearly consuming the house in flames, I started doing some research behind what used to be my beloved Anker brand. I’ve learned that they stopped UL certifications several years ago, which means these sort of devices are not being thoroughly tested by an independent third party AMERICAN company to ensure safety of the devices in various potentially dangerous situations.

That being said, I’m throwing away all of my newer Anker devices that aren’t UL certified and will be finding a new brand that takes the extra steps to ensure mine and my family’s safety.

title: BE AWARE:  Mine Sizzled & Sparked & Failed ...
text:
BE-AWARE: Read Consumer-Product-Safety Issues BEFORE You Decide to use this design.
I travel a lot, the ‘SWIVEL-PRONGS’ sound like a good space-saving feature UNTIL they start SIZZLING-SPARKING and FAIL. After approximately 1 year of use the swivel-prong connections (internal-electrical-connections) FAILED ALARMINGLY. I experienced this when ours increasingly SIZZLED-SPARKED & FAILED. The wall-electrical-sockets are perfect; I tested these and switched with the same sizzling-sparking. I then decided to to CHECK/READ the US Consumer Products online: Saferproducts .gov and click on "search for unsafe products"; once there I searched for "USB battery charger" and I used the left-hand-side-filter for Anker Technologies. THIS IS WORTH TAKING A FEW MINUTES TO DO ... since, in my opinion/experience, my detection of this sizzling-sparking gradual failure may have prevented a blown wall socket, or at the worst a fire. BE SMART - check the US product safety site BEFORE using and depending on this item. After a focused search for Mil-Spec rated wall-chargers, I finally did find a FIXED-PRONG USB CHARGER that I did purchased on A_azon ... it was the Ot_erbox brand. It has performed flawlessly for years.

title: Powerful, does what I needed it to do
text:
I was looking for a charger to keep in my bathroom on the counter for wireless charging my watch and phone while I shower. I had a one-port charger for my phone, but upgrading to two while still having rapid-charge capabilities to quickly top the watch off in a short time was hard to come by without extras or at a high expense. The newer style Anker chargers with dual USB-C and a USB-A were overkill, definitely small but also expensive and I didn't need that power (65W) or the third port, or the light weight even for this purpose, though I have at least three of those for travel and love them.

I went back and forth on a couple of models, but settled on this one for power output and price trade-off. Still should max out the charging power on both devices, though I have some concerns that even plugging the Xi charger in for my phone will lower the output on the Watch charger a bit. I haven't measured to confirm, but in daily use it's been powerful enough to charge both devices at once in the time I have--I don't care if the phone charges much at all but the Watch I want to top off and it usually either does or covers the day easily.

The light on the front is bright; my wife doesn't like it and put some electrical tape over it so it doesn't act light a night light and blind her in the night, which hasn't bothered me at all. It's in a dedicated spot for one purpose and has worked well so far.

title: Important Limitations to Consider
text: There are so many products that need charging in my house with so many different styles of USB port, I never bothered to stock many USB C to USB C cables.  Instead, I mainly have the full size USB A male to USB A male cable and every type of adaptor, so I can turn the standard USB A plug into any other type of USB plug: USB C, mini A, micro A, mini B or micro B.  I have used one at each end of the same cable, in some instances.  This has worked just fine for me...until these charging blocks arrived at my house.  They don't seem to like cables with even one adaptor on it.  Somehow, it detects the in-line adaptor and won't send power to charge the device through it.  The other problem I have is often mentioned here: it doesn't stay in the power strip.  It goes flops out, and just when I'm ready to use the device, it's deader than before.  I am also usually a big fan of Anker products, and normally I think it's obnoxious to plug a different product in a review for another.  It makes me suspicious that it's written by someone from the other company.  However, I can't help recommending the "SlimQ" chargers I bought recently.  They are much more compact, so there is less chance they will topple out of a power strip.  Also, when I plug my Android 8 phone into one, I actually get the message "Super fast charger connected" as opposed to "Fast charger connected".  I read a lot of reviews on the SlimQ that say a phone like the Android 8 is built to use a 15 volt charger and that using anything more than that will not speed up charging and may damage the phone.  I find none of that is true.  The 30 volt SlimQ does charge my phone faster and, after four months of using it, I haven't found that it has damaged my phone in any way.

title: UPDATE: works great on all my devices... now including my galaxy a71 5g
text:
Note: this review is for the model A2628, in case it gets consolidated with reviews of other models in the line.

Update: Just randomly a week or so ago I plugged my A71 5G into this and... it worked. I've also used it to charge additional USB-C devices and everything has worked fine. My phone, a T-Mobile purchased A71 5G, has received two software updates since I wrote the original review. I assume one of these updates fixed whatever the issue was, although the release notes on the updates are extremely light on details.

Anyways, taking this from 4 to 5 stars now. Perfect dual port USB-C charger. Just be aware (and the description clearly states) that it has two 20W capable ports, and that it isn't set for combining them to a single 40W output for laptop charging. The newer model (A2038) does not have this limitation, according to their description.

---original review text follows---

This charger works wonderfully on nearly everything I've tried. Newer Xbox One controllers with USB-C, Samsung Galaxy Tab S5e and S6 lite, 2020 iPad Air, Google Pixel 3, iPhone 12 Mini, Sony wireless headphones (WH-1000XM4), Logitech MX Vertical... even a Microsoft Surface Pro X all work just fine. It might even charge my laptop, a Dell XPS 13, though I've not actually tried that yet, and I don't know if it's high enough power anyways.

But for whatever reason it doesn't charge my A71 5G. I saw another review mentioning an A51 with the same problem. I've seen a few other reviews on other Anker chargers also mentioning the A71 as an issue. Fast charging disabled/enabled doesn't matter. The Anker Powerport III Nano I have charges the A71 just fine. But on this charger the A71 doesn't even react as though something has been plugged in.

I can't really put Anker at fault for that, because the device clearly works - but there are multiple user reports all stating the same thing: Anker has told them it's not compatible with this particular phone (and a few similar models, it seems), so maybe there should be a list of devices that for whatever reason don't work.

I think it defeats the purpose of a universal charger if it can't charge anything you plug in to it (assuming it can provide enough power, I mean), but it seems that Samsung is at fault here for doing something weird with the A71 5G.

I'm not going to return mine - like I said, it works for everything else, and I have a charger for this phone - but the whole point of getting one with two ports was that I wouldn't need to have more than one charger plugged in for all the things.

Anyways, if you've got an A71 5G (or an A51), this probably won't work for you.

title: Decent Dual SIM phone with decent camera - cell reception in US so-so
text:
I needed a dual SIM phone, which really limited my options. Coming from another Motorola, I wanted another one because I love the Motorola gestures (chop for flashlight, twist for camera, twist again for selfie, brilliant!).

I'm using this phone with US Mobile and T Mobile and my reception is so-so. T-Mobile uses 3G Band4 (3G), and Band 4 and 66 (LTE) which is not part of this phones repertoire. But I also think the general signal in my neighborhood is just weak. I wish more (affordable) phones for the US market had dual sim.

Phone itself is fine. I easily get a two days of use out of the battery. It's plenty fast for me, but I am not a gamer nor a "heavy user". I think my only mild dislike is that it's really big! Like unnecessarily so. Smaller screen would lead to a smaller battery but also to slower battery drain, so personally I would opt of a smaller screen next time.

As for the camera; it takes decent photos. Nothing special. The macro lens is pretty cool and takes okay photos. It's perfectly fine for a point-and-shoot camera. This is not a flagship phone, but it can definitely hold its own.

Having this phone for 2 months+ I am quite comfortable. People complain about the display, but it's bright enough, and larger than Z3. The swiping and touch screen is a little different, but it's comfortable now. Works great.

title: Does Work with 240V for international travel See Below
text:
Does work with 240V. I have also confirmed the NRTL rules.

Thank you for contacting Anker Customer Service. Sorry for the confusion we've caused.

Please know that both the AC outlets and USB ports on the Anker 615 USB C Power Strip can support 100-240V for travel use. But the product itself and the manual only state 125V. This is because of certification.

About the input--125V/10A located on the product and specification, it is the standard design for the US. In addition, according to the new changes in NRTL(Nationally Recognized Testing Laboratory) certification requirements, we are not allowed to print 100-240V on the product itself.

I will forward your case to our concerned team so that hopefully, we will have more information available on our website in the future. Sorry for the inconvenience we've caused.

If you have any other questions or would like me to clarify anything else, please, let me know. I am always glad to help in any way I can.

title: Heavy & clunky. Not as useful as comparable others. Not Returnable despite saying Free Returns
text:
I bought this on a 30% discount coupon for traveling and tried to send it back when it proved too heavy and clunky for less-than-usual utility. Despite saying "Free Returns" on the Amazon sales page, when I tried to return it, I got a message that A POWER STRIP is a "personal item that cannot be returned" !!!!!! Amazon made good on the return, but I had to contact them and complain.

The Pros: This has a longer (3 ft) cord that does store inside the unit. It says the USB-C's are 65W (I didn't test), which is enough to charge a computer. I does have the advertised 2 three-prong power outlets, 2 USB-C's, and 1 USB-A.

The Cons:
1. This beast weighs 11.2 oz (318 g) - or close to 3/4 of a pound!! For only 2 plugs, 1 USB-A, and 2 USB-C's. (For comparison, I have a Tessan that has surge protection and has 3 three-prong outlets, 1 two-prong outlet, 3 USB-A's and 2 USB-C's and weighs 5.6 oz (158 g) - or HALF the weight of this Anker product. The Tessan also cost less than half the price of this Anker - WITH the 30% coupon!!)

2. No surge protection.

3. Despite the Amazon sales page saying "Free Returns," when I went to return it, I got a message that this power strip was a "personal item" that could not be returned!!!! I had to contact Amazon and complain to get the advertised return.

My advice: Stay away. There's much more useful, less expensive, less heavy options out there.

title: Anker 615 Power Strip: Champ or Chump? 🤔
text:
First, let’s highlight some specs:

- Dimensions: 2-1/4” x 2-1/2” x 6” (including wrapped cord and wall plug)
- Weight: 11.3 oz
- Cord Length: 3 ft
- Number of Ports/Outlets: 5
- Types of Ports: 1 USB-A, 2 USB-C, and 2 Type B Sockets (Standard US w/ 3 pins: hot, neutral & ground)
- USB-C max output is 65W. When using both USB-C ports, the first port you connect to will output 45W, the second port will output 18W max.
- USB-A port maxes out at 12W.
- Voltage: 100-240V～50/60Hz (more on this later)
- Warranty: 24-Month with up to $25,000 insurance for connected devices.
- MSRP: $69.99 (often on sale for as low as $49.99 + tax)

Now, here are the 3 questions I’ve tried to answer. Also, check out my photos 📸 for a closer look 👀

1️⃣ What are you getting for your money? Are you getting a compact 3ft extension cord with 2 sockets? Or are you getting a 65W GaN fast charger with 3 ports? You are actually getting BOTH!

2️⃣ How does this Anker product compare to the competition? The best I could find browsing Amazon’s endless catalogue was a top-rated power strip by “NTONPOWER.” It has 4 ft cord, 1 USB-A , 1 USB-C with 45W Gan charging and 4 Standard US sockets. It’s listed for $48 and goes on sale for just under $40.

3️⃣ Is it worth it? It’s almost a tossup between the two, right? We’re talking a $10 difference! But once I realized that, then it was an easy choice for me: I’d rather spend a little more with a Brand I know, with good track record and solid warranty than to save $10 and possibly ruin my electronics and my trip!

Cons 👎👎👎

This power strip isn’t without its flaws, some are minor and others are inexplicably stupid! Here’s a short list:

- The Voltage Fiasco: I don’t understand why Anker has done this: The product listing and description, as well as customers’ anecdotal accounts all confirm: this power strip supports 100-240V～50/60Hz. The packaging you will receive mentions only “125V AC 60Hz 10A” 😳 Was it a printing error? Was it a certification problem? No matter, Anker should’ve cleared this mess up 😡
- The Rubber Flap is a Flop 😒 It looks neat and may serve some function but I agree with other reviewers, it’s just not necessary.
- Misleading Info: I hold Anker to higher standards. The measurements do not account for the cord sticking out 😠
- One side is glossy which looks beautiful when photographed but is a fingerprint magnet 😒

My Verdict 🧐

Despite its shortcomings, this power strip makes a good tech companion for savvy travelers. It’s compact, robust and versatile. I got mine. You should get yours before your next trip! It’ll come in handy 🧳✈️😎

Hope my review has helped you make a more informed buying decision 👍😊✌️

🚨 🚨 Anker’s Response (02/21/2022) 🚨 🚨

“Both the AC outlets and USB ports on the Anker 615 Charging Station ( GaNPrime 65W ) can support 100-240V input for travel use safely… [But] according to the new changes in certification requirements, we are not allowed to print 100-240V on the product itself.”

The fact that Anker reached out to clarify means they actually listen and care about their customers. I appreciate that and so felt obligated to include this in my review for the benefit of the readers. I also attached a screen grab from Anker’s email 😊✌️

title: Clever design for a powerful charging station

I needed something that would charge my phone and computer at the same time. This works great, both devices receive a quick charge using the two usb c ports, leaving a usb a port and a plug for other things. You could turn the charging station on its side and use the plug on the bottom, too, if needed.

I probably won't be using this for travel as I think it is heavier than my 30,000mah charging brick. The only problem I have had is that sometimes when you plug two devices into it at the same time, you have to check to be sure that both are charging and then re plug the one that isn't. Usually only have to do this once to get them both going. Just a small irritation that does not detract from the usefulness of this device that much.

This is a good value for the price.

text:
I only know so far that it can charge my Deck within 2-3 hours, I haven't clocked it for science yet.
It seems to be solid at getting from 10ish-60% in an hour with it turned off, which is decent, and from 60-80 fairly not terribly long after. I wrote a brief essay about my experience using this with the Steam Deck, which I've had all of 3 days now, for which I do not apologize - skip if you like:

[The Deck throttles charging immensely, with it taking ridiculous amounts of time to get above 90, and even moreso at 95%. I feel like it's laughing at this charger, and there's nothing I can do about it 😂 Each passing percent beyond 80, the Deck asks for less and less power - so much though, that I am going to see what keeping the battery around 18-85 will do for it's health and longevity, and not bother going past 90 due to the extreme time (like an hour?) to fill completely, and wear on the battery and new srs biznuss charger.]

I can confirm this does NOT warp charge the Oneplus 7 Pro, neither with the original cable, nor my 10 ft 65w Anker cable. With the latter it does rapid charge tho, ~75%/hr according to Accubattery, and tested for 30 mins. This is due to Oneplus' proprietary charging technology, I was hoping this charger could, ahem, outpower it haha. Sadly, not the case. Not knocking any stars for that of course.

I imagine this will work great for charging Samsung 2020+ newer devices at at least 30w, tho I have no way to test myself. May have a buddy bring his 22 Ultra and Switch, and get back to you eventually

I see myself using this same charger to powerup my Nothing 2 once it launches in the US a couple years from now 🤓

title: Much better than a standard Wall Charger!
text: I'm a fan of Anker products.  I recently received a drone as a gift that required more power than my standard chargers were capable of.  I did my standard search and this one popped up as another option.  I wanted to disregard it and move on.  But, i did a little research and this thing is way better than a standard wall charger.  It's more like a mini-surge protector.  I compare it to that because it has a hidden feature--the plug can unwind and lengthen so that you can plug it in behind the night stand--for example--then set the actual charge ports up on the nightstand to conveniently plug into.  Usually you have to move the nightstand away from the wall and try and squeeze the charge cord into it.  And, then repeat the process when leaving.  No longer.  Unwrap the cord--plug it in--and move the charge ports to where you need them. (within @ 3 feet)  Plus it comes with another spot to plug in another item--like the wall charger you normally carry if you need more charge ports or to plug your laptop into.  Great design.  Much more versatile than a standard wall charger.  I highly recommend!

title: essential travel charger
text:

I travel for work with multiple devices that need multiple different voltages and amperage, and this charges everything like a champ. For home use I have an extension cable running directly behind my nightstand, because the power cable on this unit is a little short. The short cable makes it amazing for travel because I can have all my devices charging on a hotel nightstand without a mess of cables everywhere.

text:

It’s powerful enough to charge my iPad Pro and my iPhone at the same time at full speed, as well as my wife’s MacBook Air by itself, which more than covers my power usage on the go. If you plan on traveling with a laptop that uses more power to charge (MacBook Pro, etc.), you might want to consider something with more wattage if you want full charging speed.

My only wish is that there was some way to stand the charger up on its side for the instances that you use the single outlet on it’s back, as doing so often typically leaves the adapter resting against the back plug.

title: Do not buy. I repeat, do not buy
text:
This case is garbage, and Samsung doesn't warranty it or stand behind this product.

I had my phone sitting in my bike bag all by itself. When I reached my destination and went to retrieve my phone from the bag, the thin frame around the front screen had literally snapped.

If it can simply snap while sitting in a padded bag, imagine how well this case will protect your expensive phone if it's dropped three feet. I doubt it will even protect your phone if dropped a for. This is not a very thick cover.

It also doesn't protect the camera lenses because it's not very thick.

There's no protection for the spine.

There's also no belt clip, but I knew this when I bought it. My score isn't a reflection of no belt clip. This is just informational.

Bottom line is the protector isn't worth the price you pay for it. It's maybe worth only $5.

I have a older model which still works, but I do have to be a bit more careful of how I set things down on it in order to get a charge. title: Not slim, but the stand feature is great
text:
This is slimmer than the case with the S-pen that Samsung gave out for free during the pre-order period, but just barely. If you are coming from a Fold 2 or 3 with an Aramid case, you'll definitely notice the increase in thickness. That said, the stand feature is awesome which justifies the extra bulk for me (note that the angle for the stand is not adjustable). The case feels sturdy and high quality. I took out one star because:

1. The cover for the front (outer) screen doesn't stay firmly attached, even with the included adhesives. I ended up applying some double-sided tapes of my own.
2. The phone lies flat on the desk when folded (which I love), but wobbles when unfolded. This is because the cover for the back is thicker than the cover for the front screen (due to the built-in stand).

Overall, this is a high quality Samsung case with a useful stand feature for those who don't mind a bit of extra bulk.

title: Poor, Lazy Design on Samsung's Part
text:
I normally like to add photos of the products I review. Sadly, I don't have photos of this case on my phone...because I use my phone to take photos.

This case...works. That's about the best I can say for it. Samsung has engaged in some SERIOUSLY lazy design on this one, and it's an insult that they charge what they do for it (even with the SIGNIFICANT discount you get buying through Amazon).

Does the case suck? No. It's functional. It is not tight, however, and I find it pops off too easily. The real, serious issues, however, are with the S-Pen and S-Pen holder.

First, this case DOES come with the (basic) S-Pen for the Z-Fold 4. This is NOT, however, the S-Pen Pro, so forget the Bluetooth functionality of that - and incidentally, if you DO purchase the S-Pen Pro? It won't fit in the S-Pen holder for this. It's too wide. Which then makes having the holder moot.

Let's not even begin to discuss the fact that Samsung is now charging you a MINT to buy an accessory that should be INTEGRAL TO THE PHONE, and always has been until the recent past. Focing your customers to pay extra for an S-Pen is an insult, when the S-Pen is what sets Samsung above and beyond all the other phones ont he market. Offering a "premium" S-Pen at a premium extra price, especially on what is already the most expensive phone on the market, is Apple-level skullduggery. This is nothing short of Samsung giving their loyal customers the middle finger.

Even worse, the current model's S-Pen DOES NOT WORK ON THE COVER SCREEN, ONLY THE UNFOLDED INTERIOR SCREEN. Another insult, which makes it onerous and far less useful. On the old Note phones all you had to do was pop out the pen and blam. You're taking notes on the screen. Now you have to dig it out from the holder, open the phone, awkwardly balance the screen that is not sized to hold with one hand, and try to write. The Z-Fold 4 is a great idea. The implementation of the S-Pen feels like an insulting afterthought.

Now, back to the actual case. Another piece of lazy design: this has an S-Pen holder and a kickstand so you can stand up the phablet when open on a table. Another great idea...EXCEPT YOU HAVE TO PHYSICALLY REMOVE THE PEN HOLDER TO INSTALL THE KICKSTAND, AND VICE-VERSA.

That's right, folks; you cannot have the S-Pen holder on the phablet while the kickstand is also on the phablet. I solved that issue by buying a folding pocket keyboard that came with its own folding phone stand, but still, let's be fair...THIS IS A $90 PHONE CASE (which Amazon, to their credit, is selling for $65, so good on you, Amazon).

Still, I cannot recommend this case at all. Nor can I recommend the obnoxiously expensive basic S-Pen. You're far better off to go with a third-party case and third-party Z-Fold 4 compatible stylus. You'll save tons of money and probably end up with a much nicer case.

title: Good case for not a case friendly phone
text: Cases are subjective and it depends on what you are after for your zfold4 so I will try to give my fair assessment of this product. If you are looking for a minimal case to prevent scratches and marks during daily use, and if your are careful with your phones - this is a perfect case. The case back "is" leather but not your typical what you'd think or expect (Samsung actually states this is the real deal and not vegan or faux leather) - the front piece is plastic. Fitment is excellent and yes, you'll have to use the tape for the front cover to ensure everything stays tight (back cover does not use or need tape). I have no need for the s pen, if you do then this case is probably not for you. I have purchased half a dozen high dollar cases for this phone and have been disappointed in all of them becuase of one or more failures in functionality or design (too thick, can't wireless charge, sloppy fitment, built in screen protector, erratic hinge protection movement, cheap feeling, and the list goes on) - this is the first case that meets most of my criteria. That is the true problem with this phone, you have to prioritize your needs from an accessory standpoint. I happen to like minimal cases to keep an already bulky phone in check. My only gripe so far is the price is a bit absurd but the zfold4 is the fancy new flagship phone so accessories are always going to be a premium.  If you are going to swap cases a lot, I can see a couple of potential issues with this case - 1. You'll need to be careful removing the front cover after initial install as the tape is quite strong and you could break the front portion. 2. I don't know how well the tape holds up after multiple swaps. 3. How the leather holds up - only time will tell.

title: !!There is no adhesive strips!! :D
text:
I repeat! There is no adhesive strips! I've watched quite a few videos on this case and each youtuber tends to say that there are adhesive strips. No. No, they are not adhesive. They are more like little rubbery pads to help keep the case gripped to the phone but not adhesive. There was one single comment I read somehwere that mentioned manufactures no longer using adhesive. While I can't vouch for other case brand's Z Fold 4 cases, I can say for certain that this Samsung case does NOT have adhesive. I was a Z Fold 3 user prior, and absolutely refused to use adhesive strip cases. I bought this case to test and I am happily keeping it. I tend to remove my cases for cleaning here and there and removing adhesive is a pain and it always leaves something behind and this case does NOT. I have removed this case for cleaning both the phone and the rubbery pads and it was a breeze. Here's a few things I liked and disliked albeit not many things I disliked.

Things I liked
1. Case is slightly grippy but not like previous samsung z fold cases that were too grippy and just grapped pocket lint. This case goes in clean and comes out clean.
2. The kickstand is sturdy and snaps back to the phone using two little magents. Simple and very effective.
3. Overall design and size. I gotta say, whoever at samsung designed this, did an excellent job on this case. It's not too bulky but just big enough to give you confidence when handling the phone. The cutouts on the side are perfect, the case never feels to unwieldy and while open, the edges are nice and flush with the actual phone so it doesn't even feel like there's a case on it when handling it while open.

Dislikes
1. This the only thing I can really say about the case and in my opinion, it can be overlooked but have to mention it. Initially I felt the front case didn't hold on as tight as the z fold 3 case from samsung. It might be becasue it was just put on but I gotta say, after using it for a while now, I almost feels more gripped onto the phone after some use. Weird but something to note. It stays on confidently now.

I have to say, in general having been a Z Fold 3 user, tested MANY cases with that phone and now a Z Fold 4 user, I can confidently recommend this case. The feel, size, kickstand and NO stupid adhesives. It's an easy A for me.

title: Excellent Power Delivery, Compact Unit
text:
This device is almost perfect for home or infrequent travel.
First, the device itself is solidly manufactured, 5ft long heavy-duty power supply cable, flat plug to save space, and 3 grounded/surge-protected AC outlets on the back of the device.

Next, the USB situation.
65w split between the following:
2 USB-A (12w max ea)
2 USB-C (65w max ea)
Take a hard look at your power requirements vs the infographic above regarding single to /four-port charging. If you need the full 65W (max) to charge your laptop, that's the only plug you can have connected else the draw splits between the rest of the connected devices.

The cord is 5ft long and very heavy, possibly an inconvenience when traveling if you don't have the space. The new GaN version upgraded this unit with a retractable cord which is perfect but I also read a large number of complaints about the heat generated by that unit.

If you use it next to your bed know there's a very bright LED on the front that I temporarily covered with a small piece of duct tape, YMMV.

Overall would definitely suggest this unit to anyone living or traveling in the USA with an assortment of medium-draw usb devices.

title: Generally happy with Anker but this device was disappointing
text:
I generally trust Anker to put out a high quality product that does what it is supposed to do well and is made well compared to other quite cheap feeling devices found on the internet. This device was sadly disappointing unfortunately.

It is well made from the feel and construction of the device itself to the very robust power cord, almost too robust. It does not bend easily which as others have mentioned makes it a device more suited for once placed in a home, forget about moving it around, it definitely is not for traveling IMO.

The problem, which I find a big problem and quite annoying, is if you are charging in both a USB A and USB C port. In the evening I always plug in my iPhone into the usb a port and my iPad Pro into the usb c port and leave them until the morning when I’ll need them again. Once both devices ‘top off’ the iPad in the usb c port would continually give that audible sound it makes when first plugged in to begin charging. I tried it over the course of 3 nights and it did it each night. The only way to stop it would either be to unplug it or turn off sound notifications on the iPad which is ridiculous do just to charge a device.

I did see someone else in the comments express this happened to them as well so I do hope Anker looks into this and addresses it for future devices.

title: Lacks a basic feature
text: I bought this to use in place of an Anker cube charger, which had three standard USB charging ports as well as three three-prong outlets, because I have started acquiring devices which need USB-C chargers.  I chose this particular Anker device because it has two USB-C charging ports, as well as two standard USB ports, and it does a fine job of charging whatever is plugged into it. title: Perfect for nightstand or desktop
text:
Full disclosure: I love Anker. (This isn’t sponsored but… hit me up, Anker.)

Anker products are high quality, reliable, durable, and are beautifully and thoughtfully designed. I almost exclusively buy Anker products for my power needs and own dozens of their products: power strips, surge protectors, wireless charging pads, wireless MagSafe chargers, power adapters, power banks, charging cables, etc.

I bought this as an upgrade to a previous model that only has one USB-C port because my Apple Watch and iPhone are both USB-C now, and USB-C is the direction tech is headed. The charging power is excellent, especially the USB-C, and, as with all Anker products, it looks great.

Like many of their products, and one of the reasons I’m loyal to them, Anker includes a Velcro cable manager with this. However, one let-down was that they didn’t include a 3M adhesive pad like they do with other products (including the smaller model of this that I have). The inclusion of an adhesive pad would solve the issue other reviewers have mentioned about the cable being too heavy for the charging bank itself, which, along with the brightness of the indicator light, isn’t an issue for me because of how I have it positioned on my nightstand (see photo). Both factors may be worth considering if you plan to position this parallel to the surface of your nightstand and in line-of-sight.

In addition to addressing the concerns of other reviewers, the only other improvement would be more powerful USB-C charging. With a max USB-C output of 67w, its power output is more than adequate for phones, tablets and watches. The USB-C output would be ideal for charging a MacBook Air or Chromebook but would have a hard time keeping up with performance laptops like my XPS, which uses a 120w USB-C, and newer MacBook Pro models that can use 140w.

Lastly, I used to travel weekly for work and rated this three stars for traveling because the cable is a heavy gauge and would take up a lot of space in a carry-on. I did not factor this into my overall rating because that’s not why I purchased it, nor would I recommend using it for travel. Anker makes plenty of other products that are more compact but still offer a variety of charging methods, and I would recommend those.

title: Not actually universal compatibility
text:
This seems like a solid charger. It seems well built and convenient to use. Unfortunately, I had to send it back. Despite advertising "Universal Compatibility," this charger does not provide 12 volts. Now, that wouldn't be a huge deal, except the listing doesn't list what voltages and amperages the charger supports. It just said that it has universal compatibility. Granted, it is common for chargers to leave out 12v, and it is rare for devices to require 12v to function properly. They do exist though, mainly in devices that are powered directly via USB, rather than using it to charge a battery.

I left three stars, since this will work for most things, but if Anker is going to advertise universal compatibility, the product needs to support every part of USB PD, even the optional stuff.

title: Effortless Charging for All Your Devices
text:
The best feature of the Anker 525 Charging Station is that it can speed charge seven devices simultaneously. This is an absolute game-changer for me, as I often find myself with multiple devices that need charging at the same time. I can easily plug all my devices into one charging solution in without the headache of finding extra outlets or switching cables constantly.

One standout positive is the thoughtful spacing and placing of the outlets. Often, I find with other charging stations or compact power strips, the outlets are placed too close together or placed in a absolute idiotic way, making it difficult to charge larger devices with those bulky charging bricks. However, Anker has nailed it with the spacing.

Another aspect that impressed me is the quality of the power cable. It is just the perfect length, allowing me to place the charging station exactly where I need it without having to worry about messy cables cluttering my space. I my case I didn't need to use the included cable tie but still great they included one attached to the cable. Moreover, the cable feels incredibly sturdy, indicating that it's built to last.

Negatives:
While it's tough to find any significant flaws with the Anker 525 Charging Station, I did notice one minor drawback. I personally feel that having two USB-A ports might be a bit excessive. One USB-A port would have been sufficient for most users, and having an additional USB-C port would have been more future-proof. However, this is a minor concern and in no way a deal-breaker for me.

In conclusion, the Anker 525 Charging Station is an excellent investment for anyone who juggles multiple devices that require regular charging. Its ability to accommodate seven devices at once, combined with the well-thought-out spacing, makes it a true winner. The sturdy power cable adds to the overall value of this product, assuring me that it will stand the test of time and maybe hold up the the occasional trip. I highly recommend the Anker 525 Charging Station to anyone in need of a reliable and efficient charging solution. It has made my life so much easier, and I can confidently say it will do the same for you!

title: Do NOT get this amazing phone
text:
I am late to the party but today I finally bought a replacement after issues from day 1 with this phone.

1) Bluetooth module will fail/frustrate you. It works, but just barely. Literally your hand or even a 90 page notebook is all it takes to completely interrupt the signal. Google doesnt care at all, you will not be getting any help.

2) USB port will poop out on you. I can now only use my charging cable in one direction, I tried cleaning and still to no avail.

3) The battery life is either amazing or atrocious. I know this is with any device since it needs to update and do routine things, but 2/7 days of the week my phone will be at 80% (~10% at end of shift) in the hour it takes to get to work, while other days it will be at 95%. According the battery manager nothing is hogging the juice.

4) The screen is fairly useless in direct sunlight

5) 3gigs of ram will bog you WAY down

But to be honest I am sad to get rid of this phone. Its amazing (que run on sentence). The camera I still think is top tier even after 1.5 years, it feels amazing in the hands, it is compatible with everything, the squeeze function is so insanely useful, you get all the updates and new version of android first, I get signal when others dont (on the same network), when I did game on the phone it was extremely responsive and rarely dropped frames.

Yet I paid 1k for this phone. And I learned a 1000$ lesson to never buy from Google since they refuse to stand by their product. If I was alone in my complaint I would just shut up, but google "Pixel 3 bluetooth problems" and you'll see all the complaints in their absolute glory.

And to boot, this issue had been going on through their Nexus lines and all 4 pixel generations.

text:

I am posting this on July 6th so at this moment Android Q is only available in beta. I did give it a try and it's way more stable, battery life is much better in Android Q, so I do think the phone will be great when the official version is released.
But this is a Pixel, you buy this for the camera and you're not wrong. I have compared it with iPhone Xs and it's just on another level, I have even compared it with Huawei P30 Pro and Huawei only have much better zoom, Pixel is just superior with the quality of the photos.
In the audio department, it sounds great, I've seen better like iPhone Xs and Asus ROG phone but it has front facing speakers with excellent quality and volume.
In the screen department, this generation is like 600% better than the Pixel 2, Pixel 2 were just terrible, this one is a very nice AMOLED display, colors are good and accurate, viewing angles are also top.
In the battery life, well... It's not good to be honest. I have found myself charging this thing twice a day with normal use. 3 times even with heavy use.. if you're taking a lot of photos it will just eat your battery. For example, I recorded 8 minutes of the 4th of July fireworks in NYC, it consumed 15-20% of the battery. That's just crazy.
But all this little issues has been resolved with the Android Q, even it being a beta is just much more stable than the current official Android 9.
If you want this Pixel, go for it. It's a great phone. And I hope Android Q will resolve those little issues.

text:
I've had the Google pixel 3XL for several months now and have really enjoyed it; this may even be my favorite phone thus far (and I've had 6 phones over the last 2 years, most being major flagship models). It feels super thin and lightweight, but SUPER durable - my screen is scratch-free (and I don't use a screen protector!), and this phone has survived not just getting dropped A LOT - after missing for 4 days, it was found outside under bricks after days of storms! I wiped the mud off, plugged it in and it worked perfectly (and still does!). The 6.3 inch screen is big, bright and vibrant, with excellent screen-to-body ratio. I've gotten used to the black "notch" that drops down about half an inch at the top because it allows for a great ear speaker and an awesome front camera. Pictures are sharp and portrait mode does an excellent job of putting the face in focus and softening the appearance of imperfections. I've also been very impressed with battery life - I can go a full day on a single charge and haven't noticed any decrease in battery life. I just started using a wireless charger, which works great even with a protective case.

I read reviews that complained about no microSD or headphone jack, but there's plenty of storage space, and the box includes a headphone jack adapter to resolve that issue (although you're unable to charge the device while using headphones).

As always, Amazon shipped my package quickly with next-day delivery and customer service was extremely helpful answering my questions about Amazon warehouse and item specifics. Very satisfied!

*Pictures show camera quality - depth, color, sharpness and portrait mode

title: Can't charge phone and use headphones at the same time (both require the USB port)
text:
Great phone overall; however, there are two minor annoyances.

There is no separate headphone jack -- everything uses the USB-C port. This means that you cannot charge the phone's battery and use headphones at the same time, since they both require the single USB port. The supplied ear buds have a USB-C connector. There is a USB-C to 3.5 mm headphone adapter, so you can use regular headphones.

For what it's worth, the supplied ear buds use a slightly stiffer loop in the cable that fits inside the earlobe, which I find much more comfortable and better-retained than traditional ear buds.

The back of the phone is so slippery that it will not sit in place on even a very slight (e.g., two-degree) slope without sliding off -- e.g., an open notebook in front of my computer screen. This makes a protective cover mandatory for me, which is not a problem since I have a cover.

title: Steps to set up the new Pixel in China
text:
Due to the Great Fire Wall in China, setting up a new Google phone is not that simple as in other countries. Here are the steps I went through: 1) Turn on the phone without inserting a Sim card. 2) Skip those steps that involve connection to the Google server. 3) When the phone completes the start process, connect it to a laptop with a USB cable, and send a VPN or similar app from the laptop to the phone. I have connected the Pixel with another phone or the laptop, using bluetooth, but failed in transferring the VPN app by bluetooth. 4) Connect the Pixel to wifi, run the VPN, the Pixel can now connect to Google server. 5) Continue with other steps like inserting a Sim card, go to Google account and Google Play Store, make necessary downloads and updates, etc.

An annoying issue: Even with the VPN running successfully, and hence so do the apps on the Pixel, the wifi sign keeps showing "no internet". I don't know how to figure out this issue.

The Pixel 3XL comes with Android 9. The 10 is available, and my phone is still downloading the 10 since I set up the phone 2 days ago.

12/26/2019 Update: My phone updated to Android 10 yesterday. A surprise comes out: The wifi sign returns to normal. The tiny cross sign and the wording "wifi connected but no internet" disappeared.

title: Great phone - if you get the right one
text:
The Pixel 3XL is still one of the best phones out there, especially with the camera and more processing power than the newer '3A' version. As a Techie Geek-who-can-Speak, I was especially excited to receive it!

If this phone is ordered 'reconditioned' or 'used', there is a possibility that it won't work. It advertises 'unlocked' - but that isn't always the case. Like the one I received. Indeed, mine displayed 'SIM NOT FOUND' in the upper LH corner no matter which carriers SIM I put in (hey, I tried (4) different carriers for luck?). Then I tried to activate the eSIM switch, no joy either.

Most of these hitting the market are former Verizon phones. Apparently, even when updated, there is a software/hardware bug in some that prevents their use. So 'unlocked' yes, most of the time? It also apparently depends on the last owner of the phone. I have returned it and ordered another. Meanwhile I'm out of comms for two weeks minimum. I'll update this review with pictures and diagnostic "#*CODES#*" to help others who are experiencing issues.

title: It's nothing special
text:
I really had high hopes for this phone. In deciding to upgrade my Moto G5 Plus, I was leaning toward the new G7 model, then I read how the Pixel 3 XL had a better (supposedly the best) camera. As a photography enthusiast, this was a factor in my buying decision.

The Pixel 3 XL is less than an inch taller than my old G6 and not any wider. In taking some initial photos on the Pixel 3 XL, they weren’t any better than those taken by my Moto G6. In fact, some outdoor shots I took with the Pixel 3 XL were oddly dark and required auto adjustment. The Night Sight feature for low light photos isn’t color accurate and adds an off-color tinge to the pictures.

I’ll give it more time to grow on me, but I’m not too optimistic about the camera at this point. The phone has some merits, but the balance of pros vs. cons is really 50/50. In my opinion, this phone is not worth the $500+ premium over the Moto G or Z series.

Do your research…. there are certainly better choices out there depending on your needs.

Pros:
Easy initial set up and smooth data transfer from old phone
Quick start up
Intuitive software
Excellent touch screen
Battery life (20 hours on full charge)

Cons:
Disappointing Camera
No expandable memory
Expensive for what you get
No FM radio built in
Intrusive notch at top of phone

title: NOT new - seems like a great phone if it works correctly (camera issues)
text:
Bought this (Pixel 3 XL) after accidentally destroying the screen on my Pixel 2 XL and going for this instead of trying to fix my old phone (again).

To explain the title, in the Amazon purchase section of the product, I had selected "buy NEW". However, upon immediately opening my "new" phone. Both side stickers of the phone's retail box had been cut completely. So I can only assume that this is a refurbished or renewed model, that said, everything was neatly in the box, nothing missing.

My immediate impression is that it feels great in my hands, is almost the same exact size of the Pixel 2 XL looks great. I have had the phone out of the box it came in for about 3 hours. Signed into it with my Google account and all of my apps and data that was backed up was right there on the phone ready for me to use. The interface is smooth and very similar to the Pixel 2. Took me a second to get used to how to access all open apps, but once I did I like how the Pixel 3 handles it better. Everything was great... until I tried to take a picture.

From a factory reset of turning the phone on, to setting up the phone and updating the software, the rear facing camera would not focus. The back is crystal clear, no scratches. I went though all of the troubleshooting steps recommended by Google. Nothing worked. So I'm returning it. If the camera worked I'm sure I'd love it. The Pixel 3 does have unlimited high res backups to Google Photos. So if you have one where the camera works, then excellent!

I'll update this later based on my experience with the return handling. If you select to return, Amazon contacts the seller who will then contact you (me in this case) with instructions. I'm still waiting on that.

4 stars for now because I really like the phone (aside from camera not focusing, which also seems to happen quite a bit looking around online) but it is NOT NEW. So don't tell me I'm getting a new phone when the box is not even sealed.

I am a software technology professional and I find this policy to be very disturbing and completely unprofessional, to ship a product to a customer without proper testing and validation and then when it breaks the device tell the customer it is up to them to fix is unacceptable.
